The arena actor handler builds the resident flag-API pointer-table base: lui 0x8005 at 0x260 then addiu -0x7544 gives 0x80050000-0x7544 = 0x80048abc. Offsets +0xc and +0x10 of that table are set_flag (0x80048ac8) and get_flag (0x80048acc).
Second get_flag load in the same handler: lw $v0, 0x10($s1) with $s1=0x80048abc reads 0x80048acc = get_flag (F0x800163b0). It is called at 0x298 with $a0=0x100c and $a1=1.

Delay slot of the call at 0x280 (jal 0x800853f8), taken when get_flag(0x100c, 0) returned nonzero: the queued entry id is 0x648 = 1608. The generated stage-interaction table maps s927 entry 1608 to flag_key 01580004, the pre-fight meeting with Kurt.

Delay slot of the call at 0x2a8, taken when get_flag(0x100c, 1) returned nonzero: the queued entry id is 0x64a = 1610, which the generated table maps to flag_key 01580005, the post-fight victory line.
First argument of the native completion hook that begins at file offset 0x338 (decimal 824, the offset the prior canonical doc named): flag id 0x100c.
The hook loads +0xc of the flag-API table built at 0x344/0x348 (lui 0x8005; addiu -0x7544 = 0x80048abc), i.e. 0x80048ac8 = set_flag (F0x800165ac), and calls it with $a1 = 1.
Second set_flag argument in the same hook, issued after the 0x100c write: id 0x7400. It is loaded before the second lw 0xc($s0)/jalr pair at 0x364-0x370, whose delay slot again supplies $a1 = 1.

The resident set_flag dispatcher splits the id into bank = (id>>8)&0xfffe and index = id&0x1ff, and has a dedicated arm for bank 0x74. The arm is not one of the F0x800155d4 bit-array writers used by banks 0x00-0x40.

Body of the bank-0x74 arm: it calls through the fieldstg-owned function pointer at 0x8009b6a4 with the id's low bits as the only argument, discarding the written value. Existing decoded research (docs/research/field/fishing-system-decoded-2026-07-11.md L404-L413) identifies [0x8009b6a4] as F0x800927a0, which starts the current stage's rate-0 scripted encounter record of that index.

Stage init of wstag927 materialises the encounter-descriptor pointer with the usual two-instruction lui/addiu pair: lui 0x800a at file offset 0x418 followed by addiu 0x68e0 here, giving P = 0x800a68e0. The overlay loads at 0x800a5de0, so P lies at file offset 0x2b00 inside this overlay's own extent.

P is stored into the resident field scene struct at +0x20 ($a2 = 0x800a0000-0x6280 = 0x80099d80, formed at file offset 0x3a4/0x3a8). This is the same descriptor slot tools/extract_forced_encounters.py reads (SCENE_FIELD = 0x20).

P+0x18 = 0x800a68f8 holds 0x800a68bc, the scripted (rate-0) encounter block B for s927. The word at B itself (file offset 0xadc) is zero, which is the rate marker that keeps the random-encounter driver out of this block.
Slot 0 pointer of that block: B + 4 + 4*0 = 0x800a68c0 holds 0x800a685c, the address of the slot-0 battle record. This is the slot that set_flag(0x7400, 1) selects, because the bank-0x74 index is 0.

First word of the slot-0 battle record: screen id 0x106 = 262. The following two words are param 0x2f and music tag 0x60940000. This is the concrete battle-trigger record the prior canonical doc reported as not found (empty battle_candidates).

Third word of the same record: music tag 0x60940000. The generated battle_music.json independently lists s927[0] as {bank boss03, param 47, screen_id 262, tag 0x60940000}, which matches this record word for word.
s233 (Amaterasu City - Digimon Arena) stage init forms its encounter descriptor P = 0x800a6478 (lui 0x800a at 0x364, addiu 0x6478 here).
Delay-slot store of P into scene struct +0x20 ($s1 = 0x80099d80, formed at file offset 0x2f8/0x300). The store executes because the branch at 0x37c is a jalr whose delay slot this is.
P+0x18 for s233 holds 0x800a6454, the rate-0 scripted encounter block. Its own leading word (file offset 0x674) is zero. The eight slot pointers follow at file offsets 0x678-0x694.
Slot 0 record of the s233 scripted block: screen id 0x102 = 258, param 0x14, music 0x600c0000. Slots 1-3 follow at 0x620/0x62c/0x638 with screen ids 0x103, 0x104, 0x105 and the same param and music.

Slot 4 record of the s233 scripted block: screen id 0x106 = 262. That is the same opponent screen id as the wstag927 slot-0 record, i.e. the arena ladder's last round and the scripted Kurt fight name the same battle id.
Music tag of the s233 slot-4 record: 0x608c0000, distinct from the 0x600c0000 carried by slots 0-3.
Slot 5 record of the s233 scripted block reads screen id 0; slots 6 and 7 at file offsets 0x65c and 0x668 also read 0. This is how the enumeration of the block was closed at five populated rounds.
s232 (Asuka City - Digimon Arena) stage init forms P = 0x800a647c and stores it to scene+0x20 in the following delay slot at file offset 0x380.
P+0x18 for s232 holds 0x800a6458, the rate-0 scripted block; its leading word at file offset 0x678 is zero and its eight slot pointers follow at 0x67c-0x698.
Slot 0 record of the s232 scripted block: screen id 0xfd = 253, param 0x14, music 0x600c0000. Slots 1-3 at 0x624/0x630/0x63c hold 0xfe, 0xff, 0x100 with the same param and music.
Slot 4 record of the s232 scripted block: screen id 0x101 = 257, followed at 0x650 by music tag 0x608c0000. Slots 5-7 at 0x654/0x660/0x66c read screen id 0.

wstag420 (Seiryu Leader stage) native hook: set_flag(0x8009, 1). Bank 0x80 is the per-id collection array over D0x80048d34, so this is the grant of item index 9 = Seiryu Badge. The call target is lw 0xc($s0) with $s0 = 0x80048abc, i.e. 0x80048ac8 = set_flag.

Immediately after the badge grant the same hook writes the master story-progress ordinal directly: 0x80050000-0x4c90 = 0x8004b370, with the value 5 loaded at file offset 0x184. Bank 0x60 get_flag(0x60NN) is equality against this word.

wstag520 native hook: set_flag(0x800a, 1) = grant of item index 10 = Suzaku Badge, through 0x80050000-0x7538 = 0x80048ac8. The same hook then writes 0x0b to the story ordinal at 0x8004b370 (file offsets 0x160/0x164).

wstag655 (West Sector - Mirage Room, the Byakko Leader stage) native hook: it first writes 0x11 to the story ordinal at 0x8004b370 (file offsets 0x144/0x148), then calls set_flag(0x800b, 1) = grant of item index 11 = Byakko Badge.
wstag755 native hook: it writes 0x1f to the story ordinal at 0x8004b370 (file offsets 0x138/0x140), then calls set_flag(0x800c, 1) = grant of item index 12 = Genbu Badge.

Item-name table. The file opens with 'strings = [' on L1 and an empty index 0 on L2, so L11 is index 9 and L12-L14 are indices 10, 11 and 12: Suzaku Badge, Byakko Badge, Genbu Badge. These indices are the flag ids 0x8009-0x800c used by the four leader hooks.

Arena Reception registration line used on the Asuka arena front desk: it states the entry condition to the player as the four City Badges won from the City Leaders. Nothing in this file is a predicate; it is the player-facing statement of the requirement.
The receptionist line played by the s926 event (flag_key 01580003) that sends the player into the arena: it names four defeated leaders and directs the player to the Arena.
Opening line of the finale opponent in the arena event that wstag927 queues as entry 0x648: the opponent is Kurt.

Generated per-stage interaction table for s231 (Amaterasu City - Arena Front Desk). The Arena Reception actor (npc 32, sprite p157opft) has a state gated on progress-ordinal equality 0x6026 together with stored flag 0x1a0a=1. No badge-item predicate (0x8009-0x800c) appears in any row of this stage.

The generated table reports the s232 Asuka Digimon Arena encounter slots. It labels this block 'Zone 1'; reading wstag232 directly (AR-EV-23..26) shows the block is the rate-0 scripted block reached at scene+0x20 then +0x18, not a random-encounter zone, so the label is a naming artefact of the extractor. The slot values agree exactly.
Same for s233 Amaterasu Digimon Arena: an independent extraction agreeing slot for slot with the block read directly out of wstag233 in AR-EV-18..22.

Generated walker data only, recorded at authority 6 and used as a navigation lead, not as proof: screen 262 (the arena finale battle id) lists Datamon L90, Bulbmon L95 and Armageddemon L99. The backing table 0x80094680+screen*0x1c lies past the end of the fieldstg disassembly (fieldstg.s is 16477 lines, max file offset about 0x101b4, the record needs 0x12b68), so it could not be re-read from original assembly in this pass.
It scores each of the six opposing field slots by calling the duel's installed board evaluator at +0x820 with side 1 and a single-slot bitmask.
The highest-scoring slot index is written to the selection cursor duel+0x440.
The gate SKIPS its whole scan unless duel+0x444 is below 6, so a counter at or above 6 returns permission without any check.
Permission is refused only on encountering an entry already flagged at +0x446.
The counter selected is per side (stride 0xC8) and per card category, giving a five-entry per-side array.
The counter is incremented by one and capped at 99.
The new value is pushed to the view through method +0xEA0 with the side and the category, i.e. the on-screen energy figure updates.
Scope code 1 selects view slot base 6 - the opposing side's six field slots.
Scope code 2 selects view slot base 0xC - the played-card row above the two fields.
The summon affordability gate is handed duel+0x5A8 as its energy argument, which identifies the array F0x8008D854 increments (0x59C + 0xC = 0x5A8) as the S-Energy pool.
The forward scan is bounded by duel+0x41B, the per-set availability count, so it only considers cards inside the set's usable window.
The first entry found carrying the combo-run flag becomes the cursor.
Whichever entry the cursor ends on is marked as a legal target.
It reads each candidate card record's +0x08 field.
It keeps the strict MINIMUM of that field, starting from a sentinel of 400.
The winning index is written to the selection cursor duel+0x440.
The slot is addressed as duel + side*0x72 + slot*0xE, the established field slot geometry.
The destination is chosen by a byte inside the slot record, at slot+0x0A.
When that byte is zero the card goes to the side's DISCARD pile at duel+0x614, indexed by the pile count at +0x5A2.
When it is one the card goes instead to a SECOND, separate pile at duel+0x6DC with its own count at +0x66A.
The first call starts a view animation on the given card slot.
Later calls report completion only when the view slot's own progress field has caught up to the step.
Moving the field cursor plays sound id 0x4001B.
The cursor duel+0x43C is moved by the caller's signed delta, so one helper serves both directions.
The zero branch appends the card to the array at duel+0x600 indexed by the count at +0x5A6.
The one branch appends it to duel+0x6C8 indexed by +0x66E; 0x6C8 - 0x600 and 0x66E - 0x5A6 are both exactly 0xC8, the per-player stride, so these are the SAME array for the two sides.
The branch value is passed to the view as its SIDE argument, in the same position F0x8008D854 passes the side.
A three-index lookup into the table at 0x800A5844 with a bank chosen by the global at 0x8005CCB0.
Rightward movement is clamped by a count taken from the caller's second object at its +0x0A field.
Cancel requests a distinct teardown step from the one confirm requests.
The sibling clamps against a count held in the duel itself at +0x434 instead.
Confirm is accepted only when the entry under the cursor carries the +0x446 flag, and it requests that screen's own next step.
The constructor allocates a 0x74-byte widget through the resident allocator and installs F0x80095FB4 as its per-frame handler.
It initialises a mode byte at widget+0x63 to zero.
The draw call takes its sprite from bank 0x025D0002 at frame base 0x47, positioned from the widget's own x/y at +0x54 and +0x56.
Its animation phase at +0x50 advances by the resident frame delta each call, so it is time-driven rather than event-driven.
In mode 1 the frame index is a one-shot ramp CLAMPED at 7, as against mode 0's wrapping cycle.
A per-index horizontal offset is taken from the halfword table at 0x800A59A8, so this element is laid out in a row.
A second, non-animating helper draws frame 0x18 from the same 0x025D0002 bank at a caller-supplied position.
A second widget draw from the same 0x025D0002 bank, at frame base 0x45 instead of 0x47, positioned from its own x/y pair.
Its two elements are stacked with a fixed vertical pitch of 13 pixels.
The label is CENTRED: its x is 160 minus half the measured text width, i.e. the horizontal centre of a 320-wide screen.
One particular value, 0x1F, is drawn in a different palette from every other value.
The texture page is placed at VRAM x = 0x140 + (index/8)*0x10 and y = 0x100 + (index%8)*0x20, so cards are stacked eight to a column.
Each card index gets its OWN palette one line apart, at VRAM x = 0x300 and y = 0x100 + index.
It snapshots the element's CURRENT position into a second pair of fields before setting the target, which is the shape of a tween start.
One card-back style is drawn from bank 0x025D0002 at frame 0x33 plus a per-object variant byte.
A sibling draws a fixed frame 0x0A from a DIFFERENT bank, 0x025D0003, gated on a different byte of the same object.
A third helper draws frame 1 of bank 0x025D0003 with a caller-supplied horizontal scale.
A halfword table read at 0x800A5B14.
A constructor for a 0x78-byte object on allocator group 4 with per-frame handler 0x800A35BC.
A remaining-time field is decremented by the resident frame delta each call, so the motion is time-based.
On expiry it snaps to the endpoint and raises a done flag rather than overshooting.
Fifteen consecutive per-slot bytes are set to show only when the request equals 2, i.e. one broadcast show-or-hide.
The announcement to spawn is looked up as a FOUR-BYTE record in the table at 0x800A5D14, indexed by a request code minus one.
The animation's item count is taken from one of the per-side pile counters, selected by the caller's code.
Its DURATION is computed from that count as count*4 + 10, so a bigger pile takes proportionally longer on screen.
A one-shot guard ensures the entry work happens on the first call only, with the same call repeating as a poll thereafter.
SIX consecutive counters are cleared, one per card category.
Each folder entry's card category, taken as the accessor's first byte minus one, selects which counter to increment.
The tally runs over exactly 40 entries - one whole card folder.
The tally lives in a 0x74-byte widget allocated on group 0x1C with F0x80096418 as its per-frame handler.
Up to three icons are drawn from consecutive frames starting at 0x37, stepped eight pixels apart horizontally.
A second tween channel snapshots its own current pair before setting a new target, independent of the position channel.
The textured quad's source window is 0x20 by 0x20, giving the card image's texel size.
The texture page base is (0x140, 0x100), the same origin F0x8009D0B0 computes from.
The palette base is (0x300, 0x100), matching the per-card palette line F0x8009D0B0 sets.
A script step is a four-byte record read from the table at 0x800A5BF0.
A step value of -2 is a SKIP marker: the player jumps an extra step and raises a flag.
A step value of -1 TERMINATES the sequence.
The sort's key is the availability-group byte at +0x30A, the field the opponent loader fills from CARD_NPC deck entry byte +0x02.
The primitive's draw mode word takes its BLEND MODE from the low two bits of a field on the object, so the overlay's transparency style is selectable.
Each colour channel is interpolated from its start toward its end value by elapsed time over total duration.
Exactly THREE channels are stepped - red, green and blue.
On expiry a hold flag chooses between staying at the end colour and releasing.
The fuller pile-animation setup takes an extra branch when the pile is not empty.
Each drawn card increments the HAND count at +0x5A6.
The same draw decrements the DECK remaining count at +0x5A4, which distinguishes the two counters unambiguously.
The inner loop draws exactly six cards.
The outer loop runs it for both sides.
The announcement only becomes skippable after a minimum time has elapsed.
Pressing confirm then jumps the timer straight to its end value instead of cancelling the step.
The drain's FLOOR is the OPPOSING side's stored post-battle total at +0x59E, shifted left 8 for sub-unit precision.
The running value is pushed to the view against the OPPOSING side under category 9 each tick.
The acting side's own figure animates separately under category 8.
The rebuild walks exactly six field slots for the side it is given.
Each view card slot is re-pointed at the card the duel's slot record actually holds.
It then rebuilds the played-card stack rows on top of the field rows.
The grow phase drives a scale from 0 up to the unit value 0x1000 as its timer runs down.
A sibling runs the identical grow expression on a different field of a differently shaped object.
A third sibling does the same again, confirming this as one shared scale-tween idiom rather than three unrelated routines.
One side's banner uses one hard-coded set of start and end coordinates.
The other side uses a completely different set, so the two players' banners fly in from opposite places.
Voice-flag receiver: *D0x800815a0[bank] + slot*0xB0 (same shape in 32d5c/3028c/2fbe8/2f59c).
Bit setters: arg2==1 sets bit 0, arg2==0 sets bit 1 (with 0x200/4 clears).
Note-end path sets bit 9 together with the re-seize request bit 2.
SEQ parser gates stream-event mode on bit 10 (with bit 0): alternate-sample select consumer.
Positional alloc tags the 16-bit owner halfword with constant 0x21.
The driver itself treats 0x21 as reserved, skipping pitch-field writes for it.
Sound init configures exactly 6 banks x 16 slots (sole writer of the bank/slot counts).

evidence.summary: The exclusive-track gate itself: if bit 30 ($s2) is clear, skip straight to the path-selection block at 0x8002012c without touching the dedup latch at all.

If the latch already equals the new packed id, branch to the function's shared return with $v0 forced to 0 (delay slot move_ $v0,$zr) - the sound is already the recorded exclusive track and is not retriggered.
When bit 30 is set, reads a single global latch at D0x800519ec+0x4248 (not indexed by channel - the base pointer used here has no per-channel offset added) holding the previously-recorded packed id.
Records the new packed id into the D0x800519ec+0x4248 latch, then falls through into the path-selection block at 0x8002012c to actually trigger playback.

If the latch instead held a different, non-zero previous id, loads a function pointer from D0x800519ec+0x427c and calls it (jalr at the following instruction) with the old id as its argument, before overwriting the latch.
Masks the shifted value to 7 bits, completing bits 18-24 (archive id) as F0x80020030's sole argument.
F0x8002006c shifts the packed arg0 right by 0x12 (18) into $a0, the first step of extracting bits 18-24 (archive id) for the F0x80020030 call.
Masks to 1 bit, giving $s2 = bit 30 of arg0, the flag tested by the exclusive-track gate at 0x800200f4.
Arithmetic shift right by 0x1e (30) prepares to isolate bit 30 of arg0 (the dedup/exclusive-track flag).
Logical (unsigned) shift right by 0x1f isolates bit 31 of arg0 into $s7, later used as the positional-vs-sampled path selector at 0x8002012c.
Masks arg0 directly (no shift) to 7 bits into $t0 = bits 0-6, later spilled to the stack and used as F0x8003432c's 4th argument (the note number) on the positional path.
Masks arg0 (no shift) to 8 bits into $s8 = bits 0-7, used only on the sampled path as the voice/tone slot passed to F0x800335b4/F0x80033b64/F0x80032d1c.
Masks to 7 bits: $s6 = bits 11-17 of arg0, used only on the positional (bit-31-set) path as F0x8003432c's 2nd argument.
Shift right by 0xb (11) begins extracting bits 11-17 of arg0.
Masks to 4 bits: $s5 = bits 7-10 of arg0, used only on the positional path as F0x8003432c's 3rd argument.
Shift right by 7 begins extracting bits 7-10 of arg0.
Masks to 8 bits: $s4 = bits 8-15 of arg0, used only on the sampled (bit-31-clear) path, doubled into a byte offset that selects the channel record's 'row' sub-entry.
Shift right by 8 begins extracting bits 8-15 of arg0.
Caps the scanned array to exactly 3 channel records (slti against 0x3) before giving up.
F0x80020030's loop body reads a 32-bit field at offset 0x4200 of the current channel record (base D0x800519ec, then advanced by 0x18 per iteration) and compares it against the requested archive id.

On a match, F0x80020030 jumps to its return with $v0 already holding the matching channel index (0, 1, or 2) - set unconditionally in the branch's delay slot, so the found index is returned, not a boolean.
Loop continuation: if the channel index (v1, capped by the slti test at 0x80020050 against 3) is still below 3, branch back to re-test the next channel record's +0x4200 field.
If none of the 3 channel records match, F0x80020030 returns -1 (the value the caller F0x8002006c later tests against $s3 to take its own no-op early return).
F0x8002006c calls the bank/channel lookup F0x80020030 with the archive id (bits 18-24) as its only argument, before any of the exclusive-track or path-selection logic.
Bit 31 ($s7) selects the playback path: clear branches to the sampled (2D/flat-slot) block at 0x80020178; set falls through into the positional/sequenced block.
Entry of the sampled (bit-31-clear) branch, reached only via the beqz at 0x8002012c.
Sampled path calls F0x800335b4(rowField, bits0-7) - starts playback of the flat voice/tone slot (bits 0-7) at that row's registered bank.
Sampled path's third call, F0x80032d1c(rowField, bits0-7, 1, 1) - the priority setter closing out the sampled path before falling into the shared epilogue.

$s3, the function's eventual return value, is set to -1 once at function entry and is never written again anywhere in the sampled (2D) branch (0x80020178-0x800201cc) - only the positional branch's 0x80020174 reassigns it. The sampled path therefore always returns -1, regardless of what F0x800335b4/33b64/32d1c report.

Sampled path reads the channel record's +0x4208 field (indexed additionally by bits 8-15, doubled) into $a0, the first argument to F0x800335b4/F0x80033b64/F0x80032d1c - a bank/row selector, not the tone slot itself.

Calls F0x8003432c(vabSlot, bits11-17, bits7-10, bits0-6, 0, 0x7f, 0x7f) - the positional/sequenced play routine, given the VAB slot plus three fields decoded from the packed id (row/program, tone, note).
Positional/sequenced path: reads the matched channel record's +0x4204 field (the channel's currently-registered VAB slot) into $a0, F0x8003432c's first argument.
Only the positional/sequenced branch overwrites $s3 (the function's eventual return value) with F0x8003432c's sign-extended 16-bit result, then jumps to the shared epilogue.
Both playback branches converge here: $v0 = $s3 (either the sampled path's constant -1, or the positional path's F0x8003432c result), then falls into the register-restore epilogue.

In the tech-confirm/commit handler that contains the previously-documented cost-and-debit sequence (research doc digivolution-tech-system-decoded-2026-07-11.md L244 caller 0x80096dac), the code reads the acting combatant record byte +0x1a via `lbu $v0, 0x1a($s0)` at 0x80096d78 (record base $s0 = 0x800a4460+0x10+idx*0x20, the same +0x1a Blast-active flag established by DNA-C008/DNA-Q001-E19/E20). `bnez $v0, .L0x80096be0` at 0x80096d80 branches away when Blast-active. The fallthrough (Blast-inactive) path calls the cost vtable at 0x800a466c (0x80096db0-0x80096dbc), loads cur_mp twice (0x80096dc8/dcc), does the sufficiency test `slt`+`bnez ... .L0x80096e44` (0x80096dd0-dd4), subtracts the cost (0x80096dd8 `subu $v0, $a0`), and stores the debited MP back with `sh $v0, 0xc($s0)` at 0x80096de0, falling into the tech-use continuation at 0x80096de4.

The Blast-active branch target of BLQ2-E01 (0x80096d80 bnez) is an unconditional jump straight to 0x80096de4, the instruction immediately AFTER the MP debit store at 0x80096de0. This skips the entire cost-lookup call, the MP-sufficiency comparison, and the debit store itself (all three, not merely the sufficiency test) and proceeds directly into the tech-use continuation with cur_mp untouched. This is the execution-time MP-subtraction site gated by combatant +0x1a required by BLAST-Q002: while Blast-active, using a technique charges zero MP because the debit instruction is never reached.

The specific MP-debit store instruction skipped by the +0x1a branch identified in BLQ2-E01/BLQ2-E02: `sh $v0, 0xc($s0)` writes the post-subtraction cur_mp (record +0xc) back to the acting combatant record. This is the exact write BLAST-C011's execution-time MP-debit clause refers to.

evidence.summary: The footprint tool that produced the census: per-function step byte, duel fields written, view slots driven, with explicit receiver attribution.
The routine anchors a table at 0x800A5DA8 before walking the field, and writes pairs into it as it goes.
Per iteration it forms a pointer into the field-slot flag array at duel+0x46F.
For each flagged slot that is swapped with a later empty one, the source index is written into the first byte of a table entry, with the destination in the second - a move list, not a board mutation.
The card-record selector takes a 1-based id, subtracts one, chooses the resource file with (id-1) >> 6 and offsets into it by ((id-1) & 0x3F) * 0x62C, i.e. 64 records of 1580 bytes per file.
F0x8001EBF8 is a constructor: it installs ten method pointers into the object it is handed, at +0x2C..+0x50, with +0x2C = F0x8001E7EC.
cardgame constructs the object on its own STACK (&sp10, i.e. $sp+0x10) and then calls it through sp3C, which is $sp+0x3C = object+0x2C.
The AI policy function uses the identical stack-cursor pattern: construct at &sp10, select a card with sp3C(cardId + 1), then read the record's fields back out of sp10.

The extracted catalog uses stride 1580 and holds 316 cards, which is exactly 4 files of 64 records plus one of 60 - the split the >> 6 / & 0x3F arithmetic implies. CARDPAK0..3 are 101120 bytes (64*1580) and CARDPAK4 is 94800 (60*1580).
The comparator loads the RAW CLASS BYTE +0x35C of both compared elements.
It also loads the composite weight halfword +0x35E of both elements - this is the reader of +0x35E that was previously missing.
The PRIMARY comparison is on the class bytes: swap when the second element's class is less than the first's.
Only when the two class bytes are equal does it fall through to the two-operand slt on the +0x35E weights, so +0x35E is the TIE-BREAK, not the primary key.
On a positive comparison it exchanges the two halfword entries of the array at +0x6C8, i.e. this is an in-place exchange sort over that array.
The per-player block address is formed as duel + side*0xC8 (s0*2+s0 = 3, <<3 = 24, +s0 = 25, <<3 = 200 = 0xC8), confirming the 0xC8 two-player stride.
The set counter at +0x5AE of that per-player block is loaded, incremented by one and stored back - this is the increment site the best-of-three claim asserted without citation.
Battle-Phase jump-table entry [0x0B] targets 0x800A12F8.
Entry [0x0C] targets 0x800A151C, so arm 0x0B spans 0x800A12F8..0x800A151C and therefore CONTAINS the increment at 0x800A1484 - the increment is in state 0x0B.
The duel-won path builds its sound argument in the branch delay slot as 0x6004001e and passes it to the resident sound entry loaded from 0x80055C48.
The function containing the group-equality selector begins here; its entry address is 0x800907AC, NOT the 0x80090838 previously recorded.
Its first act is a three-way dispatch on the step byte duel+0x422.
The group-equality selector is reached only on the duel+0x422 == 2 branch; the == 1 branch goes elsewhere and anything else returns without selecting.
The shipped data contains exactly one deck entry whose AI class byte is 0, a value outside the 1..7 domain the loader's range check admits.
The recompute walks a side's field slots with a 0xE stride, accumulating the halfword at slot+0x08 as that slot's AP contribution.
The freshly summed totals are compared against the four stored totals duel+0x59C, +0x59E, +0x664 and +0x666; 0x664 and 0x666 are 0x59C and 0x59E plus the 0xC8 per-player stride.
At the end of its fifteen-frame ramp the handler exchanges the two sides' stored AP totals.
A positioned effect reads an eight-byte-per-entry coordinate table at 0x800A5900 indexed by its argument.
Handlers begin by reading the step byte duel+0x422 and switching on it, which is the per-opcode step protocol.
The S-Energy handler maps several opcodes onto the same colour index; opcodes 0x20 and 0x21 both yield colour 2.
For opcodes below 0x24 the affected side is the current play-history entry's +0x584.
For opcodes 0x24..0x28 the side is that value XOR 1, i.e. the opponent's S-Energy pool.
The slot iterator advances only on a non-zero duel+0x46F entry, scanning indices 0..0x0B, i.e. all twelve field slots across both sides.
The human's confirm button is accepted only when duel+0x438 equals 1, so that word is a selection-validity gate rather than shared scratch.
The animated counter accumulates the resident frame delta into duel+0x424 each frame rather than completing instantly.
A SECOND handler, independent of F0x8008CFDC, gates the confirm button on duel+0x438 being non-zero.
On a successful confirm the handler plays sound id 0x4001C through the resident slot at 0x80055C48.
The cancel path plays a different sound id, 0x800450BD, through the same resident slot.

The discard handler appends a card id to the trash pile at block+0x614 indexed by the trash count at block+0x5A2, with the block reached as side * 0xC8 - a third independent witness to the per-player block stride and trash layout.
The function is a TWO-LEVEL step machine: the first switch is on the pending step byte duel+0x423.

Every transition arm converges on a block that consumes the pending step: it copies duel+0x423 into the current step duel+0x422 and clears +0x423, so +0x423 is a one-shot request and +0x422 is what the per-frame poll switch reads.
On entry the screen SAVES two view bytes, view+0xB0 and view+0x104, into the global word at 0x800A5DA0 and then zeroes them.
The final step 15 RESTORES view+0xB0 from that same global and sets the flag that makes the function return 1, i.e. finished.
Row 0's poll gates its up-move on the side-0 field slot count duel+0x72C.
Leaving row 0 clears the highlight bit of the view card slot at index duel+0x43C, i.e. row 0 occupies view slot indices 0..5.
Leaving row 2 clears the view card slot at duel+0x43C + 0xC, so the third row occupies view slot indices 0xC upward - past the twelve field slots.
Leaving row 1 clears the view card slot at duel+0x43C + 6, so row 1 is the opposing side's six field slots at view indices 6..0xB.
Moving from a six-wide field row to the third row HALVES the cursor, and returning DOUBLES it and adds one, so the third row has half as many entries as a field row.
Cancel, pad bit 0x0E, plays the already-decoded selection-cancelled sound 0x800450BD and requests the teardown step 0x0B.
Mode 3 issues effect opcode 0xA7 by writing the pending-opcode latch duel+0x421.
Mode 9 calls the duel's +0x810 method - the RNG pile shuffle - passing the pile header's +0x04 and +0x08 as base and count.
Mode 9 zeroes the stored AP and HP totals for both sides.
Mode 9 increments the set counter duel+0x300, and the next call recomputes the per-set availability window.
On the accepted confirm, the handler switches on duel+0x438 against composite values, not against a boolean; 0x1400 is tested first.
Mask value 0x1000 resolves the selection's size from duel+0x5A4, side 0's deck count.
Mask value 0x2000 resolves from duel+0x66C, which is 0x5A4 + 0xC8, i.e. side 1's deck count.
Mask value 0x8000 resolves from duel+0x66E, which is 0x5A6 + 0xC8, i.e. side 1's hand count.
A fourth independent function forms the per-player block as side * 0xC8 + 0x59C and then reaches the deck array at block+0x14 and the trash array at block+0x78.
F0x8009D6E0 loads disc resource 0x7A4 (LBA index 1956 = dw2003/AAA/DAT/CARD/CARD_NPC.BIN) and stores the returned pointer to duel+0x2F0.
The record index arithmetic reduces to 0xD0*(opponentId-1): the final term subtracts one stride, so opponent ids are 1-based and the stride is 0xD0.
Per deck entry i the loader stores the loop counter to duel+0x30A+2i, so the first byte of each (index, group) pair is the deck slot index.
Record byte +0x02 of deck entry i is copied to duel+0x30B+2i, the second byte of the pair array.
Record byte +0x03 of deck entry i is copied to duel+0x35C+4i.
duel+0x35C is range-checked as (value-1) unsigned-less-than 7 before indexing the 7-entry jump table at 0x800837A0, so the field's legal domain is 1..7.
Each jump-table case computes $a1 (the deck index) plus a per-class immediate and stores the halfword to duel+0x35E+4i, making the class the primary sort weight and the deck position the tie-break.
The final loop masks each entry's u16 with 0x0FFF, subtracts one, and writes the halfword to duel+0x248+2i: the opponent's 40-card deck pile holds zero-based card ids.
Record byte +0xC8 is read as a u8 and stored to duel+0x2E9.
Record word +0xCC indexes the halfword table at 0x800A5C2C (sll 1, lh) and the result is stored to duel+0x2EC.
In the greedy summon pass the class byte at duel+0x35C+4*(slot-0x28) is compared against 5 and the card is skipped on equality.
The literal the summon pass compares the class byte against is 5.
F0x8009D9E4 forms the availability threshold as 2*duel[0x300]+2 before walking the group-ordered pile.
F0x8009D9E4 stores the number of entries whose group does not exceed the threshold to duel+0x41B.
F0x8009D9E4 stores the index of the first group-7 entry to duel+0x41C, so group 7 is reached outside the per-set window.
The selector at 0x80090838 admits a pile entry only when its group byte equals 2*duel[0x300]+2 exactly.
duel+0x300 is the value the availability threshold is derived from; it is zeroed at duel start and incremented once per set, with F0x8009D9E4 re-run after each change.
The committed extractor parses all 170 records, verifies the source sha256, and reproduces the loader's derived fields (zero-based deck pile, class sort key, per-set availability).
The prompt waits 0x24 accumulated frame units before it opens, using the shared frame accumulator duel+0x424.
Moving the cursor plays sound id 0x8004513E through the resident slot at 0x80055C48.
The cursor duel+0x440 is TOGGLED with an exclusive-or against 1, so this prompt has exactly two options.
F0x8009F04C forms the resident pointer base 0x80050000-0x23FC = 0x8004DC04 and calls through +8, i.e. 0x8004DC0C = RAND_U16.
The load of the RAND_U16 function pointer is register-constructed from the base, which is why a literal text search for the address returns zero hits in the original assembly.
First RAND_U16 call of the shuffle iteration.
The first random word is reduced modulo the count argument (remainder taken from hi).
Second RAND_U16 call of the same iteration, giving the other swap index.
The two selected halfwords of the pile at duel+0x59C+0x14 = duel+0x5B0 are exchanged.
The shuffle loop runs a fixed 40 iterations (slti against 0x28).
The duel factory installs 0x800A0000-0xFB4 = 0x8009F04C into the method slot duel+0x810.
The duel initialiser reaches the shuffle only through the method pointer at duel+0x810, with base and count taken from the pile header at duel+0x5A0 and duel+0x5A4.
A second dispatch site loads the same duel+0x810 method pointer during the turn loop.

Committed call-graph tool. `imports` over pro/cardgame.s reports 0x8004DC0C as called by exactly one function, F0x8009F04C; `closure 0x800a4978 0x8009d8fc` reports 20 reachable overlay functions and exactly one reachable resident import, 0x8001EBF8.

evidence.summary: The only routine that CHANGES a field slot's stat does so by plus or minus ONE per frame, ramping toward a queued target - it never assigns a value outright.
The only other writer COPIES one slot's stats to another slot, which is the compaction that happens when cards shift along the field.
The battle roll only READS the health field, testing it against zero.
Stat changes reach the ramp only through explicit stat-change opcodes carrying a packed immediate amount.
The run detector FLAGS each field slot of a qualifying run at slot+0x446; it does not alter the slot's stats.
It stores the run card's combo-target card id into duel+0x438 and returns; no field-slot stat write follows in this function.
The combo presentation searches the duel's card-instance table for an instance whose card id equals the combo target minus one.
When no instance of the combo target is found it substitutes a fixed fallback and overwrites duel+0x438 with card id 0x13B.
The resolved instance is handed to view sprite slot 0x11, i.e. the combo target's card art is DISPLAYED.
The combo picker dims every field slot that is NOT part of a run, so the player can only confirm on a qualifying run.
The played-card stack is popped by one as each entry resolves.
When a response flag is set it pops TWO entries instead of one - a played card and the card answered against it resolving together.
The popped entry's card reference is appended to that side's discard pile, whose count then increments.
The seed value for every card is read from a per-card-id byte array in the save at 0x80048D34 + 0x3A2 - the player's OWNED count.
That array has 0x13B = 315 entries, one per card id, matching the card catalog's size.
The second pass walks the CURRENT FOLDER, whose base 0x80049372 is exactly 0x80048D34 + 0x63E, the folder entry array, at the established 0x66 stride per folder.
For each card already in the folder it DECREMENTS that card's running count.
The subtraction runs over all 40 folder entries.

F0x8003e11c has its own section and global symbol opening at L50233-50235, and its first instruction `addiu $sp, -0x18` at L50236 establishes a genuine callable entry with a stack frame, not data or padding.

The return value is the pre-consumption combined value shifted down one bit by `sra $v0, $s0, 0x1`, so a caller receives the raw combined code (1, 2, 4, 6, 8) divided by two; this is the only sra or srl in the L50600-51045 caller region, so the conversion happens inside the waiter.

F0x800980e4 is a submenu task handler. ctx (register $s1) field +0xc is the lifecycle phase (1 = already built; 2/3 = build the partner form list; >=4 exits). Field +0x10 is the submenu page: 0 -> handler at 0x800981f0, 1 -> handler at 0x80098314. The build block at 0x80098128-0x800981c0 fills ctx+0x68[] with the base profile id of roster member ctx+0x60 (profile table 0x8003ef5c, stride 0x58) followed by each of ctx+0x74[0..2] whose value is >= 3, and stores the resulting entry count to ctx+0x70 and to 0x800a3594.

Within page ctx+0x10 == 1, ctx+0x14 is the substate: 0 -> offer/pane build at 0x8009832c, 1 -> the confirm/cancel input block at 0x800984dc. Register $s4 holds ctx+0x14 (= 1 on entry to 0x800984dc) and is the value later stored as the pane 'committed' marker.

Offer-suppression gate. The active combatant record is 0x800a4470 + [0x800a4468]*0x20 (the code forms it as 0x800a4460 + idx*0x20 and therefore uses +0x10-shifted field offsets). It reads record byte +0x1a as `lbu $v0, 0x2a($v1)`; if non-zero it branches straight to 0x800983c0 with the pane entry count preset to 1, skipping the entire DNA pairing recomputation, so ctx+0x7c is NOT refreshed for the transformed form.

DNA pairing predicate. `lh $a0, 0x10($v1)` reads the active combatant record's +0x00 species/profile id and resolves it through the resident profile-lookup hook D0x8005cca0 into $s0. The selected form id is ctx+0x68[ctx+0x64] and is resolved through the same hook into $v0. If source profile byte +0x3d == 0 the code writes ctx+0x7c = 0; else if source +0x3d != partner-form profile byte +0x55 it writes ctx+0x7c = 0; else ctx+0x7c = source profile halfword +0x2a (tech_dna_dv).

Pane sizing. If ctx+0x7c == 0 the entry count written to the pane descriptor field 0x800a35b4 (= 0x800a3594 + 0x20) is 1; if non-zero it is 2. The pane object created by F0x8009b0c8 is stored at menu-stack +0x4. The DNA DV row therefore exists only when the pairing predicate produced a tech id.

Input dispatch of the DNA/Tag pane. The pad word is fetched through the resident hook D0x8004bbc4(0). Mask 0x2000 selects the confirm path (fall-through at 0x800984fc); otherwise mask 0x4000 selects cancel at 0x800984a0; otherwise mask 0x800 / mask 0x400 cycle the page; otherwise the idle path at 0x80098770 runs.

Confirm-path setup, executed BEFORE any eligibility test. $s0 = combatant record 0x800a4470 + [0x800a4468]*0x20 (the acting Digimon); $s2 = combatant record 0x800a4470 + ctx+0x5c*0x20 (the selected partner). At 0x80098530 the resident UI-feedback hook D0x80055c48 is invoked with the same constant (0x0004001c) used on successful confirms elsewhere in this function, so the confirm feedback fires unconditionally, ahead of every rejection test.

Row selector and the no-cost (first pane row) branch. `lw $v0, 0x4($s3); lw $v0, 0x50($v0)` reads the pane object's cursor index. If it is 0 (first row, the plain partner-switch commit) execution takes the branch at 0x80098550, which performs only two tests: reject to 0x80098790 if acting-record byte +0x1c & 0x10 (0x80098558), and reject if partner-record byte +0x1c & 0x10 (0x8009856c). No MP test, no HP test, no MP debit. It then writes *(ctx+0x50) = 0, ORs in (ctx+0x68[ctx+0x64] << 4), and joins the common commit tail at 0x800986d4.

DNA DV cost lookup and acting-side MP rejection. 0x800985b4 is the entry of the cost path. The cost record is D0x80042bdc + (ctx+0x7c - 1)*0x12 (Unknown3[443], stride 0x12, array[i] = skill id i+1); the cost is the u16 at record +0x00. `lh $v1, 0xc($s0)` (acting cur_mp, sign-extended) is compared with `slt` against the u16 cost: if cur_mp < cost the branch at 0x800985e4 rejects to 0x80098790. Equality (cur_mp == cost) is accepted; the fall-through instruction is 0x800985ec.

Partner-side MP rejection: `lh $v0, 0xc($s2)` (partner cur_mp) is compared with `slt` against the same cost; if partner cur_mp < cost the branch at 0x800985f8 rejects to 0x80098790. The fall-through instruction is 0x80098600.

Status-bit rejections on the DNA DV row, in exact order: acting-record +0x1c & 0x20 (mask at 0x80098608, branch 0x8009860c, fall-through 0x80098614) -> reject; partner-record +0x1c & 0x20 (mask 0x8009861c, branch 0x80098620, fall-through 0x80098628) -> reject; acting-record +0x1c & 0x08 (mask 0x80098624 sits in the previous branch's delay slot, branch 0x80098628, fall-through 0x80098630) -> reject. The partner is NOT tested for bit 0x08, and neither participant is tested for bit 0x10 on this row (bit 0x10 is tested only on the first pane row).

Liveness rejections: `lh $v0, 0x8($s0)` (acting cur_hp) at 0x80098630 with `blez` at 0x80098638 rejects to 0x80098790, fall-through 0x80098640; `lh $v0, 0x8($s2)` (partner cur_hp) at 0x80098640 with `blez` at 0x80098648 rejects to 0x80098790, fall-through 0x80098650. A dead (HP <= 0) selected partner therefore fails at 0x80098648, after the confirm feedback has already been issued.

Commit tail, reached only when every test above passes; 0x80098650 is the acting-side MP store and is the unique accept marker for the DNA DV row. Acting cur_mp (+0xc) -= cost; the cost is re-read from the same Unknown3 record and partner cur_mp (+0xc) -= the same value, so both participants pay the full cost. Then *(ctx+0x50) = pane cursor index, OR'd with (ctx+0x68[ctx+0x64] << 4); *(ctx+0x80) = ctx+0x7c (the DNA tech id), a store that exists only on the cost path; then ctx+0x2c(ctx, 0) and FIGHTSTG_F0x80097cfc(ctx, menu_stack, 0); finally pane->+0x54 = 1.

Every rejection branch listed in DNA-Q001-E08 through DNA-Q001-E12 targets the single address 0x80098790, which is `jal FIGHTSTG_F0x800979e4(ctx)` followed by the shared frame tail at 0x80098798. No error sound, no message-box call, no state change, and no write to ctx+0x50 or ctx+0x80 occurs on any rejection. Note for runtime work: 0x80098790 is also reached by the accept path, the cancel path, the page-cycle path and the idle path, so it is a convergence point and NOT by itself an accept/reject discriminator.

F0x800979e4 is a pure per-frame renderer for this pane: it acquires a draw context (D0x80044f5c with 0x04550000), builds a primitive helper via F0x8001f648, sets two render modes, always draws one element at (0x2b,0xa7,0x8f), and draws two additional elements at (0x2,0xa7,0xb8) and (0x29,0xa3,0x21) only when ctx+0x7c != 0 (the DNA DV row and its cost display). It reads no status, HP or MP and emits no message.

## 2026-07-11 live rig capture: the `D0x8008b770` theory is FALSIFIED — gym entry uses the battle-style `set_D0x8004b3f8` transition, not the screen-pack launcher

Live capture on a Windows-native PCSX-Redux rig (build 314, `tools/windows-rig/`),
standing at a working training-gym trainer with the "Train which Digimon?" menu
already open (a live Renamon Lv15 party), settled this decisively:

- An `Exec` breakpoint on `D0x8008b770` (armed *before* opening the menu, correct
  address confirmed via disasm — `jal 0x8008b770` at fieldstg file `0x5958`) **never
  fired**, across two independent full field→training entries. The mode-1/`D0x8008b770`
  generic-screen-launcher theory from the earlier 2026-07-11 follow-up is therefore
  **falsified** as the gym's entry path.
- An `Exec` breakpoint on `0x80016b44` (`set_D0x8004b3f8`, the same resident selector
  writer already proven for battle entry in `battle-invocation.md` step 5, call site
  `0x800147c8` = the f12 main-loop `state==0` screen-loader block) **did fire**, exactly
  once, on the same field→training transition: `ra=0x800147c8 a0=0x00000a00`.
  Cross-checked live: `[0x8004b3f8]=0x00000a00`, `[0x80055d28]=0x0000000a` (matches the
  high byte of the selector, exactly like battle's `0x600`→lib `6`), `[0x80055d2c]`
  (data LBA) reads `0xffffffff` (no separate data-overlay LBA set for this transition,
  unlike battle's `WFIGHTMN`/LBA 520 — training apparently doesn't swap the data slot,
  only the engine slot).

**Confirmed:** gym training entry is architecturally the *same class* of transition as
battle entry (`set_D0x8004b3f8`, generic f12 main-loop screen-swap), not the
screen-pack/`D0x8008b770` family used by shops, card trade, and DRI desks. This
directly rules out the mode-1 theory and gives a concrete, verified target: engine
lib `0x0a` for training's engine overlay slot.

**Open discrepancy, not yet resolved:** an earlier live read *in the same session*, at
the same trainer, on the same "Train which Digimon?" screen (before an unrelated rig
crash+relaunch), read `[0x8004b3f8]=0x00001600` / `[0x80055d28]=0x00000016` instead —
i.e. lib `0x16`, not `0x0a`. Both reads are internally self-consistent (`b3f8` high
byte always matches the `lib` register), but the two sessions disagree on the actual
value for what looked like the identical screen. Possible explanations, none yet
checked: (a) the lib id is a rotating/allocated overlay-slot index rather than a fixed
per-screen constant, so it varies by whichever slot happened to be free; (b) the two
sessions were actually at different physical trainer NPCs despite the identical-looking
menu (party/rank state was also HP9999/MP9999 both times, consistent with a
maxed-out debug save, so this can't be ruled out from the screenshot alone); (c) a
savestate/session artifact from the rig crash. This needs one more clean, single
uninterrupted capture (ideally with the greeter's stage id logged via
`[0x80055d2c]` *before* the transition) to resolve.

**Still open for GYM-Q001:** the caller that decides `a0=0x0a00` (i.e. the
"battle-setup/HANDOFF"-style function analogous to `0x8008b798`'s hardcoded `0x600`,
presumably a dedicated STGTRAIN-entry handoff somewhere in `fieldstg.s`) has not been
located, and neither has the rank/params encoding. The `D0x8008b770`/mode-1 dead end
should not be re-chased; the next static step is searching for the literal `0xa00`
(and `0x1600`, pending the discrepancy above) construction near a `+0x5c`/`+0x28(2)`
transition-object pattern like the battle handoff.

## What the screen is (proven)

`stagslct` is the free-roam **gate/area-travel menu**: pick any previously
warpable location in the game and jump there directly, bypassing normal
walking/warp-chain navigation.

Static evidence (no runtime capture needed — the mechanism is unambiguous
from disasm):

1. **A 239-entry destination table** sits in the overlay's own data region
   at RAM `0x80085eec` (file offset `0x323c`). Row-select handler
   (`stagslct.s` L2620-2637, RAM `0x80082ed0`-`0x80082ee0`):

   ```
   lw   v1, 0x54($s3)           ; cursor row
   lw   a0, 0x50($s3)           ; scroll offset
   lui  v0, 0x8008 ; addiu v0, 0x5eec   ; v0 = table base 0x80085eec
   addu v1, a0 ; sll v1, 4 ; addu v1, v0  ; v1 = &table[cursor+scroll]
   lw   a0, 8(v1)                ; a0 = row "type" field
   ...
   lw   v1, 0xc(v1)              ; v1 = row "value" field
   lui  v0, 0x8005
   j    0x800855d4               ; tail-call: resident transition trampoline
   sw   v1, -0x4c90(v0)          ; [0x8004b370] = v1
   ```

   `0x8004b370` is the **master story-progress ordinal**, documented in
   `docs/research/scripting/field-script-engine-verified.md` §WS4.6 (every
   story beat's overlay writes its own value there on completion; a
   35-entry `fieldstg` jump table switches on it). `stagslct` writing a
   **screen id** there and tail-calling the same resident transition
   trampoline (`0x800855d4`) that ordinary story handoffs use is the
   concrete proof this is a "pick a destination, warp there" menu, not a
   debug/data screen.

2. **The table enumerates literally every warpable screen in the game.**
   Re-scanning the table (word-pattern scan, `tools/extract_stagslct_ui.py`
   — m2c could not produce a usable struct decompile here, see below)
   recovers exactly **239 screen-id rows with zero duplicates**, matching
   `web/assets/data/screen_table.json`'s own screen count 1:1. Every single
   one resolves to a real, previously-decoded display name via
   `data/stage_names.json` (`tools/stage_names.py`, FIELDSTG name table,
   verified anchors) — e.g. `0x200`→"Central Sector — Asuka City",
   `0x270`→"Central Sector — Amaterasu City" (the 0x270+ range is the
   story-variant/alt-server screens, same convention as
   `screen_table.py`'s own `alt` field).

3. `field-script-engine-verified.md` already documented (2026-06-27,
   independently, before this session) `stagslct→0x300 (free-roam
   sentinel)`: some code path in this overlay also writes the literal value
   `0x300` into `[0x8004b370]` — outside the normal `0x01-0x2d` story-beat
   ladder and above `SCREEN_MAX=0x2ff`. That value never appears as data in
   the destination table itself (confirmed: `grep 00000300` over the whole
   table region is empty), so it is written by different code, most likely
   marking "we are now in free-roam mode" before/around opening this menu.

evidence.summary: Exact instruction addresses for the shared queue-handler's record resolution and all three mask branches. The handler resolves the target record from the QUEUE ENTRY, not from a fixed side: it loads slot from 8($v1) and side from 4($v1), then builds 0x800a4470 + slot*0x20 when side==0 and 0x800a4470 + 0x60 + slot*0x20 otherwise, so both the player and enemy records are addressable from queued events. The selector dispatch is NOT a symmetric three-way mapping: it explicitly tests only 0x0e and 0x0f. Selector 0x0e takes the andi 0xfb branch (clears bit 0x04) and selector 0x0f takes the andi 0xf7 branch (clears bit 0x08); every other selector value, including 0x0d but also anything below 0x0f or above 0x0f, falls through to the andi 0xfd branch (clears bit 0x02), which is a DEFAULT, not a 0x0d-specific test. All three branches converge on a single store at 0x800a88a0. Bit 0x04's identity as Confusion is runtime-tied by EV-a3f0e47c219d; bits 0x02 and 0x08 are NOT tied to any name by an artifact in evidence and are referred to here by bit value only.

## 1. Per-battle reward table — battle id = encounter screen id

- `disasm:` stfgtrep.s `0x2ce4/0x2d14/0x2d5c/0x26a0/0x133c` index
  `0x80086a88 + battle_id*12`; wfightmn.s `0x1eb4` copies `[0x80042b2c]` (the battle id) into
  the report workspace `[0x80042b84]`.
- `data:` `STFGTREP_D0x00003dd8 @ 0x80086a88` = `[u32; 1005]` = **335 records × 3 words**:
  **`[dvexp_base, exp_base, bits_base]`**.
- Battle id ↔ `field_encounters.json` screen key (334 screens, ids 1..334; record 0 is zero).
  Cross-check: battle 5 = 2×Numemon lv27 → `[27, 268, 645]`; battle 30 = Knightmon lv99 →
  `[99, 990, 1980]`. wfightmn's special-case battle ids 0xb/0x1e/0x143/0x144 are story fights.

Per-recipient share (exp fn `0x80086924`, bits paths `0x2cbc..0x2d88`): **1 participant → 100%,
2 → ×6/10, n≥3 → ÷n**.

- **EXP** (word1): widget `0x80084aec` (created at `0x1e3c`) adds the share into roster
  `exp @ +0x18`, cap **999,999** (`0xf423f`). **EXPAdapter** (item `0x141`=321) equipped in
  either accessory halfword (`roster +0x3c8/+0x3ca`) → **+20%** (`+ x/5`, `0x1dd0`).
- **Bits** (word2): single payout; **BITAdapter** (item `0x142`=322) → **+20%** (`0x26c0`).
- **DVEXP** (word0): per participating form, `gain = word0*10 / min(partnerLevel, 50)`,
  then the share, **min 1**, capped **10** while the form's DV level < the profile's DV cap
  (profile byte `+0x3e−2 = +0x3c`, `unknown1[0]`) and **50** at/past it (`0x80086924` tail).

## The effect registry (static fightstg data) — DECODED

One continuous table of **8-byte records** `{type:i16, texArchIdx:i16, (fileId<<16)|binIdx:u32}`
starting at **`0x800a2ea4`** (RAM), terminated by `type == -1`. Reader
`FIGHTSTG_F0x80089978(type, &texA, &texB, &texC[2])` linear-scans it; constructor
`F0x80089be4` scans it independently.

- `fileId` = **LBA file index** (== resource id; `~/ddw3/rust/dw2003_exe_data/src/lba.rs`),
  e.g. `0x79d`=E000COM1, `0x7a3`=E000COM2, `0x7e0`=E000COM3, `0x7e2`=E000COM4, `0x8a2`=E000EVOL,
  `0x7e8`=E373RENA. `binIdx` = entry inside that pack (the pack dirs in
  `~/ddw3/pack/dw2003/fight/effect/`).
- **Verified end-to-end:** Renamon clip 11 op3 types `2041/2042` → registry
  `{2041, 0x22, E373RENA bin 1}` / `{2042, 0x22, E373RENA bin 2}` (words `0x002207f9
  0x07e80001 / 0x002207fa 0x07e80002` @`0x800a3258`). Small types (2, 4, 11 …) → E000COM1 bins.
- `texArchIdx` indexes the **texture-archive table @`0x800a2b74`**: 16-byte records
  `{flags?, (fileId<<16)|texBin, vramSlot(0x140/0x1c0/0x200/0x240/0x300/0x380…), 0x100}` —
  the RLEN texture atlas of that pack + its VRAM upload slot.

## The invocation chain (Genji → Kuwagamon), every link verified

1. **Talk to Genji** → field event `0x32` plays (esdmg200 entry **11**, ends on
   "Gaining experience is the important thing!"). The event script is pure dialogue +
   `END`; its `on_complete` (`wstag200` file `0xf8`) only sets flags `0x400d=1`,`0x7401=1`.
   **No battle in the event** (confirms the old finding).

2. **Press X** → a **per-stage battle-trigger fires**. The trigger records for s200 sit in
   the wstag200 overlay at file `0x5e8` (RAM `0x800a63c8`), indexed by a **pointer array**
   at `0x800a6428` (file `0x648`; pointer at scene-ctx `[0x80099da0] = scene_ctx+0x20`,
   field `+0x18`). Each record is a fixed **12-byte struct**
   `{ screen_id:u16@+0, 0@+2, param:u16@+4, 0@+6, tag:u32@+8 }`, `tag = 0x60xx0000` (high
   nibble 6 = the battle sentinel, cf. `0x600`). Records are grouped in **zone blocks**
   of 8 (empty slots: `screen_id=0`, `tag=0x60040000`). s200's one active block:
   | idx | screen_id | param | tag |
   |-----|-----------|-------|-----|
   | 1 | 188 (`0xbc`) | 18 | `0x60080000` |
   | **2** | **200 (`0xc8`)** | **18** ← Genji (the entry that fired, `a0=0xc8`) | `0x60080000` |
   | 3 | 272 (`0x110`) | 20 | `0x600c0000` |

3. **Field caller** `fieldstg fn @0xfaf0` (RAM `0x80092780`): reads
   `entry = [[0x80099da0]+0x18][index]`, copies `entry+0x4`→working-copy `0x80042b1c+0xc`
   and `entry+0x8`→`+0x14`, then calls the battle-setup with `a0 = entry+0x0 = 0xc8`.
   *(Live BP: caller `ra=0x800927ec`, `a0=0xc8`.)*

4. **Battle-setup / HANDOFF** `fn 0x8008b798` (fieldstg file `0x8ae8`) — *live-confirmed it
   fires exactly once on the X-press*:
   - `target = ([0x8004b370] == 0x2b) ? 0xe0a : 0x600` → here `b370=3` ⇒ **`0x600`** (the
     `li $a2,0x600` at file `0x8b40`). `0xe0a` is the alternate target for progress-state 43
     (unconfirmed — probably a scripted/loss battle variant).
   - stores `0x600` into the transition object `+0x5c`, calls its `+0x28`(2);
   - copies `0x80094680[screen_id]` record bytes `+0xc/+0xd/+0xe[12]` → `0x80042b1c+0x3c`
     (first loop @ file `0x8b84`–`0x8bb0`);
     this is exactly record `+0x0c..+0x19` → globals `0x80042b58..0x80042b65`.
     The known consumers make `+0x0e..+0x18` the per-encounter Poison, Frozen,
     Confusion, Sleep, KO, direct-HP, CursedPuppet, CharmGas and SpiderWeb gates;
   - **then a second loop @ file `0x8bdc`–`0x8c0c` writes the enemy party** — this is the
     `screen_id→enemy` map (see Step 7).
     **`0x80094680` is the per-screen record table** (28-byte stride); `record[0xc8]` `+0/+4/+8`
     are three **enemy-slot struct pointers** (`0x800939b4`, `0x80092dfc`×2), **not** handler
     fn-ptrs as previously thought.

5. **Game state** `0x16c($gp)` → 0. The **f12 main loop** (`0x80014524`) "load next screen"
   block (`state==0`) runs the screen-loader and calls **`set_D0x8004b3f8(0x600)`**.

6. **`f15` / overlay manager**: `b3f8>>8 = 6 ≠ D0x80055d28 (2)` ⇒ streams engine overlay
   **lib 6 (FIGHTSTG)** to `0x80082cb0`; data overlay **LBA 520 (WFIGHTMN)** to `0x800a5de0`.

evidence.summary: F0x8009ff40 is installed as the acting-side action object's method at static table slot 0x800a4610, reached only through that method pointer; no direct jal to it exists anywhere in the dw2003 assembly.

Dispatch site of the action object's method +0x90 inside the sub-action attack runner: after the physical-accuracy roll through method 0x9c stores the hit flag at +0x7c, a hit loads the method pointer at +0x90 and calls it with dir (+0x70), move (+0x78) and base (+0x74) from the task object, stores the damage at +0x80, and runs the 0x800aabf0 finalize when the mode halfword at offset 0x4536 is nonzero.

The static nine-word table at 0x800a4670, consulted in the third branch of the field subroutine, maps attack elements to the field that subtracts a fraction of the base; its words match the canonical prose's list [0,0,4,2,5,3,7,8,6].

Checked decompilation of the match path agrees with the assembly: the acting-side effective byte (field unk37) is saved, zeroed, the tail F0x8009f6dc is called with arg2 unchanged, and the byte is restored.

Checked decompilation of the scaling path agrees with the assembly: arg2 is multiplied by the skill record's unkC and rounds via 0x1F then >> 5, or via 0x3F then >> 6 when the record byte unk1B is clear, before F0x8009f6dc receives the scaled value as its base.

The shared tail's only direct call sites in the dw2003 assembly: one from the physical-base routine and two from the second entry caller; a repo-wide enumeration of the asm tree found no other reference and no .word reference.
F0x800A0590 bounds its scan by the per-player block's +0x0A hand count
it selects entries by the same duel+0x46F flag array
and compacts the hand array at per-player block +0x64
F0x80093adc, one of the three handlers behind opcodes 0x15..0x1a, reads the occupied-slot count of the side named by its third argument from duel+0x72c + side*0x72.
It stores that count minus 1 into duel+0x428 in its jr delay slot, seeding a descending cursor over that side's occupied field slots.
Its face index is duel+0x304 minus 1, so opcode 0x1b displays a plate chosen by the Battle-Phase state-8 counter at duel+0x304 rather than by an opcode immediate.
Opcode 0x1b's update step 6 forms the same base 0x8004b7d0, encoded word 0x2453b7d0.
And loads the same slot +0x3f4 from it.
Opcode 0x1b (F0x80093c18) places view sprite id 0x11 at the fixed position 0x8300, 0x6100 through view method +0xf14.
F0x80094b78 (opcodes 0x1c/0x1d) clears the same accumulators and additionally zeroes duel+0x438 in its jr delay slot, which is the single difference from F0x80094828.
Opcodes 0x2b/0x2d set duel+0x499 to 2 on the acting path.
Opcodes 0x2b/0x2d call view method +0xec4.

The handler's third argument overrides that guard: when it is non-zero the branch is not taken and the body runs regardless of which side made the previous play. This is the 0/1 that distinguishes opcode 0x2b from 0x2d and 0x2c from 0x2e.
F0x8009518c reads the play-history index duel+0x575 and steps back one entry before testing it.
When it runs, the handler writes back a decremented play-history index, retiring the most recent play-history entry.
The guard tests byte +0x584 of the PREVIOUS play-history entry - the side that made that play - and proceeds only when it is 0.
Opcodes 0x2c/0x2e additionally set duel+0x49d, and set duel+0x499 to 1 rather than 2.
The step counter duel+0x422 is set to 1 on the acting path; the non-acting path sets it to 2 instead.
Opcodes 0x2c/0x2e are the same shape but call view method +0xec8 instead of +0xec4.
F0x80094fdc (opcodes 0x2f/0x30) clears the roll/wait timer duel+0x424 before its view call.

It then calls view method +0xee4 with the opcode-selected id (0x39 for 0x2f, 0x35 for 0x30) and three further arguments 0, 0, 1, and sets the step counter to 1. It touches no duel state other than +0x424 and +0x422, so it is a presentation-only opcode.
Interpreter case 0x4f calls F0x80091858 with instance immediate 0x50 in the jal delay slot.
Interpreter case 0x55 calls the same function with instance immediate 0x56; the seven call sites at 0x80084744..0x800847ec carry the consecutive immediates 0x50..0x56.
F0x80094828 (opcode 0x5a) zeroes the pending stat-change accumulators at duel+0x428 and +0x42c along with +0x424, +0x430 and +0x434.
The index is bounds-checked against 5, so this machine has exactly five steps.
The cursor at duel+0x428 is then advanced by one.
It compares duel+0x428 against that count - so within opcode 0x9e, +0x428 is a SLOT CURSOR, not the board AP total that opcode 0x5a leaves there.
Step 3 begins a signed division by 15 by the reciprocal-multiply method; the upper half of the magic constant 0x88888889 is loaded here.
The lower half completes the constant 0x88888889, the standard signed magic number for division by 15; the dividend is the halfword at duel+0x59c, the first field of the per-player block.
The cursor is offset by 6 to form the global 0..11 slot index passed to view method +0xf28.
F0x80088f78, the update callee for opcode 0x9e, forms a jump-table index from the step counter duel+0x422 minus 1.
Step 4 calls through +0x3f4 of the resident structure at 0x8004b7d0 - the same resident field opcode 0x1b's update step 6 reads.
Step 2 bounds its cursor by side 1's occupied-slot count at duel+0x79e.
Its jump-table base is 0x8008334c - a THIRD table in this overlay that m2c does not resolve.
Step 2 gates its per-frame work on duel+0x434 having reached at least 6, using it as a tick budget.
And the tick budget at duel+0x434 is reduced by 6, so the slots are revealed one every six ticks.
Each mark also sets duel+0x438 to 1, the per-opcode 'at least one match' flag.
For slot indices 0..5 the sweep compares the index against the live slot count byte at duel+0x72c and skips the slot when the index is not below it.
For slot indices 6..11 the same gate reads the second side's count byte at duel+0x79e, confirming the 0x72-byte per-side stride.
F0x8008d274 forms its jump-table pointer from base 0x800834fc; the preceding lui loads 0x8008 and the following sll scales the (selector-1) index by 4.
The jump-table index register is $s8 = arg3 - 1, scaled by 4, so selectors 1..8 address the eight words at 0x800834fc..0x8008351c.
The sweep body runs for slot index $s2 = 0..11, i.e. all twelve field slots (six per side).
A slot that passes its selector's test is marked by storing 1 into the per-slot selection array at duel+0x46f.
Selector 1 loads the acting side argument saved at 0x50($sp) and uses it to choose which half of the board it marks.
Selector 1 (opcode 0x8e) branches only on whether the slot index is below 6, i.e. on which side the slot belongs to, combined with the acting side passed in a2 and read back from 0x50($sp).
Selector 4 (opcode 0x91) compares the slot's colour against 1 (white) and skips the mark when they are EQUAL, so it marks every colour except white.
Selector 5 (opcode 0x92) loads the comparison constant 2 (blue) into $v1 for the same not-equal marking shape.
Selector 6 (opcode 0x93) loads the comparison constant 3 (green) in the delay slot of a jump to the shared bne test, so it marks only green.
Selector 7 (opcode 0x94) loads the comparison constant 4 (red) and uses the beq-skip shape, so it marks every colour except red.
Selector 8 (opcode 0x95) reaches the shared test with $v1 = 6 (brown) and the test is bne, so it marks only brown - the opposite polarity to selectors 4, 5 and 7.
The per-slot cursor advances by 0x0e bytes each iteration, giving the field-slot stride.
CARDPAK record byte +0x01 (AP) is read from the fetched record buffer.
AP is stored into the slot at +0x08.
That instance-table halfword is incremented by 1 before the record fetch, matching the documented 'instance table stores cardId - 1' convention and the F0x8001ebf8 accessor idiom.
The first byte of that block is read as the side's current occupied-slot count and used both as the destination slot index and as the sprite index base.
For side 1 the count is offset by 6 to give the global 0..11 slot index the view uses as its sprite id.
CARDPAK record byte +0x02 (HP) is read from the same buffer.
HP is stored into the slot at +0x0a.
The instance index itself is stored into the slot at +0x02 - the field the colour lookup F0x8009cf60 later reads.
The fourth argument is an INDEX into the card instance table at duel+0x50, not a card id: the halfword at duel+0x50+arg3*2 is loaded and passed to the CARDPAK accessor.
duel+0x308 is a placement sequence counter: its pre-increment value is taken and the incremented value written back.
That pre-increment sequence value is stored into the slot at +0x0e, giving each placed card a duel-unique placement ordinal.
F0x80091858 addresses its side's field block at duel+0x72c + side*0x72; the preceding shift/subtract/shift/add/shift chain computes side*0x72 exactly.
The owning side is stored into the slot at +0x0d.
The destination slot address is block + count*0x0e, computed as ((count<<3)-count)<<1; this independently confirms the 0x0e field-slot stride.
The slot's byte at +0x0c is set to the constant 2 on placement.
The slot's two modifier halfwords at +0x04 and +0x06 are zeroed on placement; these are the running AP/HP deltas that F0x8008def8 later adds into.
It clears the view's per-slot halfword +0x12e that step 2 had set.
Step 4 is the only step that returns 1, which is what the interpreter treats as 'opcode complete'.
It increments that count by one.
It then loads the side's occupied-slot count byte through the pointer to duel+0x72c + side*0x72.
The incremented count is stored back in the delay slot of the jump to the return path, so it executes. This is the write that makes a newly placed field slot live.

set_card_scale_endpoints: nothing alone; it sizes a slide already running by calling the shared slot scaler with an endpoint argument.
scaleSlot: one card on the board grows or shrinks where it sits; it calls the shared slot scaler and writes no field itself.
card_start_move_silent: the card slides to a new spot with no landing sound; sets sprite mode byte +0x14A to 3 and calls the slide starter.

card_start_summon: the card pops on, overshoots and settles; sets sprite mode byte +0x14A to 5, an effect selector +0x138, full scale +0x120/+0x122, and the motion's start/end/duration at +0x130/+0x134/+0x110/+0x114.

clear_hud_highlights: the lit colour cubes and labels on both strips go off; zeroes the two ten-byte highlight banks at view+0x90 and view+0xE4.

The summon selector F0x800878B4 does the same: lw 0x3fc (repeat word) for bit 7 and lw 0x3f4 (pressed word), ORing the masked results, so a held direction repeats.

The Summon Phase driver F0x800A0B80 calls duel method +0x818 (F0x800A0754, the per-side commit) itself, once per side, after each side's picker returns. The picker therefore never commits; it only reports that it is finished, and the END-of-turn signal is the picker's return, reached through Circle-Yes at the state-7 prompt.

Square sets picker state 6 unconditionally, with or without marks, so the commit prompt is raised on every Square; Triangle sets state 0xB, a short flash that loops back to the picker rather than ending the turn.

evidence.summary: Six characters on the Circuit Board each hand over one card: flags 0x9220, 0x9222, 0x921F, 0x9245, 0x92F1 and 0x9270, i.e. cards 32 Fortune Gate, 34 Desire Access, 31 Delete Matrix, 69 RosemonII, 241 Creepymon and 112 MarineAngemon. Its neighbour s885 supplies the remaining two rule-bearing Digimon, 198 Gryphonmon and 155 SaberLeomon. All five of the Digimon cards that carry a rule are therefore gifts, and nothing sells them.

A card grant in the shipped dialogue graph. Flag id 37559 is 0x92B7: bank (id >> 8) & 0xFFFE = 0x92, index id & 0x1FF = 0xB7 = 183, which is Gabumon. The state's gate and its other two on_close writes are the ordinary story bits that advance the speaker's dialogue. This is the Asuka Inn, the earliest of the 30 such writes.

The Program half of the selectable-hand test reads the duel's mode byte at +0x2F8 after calling the resident class predicate. The surrounding compares accept the card when the mode is 7, or when the mode is 5 and the predicate returned 2; a predicate result of 0, which is every Digimon card, is rejected before this load.

The selectable-hand entry point tests the same mode byte first: mode 6, the Summon Phase, takes its own arm which accepts a hand card only when the card record's type byte +0x03 is 0x10, i.e. only Digimon cards, and then applies a cost test. Every other mode delegates to F0x80085f38, the Program test.

State 0xA loads side 0's HP (lh 0x59e -> $v1) and side 1's HP (lh 0x666 -> $v0) and computes $v0 = (side1HP < side0HP). Branch taken (side1HP >= side0HP) latches 0x17 sweeping SIDE 0's board with +0x301 = 1 (winner = side 1, the tie-goes-to-side-1 rule); the fall-through (side1HP < side0HP) latches 0x18 sweeping side 1's board with +0x301 = 0. Both set +0x2F4 = 1, +0x2F9 = 0xB, +0x2FC = 0. So the swept side is the one with fewer-or-equal HP — the set LOSER — and +0x301 receives the winner.

evidence.summary: Inside the loop over the three active party positions (loop counter $s0 with `slti $v0, $s0, 0x3`), stagslct calls the helper at D0x80048d34+0x2750 with $a0 = the deployed index returned by the +0x2718 helper. That helper pair is the documented resolver that returns an Unknown4* roster record pointer, so the register $v1 used by the following halfword accesses is a DIGIMON_CUR_STATS record base.

The read-modify-write of the roster record halfword at +0x32. Unknown4Stats begins at Unknown4+0x1c and cur_chr is block index 11, so record offset 0x1c + 11*2 = 0x32 is cur_chr. The next instructions add the signed delta register $s3 (set by the preceding pad-input block to +1, -1, +10 or -10) and store the result back to +0x32.

Upper clamp of the +0x32 edit: sign-extended value is compared against 0x3e8 (1000) and, when not less, 0x3e7 (999) is stored back to +0x32; a following `bgez` test stores 0 when the value went negative. The [0, 999] clamp pair matches exactly the documented cur_chr cap of 999 in the generic clamped roster stat mutator F0x800170c8, corroborating that +0x32 is cur_chr and not some unrelated field.

After the clamp, the same routine reads cur_chr back out of the roster record into $s4 (and the paired +0x1c level field into $s5) and passes both to a numeric-print call through a vtable slot at +0x118, i.e. this screen both edits and displays the party's Charisma. This is the only site in the whole original assembly corpus that reads roster record +0x32 as a Digimon stat.

Independent confirmation that D0x80048d34.unk2750(deployed_index) yields an Unknown4* roster record: in this helper the returned pointer's unk20/unk22 and unk24/unk26 are the cur_hp/max_hp and cur_mp/max_mp pairs, which are exactly Unknown4Stats indices 2/3 and 4/5 at record offsets 0x20/0x22 and 0x24/0x26. The same +0x2718 then +0x2750 call pair, over the same three active party positions, is what stagslct uses before touching +0x32.

Canonical field-order table for the 19 halfword Unknown4Stats block at Unknown4+0x1c, giving cur_chr as stat index 11 with cap 999. Index 11 places cur_chr at record offset 0x32 and at stats-block offset 0x16, which are the two access forms censused in this work.

Anchor for an ABSENCE finding. This is one of the 31 non-stack halfword loads at offset +0x16 that make up the previously unaudited `stats_ptr + 0x16` alternative-access census. Its base $s3 is an equipment/accessory bonus record, not a roster stats block: the immediately preceding sibling loads at +0x12 and +0x14 accumulate into combatant fields +0x4 and +0xa while +0x16 accumulates into combatant +0x6, so the offsets are unrelated to the Unknown4Stats field order. Every other non-stack +0x16 halfword load in the corpus classified the same way (kernel/libspu/libgpu code, text and sprite layout, the F0x80017174 effective-stat scratch buffer, card-layout tables with 0x20/0x34 strides, shop counters, and the wstag415 windmill actor). No site in the census reads Charisma.

The disc's cmfont sprite directory ships 94 clips and its id list skips 0x12, 0x13, 0x3E, 0x3F, 0x46 and 0x47. Clips 0x3E and 0x3F -- the ones an element-driven badge would need for machine and dark -- do not exist on the disc. This is not an extraction gap.
The confirm arm reads a single BYTE from the cursor table, so the table is a run of consecutive bytes indexed by the cursor row, not an array of words.
The byte just read is stored to 0x8005cca8 (0x80084424-0x3358 form), the same global stagslct indexes to draw the current language name. This is what makes the two overlays' tables composable.
First four bytes of the cursor table, little-endian 02 03 05 04, giving cursor rows 0-3 the language indices ENG, FRA, GER, ITA.
Fifth byte of the cursor table, value 6 = SPN. Emitted as a `.byte` directive because the overlay ends mid-word; tools/overlay_scan.py cannot see it and reports zero here.

overlay_scan.py's only data pattern is WORD_RE, which matches `.word` directives alone. Offsets covered solely by a `.byte` directive are therefore absent from its word map and print as zero, which is how the 2026-07-11 reproduce command reported cnty_sel's last three table bytes as 0. Re-stamped 2026-08-30 after re-reading: WORD_RE is unchanged at L41 and still matches `.word` alone, so the cited fact holds, but commit b11422bf added a separate raw-source-line map for label shapes WORD_RE cannot parse, so the tool as a whole is no longer blind in the way this summary's word "only" implies.

Rising-edge computation: after xor of the old and new words, the AND with the new word leaves the bits that went from released to pressed this frame.
The rising-edge word is stored at record offset +0x00 (object +0x48 for port block 0, slot 0), which is the halfword F0x80018854 returns.
F0x800188c0 sources the default keymap from the 16-byte table at D0x8004bbf4 and copies it into one record's +0xa4 window.
For logical button index i (loop 0..15) the decoder loads the byte at record +0x5c + i, which is object offset 0xa4 + port*0x1c0 + slot*0x70 + i - exactly the byte F0x80018980 returns.
The keymap byte is used as an arithmetic shift count on the decoded button word, and the next instruction masks bit 0, proving the byte is a physical bit index rather than a mask.
F0x80018928 exchanges two entries of one record's keymap window, the operation a button-configuration screen needs.
The default-keymap store: 16 bytes written at object offset 0xa4 + port*0x1c0 + slot*0x70 + i. This is a writer to the exact bytes F0x80018980 reads.
The reset routine F0x80018310 passes length 0x3e0 with D0x8004b7d0 as the destination to the clear helper, bounding the object at 0x3e0 bytes (0x8004b7d0..0x8004bbb0).

Reset hands the device layer two buffers 0x22 (34) bytes apart, starting at D0x8004b7d4 = object +0x04. 34 bytes is the PlayStation controller transfer-buffer size, and object +0x04..+0x47 is exactly the space needed for two of them.
Reset iterates the outer index while it is below 2 - the port count.
The disconnected-controller clear path masks the port field of the channel id to a single bit before scaling it by 0x1c0, so the index that reaches the 0x1c0 scale is a one-bit port number.
The previous frame's button word, read from +0x06 one instruction earlier, is copied into record offset +0x04 (object +0x4c). No accessor slot was found for +0x4c.
The decoder reads the halfword at offset 2 of a transfer buffer and inverts it two instructions later, the active-low button word of a PlayStation controller packet.
The input decoder materialises the record-array base as D0x8004b818, which is D0x8004b7d0 + 0x48. This is the symbol that names the per-controller record array.

Ten instructions later the same function recovers the containing object by subtracting 0x48 from the record-array base, proving D0x8004b818 = D0x8004b7d0 + 0x48 and that the record array is a member at object offset 0x48.
The repeat bit is 1 shifted left by the byte loaded from record +0x5c, so the repeat word uses the same physical bit numbering as the current and rising-edge words.
Record offset +0x02 (object +0x4a) is zeroed at the start of every decode pass, before the 16-iteration per-button timer loop.
When a held button's repeat timer elapses, the bit for that button is ORed into record offset +0x02 (object +0x4a), the halfword F0x8001889c returns.
Reset iterates the inner index while it is below 4 - the multitap slot count per port.

Inside the decoder the low two bits of the channel id are multiplied by 7 and then shifted left by 4, giving a multitap-slot stride of 0x70 bytes; the preceding shift-left-by-6 on the port bit gives the 0x1c0 port-block stride.

evidence.summary: The generic HP/MP heal handler F0x8008dc00 compares the target's current HP (+0x6) with its max (+0x8). When they are equal (full) it spawns the presentation actor and sets message id 0x2f ('No effect!') at action+0x50; when they differ it takes the heal branch at 0x8008dc78.
