evidence.summary: CARD FOLDERS and Digivolve Demo draw the same two windows at the same places: the footer plate about (0,0xd3) and the panel clip 0x3A @ (0xA8,0x28) about (0x140,0x40).
The two-bit result is shifted to bit 5 and ORed into the texpage halfword written at sp+0x70 - i.e. it lands in the texpage's ABR field, giving hardware mode (n-1)&3.
A high nibble of 8..0xE indexes the seven-entry state-register jump table at D0x80082cb0 after subtracting 8 and bounds-checking with sltiu 0x7.
A non-zero nibble is decremented by one before use: the selector is ONE-BASED, so the stored value is not the hardware blend mode.

The extractor stores the raw 0xEn nibble under the key 'abr' on every textured primitive. Census over all 129 pack JSONs in web/assets/battle/effects/proj, every layer and every primitive (21,051 in total, no sampling): the nibble takes only the values 0 (3,565 prims / 37 packs), 2 (17,394 / 115) and 4 (92 / 2). Under (n-1)&3 those are hardware ABR 0, 1 and 3, so no shipped primitive selects the subtractive ABR 2.
The mesh display-list interpreter splits each opcode byte into nibbles: the high nibble selects a state register, the low nibble is its value.
The 0xE handler parks the low nibble in the stack slot sp+0x48. Matching '0x48($sp)' across the whole function gives two hits: this store and the read at 0x80085484.
The seventh and last entry of that table - high nibble 0xE - points at 0x800853c0. Read from fightstg's own data section, not inferred from the order of the handler blocks.
The decremented selector is masked to two bits, which is the width of the PS1 texpage's semi-transparency field.
While the tex-op assembles the texpage halfword, a stored nibble of zero branches past the blend-field computation, leaving the texpage ABR bits at 0.
Each tick the playback cursor at +0x80 advances by the global D0x800a4464 and is clamped to the stream length minus one.
The clip compiler sets the animator's playback cursor at +0x80 to 1 when it selects a clip, so the first rendered tick reads the second entry of the compiled stream.

When the advanced cursor lands on a 0xffff entry the animator sets its own finished flag at +0x7c and writes 1 into the control block's +0x10 - which, because the control block is flight+0x74, is the flight object's +0x84.
In its running state the flight object tests +0x84 and, when the animator has set it, calls its own +0x28 method with argument 3 - the teardown that ends the effect. This is the effect's lifetime.
The compiled stream's length is stored at animator+0xa0, and the cursor is reset to 1 immediately after; the length counts the terminal entry.

For a record whose last-frame field is nonzero the compiler emits `count` stream entries counting up from the record's first-frame field, which is what makes a segment a plain frame ramp - and lets a later segment replay an earlier frame range.
The compiler stops reading the meta bin when a record's first halfword is 0x7fff; the 8-byte records before it are the clip's segments.
In the tex-op the CLUT's fifth byte is added to mesh+0x70 before being shifted down by 4 and masked to 6 bits, i.e. it is a VRAM x offset from the mesh's palette base.
The sixth byte is added to mesh+0x74, the palette base Y.
The mesh-object constructor F0x8008610c stores its second argument at mesh+0x70 - the palette base X that the tex-op adds to.
and its third argument at mesh+0x74, the palette base Y.
The op6 flight object sets that base to 0x280 = 640 ...
... and 0x100 = 256, so every op6 projectile mesh uses the palette base (640, 256), which is also where its 4bpp page is loaded - so the tex-op bytes are page-local coordinates and the base cancels.
The summed y is shifted left 6 and ORed with the summed x >> 4, which is exactly the GPU's CLUT field layout (y << 6 | x >> 4). The tex-op bytes are therefore a palette POSITION, not an opaque tag.

evidence.summary: MEFT0039's page holds real palettes at exactly three slots - row 255, halfword x 0, 16 and 32 - and every other candidate slot (x 48, rows 254/253/252) is solid 0xffff fill. Its layers name exactly those three: the upright rings 0, the outward shards 16, the flat ground arc 32. Over all 129 packs the per-primitive slots resolve to 456 distinct live palettes where the old one-per-pack guess baked 129; 1,181 of 21,051 primitives name a fill slot and keep the best-ramp fallback.

The same mesh+0x70 is also the texture PAGE origin: the third tex-op byte is multiplied by 64 and added to it before the >>6 that yields the texpage x field. Page and palettes therefore share one base.

The per-frame layer builder creates each layer's mesh object with F0x8008610c, passing the animator's +0x68 and +0x6c as the palette base - which the animator constructor took from the flight object's +0x6c and +0x70.

The 1,181 primitives previously reported as naming a 0xffff fill slot name SMALL but real palettes: 1,149 slots hold two distinct entries, 16 hold three and 16 hold one, and not one of the 21,051 primitives names a slot that is actually all 0xffff. MEFT0089 layer 1 is the pattern - {0x958c, then fifteen 0x0000} - a one-colour stencil whose ink is index 0. The four-distinct-entry threshold was borrowed from _palette_score's ramp scoring and does not belong in a liveness test. With the test corrected to 'not the fill row' the fallback fires zero times and the 129 packs resolve to 476 distinct palettes.

The child's matrix is concatenated with the parent's by three GTE MVMVA passes, one per matrix column, with the parent's 3x3 loaded into the GTE control registers beforehand and the result written to the child's +0x4c.

The animator constructor sizes the layer array as count+1: it loads the program table's count from desc+0x4 and adds one before allocating (count+1)*0x21*4 = (count+1)*0x84 bytes. The extra block is layer 0, the implicit root.
FIGHTSTG_F0x800847c4 is a thin wrapper that forwards to the real animator constructor FIGHTSTG_F0x80084560 with its flag argument set to zero.

FIGHTSTG_F0x8008970c builds the mesh animator by calling FIGHTSTG_F0x800847c4, having placed flight+0x74 in the fifth argument slot as the animator's control block; flight+0x74+0x1c is flight+0x90 and +0x22 is flight+0x96.

FIGHTSTG_F0x8008970c state 0 stores the launch command's first vector into the flight object at +0x90/+0x92/+0x94 (and the second at +0x96..+0x9a), which is the block the mesh animator later reads as its control block through flight+0x74.

The layer hide test compares the bitwise OR of the three scale components against 0x31. The components are loaded with sign-extending `lh`, so a negative component sets the sign bit of the OR and hides the layer: it is a signed test, not an absolute-value test.
The layer's rotation matrix is built by EXE routine F0x8002b45c from the layer's sampled rotation at +0x18 into the matrix slot at +0x28. This is fightstg's only call to that routine.

The per-frame builder turns each layer's +0x00 parent index into a pointer: it multiplies the index by the 0x84 layer stride, adds 0x4c (the offset of the concatenated matrix) and stores the result at the child's +0x48.

The constructor's per-row copy loop writes the program row's FIRST word to layer+0x00, then the next two words to layer+0x04 (mesh bin) and layer+0x08 (ctrl bin). The first word is the parent index, not a zero pad.

Layer 0's parent-matrix pointer is set to the fixed identity matrix D0x8004dc20, which is what makes it the root of the layer tree; its mesh and ctrl bin pointers are stored as zero, so it draws nothing.

The same overwrite continues into the ROOT layer's rotation at layer0+0x18..+0x1c from the control block's +0x22..+0x26 - op6's second vector, which is therefore root rotation angles and not a target position.

After the track sampler has run, the builder overwrites the ROOT layer's translation at layer0+0x10..+0x14 from the control block's +0x1c..+0x20 - i.e. from op6's launch position - discarding anything sampled into the root.
The store of the matrix word at +0x8 places m[1][1] = sin_x*sin_y*sin_z + cos_x*cos_z. Together with m[2][0] = -sin_y this admits only the axis order Rz*Ry*Rx.
The store of the matrix word at +0xc places the negated sin_y in m[2][0] and sin_x*cos_y in m[2][1].
In the mesh rotation routine, sin_y (held in $a3) is negated immediately before the store that writes the matrix word at +0xc, giving m[2][0] = -sin_y.

The scale routine multiplies each matrix element by the scale component selected by its COLUMN index, forming M*diag(s); the local layer transform is therefore T*(R*S), with the scale applied inside the rotation.

The track sampler loops three times, stepping its selector by 3 and stopping below 9, which selects sub-track 0/1/2 and destination +0x10 (translation) / +0x18 (rotation) / +0x20 (scale) on the layer.
The fourth emit path repeats it again, so all four primitive shapes agree: no branch anywhere sets the semi-transparent bit for a zero nibble.
The textured-quad emit path writes the GPU command byte 0x3C, the OPAQUE textured quad, into the packet before considering semi-transparency.
It then loads $a3+0x18. $a3 is sp+0x30 in the interpreter's frame, so this is the same sp+0x48 slot the 0xEn state register writes: the blend selector gates the command bit.

Only when that slot is non-zero does it OR bit 1 into the command byte - the GPU's semi-transparent flag, turning 0x3C into 0x3E. A zero nibble therefore draws the primitive OPAQUE, with no blending at all.
The textured-triangle emit path writes the opaque command 0x34 and repeats the same gate two instructions later.
The triangle path's semi-transparent bit, set under the identical zero test on the 0xEn slot.

evidence.summary: Per-texel STP census. The PS1 blends a semi-transparent primitive only where the palette entry's bit 15 is set; where it is clear the texel is drawn solid, which a uniform per-primitive blend cannot reproduce. Over the 18,120,302 texels inside the 16,382 BLENDED primitives of all 129 packs: 12,686,288 (70.01%) have STP set, 5,434,014 (29.99%) are the transparent 0x0000 entry, and ZERO have STP clear. No primitive mixes the two classes, in any pack. Uniform per-group blending is therefore exact for this artwork, not an approximation.

Texel census over all 129 pack pages. Whole-page, index 15 is 89.2% of texels and index 0 is 3.7% - which is why index 15 was taken for the background. Restricted to the rectangles the meshes actually sample (1,057,649 texels inside the primitives' UV boxes) the order reverses: index 0 is 29.4% and index 15 is 7.7%, an ordinary ramp step. Entry 0 of the palette is 0x0000 in 318 of 456 live palettes, and 0x0000 is the PS1's transparent texel. The 89% figure is the unused remainder of each 256x256 page, filled with 0xffff halfwords, which no mesh samples. Index 15 is the ramp's BRIGHTEST step and was being punched out as transparent.

F0x8002a730 returns the bit length of a positive argument by counting right shifts, and 0 for a non-positive one.

evidence.summary: The New Game routine's first act. That helper is F0x80017CB0, whose entire body is a zero-fill: word stores of $zero when the length is a multiple of four, byte stores otherwise, and nothing else. F0x8002a7cc divides its angle argument by 360 with the signed magic multiply 0xb60b60b7 (hi + n, >> 8, minus the sign) before using it. It builds a pure Z rotation from that angle - m[0][0]=m[1][1]=cos, m[0][1]=-sin, m[1][0]=+sin, m[2][2]=0x1000, translation zero - and MulMatrix's it onto the caller's matrix. The zero test at .L0x8002a81c makes a zero angle a no-op.
One word stores m[0][0] = cos(vy)cos(vz) + sin(vy)sin(vx)sin(vz) and m[0][1] = cos(vz)sin(vy)sin(vx) - cos(vy)sin(vz). These two are the elements that fix Rz's handedness and confirm the Y.X.Z order.
One word stores m[0][2] = sin(vy)*cos(vx) (from the mult at .L0x8002b7b4) and m[1][0] = cos(vx)*sin(vz). The sign of m[0][2] fixes Ry's handedness.

RotMatrix element m[2][2] is stored as cos(vx)*cos(vy).

Word 0 of the file is 0x80082cb0. It is the address every interior self-pointer in the file resolves against: subtracting it from any of the 249 pointers in sections 2 and 3 yields an offset inside this same file.
Word 1 is 0x10, the offset of the first section - which is the very next word after the four-word header. This is what identifies words 1..3 as section offsets rather than data.
Word 2 is 0x2458, the offset of section 2.
Word 3 is 0x4e74, the offset of section 3. Section 2's measured extent lands on exactly this value: 0x2458 + 55 * 0xC4 = 0x4E74. The header offset and the measured stride agree without adjustment.

Section 2 record 0 carries a self-pointer 0x800830a4 at file 0x2464, i.e. record offset +0x0C. 0x800830a4 - 0x80082cb0 = 0x3F4, which lands in the shared pool that begins at file 0x3F0. The remaining 54 records repeat this at exactly 0xC4 intervals (0x2464, 0x2528, 0x25EC, ... 0x4DBC).
Section 3 record 0 carries a self-pointer 0x800837d8 at file 0x4e80, again record offset +0x0C. The stride changes here from 0xC4 to 0x48 and holds for 193 records.

The last section-3 self-pointer sits at file 0x8480, which is record 192 under the 0x48 stride starting at 0x4e80. 0x4E74 + 193 * 0x48 = 0x84BC, and the file's last word is at 0x84B8, so section 3 ends exactly at end of file with no slack.

First entry of the index table at file 0x10, word 0x350001d4. Split little-endian by field: key = 0x01d4, self-index = 0x00, slot = 0x35. Across the 55 entries the self-index field runs 0,1,2,...,54 without a gap, which is what proves the 4-byte stride and the field split.

First entry of the second index table at file 0xec, word 0xa800017e: key = 0x017e, self-index = 0x00, slot = 0xa8 (168). The self-index field restarts at 0 here after reaching 54 at file 0xe8, which is what separates the two tables.

The five window clips the status overlay picks between, by row count, measure 172x37, 172x51, 172x65, 172x79 and 172x93. Each step is 14 pixels, the same as the decoded row pitch, and each adds about five layers, so these are tiled frames whose height follows the row count. The tallest is the five-row one at 93.

The pause-menu field Use-Item applier. It resolves the selected item's effect record (resolver [0x80042b98]) and dispatches on the record's byte +1, the pair's effect selector: 1 -> the HP path at 0xc980 (adds the pair value at +0x2, caps at +0x20/+0x22), 0x11 -> the TP path at 0xca08 (adds to +0x1e, caps 99), anything else -> the stat/element table applier at 0xca50. $a1 is the applied flag: the no-effect branch at 0xcb30 ($a1==0) shows message 0x6a and plays sound 0x1c then returns; the applied branch shows the selector-indexed message (0x52 + selector) plus the delta, then decrements the bag count at 0x80048d34 + 0x7c + slot (0xcbac) and plays sound 0x14. So a refused use does not consume, and a successful one consumes exactly one.

$a1 is the applied flag every arm starts at 0 (set by the delay slot at line 12891) and only sets to 1 when it changed something. Line 13011 `beqz $a1` sends a refusal to message id 0x6A (line 13063) with no amount and sound 0x0004001C (lines 13064+13067), and leaves the bag byte alone; the success path prints selector+0x52 (lines 13023+13027) with the rolled amount through *(page+0x88)+0x118 (line 13033) and sound 0x00040014 (lines 13046+13050). The one exception is a heal clipped by max HP, which takes its own branch with the CONSTANT id 0x52 (lines 12933+12934) and no amount.

The pause ITEMS applier F0x8008F584 reads the item's EFFECT record, not the master row: F0x8001355C returns &D0x80041844[id] and line 12880 `lw $s2, ($v0)` dereferences it, so the selector is byte +1 of *(0x80041838 + 12*id) and the roll's divisor is the halfword at +2 (line 12910 `lhu $v0, 0x2($s2)`). The routine's entry is file 0xC8D4 (line 12860); the earlier claim's 'ststatus 0xc8fc' is its last prologue store, line 12870.

The status screen resolves the highlighted partner's roster slot (method +0x2718), computes the record and reads +0x764; when it is nonzero it labels the partner with string id 0x3C, otherwise it takes the other branch. A second independent consumer of +0x764 as the partner's form id.

The field boost applier's 6-byte entry table: {selector, stat index, cap}. 15 entries: selector 2 (max HP) cap 9999 (0x270f), selector 3 (max MP) cap 9999, selectors 4..0x10 (STR, DEF, SPT, WIS, SPD, CHR and the seven elemental tolerances) cap 999 (0x3e7); terminated by selector 0xffff.

The permanent stat/element chip applier rolls the boost instead of granting the item's value: it calls a random function through `0x8004dc04->+0x8` and then `div $zr, $v0, $v1` / `mfhi $a0` with v1 = the item record's value word, so the delta is `rand % value + 1` (1..value). It adds that to the stat word at record +0x1c + 2*statIndex and then clamps it at the entry's cap.

F0x8009A3E8's worn-gear arm tests byte +2 of the item's EFFECT record (line 24059/24163 `lbu $v1, 0x2($v1)` after `lw $v1, ($v0)`), where 7 occurs for 23 shipped weapons, ids 176..198 - so it is reachable, and the 'cannot fire' census read byte +2 of the MASTER row, which is a pointer byte. Rule: take the RIGHT hand's item back to the bag when the right hand is occupied (line 24081 `bnez`), otherwise the LEFT hand's (line 24085), and when both are empty take nothing (line 24086's delay slot `move_ $a1, $zr` zeroes $a1 so line 24088 jumps past the removal, so no phantom item-0 byte moves). The equip side writes only record+0x3C4 and +0x3C6 (lines 24167/24169) and returns, so a two-hander put into the head or an accessory slot empties that slot and fills nothing.

write_card_sector is a bare BIOS trampoline (bios_jump 0xb0,0x4e), and the only wrapper around it visible at this address is a 1-sector, sector-0x3f, offset-0 write with no game-specific buffer construction in view.

A wrapper function F0x8003da4c calls write_card_sector with a1=0x3f (sector) and a2=0 (offset), taking only the sector-relative buffer pointer in a0 from its caller; no roster/ledger-shaped struct is visible at this call site.

F0x8002b41c writes a1[i][j] = a0[j][i] for all nine elements - a matrix TRANSPOSE. For the rotation of the shot's frame that is its inverse, which is why the view builder pairs it with a negated rotated translation to form a true rigid inverse.

F0x8002ac9c takes the absolute value of its argument and masks it to 0xfff before the table lookup - an EVEN function over a 4096-unit period, i.e. cosine. Its odd counterpart F0x8002abcc (which negates the result for a negative argument, .L0x8002abf4) is sine.
F0x8002abcc negates its result for a negative argument, making it the ODD function of the pair - sine.

F0x8003171c is a caller of both F0x800340ec and F0x800349cc: it reads the whole 0x18-byte record via the getter into a stack copy, overwrites only the first byte field (unk0) with (s8)argC, then writes the whole record back via the setter -- a read-modify-write single-field update. Audio initialization zeroes the phase, requests bank 0/slot 1, and loops while the phase poll is nonzero, ticking the resource bank and audio phase machine each iteration.

The loader dispatches exactly on phase 1, 2, or 3. Phases 1 and 2 return without advancing while the resource-bank busy method is nonzero, then increment the phase after completing their stage. Phase 3 returns while its sound-driver predicate is zero, installs the tone entries when ready, and clears the phase to zero.

The poll returns whether D0x80055c40 is nonzero. The bank-request routine tears down the previous bank, writes literal 0x1 as the first phase, records the requested bank/table entry, and starts the first resource request.

F0x8001e5bc allocates two ordering-table word arrays at object +0x5c/+0x60 and installs F0x8001dfa8 at object method +0x138. That complete method selects one array using D0x8004de44, shifts the bucket index by 0x2, and returns the resulting word address without a bounds branch.
The screen-dim caller resolves a view and bucket, gets the current packet cursor, fills and ordering-table-links a 0x20-byte primitive, and only then publishes cursor+0x20 through +0x15c.

Frame-buffer setup allocates two packet buffers, selects one into display-service +0x20 at D0x8004de30, +0x158 returns that word without modifying it, and +0x15c stores its sole argument back to the same word without any test.
The shipped static data resolves display-service +0x158 to F0x8001d844, +0x15c to F0x8001d854, +0x16c to F0x8001dbe0, and +0x17c to F0x8001da84.

It dispatches to whatever is queued against the entity rather than performing a hard-coded push.

F0x8008ed2c is a per-tick method on the entity's own linked sub-record array (indexed via self+0x8, a counter incremented modulo 0x40): each call clears three fields (+0xc/+0x10/+0x14) of the current sub-record, advances the counter, copies the PRIOR sub-record's +0xc field into self+0x50, and if a queued caller-mode (self+0x10 == 3) exists calls that entity's own +0x2c interact callback with mode 3 before, at counter wrap, zeroing every sub-record and self+0x108 itself. evidence.summary: A representative call site: the caller passes a routine address and an object size, then stamps a flag word at +0x54, a kind at +0x58 and its own argument at +0x50.

The shared actor factory F0x800143dc stores its first argument into the new object at +0x48, which is why the stage constructors' varying first argument is the actor's own per-stage entry point rather than a data table.
The factory saves its first argument before shifting the remaining arguments down, so argument one is the caller-supplied routine and not the size.
That saved first argument is written into the new object at offset +0x48.

The one harvested callback address that the inventory does not list as a function start nevertheless opens a stack frame there, so it is a function start the boundary recovery missed rather than a counter-example.
The three-argument entry to the shared actor factory is a wrapper: it zeroes the fourth argument in the delay slot of its tail call, so a caller that omits the class gets class 0.
Prior research (DigimonProfile, 0x58 stride): the species profile carries per-level growth rates for hp, mp, str, def, spt, wis, spd and chr, which is the only identified origin of charisma change.

evidence.summary: The type-0x16 FIELDCOM sparkle actor has no stop condition: every animation program is an infinite loop, and no code in the EXE or any pro overlay ever sets its state inert or suspends it. Its only gates are creation-side and owner-side.
evidence.exact: (1) Script bytes read from the fieldstg data blob: program 0 at file 0x149e0 = 23 08 24 08 25 08 26 08 ff 00 (jump to pair 0); program 3 at file 0x14a30 = 24 flourish pairs then 23 08 24 08 25 08 26 08 ff 18 (jump to pair 0x18 = 24 = that idle tail). The pointer table 0x8009771c sits at file 0x14a6c, confirming base 0x80082cb0. 0xff is the only control byte and is an unconditional jump, so no program can terminate; program 0, the actor's default, is itself an infinite idle-sparkle loop. (2) The tick at file 0x6f2c has exactly three non-drawing exits: own state +0xc in {2,3} (0x6f5c), owner +0x50 NULL (0x6fec), owner state +0xc != 1 (0x6ffc). Everything from 0x7000 to the draw at 0x7254 is unconditional. Its only state write is advState at 0x6f64 (0 -> 1), unreachable thereafter. (3) The eight shared methods copied into every object by F0x800143dc are fns.s L4740-4791: +0x28 setState(n) {+0xc=n, +0x10/14/18=0}, +0x2c setSub1(n), +0x30 setSub2, +0x34 setSub3, +0x38 advState, +0x3c advSub1, +0x40 advSub2, +0x44 advSub3. The object tick driver at 0x80018164 calls cb(obj, [obj+0x24]) at 0x800181a8, so the callback's a1 is the extra block, and it honours a suspend field +0x1c. (4) Writer census, exhaustive: scanning every ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003/pro/*.s for 'li $a0,0x16' followed within 8 instructions by a load of D0x8004b7bc yields exactly one site, fieldstg 0x0bac; the EXE has exactly one, F0x80015d4c at fns.s L6446. Both call slot +0x2c (setSub1) only - op 0x50 with 3, fieldstg 0x800837ec with 1, 2 or 3 for notify ids 0x338, 0x339, 0x34a, with no branch passing 0. fieldstg 0x800837ec has no jal or j reference and is not materialized as a pointer in code; it appears once in the data blob at file 0x187dc as the third word of the {id=0x32d, ctor=0x80083cd8, notify=0x800837ec} triple in the object type table, so its a1 is a type id in that table's space. (5) The other route to the object, charObj->extra[0] (written once at 0xe380, sw $v0,($s1)), is never read back: the mode dispatcher 0xd220 takes the extra block in $s5 and touches only +0x4, +0x8 and +0xc, and no bare ($s5) load exists in the overlay. The sibling child actor at extra[+0x4] does receive setState(2) at 0xddbc after a 0x3c-unit timer on the char's +0x18, which is the shape an off switch takes in this codebase; the sparkle has no such site. No setState (+0x28), advState (+0x38) or +0x1c write anywhere targets the type-0x16 object. (6) Lifetime gates only: the ctor at 0x7274 refuses unless [0x8004b438]() < 0x2d7, and the call site at 0xe378 is gated on the owning type-5 character's +0x8 == 0; the char ctor at 0xe4bc stores +0x4 = charId (0xe5e4) and +0x8 = index (0xe5e8), and 0x80090e70 (file 0xe1c0) iterates exactly 3 type-5 characters, so index 0 is the player.

Because program 0 is also an infinite idle loop and all four idle frames (0x23-0x26) are opaque 16x16 sprites at dy=-36 in the extracted atlas, this static reading implies a permanent head sparkle on the player, which does not match play. Exactly one of the following must hold and none is decoded: the owner character leaves state +0xc == 1 during ordinary field movement; [0x8004b438]() < 0x2d7 excludes ordinary field screens so the actor usually does not exist; or the draw at 0x7254 is culled downstream by the sprite interface built at F0x8001f648. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Extract the STAGSLCT gate/area-travel destination table.

Decode source: ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003/pro/stagslct.s (RAM base 0x80082cb0).

`stagslct` is the free-roam "travel to a discovered area" menu. Static
disasm (stagslct.s L2620-2637, RAM 0x80082ed0-0x80082ee0) shows the row-
select handler doing:

    lw   v1, 0x54($s3)          # cursor row
    lw   a0, 0x50($s3)          # scroll offset
    lui  v0, 0x8008 ; addiu v0, 0x5eec   # v0 = table base 0x80085eec
    addu v1, a0 ; sll v1, 4 ; addu v1, v0   # v1 = &table[cursor+scroll]
    lw   a0, 8(v1)               # a0 = row "type" field (+8)
    ...
    lw   v1, 0xc(v1)             # v1 = row "value" field (+0xc)
    lui  v0, 0x8005
    j    0x800855d4              # tail-call: resident transition trampoline
    sw   v1, -0x4c90(v0)         # [0x8004b370] = v1  (MASTER STORY ORDINAL)

0x8004b370 is the same master story-progress ordinal documented in
field-script-engine-verified.md WS4.6 (each story beat's overlay writes its
own value there on completion; fieldstg's 35-entry dispatch table switches
on it). stagslct writing a *screen id* there and tail-calling the same
resident transition trampoline (0x800855d4) used by ordinary story
handoffs is the concrete proof this screen is a "pick a destination, warp
there" gate-travel menu, not a data/debug screen.

The destination table at RAM 0x80085eec (file offset 0x323c) packs two
record shapes back-to-back with no fixed stride (16-byte "primary" rows
{ptr,ptr,type,val} for base stage screens 0x200-0x26f and top-level
category rows, immediately followed by compact 12-byte "variant" rows
{ptr,type,val=0} for story-variant screens 0x270+) -- m2c could not
decompile this overlay (every entry the auto-splitter found was a spurious
"function" carved out of this data table, see stagslct_c/_failures.txt:
256/256 fail), so there is no clean struct decompile to lean on. This
extractor instead re-derives every record with a stride-independent scan:
any word in [0x200,0x2ee] (a valid FIELDSTG screen id, per
data/screen_table.json's own SCREEN_MIN/MAX) or in the fixed top-level
CATEGORY_TYPES set found by inspection is a "type" field; the following
word is kept as "val" when it looks like a small in-table index (<0x100),
else val=0. Verified against data/screen_table.json: this recovers
exactly 239 screen-id rows with ZERO duplicates, matching that file's
screen count 1:1 -- i.e. the table enumerates literally every warpable
FIELDSTG screen in the game, exactly what a "travel anywhere" gate menu
needs.

CATEGORY_TYPES (31 rows, 13 distinct top-level type tags plus two
sub-indexed groups: 0xf00 x{0,1,2,3,4,0x1c,0x1e} and 0xa00 x{0..7}) are the
higher-level menu the 239 destinations are presumably grouped under. Their
semantic meaning (which real-world "sector" each tag names) is NOT
resolved -- no string table or pack was found anywhere in stagslct.s (no
`lui $a0, 0x<pack-hi>` screen-pack load at all, and no lang_file/*.toml
named after this overlay exists), so this script emits the raw type/val
pairs only. See docs/research/ui/stagslct-decoded-2026-07-11.md "Open
gaps" for what remains unproven.

Output: web/assets/data/stagslct_ui.json
"""

import re
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).parent.parent
DDW3 = Path.home() / "ddw3"
STAGSLCT_S = DDW3 / "asm/dw2003/pro/stagslct.s"
SCREEN_TABLE = ROOT / "web/assets/data/screen_table.json"
STAGE_NAMES = ROOT / "data/stage_names.json"

The compared value is loaded unsigned from the same byte the store writes back, which is what makes this a saturating counter rather than an unrelated threshold.
When the compare fails the store is branched over, so the byte is left unchanged.
The branch delay slot forms counter+1; it executes on both paths but only the fall-through stores it.
The incremented value is stored back as a single byte at +0xC of the per-element record.

Targeting kind 0x7F asks the zone accessor about side 0's hand (zone 2). The AI's legality gate calls this function, so evaluating a card that targets the opponent's hand inspects the human player's concealed hand. The sibling cases 0x72 at L58 and 0x80 do the same for side 0's deck and trash.
The combo scan of the first side raises banner 0x19 for each run it finds.
The second side's scan raises a different banner, 0x1A, so the two sides' combo announcements are distinguishable on screen.
Each banner id is written to the pending-message latch duel+0x421 rather than drawn directly.
A third banner, 0x1B, is raised while a counter at duel+0x304 is non-zero, once per unit of duel+0x305, which is decremented each pass.
The tick count accumulates into duel+0x2FC, the same counter the machine's other timed states use.
It then creates an overlay whose three colour arguments are all 0x80, a mid grey, passed as $a1 and copied into $a2 and $a3.
That overlay is given a life of 10, passed as the stack argument.
The roll itself runs while its accumulated tick count is below 0x33, fifty-one ticks of the resident frame delta.
The counter roll opens by playing a packed sound whose high half is 0x009C.
Its low half, in the play-sound call's delay slot, completing the packed id 0x009C0002.
The fall-through - side 1 strictly lower - writes 0 to the set winner duel+0x301.
The taken branch, reached when side 1's total is not strictly lower, writes 1 instead. Equal totals therefore go to side 1.
That path's banner is 0x17, distinct from the 0x18 the other path keeps.
The comparison is set-less-than of side 1's total against side 0's, so it is true only when side 1 has strictly less HP.
The branch on that comparison, whose delay slot loads banner 0x18 and therefore runs on both paths; only the fall-through keeps it.
And side 1's from duel+0x666, the same field in the other per-player block.
The set is awarded on total HP: side 0's total is loaded from duel+0x59E.
Mode 3 stores duel+0x2F5 = 0 when the selector result duel+0x440 is zero, and 1 otherwise, at the two adjacent store sites.
F0x8009D9E4 begins its admitted-run scan at duel+0x668, the opponent's deck read cursor, not at slot 0.
The scan stores the slot index it stopped on into duel+0x41B.
F0x8009D9E4's downward scan compares each slot's group byte against the constant 7, walking from slot 0x27, and stores where the trailing run of 7s begins into duel+0x41C.
The driver clears duel+0x4dd on the step before it starts a card's program, so the flag is per-program rather than per-turn.
The value that loop writes is the constant 7, loaded once into $t3 before the loop.
The retirement loop writes $t3 into the group byte of the slot it has rotated to index duel[0x41C]-1.
The decremented deck read cursor is stored back to block+0x04 before it is turned into the destination halfword index.
The deck count block+0x08 is read and, in the loop's branch delay slot, stored back raised by one for each card returned.
The raised deck count is stored to block+0x08 in the loop's branch delay slot, so it runs on every pass including the last.
The hand-return loop decrements the deck read cursor block+0x04 by one; the next instruction decrements the hand count block+0x0A by one, so the two walk together.
The hand count is decremented alongside the deck read cursor, so the source index and the destination index step together.
The decremented hand count is stored back to block+0x0A, which is also the loop's own termination test.

The extractor's own layout section documents +0x20 as the zone-group selector record {u32 tag; u32 key; u32 zero; ZoneBlock *zone[4]} decoded 2026-07-27, whose literal shape {0x83,0,0,ptr*4} is what an earlier reading of wstag200 had labelled a tile-animation master block.

In the field entity constructor, +0x28 is read twice: once with an index scaled by 16 added to it (`sll $s1, $s1, 4` / `addiu $s1, $s1, 0x20` / `addu $v0, $v0, $s1` at file 0x00e620-0x00e638, stored to entity +0x6c) and once unscaled (stored to entity +0x70). A base plus index*0x10 addressing pattern establishes +0x28 as an ARRAY of 0x10-byte records, matching the VRAM texture-slot array decoded for the character drop shadow on 2026-07-27.

Record halfwords +0x1c and +0x1e are loaded into $a0/$a1 immediately before this call (file 0x0034dc/0x0034e0) and the 16-bit result is stored into the primitive's CLUT field, identifying the pair as a CLUT x/y and the callee as the PSX GetClut. Together with the tpage pair this makes the record a VRAM texture-slot descriptor.

Called with $a0=0, $a1=1 (file 0x0034f4/0x0034f8) and $a2/$a3 = record halfwords +0x10/+0x12 (file 0x003530/0x003534): the PSX GetTPage(tp, abr, x, y). The enclosing loop runs exactly four times (`slti $v0, $s4, 4` at file 0x003584) and hardcodes width and height to 0x40 (file 0x0034c4-0x0034cc), so the builder emits four 64x64 SPRTs forming one fixed 128x128 block, not a tiling background layer.

Inside the sprite builder whose entry is file 0x000033b0 (ram 0x80086060), scene descriptor field +0x28 is loaded through $s6, which the entry established as 0x80099D80 via `lui $v0, 0x800a` + `addiu $s6, $v0, -0x6280` at file 0x00343c/0x003440. The loaded pointer is then dereferenced for texture parameters, so +0x28 is a pointer to a texture descriptor, not inline quad data.

The byte at record +0x18 is read and stored as the SPRT u coordinate (`sb $v0, -2($s0)` at file 0x0034b4); record +0x1a supplies v the same way at file 0x0034c0/0x0034d0. Both are re-read unchanged from the record on every one of the loop's four iterations and no instruction in the loop adds an offset to either, which is what rules out a scrolling or cycling surface: the texture coordinates are constant for the life of the draw.

Immediately after the +0x10 and +0x14 registrars, scene init loads descriptor +0x4c and walks it as a null-terminated pointer array with stride 4 (file 0x008284-0x008294). Each element's halfword +0x8 is an entity type tested against 0x6a, 1 and the range 0x146-0x147 (file 0x008218-0x00824c), gated by an optional predicate function pointer at element +0x0, then instantiated through F0x8009116c. 281 of 294 stage overlays write this field and the walker has no consumer for it.

The store census that produced the published descriptor field map only records a store whose stored value the constant tracker already knows. This single condition is why three descriptor offsets are under-counted or missing entirely.

evidence.summary: Inside the DNA commit block (0x800984dc..0x800986f4), current HP (record offset +0x8, the documented current-HP field) of combatant s0 (the acting/source party or enemy record) is loaded and tested with blez; nonzero (alive) falls through, zero-or-negative (dead) branches to the shared exit label .L0x80098790, skipping the MP debit and fusion-commit code that follows.

Immediately after the s0 HP check, current HP (+0x8) of combatant s2 (the selected DNA partner record) is loaded and blez-tested the same way; a dead partner also branches to the same shared exit .L0x80098790, aborting the fusion before any MP is spent.

The technique's MP cost is fetched as a halfword from a per-technique cost table (base computed at L22294 from ctx+0x7c-1, i.e. the selected technique index) into $a0, immediately before the two MP-sufficiency checks below.

s0's MP is only decremented (subu then stored back to +0xc) after every HP/MP/ailment check above has been passed -- confirming the checked block gates MP expenditure and fusion commit, not merely a cosmetic/pre-check step.

s0's current MP (record offset +0xc, the documented current-MP field) is loaded, then slt compares it against the MP cost fetched in $a0; if current MP is less than the cost, bnez branches to the same shared exit .L0x80098790 -- s0 having insufficient MP aborts the DNA fusion.

Immediately after the s0 MP check, s2's (the partner's) current MP (+0xc) is loaded and slt/bnez-compared against the same fetched cost; insufficient partner MP branches to the same shared exit .L0x80098790.

Every refusal branch above (dead s0, dead s2, insufficient s0 MP, insufficient s2 MP, ailment 0x10/0x20 on either side, ailment 0x8 on s0) targets this single label, which unconditionally calls FIGHTSTG_F0x800979e4(ctx) with no argument distinguishing which condition fired.

evidence.summary: The exact probability mass function of the encounter step-counter reload, derived from the reload site rather than from the two runtime samples. The fold is a deterministic piecewise map that makes every value from 256 up exactly twice as likely as every value below 256, over the support 0..1279.
evidence.transcription: RELOAD SITE, transcribed: '.L0x0000f87c lui $v0, 0x8005' / '.L0x0000f880 lw $v0, -0x23f4($v0)' gives v0 = [0x8004dc0c], the resident rand() pointer; '.L0x0000f88c jalr $v0' produces r0 = rand(); '.L0x0000f894 lui $v1, 0x38e3' / '.L0x0000f898 ori $v1, 0x8e39' builds 0x38e38e39; '.L0x0000f89c mult $v0, $v1', '.L0x0000f8a0 sra $v1, $v0, 0x1f', '.L0x0000f8a4 mfhi $a1', '.L0x0000f8a8 sra $a0, $a1, 0x9', '.L0x0000f8ac subu $a0, $v1' give a0 = r0 / 2304 signed and truncating; '.L0x0000f8b0 sll $v1, $a0, 0x3', '.L0x0000f8b4 addu $v1, $a0', '.L0x0000f8b8 sll $v1, 0x8' give v1 = quotient * 9 * 256 = quotient * 2304; '.L0x0000f8bc subu $a0, $v0, $v1' gives r = r0 % 2304; '.L0x0000f8c0 slti $v0, $a0, 0x100' with '.L0x0000f8c4 beqz $v0, .L0x0000f8d4' selects the leg; '.L0x0000f8d0 sw $a0, -0x729c($v0)' stores counter = r when r < 256; otherwise '.L0x0000f8d4 addiu $v1, $a0, 0x100', '.L0x0000f8d8 srl $a0, $v1, 0x1f', '.L0x0000f8dc addu $v1, $a0', '.L0x0000f8e0 sra $v1, 0x1' and '.L0x0000f8e4 sw $v1, -0x729c($v0)' store counter = (r + 256) / 2 rounding toward zero. 0x80050000 - 0x729c = 0x80048d64, the counter; 0x38e38e39 = ceil(2^41 / 2304), so mfhi>>9 is the exact division by 2304. THE FOLD f(r) = r for 0 <= r <= 255, (r + 256) >> 1 for 256 <= r <= 2303. It is exactly 2-to-1 on the upper leg: the 2048 inputs 256..2303 map onto the 1024 outputs 256..1279, two inputs per output, with no gaps and no overlap into the lower leg. Support is exactly 0..1279, both endpoints attained (r=0 gives 0, r=2303 gives 1279). PMF ASSUMING rand() UNIFORM ON THE MODULUS: P(c) = 1/2304 for c in 0..255 and 2/2304 = 1/1152 for c in 256..1279; P(c <= 255) = 256/2304 = 1/9 exactly (11.11 percent); mean = 1604480/2304 = 696 + 7/18 = 696.3889; median = 703 (the CDF at 703 is 1152/2304, exactly one half); E[c^2] = 1390903680/2304 = 603690.833, variance = 118733.35, sd = 344.58. PMF IF rand() IS THE CONVENTIONAL 15-BIT GENERATOR (uniform on 0..32767): 32768 = 14*2304 + 512, so residues 0..511 occur 15 times and 512..2303 occur 14 times, giving weights 15/32768 for c in 0..255, 30/32768 for c in 256..383 and 28/32768 for c in 384..1279; then P(c <= 255) = 3840/32768 = 11.72 percent, mean = 22577152/32768 = 689 exactly, median = 694. The qualitative shape is identical; the modulo bias moves the mean by about 7. CONSISTENCY WITH THE ONLY TWO OBSERVED SAMPLES: 17 lies on the single-weight lower leg, 826 on the double-weight upper leg; both are inside 0..1279 and neither is excluded by the fold. Two samples cannot distinguish the two PMFs above and were never going to; the fold does. EXPIRY ARITHMETIC AT THE DRIVER: '.L0x0000faa4 lw $v0, 0x30($a0)' with $a0 = 0x80048d34 (built at .L0x0000fa78 and .L0x0000fa80 as lui 0x8005 / addiu -0x72cc), '.L0x0000faac subu $v0, $v1', '.L0x0000fab0 bgtz $v0, .L0x0000fadc' with '.L0x0000fab4 sw $v0, 0x30($a0)' in the delay slot -- the decremented value is stored unconditionally, and expiry is 'not greater than zero', not 'equal to zero', so the counter may end a cycle negative. On expiry the launcher F0x800925a8 runs only if [0x80042b1c] is set (.L0x0000fab8-.L0x0000facc) but the reload 'jal 0x8009252c' at .L0x0000fad4 is unconditional, so no reload is ever skipped and the cycle cannot drift. DERIVED WALKING DISTANCE, at 8 movement ticks per driver run: expected runs to expiry = E[ceil(c/rate)] approximately mean/rate + 0.5, i.e. about 233, 175, 117, 78 and 39 runs for rates 3, 4, 6, 9 and 18, i.e. about 1861, 1397, 933, 623 and 314 movement ticks of continuous walking. The runtime walk of 2026-07-26 measured inter-run gaps of exactly 8 frames under a held direction, so those tick counts are frame counts while walking.

evidence.transcription: MATCHERS AND RESULTS, corpus = original assembly ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003, 590,078 lines scanned by dw3-research code-search. '80048d64' returns 0 hits: the literal counter address occurs nowhere, because both materialization forms are base-relative -- exactly the trap that burned this frontier three times. '-0x729c\(' --regex returns 5 hits in 4 files: two are the reload's own stores (fieldstg L15931 and L15936); three are false positives, .word data lines in stgtrain.s, wstag865.s and wstag895.s whose disassembly comment happens to render as 'lb $t0, -0x729c($zr)'. '8009252c' returns 3 hits: one 'jal 0x8009252c' (fieldstg L16060, the driver's expiry path), one duplicate index row for the same line, and one unrelated fightstg label at the same RAM address in a different overlay. '-0x4964\(' --regex returns 0 hits, so the reload's function-pointer cell at 0x8009b69c is never loaded through a lui/lw pair and there is no indirect entry point in that form. So, within decidable forms, the counter is written by exactly the two reload stores plus the driver's own 'sw $v0, 0x30($a0)' decrement at fieldstg L16052, and the reload has exactly one caller. WHAT THIS CENSUS CANNOT DECIDE, stated so the negative is not over-read: a store to 0x80048d64 through a register-held base with offset 0x30, the same shape the route-pair writers used. 'sw \$[a-z0-9]+, 0x30\(\$' --regex returns 509 hits of 590,078 lines across 313 files, dominated by $sp frame stores, which is too broad to audit by text. evidence.exact: Static reads: every one of the 15 gating step records is {cond_a 0x0f, arg_a 0, cond_b 0xffff}; flag_setters.json lists exactly one writer of 0x0f (fieldstg, value 1 -- this handler); code-search '0x2404000f' (li $a0, 0xf) returns 3 of 590078 lines, two in cardgame.s and one at fieldstg 0x8008bf7c; no store lands in the byte of the bank-0 bitfield holding bit 15 (bank 0 resolves through F0x800165ac -> F0x800155d4 to the 12-byte field at 0x80048abc, below the API's own fn pointers at +0xc/+0x10). Those reads alone imply a single GLOBAL one-shot. Contradicted by play: Minotarumon attacks every time the player drops down into Protocol Ruins (user, 2026-07-28). Structural support for per-visit: s530 (Jungle Shrine) carries TWO patches reaching the same event, which a global one-shot makes pointless, and fourteen patches for one lifetime firing is not a mechanic. The walker therefore reproduces the gate and the set exactly and clears the latch on stage entry.
evidence.caveats: The clearing site in the original is UNLOCATED, not proven absent: neither an immediate-argument search nor a bitfield-store search can see a clear made through a computed register, and fightstg's battle-return path was not swept. Settling it needs either the writer found statically or a controlled capture that reads bit 15 of 0x80048abc across an area re-entry. Until then the latch SCOPE is authority-6 (play observation), while the gate and the set are authority-2.

evidence.locator: fieldstg F0x8008bf38 (file 0x9288-0x92ec) and its indexed twin F0x800927a0 (file 0xfaf0-0xfb48); battle setup F0x8008b798 (file 0x8ae8); EXE F0x800165ac -> F0x800155d4; per-stage pointer stored to scene_struct+0x20 by each stage init
evidence.summary: Fourteen stages mark a floor patch whose op-8 step starts an event handled by the RESIDENT fieldstg routine F0x8008bf38. The routine carries no enemy id: it reads slot 5 of the stage's rate-0 (scripted) encounter block via scene_struct+0x20 -> +0x18 -> +0x18 and hands that screen id to the ordinary battle-setup path, so the ambush is always a fight the game itself assigned to that area.
evidence.exact: F0x8008bf38: v0 = [0x80099da0] (scene_struct+0x20), v0 = [v0+0x18], a0 = [v0+0x18]; [0x80042b28] = [a0+4], [0x80042b30] = [a0+8], a0 = [a0]; jal F0x8008b798; then set_flag(0xf, 1) and return 0. F0x800927a0 is the same with a0 = [[P+0x18] + 4 + 4*index], so 0x18 = index 5. F0x8008b798 stores that screen id to [0x80042b2c] and indexes the global 0x1c-stride record table at 0x80094680 by it (sll 3 / subu / sll 2 = *28) -- the table already extracted to field_encounters.json. Read per stage, R = {screen_id, param, music_tag}; all fourteen give music_tag 0x60080000 and a single-Digimon party. Cross-checked against stage_encounters.json: every screen id is slot 5 of a rate_level-0 block (14/14). The Fire Dungeon's slot 0 in the same block is screen 20 = Meramon L45 / SkullMeramon L47 / BlueMeramon L50, exactly the Fire Knight team WALKTHROUGH_FULL.txt names as that floor's boss, confirming the block is the stage's scripted shelf and that slot 5 is not the boss. s949/s953 carry the same event with an empty slot 5 and no step reaching it; the structural sweep drops them.
evidence.caveats: No controlled runtime capture. The mechanic is recognised structurally (op-8 step whose event's native_fn is 0x8008bf38) rather than from a stage list, but every conclusion is a static read. The record's middle word (param, 3..24) is a battle type and is NOT decoded. The trigger grid's top-3-bit approach-facing group is not modelled by the walker.

evidence.locator: F0x8008f4b4/F0x8008f4c8/F0x8008f9c0; highest-numbered .bin clip directories in 179 sprite packs
evidence.summary: Field clip ids resolve through each sprite's directory; clip 1 is idle, clip 4 walk, and clip 5 run, with per-frame duration counters reset on clip changes.
evidence.exact: The clip latch writes actor+0xa0 and clears animation state including +0xcc/+0xd0/+0xe8. F0x8008f9c0 reloads when +0xa0 differs from previous clip +0xa4, selects one of five authored direction lists (right-side facings mirrored), and advances the list using its stored frame-duration timer. The statically decoded sprite directories map clip 1 to idle, clip 4 to walk, and clip 5 to run; the mapping and frame lists were validated across all 179 field sprite packs.
evidence.limitations: This establishes the SLES asset timing in native field ticks; it does not assert NTSC presentation timing.

evidence.summary: The original field helper queries the actor's typed TMPK byte and applies one of seven eight-direction signed 20.12 vector rows, including bit-0x10 slope mirroring.
evidence.limitations: High TMPK code bits other than 0x10 are not consumed by this movement helper and remain semantically unnamed.

evidence.exact: F0x800a606c: a0 = 0x800a5de4, a1 = 0x54, a2 = 0xc, jal 0x80014504. F0x800a5de4 phase 0 looks up actor (5, -1, 0), calls its method +0x2c with a1 = 1, plays packed 0x800410bd through [0x8004b8c8], then accumulates the frame delta into obj+0x18 until slti 0x1e fails. Per target it loads a2 = [0x800a6ad0 + 4*(phase-1)] = 2/4/8, looks up (5, -1, key), passes actor+0x58/+0x5c to F0x800a64bc, plays packed 0x800446c9, calls actor method +0x2c with a1 = 4, then a0 = 0x80048d34, v1 = [a0+0x70+4*i] (= [0x80048da4 + 4*i], the active-roster slot array), v0 = ((v1<<5 - v1)<<3 - v1)<<2 = v1*0x3dc, and sh $s3(=1), 0x788(v0 + a0). For i = 0 that address is 0x800494bc, the exact halfword the 2026-07-28 replay's write breakpoint caught at PC 0x800a5fc0 with old value 150, and the replay's three writes hit roster slots 0, 6 and 7 in that order. F0x800a64bc calls F0x80014504(0x800a6324, 0x6c, 0) and stores x/y to obj+0x54/+0x58. F0x800a6324 loops two components i = 0,1: cursor obj+0x5c+4i on program [0x800a6b30 + 4i], via F0x800a6194 with a2 = 0; return 0xff hides the component and increments the done count, 0x12c hides it only; the draw call passes a3 = obj+0x58 + (i ? 0x14 : -0xf0) and sp+0x10 = i; done == 2 calls obj->0x28 with a1 = 3. Programs read as {value, hold} u16 pairs: 0x800a6adc = {50,4}{51,4}{52,4}{53,4}{54,4}{55,4}{255,999}, 0x800a6af8 = {300,4}{56,4}..{67,4}{255,999}. F0x800a6194 is the 3-argument one-shot animator (a2 is a recursion flag, not a wrap flag): it returns 0xff at the terminator instead of wrapping, unlike wstag735's 4-argument variant. tools/extract_fire_traps.py recognises the controller structurally (0x54-byte type-0x0c allocation whose update contains the 0x788 store) and finds it in wstag740 and wstag741 and in no other overlay of the 321 scanned.

Behaviour with fewer than three walking Digimon is read from the actor-lookup beqz branch, not observed. The tail is unexplained: the replay restored control 31 frames after the last explosion, longer than a 30-tick wait at the capture's own 26-frames-per-30-ticks ratio, so the controller's destroy/release handshake is not modelled. The two effect components' blend/priority handling beyond the y-sort offset is not decoded.

evidence.locator: wstag740 on_complete stubs from RAM 0x800a659c, stride 0x2c, 16 of them; step program records 2..17 of stage 740; the same pair in wstag741
evidence.summary: Each fire-trap event's on_complete is a three-instruction stub that sets ONE flag, and that flag is exactly the flag its own step record requires to be clear. Every patch of trap floor is therefore one-shot and permanently spent once sprung.
evidence.exact: 0x800a659c: addiu $a0, $zero, 0x40aa; lui $v0, 0x8005; lw $v0, -0x7538($v0) (= [0x80048ac8], the set_flag slot otherwise reached as flagapi+0xc); jalr; addiu $a1, $zero, 1. The next 15 stubs repeat at stride 0x2c with a0 = 0x40ab..0x40b9. Stage 740's step records 2..17 are op 8 with params[0] = 9000..9015 and cond_a = 0x40aa..0x40b9, arg_a = 0 (get_flag(cond,0) passes only while the flag is CLEAR), cond_b = 0xffff. wstag741 is the same shape on 0x40ba..0x40c9. tools/extract_fire_traps.py cross-checks gate against on_complete per region and refuses to write output on a mismatch: 32 of 32 agree, and within a stage all 16 flags are distinct.
evidence.caveats: Static only: no replay re-entered a sprung patch, so 'permanently spent' rests on the get_flag polarity documented in field-script-engine-verified.md SS-WS4.7 rather than on observation. Corroborated at authority 6 by npm run verify:fire-trap, which springs the traced patch in the browser and then walks the same cell again with no effect.

evidence.summary: Field-script FN6A/FN6B configure the resident type-0x10 field camera controller; mode 1 snaps/follows and mode 0 pans.
evidence.exact: FN6A stores mode at controller+0x80 and actor id at +0x84, then sets target kind +0x10 to 0. FN6B stores mode at +0x80 and x/y at +0x88/+0x8c, then sets target kind +0x10 to 1. F0x8008d998 resolves kind 0 through the type-5 actor lookup and kind 1 from +0x88/+0x8c. When mode is zero it enters the +0x14=1 easing path; nonzero mode uses the exact target. F0x8008d788 subtracts the 160x140 view center, clamps x/y against field width-320 and height-240, and calls the camera object's +0x120 position setter with x/y shifted by 8. The callback chain contains no sprite, clip, point-table, GPU, or draw call. The signed globals are 0x8004b7bc and base 0x8004b610, not the previously reported 0x8005 addresses.
evidence.limitations: The controller behavior is generic and statically complete. Browser interpolation uses a time-based approximation for the native integer easing curve rather than a bit-exact fixed-point port.

evidence.locator: fieldstg 0x800882c4-0x800882e4 (file 0x5614-0x5634); dispatch 0x8008849c; F0x8008f0a4 at 0x8008f0b8-0x8008f0d8; story_trigger_grids stages 735/736; story_steps op 11/12
evidence.summary: The type-7 trigger cell's low 5 bits select the step-program record and its high 3 bits are the opcode argument, which op 11 passes through as the ice-slide glide facing; ops 11/12 exist only in stages 735 and 736.
evidence.exact: At 0x800882c4 the step VM masks the grid byte to 8 bits, and at 0x800882d0-0x800882e4 splits it: `srl $v0,$v1,5` then `sw $v0,0x60($s0)` stores the high 3 bits at controller+0x60, and `andi $v1,$v1,0x1f` then `sw $v1,0x5c($s0)` stores the low 5 bits at controller+0x5c before scaling that index by the 24-byte record stride. Op 11's dispatch at 0x8008849c loads `$a0 = [s0+0x58]` (the leader actor) and `$a1 = [s0+0x60]`, and F0x8008f0a4 stores that argument at actor+0x60 (the facing) at 0x8008f0d8. Over the extracted step programs, op 11 and op 12 each occur exactly twice in the whole game, in stages 735 and 736 only. Each of those stages' trigger grids (cell 32, 44x28) carries 35 cells whose record is op 11 and 33 whose record is op 12; the op-11 cells' high bits take only the values 1, 3, 5 and 7, the four diagonal facings. The controlled capture entered at tile (29,7), whose cell byte has high bits 1, and the actor's facing became 1 (down-left) on that frame.
evidence.limitations: Cell-to-facing transfer is established statically plus one matching runtime cell; the remaining 34 op-11 cells were not individually runtime-sampled. The mode-0x50 recovery gate actor+0x14 == 0x1e corresponds to 25 PAL field ticks in the capture because +0x14 advances about 1.2 units per vsync; what drives +0x14 at that rate is unidentified.

evidence.locator: wstag735 pad callback F0x800a620c state-1 branch 0x800a62a4-0x800a62d0 and state-2 branch 0x800a630c-0x800a6390; idle script RAM 0x800a6854; animator F0x800a5f40 one-shot branch 0x800a5fe0-0x800a6028; draw callback F0x800a6060 0x800a6068-0x800a60ec; EXE F0x8001f648 (ctx method table), F0x8001ecec (fns.s L16332-L16334), F0x8001ed6c CLUT expression (exe-decomp/c/F0x8001ed6c.c L174, L259)
evidence.summary: A type-0x17 launch pad runs a SECOND, looping animator script from the moment its stage builds it. Its value lands in obj+0x66, which the pad's draw hands to the draw context's method +0x88 = EXE F0x8001ecec -> ctx+0x20, the value F0x8001ed6c ADDS TO THE SPRITE'S CLUT ROW. The idle value is therefore a palette-row offset on the pad's floor disc, not a clip id: an untouched pad cycles its disc through three palettes, 88 ticks a cycle. The disc's hue is its own record's clipBase, so pads come in red, green and blue.
evidence.exact: wstag735 0x800a62a4: a0 = obj+0x60, a1 = 0x800a6854, a2 = 0 (one-shot flag), a3 = 0, jal F0x800a5f40, delay slot sh (lhu obj+0x50) -> obj+0x64; the animator's return is stored to obj+0x66 at 0x800a62d0. State 2 (0x800a630c) first stores 0 to obj+0x60 and reloads obj+0x62 from [0x800a6856] (entry 0's hold), then runs the SAME idle script (0x800a6350, a2 = 0) into obj+0x66 and only then the strobe script at 0x800a686c on cursor obj+0x5c with a2 = 1, into obj+0x68 = obj+0x50 + value. In F0x800a5f40 the a2 = 0 path at 0x800a6000-0x800a6028 answers the 0xff terminator by storing 0 to the cursor index, adding script[0].hold and recursing, so an a2 = 0 script never ends; the a2 = 1 path at 0x800a5fe8-0x800a5ffc returns 0xff instead. Draw F0x800a6060 computes s3 = a0 + 0x64 + (a2 << 2), calls ctx method [sp+0x98] with lh 2($s3) and then [sp+0x94] with (pack, lh 0($s3), x, y); the ctx built by F0x8001f648 at sp+0x10 puts unk88 = F0x8001ecec at sp+0x98, and F0x8001ecec is 'lw $v0, 0x1c0($gp); sw $a0, 0x20($v0)'. F0x8001ed6c reads it once: clutId = ((clutY + ctx->unk20) << 6) | ((clutX >> 4) & 0x3f). Idle script bytes at 0x800a6854: 00060000 00060001 00440002 00040001 00040000 000000ff = {0,6}{1,6}{2,68}{1,4}{0,4}{0xff,0}, 88 ticks. All ten launch-pad overlays carry a byte-identical idle and strobe pair (tools/extract_launch_pads.py reads each stage's callback and both scripts by simulating the ctor's $a0 and discriminating the animator calls on their a2 argument; idle addresses 0x800a8418/0x800a6854/0x800a6878/0x800a6ccc/0x800a6ca0/0x800a7268/0x800a7730/0x800a74dc/0x800a6d50/0x800a71dc). Cut from the discs, rows +0/+1/+2 are a brightness ramp of one hue whose peak channels are (96,0,0)(168,32,0)(248,72,0) for clipBase 20/44 = red, (0,0,80)(0,32,104)(0,64,128) for 28/52/68 = blue, and (0,48,0)(0,64,0)(0,80,0) for 36/60 = green.
evidence.caveats: obj+0x6a (the strobe column's CLUT field) is never written by the pad, so the column is assumed to draw on row 0 on the strength of the allocator zeroing the 0x6c-byte object; that zeroing was not read. No runtime capture was taken for this decode - the 2026-07-28 s735 capture predates it and did not sample obj+0x66. Corroboration is a headless render check (npm run verify:launchpad, authority 6): on the live canvas the s735 disc cycles exactly 3 colours with run lengths 68/4/10/6 repeating, the 68-tick hold on the brightest row, against a static empty-floor control.

evidence.locator: F0x8008fed0 action-mode jump-table entry 0x4c (file 0x0a10) to 0x800900e4-0x80090188; F0x80092da0; slot-3 RAM 0x8009b710=0x80092da0
evidence.summary: Field actor action mode 0x4c latches clip 1 and applies a flat-facing slide vector while reducing actor+0x68 by eight per update.
evidence.exact: Jump-table entry 0x4c dispatches to 0x800900e4. At 0x800900e4-0x8009011c, that handler latches clip 1 and enters the actor animation callback. evidence.summary: Full re-read of the bobber tick against the generic vtable it dispatches through. +0x5c is a meter that OSCILLATES between 0 and 0x3000 with +0x64 as its direction bit (not a one-way progress accumulator with a bite flag). The strike is pad bit 0x2000 (CIRCLE), read only in phase 1 sub-state 0; on the press rand()&3 selects a brake of 0x10 (3 cases in 4) or 4 (1 in 4), which decays the 0x100 speed to zero while the marker keeps travelling. When it stops, sub-state 3 samples a 2-bit band from the pattern track at [0x80097b14][pattern] indexed by meter>>8, holds 0x3c ticks, and then dispatches on that band: 1 and 2 call [0x8009b6a4] = F0x800927a0 with slot index 4 and 7 respectively and set mode 2; 0 sets mode 3 and ends the cast with nothing. F0x800927a0 reads the stage's scripted (rate-0) encounter block, rec = [[scene+0x20]+0x18] + 4 + 4*slot, copies rec+4/rec+8 into the battle globals at 0x80042b1c+0xc/+0x14 and passes rec+0 to F0x8008b798 -- the same block and the same battle-setup path the ambush tiles use at fixed slot 5. The catch is therefore a BATTLE, and no item or flag write exists on any branch.

The first builder ORs the GPU command byte 0xE3 into the top of its result word.
The vertical coordinate is masked to 10 bits and shifted left by 10, so X occupies bits 0-9 and Y bits 10-19 of the command word.

F0x80013e5c(id): looks up a slot via F0x800139fc(id). If found and the state halfword at +0x0 equals 3 (delay slot after 'bne' loads hi(D0x80044b04) but the taken path recomputes v0 to D0x8004de10+0x62*4), it calls the poll-clock, stores the return at slot+0x8, loads slot+0xC into v0 and returns immediately (jumps past the spin loop). Otherwise (not found, or found but state!=3), s0 is set to D0x80044b04 and the function spins: it calls the function pointer at D0x80044b04+0x2c and loops (bnez v0, back to the same call) while that call returns nonzero. Once it returns 0, it calls F0x80013e20(id), then re-resolves the slot via F0x800139fc(id) and returns slot+0xC.

F0x80013cdc's per-slot body (within the outer routine that first checks the D0x80044b38 dirty flag and a D0x80044b04+0x2c poll before entering this loop, per already-recorded evidence). It skips a slot whose owner (-0x4(s0), i.e. slot+0x4) is zero. If state==1 ('requested') and no other slot was already serviced this pass (bnez s4 skip), it calls the dispatch function at s8(=D0x80044b04)+0x30 with a0=owner, a3=slot+0x8, sets state(+0x0)=2, then falls into the shared tail that calls the function at D0x8004de10+0x188 and stores its return at slot+0x8. If state==2 ('dispatched'), it sets state=3 ('ready') and falls into the same shared tail (call D0x8004de10+0x188, store at slot+0x8). The loop bound is slti v0,s2,0x40 with stride 0x10, confirming the 64-entry, 0x10-stride table independently of F0x80013adc's loop.

F0x80013be4 calls F0x80013adc to select the eviction victim, releases the resource at the victim's slot+0xC through the function pointer D0x8004b5ec (a0=slot+0xC), then zeroes slot+0x4, slot+0xC, slot+0x8, the halfword at slot+0x2, and the halfword at slot+0x0, resetting the slot to the free state.

The per-slot body of F0x80013adc's 64-entry scan loop. A slot is skipped unless owner(+0x4) is nonzero AND state(+0x0)==3 (li v0,3; lh v1,(s1); bne skip). Among eligible slots it keeps the running-minimum tick at +0x8 (slt v0,s2,v1 skips if the candidate tick s2 is already smaller; bne s2,v1 branches around a tie-break call through D0x80048740+0x4 when ticks are equal; otherwise it calls the same D0x80048740+0x4 function, updates s5=candidate slot pointer, s4=its return value, s2=the new minimum tick from slot+0x8). The loop bound is slti v0,s3,0x40 and the stride is addiu s0,0x10 / addiu s1,0x10, and the function returns s5 (move v0,s5).

evidence.summary: F0x80013a6c(id): looks up a slot via F0x800139fc(id). If found, calls the poll-clock at D0x8004de10+0x62*4, stores the result at slot+0x8, then compares the state halfword at slot+0x0 to 3: the delay slot after the 'bne' sets v0=1 unconditionally, so a taken branch (state!=3) returns with v0=1, while the not-taken fallthrough (state==3) reaches an unconditional 'j' whose delay slot sets v0=0, so it returns 0. evidence.summary: F0x80013c30(id): looks up a slot via F0x800139fc(id). If found (s0 nonzero), it calls the poll-clock function at D0x8004de10+0x62*4 and stores the return at slot+0x8 (the LRU tick) with no read or write of the state field, then returns. If not found, it allocates a slot via F0x80013a34, sets slot+0x4=id, sets slot+0x0 (state, halfword) to 1, sets slot+0x8 and slot+0x2 (halfword) to 0, computes D0x80048744(id) and shifts the result left 0xb (0x800), passes that with the constant 3 to D0x8004b5f4 and stores its return at slot+0xC, and sets the global D0x80044b38 to 1.

F0x80013e5c takes an id in a0, passes it to F0x800139fc, and tests the returned pointer: a null result, or a halfword at +0x00 that is not 3, both branch to a path that spins on a poll called through +0x2c of D0x80044b04 until it returns zero. On the non-branching path it calls the routine held at D0x8004de10+0x188, stores that result into +0x08 of the record, and returns the word at +0x0c. So the value this routine returns is a field of a per-id record that is only read when the record's state halfword is 3, and the caller F0x800140d8 uses that value as a base to index from.

evidence.summary: The value domain of the route pair is fixed by its only predicate consumer. 0x80048d78 is meaningful only for values 1..30 and 0x80048d7a only for values 1..0x1e2; 0 on either scalar makes every bank-0x7E equality predicate on that scalar false, which is what makes the unconditional store of a (0,0) record a genuine clear.
evidence.transcription: F0x800160a8(a0 = bank-0x7E index, a1 = expected polarity), read verbatim: '.L0x800160a8 move_ $a2, $a0'; '.L0x800160ac slti $v0, $a2, 0x1e' (SIGNED compare, index < 30); '.L0x800160b0 beqz $v0, .L0x800160f0'; '.L0x800160b8 beqz $a1, .L0x800160d8'; '.L0x800160bc lui $v0, %hi(D0x80048d78)'; '.L0x800160c0 lhu $v1, %lo(D0x80048d78)($v0)'; '.L0x800160c4 addiu $v0, $a2, 0x1'; '.L0x800160c8 bne $v1, $v0, ...' returning 1 on equal and 0 otherwise. For index >= 0x1e, .L0x800160f0-.L0x8001610c load D0x80048d7a and compare against (index - 0x1d). Both scalars are read with lhu, i.e. they are unsigned 16-bit. a1 is pure polarity: nonzero selects the equality test, zero selects the inequality test; the two arms are otherwise identical. CONSEQUENCES FOR THE DOMAIN: index 0..0x1d addresses key values 1..30 exactly; index >= 0x1e addresses companion values index-0x1d, so with the bank index masked to 0x1ff by the dispatcher F0x800163b0 the companion is addressable up to 0x1e2. Key value 0 (and companion value 0) is addressed by NO index. This is the code-side bound; the tighter shipped-data bound (ids 0x7E00-0x7E25, i.e. 30 key slots plus 8 companion slots) is already recorded at authority 4 in the route-pair evidence and is not re-derived here. CROSS-CHECK AGAINST THE OBSERVED KEYS: the group keys and entry-warp keys already extracted for family-B stages (s825 1,2,7,8,11,12,17,18; s835 up to 19; s840 up to 19) all lie inside 1..30, i.e. inside the only domain this consumer can address.

WITHDRAWAL: the recorded conclusion 'the maze tables are built at runtime, so one legitimate in-game transition must be dumped' rested on the 2026-07-09 rig harvest, which read s845's live table as two exits to s850 that are absent from its static image. That harvest was ALREADY SUPERSEDED inside this repo by the 2026-07-10 ordinal-45 re-harvest recorded in docs/todo/2026-07-09-self-warp-maze-wiring.md, which re-read all 15 underground screens at ordinal 45 and states 'every live exit table contains ONLY the same self-records as the static overlays' and explicitly FALSIFIES the patching hypothesis. The static read here matches those live tables record-for-record: s865 (744,576,208,d4)+(744,176,360,d1); s870 (745,176,248,d4)+(745,576,240,d5); s875 (746,224,512,d1); s880 (747,576,160,d5); s890 (749,928,128,d5)+(749,848,504,d1)+(749,224,192,d1); s895 (750,928,416,d5)+(750,304,200,d5)+(750,224,576,d1); and s885, which the 2026-07-09 harvest failed to capture, reads (748,944,120,d5)+(748,240,472,d1). WHAT THE CENSUS SHOWS: screens 744 and 745 receive 49 and 36 keyed op-9 warps from surface stages -- 44 and 32 DISTINCT route pairs -- every one arriving at the same coordinates ((176,248) for 745), so the pair, not the coordinate, is what differs between entrances; screens 736/737/738/739/741 receive 17/6/24/14/11 op-10 warps. Screens 742, 743, 746, 747, 748, 749 and 750 receive NO keyed warp from any of the 282 programs; the only records targeting them are their own self-warps, which carry params[5]=params[6]=0. RE-STATED OPEN QUESTION: not 'what is in the deep maps' tables' (known) but 'what sets a NONZERO route pair on screens 746-750', given that their NPCs are gated on 8/18/8/19/21 distinct nonzero pairs each and the only warp that targets them clears the pair. NUMERIC FINGERPRINT for the leading candidate -- that a dive resolves screen 744/745 to one of the seven circuit stages BY the route pair, i.e. the aliasing is pair-driven: screens 744+745 deliver 76 distinct pairs while s865+s870 consume only 5+6, and the five deep stages require 74. This is a candidate, not a decode: no pair-consulting screen-to-stage resolver has been located.

evidence.summary: The route pair is now carried by the walker and bank 0x7E is evaluated instead of returning null, so family-B maze NPCs are gated on the entrance the player dived through.
evidence.exact: BEFORE: bank 0x7E returned null (unmodelled) from web/flag-store.js, and the tri-state spawn model treats null permissively, so ALL 161 route-gated NPCs spawned simultaneously on every family-B screen regardless of entrance. evidence.exact: EXHAUSTIVE WRITER SCAN, replacing the earlier text matchers: a scanner propagating lui/addiu/ori/move and resolving the effective address of every sb/sh/sw/swl/swr with any base register and any offset, run over all 345 .s files under ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003 (595,489 lines), flags every store whose statically resolvable EA lands in 0x80048d70..0x80048d7f. Result: 10 hits, of which only 4 touch the pair, forming 2 site pairs, both in pro/fieldstg.s -- L5773 @0x800886c8 sh $v0,0x44($v1) with L5778 @0x800886dc sh $v0,0x46($v1), and L8780 @0x8008b5c4 with L8785 @0x8008b5d8. The other 6 are word stores to 0x80048d70/0x80048d74, adjacent fields of the same global struct. This covers sw/swl/swr/sb and every base+offset decomposition, so the negative is no longer a single-matcher artifact. SITE B IS NOT INDEPENDENT: ops 9 and 10 (table entries file 0x5bac and 0x5ba4) converge at file 0x5bb0, load a0 = [$s0+0x58] (field character) and a1 = [$s0+0x64]+0xa (= cmd+0xa), and jalr [char+0x124]. Slot +0x124 is installed at fieldstg.s L14682 with F0x8008f3e4, which calls the transition-screen constructor F0x8008c078 with a2 = cmd+0xa, and that constructor stores it at obj+0x7c (fieldstg.s L9486). Hence [$s4+0x7c] == cmd+0xa and site B writes the SAME step-record fields +0x14/+0x16 as site A. F0x8008c078 has exactly one caller; F0x8008f3e4 has zero jal sites and its address literal appears nowhere in the corpus, i.e. it is reachable only through the vtable slot, and no wstag*.s contains the token '0x124('. Ops 2-8 and 11-14 write nothing. RECORD SOURCE: the dispatcher at file 0x55d8 queries the type-7 map layer at the player tile via [0x8005b708](7,{x,y}); on a nonzero byte it sets +0x60 = byte>>5, +0x5c = byte & 0x1f and computes cmd = [$s0+0x54] + (byte & 0x1f)*0x18, where +0x54 is loaded from scene_struct+0x14 (file 0x5bf8-0x5c00). So the whole mechanism is route_pair := ([scene_struct+0x14])[grid_byte & 0x1f].params[5..6], written whenever the selected record's op is 1, 9 or 10. RESIDUE: the scan cannot resolve a store through a base loaded from memory or a bulk memcpy/DMA over the 0x80048xxx block; that is the only static shape left.

evidence.summary: First half (upper 16 bits) of building the BIT cap constant 0x0098967F (9,999,999 decimal) into $v1.
Completes the BIT cap constant: $v1 = 0x0098967F = 9,999,999, matching the decompiled 0x98967F literal at F0x80086bfc.c line 36.
addu $v0,$t0 adds the low word of the sell-price*quantity product to the current BIT balance ($v0 was loaded from struct+0x6C at the preceding lw).
Computes the resident game-state struct base address 0x80048D34 (lui 0x8005; addiu -0x72cc == 0x80048d34), used as the base for both the BIT-balance field (+0x6C) and the per-item owned-count array.
When the cap comparison is true, the balance is overwritten with the 0x98967F cap constant (executed only on the taken side of the beqz at L4153).
slt $v0,$v1,$v0 with v1=0x98967F (cap), v0=new balance: result is 1 iff cap < new balance, i.e. the sale would push the balance over 9,999,999.
The new (pre-cap) BIT balance is stored back to 0x80048D34+0x6C before the cap check runs.

When the slt at L3812 is nonzero (requested qty > stock), the quantity field is overwritten with the cached stock value instead of the incremented amount: a MIN(qty+10, stock) clamp, executed only inside the taken-branch fallthrough after the beqz at L3813.
Quantity-selector +10 handler adds 10 to the pending quantity (object field +0x68) before the stock-ceiling clamp.
slt $v0,$v1,$v0 with v1=cached stock (object +0x6C), v0=qty+10: result is 1 iff stock < requested quantity, i.e. the requested amount exceeds available stock.
mult $v1,$v0 multiplies the item's sell-price field (record+0x6, loaded via lhu at the immediately preceding instruction) by the confirmed quantity (object +0x68) to produce the sell total.
The stock/owned-count byte at item record offset +0x7C (record base = 0x80048D34 + item_idx) is read as the source of the object's cached stock cap (+0x6C).
The stock byte just loaded is stored into the shop-state object's +0x6C field, which the +10 handler (EV-shop-qty-slt-stock) later reads as the clamp ceiling.
On the not-taken side of the bgez at L4168 (count went negative), the owned-count byte is forced to 0, floor-clamping the sell decrement.
bgez tests the just-decremented count re-read as a signed byte; if it is still >= 0, the floor-clamp store is skipped.
The decremented owned-count is written back to (0x80048D34+item_idx)+0x7C.
subu $v0,$a0 subtracts the sold quantity (a0, loaded as a byte from object+0x68) from the player's owned-count byte for the item (v0, loaded from record+0x7C).
