evidence.summary: The constructor stores its own three arguments into the returned object at +0x54, +0x58 and +0x50.
The constructor's first factory argument is a per-stage address (0x800a70f8 in wstag311); this is the only word that differs between the ten copies.
The same constructor passes 0x17 as the factory's fourth argument - the actor class that the factory writes to object offset +0 before registering it.
The replicated stage-actor constructor asks the shared actor factory for a 0x6c-byte object.
On hold-timer expiry the stepper advances the script pointer by 4 bytes, confirming the 4-byte entry stride independently of the index scaling.

The stepper reads the frame delta through the global function pointer at 0x8004df9c and clamps it to 4: values below 5 pass, anything else becomes 4. This is the per-tick amount subtracted from the cursor's hold timer.
The looping stepper's copy in wstag735 at file 0x0160 (RAM 0x800a5f40) - the routine the launch-pad research already calls 'the stage's generic animator'.
In this variant the cursor's entry index is the halfword at object offset +0 (and its hold timer at +2).
The second variant, whose head is wstag310 .L0x000002d0 (RAM 0x800a60b0), is the same 72-instruction routine reading its cursor at object offset +4 (hold timer +6) instead of +0/+2.
The wstag800 copy of the +8 cursor form reads the script entry's hold field as an unsigned byte rather than an unsigned halfword.
That copy saves a fourth incoming argument, so it is the four-argument form with a caller-supplied one-shot flag, not the three-argument form.
A third cursor slot of the four-argument stepper: the entry index is read from object offset +8.
The fourth stepper form, at wstag232 file 0x0000 (RAM 0x800a5de0), zeroes its entry index on the terminator with no preceding test of any one-shot flag, so this form always loops.
Its terminator test branches only on whether the entry value is 0xff. The three-argument signature leaves no register carrying a one-shot flag, which is why the restart is unconditional.
The 54-instruction one-shot stepper in cnty_sel reads its entry index from object offset +0, not +4 as the fieldstg copy does.
On the 0xff terminator this form branches past its own recursive call to the epilogue, so it has no path that resets the index and repeats the script.
The matching hold timer of that cursor is the halfword at object offset +2.

The shorter 54-instruction variant, present in the shared fieldstg overlay at file 0x2e4c (head .L0x00002e4c, RAM 0x80085afc), branches straight to the epilogue with 0xff in v0 on the terminator. It has no one-shot parameter and no restart path, so it always ends the script.
When the caller's one-shot flag (a2) is zero, the terminator does not end the script: the cursor's entry index is stored back as 0 and entry 0's hold is added, so the script loops.

The looping stage animation-script stepper in wstag310 (routine head .L0x00000ff8, RAM 0x800a6dd8) scales the cursor's entry index by 4 before adding it to the script base, so a script entry is 4 bytes wide.
The stepper compares the newly reached entry's first halfword against 0xff; 0xff is the script terminator.
A zero end-of-sequence flag takes the branch that advances the entry index; a non-zero one falls through to advance the sequence index and reset the entry index.
On the outermost call only, byte 0 of the current entry is written to the actor at offset +4.
The end of a sequence is marked by a non-zero byte 3 inside the entry itself, not by a 0xff value as in the single-level forms.
When the next sequence pointer in the table is null the sequence index is reset to 0, so the table of sequences loops as a whole.
and byte 2 of the same entry is written to the actor at offset +9, so one entry drives two separate actor fields.
The two-level stepper's hold timer is a full word at cursor offset +4, not a halfword as in the single-level forms.
The per-stage class-0x17 actor callback in wstag310 (RAM 0x800a7604). It switches on the actor's phase at +0xc and drives the actor's animation cursors through the stage's own script stepper.
It adds a per-stage constant (0xe1 = 225 in wstag371) to that language index.
The stage scene-setup routine materialises the scene descriptor address 0x80099d80 into a2 once and then writes every descriptor slot through it.
It loads the word at 0x8005cca8 - the seven-language selection index that cnty_sel writes - into v0.
It then calls the zone manager's +0x40 method once per resource the stage needs, with a small kind selector in a0 and a 32-bit resource id in a1.
The routine ends by calling the zone manager's +0x50 method with 0, which is what starts the queued loads.
Each resource request loads the zone manager's +0x40 method and calls it; the routine finishes by loading +0x50 and calling it with a0=0 to start the queued loads.

Descriptor +0x3c and +0x40 are written as a pair from the same selector: this copy writes 5 to +0x3c and 0x6014<<16 to +0x40, and the override pair is 0x1f with 0x607c<<16 - in both cases the +0x40 high half is 0x60 plus selector*4.
The per-stage setup routine holds the scene descriptor 0x80099D80 in $s1 (0x800a0000-0x6280) and the zone manager 0x8009B6C4 in $s0 (0x800a0000-0x493c) across the whole body.
The same routine stores the zero register to descriptor +0x34. A census that reads the stored value out of a tracked-register map misses this too, because register 0 is never an entry in that map.
The sum is stored to scene descriptor +0x44. Because the value comes from a memory load, no constant-tracking store census can see this store.

After starting the loads, this copy loads a story word from the resident data area and compares it against an immediate; on mismatch it branches straight to the override, and only when it matches does it fall through to a flag query whose non-zero result also takes the override. The compare, the query call and the two override stores are all inside the cited range.
The routine materialises the zone-manager object address 0x8009b6c4 into s0.
The advance path loads the record list pointer held at 0x80099d90, formed here as 0x800a0000 minus 0x6270.
Each cursor is advanced by a call to the overlay's shared stepper primitive at 0x800a5de0, taking the cursor field address and a per-stage script address.
The reset path calls the actor's own +0x38 method and then seeds six halfword cursor fields at +0x50 through +0x5a, three of them cleared and three loaded from per-stage overlay halfwords.
The stepper reads the actor state word at +0xc and splits three ways: equal to one takes the advance path, below two or four and above takes the reset path, and the remaining band returns.

evidence.summary: The step-program selector. The zonecheck type-7 return byte is masked to 8 bits at 0x800882c4, split at 0x800882d0 (srl 5 -> the opcode argument, stored to controller +0x60) and 0x800882d4 (this line, andi 0x1f -> the step index, stored to +0x5c). Default handler F0x8008e8ac never writes +0x50/+0x54 and instead feeds the D-pad nibble to F0x8008e13c (facing table 0x80097c28), and F0x8008e45c contains no jal 0x8008e13c.

evidence.summary: Static localization of the Tag-commit cleanup that cancels Blast, previously captured only at runtime by TAG-C002. The shared cleanup tests the combatant's Blast flag +0x1a, and when it is set zeroes the DV/Blast gauge at +0x58 and clears the flag. Confirms Tag is not blocked while Blast is active - tagging out simply forfeits the charge.
The write cursor at +0x2c is pointed at the object's own small buffer at +0x24.
A dispatcher switches on the object's state byte at +0x46 and calls one builder per state, passing the object's payload byte at +0x47.
Each builder stamps a one-letter kind code into the object at offset +0x37.
The record length at +0x36 is set to 1 in the return delay slot.
The caller's byte argument is stored as the first and only byte of that buffer.

The 44-entry bound on a roster slot's acquired-form ledger is enforced here, in F0x8001764c, NOT in F0x80017a1c which TL-001 originally cited: the search loop increments the index and continues while it is below 0x2c (44). evidence.exact: typed-terrain-layer-decoded-2026-07-28.md Sec.8 item 1 previously flagged these eight stages as re-registering type 0 outside the init stub, from a linear scan that does not distinguish code from data. The flagged file offsets are all past the overlay's real end of code: wstag295's disassembly-terminating `# End of code` marker sits at line 197 while the flagged word is at line 469; wstag305's sits at line 541 while its three flagged words are at lines 827, 1068 and 1430 -- i.e. the flagged bytes are inside the overlay's DATA region, not instructions ever fetched by the CPU. The specific flagged words, 0x006c0009 and 0x00650009, are plain data that happens to decode as a jalr when a disassembler runs over a data region as if it were code; they are never executed. (Decoding them exactly: both have rs = 0 = $zero and rd = 24 = $t8 for 0x006c0009, rd = 10 = $t2 for 0x00650009 -- i.e. `jalr $t8, $zero` and `jalr $t2, $zero`. An earlier version of this record wrote them as `jalr $t3`/`jalr $t2`, taking rt rather than rd for the first; corrected 2026-07-28.) tools/zone_registration.py's register tracker does not produce these phantoms, and the STRUCTURAL reason is the jump register, not caller-saved invalidation: the parser only records a registration when the jalr's rs register is in its `isreg` set, and `isreg` can never contain $0 -- tools/zone_registration.py:93 adds the load destination only `if rt != 0`, and setr() likewise refuses to write register 0. Since both flagged words jump through $zero, they can never be mistaken for a call through zonemgr+0x40 no matter what precedes them. (The parser's caller-saved invalidation at every jal/non-registrar jalr is a real and separate property that stops stale $a0/$a1 values from masquerading as fresh registration arguments, but it is not what makes these two words harmless.) tools/test_zone_registration.py's TestPhantomRegistrationRegression asserts, and the suite confirms passing, that each of the eight stages (s295 s305 s311 s366 s620 s655 s947 s922) records EXACTLY ONE type-0 registration (subs 1,1,1,1,1,1,1,4 respectively).
evidence.summary: The 'eight stages re-register type 0 outside the init stub' residual is a false positive: the flagged offsets are inside overlay data regions, past each file's real end of code, and decode as a jalr through $zero only when misread as instructions -- which the register-tracked parser can never accept, since $0 is never in its registrar set -- and its regression test confirms exactly one real type-0 registration per stage.
evidence.limitations: Static; confirms absence of a second CODE-region registration for these eight stages specifically, not a formal proof that no overlay anywhere re-registers type 0 mid-play. Does not touch open items 2-5 in Sec.8 (the field-script raw-setter opcode, wstag415, s961's missing sub-0 bins, or the setter-guard semantics), which remain open.

evidence.exact: EXHAUSTIVE NEGATIVE, any-slot: across all 1,679 step records in all 282 readable programs, no record from any stage other than the deep screen's own overlay names screens 742/743/746-750 in ANY of its seven param slots. The eight raw matches are all Y coordinates (872,748 / 280,748 / 911,746 / 112,748) in slot 2. Restricted to slot 0 (the destination screen), only ops 9 and 1 ever target the underground at all, and only screens 736-741, 744 and 745. FOUR CANDIDATE MECHANISMS FALSIFIED. (1) Post-terminator record indexing: the type-7 dispatcher indexes scene+0x14 by (tile byte & 0x1f) with NO bounds check (fieldstg .L0x00005620-.L0x00005644), so records past the op==0 terminator would be live -- but the shipped grids never index past it. Grid step-indices vs record counts: s845 [0,1]/2, s860 [0]/1, s865 [0,1]/2, s870 [0,1]/2, s875 [0]/1, s880 [0]/1, s885 [0,1]/2, s890 [0,1,2]/3, s895 [0,1,2]/3, s635 [0,1,2,3]/4, s850 [0,1,2]/3, s835 [0,1]/2 -- exact match on all twelve, and every program ends within 0x24 bytes of the image end anyway. (2) Runtime table construction: every record the 2026-07-09 rig harvest reported as a 'live' exit exists VERBATIM in a static overlay image, mis-attributed by one stage. The harvest's 's845 live table = s850 (224,288) d5 + s850 (944,216) d1' is byte-for-byte wstag850's own records idx2 and idx1 at file 0x00f22 and 0x00f0a; 's850 -> s855 (160,336)' is wstag855 idx1 at 0x0190a; 's825/s840 -> s855 (1104,584)' is wstag855 idx0 at 0x018f2. A byte search for those triples across all overlays returns exactly those static sites (plus their s96x alias twins) and nothing else. (3) A second, door-shaped warp table: there is none -- the ffff0000ffff0000 'signature' IS the step record's own header (cond_a=0xffff, arg_a=0, cond_b=0xffff, arg_b=0), so wstag_extract's signature records and the scene+0x14 program are the same table, and the active-record counts agree stage for stage (s865 2, s870 2, s875 1, s880 1, s885 2, s890 3, s895 3). (4) A pair-driven screen-to-stage resolver: F0x80092110 selects the alias table start purely on [0x8004b370] == 0x2d and takes the first record matching the screen id; the corpus-wide read census for 0x80048d78 is 3 of 590,078 lines, all inside the bank-0x7E predicate F0x800160a8, so the pair is never read by any transport code. CONSEQUENCE: s855, s860, s875, s880, s885, s890 and s895 have no entrance of any kind in the shipped step data, and the 76 route-gated NPCs on them (s860 2, s875 8, s880 18, s885 8, s890 19, s895 21) require nonzero pairs that nothing in the corpus can set there. def pack_unknown0(u: dict) -> list[int]:
    """The 20-byte Unknown0 equip-stat record, as the game's own byte loads see it.

    Layout (~/ddw3/rust/dw2003_exe_data/src/data.rs:134 `struct Unknown0`):
      +0x00 f0 u16 | +0x02 f1 u8 | +0x03 f2 u8 | +0x04 f3 u16 | +0x06 f4 i16
      +0x08 f5 i16 | +0x0A f6 u16 | +0x0C f7[2] | +0x0E f8[2] | +0x10 f9[2] | +0x12 f10 u16

    The bytes are emitted instead of pre-labelled fields on purpose: stitshop
    F0x80088a64 (the shop effect-card stat builder) reads them BY OFFSET and what an
    offset means changes with the item's family byte — +0x0A is the displayed POW bonus
    for a family 2-14 weapon and a pair of stat CODES for a family 15-20 armour piece.
    The rule lives in engine/dw3/equipment.ts `gearStatContributions`.
    """
    b = bytearray()
    b += _u16(u["f0"]) + _u8(u["f1"]) + _u8(u["f2"])
    b += _u16(u["f3"]) + _u16(u["f4"]) + _u16(u["f5"]) + _u16(u["f6"])

Opcodes 0x8D/0xAE (the combo/summon sprite step, per §G.0) enter through F0x8008ad48(duel, arg2), a 2-statement handler that only writes the immediate arg2 into duel+0x438 (yet another distinct meaning of that offset within this registry) and arms the interpreter (duel+0x423=1). The real sprite-stepping work is in the unread 400-line stateful sibling F0x8008ad98.

Opcode 0x97 enters through F0x8008bc6c, which takes no duel/view arguments in the recovered signature and does nothing but call F0x8008baa4(0) -- i.e. it is a pure zero-argument passthrough into the same zone-selection setup used by opcodes 0xA9/0xAB/0xAC/0xAD (OPCA-018), with side/kind forced to (0,0). It performs no board write of its own beyond what F0x8008baa4 does.

Opcodes 0xA9/0xAB/0xAC/0xAD (and 0x97 via OPCA-017) enter through F0x8008baa4(duel, view, side, kind). For kind==1 it invokes the duel's own +0x814 method -- confirmed elsewhere in §C as sortCardArrayByCardId -- to sort that side's draw pile by card id before presenting it, sets a message code into duel+0x438 (7 for side 0, 0xD for side 1), and records the pile's card count into duel+0x434 as the legal-selection limit. Other kinds (0, 3) instead use hand count or trash count with different message codes, without the sort call. It then initialises the selection/highlight flags (+0x46F, +0x49E) for up to duel+0x434 of the relevant 40-entry array based on each entry's own +0x446 flag, arms the interpreter (+0x423=1), and resets the pending selection result (duel+0x440=-1).

Opcode 0xA8's enter-phase handler F0x80089ec8 performs no board read or write beyond arming the interpreter (duel+0x423=1); the opcode's actual behaviour is in the unread 366-line stateful sibling F0x8008a068.

Opcodes 0x99/0x9A enter through F0x80086d78(duel, view, block), where block is a per-player-block pointer (§E.3). For each of up to 40 hand entries within the block's hand count it re-checks summon usability through the same gate F0x80085FD0(duel, block+0xC, instance) used by opcode 0x98 (block+0xC being that side's S-Energy array), sets duel+0x446=1 and clears the highlight-disable flag duel+0x49E for usable cards (or the reverse for unusable ones), clears duel+0x46F for every entry, then sets the view-mode byte duel+0x499 from the ACTING SIDE -- block+0x11, the side index -- writing 5 and calling view->unkEC0(view, side) for side 0 and 0xB with no such call for side 1, arms the interpreter (+0x423=1), clears the cursor duel+0x43C and resets duel+0x440=-1.
Original-assembly confirmation that F0x80086d78 also calls F0x80085FD0 (the same summon-usability gate as F0x80086330/OPCA-004), inside its per-hand-entry loop.

Opcodes 0x9B/0x9C (a count and a banner id, per §G.0: 'handCount/trashCount, 5/9') enter through F0x80086eb0(duel, count, bannerCode). When count>0 it clears the highlight-disable flag +0x49E across a 40-entry run (arg0+0x27 down to arg0+0, i.e. duel+0x49E..+0x4C5); when count<=0 it clears only duel+0x49E itself (one entry). It then calls the helper F0x80086A18(duel) (not read this pass), arms the interpreter (+0x423=1), writes bannerCode into duel+0x499, and resets duel+0x43C=0 and duel+0x440=-1 (pending selection).

F0x80090058, the update-phase handler for opcodes 0x42/0x43 ('the draw paths', per §G.0), is a 6-state machine on duel+0x422 keyed to side arg2. State 1 waits for the view sprite to settle then arms the draw animation. State 2 is the actual draw: it decrements the per-player block's deck count (block+0x5A4, matching §E.3), increments the deck-read cursor (block+0x5A0) and the hand count (block+0x5A6), copies the drawn instance into the hand array (block+0x600), looks the drawn card up through the resident catalog getter F0x8001ebf8, and pushes the post-draw deck/hand/trash counts of BOTH sides (block+0x5A4/0x5A6/0x5A2 for side 0 and the +0xC8-shifted block+0x66C/0x66E/0x66A for side 1) to the view via unkEA0 fields 5/6/7. It then branches to state 3 (still under 6 cards, more draws pending) or state 4 (arms a 0x2D-tick timer and stops). State 3 uses block+0x5A2 (trash count) similarly.

F0x8009076c, the enter-phase (immediate) handler for opcode 0x44, is a 5-line setup: zeroes the frame accumulators duel+0x424 and duel+0x434, seeds duel+0x428 from the acting side's per-player-block trash count (block+0x5A2) and duel+0x42C from its deck count (block+0x5A4), then sets duel+0x422=1 to hand control to F0x800907AC. F0x800907AC is already decoded in card-battle-complete-model-2026-08-06.md §G.4 as 'twin of F0x8008F0F4', the 7-frame animated counter reaching block+0x14 (deck) and block+0x78 (trash) through the base duel+side*0xC8+0x59C. This ties the counter's seed values directly to trash/deck counts rather than leaving them opaque.

F0x80090a6c, reached by opcodes 0x45 and 0x47 (per §G.0's 'set the selection quota +0x444' entry and its 0x46 sibling), writes the selection quota directly from its own immediate operand: duel+0x444 = arg2 (the '2'/'6' constants passed at the two call sites in §G.0), and clears the clamped-selection flag duel+0x445 to 0. Before that it zero-fills a run of 0x28 (40) bytes starting at duel+0x46F using pointer decrement (not the 12-byte width implied elsewhere in the document for the 'shared selection-flag array').

Original assembly for F0x80090a6c's clear loop: `li $v1, 0x27` then a loop storing a single byte `sb $zr, 0x46f($v0)` while decrementing both $v0 (the base pointer, i.e. duel+0x27 down to duel+0) and $v1 from 0x27 to 0. Each store address is (duel + i) + 0x46f for i = 0x27..0, i.e. absolute addresses duel+0x46F through duel+0x496 inclusive (40 bytes), confirming the C lift's byte count and that the field this handler clears extends past the previously documented 12-byte 'hand slots 0..9 / field slots 0..11' array at +0x46F into currently-undocumented bytes +0x47B..+0x496.

F0x80090a90, reached by opcode 0x47 (§G.0's 0x45/0x47 row), is the actual quota-to-flags fill that follows F0x80090a6c's quota write. If duel+0x444 (the quota) is non-zero: for arg2==0 it walks the OWN side's hand starting at duel+0x5A0 (deck-read cursor, i.e. the just-drawn cards) and sets duel+(0..0x27)->unk46F = 1 for up to `quota` consecutive slots, clamping at slot 0x28 and, if it ran out of room, writing back the actually-flagged count into duel+0x444 and setting duel+0x445=1 (the clamp flag written by F0x80090a6c). For arg2!=0 it instead flags OPPONENT-side slots: it clamps the quota to the opponent's deck count (duel+0x66C, side-1 mirror of +0x5A4) into duel+0x444/+0x445, then alternates writing duel+0x46F flags from the low end (opponent's deck cursor duel+0x668-relative slots matching class duel+0x300*2+2) and from the high end (index 0x27 downward) depending on whether each opponent deck slot's class byte (+0x30B) matches the acting side's chosen colour.

F0x80090ba0, the enter-phase handler for opcode 0x48, moves every deck-read-cursor card flagged in duel+0x46F for side arg2 into that side's hand array: for cursor position 0..0x27, if duel[cursor]->unk46F != 0 it copies the drawn pile's card (block+0x5B0[cursor]) into block+0x600[handCount] and increments the per-player block's hand count (block+0x5A6, matching §E.3's hand array). duel+0x438 is set to the pre-move hand count and duel+0x42C flags whether any card was actually moved. It then clears the 40-byte view-highlight array duel+(0..0x27)->unk49E, computes a banner/animation id in duel+0x499 (values 5/0xB/0x11/0x12 depending on whether any card moved and which side), calls view->unkEC0(view, side, moved?, cursor), and sets duel+0x422=1. This is the concrete effect of a Selection-family opcode actually delivering the previously-flagged cards into the hand -- the counterpart write to the flags F0x80090a90 (op 0x47) and F0x8008CB5C (target-zone bound check, §G.4) set up.

evidence.summary: F0x80090cd8 dispatches on duel+0x422 (values 1..10, `sltiu $v0,$v1,0xa` bound check) through a jump table at 0x80083554 + (state-1)*4. Its state-2 body (from .L0x0000e0c0) computes a per-side field-slot base at duel + side*8*8 + side*8 (i.e. duel + side*0x48, the play-history-adjacent region used elsewhere for selection scratch) and, for a slot index bounded by `lw $a0, 0x438($s1)` compared against `lh $v0, 0x5a6($v1)` (the side's hand count, block+0x5A6), writes a sprite command word 0x00014A00 into that slot's view unk108 and reads block+0x5A6 again to advance. This is a second, independent confirmation (opcode 0x48's own update phase, not just F0x8008CB5C from §G.4) that duel+0x438 is read and bounds-checked against a hand-count field during a selection opcode -- corroborating, from a different opcode family, §G.4's finding that +0x438 carries a per-opcode selection-bound meaning rather than being pure shared scratch.

F0x80091858, opcodes 0x4F..0x55 (per §G.0, called with a kind '0x50+k'), appends a new field-slot record for card instance arg3 to side arg2's field: it reads the slot-count byte at duel+arg2*0x72+0x72C, writes the new record at that count's offset (base duel+0x72C+count*0xE), sets the record's card-instance field (local +0x0 within the §E.4 layout) to arg3, zeroes the AP/HP target fields (local +0x2/+0x4), fills the displayed AP/HP fields (local +0x6/+0x8) from a catalog lookup via F0x8001ebf8, and stamps two undocumented slot bytes past §E.4's table (local +0xA = a constant 2, local +0xB = the side arg2) plus a monotonically increasing sequence number from duel+0x308 into the documented 'class/colour' byte at local +0xC. It then drives the new sprite's view fields (unkF14/unkF3C/unk14B/unk120/unk14C) and calls the shared helper F0x8009170c (unliftable, common to opcodes 0x4F-0x57) before returning control at duel+0x422=1.

F0x800919fc, opcode 0x56, removes a field slot for side arg2: it scans the acting side's play-history for the most recent play's target class byte (duel+(playCount-1)*8+0x586) against each occupied field-record's class/colour byte (slot+0x64 in this function's indexing, matching §E.4's +0xC local class field after base adjustment), and on the first match calls duel->unk81C(duel, side, class) -- a method-table dispatch, not decoded here. It then shifts every later slot record down by one (closing the gap) and decrements the side's slot-count byte at duel+arg2*0x72+0x72C, before pushing the new hand-count-shaped count to the view (unkEA0 field 6) and control to F0x8009170c. This is the field-slot deletion counterpart to F0x80091858's insertion -- 'a slot removed' behaviour item 9 in the model's §F rules ('a slot at 0 HP is removed') is consistent with this being the generic removal primitive, though this function itself removes by CLASS MATCH against the play-history target, not by an HP==0 check; the HP trigger is elsewhere (see F0x8009535c below).

F0x80091eb0, opcode 0x57, scans all 12 field slots across both sides (indices 0..5 gated by duel+0x72C, 6..11 gated by duel+0x79E) for the last one flagged in duel+0x46F, then copies that flagged slot's whole sprite animation state (view sprite +0x108..+0x148, 0x40 bytes via a 4-word-stride loop) onto the acting side's own new/target slot sprite, and copies the flagged slot's class byte (local +0xC) into the target record's local +0xE (priority) field. It also walks the play-history up to duel+0x575-1 entries and, for entries whose +0x585 byte is 0, propagates a 'highlighted' sprite flag (+0x146) from the flagged slot's sprite onto the target slot's sprite at the matching history index. This looks like the visual/board 'merge onto target slot' step of a combo or replacement effect (candidate for the unresolved 'does the game replace the run with the +0x0A Digimon' question in the model's open item 3), but the exact opcode-level semantics of which slot is 'target' vs 'source' were not fully traced here.

F0x80092438, opcodes 0x12/0x13, is the play/cancel branch for the card being played (view slot 0xF). If the view is idle (arg1->unk64==0) it treats the play as CANCELLED: clears the selection cursor duel+0x440=0, plays a sound tied to the most recent play-history entry's card id (block+0x580), resets view field unk594, clears the twelve-slot flag array duel+(0..0xE)->unk46F only when arg2==0 (i.e. only for the human/side-0 branch), and sets duel+0x499=1 (a banner code) and duel+0x422=1 (done). If the view is NOT idle and arg2!=0, it instead reads a coordinate pair from the table at 0x800A5910[duel+0x575] and positions the effect sprite there, transitioning to state 5. If neither branch's guard holds (arg2!=0 and view busy is false, i.e. the normal play-continues path) it re-arms the sprite-move command for slot 0xF and moves to state 2. In every path it also clears the highlight bit (+0x151) on 15 sprites starting at view+0x428.

F0x80092ba4, opcode 0x14, unconditionally zeroes BOTH sides' hand counts (duel+0x5A6 and its side-1 mirror duel+0x66E), pushes both zeroed counts to the view (unkEA0 field 6 for side 0 and 1), clears the selection cursor duel+0x440, and sets duel+0x423=1 (a second step-state byte distinct from +0x422, used by the stateful counterpart F0x80092e60 per the census). This is a hand-wipe step, consistent with §F.1 item 8's 'the field is rebuilt from scratch every Summon Phase' but for the HAND rather than the field -- likely the Load-Phase 'discard remaining hand' or a compile-phase reset the model's rule list does not currently name.

F0x8009403c, opcodes 0x19/0x1A, sums the AP (duel-relative +0x734) and HP (+0x736) of every field slot flagged in the SIDE-0-SHAPED array duel+0x446 (§E.2's 'side 0 field-slot flags', reused here for whichever side arg2 selects) into duel+0x42C (AP total) and duel+0x430 (HP total), each individually capped at 0x63 (99). If 4 or more slots were flagged it adds a further +0x14 (20) to BOTH totals, capped again at 99 -- an exact, code-legible confirmation of §F.1 item 12's 'plus 20 to each at four copies'. It then looks up a text/sound index by matching duel+0x438 - 1 against a table at duel+0xB2 bounded by duel+0x244, falling back to index 0x57 and resetting duel+0x438=0x13B when no entry matches, and writes the capped totals into view fields unk657 (AP) / unk658 (HP) for a combo banner (view+0x64C=5). Finally it sets a per-slot sprite highlight bit (+0x150 |= 4) on every flagged slot. This is the SCORING/PRESENTATION side of a combo; it does not resolve whether the run is additionally replaced with catalog +0x0A's Digimon (§F's open item 3 remains unresolved), but it does show duel+0x438 here is read as 'the combo's matched catalog index', a further per-opcode meaning distinct from both the selection-bound reading (§G.4, OPCB-006) and the plain frame-accumulator reading already on record.

F0x8009535c is the update-phase handler chained from opcode 0x5D (per §G.0: '+0x422=1; update takes F0x8009535C's result'). On entry (duel+0x422 in {1,2}, first pass) it clears the twelve-slot array duel+(0..0xB)->unk46F, sets duel+0x422=2 and duel+0x438=0. On every following frame it walks BOTH sides' occupied field slots (bounded by duel+0x72C and duel+0x79E) and steps each occupied slot's SPRITE displayed-AP field (view sprite unk43) and displayed-HP field (unk44) by +/-1 per frame toward the duel's stored true AP/HP for that slot (the +0x734/+0x736-relative fields used elsewhere for the field totals) -- the same 'roll toward target' behaviour §E.4 documents for F0x8008E08C, but driving the view SPRITE fields directly rather than the duel slot's own +0x6/+0x8 display bytes. Whenever a slot's true HP value has reached exactly 0 during this walk, it flags that field-slot index in duel+0x46F and sets duel+0x438=1 -- this is a second, concrete answer to §G.4's open item ('what sets the +0x46F flags during Battle state 9' / P2 item 7 in §F): after a stat change drives a slot's HP to 0, THIS handler (not just F0x800915D4, which only consumes the flags already decoded in §G.4) is what actually sets one of them. It returns 0 while any value is still moving, 1 once nothing changed and no zero-HP flag fired this pass, or 2 once nothing changed but a zero-HP flag was set on a prior pass (duel+0x438!=0). A sound is queued through the resident dispatcher at 0x80055C48 with id 0x800452C6 whenever any AP/HP value actually stepped this frame.

Tail of the resident native handler 0x8008bf38: a0 = 0xf, then lui $v0,0x8005 / lw $v0,-0x7538($v0) loads the function pointer at 0x80048ac8 (flag-API base D0x80048abc + 0xc = the set_flag slot), a1 = 1, jalr. So the handler performs set_flag(0x000f, 1) — bank 0x00, bit 15 — and then returns v0 = 0 (move $v0,$zero at 0x8008bf98), which is the field interpreter's native-path completion value.

Full body of the in-overlay native event handler shared by all 16 of s740's native events. It is eleven instructions: a0 = 0x800a5de4 (overlay base 0x800a5de0 + 4, the overlay's per-stage handler entry), a1 = 0x54 (object size), a2 = 0xc (object type), jal F0x80014504 (the same object allocator the field event runner uses), then return its result. The handler therefore installs a per-stage native state machine whose per-frame body is the overlay +0x04 routine, and contributes no field-VM bytecode.

Storage banks 0x00,0x02,0x04,0x06,0x08,0x0A,0x0C,0x0E,0x10,0x18,0x1A,0x1C,0x20,0x40 all route to the bitfield writer F0x800155d4; then 0x70 -> F0x80015d90, 0x74 -> D0x8009b6a4, 0x76 -> F0x80016378(...,0), 0x78 -> F0x80016378(...,1), 0x80-0x8E -> F0x800161d8, 0x90 -> D0x8008bfa4, 0x92 -> F0x80016314, 0x94 -> D0x8008b770(0xA00,...), 0x7A -> D0x8008b770(0xF00 or 0x1300) / D0x8008c000, and 0x7C -> D0x8008b770(0xD00 or 0xB00). Banks 0x00,0x02,0x04,0x06,0x08,0x0A,0x0C,0x0E,0x10,0x18,0x1A,0x1C,0x20,0x40 route to the bitfield reader F0x80015590; 0x60 -> F0x80015ec8, 0x70 -> F0x80015d90, 0x72 -> F0x80015fbc, 0x7E -> F0x800160a8, 0x80-0x8E -> F0x80015f04, 0x92 -> F0x80015f70. F0x80098864 returns pitch 0x2900 per index whenever the card count is less than 7. 0x2900 against the 8.8 position format is exactly 41.0 pixels.
The flip animator writes scale_x (+0x18) as 0x1000 minus the sine call F0x8002abcc((t << 12) / 24, (t << 12) / 6), sweeping the card's width from unity to zero and back as a half sine.
F0x8009a75c (state 4, the flip) XORs the sprite's render kind at +0x45 with 3 at the halfway point of the flip, loaded at L24273 and stored back at L24276. The XOR pairs kind 1 with kind 2.
At timer >= 0xC the flip ends: it writes state 1 to +0x42, clears +0x26, and restores scale_x to unity 0x1000, bounding the flip at 12 frames.

The render-kind XOR is gated on +0x2C still being zero AND the timer having reached 7, and it sets +0x2C to 1 in the same block, so unk45 ^= 3 fires exactly once, at the midpoint of the 12-frame flip.

F0x8009a540 counts its timer up and, at 10 frames, writes state 0xB (11) to +0x42, zeroes timer and duration, clears +0x26, and clears the effect selector +0x47. It is a pure timer that hands over to state 11.

The two dispatch arms that call F0x8009a5b0 load its duration argument as a literal: 0x24 for one state and 0x1C for the other, immediately before the shared jal. These are the only two call sites of that animator.
F0x8009a5b0 compares its up-counting timer against its duration argument and on expiry writes state 1 (idle) to +0x42, zeroes timer and duration, clears +0x26, and clears the effect selector +0x47.
First entry of the 12-word switch jump table at 0x80083748 (file 0xa98), the state dispatch for F0x8009b890. Twelve consecutive .word entries follow, one per animation state 0..11.

The move animator guards the position update on current != destination for either axis, and separately guards the scale update the same way on L16, so an axis already at its destination is skipped rather than recomputed.

On timer expiry the move animator writes state 1 to +0x42, zeroes the timer +0x28 and duration +0x2C, and snaps position +0x00/+0x04 and scale +0x18/+0x1A to their destination fields, so the sprite lands exactly on target and returns to the idle state.
The +0x26 draw-layer field is cleared with a HALFWORD store (sh $zr, 0x26($s0)), not a byte store; the decompilation's untyped 'unk26 = 0' does not carry the width.
On move completion the animator clears the +0x26 draw-layer byte, but only when +0x48 is zero, so a sprite flagged in +0x48 keeps its layer after landing.

The move animator computes cur = dest - (dest - start) * timer / duration for the x axis (and the identical form for y on L14). The interpolation is a single multiply and divide against the linearly counting timer, with no easing curve, table lookup, or squared term of any kind.

The move animator's position guard is PAIRWISE, not per axis: bne on x jumps straight to the update, and only when x matches does beq on y skip the block. If either axis differs, BOTH axes are recomputed.

The move animator's scale guard is a single 32-bit lw/lw/beq comparing +0x18 against +0x1C, which spans both halfword scale axes (+0x18/+0x1A vs +0x1C/+0x1E) in one compare, so the pair is skipped or updated as a unit.
F0x80099ffc's completion path plays a sound only when the state is not 3, which is the entire behavioural difference between states 2 and 3 given that the jump table sends both to the same animator.

The only behavioural difference between the two states sharing this animator is on the completion path: the call at 0x80055C48 (with argument 0x800460BD) is executed only when the state byte +0x42 is not 3, so state 3 completes silently where state 2 does not. No other branch in the function tests +0x42.

The jump-table word 0x8009b8e0 held by BOTH state 2 and state 3 is a thunk at file offset 0x18c30 whose body jals 0x80099ffc. This ties the shared table entry to the concrete animator F0x80099ffc, which the jump table alone does not establish.

The move animator's timer field +0x28 is decremented every frame by the value returned from the resident call at 0x8004DF9C and the interpolation branch is taken only while the result is greater than zero, so the timer counts DOWN to zero rather than up.
F0x8009bac8 initialises its walk of the card sprite pool at duel offset 0xC9C, counting 0x27 down to 0 in steps of -0x4C, i.e. 40 sprites of 0x4C bytes spanning duel+0x108..duel+0xCE7.
F0x8009b76c draws the card sprite at (unk0 >> 8, unk4 >> 8) plus a constant screen bias, showing that the sprite position fields +0x00/+0x04 are 8.8 fixed point with the low byte a fraction.

The card draw function F0x8009b168 switches on +0x45 with cases 0, 1, 2 and 3, each drawing a different card form. This is what makes +0x45 the sprite's render kind, and what makes an XOR of 3 a pairing of kind 1 with kind 2 and of kind 0 with kind 3.

evidence.locator: L6638 @0x80016008 (F0x80015fbc, loop body over party positions 0..2)
evidence.summary: F0x80015fbc calls resident helper ctx+0x2718 (party position -> roster slot) then ctx+0x2734 (F0x80017174, build battle-effective stats into a caller buffer at sp+0x10) for each of the three deployed party positions.

The accumulated field is the signed halfword at offset 0x16 of the effective-stat buffer (buffer base is sp+0x10, so 0x26($sp)). F0x80017174 fills that buffer by a verbatim block copy of roster record bytes +0x1c..+0x48, so buffer+0x16 is roster record +0x32 = cur_chr (Unknown4Stats index 11). This is a STACK load, which is exactly the access form pass 1 excluded when it classified only non-stack 0x16($reg) halfword loads.

The accumulated party charisma is compared against word table D0x80048cf8 indexed by (flag_id & 0x1FF) * 4. Only two instructions in the entire main-executable assembly reference D0x80048cf8, both inside this function and both reads, so the table is never written by code.

The predicate is 'sum < threshold' inverted, i.e. the flag reads as TRUE exactly when the party charisma sum is greater than or equal to the table entry; the two exit arms (arg1 nonzero / zero) implement the requested-value comparison so that '=1' means at-or-above and '=0' means below.

evidence.locator: L7908 @0x80017414 (F0x80017174, equipment projection loop over the six equipped slots)

ABSENCE ANCHOR: the flag-write dispatcher's bank chain jumps straight from 0x70 to 0x74; the literal text '0x72' does not occur anywhere in this file (rg -c returned no match), and 'li $v0, 0x72' occurs exactly once in the whole main-exe assembly (the READ dispatcher, evidence chr-q001-p2-e1). setGameState (F0x800165ac) splits the packed id into an even bank (s3) and an index (s0, masked to 0-511), matching the doc's bank/index packing.

setGameState tests (bank-0x80) unsigned < 0xf, i.e. bank in {0x80,0x82,...,0x8e}, to route into the item-count handler; all eight bank values in that span funnel into the SAME F0x800161d8 call with only the index (not the bank) selecting the byte, so they alias one flat count array rather than eight separate ones.

F0x800161d8 indexes its per-item count byte off the save base D0x80048d34, the same struct already used for the FishingPole/TreeBoots collection-possession bytes at +0x7c+id in prior verified evidence.
Direct call site: setGameState invokes F0x800161d8(index, value) for the 0x80-0x8e bank span.
On underflow, the count byte is forced to 0 instead of going negative or below zero.
Decrement path (arg1==0) re-reads the same base+index+0x7c count byte before subtracting 1.
The decremented byte is sign-extended and its sign bit tested to detect underflow below 0.
Original assembly label for the item-count clamp function F0x800161d8, called (arg0=index, arg1=increment/decrement flag) from the setGameState dispatcher.
On overflow past 99, the stored byte is forced back down to 0x63 (99) instead of wrapping or rejecting the pickup.
After incrementing and re-storing, the sign-extended result is compared against 0x64 (100) to detect overflow past the 99 cap.
Increment path (arg1!=0) reads the current stackable-item count byte at base+index+0x7c before adding 1.
The low 9 bits of the packed id become the per-item index passed into the count array.

Checked decompilation of the increment clamp; matches the assembly cited above line-for-line (temp_v0 = unk7C+1; clamp to 0x63 on overflow).

evidence.summary: The committed audit that produced both measurements. Per map cell it rasterises every layer-0 and every layer-2 object into the cell's own coordinate space via world_offset/img_offset/size, keeps only texels with alpha > 0 in the cell's extracted tile image, and intersects the two sets. Repository tooling, so authority 6: it is the method, not the proof. The proof is the extracted map-tile data it reads.

s276 map cell 10 (col 3, row 1): map-tile layers 0 and 1 both carry `objs = []`, and layer 2 carries a single object at world_offset [0,0] with size [128,128]. The whole 128x128 cell is layer-2 art with no ground art beneath it at all. Nine of s276's sixteen layer-2 cells have this shape (2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10, 17, 25, 26).

evidence.locator: L5-L8 (layer 0 object) and the layer-2 object at world_offset [0,0] size [120,128]

Rectangle overlap alone would have given the wrong answer here.

s411 is the counter-example that stops the s276 result from being generalised: it is the worst overlapping stage in the fleet, with 16,112 of its 34,070 opaque layer-2 pixels (47.3 percent) sitting over opaque layer-0 art across its 17 layer-2 cells. Its 8x4 grid is quoted here as the anchor for that stage identity.

The advance glyph is gated on self+0x98 (lw + beqz jumping past it to the panel), and the window picture is drawn on every pass with no hide path: cel 0x31 at (0xb, 0xbc), the glyph CMFONT cel 0xa at (0x123, 0xd0) with its frame at self+0x90 stepping once every 4 ticks through five. The real reveal machine, five phases off the table at 0x80083124 indexed by self+0x10: phase 0 waits for the VM's self+0x74 then on; phase 1 stamps self+0x84, sets self+0x80 = 3 and SHOWs *(a1 + 4*self+0x78); phase 2 waits out the gap and either returns to phase 1 (setting self+0x98 = 1 when nothing is left) or enters phase 3; phase 3 waits for pad bit 0x2000, plays [0x80055c48](0x1c), advances self+0x88 and either ends the line (state 3) or runs the VM on self+0x50 + 4*self+0x88 and returns to phase 0 with the gate cleared; phase 4 closes after 0x15 = 21 ticks or on Circle and is reachable only from +0xb0.

The timed close switch: self+0x10 = 4, self+0x98 = 0, self+0x14 = [0x8004df98](). It is installed at the controller's +0xb0 and no instruction in the decoded corpus calls through +0xb0: grep of pro/fightstg.s for 0xb0( yields only the constructor's store and .L0x8008bdf0 (an unrelated object), and a scan of all 17 exe/*.s and 30 pro/*.s files for a load of 0xb0($reg) followed within three lines by jalr yields two object-shaped hits, that same .L0x8008bdf0 and wfightmn.s:3738 lw $v0, 0xb0($a0), which reads +0xb0 of 0x1c($s1), a menu list row. So every battle message line waits for Circle with no timeout.

What clears a battle line owner's child pointer. F0x80018230 walks the owner's child list at owner+0x24 (count at owner+0x20), steps each child with F0x80018140 and stores the stepper's RETURN VALUE back over the slot; F0x80018140 returns 0 exactly when the child reached self+0x0c = 3 (bnez to the self+0x4c teardown, then move_ $v0, $s0 with $s0 zeroed). So the message line reaching state 3 zeroes the owner's slot, which is what releases the lw ($s2)/bnez waits in FIGHTSTG_F0x80090e84 (.L0x80091094, .L0x800910e8, .L0x800911c8, .L0x8009123c, .L0x80091328, .L0x80091350) and FIGHTSTG_F0x80088564 (.L0x80088680, .L0x8008876c, .L0x80088ac0, .L0x80088afc, .L0x80088b70, .L0x80088bb8).

The op-0x30 story-step range has no 'no upper end' encoding. F0x80015b9c loads the master story ordinal from 0x8004b370 (lw), indexes the u8 pair at D0x80048cb4 + param2*2, and returns (lo < ordinal -> 0) then !(hi < ordinal) — i.e. (ordinal >= lo) && (ordinal <= hi), both bounds inclusive, with no special case on hi. The 33 pairs read out of the static EXE splat hold the byte 0x63 = 99 as hi in exactly 7 slots (param2 6,7,8,10,11,12,13) and nowhere else; the largest closed upper bound is 44. So 99 is the disc's own end-of-story bound and an open-ended record means lo <= ordinal <= 99. F0x80015d90 then returns (result == expected) (.L0x80015eb0 xor + .L0x80015ebc sltiu 1), the polarity the walker already models.

Step 1 of wfightmn F0x800a7418 tests the freeze bit and rolls it. lbu $v0, 0x1c($s0) / andi $v0, 0x2 / beqz $v0 -> .L0x000017f8 skips the roll when the bit is clear. When it is set the routine loads the pointer at 0x4660, calls it with `move_ $a0, $zr` in the jalr delay slot (so the argument is 0, the player side), and `beqz $v0, .L0x000017f8` sends a ZERO answer past the arming code: a nonzero answer is the blocked turn.

The blocked branch stores message id 0x56 and a zero second word into the instruction and shows it through the line object's method +0xac with argument 2 and the address of the first word, then re-queues the turn by calling the pointer at 0x437c with (0, 0) into jal 0x8009c4bc, then calls instr+0x2c(2). Falling through instead tests the confusion bit 0x4; set, it calls instr+0x2c(0x11); clear, it arms the list with jal 0x80092d80(2) and stores step 2 at 0x14($s1).

The auto-equip scan. ctx+0x2744 is called with the new form id as $a1 (acquire), then ctx+0x2738 is called with sp+0x28 (get_equipped) to read the triple. The walk starts at index 0 and buffer offset 0; `slti $v0, 0x3` (the short form of slt $v0, $v0, 0x3, and $v0 holds the slot value read by `lh $v0, ($v1)`) branches to the write when the slot is below 3, with `addiu $a0, 0x1` in the delay slot. `slti $v0, $a0, 0x3` loops while the index is below 3, advancing the buffer pointer in the delay slot. At index 3 the routine falls out to 0x80086590 with the new form id in $v0 and nothing stored.

The write arm of the same scan: `sh $s1, ($v1)` stores the new form id into the one slot the scan stopped on, then ctx+0x273c (set_equipped) is called with the whole triple buffer sp+0x28 as $a1 and the routine returns the new form id.

The resident get_equipped F0x800176ac is what makes an empty slot visible to the scan. For each of the three halfwords at roster record +0x7b0 it tests `slti $v0, $a1, 0x3` and skips anything below 3, so only real ids are compacted into the caller's buffer; it then fills the remaining positions of the three with -1 (`li $v1, -0x1` / `sh $v1, ($a1)`). A padded position therefore reads back as 0xffff, which is not below 3 and cannot be the slot a new form is written into.

The digivolution-unlock routine F0x8008634c picks the tree by ROSTER SLOT: `lui $v1, 0x8009` / `addiu $v1, -0x6fc4` gives 0x8008903c, `sll $v0, $s4, 0x2` / `addu $v0, $v1` indexes it, and `lw $s7, ($v0)` loads that line's tree pointer into $s3. The record loop then reads the record's first word, resolves it to a profile row halfword at 0x8003ef5c with stride 0x58, and calls ctx+0x2748; `bgez $v0, .L0x000038c8` skips the record when the form is already in the ledger.

The gate block of F0x8008634c, read clause by clause. TWO requirement pairs: `lh $v1, 0x4($s0)` is the first partner, `lh $v1, 0x6($s0)` its required form level, and `slti $v0, $s2, 0x2` with `addiu $s0, 0x4` walks the second pair at +0x8/+0xa. A requirement passes when the partner is in the ledger and its ledger level byte is not below the required level (`slt $v0, $v1` / `beqz $v0, .L0x000037b0`); a fail sets $s1 to -1. Then `lh $v0, 0xc($s3)` is the requirement kind and `beqz $v0, .L0x0000386c` skips the whole stat test when it is zero: `slti $v0, $v1, 0x7` separates kinds 1..6, which read `lh $v0, 0x26($v0)` (a combat stat at 0x26 + 2*kind), from kind 7, which reads `lh $v0, 0x1c($a0)` (the roster level), and kinds 8 and up read `lh $v0, 0x24($v0)` (an elemental stat). Each result is compared with `lh $v1, 0xe($s3)`, the record's threshold.

The record walk is bounded by the tree's own extent: `addiu $v0, $s7, 0x2c0` builds the end pointer 0x2c0 bytes past the tree base, `slt $v0, $s3, $v0` / `bnez $v0, .L0x000036fc` returns to the top of the record loop while the cursor is below it, and the cursor advances `addiu $s3, 0x10` - a 0x10-byte record stride, so 0x2c0 bytes is 44 records per line. After the loop the routine returns 0 (`move_ $v0, $zr`), which is how one call grants one acquisition and no more.

The m2c body of the same routine, checked line by line against the assembly above and agreeing on every clause: tree by `*((arg0 * 4) + 0x8008903C)`, profile rows by `*(((var_s3->unk0 - 1) * 0x58) + 0x8003EF5C)`, ledger skip through unk2748, two requirement iterations, kind dispatch to unk26 / unk1C / unk24, then unk2744 (acquire), unk2738 (read triple), a walk that returns without writing when all three slots are >= 3, and unk273C (set_equipped) only on the write arm. It is the independent read that the routine grants at most one form per call.

The DNA pane's constructor: `lui $v0, 0x8005` / `lw $v0, -0x4bb4($v0)` resolves the service cell 0x8004b44c, `lw $a0, ($s1)` is the party position the pane was built for, the pointer is called and its answer is stored at +0x60 of the fresh object. So +0x60 is a ROSTER SLOT resolved from the party position, not a profile row.

The partner strip's build. `lw $s0, 0x60($s1)` takes the roster slot; the get_equipped cell 0x8004b46c (ctx+0x2738) is called with it as $a0 and sp+0x74 as $a1. Row 0 is then read straight out of the profile table: `lui $v1, 0x8004` / `addiu $v1, -0x10a4` gives 0x8003ef5c and the four shift/add instructions that follow build 0x58 * rosterSlot - 1 in $v0 before `lhu $v0, ($v0)` loads the first halfword of that row into +0x68. So the first row is the roster slot's own base species and the equipped forms follow it.

The other path of F0x80016d94, the routine the DNA pane and the Digivolve form list both call: `sltiu $v0, $a0, 0x3` / `beqz $v0, .L0x80016db8` sends a party position of 3 or more to a bare `jr $ra` whose delay slot holds `li $v0, -0x1`. A position the party does not have answers -1, not the caller's leftover register.

The battle-outcome sweep. `lh $v0, 0x8($s1)` is the position's live current HP; `bgtz $v0, .L0x00002084` leaves a survivor alone. A position at 0 or below instead gets 1 HP written into its roster record at +0x788 (the write-back floor) and four flag bytes cleared with `sb $zr` at +0x6, +0x7, +0x8 and +0x9. The reward participant flag is the byte at +0x6.

The report's divisor: `lbu $v0, 0x6($a0)` reads a row's participant flag, `beqz $v0, .L0x00002cac` skips a cleared row, and only a flagged row reaches `addiu $a2, 0x1`, which increments the count the reward is divided by.

The payout call for a row whose flag was cleared: `jal 0x80084aec` with `move_ $a2, $zr` in the delay slot, so the EXP applier is handed a share of zero. The flagged arm instead stores its own result at +0x64 of the report row, which this path never reaches.

The forced-Tag partner list's row build. Per party position it computes the combatant record at 0x800a4460 + 0x20 * position, reads a byte at +0x1a of it, then `lh $v0, ($s1)` reads the record's leading halfword; `beqz $v0, .L0x8009758c` skips an EMPTY slot and `beq $s0, $v0, .L0x8009758c` skips the ACTING slot. Those two tests are the whole filter - no instruction in the loop reads +0x8, the live HP, so a knocked-out partner keeps its row. The position is stored into the row at +0x5c and the row count at +0x64 of the list.

The list's cursor row word is seeded, not initialised: `lw $v1, 0x54($s2)` takes the caller's cell, `lw $v1, ($v1)` reads the word behind it, and `sw $v1, 0x50($v0)` in the jalr delay slot hands that word to the freshly built list. There is no compare and no clamp against the row count on this path.

The confirm arm. `lw $a0, 0x50($v0)` is the list's cursor row word; the row's member position is read at +0x5c and the combatant record at 0x800a4470 + 0x20 * position is read for `lh $v0, 0x8($v1)`. `beqz $v0, .L0x80097960` returns having done nothing when that live HP is zero, so a fallen partner is refused; otherwise `lw $v0, 0x54($s2)` / `sw $a0, ($v0)` writes the confirmed row word back into the SAME cell the seed read.

Where the Lab's learned-form list comes from. `lw $v0, 0x2718($s0)` resolves the party position to a roster slot and stores it at +0xbc; `lw $v0, 0x2740($s0)` then loads ctx+0x2740, which is the resident F0x80017898 that enumerates the ACQUIRED ledger (see DIGI-C010-form-ledger-api), and calls it with that slot as $a0 and the screen's own buffer at +0x60 as $a1 in the jalr delay slot. Its returned count is stored at +0xb8 in the next call's delay slot.

The membership test F0x80083484 runs for a chart row. It loops `lh $v0, 0x60($a0)` over the learned-form buffer, counting in $v1 and advancing the address by two in the branch delay slot, for the count held at +0xb8; `beq $v0, $a2, .L0x000007f0` returns 1 on the first match. Nothing in this loop consults the unlock rule, the partner's level or its stats - the answer depends only on what is in the learned list.

Shape A (two flags) and shape C (the story step alone), side by side in one overlay. Shape A materialises the flag-API base as `lui $s0, 0x8005` / `addiu $s0, -0x7544` = 0x80048abc and calls the pointer at +0xc (the cell 0x80048ac8) twice, with `li $a1, 0x1` in each jalr delay slot: first set_flag(0x400d, 1), then set_flag(0x7401, 1). Shape C is three instructions that store the step in the `jr $ra` delay slot: `lui $v1, 0x8005` / `li $v0, 0x4` / `jr $ra` / `sw $v0, -0x4c90($v1)`, i.e. 4 into 0x8004b370.

Shape D: the story step first, then one flag. `sw $v0, -0x4c90($v1)` writes 15 into 0x8004b370, and the flag call uses the other calling form - `lui $v0, 0x8005` / `lw $v0, -0x7538($v0)` reaches the same cell 0x80048ac8 directly - to store set_flag(0x8010, 1), with `li $a1, 0x1` in the jalr delay slot.

Shape B: one flag and nothing else. `li $a0, 0x4016` then the displacement form of the flag cell (`lui $v0, 0x8005` / `lw $v0, -0x7538($v0)` = 0x80048ac8) and `li $a1, 0x1` in the jalr delay slot; the routine then returns with no other store.
Shape E: three flags and no step - 0x0c23, then 0x40a4, then 0x7400, each through the base-relative form of the cell 0x80048ac8 with `li $a1, 0x1` in the jalr delay slot.

The first of the two routines outside the five shapes: two flags (0x8028 then 0x8009) and only THEN the story step, 5, stored through `lui $v1, 0x8005` / `li $v0, 0x5` / `sw $v0, -0x4c90($v1)`. It is the same ordered list of writes as shape A, with the step appended rather than the step alone.

The second outlier, and the proof that a CLEAR is a write: five consecutive calls through the cell 0x80048ac8 for 0x1a26, 0x1c4b, 0x1c4c, 0x1c4d and 0x1c4e, each with `move_ $a1, $zr` - not `li $a1, 1` - in the jalr delay slot. A reader that keys on the value literal alone reads five shape-B routines plus an unread tail instead of one routine that clears five flags.

One shape-C routine that stores the step ZERO: `lui $v0, 0x8005` / `jr $ra` with `sw $zr, -0x4c90($v0)` in the delay slot, so the master story ordinal at 0x8004b370 is written with 0. An extractor that treats a zero literal as 'no value' reports this routine as empty; it is a real write, and the one the shipped per-stage ladder did not list.

With STR equal to DEF the base is the power the routine used, 62 = trunc(50*20/16); unscaled it would be 50. A later player hit (move 1, STR 72, power 60, defender DEF 62) had base 69 and final 114; the +45 fits the critical stage with r=42 but the field and affinity inputs were not logged.

In the enemy branch of F0x8009ec94, a3 is the descriptor 0x80042b1c + s0*0xc. The loop runs five times: each species stat halfword (+0xe onwards of the record returned by [0x800a37fc]) is multiplied by the signed halfword at descriptor +0x22, rounded toward zero by the +0xf fixup, shifted right 4, and stored at block +2 onwards. Level is copied from descriptor +0x1c.

The message object's reveal machine F0x8009a514 reaches its only state-3 write (.L0x8009a664 li $v0,0x3) solely through the pad test .L0x8009a618 andi $v0,$s2,0x2000; when the bit is clear it returns with the line still up (.L0x8009a61c). The screen object F0x8009a898 reads that state at .L0x8009ab38 and clears the caller's pointer at .L0x8009ab50 only when it is 3, so callers that wait on the pointer stay blocked until the confirm bit.

On entering a field screen the field calls the screen-id getter through ctx+0x2704, adds 0x1e00 to the id it returns, and calls set_flag through 0x80048ABC+0xc with $a1 = 1. The screen id therefore lands in bank 0x20 at index screen & 0x1ff.

The pause-menu MAP page walks the current server's screen ids and asks get_flag((id & 0xff) | 0x2000, 1) through 0x80048ABC+0x10; a 1 marks the location record the byte table at 0x8009b5fc (index id & 0xff, masked 0x7f) names.

Arriving at Kusanagi Street Corner (screen 0x2D7) logged set_flag(0x20D7, 1) from ra 0x8008ACDC; the next screen logged set_flag(0x2076, 1) from the same return address. Both are 0x1E00 + the screen id.

F0x80015F04(id, flag) is an EQUALITY predicate over possession, not a count: with flag != 0 it returns 1 while either count byte (bag 0x7c+id, worn 0x20f+id) is non-zero, and with flag == 0 it returns the exact mirror, 1 only while both are zero. Both answers are written in a branch delay slot (li $v0,1 / move_ $v0,$zr), so the loaded byte never survives. The raw word at 0x80015f10 is 0x00822021 = addu $a0,$a0,$v0, so the base+id lands in $a0 and the loads are correctly addressed.

F0x800161D8's non-zero arm adds one and holds the byte at 99 (li $v0,0x63 when the sign-extended count reaches 0x64); its zero arm removes one, floors at 0, and only when the carried byte was ALREADY zero and the worn byte is non-zero walks the three party slots (pointer at 0x80048D34+0x2718) and then eight roster records at stride 0x3DC gated on record+0x760 >= 3, calling f10, before decrementing the worn byte.

evidence.summary: The battle vertex loop's screen write. It ctc2's the point's three words into GTE R0-R4, loads the projection distance from the point struct at +0x58 into R15, runs the GTE perspective transform (c2 0x486012 = RTPS) at :775, and stores GTE[25], GTE[26], GTE[27] = SX1, SY1, SZ1 into sp+0x10/+0x14/+0x18, which it then adds to the point's own +0x10/+0x12/+0x14. So the console's screen X is row 0 of the GTE view matrix divided by depth and its screen Y is row 1, with no per-side term anywhere in the loop: the handedness is decided entirely by the basis F0x8002a1ac builds.

The view builder takes the shot's vertical component as (eye.y - target.y) over the eye-to-target length and builds the basis through the two elementary rotations F0x8002a0dc (axis codes 0x78/0x79) composed by F0x8002afbc, writing a row-major 3x4. Because the camera struct stores Y DOWN (the same frame the fighter slots use: y = -hover), the +Y it hands the basis is the screen-DOWN axis, which is what makes docs/research/fight-3d/battle-camera.md section 1's right = cross(up=+Y, forward) read as screen right. The vertical sign is readable here; the horizontal cross-product handedness is section 1's own 0.3-degree agreement with the live matrix D0x80081338, not a fresh read of the axis-code switch.

Every reachable one is inside a writer call that moves the byte ONCE per call, and none of them counts a halfword. The pause page's equip-apply F0x8009A3E8 (file 0x17738) does displace `worn[old] -= 1; bag[old] += 1` once and equip `worn[new] += 1; bag[new] -= 1` once; the merchant's F0x8008C800 (file 0x9B50) is the same routine with the same two arms; F0x800161D8's depletion branch has a single `sb $v0, 0x20f($v1)` at 0x800162F8 reached once however many hands f10 cleared. FIGHTSTG_F0x8009a514 is the joke owner's three-phase reveal machine over self+0x10. phase 0 (.L0x8009a568) advances only while self+0x88 != 0, the flag F0x8009a734 sets (:24517). phase 1 (.L0x8009a580) stamps self+0x98 from [0x8004df98](), sets the gap self+0x94 = 3 and shows child self->+0x24[self+0x8c + 1] through its +0x144. phase 2 (.L0x8009a5d8) waits until the frame counter passes the stamp, adds 1 to self+0x8c, returns to phase 1 while self+0x8c < self+0x90 (the line count F0x8009a734 writes in F0x8009a6bc's delay slot, :24575), and otherwise tests pad bit 0x2000: on the press it plays 0x0004001c, sets the prompt gate self+0xac in the delay slot of that test (.L0x8009a620), adds 1 to self+0x9c, and either runs self+0xc0 or writes self+0x0c = 3 when the word at self+0x64 + 4*self+0x9c is zero -- which it always is, nothing writes entry 1 -- so the gag closes on the first Circle and no timeout exists.

FIGHTSTG_F0x8009a734(self, id) builds the joke gag's two lines from the table at 0x800a35e4: entry id is the halfword pair 0x0073+id / 0x0001+id, id = 2*shuffledJoke + (rand()&1) from .L0x8009aafc/.L0x8009ab04. evidence.summary: The pause EQUIP page's row admission is TWO routines. F0x80099F84 (service slot [0x8009B5EC]) dispatches on the six-word table at 0x8009A7E4 = 6,7,5,5,4,4 for rows 0..5 = head, body, right hand, left hand, accessory, accessory; 6 and 7 are F0x8009A1BC(4)/(5) (directories 2 then 3, descriptor exactly 4 or 5), 5 is F0x80099FF8 for BOTH hand rows (descriptor in the four bytes at 0x8009B5F8 = 01 02 03 07), and 4 is the shared resident directory of accessories whole. F0x8009A344 (service slot [0x8009B5F0]) then admits an id unless the member's starter line is not in the record's wear mask (equip-stat byte 4, read through the item record's word-0 pointer, shifted by screen+0x5C which is rosterSlot(partyPosition)), or it reads descriptor 1 in row 3, or descriptor 2 in row 2; item id -1, the take-off row, is always admitted. So a two-handed weapon is offered in BOTH hand rows, a one-hand 'Left or Right' weapon in both, a shield only in the left (it is LISTED in the right-hand row too, refused and greyed after the accepted ones), and an accessory only in the two accessory rows. All three builders call the directory walker with a POSITIVE kind, so a worn-only piece is not listed. F0x8008744C writes the take-off row at the list's first halfword unconditionally, so it is there even on an empty slot.

evidence.summary: Nothing on the hit path changes a struck fighter's colour, alpha or palette. The only submitter of a fighter's triangles is FIGHTSTG_F0x80085110, reached only through the model object's +0xA4 method that FIGHTSTG_F0x8008610c installs once, whose sole caller is the fighter-model builder FIGHTSTG_F0x80083e0c (:1209); it takes the model object and an 8-word world matrix (F0x80085f3c :3289-3299 copies the matrix into model+0x84..0xa0) and no colour, alpha or blend argument. Inside it nothing stores to a primitive's colour bytes; the per-frame writes are positions and texture coordinates (:2783-2812 copies u/v bytes from the model's table at model+0x80, each plus a u or v page offset - lead correction 2026-10-04, the helper had labelled these as vertex colours); the command descriptor byte that would carry the semi-transparency flag is the constant 0x0c (textured) or 0x09 (flat), chosen by whether the primitive is textured and never by a frame or a damage state. op1 (F0x8008b69c :8769-8793) stores only the child action actor's +0x50 (side) and +0x54 (clip); the damage-reaction machine F0x8008d3b4 (:10676-11129) stores only the attack object's +0x14/+0x18/+0x74/+0x78/+0x7c, the result block's +0x10/+0x12, and the child actor's +0x50/+0x54/+0x64/+0x68/+0x6c/+0x70. The one VRAM-picture mechanism on a fighter is the animated texture patch (F0x8008b118, F0x8008b200), whose slots 0 and 1 are the eye and whose only hit-driven change is the forced-shut variant 2 on state codes 4..11. There is no rand_u16 call anywhere in the camera/HUD range 0x80090c44-0x80093xxx, so a landed hit brings a cut to an authored op5 shot and no shake.

The merchant writes the two item count arrays and the wallet AS THE SESSION RUNS, and its four leave states write none of them. Census of every byte store in the overlay: `sb ...,0x7c(...)` (held count, base 0x80048D34 + 0x7C + id) at stitshop.s:1903 (BUY commit, file 0x1DA0), :4162 and :4170 (SELL commit, file 0x40EC and 0x410C), :9980 (displace arm of F0x8008C800, file 0x9BD4), :10034 (its two-handed hand pick, 0x9CAC), :10073 (its accessory pair loop, 0x9D48) and :10088 (its equip arm, 0x9D84); `sb ...,0x20f(...)` (worn count) at :9979, :10027, :10066 and :10087, all inside that same routine, with the overlay's only worn READ at :7310; `sw ...,0x6c(...)` (the wallet word) at :1926, :4151 and :4155. The root state table at file 0x4E8 sends states 20-23 to file 0x90E4 (line 9280), 0x91B0 (:9331), 0x9280 (:9383) and 0x92C4 (:9400), and those four arms contain no store to 0x7C, 0x20F or 0x6C: state 20 calls the fold (jal 0x800835c4 at :9284), hides two windows and calls service slots before `j 0x8008bf60` (:9329), state 21 reaches that same return at :9381, state 22 steps the main state on through `j 0x8008bf90` (:9417), and state 23 falls into the dispatcher's own epilogue at 0x92E0 (:9416). The `sw ...,0x7c($s2)` sites at :2362, :2613, :2616 and :4527 are a WORD at the same offset of a screen/widget record (beside +0x78, +0x8C, +0x9C, +0xAC), not the item array.

The whole of F0x8002b40c is one GTE write and a return: no compare, no branch, no clamp. It is the only place the engine puts a value into the projection-distance register, and it is what the close-up face box's own view calls once per frame with the halfword its framing record carries (view+0x158 = F0x8001e470, exe/fns.s:15748 -> F0x8002998c -> here), and what the main battle camera's view calls with its focal distance (FIGHTSTG_F0x80092158, pro/fightstg.s:157bc-157cc, lw $a2, 0x84($s3)). So a value the record carries reaches the GTE exactly as read: a zero is a zero, and nothing on the path decides to skip the draw because of it. There is no SetGeomScreen and no BIOS call anywhere on this route.

evidence.summary: Confirming a form in battle runs ONE store into the fighter's battle record: `sh $v1,($s0)` in the delay slot of `jal 0x800a69f0` writes the species id the command screen parked at its +0x64 (`lhu $v1,0x64($v1)`) into live record 0x800A4470 + 0x20*actor at +0x00. The routine then calls the participant marker 0x800A69F0 (which sets byte 6 of the word at 0x80042B84 + position*4, and byte 7 + row for the equipped form taken), the shared Blast/T ag release 0x800A7328 (which, only while the reserved second form stands, zeroes the gauge at 0x80042B1C + rosterKey*2 + 0x58, clears record +0x1A and up to two timeline counters), starts the change presentation `jal 0x8008a7f4` with a1 = 0 and stores it at ctx+0x1C, and steps the turn on with `sw $v0,0x14($s1)`. NO HP, MP, stat, technique or ailment value is written anywhere on the path, and nothing writes the persistent roster record at 0x80049494 + slot*0x3DC. The battle then shows the change presentation and, on the following tick (phase word 1), a message panel from F0x8009A298 with the species looked up from live record +0x10 and its name byte +0x55 read: `sw $zr,0x50($s1)` / `sw $v0,0x54($s1)` / `msg->0xAC(msg, 0xC, &ctx+0x50)`, which is presentation selector 0x0C with the payload {0, profile id}.

The numbers a changed form fights with are re-derived on every READ, not written at the change. F0x8009EC94 compares the roster row's own species id (`lhu $v0,($s0)`) with the live combatant record's form id (`lh $a0,($s3)`) and `beq` skips the addition when they are equal; while they differ it ADDS the live form's own species-record core stats from +0x02 (five iterations) and its seven element values from +0x0E, plus the same form's six core-stat bytes from +0x2C, onto the caller's block. That is why the panel's page zero can show the acting Digimon's roster numbers plus a candidate form's base without anything being stored, and why a manual Digivolve leaves HP, MP and the stored stats alone.

evidence.summary: The second call writes four halfwords/bytes, none of them a stat, and three of them only while Blast's reserved second form is standing. It looks the position's roster key up twice ([0x800A4374] = F0x8009BC94 with code 0x13, :1379-1381; [0x8004B44C] = F0x80016D94, :1395-1404) and tests the record's Blast-active byte `lbu $v1,0x1a($s1)` (:1408) - zero returns at :1411. While it is set: `sh $zr,($v0)` (:1402) frees the queued status event the first lookup found (the queue is 99 entries of 0x1C at 0x800A3868, entry +0x0 = code, 0 = free), `sh $zr,0x58($v1)` (:1408) with v1 = 0x80042B1C + 2*rosterKey zeroes that roster slot's Blast gauge at 0x80042B74, `sb $zr,0x1a($s1)` (:1409) clears the Blast-active byte, and the routine then always makes a second lookup with code 8 and frees that entry too (`sh $zr,($v0)`, :1421). The live combatant record is 0x800A4470 + 0x20*position and its +0x06/+0x08 are max/current HP and +0x0A/+0x0C max/current MP; NONE of those six halfwords is written here, and neither is any stat, technique or ailment word - the only record byte touched is the +0x1A flag itself, which is why a manual Digivolve leaves HP, MP and the stored stats exactly as they were and the numbers a new form fights with are re-derived on every read by F0x8009EC94.

The pad service's logical-button accessor F0x80018980 takes TWO arguments, (port, logicalId), and returns mem[0x8004B7D0 + logicalId + port*0x1C0 + 0xA4]. The assembly LISTING renders the instruction at 0x80018994 as `addu $a1, $v1`, which reads as if $a1 were clobbered and only the port survived, but the word is 0x00a32821 whose rs field is $a1 and whose rd is also $a1, so the renderer elided a source register equal to the destination and the instruction is `addu $a1, $a1, $v1`. The overlays' hottest idiom depends on the surviving argument: `la_ block` / `lw f, 0x3f4(block)` / `jalr f` (the PRESSED word, F0x80018854) / `li $a1, id` / `lw f, 0x408(block)` / `jalr f` / `move_ $s0, $v0` IN THE JALR DELAY SLOT / `srav $s0, $s0, $v0` / `andi $s0, 1`. The delay slot runs before the jump, so it captures the pressed word into $s0 before the map call overwrites $v0 with the bit index; the caller then shifts the pressed word by the index and tests bit 0. pro/stitshop.s:9148-9160 does this for logical 4 (Up), :9169 for 6 (Down), :9205 for 0x0d (confirm, sound 0x8004503C) and :9229 for 0x0e (back, sound 0x800450BD); pro/cardgame.s:1223-1230 is the same shape. engine/systems/pad-block.ts documents this and tests/native-screen-pad-input.test.js asserts both the identity map and that the +0x408 cell answers a logical id. CONSEQUENCE: the merchant reads the PRESSED word (the edge), not the held word, so a key held for one frame is one press and a key the player holds does not repeat unless the screen also reads the repeat word at +0x3fc.

evidence.locator: L8798-L8988 @0x8008b60c (F0x8008b60c, the shop ROOT draw routine)
evidence.summary: The shop root's draw routine (F0x8008b60c, stitshop.s:8798-8988) reads its picture-service methods out of the context F0x8001f648 builds (exe-decomp/c/F0x8001f648.c:24-35, giving sp+0x84=setOrigin 0x8001ecbc, sp+0x8c=setLayer 0x8001ed34, sp+0x94=drawSprite 0x8001ed6c, sp+0x9c=setScale 0x8001f5d0, sp+0xa4=setPos 0x8001f608), calls setOrigin(640,256) (:8807-8813) and setLayer(handle,1) (:8810-8813), and then runs FOUR arms that each load a different 12-bit word from the root object and gate one plate on it: +0x70 gates clip 1 at (0x16,0x12) (:8814 load, :8816 'beqz $a0, .L0x00008a08' branches PAST the draw, :8835 'li $a1, 0x1'); +0x80 gates clip 2 at (0xD6,0x0F) (:8841, :8843, :8870); +0x90 gates clip 5 at (0xA9,0x26) (:8876, :8878, :8905); +0xA0 gates clip 0 at (0xC6,0xC4) (:8911, :8913, :8941). A word of zero skips that plate's draw entirely. A word that is neither zero nor 0x1000 goes into setScale as X with Y and Z held at 0x1000 (:8819-:8823 arm 1, :8846-:8850 arm 2) and is followed by one setPos, and those pivots differ per arm: (0x57,0x19) for the header (:8824/:8828), (0x140,0x18) for the BIT plate (:8851/:8855), (0x140,0x3b) for the BUY/SELL window (:8886/:8890), (0x140,0xd2) for the bottom plate (:8922/:8926). A word of exactly 0x1000 takes a different path in each arm and the four paths are not alike: arm 1 branches to :8829 and makes NEITHER call, while arms 2, 3 and 4 branch to :8858, :8893 and :8929 and still call setScale with 0x1000 in all three slots, skipping only the setPos. The fifth clip carries no such gate: from :8947 the routine calls setLayer(obj+0x50, 7) (:8951 'li $a1, 0x7'), steps the scroll offset obj+0x58 by one through the every-other-frame flag at obj+0x5c and wraps it at 0x60 (:8952-:8966), calls setScale(0x1000,0x1000,0x1000) (:8967-:8972) and draws clip 20 at (obj+0x58, obj+0x58) (:8980 'lw $a2, 0x58($s0)', the y copied in the jalr delay slot at :8984). The only two branches left in that arm test the scroll flag and the wrap, and both paths reach that same drawSprite. Consequence for a player: with the four words reading 0x1000 the routine's FIRST picture already carries the backdrop and all four plates, so a renderer that paints that picture before the shop's sheet has arrived does not show a smaller fade, it shows the fade with its backdrop and every plate missing. The clip ids and positions were already in docs/research/ui/shop-system-decompiled.md section 3b; what is new here is the four per-plate words and the ungated backdrop arm. Which routine writes those four words, and whether they are the root state's greeting fade (this document's root state list calls it a greeting fade without naming the words), is not established by this record.

evidence.summary: Bank 0x6a + language is the disc's ESITMNAM.BIN, the item-name bank. A bank id IS the disc's file index, so the research repo's own index table has to carry the name at that id: LBA_ESITMNAM_BIN_IDX = 108 and 0x6a + 2 (English) = 108. The same check runs over the four banks whose English images the walker does ship -- 0x4e -> 80 (ESDIGNAM), 0x7f -> 129 (ESMFIGHT), 0x9b -> 157 (ESSKLINF), 0xa2 -> 164 (ESSKLNAM) -- so the naming convention is pinned by four known-good cases rather than assumed, and each of those four also has its language file's entry count matching its shipped .bin (251, 145, 220, 444). Bank 0x6a's own disc image ships too, at web/assets/data/shop-banks/108.bin (not under battlecmd/), and its u32 entry count is 403, which tools/extract_battle_text.py::verify_bank_layout() now checks for all six banks, the decoded language file against whichever image the walker ships. The exe's bank directory then says bank 0x6a + 2 occupies sectors 2422..2425 (4 sectors), and a token-size estimate of the 403 esitmnam entries in the game's own encoding lands on exactly 4 sectors; the estimate reproduces all three other name banks (0x4e 2, 0x7f 2, 0xa2 3) and over-runs both description banks (0x9b measures 3 against 4, 0x63 measures 6 against 8), so it is applied to name banks only. The battle message panel's VM method +0xac (FIGHTSTG_F0x80099588) takes a page KIND in $a1 and a payload pointer in $a2. The kind is bounded by `sltiu $v0, $v1, 0x16` over `kind - 1` (the SHORT form of sltiu $v0, $v0, $v1; $v1 is the subtracted value, set by addiu $v1, $s0, -0x1), so kinds 1..22 have an arm in the 22-word jump table at .L0x8008318c and everything else lands on .L0x8009a204, which writes no text and hides both lines through the element's +0x144 with a1 = 0. Kind 0 is therefore NOT arm 1.

A jalr delay slot overwrites $a1: at the technique machine FIGHTSTG_F0x8008ee84 step 0 the load `lw $a1, 0x10($s1)` is dead, because the jalr's delay slot is `addiu $a1, 0x5`, so that call site asks for kind 5 and not for the kind the dead load would have implied. The payload it writes is the technique id in word 0 (lbu $v0, 0x70($s1) at :12546) and the technique's name index in word 1 (:12532 lh $v0, 0x8($v0) off the skill record).

A branch delay slot runs on BOTH paths, so a call site with no li of its own still has a kind: `bgtz $v0, .L0x8008e650` carries `li $a1, 0x14` in its delay slot, so the +0xac call at .L0x8008e658 (the taken path) asks for kind 20, while the fallthrough's own `li $a1, 0x4` at .L0x8008e628 asks for kind 4 at .L0x8008e62c. Kind 20's arm .L0x8009a050 re-enters the VM with kind 4 (`move_ $a0, $s4` / `li $a1, 0x4` / `jal FIGHTSTG_F0x80099588`), writes 21 into the step ring and then hides both lines.

FIGHTSTG_F0x80091534 is the signature-weapon machine and it owns three page kinds off its effect opcode: opcode 5 asks for kind 17 (li $a1, 0x11, :15005) with the stolen ItemId in payload word 0 (sh $v0, 0x18($s0), :15000), opcode 12 asks for kind 18 (:15056) with payload[2] = 0 (:15052) and opcode 32 asks for kind 18 again (:15087) with payload[2] = $s7 = 1 (li $s7, 0x1, :12568), which is what picks esmfight[0x8f] over esmfight[0x22]. Opcode 33 asks for kind 19 (:15171) with payload[1] = 0/1/2 from the stat-bit test at :15093-:15107, so the arm's `addiu $a2, 0x49` reaches esmfight 0x49/0x4a/0x4b. No other overlay builds a message panel: pro/fightstg.s has 65 `jal FIGHTSTG_F0x8009a298` sites, pro/wfightmn.s has 23 and pro/wfightts.s has none.

Three arms of the 22 have no caller in either battle overlay: kinds 6, 11 and 21. Every call-shaped `lw $v0, 0xac($aN)` site in pro/fightstg.s and pro/wfightmn.s was read (97 sites), and two further reads are NOT calls to this VM: .L0x8009a3e4 is followed by `beqz $v0, .L0x8009a4b8`, a null test on the method pointer, and .L0x8009d31c calls through [0x800a4580 + 0xac] in FIGHTSTG_F0x8009d2c4, whose $s2 is the battle manager (addiu $s2, 0x4580, :27452), not a panel. Kind 18's own second index is chosen by `lw $v0, 0x8($s2)` / `bnez` on the THIRD payload word, and kind 16 writes three numbers with the third being the product of the first two (mult $a2, $v0, :23914 then move_ $a2, $s0, :23931).
