claims.statement: Neither Digimon Arena floor can start the five scripted battle records it ships, so the tournament has no round-to-round advancement in the shipped data. The records are real: the rate-0 block at descriptor +0x18 holds screen ids 253-257 on s232 and 258-262 on s233, closed at five by zero slots 5-7 (ARENA-C012). The only routine that starts such a record is FIELDSTG F0x800927a0, reached through the set_flag dispatcher's bank-0x74 arm via the pointer at 0x8009b6a4; dw2003_pro_fieldstg data.rs places 0x800927a0 at file offset 0x189f4, which is exactly RAM 0x8009b6a4 at load base 0x80082cb0, re-deriving statically the pointer identity ARENA-C011 left resting on a research note. F0x800927a0 takes the record index as its only argument and keeps no counter, so a round number can only come from its caller. Both arena floors' stage descriptors store an encounter zone-group selector (+0x20) but no story-step program (+0x14), no event table (+0x24) and no cast list (+0x4c), so neither floor carries an event hook, a step program or an NPC - the three shipped mechanisms that write a flag id. The arena's tournament presentation state exists regardless: wstag233's descriptor overrides the stage BGM to the arena track when the master progress ordinal is 0x26 and flag 0x1a0a is set.
claims.notes: Three gaps keep this at partially_verified rather than verified. (1) Only the first 64 KB of FIELDSTG_PRO is disassembled in ~/ddw3, so a writer inside the undisassembled remainder is excluded by no text search performed here. (2) The 0x7400 matcher finds ids built as a single immediate; an id computed into a register - base plus round number, precisely the shape a ladder would use - is invisible to it. None was found among the 72 hits, but their absence elsewhere is not proven. (3) The NPC dialogue census is taken from walker-extracted scene data (authority 6), not from the original set_ptr tables. A controlled runtime check - entering s233 at ordinal 0x26 with flag 0x1a0a set and observing whether anything starts a battle - would settle it directly and was not run. Corroborating but not evidence: the Asuka arena receptionist's shipped lines say registration is closed for maintenance. || RUNTIME CONFIRMATION 2026-08-13 (authority 1, Windows PCSX-Redux build 314): driven onto the live s233 arena floor in the tournament state (ordinal 0x26, flag 0x1a0a set) via savestate 3 on s330 with its unconditional op-1 warp steps repointed to screen 632 (script tools/windows-rig/arena-s233-entry.lua). Read live: scene+0x14 (step program)=0, +0x24 (event table)=0, +0x4c (cast list)=0, while +0x20=0x800a6478 and its rate-0 block held slots 258,259,260,261,262,0,0,0 - the five opponents loaded with no trigger table of any kind. The stage walked in from (s330) HAS both a step program and NPCs, so those nulls are not stale reads. BGM read 5/0x60140000, the arena track wstag233's descriptor selects only in that ordinal+flag state, so the game agreed the tournament was on. The stage left the encounter driver module gate at 0; after re-arming it, two full sweeps of the floor with confirm and cancel presses started nothing (stayed on lba 595, no battle). The same session read the live warp table: screen 632 carries lba 595 (WSTAG233) in the normal region and lba 2224 (WSTAG927) in the ordinal-0x2d alias region, confirming the two-room structure at runtime. Captures: docs/research/field/captures/arena-s233-2026-08-13/. This closes limitation (3) and the practical force of (1) and (2); a writer inside undisassembled resident code remains formally unexcluded, so the claim stays partially_verified pending the review gate. || PLACEHOLDER PARTIES 2026-08-13: joining the five s233 records against extracted encounter parties shows screens 258, 259, 260 and 261 are each a single Kunemon, while 262 is the real boss party Datamon/Bulbmon/Armageddemon. Four identical starter-tier stubs are unauthored placeholders, so the ladder's opponents were never written, not merely left untriggerable. || PLAYER-DOCUMENTATION CROSS-CHECK (navigation lead, authority 6, NOT proof): PAL post-game guides describe the arena as one match - beat the four Amaterasu Leaders in the field, then talk to Arena Reception to fight the World Champion - and community Q&A states the US release has no tournament at all. This disc is SLES03936 (PAL). No source describes a multi-round arena ladder, so the check corroborates rather than falsifies the claim. || SCOPE CORRECTION 2026-08-13: the game CANCELS the tournament in dialogue, so its absence is authored at the story level and this claim must not be read as 'the developers forgot'. The Asuka Arena Reception (s230 npc 32) carries both entry-rule lines (estalk05 #434/#337 'you need the four City Badges', #457 partner-less variant) and closed-for-maintenance lines (#437/#438/#441), and the desk onlookers react to the cancellation (#475, #502/#503). Whether arena matches were built and cut, or the cancellation was always the design and the five records are leftover scaffolding, is NOT established and this claim does not choose. What the claim asserts is unchanged and unaffected: nothing can start the five records, and four of the five opponents are unauthored Kunemon placeholders.

claims.statement: docs/research/audio/soundtst-all-categories.json is INCOMPLETE. It carries 201 sounds across categories 0-69, while a structural walk of the decoded tables yields 231 sounds across 71 categories. It omits category 70 (TTLBGM, archive id 71, containing TITLEBGM / 0x611c0000) entirely and undercounts eighteen further categories, among them BGM011 (5 rather than 3), CBTL00 (5 rather than 3), ENV001 (8 rather than 4) and ENV206 (6 rather than 3). Its category-0 rows are correct. Separately, docs/research/audio/gen_soundtst_ids.py contains TWO defects that cancel: its word regex accepts only `.word 0x...` and therefore drops every symbolic terminator name pointer, and its terminator test compares the record against {0, 0}. Because the dropped word reads back as 0, the walk happens to stop in the right place, which is why its 113 common-bank records are correct. Repairing only the regex would silently over-run every array. tools/extract_soundtst.py replaces both: it reads symbolic words, tests the packed_id field as the overlay does, and asserts the three-table tiling so a wrong category count fails instead of emitting. Its category-0 output matches the trusted soundtst-common-ids.json on all 113 names and ids with zero mismatches.

claims.statement: soundtst is fully decoded and byte-accounted across its 0x2d98 bytes in eight functions and four data regions: file 0x0000-0x0004 the zero word every terminator points at; 0x0004-0x16c0 name strings, whose tail holds the screen's own heading at 0x167c, title at 0x16ac and cursor at 0x16bc; 0x16c0-0x20c4 code; 0x20c4-0x2a34 the sound arrays; 0x2a34-0x2b50 the array pointers; 0x2b50-0x2d90 the category table; 0x2d90-0x2d98 a UI service descriptor. The screen is a three-step flow driven by base state1: state1 == 0 the category list (F0x800848bc), state1 == 1 the archive loader (F0x80084808), state1 == 2 the sound list (F0x800844a8), with state0 == 3 leaving for the Stage Select. Both list screens share the mover F0x8008443c(self, delta, &cursor, &scroll) with the row count on the stack: the cursor is an ABSOLUTE row index clamped to 0..count-1, and the scroll then slides to keep it inside an EIGHT-row window (scroll = cursor-7 past the bottom, scroll = cursor past the top). Fields are +0x50/+0x54/+0x58 for the category list and +0x60/+0x64/+0x68 for the sound list, with +0x5c holding the chosen archive id, +0x6c the playing flag and +0x70 the s16 play handle. Geometry is entirely code-traced from eleven class-A widgets built by F0x8001ae38(0x1000, 1, x, y): title at (16, 30), heading at (32, 50), eight rows at (48, 70 + 16*i), cursor at (32, 70). This differs from stagslct, which stores the row within its window and shows fourteen rows at a 12 pixel pitch.

claims.statement: The soundtst overlay carries three tables that tile exactly. At file 0x20c4 sit 71 per-category sound arrays of 8-byte records {char *name, u32 packed_id}, each terminated by a record whose packed_id is 0; at file 0x2a34 sit 71 pointers, one per category; at file 0x2b50 sit 72 category records {char *name, s32 archive_id}, being 71 real categories plus a terminator whose archive_id is 0. Record shape is proven from the overlay's own code rather than assumed: the play path takes the id from +4 (file 0x19e8), the row drawer takes the drawn name from +0 (file 0x1a98), and both count loops test the second word for zero (file 0x186c for sounds, 0x1c54 for categories). THE CATEGORY COUNT IS 71, established by mutual agreement of the three regions: 0x2a34 + 71*4 == 0x2b50 and 0x2b50 + 72*8 == 0x2d90, and the sound arrays span exactly 0x20c4..0x2a34 with no gaps. Category 0 is COMMON with archive id 1 and 113 sounds; the remaining 70 are per-VAB banks of 1 to 8 sounds; 231 sounds in total. TERMINATOR TRAP: an array terminator is {name_ptr = 0x80082cb0, packed_id = 0}, where the name pointer aims at the overlay's leading zero word (the empty string), NOT {0, 0}. Because that pointer equals the overlay base the disassembler renders it as `.word D0x80082cb0`, so a regex matching only `.word 0x...` drops it and reads {0,0}.

There are four routes and no fifth: (1) the new game, F0x80016E6C, granting one copy of each of the 40 ids at 0x8004B49C by direct jal; (2) buying a card, stcrdshp 0x8008770c, one call with a quantity of 1 followed by the price being subtracted from the money field at +0x6C; (3) opening a booster pack, stcrdshp 0x80084dbc, six calls in a bounded loop followed by a decrement of the pack-stock byte at +0x7C, which shows the booster is implemented and lives in the card shop; and (4) a game-state write in bank 0x92, dispatcher F0x800165AC arm at 0x8001683c, whose flag index is the card id and whose written value chooses give (non-zero, one copy through the same pointer) or take (zero, decrement and floor at zero). Route 4 is also the only thing in the game that removes a card. Because all four end in F0x80016E2C, which raises the album flag at +0x4DF, everything obtained from any source is recorded in the Card Album.
claims.coverage: The word 'every' rests on three complementary corpus-wide searches over the 590,137-line original assembly, each of which would have exposed a fifth route, plus the pointer image. First, the pointer is read in exactly one place: code-search "8004b454" returns 2 hits, both the lui/lw pair inside F0x80016314. Second, the routines are called in exactly the places named: code-search "80016314" returns 3 hits, of which one is the label, one the prologue and one the single jal at L7123; code-search "80016e6c" returns 2 hits, both the starter grant's own label and prologue, so it is only ever reached through its own pointer at 0x8004b458, whose one reader code-search "0x2724(" locates at fns.s L7439. Third, the offset form the shop uses was enumerated separately: code-search "0x2720" returns 23 hits in 17 files, of which exactly two are instructions and both are in stcrdshp.s - the buy at L4766 and the pack loop at L2122 - the other 21 being coincidental .word data in smdldata and five wstag overlays, each of which was read and classified by hand. Independently, the existing claim's own enumeration of the four stores to the owned-count array at +0x3A2 bounds the write side, and a re-run of code-search "0x3a2(" reproduces it at 14 hits in 4 files with all four stores inside F0x80016314 and F0x80016E2C. The residual risk is the standard one: a call through a differently spelled or register-computed address would be invisible to all of these, which is why the claim is scoped to routes reachable by symbol, by the +0x2720/+0x2724 context offsets, or by the flag dispatcher.
limitations: Nothing here was observed on the running original; every statement is read from the original assembly and the shipped pointer image.

No shipped writer of game-state bank 0x92 turned up in the extracted story-step or dialogue data (flag_setters.json, story_steps.json, talk_item_grants.json, npc_flag_sets.json all return zero for that bank), so the story-side card grant is decoded as a mechanism without a located use. Nine of the 24 were mentioned in no document and no prior claim. The marker sprite's three: F0x80096180 installs F0x80096144 set-position at +0x68, F0x80096160 scale-out at +0x6C and F0x80096150 start-oneshot at +0x70, and F0x80095e58 reads +0x54/+0x56 as the draw position and clamps the frame at 7 when +0x63 is set. The element panel's two: F0x80096828 installs F0x800967F8 start-oneshot at +0x6C and F0x80096808 scale-out at +0x70, its constructor counts 40 cards of one folder into six element buckets, and +0x68 on that object holds the scale-tween counter rather than a method pointer, so the panel installs two methods and not three. The colour wash's four: F0x800a367c installs F0x800A3548 set-colour at +0x68, F0x800A3558 start-fade at +0x6C, F0x800A35A4 is-idle at +0x70 and F0x800A35B0 close at +0x74, which is set/start/is-finished/close read out of the tick F0x800a3488 rather than assumed from the slot shape: the starter copies the live colour to +0x61, stores target at +0x5E, countdown at +0x54/+0x58 and hold flag at +0x5D, the tick interpolates on exactly those and writes state 0 when the countdown ends with the hold flag off, is-idle returns state == 0, and close writes state 2. Three more are the duel object's own already-established methods at +0x810 pile shuffle, +0x814 card sort and +0x818 per-side summon commit. The last twelve are further board-view slots: +0xEBC slide-panel-main-out, +0xEC0 slide-panel-main-in, +0xECC hide-player-panels, +0xED0 turn-marker-grow-in with mode 1, scale 0 and a 12-frame timer, +0xED4 turn-marker-shrink-out with mode 3, scale full and a 6-frame timer, +0xEDC place-float-number, +0xEE0 start-float-number-move, +0xEE4 openPrompt already named, +0xEF0 set-prompt-cursor, +0xEF4 open-prompt-b, +0xF0C card-start-move-silent already named, +0xF34 card-start-hold, +0xF38 card-start-effect, and +0xF44 which is LEFT UNNAMED because nothing on the object reads the table it fills and its call site was not found.

At the cardgame.s call site 0x80084fd8 the argument is a stack local (a0 = sp+0x18), i.e. the caller is building a 0x54-byte drawing context in its own frame, so the bytes subsequently read at +0x1 and +0x2 of that buffer lie inside the constructed context header and cannot be catalog card data. The claimed cross-overlay 'convergence' of AP/HP through this getter therefore does not constitute independent corroboration of a shared card catalog. This claim does NOT establish that the AP/HP values the walker displays are wrong — only that their documented source is misattributed; the true source (plausibly the 0x80048d34 catalog already cited in the same document for ownership at +0x4df) has not yet been traced.

claims.statement: The Card Folder editor refuses to place a card in a folder slot once four copies of that card are already in that folder. In stcrddek.s the swap confirm branch first compares the chosen card id with the id already in the target slot and skips the gate when they are equal; when they differ it loads the player's owned count for the chosen card (lb 0x3a2), subtracts the working still-available count (lb 0x2fe) - that difference is how many copies are already in this folder - and branches on slti 0x4: below four it writes the chosen id into the slot, at four or more it jumps to editor state 0x3c, which draws card-shop bank string 0x1e, 'Only four of the same card\\nin one folder.'
claims.notes: docs/research/ui/card-folder-editor-2026-08-14.md sec 4. Independently matches the community-documented rule (four per folder, nine owned), which was not used as evidence.
claims.coverage: The owned-count array 0x3a2 is referenced at exactly two lines in stcrddek.s (L1746 in the availability builder F0x800847c0, L3293 here); this is the only one followed by a subtraction and a comparison, so no second copy limit exists in this overlay. The refusal state's string index was read from the state machine's own draw call (state 0x3d, bank [0x8005cca8]+0x32 index 0x1e) and resolved against escrdshp.toml, the bank F0x8008a100 actually requests.
claims.frontier_rationale: The folder editor screen has no frontier of its own; this is the placement rule the screen enforces, recorded against card-battle because it is a card rule rather than chrome. Related chrome corrections are filed under ui-chrome/UI-Q002.

claims.statement: Editing a folder does not change what the player owns. The per-card owned-copy array at 0x80048d34+0x3a2 is loaded twice in stcrddek.s - once to build the working still-available table and once for the four-copy gate - and stored to nowhere in the overlay, so putting a card in a folder does not consume it and taking one out does not grant one. The editor's only change to a folder is to overwrite the highlighted slot with the chosen card id; availability is recomputed as owned minus placed rather than tracked, so the displaced card becomes placeable again immediately.
claims.notes: docs/research/ui/card-folder-editor-2026-08-14.md sec 5. The card-count decrement routine F0x80016314 is decoded in docs/research/ui/card-album-screen-2026-08-14.md and is not reached from this overlay.
claims.coverage: The absence is scoped to one overlay and one array: a regex over all lines of ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003/pro/stcrddek.s for the token 0x3a2 returns exactly two lines, L1746 (lbu) and L3293 (lb), both loads, and no store instruction mentions the offset. It does not claim anything about other overlays, and the walker's own folder model is not evidence.

claims.statement: STARTING A NEW GAME ZEROES THE WHOLE SAVE BLOCK, so the card collection and the album always start empty. F0x80016A94, the New Game routine, calls the resident zero-fill helper F0x80017CB0 with the save context base 0x80048D34 and a length of 0x26C4 as its very first action, before it writes a single field and before it calls the setup routine F0x80016BAC that names the folders and runs the starter grant. The helper's whole body is a zero store loop with no other behaviour. This closes the last open question about the album's lifetime, which earlier passes had reserved for a runtime observation: the answer does not depend on whether a save was loaded first, because the clear is unconditional. Note the asymmetry: the clear covers 0x26C4 bytes and the memory-card serialiser copies 0x26C0, so the four bytes at +0x26C0..+0x26C3 are cleared on a new game but never written to the card.
claims.coverage: The absolute words are about one short call chain, read end to end rather than sampled. F0x80016A94 is 26 instructions and every one was read; the clear is the first call and no branch precedes it, so no path into the routine skips it. The helper F0x80017CB0 is 21 instructions, also read whole: it contains exactly two store instructions, sb $zero and sw $zero, and no other memory write, which is what licenses calling it a zero-fill rather than a copy. The routine's single caller was established by search rather than assumed - code-search "80016bac" returns 3 hits of which one is the jal at L7310 inside F0x80016A94 - so the setup path cannot be entered without passing the clear.
limitations: The grant sweep is over the walker's GENERATED scene graph, authority 4, not over the original dialogue tables directly. It is calibrated against one independently known count (bank 0x90 = 226) but a scene the generator drops would be invisible to it.
s972 is a stage whose role was not established here; it repeats fifteen of the same grants and is treated as a repeat, not analysed.
The new-game clear is read from the routine's own code. It was not observed, and no capture covers a new game.
Nothing here establishes WHEN each grant fires beyond the dialogue state it sits on; the gates were not analysed.

claims.statement: THIRTY DIALOGUE STATES HAND THE PLAYER A CARD, AND THE FIVE RULE-BEARING DIGIMON CARDS ARE AMONG THEM. This corrects the stated limitation of CARD-COLLECTION-ENTRY-POINTS-2026-08-14, which reported no located use of the bank-0x92 grant; that negative came from searching the item-grant extractions rather than the scene graph. Sweeping all 294 generated scene files, 30 dialogue-state on_close entries write into bank 0x92, across 9 stages, naming 16 distinct cards, and every one writes the value 1, i.e. a give - no shipped state takes a card away. The distribution: Gabumon at the Asuka Inn (s235), one Program card in each of five sector stages (Wire Forest, Kicking Forest, Tranquil Swamp, Mirage Hall, Kulon Pit), ten more on the Circuit Board stages s875 and s885, and fifteen repeats at s972. All five Digimon cards that carry text - RosemonII, MarineAngemon, SaberLeomon, Gryphonmon and Creepymon - are Circuit Board gifts, which explains why the shop shows those five an R1 hint on the line where every other card shows a price: they are not sold. claims.statement: What decides whether a roaming card tamer will duel you, end to end. Their duelling NPC variant is placed only while the player carries the Folder Bag - at s335 the npc-47 variants split on collection flag 0x8192, item 402, whose description reads 'Bag that can fit 3 Card Folders.' - and only inside a story-ordinal window (roster predicate record 3, ordinals 4 to 23 for that tamer). Given the variant, their dialogue ladder pairs a brush-off line gated on flag bank 0x72 being unmet with a challenge line gated on it being met, and only the challenge line carries the bank-0x76/0x78 duel launcher. claims.statement: The species-profile lookup is a two-function pair reached through a shipped pointer. ~/ddw3/rust/dw2003_exe_data/src/data.rs L14919 initialises the resident slot D0x8005cca0 to f0: pub static mut D0x8005cca0 @ "0x8005cca0": *const u32 = unsafe { ptr::addr_of!(f0) }. f0 (exe/f0.s, 0x800134E8) calls f1, returns 0 when f1 returns a negative index, and otherwise returns DIGIMON_PROFILES + idx*0x58, the stride built by shift-and-subtract (idx*2, +idx = 3idx, <<2 = 12idx, -idx = 11idx, <<3 = 88idx). f1 (exe/f1.s, 0x800134AC) is a linear scan of 0x34 profiles at stride 0x58: it loads the unsigned halfword at each profile's offset 0, compares it against its argument, returns that index on the first match, and returns -1 after 0x34 comparisons without a match. So a DigimonProfile record is 0x58 bytes, the table holds 0x34 of them, its key is the leading halfword rather than the array position, and every lookup is a scan. Two consequences follow. First, the acquire path F0x80017924 of DIGI-C010-form-ledger-api calls this pointer with the newly acquired form id and DISCARDS the result -- the next instruction reloads $v0 with 1 -- so that call is not the source of any value the routine stores, and the acquire path is not an announcement. Second, pro/fightstg.s reaches the same pointer and reads fields at +0x1C and +0x8 of the returned profile, so the battle overlay resolves species data through this scan rather than through an index.
claims.notes: Measured with tools/decode_audit.py on 2026-08-10: f0 has 29 callers over 32 call sites, all of them through the resolved pointer rather than a jal, which is why no symbolic caller appears for it. f1 does not appear in that ranking at all because its only caller is f0, whose jal lives in an unindexed hand-annotated file. This corrects a working note made earlier the same day that read the F0x80017924 call as an announcement of a newly acquired form; it is a profile lookup whose result is thrown away.
claims.coverage: The two quantified constants are the loop's own literals, read from exe/f1.s: the bound is slti cur_idx, 0x34 and the advance is addiu cur_ptr, 0x58, so 0x34 records and the 0x58 stride are not counted or inferred. The 0x58 stride is independently re-derived from f0's shift-and-subtract chain in exe/f0.s and the two agree. "Every lookup is a scan" is scoped to these two routines: f0 has no index-taking sibling in exe/f0.s and reaches the table only through f1, which was read in full; no corpus-wide search was run for other readers of DIGIMON_PROFILES, and code-search finds the symbol on only two lines of the original assembly (fns.s L7445-L7446) because overlays address resident data as raw lui/offset pairs. That is also the limitation on the evidence: exe/f0.s and exe/f1.s are hand-annotated files with no address labels, so the research index holds no line from either and neither can be cited by an indexed anchor -- both were read in full from the working tree, 31 and 36 lines. claims.statement: The 16 bytes at pad-record +0x5c, that is object offset 0xa4 + port*0x1c0 + slot*0x70, are a logical-button-to-physical-bit table, and F0x80018980(port, logicalId) is its read accessor. Record +0x5c lies 0x34 bytes past the start of the next 0x70-byte record when expressed from the object base as 0xa4; that is an artefact of the object-relative displacement the compiler emitted, and the per-record layout was resolved from the decoder's own record base D0x8004b818. claims.contradiction_rationale: UI-PADSERVICE-STATIC-TABLE-001 states that the input state lives in per-port records of 0x1c0 bytes. The decoder loads its record base as D0x8004b818 at 0x80018c44 and recovers the containing object as that symbol minus 0x48 at 0x80018c54, so the record array starts at object offset 0x48, not at D0x8004b7d0. Within the record the scaled index is port*0x1c0 PLUS slot*0x70, with the slot field taken from the low two bits of the channel id and the port field masked to one bit, and the reset routine iterates 2 ports by 4 slots. A 0x1c0 span therefore holds four 0x70-byte records, one per multitap slot, and the record itself is 0x70 bytes. The remaining assertions of UI-PADSERVICE-STATIC-TABLE-001 are corroborated here and are not contradicted: the accessors are indexed by controller port, F0x80018854 and F0x80018878 do return two separate 16-bit button words at object +0x48 and +0x4e, and F0x80018980 is the logical-button remap.
claims.statement: Contradicted sub-assertion of UI-PADSERVICE-STATIC-TABLE-001: the controller input state does not live in per-port records of 0x1c0 bytes based at D0x8004b7d0. The pad record is 0x70 bytes, the record array starts at D0x8004b818 (object offset 0x48), and 0x1c0 is the size of a per-port block holding four 0x70-byte multitap-slot records. The port-indexed reading of the accessors, the two 16-bit button words at object +0x48 and +0x4e, and the identification of F0x80018980 as the logical-button remap are corroborated rather than contradicted.
claims.coverage: The contradicted quantity is a single number, the record size, and it was tested three ways: the decoder's own base symbol arithmetic (D0x8004b818 = object + 0x48), the two-term index expression port*0x1c0 + slot*0x70 read in full from the decoder at 0x80018c1c..0x80018c50 and again from the clear path at 0x80018f94..0x80018fbc, and the array extent 0x48 + 8*0x70 = 0x3c8 landing exactly on the next symbol D0x8004bb98. The remaining assertions of the contradicted claim were each re-read against the assembly and left standing rather than being contradicted by association.
limitations: UI-PADSERVICE-STATIC-TABLE-001 was not read from docs/research/evidence/ledger.json by this worker; the researcher was quoted its content in the assignment brief. The contradiction is stated against that quoted wording and should be re-checked against the ledger text before integration.
This entry contradicts one sub-assertion, not the whole claim. Retiring the whole of UI-PADSERVICE-STATIC-TABLE-001 would discard correct content.

claims.statement: The three halfwords the high-fan-in accessors return are the per-frame button words the resident input decoder F0x80018bcc writes into a pad record. At the end of a decode pass it stores the freshly decoded button word at record +0x06, copies the value that was there into record +0x04 as the previous frame's word, and stores new AND (new XOR previous) at record +0x00, which is the set of buttons that went from released to pressed on this frame. Record +0x02 is zeroed at the start of the pass and receives 1 shifted left by a button's physical bit number when that held button's repeat timer elapses. Mapped through the record base D0x8004b818 these are object offsets +0x4e, +0x4c, +0x48 and +0x4a for port block 0 slot 0, so F0x80018854 returns the buttons newly pressed this frame, F0x80018878 returns the buttons currently held, and F0x8001889c returns the auto-repeat pulses, for the port given in the first argument. The routine at 0x80018f44 zeroes object +0x48, +0x4a and +0x4e for a channel whose controller check fails.
claims.coverage: The offset mapping was tested by two independent routes that had to agree: (a) the decoder's own base register, traced to `la_ $v1, D0x8004b818` at 0x80018c44 with the object recovered as that symbol minus 0x48 at 0x80018c54, giving record+0x00 = object+0x48; and (b) the disconnected-controller path at 0x80018fc0..0x80018fcc, which uses the raw object base D0x8004b7d0 and clears 0x48, 0x4a and 0x4e with the same port*0x1c0 + slot*0x70 index. The store sequence at 0x80018efc..0x80018f10 was read in full, including the load of the old value before the overwrite, so the previous/current direction is not inferred from a single instruction. Writers to these halfwords were searched corpus-wide with `code-search 'sh .*, 0x4[8ae]\('` over 590137 lines of ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003; the non-stack, non-gp hits in exe/fns.s outside 0x80018f00..0x80018fcc belong to other objects and were not attributed to this one.
limitations: Which physical controller bit corresponds to which face or shoulder button is not established here; only that all three halfwords share one bit numbering, keyed by the keymap byte.

The repeat-timer arithmetic at 0x80018e34..0x80018eb0 (period from object +0x3d4, per-button timestamps at record +0x0c + bit*4, per-button delay bytes at record +0x4c + bit, delay increment 0xa clamped at 0xc) was read but is not claimed in detail.

The analog-stick to direction-bit thresholds at 0x80018d90..0x80018ddc (comparisons against 0x41 and 0xc0 on record bytes +0x0a and +0x0b, ORing bits 0x80/0x20/0x10/0x40) were read but are not claimed here.

claims.statement: The fan-in of these routines comes from function-pointer slots in the tail of the same object rather than from direct calls: the recovered inventory resolves D0x8004bbc4 (object +0x3f4) to F0x80018854, D0x8004bbc8 (+0x3f8) to F0x80018878, D0x8004bbcc (+0x3fc) to F0x8001889c and D0x8004bbd8 (+0x408) to F0x80018980, and reports 533, 39, 191 and 723 call sites respectively, with 0 direct callers in each case. Overlays reach the slots by materialising the object base with lui 0x8005 followed by addiu -0x4830, which borrows to 0x8004b7d0; the load of slot +0x3f4 alone occurs 597 times across 26 assembly files. In the three call sites read (exe/fns.s 0x80011320 and pro/cardgame.s 0x80086524 and 0x8008655c) the first argument passed to the +0x3f4 slot is zero, that is controller port 0.
claims.coverage: Slot-to-function bindings were taken from the recovered inventory's extracted static initializers (`query_recovered_inventory.py callers` on each of the four functions, which reports the resolved global_symbol per edge) and cross-checked against the call sites' own displacements from the base register in the assembly. The 597/26 figure is the reported hit and file count of `code-search 'lw \$v0, 0x3f4\(' --regex` over 590137 lines; it is a lower bound on consumers because it fixes both the destination register and the displacement and therefore misses call sites that use a different destination register or a different service slot. The port-0 statement is deliberately narrowed to the three call sites actually read; the argument values at the remaining sites were not enumerated.
limitations: Argument recovery is not automatic for these routines, so the first-argument value was established only for the three call sites read. No claim is made about the other call sites.

The inventory's caller counts come from a base-register recovery pass and use `nearest_local_literal_base_non_flow_sensitive` on some edges; those edges are not flow-sensitive and could mis-attribute a base.

claims.statement: D0x8004b7d0 is a 0x3e0-byte resident controller-input service object, and the array the high-fan-in accessors index is an array of 0x70-byte per-controller records that begins at D0x8004b818 = D0x8004b7d0 + 0x48, not at D0x8004b7d0 itself. A record is addressed as D0x8004b818 + port*0x1c0 + slot*0x70, so 0x1c0 is the size of a per-port block that holds four 0x70-byte multitap-slot records, and the 8 records span object offsets 0x48..0x3c7. The reset routine F0x80018310 clears 0x3e0 bytes from D0x8004b7d0, fills 12 bytes at object +0x3c8 with 0xff, and runs a nested loop whose outer index is bounded below 2 and whose inner index is bounded below 4, passing the packed channel id (outer << 4) + inner to the per-record keymap initialiser F0x800188c0. The clear path at 0x80018f8c masks the port field of that channel id to one bit before scaling by 0x1c0, so the index that reaches the 0x1c0 scale is a controller port number of 0 or 1. Object offset +0x04 is handed to the device layer as two buffers 0x22 (34) bytes apart, the PlayStation controller transfer-buffer size.
claims.coverage: The object extent was tested from both ends rather than assumed: the reset length 0x3e0 gives the upper bound, and every named symbol that falls inside it was enumerated with `code-search D0x8004b7d0` (82 hits, all in exe/fns.s, none outside) plus the symbols D0x8004b7d4 (+0x04), D0x8004b818 (+0x48), D0x8004bb98 (+0x3c8), D0x8004bbc4 (+0x3f4) and D0x8004bbd8 (+0x408) reached by arithmetic. The 8-record claim was checked by arithmetic against those symbols: 0x48 + 8*0x70 = 0x3c8, which is exactly where the next symbol D0x8004bb98 begins, and the highest byte the keymap initialiser can write (port 1, slot 3, entry 15) is object +0x3c3, one byte below it. The port/slot bounds are the literal loop terminators at 0x8001839c and 0x8001838c, not an inference from observed data.
limitations: Object offsets +0x3d4, +0x3d6, +0x3d8 and +0x3dc are read and written by this code but are not decoded here beyond noting that +0x3d4 is set from an argument masked with 0x7f and defaulted to 0x10, and that +0x3dc is a counter compared against 0x707.
The bit assignments inside the u32 status word at object +0x00 (bits 1<<((port<<2)|slot) plus 0x00800000, 0x00c00000, 0x0c000000, 0x20000000, 0x40000000, 0x80000000) were observed but not decoded.

claims.statement: The per-Digimon acquired-form ledger in exe/fns has a seven-function read/write API over two fields of the roster record at D0x80048d34 + slot*0x3DC: the equipped triple at +0x7B0 (three halfwords) and the 44-entry ledger at +0x7B8 (0x14 bytes per entry, layout per TL-001: form id, form level, DVEXP, six technique halfwords). F0x8001764c(slot, formId) walks the 44 entries (bound slti 0x2c, stride addiu 0x14), skips any entry whose leading halfword is below 3, and returns the index of the entry whose leading halfword equals formId, or -1. F0x80017924(slot, formId) is the ACQUIRE path: it returns 0 when F0x8001764c already finds the form; otherwise it scans for the first entry whose leading halfword is 0, and when there is none it returns 0 without writing; when there is one it calls the function pointer held at D0x8005cca0 with the form id, then writes the id as a halfword at entry+0 and the byte 1 at entry+2 (TL-001's form-level field), and returns 1 -- so a newly acquired form starts at level 1 and the notification fires before the write. F0x800177d0(slot, src) writes the equipped triple: for each of three halfwords of src it stores the ledger entry's own id when F0x8001764c finds it and -1 when it does not, so an unacquired form cannot be equipped. F0x800176ac(slot, dst) reads that triple back, emitting only ids of 3 or more that still resolve to a ledger entry whose id is 3 or more, padding the unused positions of the three with -1, and returning the count. F0x80017898(slot, dst) writes each ledger id of 3 or more into dst as halfwords, zero-fills dst to 44 halfwords, and returns the count. F0x80017a1c(slot, formId, dst) and F0x80017ab4(slot, formId, src) copy one whole 0x14-byte ledger entry out of and into the record, addressed by form id through F0x8001764c, and both return the ledger index or -1 without touching memory when the form is absent.
claims.notes: Offset labelling differs from TAG-C001, which places the equipped triple at roster record +0x50. Read statically here, +0x50 relative to DIGIMON_CUR_STATS (0x8004949c = D0x80048d34+0x768) is the LEDGER (0x7B8-0x768) and the triple is at +0x48 (0x7B0-0x768). TAG-C001's own evidence is an authority-1 runtime capture whose quote does not pin the base it counts from, so this is recorded as a labelling difference to resolve, not as a contradiction. D0x8005cca0 holds a function pointer called with the form id on acquisition; its target is not identified here.
claims.coverage: Every quantifier here is a loop constant read out of the assembly, not an inference. The 44 bound is the literal in `slti $v0, $a2, 0x2c` at 0x80017690 and `slti $v0, $t0, 0x2c` at 0x800178e8, with the 0x14 stride in `addiu $a0, 0x14` at 0x80017698 and `addiu $a3, 0x14` at 0x800178f0. The three bound is `slti $v0, $s0, 0x3` at 0x80017768 and `slti $v0, $s2, 0x3` at 0x80017868 with the 0x2 stride at 0x80017770 and 0x80017870. The "below 3 is empty" rule is the `slti ..., 0x3` guard read at 0x80017678, 0x80017714, 0x8001774c and 0x800178cc -- all four readers, checked individually. The 0x3DC stride is re-derived here from the shift-and-subtract at 0x80017658-0x80017668 and agrees with the independently recorded resident-digimon-stats-record-address. NOT tested: that these seven are the COMPLETE set of accessors for +0x7B0/+0x7B8. Only exe/fns.s lines 8055-8358 were read and no corpus-wide search for other writers of those two offsets was run, so the claim is about these seven functions and does not assert exclusivity. The purpose of the pointer at D0x8005cca0 is also untested -- only that F0x80017924 calls it with the form id.

claims.statement: In the persistent per-starter roster record (base 0x80049494 + slot*0x3dc, decoded in digivolution-tech-system-decoded-2026-07-11.md), the record-layout table names every field from +0x00 through the acquired-forms ledger, but the ledger's own documented extent (+0x58, stride 0x14, 44 entries = 0x58+0x2E0 = +0x338) does not reach the next named row (equipment items at +0x3c8). This leaves record offsets +0x338..+0x3c8 (0x90 = 144 bytes) with no field name or meaning anywhere in the existing decode, even though it falls inside the persistent record and inside the rust-side un3[0xdf] catch-all array. This is a genuine unnamed-field gap, derived by arithmetic on the cited rows, not an independent trace of new field semantics -- candidate pending a disasm or controlled-capture pass that names what (if anything) occupies it.
claims.coverage: CONFIRMED 2026-09-06: the +0x338..+0x3C8 span is the tail of the un3 catch-all; the pack id is NOT in it (it is at 0x8004B374, DIGI-Q001-PACK-ID-001).

claims.statement: The rust-side Unknown4 struct places field un5 ([u16;8], 16 bytes) at Unknown4+0x3ce, i.e. record+0x3d6 (record = Unknown4-8 per the roster-record decode). Adding un5's own size reaches record+0x3e6, which is 0xa (10) bytes past the record-layout table's documented stride of 0x3dc per slot. un5 is not referenced by any row of the record-layout table. This is an unresolved boundary inconsistency between the rust struct annotations (authority 4, unverified against disassembly in this pass) and the decoded record stride (authority 5) -- it is not established whether un5 is mis-sized/mis-offset in the rust source, whether the true per-slot stride is larger than 0x3dc, or whether un5 legitimately overlaps the following slot's header. Marked candidate; needs disasm confirmation of the actual per-slot stride and of any code that reads Unknown4+0x3ce.

The persistent per-starter roster record's own layout table (record base 0x80049494+slot*0x3dc) has an imprecise boundary between its stats row (+0x24..) and its 'un2 + pad' row (stated as +0x48..+0x4d): cross-referencing the Unknown4Stats rust struct, the 19th and final stats halfword (cur_dark) sits at Unknown4+0x40 = record+0x48..+0x49 (record = Unknown4-8), so record+0x48..+0x49 is the LAST stats field, not pad. The genuinely unnamed span inside that row is therefore only record+0x4c..+0x4f (4 bytes: the un2 halfword at record+0x4a..+0x4b is already named-but-unexplained, and record+0x4c..+0x4f is the un3 array's first word, immediately preceding the equipped-forms triple at record+0x50). Separately, and not previously flagged anywhere in the ledger or the canonical doc, the equipped-forms triple (u16x3, record+0x50..+0x55) and the acquired-forms ledger (starting record+0x58) leave record+0x56..+0x57 (2 bytes) with no row at all. Both spans (record+0x4c..+0x4f and record+0x56..+0x57) are located and their byte extents are exact, but their meaning and writer are NOT determined by this pass: a literal-offset overlay scan (tools/run-overlay-scan.sh stores) against stfgtrep.s and stgdglab.s at the corresponding ctx-relative offsets (ctx+0x7ac, ctx+0x7ae, ctx+0x7b6, where ctx=D0x80048d34 and record+0=ctx+0x760 per the same doc) found no literal sw/sh/sb instruction at any of those offsets in either file. This negative result is NOT proof of absence: the same scan against ctx+0x7b8, the offset of the already-proven acquired-forms ledger, also returns zero hits, showing that writes to fields in this region of the record are reached through a base register already advanced by a computed/indexed address rather than through a literal immediate from ctx -- exactly the addressing style documented for the ledger's own helper API (F0x80017ab4 ledger_write etc., which lives in the resident EXE fns.s, outside this frontier's two named overlays). So the writer(s) for these two small gaps, if any, most likely live in fns.s or are reached through register-relative addressing invisible to this offset-literal scan.
claims.limitations: Not applicable at the evidence level; see packet-level limitations.

Explicit mode writes 14 int16 fields to camera struct 0x800a46d8 - eye (X, -Y, -Z at +0x00/+0x04/+0x08), target (X, -Y, -Z at +0x0c/+0x10/+0x14), a third vector (+0x18/-0x1c/-0x20), a u16 vector (+0x24/-0x26/-0x28), a scalar (+0x2c), and H = GTE projection distance/FOV (+0x30). D==0 calls camera method +0xf8 (instant cut); D>0 calls +0xfc (glide over D ticks). op4 (motion, F0x8008c2cc, manager id 0x15): plays a blended skeletal motion via +0xe8; motions 29 and 30 save-zero and restore the render field at 0x800a46d0, which is the arena-suppress (void enter) and reveal (void exit) hook used by clip-12 segments 0 and 2. op2 sub-3 (slot position, 0x8008ba18): targets (x, -y, -z); ticks==0 snaps, ticks>0 runs a linear tween (F0x8009b650) with fixed-point per-tick step 0x1000/ticks. op2 sub-4 (slot rotation, 0x8008ba78): sets (rx, -ry, -rz) instantly. claims.statement: The in-battle DNA DV confirm has exactly seven rejection tests, all inside FIGHTSTG_F0x800980e4's ctx+0x10==1 / ctx+0x14==1 block, evaluated in this order after the pane's second row (DNA DV) is confirmed with pad mask 0x2000: (1) acting combatant cur_mp (record +0xc) < Unknown3[ctx+0x7c - 1] u16 at +0x00, branch at 0x800985e4; (2) selected partner cur_mp < the same cost, branch 0x800985f8; (3) acting combatant status byte +0x1c & 0x20, branch 0x8009860c; (4) partner status byte +0x1c & 0x20, branch 0x80098620; (5) acting combatant status byte +0x1c & 0x08, branch 0x80098628; (6) acting combatant cur_hp (record +0x8) <= 0, branch 0x80098638; (7) partner cur_hp <= 0, branch 0x80098648. The partner is deliberately not tested for bit 0x08 and neither participant is tested for bit 0x10 on this row. The pane's FIRST row (the plain partner-switch commit, pane cursor +0x50 == 0) has a different and disjoint two-test set: acting +0x1c & 0x10 and partner +0x1c & 0x10 at 0x80098558 and 0x8009856c, with no MP, HP or cost logic at all. Both participants pay the full cost on success; the cost is read twice from the same Unknown3 record. Authority 2 (original assembly); held at partially_verified because no controlled runtime capture of any rejection branch exists yet.

Every DNA DV rejection is silent and side-effect-free. All seven DNA-row tests and both first-row tests branch to the single address 0x80098790, which only calls the pane renderer FIGHTSTG_F0x800979e4(ctx) and falls into the shared frame tail; no message call, no error sound, no state advance, no write to *(ctx+0x50) or *(ctx+0x80), and no MP debit occur. Because the confirm feedback hook D0x80055c48(0x0004001c) is invoked at 0x80098530 before the first test, a rejected DNA DV confirm produces the ordinary confirm feedback and then nothing: the pane stays open with the cursor still on DNA DV. In player terms, pressing confirm on DNA DV with a dead partner, with either Digimon short of MP, or with a blocking status bit set behaves like a dead button press with a normal confirm beep, and the game never says why. Authority 2 (original assembly).

DNA cancellation is a pane pop, not a command cancel. Pad mask 0x4000 on the DNA/Tag pane runs D0x80055c48(0x800450bd), the shared fightstg cancel-feedback constant, then ctx+0x2c(ctx, 0), then FIGHTSTG_F0x80097cfc(ctx, menu_stack, 0), then the same 0x80098790 redraw. It does not write the -2 sentinel into *(ctx+0x50) and does not call ctx+0x28(ctx, 3), which is what the page-0 form-list cancel at 0x8009841c does; backing out of the DNA pane therefore returns to the form list rather than aborting the whole battle command. There is no cancellation path after the commit tail at 0x80098650: once the dual MP debit and the *(ctx+0x50) / *(ctx+0x80) stores execute, this function offers no way back. Pad masks 0x800 and 0x400 only cycle ctx+0x54 modulo 3 and are not cancellations. Authority 2 (original assembly).

There is an eighth, earlier suppression branch that is not part of the confirm handler: in the offer build at 0x8009832c the code reads the acting combatant record byte +0x1a and, when it is non-zero, jumps straight to the pane-sizing code with the entry count forced to 1, skipping the entire pairing recomputation so that ctx+0x7c is not refreshed from the transformed form. Cross-overlay identification of that byte: wfightmn's Blast transform (file 0x00002f90) saves the pre-transform species id into record +0x02, writes the Blast form's profile id into record +0x00, and sets record +0x1a = 1; the Blast revert (file 0x000015e8) tests +0x1a, zeroes the DV/Blast gauge halfword at 0x80042b74 + idx*2, and clears +0x1a. A corpus-bounded regex search of the original assembly over byte/halfword/word stores at displacement 0x1a (51 hits over 590078 lines scanned) finds no other byte writer of that field in the fight overlays. Therefore combatant record +0x1a is the 'currently Blast-transformed' flag, record +0x00 is the live fighting species/profile id, and +0x02 is the saved pre-transform species id; and the DNA offer is not recomputed while the acting Digimon is Blast-transformed. This corrects two rows of the research document docs/research/battle/battle-ram-layout.md, where +0x00 is described as a static per-combatant value and possible turn-initiative seed and +0x1a is listed as always zero. No ledger claim was found bound to those rows, so this is a documentation correction and not a ledger supersession; if the lead finds such a ledger claim, that claim should be re-filed as contradicted with supersession fields instead. Authority 2 (original assembly).

Three of the enumerated status-bit rejection branches appear unreachable in ordinary play: bits 0x10 and 0x20 of combatant byte +0x1c have no applier anywhere in the original assembly (prior finding STATUS-C001/C008), so rejection tests (3) and (4) of DNA-C005 and both first-row tests can never fire from an inflicted ailment; and bit 0x08 is Sleep, which makes the acting combatant skip its turn before the command menu opens, so test (5) should be unreachable for the acting Digimon. Under this reading the only DNA rejection branches a player can actually trigger are insufficient MP on either participant and a dead selected partner, and a sleeping, poisoned, frozen or confused reserve partner does NOT block DNA DV. Held at candidate rather than partially_verified because 'no applier exists' is a corpus-bounded negative about ailment appliers only and does not exclude these bits being set by some non-ori writer or by an equipment or scripted path, and because the Sleep turn-gate interaction was not re-derived in this pass.

DNA-Q001 pass 10 corrects pass 9: ctx+0x38 is generic F0x800142ac task-state advancement, not a form swap. DNA offers match reciprocal source-profile unknown1[1] against partner-profile this; source tech_dna_dv supplies the result/action ID. The command dispatches as action type 6 through FIGHTSTG_F0x80090c44 and clip 12. A visible Stingmon + ExVeemon to Paildramon run confirmed a full 100 MP debit from each source with unchanged active roster index and equipped forms, establishing temporary-action rather than persistent form-swap semantics.

claims.statement: In the DNA commit block of FIGHTSTG_F0x800980e4 (fightstg.s 0x800984dc..0x800986f4), a DNA digivolution requested by the player is refused (control jumps to the shared exit label .L0x80098790, skipping MP debit and fusion commit) under any of: (1) either combatant's current HP (+0x8) is <= 0 (a dead source or dead partner); (2) either combatant's current MP (+0xc) is less than the selected technique's MP cost (read from a per-technique halfword table); (3) either combatant's ailment bitfield (+0x1c) has bit 0x10 set, or bit 0x20 set (checked symmetrically on both the acting combatant s0 and the partner s2); (4) the acting combatant s0's ailment bitfield has bit 0x8 set -- this last bit is checked only for s0, not re-tested for the partner s2, unlike bits 0x10/0x20. Bits 0x10/0x20 have no known applier or ailment name (confirmed by prior research as 'tech-abort flags'); bit 0x8 is the documented Sleep bit elsewhere in the ailment system, but within this DNA gate it is tested asymmetrically.

Every DNA refusal branch (dead source, dead partner, insufficient source MP, insufficient partner MP, ailment bit 0x10/0x20/0x8) and the successful commit path itself all converge on the identical call FIGHTSTG_F0x800979e4(ctx) at .L0x80098790, invoked with no parameter that varies by which condition (if any) fired. No separate error/refusal message call site was located for this DNA commit gate in this pass; the player-visible behaviour this static evidence supports is that the DNA action silently fails to advance (no fusion animation plays, no MP is spent) rather than producing a confirmed distinct on-screen rejection line at this call site. What text (if any) FIGHTSTG_F0x800979e4 itself displays, and whether it varies by outcome internally, is unresolved by this pass.

claims.statement: Effective-record bytes +0x3a and +0x3b are the combatant's accumulated to-hit and evasion pools, not weapon-power and armor-defence pools. A struct-offset reader census over fightstg.s (tools/run-overlay-scan.sh loads fightstg 0x3a and 0x3b, matcher = every lb/lbu/lh/lhu/lw at exactly that signed offset through a non-$sp, non-$gp pointer) returns exactly three sites each: two inside the initializer FIGHTSTG_F0x8009ec94 (the read-modify-write of the equipment loop at 0x8009f058/0x8009f0a4 and of the accessory ladder at 0x8009f39c/0x8009f3dc) and one consumer, FIGHTSTG_F0x800a06ac, the physical accuracy roll. There, +0x3a of the attacking side is ADDED to the attacker's own +0xa (SPD) term at 0x800a0790/0x800a0798, and in the side-swapped branch +0x3b of the side under attack is SUBTRACTED from the same term at 0x800a0844/0x800a084c, before hit_chance = skill_base_acc + skill_base_acc*term/128 and the roll (RAND_U16 & 0x7f) < hit_chance. Consequently the equipment loop's contributions - stat-record byte +0xe for family 2-14 items into +0x3a, stat-record byte +0x10 for other families into +0x3b - are weapon accuracy and armour evasion contributions, and Glasses/Goggles (accuracy_up) and DanceFeather/DanceWing (evade_up) stack additively into the same two pools, exactly as the accessory opcode table states.
claims.notes: This resolves the recorded EQUIP-Q001 contradiction in favour of the data table: the addu into +0x3a/+0x3b is not a fold into a damage pool, and the two accessories are genuinely accuracy and evasion. In player terms, Glasses/Goggles make your Digimon's attacks connect more often, and DanceFeather/DanceWing make enemy attacks miss you more often; they stack if you wear two.

claims.statement: In the item shop, whether one of your Digimon can use a piece of gear is a single bit test. stitshop routine F0x8008c4cc (installed at RAM slot 0x8008d1cc) is asked, per party card, 'can this member equip this item?'. It reads the item's record (0x80041838 + itemId*12 via getter f5/0x80041844), takes the record's first dword as a pointer to the equipment descriptor, and returns bit S of the descriptor's byte +0x4, where S is the dword the caller reads from party context 0x80048da4+memberIdx*4 (ctx+0x70) via resident F0x80016d94 (memberIdx<3, else -1). S is a ROSTER-SLOT index, not a form id: its sibling F0x80016fd8 multiplies a ctx+0x70 value by 0x3DC (the one-record-per-line roster stride) to address that line's record, and F0x80016dc0 (starter-pack select) writes roster-slot values (from D0x8004b490 + pack*3) into ctx+0x70. Because the bit is the LINE index, not the record's current-form field, the test does not depend on which form the Digimon currently wears - it is the same gate across that line's digivolution chain. So the descriptor byte +0x4 is an 8-bit 'which starter lines may wear this' mask: a specialized weapon opens one line (Short Sword = 0x01, the starter in slot 0), some several (0x38/0x39/0xC0/0xB8), and all 68 accessory records carry 0xFF so any Digimon may wear any accessory. When the predicate returns 0 the shop draws the can't-equip X (clip 22, F0x8008a450) and the 'Equip who?' cursor skips that member (F0x80083eb0). The predicate reads only these two stored values; it performs no other per-species check.

The shifted value S is proven a roster-line index three ways in this packet: F0x80016d94 reads ctx+0x70, F0x80016fd8 uses a ctx+0x70 value as `*0x3DC` to index the one-record-per-line roster, F0x80016dc0 writes roster-slot values into ctx+0x70 at pack select. 'No other per-species check' is scoped to the F0x8008c4cc body (derefs getter, loads byte+4, shifts, masks - no branch).
limitations: Two-handedness is a separate check (Unknown0 byte 2 == 7, exe/f10 unequip + ststatus equip screen), not part of this predicate.
Only 3 party positions are defined (F0x80016d94 returns -1 for memberIdx>=3); an 8th-starter line's mask bit was read from data but no 4+-member party position was exercised live.

claims.statement: What a piece of gear does to the stats the game shows is decided by stitshop F0x80088a64 reading each item's stat record BY BYTE OFFSET, and what an offset means changes with the item's family byte (Unknown1 +0x9). For family 2..14 (weapons) the record's u16 at +0x0A is added to POW and two signed pairs follow - (byte +0x0C, s16 +0x06) and (byte +0x0D, s16 +0x08). For family 15..20 (armour) the record's u16 at +0x0C is added to DEF and the two pairs read the same two amounts against code bytes +0x0A and +0x0B. For family 21..24 (accessories) there is one pair, code byte +0x08 against the u16 at +0x06 - the Unknown2 handler table's own code and magnitude. All three then reach one convergence that adds the record's u16 at +0x00 to CHARISMA, so every weapon, armour piece and accessory carries a charisma value; a code of 7 moves all six core stats at once and codes outside 1..6 and 8..14 (the status-resist codes 17..21 among them) move no stat at all. Each add is a u16 store saturating at 999. A stat code names buffer +0x0C+2*(code-1) for 1..6 and buffer +0x18+2*(code-8) for 8..14, which the live display-index table at 0x8008CAE8 (= k+6 over thirteen entries) and Kotemon's live stat block (halfwords 6..11 = STR 48, DEF 44, SPT 41, WIS 34, SPD 33, CHR 1) pin in that order to STR, DEF, SPT, WIS, SPD, CHR and fire..dark. The card's own row order is set by its caller F0x80089274, which sends the mode it gets from 0x8008D1AC->unk24 through the six-entry jump table at 0x80083400 (modes 0/2/3, mode 1, modes 4/5 - three bodies): a weapon card leads with POW and puts Charisma second, an armour card leads with DEF then Charisma, and an accessory card leads with Charisma and puts its coded stat second, hiding that row when the code names no single stat, and making the after column by copying the member's equip slots aside, putting the candidate into them, recomputing, and writing the slots back; up to two further rows (four in total) list the stats whose before and after differ, in that same index order. Live: Short Sword on an unequipped Kotemon reads POW 48->62 and CHR 1->16, Leather Coat reads DEF 44->49 with the Charisma row second, and Power Gem reads CHR 16->19 then POW 62->72. The record's +0x0E and +0x10 bytes are NOT stats: they are the combatant's +0x3a to-hit and +0x3b to-evade pools per claim EQUIP-C009, so the walker's old `power` (from +0x0E) that it folded into STR was the wrong register, and the charisma word was never applied at all.

claims.statement: Reward payout depends on participation but not on survival or battle type. Every roster slot marked at battle setup or on a Tag-in is a participant, and the marking write is unconditional - neither marking loop ever reads current or max HP, so a KO'd member is marked identically to a survivor and still earns its share. The share formula gives a lone participant the full amount, two participants six tenths each, and three or more an even split. Story-fight battle ids 0xb, 0x1e, 0x143 and 0x144 do NOT bypass the reward path: each writes an extra chapter/outcome word and then jumps to the same continuation the ordinary path falls through to, and all four have nonzero records in the reward table, so story bosses grant real EXP, Bits and DVEXP like any other fight.
claims.notes: Written as an exp-leveling claim specifically because a frontier resolution may only cite same-system claims: the equivalent facts existed only as PARTY-C002/PARTY-C003 in party-management, which would have passed packet validation and then failed handoff-check. Convergence proof for the story-fight branches is jump-target arithmetic - 0x800a6e8c minus the overlay base 0x800a5de0 is 0x10ac, exactly the default fallthrough instruction. Reward table records read directly: id 0xb = [40,380,800], 0x1e = [99,990,1980], 0x143 = [15,153,275], 0x144 = [68,4,0]. UNKNOWN: the final jal from that shared continuation into the stfgtrep reward lookup was not walked instruction by instruction; convergence plus nonzero table rows is the basis. Also not examined: whether some unrelated later path zeroes a KO'd member's share after marking - a different mechanism than participant marking.
claims.contradiction_rationale: CONTRADICTED 2026-10-03 on its survival clause only. Its statement said that because neither marking loop reads current or max HP, a KO'd member 'is marked identically to a survivor and still earns its share'. The first half is still true and re-recorded as the marking rule in knocked-out-participant-loses-its-battle-reward-2026-10-03; the conclusion is false. The battle outcome sweep in wfightmn.s L2072-L2087 clears a position's reward-participant flag (+0x6, with +0x7 through +0x9) when its live HP is 0 or below, and the report both divides the reward by the rows still flagged (stfgtrep.s L2786-L2790) and hands a cleared row a share of zero (stfgtrep.s L2884-L2886). SURVIVING CONTENT, unchanged and still supported by its own evidence: the share formula (1 participant 100%, 2 participants 60% each, 3 or more an even split) and the four story-fight battle ids 0xb/0x1e/0x143/0x144 having nonzero reward rows. Only the statement's conclusion about a knockout is withdrawn. See also knocked-out-participant-loses-its-battle-reward-2026-10-03.

claims.statement: The field engine names the place you are standing in from a table of four-byte records at 0x80097098 in fieldstg, walked until a record's scene-id halfword is zero. Each record is {area string index at +0x0, place string index at +0x1, scene id at +0x2}. The area string comes from the resource bank at index 0xa9 plus the language global and the place string from 0xb7 plus the language global; those are the STAREA and STNAME banks, seven of each, in the same MS/US/ES/FS/IS/DS/SS language order already established elsewhere. The two labels are built with the shared class-A text-widget constructor at fixed positions (128, 26) for the area and (40, 68) for the place. The shipped table holds 239 records.
claims.coverage: The record count of 239 comes from walking the shipped table from its base to the zero terminator the loop itself tests, in the data crate rather than by assuming a length. The four-byte stride is the loop's own increment and the field offsets are the loop's own loads, so the record shape is read rather than inferred. The bank identification was checked by resolving the two base indices plus the English language index against the archive index and confirming both resolve to STAREA and STNAME rather than assuming a similarly-named file.
limitations: The code that turns a scene id into an overlay load was not found. The scene-to-overlay assignment here rests on a one-to-one uniqueness argument over the stage-select table and the set of stage overlays on the disc.
The two remaining empty rows resolve the same way to overlays 233 and 661, but their scene ids were not investigated further and no name is claimed for them.
Only the English banks were read. The other six language banks are asserted only to exist at the six sibling resource indices.
The two label widgets' positions are the constructor's literal arguments; whether both labels are always shown, or one is suppressed in some scenes, was not established.

claims.statement: FishingPole possession (flag 0x8005) gates 56 op-7 story-step records across 12 stages, each tagging a per-spot SAY/scene-controller object at its own +0x8 with mode = 5. IDENTITY GAP CLOSED STATICALLY 2026-07-27. The chain, all in pro/fieldstg.s (overlay RAM base 0x80082cb0): the op-7 exec#1 dispatch table at file 0x1c0 (RAM 0x80082e70, 7 entries, idx = record.op - 1, bounded by sltiu 0x7 at file 0x5854) has entry 6 = 0x80088544 = file 0x5894, whose body is j 0x80088568 with delay slot li $s0,0x5 at file 0x5898; the shared tail stores that mode with sw $s0,0x8($v0) at file 0x58e0. (Entry 0 of that table is 0x8008854c, the op == 1 case -- an earlier working note mislabelled it as entry 6.) The op-7 exec#2 table at file 0x1e8 (RAM 0x80082e98, 14 entries, idx = op - 1, sltiu 0xe) has entry 6 = 0x80088808 = file 0x5b58, which does lw $v1,0x58($s0) then lw $v0,0x120($v1) then jalr, i.e. it calls slot +0x120 on the controller. The controller constructor installs +0x120 = 0x8008f304 at file 0xe538-0xe540. F0x8008f304 (file 0xc654-0xc730) calls 0x8008d744 at file 0xc708 with the spot offsets params[0..1] added to the controller position ([ctrl+0x58], [ctrl+0x5c]) and stores the returned pointer into the controller extra array at [ctrl+0x24]+0x8. 0x8008d744 (file 0xaa94) is F0x80014504(tick = 0x8008d27c, size = 0x68, extra = 0). Therefore the actor captured live at 0x800b576c is the CHILD of the mode-5 controller and a distinct 0x68-byte class. CORRECTION TO THE 2026-07-11 DISPROOF: reading +0x8 == 0 on that child was a FALSE DISPROOF, because +0x8 is the CONTROLLER mode-tag field, not a field of the child class. Authority 2, original assembly.
claims.notes: Held at partially_verified, not promoted: the chain is a static one, and no runtime capture has yet shown the parent pointer or the extra-array slot linking a live controller to the live bobber at 0x800b576c. Exact evidence to close: a field capture at a fishing spot reading [controller+0x24]+0x8 and matching it to the bobber address.
claims.frontier_rationale: Resolves the fishing-controller/child-bobber class identity and the FishingPole gate chain; its only residue is a narrow runtime confirmation of one parent-pointer link, a question no catalogued FISH-Q00x frontier asks.

claims.statement: The bobber progress field (+0x60) is used both as the per-tick increment added to the progress accumulator (+0x5c, capped 0x3000) and as a counter that is unconditionally decremented by fixed amounts (0x10, then 0x4) each tick, firing a callback when it reaches exactly zero. Reaching the +0x5c cap sets a bite-ready flag (+0x64=1). A tile-type table at 0x80097b14 gates an ambient SFX (SYSTEM06, 0x80045341) while the actor's own position samples a tile-type code equal to its own target field (+0x10); the semantic identity of that tile-type code (e.g. water vs. other) is NOT established, only the equality gate.
claims.notes: Runtime +0x5c=0x1d00 with +0x64=1 already set is consistent with the flag firing in a prior tick before the capture; the capture does not independently prove the exact cap-crossing frame, only that the flag/accumulator relationship is live in a real fishing spot object.
claims.frontier_rationale: Documents the bobber's progress-accumulator/decrement-counter tick mechanics and an unresolved tile-type semantic gate for ambient SFX; no catalogued fishing frontier covers this tick/tile-gate mechanic.

claims.statement: Fishing grants NO item and sets NO flag. The catch is a BATTLE. The bobber's own code has no inventory or flag write on any branch (complete store census, 2026-07-27), and the branch that was open -- what happens on a successful strike -- is now read: the bobber calls F0x800927a0 with the band it stopped on, which hands slot 4 (band 1) or slot 7 (band 2) of the stage's own scripted (rate-0) encounter block to the ordinary battle-setup path F0x8008b798, exactly as the ambush tiles do at fixed slot 5. Slot 4 is a Cardmon variant on all 46 fishing stages; slot 7 is the area's large water Digimon. Band 0 ends the cast with nothing at all.
claims.notes: Verified for the fieldstg path, which is the only path: the reward question that kept this partially_verified was 'does some other overlay grant on a fishing outcome', and the answer is that the outcome does not reach another overlay as a reward at all -- it reaches the battle setup routine. No fightstg/cardgame census is needed to close it because the branch target is now read directly rather than inferred from an absence.

claims.statement: The already-decoded fishing-spot stage s485 shares its random-encounter pool with Cardmon-family enemies: stage_encounters.json zone[1] slots = [11,0,0,329,328,0,48,66] -- Cardmon3 (screen 329) and Cardmon2 (screen 328) sit in the same 8-slot rand()&7 pool as ordinary enemies Zanbamon (11), Flymon (48), and Seadramon (66). The same co-occurrence pattern (Cardmon variants mixed with regular enemies in one pool) repeats across every water-adjacent stage in the extracted sweep (s202,203,330,335,340,345,350,355,380,395,400,445-496,550-576,690-716,940-953), confirming that being at/near a fishing spot exposes the player to the same field random-encounter roll as elsewhere, which can select a Cardmon. This matches the player-reported mechanic that fishing areas can trigger Cardmon encounters mixed with ordinary attackers. NOT confirmed: a Cardmon-to-booster-pack reward. Cardmon's own enemies.json drop_item is literal 'Null' with drop_rate 0, and every Booster/RBooster item's only extracted acquisition source is a shop entry (no enemy-drop source found for any booster item in item_obtain_index.json) -- so a Cardmon-kill reward, if it exists, is not visible in the generic drop-table extraction and would need a separate reward path traced in the still-unresearched card-battle system.

In the process found the stage_encounters.json extractor was re-run since these were first captured (commit 9c67671, the encounter step-counter decode) and s485 gained two new all-zero zones ahead of the Cardmon pool, so the same slot values [11,0,0,329,328,0,48,66] that were at zones[1] now live at zones[3]; all 8 stage_encounters.json locators in this claim's evidence were corrected from zones[1] to zones[3] to match. claims.statement: There is a per-map fishing catch budget at D0x80048d34 + 0x26f8. On map change it is set to 0x10 (16): fieldstg file 0x488c li $v0,0x10 / file 0x4894 sw $v0,0x26f8($s0), in the same branch that writes the map id at +0x26dc and sets +0x26d8 to 1 (files 0x4880-0x4888, RAM 0x80087530-0x80087544). The bobber tick reads it at file 0xa60c and, while it is greater than zero, rolls the bobber variant as rand() & 7 (call through 0x8004dc0c at file 0xa61c-0xa624, andi 0x7 at file 0xa62c, stored to bobber+0x58 at file 0xa630) and then decrements it once (files 0xa634-0xa644). When it reaches zero the blez at file 0xa614 diverts to file 0xa648, which forces the bobber variant to 8 -- the no-bite value -- instead of rolling. Corpus check that this counter has no other reader or writer: dw3-research code-search "0x26f8" over the original assembly reports 5 hits of 590,078 lines scanned across 2 indexed sources; 4 are code lines and all 4 are in pro/fieldstg.s (files 0x4894, 0xa60c, 0xa634, 0xa644), the fifth being an indexed research-evidence row. Authority 2, original assembly.

claims.statement: The fishing minigame is a timing game against a hidden pattern. A cast rolls one of eight 48-band patterns (or the empty ninth once the map's 16 catches are spent), the float settles for 0x5b ticks, then a marker sweeps the 0x3000-long meter at 0x100/tick, bouncing at both ends. Pressing CIRCLE (pad bit 0x2000) brakes it -- 0x10/tick three times in four, 4/tick one time in four, so the rare slow brake glides four times as far past the press -- and the band under the marker where it stops decides the cast: 1 = Cardmon, 2 = the area's water Digimon, 0 = nothing. Band 1 also plays SYSTEM06 the instant the marker settles, a one-second tell before the fight starts.
claims.notes: The pattern bytes are authority-1 RAM rather than authority-2 assembly (the table is past fieldstg.s's disassembled end); everything else is read from the original assembly. NOT covered: the meter's and float's ART (sprite cells 0x18+meter>>8 and pattern+0x3e on texture page 0x0160 are not extracted), and the 2026-07-29 replay pressed CROSS, not CIRCLE, so it exercised the scene controller's withdrawal rather than this strike branch -- no runtime capture of a CIRCLE strike exists yet. The packed id 0x80045341 is named SYSTEM06 through the sound-id index (docs/research/audio/soundtst-common-ids.json), not through this packet.

claims.statement: The fishing presentation is drawn from FIELDCOM.BIN, which is already extracted, and needs no new asset work. Per tick the bobber draws four cells: the 64x24 bar frame (sub-entry 1 id 0x3c) at screen (0x18,0xc0), this cast's 48x8 pattern strip (sub-entry 1 id 0x3e + pattern) inset 8,8 into it, the 16x24 marker (sub-entry 1 id 0x3d) at x = (meter>>8) + 0x18, and one of four 16x16 float cells (sub-entry 0, id 0x60 + (rand()%48)/12, re-picked every tick) at the bobber's world position. The strip is one pixel per band, so the game SHOWS the player this cast's pattern. Nothing is drawn during the settle, because the draw block sits after the meter update and the settle phase returns before reaching it.
claims.notes: The strips' 432 pixels agree with the independently RAM-read pattern table on all nine patterns with exactly three colours and no exceptions, so the art and the table corroborate each other. Not covered: the draw context's scale/colour setup calls (F0x8001ecbc with 0x200/0x240 and 0x100, F0x8001ed34 with 0x1002) are not decoded, so the bar's on-screen SIZE may be scaled relative to the raw cell size; the walker draws the cells unscaled.

claims.statement: Casting does not just spawn the float: it puts the player in leader mode 0x48 for the whole cast. F0x8008f304 calls the leader entity's set-mode slot +0x2c with 0x48 and raises the scene lock at 0x800a9dd8; the shared leader dispatcher F0x8008fed0 indexes a 0x51-entry jump table at RAM 0x80083590 with the entity's mode field +0x10, and entry 0x48 is 0x8009092c. That block re-dispatches on the sub-state +0x14 through a six-entry table at RAM 0x800836d8 and runs: SETANIM 0x11 (advance); on the SETANIM completion flag +0xe8, PLAYER09 (0x80045cc5) + SETANIM 0x13; on +0xe8, PLAYER10 (0x80045d46) + SETANIM 0x14; when the cast controller's mode field [s5+8] reaches 0, F0x80088144(0, 1, 6) - the generic 0x6c-byte balloon actor with tick 0x80087f84, whose a1=1 selects the variant that plays no FUKIDASH cue - stored into [s5+4], plus SETANIM 0x12; after the +0x18 timer reaches 0x3c, [[s5+4]+0x28](2) plus SETANIM 0x15; and on +0xe8, set-mode 1, SETANIM 1 and clear 0x800a9dd8. The blocks fall through into one another, which is safe because SETANIM (F0x8008f4b4) clears the same +0xe8 the next block tests, and the advance stub F0x800142e0 zeroes +0x18 as it bumps +0x14. Those five clip ids resolve to the dedicated fishing sprite pack P002PLYF (LBA index 970, 70 frames): a scan of all 179 packs' clip directories finds exactly one pack defining any of clips 17/18/19/20/21, and it defines all five, and the SETANIM loader resolves clip ids as keys into the entity's own pack directory (with the clip-range remap applying only to the partner actor, not the player), so the player's animation-directory handle must be P002PLYF's for the whole of mode 0x48 or none of these five SETANIMs would match anything. Its frames show Junior kneeling and swinging a fishing rod.
claims.notes: Corrects two earlier records. (1) docs/research/audio/sfx-triggers.md filed PLAYER09/PLAYER10 as 'an alternating walk-footstep pair' in an unidentified dispatcher case, and mis-transcribed the jump table as 0x8008b590; the case is mode 0x48, the fishing cast, the table is 0x80083590, and [s0+0xe8] is the SETANIM animation-complete flag (F0x8008f4b4 clears it), not a grounded flag. (2) The 2026-07-29 s485 capture labelled its second X press a 'withdrawal' and inferred a separate withdrawal controller; the bobber tick's only pad read masks 0x2000 (CIRCLE) alone and mode 0x48 reads no pad in any sub-state, so no CROSS withdrawal path exists in either - the press is best explained as the strike. NOT covered by this claim: WHERE the player's animation-directory handle (+0x9c) is repointed at P002PLYF. Mode 0x48 itself does not write +0x9c, and F0x8008f304 does not either; the swap site is unlocated, exactly as it is for the ladder pack P002PLYL (clips 26-32). Only the necessity of the swap is established here (FISH-Q009). Also not covered: what the result balloon DRAWS - its display handle (+0x50, from [0x8004b7bc](5,-1,0)) and geometry (+0x54/+0x58/+0x5c = 0xc8/0xd4/0xdc) are undecoded, so the walker plays the 60-tick beat and draws nothing for it (FISH-Q008).

claims.statement: The bubble that pops over the player at the end of a fishing cast is not a distinct result widget: it is the same balloon actor the field proximity indicators use, spawned by the same factory from player mode 0x48 sub-state 3, attached to the player, and showing the same two-frame fishing rod-and-splash glyph (FIELDCOM animation program 5) that the spot itself shows while you stand on it. It differs from a proximity indicator only in being spawned with the silent subtype, so it plays no FUKIDASH cue.
claims.notes: The glyph identity is USER GROUND TRUTH from playing the original, corroborated by (a) the shared actor class and factory call, (b) the same player attachment lookup, and (c) the 2026-07-29 capture's 'white bubble with a creature/fish-like glyph' at frame 576. It is NOT read out of the original draw path: 0x80087f84's use of its +0x50 display handle and its +0x54/+0x58/+0x5c geometry remains undecoded, which is why this stays partially_verified rather than verified. Promotion needs either that decode or a pixel comparison of the capture's frame 576 against FIELDCOM program 5. Correction 2026-09-13: the shared actor class / same factory / silent-subtype facts hold, but the 'same two-frame rod-and-splash glyph (program 5)' clause is refuted. The draw path F0x80087E7C takes the bubble's ICON from glyph_table[subtype*9+cursor]; the result bubble is spawned with subtype 1 (F0x80088144(0,1,6)), i.e. row 1 (ids 1/2, KIND.smoke), whereas the fishing-spot indicator's step kind 5 selects row 5 (ids 10/11, KIND.tool). See claim fishing-q008-balloon-draw-cel-and-owner-anchor-2026-09-13.

claims.statement: The two calls FISH-Q007 named as undecoded in the bobber's draw setup are neither of them scale setters. F0x8001ecbc (DrawContext method slot +0x74) writes only the texture-page pair +0x08/+0x0c and seeds the CLUT pair +0x10/+0x14; F0x8001ed34 (slot +0x7c) resolves a layer/target through the 0x8004de10+0x17c lookup and binds it to ctx+0x00/+0x04 via F0x8001ecf8, whose second argument is dead.
