claims.statement: stgtrain's two rank-table helpers (count-helper RAM 0x8008c158, find-by-key helper RAM 0x8008c1c8; stgtrain.s L9065-L9115) contain NO +1/-1 conversion instruction on their id argument: both use the caller's raw `a0` directly as `a0<<7` (a0*0x80) added to table base 0x8008c4e4. But the helpers' own bounds check `(id-1) unsigned < 14` is genuinely ASYMMETRIC with the table it indexes: the check admits raw id in {1,...,14} unclamped and forces any other id (including 0) to 0, while the physical table (EV-bc0f4ae42dec: group g at base+g*0x80 for g in range(14)) only has valid slots {0,...,13}. Concretely: id=0 is REJECTED by the check itself (0-1 wraps unsigned, not <14), falls through the clamp branch, and is force-set to 0 -- landing on the correct, populated first group ONLY because clamping an already-zero value to zero is a no-op, not because the check treats 0 as valid. id=14 is ADMITTED unclamped by the check, producing group_ptr = 0x8008c4e4 + 14*0x80 = 0x8008cbe4, exactly one group PAST the table's last populated slot (group 13 occupies 0x8008cb64-0x8008cbe4) -- a real out-of-bounds read relative to the table if that path is ever taken. So the check's window is off by one relative to the table on BOTH ends: it excludes the table's real slot 0 from its 'valid' branch (reaching it only by clamp coincidence) and includes a nonexistent slot 14 in its 'valid' branch. The multiplication/offset arithmetic itself performs no shift; the asymmetry lives entirely in the bounds check. Whether id=14 is ever actually emitted, and whether id=0 always reaches these helpers through the clamp path rather than some other route, is NOT settled by this static evidence: GYM-C009/GYM-C010 (EV-gymq001-observed-0-13) show the ONE known caller chain (bank-0x94 set_flag launcher) exhaustively emits only 0..13 across all 25 writes/8 greeters, so the mismatch is dormant on that chain, but no `jal`/pointer caller of either helper (0x8008c158, 0x8008c1c8) was statically located, so it is UNPROVEN -- not established -- that no other consumer feeds these helpers a genuinely 1-based id or ever reaches 14. See limitations for the exact runtime step that would settle this.

The two helper addresses cited in docs/research/battle/stgtrain-static-investigation-2026-07-08.md (0x800894bc, 0x80089518) as the id-keyed rank-table walkers are mislocated: in the current checked-out ~/ddw3 asm those addresses hold generic vtable-dispatch/task-init boilerplate byte-identical across >=9 unrelated overlay object files at the same file-relative offset, not stgtrain-specific table-scanning code. The functions that actually construct and walk table 0x8008c4e4 are at RAM 0x8008c158 (count-helper) and 0x8008c1c8 (find-by-key helper), roughly 0xca0 further into stgtrain.s than previously cited. This corrects the address citation only; the July-08 doc's structural conclusion (14-group x 16 x 8-byte, id-keyed table) is independently re-derived at the corrected addresses by GYM-C011.

claims.statement: tools/overlay_scan.py could not read shocktst at all, and the same defect affects three further overlays. The assembly corpus uses THREE `.L0x` line shapes: `.word 0x... # mnemonic`, `mnemonic # .word 0x...`, and a bare `mnemonic` with no encoding comment anywhere. WORD_RE handles only the first two, so offsets in the third shape are absent from the word map and every word-driven subcommand renders them as 0x00000000 or `nop`, which is indistinguishable from genuinely empty space. Measured over all 317 overlays in ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003/pro: fightstg.s 31531 of 34145 lines invisible (92%), stdwtitl.s 5044 of 6512 (77%), wfightts.s 2796 of 3651 (77%), shocktst.s 1802 of 1937 (93%), with 41281 unparsed label lines corpus-wide. The tool already refused ranges that were ENTIRELY unreadable, but its guard tested `not any(word in range)`, so a MIXED range -- readable data at the front, bare-mnemonic code behind it -- passed the check and then rendered the unreadable half as zeros; that is exactly how a full-file `dis shocktst 0x0 0x1e44` came back as a solid run of nop. overlay_scan.py now loads the source text for unparsable label lines, prints them as `[src]` lines in `dis` and `fn`, warns on stderr with a count, and prints `????????` rather than a fabricated `00000000` in `words`. This is the fourth distinct variant of the same failure mode found in this series, after dropped `.word D0x...` symbolic words, the two cancelling defects in gen_soundtst_ids.py, and `.byte` blindness in cnty_sel.

claims.statement: The Digimon Lab's Switch screen offers the partners you own but have not deployed. Its candidate builder walks all eight roster slots at the 0x3dc record stride from 0x80048d34, reads roster_owned[slot] at +0x760 (the field writes slot+3 there when an NPC hands a partner over), turns it into a slot ordinal by subtracting 3 and drops the entry when that is negative -- roster_owned 0 means never obtained. Each surviving ordinal is compared against exactly three words, the deployed party, and is dropped on a match. What is left is appended to the screen's candidate array at +0xe4 with the count at +0x104. So an obtained but inactive partner IS selectable at the Lab, which is the step that turns a handover into a Digimon the player can use, and the deployed party is capped at three.

claims.coverage: The quantifiers are the two loop bounds of one routine, read whole rather than sampled: the outer loop is a single `slti $s0, 0x8` at file offset 0x94f4 with one `addiu $a3, 0x3dc` increment, and the inner comparison loop is a single `slti $a0, 0x3` at 0x94b0 with one `addiu $v1, 0x4`. Both were read in the original overlay assembly (stgdglab.s L9505-L9542) together with every instruction between the loop head at 0x9470 and the tail at 0x94fc -- 36 consecutive instructions, no branch leaving the block unaccounted for -- so a second bound or a second append site inside this builder would have been visible. It does NOT claim to be the only place the screen's list can be filled: other callers of the same widget array were not enumerated.

claims.statement: The pause menu overlay ststatus installs 6 routine pointers into objects and none of the 6 had ever been lifted to C, because the disassembler's function-entry list did not mark them. The overlay was additionally invisible to tools/lift_installed_routines.py until 2026-09-02: the tool builds each overlay's normalized-assembly path as <name>.norm.s and this overlay's is named ststatus_c_norm.s, so it failed the tool's existence check and never appeared in --list at all, which is why the earlier screen-object pass reported 174 missing routines over 14 screens rather than 180 over 15. The 6 belong to three objects. F0x80084f10 builds a dim wash, handler F0x80084e5c, and installs F0x80084C90 at +0x64 as its fade starter: it stores a direction at +0x58, a start level of 0 or 0xFF00 at +0x5C and a per-frame step of plus or minus 0xFF00 divided by the caller's duration at +0x60; the handler adds that step to +0x5C each frame and the draw takes the high byte of +0x5C as the wash's red, green and blue together, so the ramp drives the full-screen wash. F0x8008e8f8 builds the STATUS screen and installs F0x8008C460 at +0x148 as an equipment-preview fill: with argument -1 it calls the plain grid fill, and otherwise it snapshots the six equipment halfwords, writes the previewed piece, rebuilds the stats into a second block and restores the original six, after which each number widget takes the new value clamped at 999 and a colour that differs according to whether the snapshot was lower or higher, the same colour pair as the gym's delta fill. F0x80099684 builds the See Equipment bag's scroll bar, handler F0x8009946c, and installs four methods: +0x8C F0x80099430 writes the bar's left edge at +0x58 and width at +0x60 which the handler uses as the quad's x and x-plus-width, +0x90 F0x8009943C writes the travel span at +0x7C and +0x80 and arms +0x78, +0x94 F0x80099450 writes the visible row count at +0x6C and the total row count at +0x70 and arms +0x68, after which the handler computes the step as the span shifted left 8 divided by the total and the thumb height as that step times the visible count, and +0x98 F0x80099464 writes the scroll index at +0x74 from which the handler places the thumb's y and parks it at the bottom on the last step. The bar is built by the See Equipment tick only when the bag holds nine or more rows, and the caller passes 8 as the visible row count.

claims.coverage: The denominator is mechanical: tools/lift_installed_routines.py --list enumerates every routine pointer each screen constructor installs and reports 6 of 6 for this overlay as absent from the entry list, and a script checked each of the 6 against both canonical screen documents and the whole ledger, finding no mention of any. The worker independently reported the same absence against four further pause-menu documents. THE LIFT HAD NO CONTROL OF ITS OWN, because not one of the 6 already had C, so the tool's self-check had nothing to compare and would have printed CONTROL OK regardless; the tool now reports that case as NO CONTROL. The lift was instead controlled by hand: 8 routines of this same overlay that do have C were re-lifted through the identical promoted-assembly path and all 8 came back character-for-character identical. Verification is partial and the split is stated: the lead read the writer and the reading handler for all four scroll-bar methods, which is 4 of the 6; the dim wash and the equipment-preview fill are the worker's findings, the latter read against the original assembly at authority 2 by the worker but not re-read by the lead, and neither was checked against the running game.

claims.statement: Every window on every pause-menu screen opens and closes through the shared tween at F0x80099d5c/F0x80099df0 with steps = 10: opening ramps the window's horizontal scale 0 -> 0x1000 over 10 vsyncs and plays packed SFX 0x40019 (SYSTEM03), closing ramps 0x1000 -> 0 at twice the step -- 5 vsyncs -- and plays 0x4001A (SYSTEM04). No screen starts two folds and waits; each state starts one (or one pair), waits for window_fold_tick to return non-zero, and only then starts the next, so a screen builds itself up and takes itself down one window at a time. The sidebar screens (Choose Digimon, SORT, CARD FOLDERS, Digivolve Demo, TECHNIQUES, ITEMS) open the first party card together with the header plate, then one further card per step, and open the FOOTER plate beside the LAST card -- beside the first when the party holds one. Window slots and hinge points per screen are recorded in docs/research/ui/pause-menu-window-choreography.md and, for the machine-readable geometry, in web/assets/data/status_ui.json.

claims.statement: The master story-progress ordinal at RAM 0x8004b370 has a documented maximum value of 0x2d (45). A leaf function inside s780's own overlay (wstag780.s, file offset 0x1864-0x1870: lui $v1,0x8005 / li $v0,0x2d / jr $ra / sw $v0,-0x4c90($v1)) is the writer of this terminal value. That exact same value (0x2d) is the single condition tested by fieldstg.s's field-screen-table loader (file offset 0xf460-0xf4ac): it loads the ordinal, compares it against 0x2d, and on equality re-bases the screen-record table walk at RAM 0x8009a5f0 (the head of the 55-record s920-s974 endgame-alias screen table) instead of the default RAM 0x8009a884 (the head of the corresponding 55 base-overlay screen records). In player terms: reaching story-progress ordinal 45 is the exact, single mechanical trigger that swaps every one of the game's 55 shadowed field maps over to their post-game 'Amaterasu/Underground alias' variant -- this is DW2003's post-game marker for field progression, proven directly from the original assembly, not inferred from a string or a walker-side table.

Both fire the event and run the cutscene's `HANDOFF 670`; screen 670 resolves to base s431 at 44 and to post-game alias s958 at 45, at the same spawn (200,420) facing up. The two consumer worlds really differ: s431's own exit leads to s421 and it carries 26 npc records, while s958's exit leads to s956 and it carries 5 different ones. This matches web/game.js's `useAlt: () => ordinal === 0x2d` (engine/dw3/screen-routing.ts). Status stays partially_verified because the '55 records' half still rests on the evidence summary, not on a raw record-count read.

claims.statement: The resident clamped stat mutator of stat-block-nineteen-field-display-set has a SET twin that no claim names. exe/f11.s defines f11 at 0x80017028 -- one of seventeen hand-annotated single-function files whose bodies carry no address labels, so the research index holds no line of them and code-search reports them ABSENT -- and f11(slot, statIdx, value) STORES value where F0x800170c8(slot, statIdx, delta) adds a delta to the previous halfword. Everything after the store is identical in the two routines: the same sltiu 0x13 index gate that returns without writing at index 0x13 or above, the same sign-extension of the stored halfword from 16 bits, and the same three-band clamp with the same constants in the same branch order -- statIdx below 2 stores 0x63 when the value is 0x64 or more, statIdx-2 below 4 stores 0x270F when the value is 0x2710 or more, otherwise 0x3E7 when the value is 0x3E8 or more. Both also carry a floor the earlier claim does not state: when the halfword read back sign-extended is negative, the writer stores 0 and returns before any band is considered. The 99/9999/999 ceilings of the nineteen-field block are therefore enforced on the set path as well as the add path, and neither of these two writers can leave a stat below zero.

The seventeen files exe/f0.s..f16.s carry English descriptions of their routine and are worth reading directly, but they are not authoritative: f5.s says it returns &D0x80041844[idx+1] while its own code computes D0x80041844 - 0xc + idx*0xc, i.e. entry idx-1.

claims.statement: Status bits 0x02, 0x04 and 0x08 each receive a timeline recovery event when applied, scheduled on whichever side the applier is called for. Applier queue codes 0x0a/0x0b/0x0c carry side and slot in the queue entry and expire into a shared recovery handler that resolves the target record from that entry (0x800a4470 + slot*0x20, +0x60 for the non-zero side). That handler explicitly tests only two selectors: 0x0e clears bit 0x04 (andi 0xfb) and 0x0f clears bit 0x08 (andi 0xf7); every other selector value falls through to a DEFAULT branch that clears bit 0x02 (andi 0xfd). There is no 0x0d-specific test, so the 0x0d->bit-0x02 association holds only insofar as 0x0d is what the appliers enqueue. F0x8009bda4 computes exact timeline-unit delays as: bit-0x04 mode 0 clamp(RAND%8001,2000,6000); bit-0x02 max(1000,RAND%500+3000+8*(T[+0x06]+G-O[+0x14]-O[+0x1c])); bit-0x04 mode 1 max(1000,RAND%500+3000+8*(T[+0x06]+G-O[+0x12]-O[+0x1e])); bit-0x08 max(500,RAND%500+1000+8*(T[+0x06]+G-O[+0x10]-O[+0x20])), where T and O are afflicted/opposing effective-stat structures and G=u8[0x800a435d]. The separate roll F0x800a19d8 only lets a still-afflicted actor act for that turn and never clears bit 0x02: its body contains no store outside its own stack frame. Bit 0x08 suppresses the action while set and recovers through its queued 0x0f clear, not a per-turn wake roll. Bit 0x04 is Confusion (runtime-tied); bits 0x02 and 0x08 are referred to by bit value only, as no artifact in evidence binds them to a name.

claims.statement: The status/event delta queue at 0x800a3868 is the battle clock. Normal player and enemy actions are distinct events: F0x8009c4bc stages code 2 (player) and F0x8009c4f8 stages code 3 (enemy), both singleton side -1 entries. Player completion paths re-enqueue code 2 with F0x8009bda4(side 0, opcode 0); enemy completion at 0x80088acc-0x80088af0 re-enqueues code 3 with F0x8009bda4(side 0x10, opcode 0). Queue bootstrap inserts code 2 at time 0 and code 3 at half of delay(0,0), creating the initial stagger; the wfightmn event jump table dispatches code 2 into the player controller and code 3 into the enemy controller. F0x8009bda4's default branch returns integer param[opcode].h0 * opp[+0xa] / isqrt(own[+0xa] * opp[+0xa]) using truncating division and a 10-iteration Babylonian integer sqrt seeded 999, with optional min/max clamps. Param entry 0 is [1000,707,1414], so each side's normal action delay is clamp(trunc(1000*opp[+0xa]/isqrt(own[+0xa]*opp[+0xa])),707,1414) in the same queue units as ailment recovery. F0x8009b930 is enqueue, F0x8009bc94 is find, and F0x8009b9d0 is preempt-enqueue. The enemy pre-turn gate consumes a code-4 special-command event; it is not the normal enemy scheduler.

claims.statement: The stat-dependent timed-recovery formulas use browser-addressable fields. F0x8009ec94 lays out SPT at effective +0x06, elements at +0x0c..+0x18 in Fire/Water/Ice/Wind/Thunder/Machine/Dark order, and status resistances at +0x1a..+0x22 in Poison/Paralyze/Confuse/Sleep/KO order. Therefore Frozen/opcode 9 uses afflicted SPT + magnitude - opponent Thunder - opponent Paralyze resistance; Confusion mode 1/opcode 10 uses afflicted SPT + magnitude - opponent Wind - opponent Confuse resistance; Sleep/opcode 11 uses afflicted SPT + magnitude - opponent Ice - opponent Sleep resistance. Status-resistance accessories are processed acc0 then acc1; target codes 0x11..0x15 assign item +0x06 directly to the corresponding effective resistance, so a later matching ring replaces rather than stacks. The byte 0x800a435d is the current applier magnitude scratch. For normal skill effects Frozen/Confusion/Sleep, magnitude is skill f9/effect_p2, doubled if victim record +0x1b is nonzero. Both special/direct Confusion callers are ChaosWave paths, use item magnitude 96 and mode 0; the normal battle action/status caller passes its nonzero context field as mode and therefore selects mode 1.

claims.statement: The memory-card I/O primitives used by the original executable (write_card_sector/read_card_sector, both bare BIOS trampolines at 0x8003da8c/elsewhere in exe/fns.s, and their higher wrappers such as F0x8003da4c/F0x8003e64c) exist only in exe/fns.s and operate on a generic fixed 128-byte (0x80) card-frame staging buffer (D0x80082c30), not a roster/form-ledger-shaped structure. A corpus-wide code-search for 'card_sector' across the entire original assembly tree (590072 lines scanned, which includes stfgtrep.s, stgdglab.s and fightstg.s) returns hits only in exe/fns.s and none in any of the three overlay files assigned to this frontier's source map, so the form-ledger's actual on-card serialization -- the routine that copies the persistent roster records (including the 44 acquired-form entries per starter) into card-sector buffers -- is not implemented in stfgtrep.s, stgdglab.s, or fightstg.s and must live in a still-unidentified higher-level save/load routine elsewhere in the executable (plausibly among the undifferentiated exe/fns.s callers already surfaced, e.g. F0x8003e27c/F0x8003e64c/F0x8003d370, which this pass did not fully trace).

The four-slot task subclass built by exe/fns:F0x8001b7b8 (handler F0x8001b724, size 0x84) is an asynchronous request object with a start / poll / dispose interface, and its bodies independently confirm the base task-object state fields of UI-TASKOBJ-STATEMACHINE-001. +0x74 F0x8001b63c stores the constant 0x10000000 into receiver+0x70, calls F0x8001b48c, and when receiver+0x58 is nonzero calls F0x8001b4cc and F0x8001b554 and reads receiver+0x64. +0x7c F0x8001b698 is the same entry point taking the +0x70 value from argument a2 instead of the constant, and after F0x8001b4cc it invokes the receiver's OWN slot +0x2c with argument 1 — that slot is the base object's set-state1 setter F0x80014288, so this subclass drives the inherited state machine through the inherited table. +0x78 F0x8001b6ec is the completion poll: it returns 0 when receiver+0x10 is nonzero, otherwise returns receiver+0x64 when receiver+0x58 is nonzero and receiver+0x50 when it is zero; receiver+0x10 is the base object's state1 field, so 'still running' is expressed as a nonzero state1. +0x80 F0x8001b444 is the dispose method: when receiver+0x64 is nonzero it passes that pointer to the global deallocator D0x8004b5ec, then clears receiver+0x64 and receiver+0x60. The handler F0x8001b724 branches on receiver+0xc, the base object's state0 field, confirming state0 at +0xc and state1 at +0x10 from a second, independent site.
claims.notes: What the request actually fetches is NOT established: F0x8001b48c, F0x8001b4cc and F0x8001b554 are unread, as is the meaning of receiver+0x50, +0x58, +0x60, +0x64 and +0x70 and of the constant 0x10000000. The start/poll/dispose SHAPE is established; the payload is not.
claims.frontier_rationale: Closes the slot semantics of one of the four remaining unnamed dispatch tables and independently corroborates the base state-machine field offsets underpinning the largest dispatch claim.

claims.statement: stgtrain, stitshop, and stfgtrep DIVERGE from the fieldstg/status pattern: at every dispatcher call site sampled (stgtrain pro/stgtrain:F0x800851d0 at stgtrain.s L1943-L1951; stitshop pro/stitshop:F0x800854ec at stitshop.s L2594-L2598; stfgtrep pro/stfgtrep:F0x80083ec8 at stfgtrep.s L1114-L1119 -- one representative dispatcher chosen per overlay, each shown driving multiple window-tween struct instances through the same fixed pointer cell), the caller consumes ONLY windowFoldTick's boolean 0/1 completion return via a `beqz`/`bnez` branch to gate a state transition; it never loads the tween's continuous +0x08 fold value or forwards it into any call, in contrast to fieldstg's F0x80084200, which loads +0x08 every animating frame and passes it as the first of three arguments into the DrawContext setScale slot (+0x8c). Whatever geometry/primitive the value actually animates in these three modules -- if it is consumed for drawing at all rather than being purely an internal timer -- is NOT set by the traced dispatcher itself. initDrawContext (F0x8001f648) is called elsewhere in each of the three overlays (7/6/3 sites respectively per `tools/run-overlay-scan.sh jal <overlay> 0x8001f648`), but none of those call sites fall inside the sampled tick-consuming dispatcher blocks, so this round did not locate the actual visual consumer, if one exists, and cannot assert scale, a divergent field (width/height/clip/alpha), or 'value is purely a gate, never drawn' as the final answer.

claims.contradiction_rationale: UI-C-FOLD-NONSTATUS-BOOLEAN-ONLY-DIVERGE-2026-08-04 states that at every dispatcher call site sampled in stgtrain, stitshop and stfgtrep the caller "consumes ONLY windowFoldTick's boolean 0/1 completion return ... it never loads the tween's continuous +0x08 fold value or forwards it into any call". For stfgtrep that is falsified by stfgtrep.s L859, which loads the fold value from screen+0x150, and by L864/L865/L867/L868, which forward it into the draw-context set-scale slot with the fold maximum as both remaining arguments. The falsification is consistent with the original claim's own stated method: it sampled "one representative dispatcher chosen per overlay", while the companion claim UI-C-FOLD-NONSTATUS-DISPATCHERS-RESOLVED-2026-08-04 counts 6 distinct dispatcher call sites in stfgtrep, 10 in stgtrain and 14 in stitshop. The consumer lies in a different function from the sampled dispatcher, so the original reading was a property of the sample rather than of the overlay.
claims.statement: The stfgtrep half of UI-C-FOLD-NONSTATUS-BOOLEAN-ONLY-DIVERGE-2026-08-04 is contradicted: stfgtrep does load the window-fold tween value and does forward it into a draw call, at stfgtrep.s L859 and L864/L865/L867/L868. The stgtrain and stitshop halves of that claim are NOT addressed by this entry and remain open on the evidence recorded here.
claims.coverage: This contradiction is scoped to stfgtrep alone. It was tested by reading the complete extent of the consuming function (L624 to L1029, bounded by jr $ra on both sides) rather than by sampling a single dispatcher, which is the check that would have confirmed the original claim had no such load existed anywhere in the frame. No statement is made here about stgtrain or stitshop, whose 10 and 14 dispatcher call sites were not read in this pass.
limitations: WHICH axis the fold value scales is not established, for the same reason as in fieldstg: the three scale components carry identical defaults and nothing here distinguishes them.
The two further loads of screen+0x150 at stfgtrep.s L882 and L986 were not traced to their dispatched slots.

stgtrain and stitshop were NOT re-read in this pass; their 10 and 14 dispatcher call sites remain unsampled in the ledger. web/shop.js and web/gym.js both carry source comments asserting the same scale-around-pivot reading, but browser code is authority 6 and is a navigation lead only, never proof.

The object identity between the consuming function and the dispatcher rests on both taking the screen object as an argument plus the offset coherence of tween base +0x148 against the value read at +0x150; no single instruction proves they are the same allocation.

claims.statement: For all three of stgtrain, stitshop, and stfgtrep, the fold-start/tick pair's callers ARE statically identifiable, despite zero direct jal/j to any of the six addresses anywhere in the 590074-line original corpus. `python3 tools/query_recovered_inventory.py callers <target>` (the allowlisted researcher tool over recovered/ddw3/function-inventory.json) resolves them as indirect callers through extracted overlay static initializers: stgtrain F0x8008b8fc has 20 indirect-caller edges (10 distinct dispatcher call sites, e.g. pro/stgtrain:F0x800851d0 at callsite 0x800851e4, reading a shared global function-pointer cell D0x8008d2b0 materialized from a literal `lui 0x8009/addiu -0x3034` base, independently confirmed by hand in the raw assembly at stgtrain.s L1928-L1930), stitshop F0x8008c2dc has 21 edges across 14 distinct call sites via cell D0x8008d1b8, and stfgtrep F0x80085c90 has 6 edges across 6 distinct call sites via cell D0x80089144. The same method resolves fieldstg's already-established caller (F0x80084200, cell D0x8009983c) identically, confirming the tool measures the real dispatch mechanism rather than an artifact.

claims.contradiction_rationale: The remaining two thirds of UI-C-FOLD-NONSTATUS-BOOLEAN-ONLY-DIVERGE-2026-08-04 are now falsified on the same footing as its stfgtrep third. That claim asserted that stgtrain, stitshop and stfgtrep all "never load the tween's continuous +0x08 fold value or forwards it into any call". stitshop loads it and forwards it into draw-context +0x8c, and stgtrain does the same. All three overlays dispatch through the identical stack slot sp+0x9c under an identical sp+0x10 context base, so the asserted divergence from the fieldstg/status pattern does not exist for any of the three.
claims.statement: UI-C-FOLD-NONSTATUS-BOOLEAN-ONLY-DIVERGE-2026-08-04 is contradicted in full. All three overlays it named -- stgtrain, stitshop and stfgtrep -- load the window-fold tween value and forward it into the draw context set-scale slot at offset +0x8c, reached through stack slot sp+0x9c under a context based at sp+0x10. There is no boolean-only divergence from the fieldstg pattern in any of them.
claims.coverage: The universal "all three" was tested by reading one complete consuming function in each of the three overlays, located by following the tween object offset that each overlay's own dispatcher passes to the fold tick, then searching that overlay for loads of that offset plus 8. That search is what would have exposed a genuine boolean-only overlay: an overlay with no such load would have returned none. The claim does NOT assert that every dispatcher call site in each overlay consumes the value -- 6, 10 and 14 sites are counted by UI-C-FOLD-NONSTATUS-DISPATCHERS-RESOLVED-2026-08-04 and only one consuming function per overlay was read.
limitations: WHICH axis the fold value scales remains unestablished in all four modules; the three scale components carry identical defaults and nothing in this evidence distinguishes them.

One consuming function was read per overlay. The 6, 10 and 14 dispatcher call sites counted for stfgtrep, stgtrain and stitshop were not individually read, so this does not establish that every window in these screens folds by scale.

Object identity between each consuming function and its dispatcher rests on offset coherence (tween base, value at base+8) plus both taking the screen object as an argument, not on a single proving instruction.
derivation: grep -n for the fold pointer-cell reads in stitshop.s and stgtrain.s
scratchpad extents.py -- nearest jr $ra either side of each initDrawContext/fold-read pair

claims.statement: The window-fold tween's value is a SCALE factor, not a width, height or alpha. Resolving the vtable slot that claim UI-CHROME-fieldstg-fold-value-consumer-2026-08-04 left open: the fieldstg window dispatcher calls initDrawContext (F0x8001f648) on its stack local sp+0x10 immediately before the fold loop, so the slot it dispatches through at sp+0x9c is draw-context offset 0x8c. initDrawContext installs F0x8001f5d0 there, and that function writes its three arguments into the current context's +0x38/+0x3c/+0x40 and raises the dirty flag +0x2c. claims.statement: The card album's two unresolved string banks are the game's card-name and card-text files, reached the same way every localised bank on these screens is. F0x800840ac fetches text with 0x80044B38->unk414(*(s32*)0x8005CCA8 + K) for K = 0x16 and K = 0x1D. 0x8005cca8 holds the language index 0..6, so each K is the base of a run of seven consecutive LBA entries: 0x16 is 22, the run LBA_MSCARDNM..LBA_SSCARDNM at 22..28, and 0x1D is 29, the run LBA_MSCARDST..LBA_SSCARDST at 29..35. The MS/US/ES/FS/IS/DS/SS filename prefixes of those two runs appear in exactly the decoded language order jpn, usa, eng, fra, ita, ger, spn. So K 0x16 selects the card NAME bank, which for English is LBA 24 escardnm.toml, and K 0x1D selects the card TEXT bank, which for English is LBA 31 escardst.toml and holds the effect and description lines rather than the rarity or class label an earlier note guessed. Both banks already ship in the walker: every one of the 316 entries in web/assets/data/card_catalog.json carries the escardnm string at its own card id, and the catalogue's effect field is escardst.
claims.notes: Resolves the stcrdabm_ui.json gap 'card name string bank (+0x16) and mystery/class label bank (+0x1D) at 0x8005CCA8 located but not resolved'. This is a third independent reproduction of the language index order (after cnty_sel's own table and the NAMEDTCS button art in UI-STDGNAME-ACTIONKEY-SPRITES-2026-08-14). NOT established: which string index the album's own card-detail popup passes to these banks; escrdabm.toml has only 9 strings so its popup's 0x0b/0x0c cannot come from this overlay's own bank, and that bank was not re-read. The evidence for F0x800840ac is the checked decompilation, authority 3; the two banks' identity rests on the LBA constant block, authority 2.

The seven-entry extent of each LBA run was read from the consecutive constant block in lba.rs, where entry 22 through 28 and 29 through 35 are the only CARDNM and CARDST entries and the next constant after each run is a different file, which is what bounds the runs at seven rather than assuming it from the language count.

claims.statement: In the field-stage window dispatcher F0x80084200 (pro/fieldstg.s, the only static caller of the fieldstg window-fold-start/tick pair F0x80091fdc/F0x80092070), the window-fold tween lives at the dispatcher's local state offset +0x58, so tween.value (tween+0x08) is read from state+0x60. On every dispatch after ticking, that raw value is read into $a0 and, whenever it is nonzero and not yet at the 0x1000 maximum (i.e. while the fold is still animating), it is passed directly as the first argument to a per-window vtable method (function pointer loaded from a stack vtable slot) together with the fold maximum 0x1000 twice as the second and third arguments. When value reaches exactly 0x1000 (fully open), the dispatcher instead takes a different branch that calls two other vtable methods with unrelated fixed constants. This proves tween.value is consumed on every animating frame as a live proportional argument (current amount out of the 0x1000 maximum) to a generic window-object draw/update method, not merely an internal bookkeeping counter -- i.e. it is exactly the kind of value-of-max pair a caller would use to compute an intermediate clip width/height, scale, or similar per-frame geometry for the folding window, though the callee's concrete geometric interpretation (width vs height vs alpha vs scale) was not resolved in this pass because the callee is reached only through a runtime-populated vtable slot.

cnty_sel is byte-accounted across its 0x177b bytes in five regions: file 0x0000-0x0038 a 14-entry state jump table; 0x0038-0x1710 code; 0x1710-0x173c the UI service descriptor block; 0x173c-0x1774 three window-fold timing tables with trailing words; and 0x1774-0x177b the seven-byte cursor-to-language table. The 14 words at file 0 are the switch table of the main state machine in F0x80083d18, targeting file offsets 0x1110, 0x111c, 0x113c, 0x1160, 0x1180, 0x11a4, 0x11c4, 0x11d4, 0x1588, 0x15a8, 0x1608, 0x1628, 0x1648 and 0x1684. Case 7 at 0x80083e84 is the input and confirm arm; docs/research/ui/cnty_sel-decoded-2026-07-11.md names that address as a FUNCTION F0x80083e84, but it is a case arm inside F0x80083d18, which is why exe-decomp/cnty_sel_c/ contains no such file. The cursor at +0x50 moves within a two-pane layout selected by the mode field +0x14: in the main list Up decrements with a floor of 0 and Down increments with a ceiling of 4, while in the side mode Left jumps to cursor 6 and Right moves cursor 6 to 5 or otherwise returns to the main list, giving the seven positions. Cursor movement plays packed sound 0x4001b and confirm plays 0x4001c, both through D0x80055c48. The post-confirm arm hands 0xE01 to D0x8004b440 when the global is zero and 0xE02 otherwise, which with UI-LANGUAGE-TABLE-001 means 0xE01 is specifically the JPN path; D0x8004b440 is the resident screen launcher of UI-STAGSLCT-LAUNCH-001, so this is an ordinary screen transition.

cnty_sel's cursor table is SEVEN bytes and every cursor row is wired to a distinct language. This CONTRADICTS docs/research/ui/cnty_sel-decoded-2026-07-11.md section 3, which recorded the table as `04 05 03 02 00 00 00 00` and concluded that only 4 of the 7 cursor rows were wired and that rows 4 to 6 selected 0. The error originates in that document's own reproduce command, `overlay_scan.py words cnty_sel 0x80084424 0x80084444`. The overlay stores the table as one `.word` at file 0x1774 followed by three trailing `.byte` directives at 0x1778, 0x1779 and 0x177a holding 6, 1 and 0, and tools/overlay_scan.py's only data pattern is WORD_RE, which matches `.word` alone; offsets covered solely by a `.byte` directive are absent from its map and print as zero. `.byte` occurs in just nine files across the whole assembly corpus, always as a run of two or three at end of file and always with a stride-4 label, which is a splat formatting artifact rather than real spacing: the label counter advances per directive instead of per byte. The consecutive reading is supported by wstag925.s, whose trailing run is a nonzero d1 d1 pair, and by the fact that only the consecutive reading makes cnty_sel's seven values a permutation of the seven language indices. LIMITATION: the shipped overlay binary is not present in the repository, so the .s file is the sole authority and this rests on the corpus-wide `.byte` convention plus the permutation check rather than on a byte-level dump.

The five cursor frames of the menu selection cursor (UI-CURSORCLASS-B364-001) are resolved, and the animation is a four-glyph PING-PONG, not a five-frame loop. The pointer table D0x8004dce0 that the cursor handler indexes by its frame counter holds, in order, the addresses D0x8005ccdc, D0x8005ccd8, D0x8005ccd4, D0x8005ccd0 and D0x8005ccd4 again, and those four words hold 0x00008581, 0x00008681, 0x00008781 and 0x00008881 - little-endian, so each is the two-byte string 0x81 0x85, 0x81 0x86, 0x81 0x87 and 0x81 0x88 followed by the terminating zero. Under the game's documented text encoding (docs/research/ui/menu-assets-decoded-2026-07-03.md: a 2-byte sequence 0x81 N selects extended glyph N-1) the five frames are extended glyphs 0x84, 0x85, 0x86, 0x87 and then 0x86 again. So the cursor plays glyph 0x84, 0x85, 0x86, 0x87, back to 0x86, then wraps to frame 0 and returns to its resting dwell. Combined with the shipped timings, the complete on-screen behaviour is: rest on glyph 0x84 for 32 ticks, then step through 0x85, 0x86, 0x87, 0x86 at 6 ticks per frame, then rest again.
claims.notes: The pointer table and its string words are authority 3 (the transcribed data segment ~/ddw3/rust/dw2003_exe_data/src/data.rs L4006-L4010 and L14940-L14946); the indexing code that consumes them is authority 2 (exe/fns.s F0x8001b0a4). NOT established: what extended glyphs 0x84-0x87 look like - they are indices into the UI font's extended table, and the four images have not been extracted or compared against a capture; and whether the tick unit is a vsync or a frame counter, which decides whether the dwell is 32 vsyncs or 32 frames. Both are needed before this can be treated as a pixel-accurate reproduction rather than a correct sequence and ratio.

claims.statement: F0x8001b364(a0,a1,a2,a3) is the constructor of the menu SELECTION CURSOR object: it allocates a 0x98-byte task through F0x80014504 with per-frame handler F0x8001b0a4 and priority 4, stores its four sign-extended s16 arguments at self+0x50/+0x54/+0x58/+0x5c, presets self+0x64=1 (visible), self+0x74=0x20 (32) and self+0x78=6, and installs a six-slot table at +0x80..+0x94. The cursor does not draw itself: on its first tick its handler creates a class-A TEXT WIDGET with F0x8001ae38(self+0x50, 1, self+0x58, self+0x5c) and thereafter drives that widget through the widget's own slots. The cursor GLYPH is therefore a text string: the handler indexes the five-entry pointer table D0x8004dce0 by the current frame at self+0x6c and installs the selected string through the widget's +0x110 set-line-0-text slot. The animation is a rest-then-cycle blink: while base state1 (self+0x10) is 0 the cursor sits on frame 0 until self+0x74 ticks have elapsed since the timestamp at self+0x70, then it latches frame 1 and sets state1=1; while state1 is 1 it advances one frame every self+0x78 ticks, and on reaching frame 5 it resets to frame 0 and returns to state1=0. Elapsed time comes from the shared UI service block slot D0x8004de10+0x188. So the shipped defaults are a 32-tick dwell followed by a five-frame cycle at 6 ticks per frame. Setting self+0x7c (slot +0x94) freezes the cursor: the handler snaps the frame back to 0 and skips the animation entirely.
claims.notes: Slots: +0x80 F0x8001b04c(self,enable) sets self+0x64 and, when disabling, also clears base state1 (+0x10) and the timestamp (+0x70); +0x84 F0x8001b068(self,x,y) sets +0x58/+0x5c (position); +0x88 F0x8001b07c(self,v) sets +0x60; +0x8c F0x8001b08c(self,v) sets +0x74 (dwell); +0x90 F0x8001b094(self,v) sets +0x78 (frame interval); +0x94 F0x8001b09c(self,v) sets +0x7c (freeze). The first three also raise the dirty flag +0x68, which the handler consumes by re-pushing visibility, position and +0x60 into the widget. claims.statement: The tick that the pad service's repeat timer is measured in is the display service's counter at 0x8004DE10+0x10, published by GPU slot +0x188 (F0x8001D6F4). That counter is not incremented directly: the display callback F0x8001D3F4 adds 0x100 to an accumulator at 0x8004DE10+0x14 when D0x8005CCAC is non-zero and 0x133 when it is zero, and F0x8001D504 republishes the counter as that accumulator shifted right by 8. 0x133/0x100 is 1.1992, i.e. 60/50 to within the fixed-point step, so the two increments are a region normalisation and the counter is a 60-per-second-equivalent count on both, provided the callback runs once per vertical blank.

claims.statement: UI-DISPLAY-TICK-2026-08-21 is narrowed. Its region reading was not new: submarimon-throttle-tank-steering already established that D0x8005CCAC selects the video mode, that F0x8001D3F4 branches on it for 0x133 versus 0x100, that this is a video-mode compensation in the 6:5 ratio, and that the non-zero branch is NTSC and the zero branch PAL. The withdrawn claim presented that as an untested inference when it was already established elsewhere, and it should have cited the prior claim. What stands, and is recorded as new in UI-DISPLAY-TICK-CHAIN-2026-08-21, is only the publication chain: the accumulator at display +0x14 is republished as the counter at display +0x10 by a shift right of 8 in F0x8001D504, GPU slot +0x188 (F0x8001D6F4) returns that counter, and it is the clock the pad service's repeat timer divides against.

The clock the pad service's auto-repeat divides against is the display service's counter at 0x8004DE10+0x10, which GPU slot +0x188 (F0x8001D6F4) returns. That counter is republished rather than incremented: the display callback F0x8001D3F4 advances an accumulator at 0x8004DE10+0x14 by 0x100 or 0x133 depending on D0x8005CCAC, and F0x8001D504 stores that accumulator shifted right by 8 into +0x10 once per pass. Combined with submarimon-throttle-tank-steering, which establishes D0x8005CCAC as the video-mode selector with 0x100 for NTSC and 0x133 for PAL in a 6:5 compensation, the counter therefore advances at the same rate in both regions, so a repeat cadence expressed in these ticks is the same wall-clock cadence on a PAL and an NTSC machine.
claims.coverage: The two increments and the shift were read directly in the two decompiled routines quoted, not pattern-matched. claims.statement: Display-service +0x17c is a 30-cell exact-key lookup for registered render-view objects, not directly an ordering-table bucket lookup. Each registry cell pairs an object pointer at service +0x60+i*4 with a key at +0xd8+i*4. F0x8001dbe0 creates a view and stores its third argument verbatim as that key; F0x8001da84 returns the occupied cell whose key equals its argument or zero after 30 misses. The returned view's method +0x138 is the second stage: F0x8001dfa8 selects the current frame's ordering-table word array at view +0x5c/+0x60 and returns base + bucketIndex*4. Shared wrapper F0x8001ed34 and the screen-dim caller both preserve this order: first resolve the view key, then pass the independent bucket to view +0x138. Thus the key selects a registered viewport/draw environment and the bucket selects relative draw depth inside it.
claims.coverage: The +0x17c lookup and +0x16c creator were read over their complete assembly extents, including the 30-iteration termination and zero return. The constructor was followed through both ordering-table allocations and the +0x138 method install. The +0x138 body is complete and contains no bounds branch. Both the shared wrapper and a concrete dim caller were followed through argument preservation. Recovered inventory reports 90 indirect F0x8001da84 calls across 37 modules and zero unattributed calls; those callers were not individually assigned numeric key meanings.
limitations: The exact player-facing vocabulary of every numeric registry key is not yet inventoried.
The full semantic name of F0x8001dbe0 arg1 is not established beyond indexing D0x8004dfa0 to size the ordering table and being stored at view +0x68.
The existing canonical shorthand that calls +0x16c's third argument a scale must be corrected: its verbatim key storage is direct assembly, but no tracked document was edited by this worker.
No runtime frame trace or overlap/clip capture was taken, so walker presentation parity is not established.

claims.statement: Inside the draw entry point F0x8001ed6c the draw-context fields are consumed as follows. Screen position: each piece's own x/y (+0x2/+0x4 of the piece record) is added to the caller's x/y arguments (saved at sp+0x90/sp+0x94) and then the context anchor at +0x30/+0x34 is SUBTRACTED, so +0x30/+0x34 is an origin/pivot offset rather than a position. Palette selection: the CLUT id is assembled as ((clutY + ctx+0x20) << 6) | (((clutX) >> 4) & 0x3f), taking clutX/clutY from ctx +0x18/+0x1c when the piece flag at +0xc is nonzero and from ctx +0x10/+0x14 otherwise, so +0x20 is a CLUT row offset applied to both palette banks. Transform fast path: the routine compares +0x38, +0x3c and +0x40 against 0x1000 and checks +0x48/+0x4c before taking an unscaled/unrotated path, confirming those fields are scale and rotation. Flag +0x24, when nonzero, makes the routine call method +0x11c on the bound sheet object at ctx+0x0 with a stack buffer.

claims.statement: stdwtitl's F0x8008453c is the game's END card, not the boot-animation dispatcher an earlier note took it for. It reads the language global at 0x8005cca8 (stdwtitl.s L0x00001890), gates it with sltiu 0x7 (L0x000018a8) and jumps through the seven-word table at the overlay's file offset 0, whose targets set a clip number in s0 (L0x000018d4-L0x000018ec). The seven words give clip 0 for languages 0, 1 and 2, clip 2 for 3, clip 3 for 4, clip 1 for 5 and clip 2 for 6; a language outside the gate keeps the s0 = 0 the function started with. It then resolves pack handle 0x08A60000, which is LBA_END__ALL_BIN_IDX 2214, through [0x80044f5c] (L0x00001944) and draws clip s0 at (0, 0) (L0x0000194c-L0x0000195c). That pack holds four 128x40 images whose clip records each carry the layer offset (96, 100), so the card lands at (96, 100) - exactly centred on the 320x240 screen both ways. The four images read END, Ende, Fin and Fine, which places them on jpn/usa/eng, ger, fra/spn and ita in the decoded language order. The fade is a CLUT row walk rather than alpha: the screen object's level at +0x50 is pushed through draw-context slot +0x88, the set-CLUT-row-offset slot of UI-DRAWCTX-VTABLE-001 (L0x00001920-L0x0000192c), and the frames name CLUT y 240 inside a 256-row page, so the levels are palette rows 240 to 255, a ramp from green at level 0 to white at level 15. F0x80084628 drives it: entry sets level 15 and the timer 0, then state 0 steps the level down to 0 one step per 2 timer units, state 1 holds to 0x78, state 2 holds to 0x4650 or until the player presses logical button 3 which sets the timer straight to 0x4650, state 3 steps the level back up to 15, state 4 holds to 0x3c, and state 5 makes the resident loading call 0xE01 and hands off.
claims.notes: Closes the stdwtitl_ui.json gap that called F0x8008453c a per-state boot/connect dispatcher, and corrects the logo gap's claim that the logo draw is consumed by it - it is not, so the logo's own draw site is unlocated rather than merely un-decompilable. This is a fourth independent reproduction of the language index order. Wired: tools/extract_screen_packs.py SPLIT_PACKS emits endall_sheet with all 16 CLUT variants per clip, tools/extract_stdwtitl_ui.py emits end_screen, web/endscreen.js renders it, and it is reachable as __labOpen('endscreen'). NOT established: what the card is drawn OVER - the levels ramp toward white, not toward the black the walker paints behind it, so the original may run this over something; where in the game's flow the screen is entered from, since only F0x80084628 was traced and not its caller; the unit of the timer delta, so 0x4650 cannot be converted to seconds; and F0x800869d0, the overlay's other jr-dispatcher, is still unread. The decompilation evidence for F0x80084628 is authority 3; every coordinate and table value rests on the assembly at authority 2.
claims.coverage: All seven words of the language table were read individually at file offsets 0x00 through 0x18, so the mapping is the whole table rather than a sample, and the word at 0x1c is zero, which is what bounds it at seven independently of the sltiu gate. Every one of the four targets was followed to the li that sets s0. The pack side is an enumeration too: the splat directory holds exactly four frame records of 14 bytes, an id list terminating at 0xff after 0, 1, 2, 3, and four clip files, and all four were decoded and rendered to read their text. The 16 fade levels are bounded by arithmetic, not assumption: CLUT y 240 in a page whose decompressed size is exactly 20 header bytes plus 64 halfwords by 256 rows leaves precisely 16 rows. The state machine was read end to end from the decompilation of F0x80084628, all six arms.

claims.statement: Walking into a field screen plays a LOCATION TITLE CARD. The field's own stage-entry sequence builds it - F0x80087d68(1), a 0x1C0-byte task object whose per-frame callback is F0x80087974 - with a literal 1, so it runs on every entry with the names shown, and it raises the global 0x80099DD4 for as long as it is on screen. It draws the current scene's area name at (128, 26) and its place name at (40, 68), both built with the shared class-A text widget in group 0x1003 and both armed with a typewriter reveal of delay 5, which is one character every six frames because the widget update advances only when its per-frame counter EXCEEDS the delay. The card then enters its second state PARKED: the shared set-state method zeroes the sub-state and state 2 does nothing below sub-state 2, so the finished card sits on screen until the field, which kept its handle, sets the sub-state to 1. Only then does it hold 60 frames and close, the clip rectangle of group 0x1003 starting at the full 320x240 screen and shrinking by 8 at the top and 16 in height per frame - fifteen frames to nothing - after which the card clears 0x80099DD4 and stops drawing.
claims.coverage: Every number is the instruction's own immediate, read from the original assembly rather than sampled: the two label positions are the constructor's third and fourth arguments, the reveal delay is the +0x130 call's argument, the hold bound is the compare, and the wipe rectangle and its two steps are the four stores. The park was established by reading state 2's dispatch in the assembly rather than trusting the decompiler, and the release site is the only other place that holds the card's handle. Both text widgets are the same constructor the project has already decoded across seven other screens.
claims.limitations: Whether the closing slit clips the bars as well as the two labels was NOT established: the rectangle is set on widget group 0x1003, and both the labels and the bar primitives name that group, but the bars are pushed through a generic primitive linker whose ordering-table depth was not read. claims.statement: The pad service's auto-repeat is a per-physical-button accelerating timer, not a fixed interval. For each held button the poll F0x80018BCC tests (tick - last_pulse_tick + credit) / rate with a signed divide, where rate is the service-wide half-word at 0x8004B7D0+0x3D4, last_pulse_tick is the s32 at record +0x54 + 4*bit and credit is the byte at record +0x94 + bit. A non-zero quotient sets that button's bit in the repeat word at record +0x4A, stamps last_pulse_tick to the current tick, and raises credit by 10 saturating at 12. Releasing the button restamps last_pulse_tick and clears credit to 0. The rate is 0x10 and does not vary: pad init F0x80018310 is reached from a single call site, at 0x80018488, whose delay slot passes a1 = 0x10, and pad init is the only writer of +0x3D4. With rate 16 the successive hold intervals are therefore 16 ticks to the first repeat, then 6, then 4 for every repeat after that.

The 16/6/4 figures are arithmetic on the read constants, not measurements: they assume the divide is the one at 0x80018e68 and rate 16, and they were not observed in the running game. The claim says nothing about how long a tick lasts in real time; see UI-DISPLAY-TICK-2026-08-21.

claims.statement: The DDW3 logical-button remap is the IDENTITY as shipped, so a menu that reads logical button id N is reading PS1 pad bit N. UI-PADSERVICE-STATIC-TABLE-001 established that pad-service slot +0x408 (F0x80018980) returns the byte at pad record +0xa4+logicalId, i.e. that logical ids pass through a per-controller byte array rather than naming bits directly. That array is filled by F0x800188c0, which copies 16 consecutive bytes from the static table at D0x8004bbf4 into record+0xa4, and the four words of that table hold 0x03020100, 0x07060504, 0x0b0a0908 and 0x0f0e0d0c -- little-endian, the byte run 0x00 through 0x0f, an identity permutation. Pad init F0x80018310 calls F0x800188c0 for all 2 ports x 4 multitap slots unconditionally, with no test of the language global D0x8005cca8 or any other region value, so the identity is installed for every controller on every build. The sibling F0x80018928 swaps two entries of the same array and would break the identity, but it is NOT called by pad init. CONSEQUENCE for the menus: the shop's decoded buttons up=4, down=6, confirm=13, cancel=14 are pad bits 4, 6, 13 and 14, which under the standard PS1 layout are Up, Down, CIRCLE and CROSS. Circle confirms and Cross cancels. This CONTRADICTS community guides for the English release which state that Cross confirms and Triangle cancels; those are not evidence and do not disturb this reading.
claims.coverage: The universal "for every controller on every build" was tested against the init function body rather than assumed: F0x80018310 contains exactly one nested loop, 2 outer by 4 inner, calling F0x800188c0 with no conditional around it, and no branch anywhere in the function reads the language global or any region byte -- a region-dependent mapping would have required such a branch and there is none. The bit-position reading is corroborated from two independent in-repo directions rather than from external convention: the shop's own decoded up=4/down=6 match the standard layout's Up and Down bits, and UI-SHOCKTST-IDENTITY-001 ties shocktst's displayed Cross legend to a read of bit 14. NOT tested: whether any code path anywhere calls the swapper F0x80018928 after init. tools/query_recovered_inventory reports zero callers for it, but that tool resolves overlay pointer cells rather than static-table dispatch, so its zero is not proof of absence and the claim is scoped to the state left by initialisation.
limitations: Whether any code path calls the entry swapper F0x80018928 after initialisation was not established; the claim describes the state left by init.

The mapping from pad bit position to physical button name relies on the standard PS1 layout, corroborated in-repo by the shop up/down bits and the shocktst Cross legend, but no controller-protocol document in this repository was cited.
The four table words were read from the transcribed data segment (authority 4), not from a byte-level dump of the shipped executable.

claims.statement: The two hottest apparently-unresolved indirect-call offsets in the whole DDW3 corpus are not dynamic dispatch at all - they are reads from a STATIC function-pointer table, and both now resolve to concrete functions. Call sites of the documented shape la_ base, D0x8004b7d0 then lw f, 0xNNN(base) then jalr f (e.g. exe/fns.s L1691-L1700 in F0x80011318) take base as the ADDRESS of the global D0x8004b7d0, so slot +0xNNN is the absolute data word 0x8004b7d0+0xNNN, and the decompiled data segment shows a run of seventeen consecutive function-address words starting at D0x8004bbb0 that covers offsets +0x3e0..+0x420. Resolving the hot offsets through it: +0x3f4 (489 unresolved sites) = F0x80018854, +0x3f8 = F0x80018878, +0x3fc (207 sites) = F0x8001889c, +0x404 = F0x80018928, +0x408 (760 sites, the single hottest offset in the corpus) = F0x80018980, +0x40c = F0x800189a8, +0x414 (270 sites) = F0x800189b8. Reading the targets settles what the pad service actually is: the input state lives in PER-PORT RECORDS of 0x1c0 bytes laid out from D0x8004b7d0, since F0x80018854 computes ((port*8 - port) << 6) = port*0x1c0 before its load. F0x80018854(port) returns the halfword at record+0x48 and F0x80018878(port) the halfword at record+0x4e - two separate 16-bit button words per port. F0x80018980(port, logicalId) returns the BYTE at record+0xa4+logicalId, i.e. it indexes a per-port byte array by the logical button id - this is the logical-button remap that docs/research/ui/shared-ui-service-families-2026-08-04.md L241-L247 records as reached through +0x408 and explicitly NOT yet read. F0x800189a8 is a two-instruction stub returning zero. F0x800189b8 tests bit 0x00800000 of the first word at D0x8004b7d0 and returns 0 when clear.
claims.notes: The table contents are authority 3 (the transcribed data segment ~/ddw3/rust/dw2003_exe_data/src/data.rs L3667-L3683), but every TARGET body quoted above was read at authority 2 from exe/fns.s and its content is consistent with a pad service, which is strong corroboration that the offset-to-function mapping is right. NOT established: the physical PS1 button each logical id maps to - that needs the per-port byte array at record+0xa4 dumped with actual values, which the static data does not give (D0x8004b7d0 itself is zero-initialised, so the records are filled at runtime); which of record+0x48 and record+0x4e is held-buttons versus newly-pressed; and what bit 0x00800000 means to F0x800189b8. IMPORTANT NEGATIVE: offset +0x424 (308 sites) does NOT resolve this way - 0x8004b7d0+0x424 = 0x8004bbf4 holds the data word 0x03020100 followed by 0x07060504, a byte sequence, not a function pointer, so those 308 sites either use a different base global or are misclassified as calls by the inventory. Do not attribute them without separate evidence.
claims.frontier_rationale: +0x408 and +0x3f4 are the two highest-traffic unresolved dispatch offsets in the corpus (1,249 sites between them); they were unreachable by the installer-idiom scan because the table is initialised data, not code.

claims.statement: The pause menu's list cursor is a small solid TRIANGLE that pulses, and it is a font glyph rather than a sprite. Its widget owns one text child and swaps that child's string on a five-step cycle: it rests 32 vsyncs on the first frame, then steps every 6 vsyncs through four more and begins again. The four frames are the four contiguous cursor glyphs the game's own codec names [enter], [enter2], [select] and [space2] -- a small solid triangle, a large one, a short bar and nothing. The walker drew the tailed arrow (extended glyph 54), which belongs to the SHOP, and drew it as a still image.
claims.notes: The animation shape, the two frame counts and the five-entry frame table are read straight from the assembly and the EXE image. Which of the four codes selects which of the four glyphs is an assignment, not a reading: the four codes are contiguous, the four cursor-family glyphs are contiguous, and the frame the rig capture shows matches [select] pixel for pixel, which fixes the offset. The EXE's inline string encoding is NOT the lang-file codec (those bytes decode to hiragana there), so the offset itself is unexplained and the frame ORDER should be re-checked against a rig capture of two different frames before this is promoted.

claims.statement: F0x800301dc(arg0, arg1) is a shared byte-stream decoder/accumulator: it selects a 0xB0-byte record from the pointer array D0x800815a0[arg0] (window/slot id, table-indexed) at element arg1, reads a base-128 continuation-encoded value from a cursor field at the record's offset +0x00 (advancing the cursor), multiplies the decoded value by 10, and adds it into a 32-bit accumulator field at the record's offset +0x88, returning the added delta. This matches the widget/task-object per-item record referenced by F0x8002f59c's dispatch loop (same D0x800815a0 base, same 0xB0 element stride, same per-window/per-item iteration), so the record is the same 0xB0-byte task-object slot documented informally elsewhere as a per-window item table, not a new struct.
claims.coverage: Checked by reading the full assembly body (L35053-35093, 41 instructions) against the full decompiled C body line-for-line; both agree on every arithmetic step. Not tested against every one of F0x800301dc's 24 static callers -- only its own body and F0x8002f59c's D0x800815a0/0xB0 usage were cross-checked.
limitations: I did not resolve what field +0x88 semantically represents (list scroll offset, spline/path advance, or something else) -- only that it is a 32-bit accumulator fed by a scaled VLQ-decoded delta. I did not trace any caller far enough to see +0x88 consumed by a draw routine.

I did not confirm the record at D0x800815a0[id]+arg1*0xB0 is identical in every respect to the record used by F0x800340ec/F0x800349cc's D0x80082658-based table (different base globals, same 0xB0-ish scale is a lead only).

claims.statement: F0x80037d0c(arg0, arg1) is a bounds-checked bank selector shared by F0x800340ec and F0x800349cc (and 7 other exe-resident callers): for a bank id arg0 in [0,0x10), if the per-bank validity byte D0x80082688[arg0]==1 and the element index arg1 is below the count halfword D0x8008264a, it re-points exactly three global cache variables from exactly three parallel bank-indexed tables -- D0x80082658 <- D0x80082608[arg0*4] (record-table base), D0x80082654 <- D0x800825c0[arg0*4] (a second base), and D0x8008264c <- D0x80082580[arg0*4] (a scalar) -- and records arg0 and arg1 into the status struct D0x80082669 at +0 and +5, plus a byte at +6 read from offset +8 of (arg1*0x10 + D0x80082580[arg0*4]); otherwise it returns -1 without touching those globals. NOTE: D0x8008264a is loaded with no index register and is therefore a SINGLE global halfword count, not a per-bank count; it presumably reflects the currently selected bank, but this routine does not establish that and no writer of it was traced.
claims.coverage: LEAD CORRECTION 2026-08-10, verified against the original assembly (authority 2) at fns.s L43303-43350, the function's complete extent through the jr $ra delay slot. The worker's original statement said 'four global cache variables' and 'four parallel 16-entry tables' while listing only three of each, and mistyped D0x80082580 as 'D0x82580'. Counting the bank-indexed loads (addu of bank*4 before the %lo load) across the whole body yields exactly three: L43326-43328 (D0x800825c0), L43329-43331 (D0x80082580), L43332-43334 (D0x80082608); and exactly three sw stores to globals: L43339 (D0x80082658), L43343 (D0x80082654), L43345 (D0x8008264c). The 'four' was untested and is corrected to three. The worker's 'per-bank count D0x8008264a' was also untested and is falsified by L43318-43319, which is a bare lui/lh with no index added. The guard boundaries themselves (arg0==0x10, arg1==count) were read statically as comparison operators only and were not exercised at runtime.
limitations: This function was not in the assigned four-address worklist; it is recorded because both assigned getter/setter routines are unintelligible without it -- D0x80082658 is otherwise an opaque global.
I did not identify what D0x80082654 or D0x8008264c (the two other cache fields this function sets) are consumed by.

claims.statement: Every direct caller (by address-literal jal) of the four assigned routines F0x800301dc, F0x800340ec, F0x800349cc and F0x8003dabc found by a corpus-wide code-search is located in the main-EXE assembly file exe/fns.s itself, not in any pro/ overlay source file -- the brief's framing of these as routines the 'menu/UI overlays share' is not directly demonstrated by a jal-target text match from any overlay file; if overlay code reaches them, it does so indirectly through some other exe-resident dispatcher, or through a function-pointer call this text search cannot see.
claims.coverage: Ran ./dw3-research code-search over the whole original-assembly corpus (~/ddw3/asm/dw2003, 590160 lines, all overlay and EXE .s files) for the literal hex text of all four addresses (800301dc, 800340ec, 800349cc, 8003dabc) plus F0x800301dc's/F0x800340ec's/F0x8003dabc's own labels; every one of the four searches reported files=1, matching only exe/fns.s. claims.statement: F0x800340ec and F0x800349cc are a getter/setter pair for one shared 0x18-byte-payload record type (14 u8 fields at offsets 0x0-0xD plus 4 u16 fields at offsets 0x10,0x12,0x14,0x16, at a 0x20-byte table stride): both guard on the per-bank validity byte D0x80082688[arg0]==1, both call F0x80037d0c(arg0, arg1) to re-point the shared table-base global D0x80082658 at bank arg0, and both index the same record with (arg2 + D0x8008266f*0x10)*0x20 before copying the 0x18-byte payload between the table and the caller's stack struct (arg3), one direction each. F0x8003171c demonstrates the constructor-argument path the frontier asked for: it calls the getter, overwrites exactly the first byte field (record offset 0) with its own argC parameter, and calls the setter -- so a caller's per-call literal argument becomes one named byte field of this shared record, not a pixel-measured screen coordinate invented independently per menu.
claims.coverage: Read both full function bodies (F0x800340ec L5-34, F0x800349cc L5-34) line-for-line against each other and against the assembly index-math instructions; confirmed they are structural mirrors (get vs set) of the same address arithmetic and the same field list, in the same field order including the unk7-before-unk6 swap. Read one caller (F0x8003171c) in full to confirm the read-modify-write pattern; did not read the other 14 near-identical callers (F0x800317ac, F0x8003186c, F0x800318fc, F0x8003198c, F0x80031b3c, F0x80031bfc, F0x80031cac, F0x80031d5c, F0x80031e0c, F0x80031ecc, F0x80031f7c, F0x8003202c, F0x8003210c, F0x800321ac) individually, so I cannot state which single byte or u16 field each one overwrites -- only that F0x8003171c overwrites offset 0.
limitations: I did not name the 14+4 fields (x/y/w/h/flags/etc.) -- static reading gives only offsets and sizes (u8 x14, u16 x4), not meaning. Attributing a specific field to 'geometry' (x, y, width, height) versus another menu attribute (color, animation state, sound id) would need either a caller that writes a value with an obviously geometric range, or a runtime trace.
I did not resolve what D0x8008266f (the 'page'/bank-scale byte multiplied by 0x10 into the index) represents, beyond that it shifts the addressed record by a constant number of table slots per unit.

claims.statement: F0x8003dabc(arg0) pushes one level onto a small stack whose depth counter is the global D0x8005cb40. It loads the counter, forms depth=counter+1, and tests `slti $v0, $a2, 0x4`: when depth is NOT below 4 it calls the handler F0x800283fc with a0=&D0x80010e38 and returns without pushing or committing the counter; otherwise it commits depth back to D0x8005cb40, stores arg0 into the word array D0x800829a0 at index depth (a 4-byte stride, `sll $v0, $a2, 0x2`), and zero-fills a 16-byte per-level record. The record address is computed as D0x8008296c + depth*0x10 (a 16-BYTE per-level stride, EV-UIQ002-A6), but the clear loop writes DOWNWARD from that address in 4-byte steps for exactly 4 stores (EV-UIQ002-A7), so the bytes actually zeroed for level `depth` are D0x8008296c + depth*0x10 - 0xC through +0x3. Equivalently the record array base is D0x80082960 with a 16-byte stride, and the symbol D0x8008296c names the LAST word of each record, not the first. The highest level index this routine can write is therefore 3. arg0 is an opaque caller value; the immediately following routine F0x8003db38 indexes the same D0x800829a0 array and calls through it with jalr, which is a lead that arg0 is a callback or context pointer, but that routine was not decoded here and the reading is not established.
claims.coverage: LEAD CORRECTION 2026-08-10 against the original assembly (authority 2), F0x8003dabc's complete extent fns.s L49769-49799 read through the jr $ra delay slot. The worker's claim said the routine 'zero-fills a 16-byte-stride per-level record', while its own coverage said m2c 'misrepresents the real 4-byte step as a 16-byte step' -- the two contradicted each other and the worker reported the start address of the record as unresolved. Both quantities are real and distinct: the per-level STRIDE is 16 bytes (L49783, sll by 4) and the clear-loop STEP is 4 bytes (L49795, addiu -4). The loop count was settled by tracing $a1 = 3,2,1,0 against `bgez`, whose delay-slot decrement executes on the final non-taken iteration too, giving exactly 4 stores and 16 bytes; the descent direction resolves the start address to base-0xC. The 'highest level index is 3' follows from the single `slti ... 0x4` guard, which is the only bound in the body. NOT tested: the initial value of D0x8005cb40, so the number of usable levels (3 or 4) is not established here, and no writer or initialiser of that counter was traced.
limitations: I could not determine, from static reading alone, whether the zero-filled 16 bytes belong to the record at depth*0x10 or to a range straddling depth*0x10-0xC through depth*0x10 (see EV-UIQ002-A3); this affects which per-level struct offsets are 'zeroed by push' if that struct is ever tied to widget geometry.

All 14 direct callers of F0x8003dabc live in exe/fns.s in the 0x8003be78-0x8003cfe4 range; I did not open any of them, so I cannot say what menu/window-open event triggers a push, only that the mechanism is a shared depth-4 stack primitive.

claims.statement: F0x8003210c writes record offset 0x9 directly from the low byte of its own word-sized incoming stack parameter (loaded via lw $s3,0x70($sp), stored via sb $s3,0x55($sp)). F0x800321ac writes record offset 0xa the same way (lw $s3,0x70($sp), stored via sb $s3,0x56($sp)). In these two wrappers the direct byte write coexists with a call to the re-encode helper F0x80031a98 that is not preceded, anywhere in either function, by a read of record offsets 0x10/0x12 or a call to the decode helper F0x80031a3c -- the same no-decode pattern seen in F0x80031f7c and F0x8003202c.
claims.limitations: As with F0x80031f7c and F0x8003202c, the effect of the unpopulated encode call on record offsets 0x10/0x12 in these two wrappers is unresolved without a runtime trace of the stack contents at the call site; only the direct byte writes to offsets 0x9 and 0xa are established with confidence.

claims.statement: F0x80031f7c departs from the decode/re-encode shape of its seven siblings in UI-Q002-WRAP-PACKED-FIELD-2026-08-10: after the shared getter call it goes straight to setting up the re-encode call's arguments, omitting the lhu reads of record offsets 0x10/0x12 and the call to the decode helper F0x80031a3c that every other packed-field wrapper performs first. It sets temp-struct suboffset 0xe to 1 and writes its own byte parameter (loaded via lbu $s3,0x70($sp)) into temp-struct suboffset 0x8, then calls the re-encode helper F0x80031a98 and the shared setter, matching F0x80031ecc's suboffsets (0xe flag, 0x8 value) but with F0x80031ecc clearing the flag instead of setting it.
claims.limitations: Because the temp struct is not populated by a decode call in this function, the record offsets 0x10/0x12 written by the encode call also depend on whatever values already occupy stack offsets sp+0x10..sp+0x22 in this call frame; this packet does not determine what those values actually are (uninitialized local stack, not traced at runtime), so the full effect on record offsets 0x10/0x12 beyond the two suboffsets explicitly written (0x8, 0xe) is unresolved.
claims.coverage: The scope word 'every other packed-field wrapper' was tested by enumeration, not asserted: the assignment fixed the denominator at the 14 known callers of the getter/setter pair (F0x800317ac, F0x8003186c, F0x800318fc, F0x8003198c, F0x80031b3c, F0x80031bfc, F0x80031cac, F0x80031d5c, F0x80031e0c, F0x80031ecc, F0x80031f7c, F0x8003202c, F0x8003210c, F0x800321ac), and every one of those 14 bodies was read in full in this pass; the packed-field subset is the 8 identified in UI-Q002-WRAP-PACKED-FIELD-2026-08-10.
