The claim's scope does NOT extend beyond these 14 wrappers: other callers of the getter/setter pair outside this enumerated set were not searched for.

claims.statement: Seven of the fourteen assigned wrappers (F0x8003198c, F0x80031b3c, F0x80031bfc, F0x80031cac, F0x80031d5c, F0x80031e0c, F0x80031ecc) do not write a single scalar record field directly. Instead, after the shared getter call, they read the record's u16 fields at offsets 0x10 and 0x12 together, pass them to a decode helper F0x80031a3c that unpacks them into a temporary bitfield structure on the stack, overwrite one suboffset of that temporary structure with their own incoming byte parameter (loaded via lbu $sN,0x70($sp)), and pass the result to a re-encode helper F0x80031a98 that packs it back into the same two record u16 fields before the shared setter is called. The suboffset written differs per wrapper: F0x8003198c and F0x80031b3c write temp suboffset 0x0 (and additionally clear/set a companion suboffset 0xa to 0/1 respectively); F0x80031bfc writes suboffset 0x2; F0x80031cac writes suboffset 0x4; F0x80031d5c and F0x80031e0c write suboffset 0x6 (and clear/set companion suboffset 0xc to 0/1 respectively); F0x80031ecc writes suboffset 0x8 (and clears companion suboffset 0xe to 0). Because the encode helper always repacks both halfwords together, all seven of these wrappers rewrite record offsets 0x10 and 0x12 as a pair even though only one bitfield changes semantically.
claims.coverage: Read the complete assembly body of all seven wrappers end to end (F0x8003198c L36631-36678, F0x80031b3c L36751-36799, F0x80031bfc L36803-36850, F0x80031cac L36851-36898, F0x80031d5c L36899-36946, F0x80031e0c L36947-36996, F0x80031ecc L36999-37046), plus the two shared helper bodies F0x80031a3c (L36679-36705) and F0x80031a98 (L36706-36750), and confirmed each of the seven follows the identical getter -> lhu(0x5c,0x5e) -> jal F0x80031a3c -> [optional flag sh] -> jal F0x80031a98 -> [own-param sh] -> setter sequence with no other store into the shared record buffer.
claims.limitations: The decode/encode helpers' bit-level semantics (e.g. what real-world attribute each suboffset represents, such as a date or duration component) were not decoded; only their structural role (unpack/repack two record u16 fields) is established. Suboffset naming is purely positional (temp-struct byte offset), not attributed to a named field.

claims.statement: F0x8003202c is structurally distinct from all other assigned wrappers: its own incoming stack-passed parameter is loaded as a full word (lw $s0,0x70($sp)), not a byte, and is never copied directly into any record or temp-struct field. Instead the function branches on two range tests -- whether (param-1)&0xff is below 0x3f (i.e. param in [1,0x3f]) and whether (param-0x40)&0xff is below 0x40 (i.e. param in [0x40,0x7f]) -- writing temp-struct suboffset 0x10 to 0 on the first range and to 1 on the second; if the parameter lands in neither range, that suboffset is left unwritten by this function. Like F0x80031f7c, F0x8003202c contains no lhu read of record offsets 0x10/0x12 and no call to the decode helper F0x80031a3c anywhere in its body, so the temp struct passed to the re-encode helper F0x80031a98 is not populated by a decode step for the fields F0x8003202c itself does not write.
claims.limitations: This claim does not determine the concrete meaning of the two tested ranges [1,0x3f] and [0x40,0x7f], nor what value results when the incoming parameter is 0 or >=0x80. The register-shuffle in this function's prologue (a0/a1/a2 routed through v0/v1/t0) was read but not independently cross-checked against a decompiled-C rendering, since none was queried for this address.
claims.coverage: Two distinct quantifiers, both tested. (1) 'structurally distinct from all other assigned wrappers' was tested against the same fixed denominator of 14 enumerated callers, every one of which was read in full in this pass; F0x8003202c is the only one whose parameter is loaded with lw rather than lbu and the only one using range comparisons. (2) 'never copied directly' and 'no decode call anywhere in its body' are bounded by a complete instruction-by-instruction read of F0x8003202c's own extent through its return delay slot -- a direct copy or a jal to F0x80031a3c would necessarily lie inside that extent and would have been seen. NOT tested: whether the unwritten-suboffset case can actually occur at runtime, i.e. whether any caller passes a parameter outside [1,0x7f]; the callers' argument values were not enumerated, so the third branch is a static possibility, not an observed one.

claims.statement: Three of the fourteen assigned wrappers over the shared getter/setter record (UI-Q002-RECGETSET-800340EC-349CC-001) are simple single-byte field setters that copy the low byte of their own incoming stack-passed parameter straight into one record byte offset: F0x800317ac writes record offset 0x1 from a parameter loaded via lw $s1,0x58($sp); F0x8003186c writes record offset 0x6 from a parameter loaded via lw $s4,0x58($sp); and F0x800318fc writes record offset 0x7 from a parameter loaded via lw $s4,0x58($sp). In each of the three, this write is the only store into the buffer besides the getter/setter calls themselves.
claims.coverage: Read the complete assembly body of all three wrappers end to end (F0x800317ac L36501-36549, F0x8003186c L36552-36589, F0x800318fc L36592-36629) and enumerated every sb/sh instruction targeting the record buffer range (sp+0x34..sp+0x4c in these three's frames); exactly one such store exists in each body, at the offset cited.
claims.limitations: F0x800317ac additionally dispatches to F0x8003498c or F0x800349ac depending on whether the same parameter equals 0 or 4 (not analyzed here beyond noting its existence); that behavior is outside the record-field-write question this claim answers. Parameter naming ('own incoming stack-passed parameter') is inferred from the stack load offset and the decompiled C signature's argC parameter for F0x800317ac only (authority 3, cross-checked against the assembly); it was not independently re-derived for the other two from decompiled C, only from the assembly's identical load-and-store shape.

claims.statement: The ten slots of the second drawing context (constructor F0x8001ebf8, 0x54 bytes, table at +0x2c..+0x50, shape recorded in UI-QUADCTX-VTABLE-001) are decoded, and the class turns out to use a GLOBAL-SINGLETON calling convention that no other DDW3 dispatch table uses. None of its methods takes a receiver: every one begins by loading the active-context pointer from gp+0x1b8 and operates on that. The constructor's last act is to register itself there - it calls F0x8001e7e0, whose entire body is a single store of its argument into gp+0x1b8 - so constructing one of these contexts makes it the current one system-wide. Slots +0x3c F0x8001e98c(a,b), +0x40 F0x8001e9a0(a,b) and +0x44 F0x8001e9b4(a,b) set the three pairs at ctx+0x4/+0x8, +0xc/+0x10 and +0x14/+0x18; +0x48 F0x8001e9c8(v) sets ctx+0x1c (preset to 8 by the constructor) and +0x4c F0x8001e9d4(v) sets ctx+0x20. +0x2c F0x8001e7ec(code) resolves a 1-based code into a descriptor pointer cached at ctx+0x0: for code > 0 it takes bank (code-1)>>6 from the table D0x8004dfb8, calls the function pointer D0x80044f4c on that bank, and adds a per-entry byte offset derived from (code-1)&0x3f; for code <= 0 it takes a fixed default bank instead. +0x38 F0x8001e938(a,b) resolves a resource through the global function pointer D0x8004df8c, caches the handle at ctx+0x24, then calls that handle's own +0x138 slot and caches the result at ctx+0x28. +0x34 F0x8001e9e0(x,y) is the DRAW: it allocates a primitive through the shared UI service block D0x8004de10 slot +0x158, writes the primitive tag bytes, assembles a CLUT/TPage word from ctx+0x8, ctx+0x14*ctx+0x1c, ctx+0x20, ctx+0x10 and (ctx+0xc >> 4) & 0x3f using the same shift-6/mask-0x3f idiom as the main draw context's palette slot, sets the colour bytes to neutral 0x80/0x80/0x80, writes the caller's x and y at primitive +0x8/+0xa, writes a FIXED 0x20 by 0x20 source cell at +0x10/+0x12, calls the documented SetDrawTPage F0x8002915c, and links the finished primitive into the display list through D0x8004de10 slot +0x15c. +0x30 F0x8001e890 is the placement pass that converts the stored cell indices into pixels (base +0x4 plus ctx+0x14 times 16 on x, base +0x8 plus ctx+0x18 times 32 on y, plus a ctx+0x1c-scaled term) and issues three calls through a service block fetched with F0x8001ffa8. +0x50 F0x8001ebcc takes no argument and RETURNS rather than calls: it reads the type byte at descriptor+3 and returns the matching entry of the function-pointer table D0x8004dfcc, i.e. it is a per-descriptor-type handler lookup. So this context is an immediate-mode fixed-cell quad drawer - select code, set cell position, draw a 32x32 cell - rather than the main 0xA0 context's general draw-by-id sprite facility.
claims.notes: Lead re-verified the load-bearing structural claim against raw MIPS: F0x8001e7e0 at fns.s L15960-L15963 is exactly 'sw a0, 0x1b8(gp); jr ra', and F0x8001e98c at L16082-L16087 loads gp+0x1b8 before storing its two arguments, taking NO receiver. That confirms the singleton convention. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE DISPATCH GOAL: because these ten methods are reached through gp+0x1b8 rather than through a receiver argument, any call site using offsets +0x2c..+0x50 against a pointer loaded from gp+0x1b8 belongs to THIS class unambiguously - offset plus base-register provenance is enough here, unlike the +0x110..+0x168 range shared by widget classes A and B. NOT established: what D0x8004dfb8, D0x80044f4c, D0x8004df8c and D0x8004dfcc contain; what the descriptor type byte at +3 encodes; whether callers save and restore gp+0x1b8 around nested use, which determines whether more than one such context can be alive at once; and no caller of F0x8001ebf8 was traced, so calling this specifically a FONT context rather than some other fixed-cell quad user is an inference from the 16/32-pixel cell arithmetic, not a confirmed call site.
claims.frontier_rationale: Last unopened table of the eight in UI-DISPATCH-CENSUS-COMPLETE-001 apart from the texture-upload class; its singleton convention is what makes its call sites attributable without receiver typing.

claims.statement: Qualify the last clause: 'is the sole instance-table installer of +0x50' - the resident static function table F0x8003086c builds into D0x80081500 also carries a +0x50 entry, but it is a global table, not an instance method table (per UI-DISPATCH-INHERITANCE-001's corrected census of eight instance tables plus one static global table).
claims.notes: Three coordinate pairs plus two scalars and a bound sheet is consistent with a textured quad/polygon primitive rather than the sprite-sheet blitter of the 0xA0 draw context, but the exact primitive is NOT established: F0x8001e9e0 was read only to its service-block entry. F0x8001ebf8 is already used by card UI code (docs/research/ui/stcrdabm-decoded-2026-07-12.md L84, docs/research/card/card-duel-engine-2026-08-04.md L39) where its result is read as a per-card record with unk1=AP/unk2=HP; that reading and this one must be reconciled before either is promoted.
claims.frontier_rationale: Identifies the receiver type behind the slot-offset collision recorded in UI-SLOTOVERLOAD-CAVEAT-001 and resolves the third-largest block of unattributed dispatch slots.
limitations: Keep the existing limitation about F0x8001e9e0 (read only to its service-block entry) - this review confirms it takes +0x158 and links via +0x15c, but the primitive's full field set was not re-derived. The card-UI reconciliation note (stcrdabm L84 / card-duel L39) still stands unresolved.

claims.statement: The bank's eviction victim is chosen by F0x80013adc, which walks the slot table based at D0x80044b3c = 0x80044B38 + 4 at a stride of 0x20 bytes and picks the least-recently-touched slot, tie-broken by size. It considers a slot only when the slot is occupied and its state field is 3, so a slot still loading cannot be evicted. It seeds its running minimum with the current frame tick from the display service's +0x188 getter, so any slot that has ever been stamped compares older than the seed. On an exact tie of touch ticks it prefers the slot whose id yields the larger size from the size lookup D0x80048740's slot +0x4.
claims.coverage: The scan loop was read in full, including both arms of its tie branch; the ordering claim rests on the two comparisons quoted and nothing else. The claim describes the victim CHOICE only. It does not say when eviction runs, how many slots the table holds, or what the size lookup's units are - the loop bound and the table length were not read.
limitations: What bank state values other than 1 and 3 mean is not established.
The slot table's length was not read, so 'walks the slot table' is not quantified over a known count.
The units of the size lookup used as a tie-break are unknown.
Nothing was compared against the running game.

claims.statement: The resource/language bank object at 0x80044B38 has slot +0x404 = F0x80013a6c, +0x408 = F0x80013be4 and +0x40C = F0x80013c30, and the long-standing naming dispute over +0x404 and +0x40C resolves against stgdglab and in favour of stcrdabm. F0x80013a6c is a BUSY predicate, not a ready one: it looks up the slot for its id argument, and when a slot exists it stamps that slot's LRU field with the display service's frame tick and returns 0 if and only if the slot's state field equals 3, returning 1 on every other path. When no slot exists it calls F0x80013c30 itself and returns 1, so +0x404 is SELF-REQUESTING and a caller polling it does not have to call +0x40C first. F0x80013c30 is the raw allocate-or-touch request already established by resident-cache-touch-or-request-2026-08-10b, which sets a fresh slot's state to 1 and issues the load. F0x80013be4 frees a slot: it releases the slot's buffer through the heap pointer D0x8004b5ec and zeroes the record's state, id, LRU and size fields. This also closes the question core-q001-80017e84-blocking-retry-2026-08-10 left explicitly open about what the 0x408 slot does between attempts of its unbounded retry loop - it evicts, so that loop is 'retry, and if it still fails, free a slot to make room'.
claims.coverage: F0x80013a6c was read to all four of its returns, not sampled: the function is 12 lines of decompiled C with one nested branch, and the polarity claim rests on the single `== 3` test and the fact that every other exit returns 1. The dispute being resolved is the one recorded in docs/research/ui/symbols/shared-objects.md section 9, whose two named sides are stgdglab (+0x404 bank_ready, +0x40C bank_busy) and stcrdabm (+0x404 busy, +0x40C request); no third naming exists in the seventeen harvested overlays. What state 3 MEANS is taken from resident-cache-touch-or-request-2026-08-10b, which reads the allocate path setting a fresh slot to 1; no claim is made here about states other than 1 and 3.
limitations: What bank state values other than 1 and 3 mean is not established.
The slot table's length was not read, so 'walks the slot table' is not quantified over a known count.
The units of the size lookup used as a tie-break are unknown.
Nothing was compared against the running game.

claims.statement: The save-context selector is a 32-bit code whose high byte selects the engine library; its low byte is compared per consumer, not decoded through a shared table. In the shipped corpus only stdwtitl compares it, against 0x00 (title init) and 0x0d (END); every other low byte falls through to the movie arm, which passes low-byte-minus-one as the movie index. Full codes are produced by the stagslct launch table (0x1500 STSLCT, 0x1400, 0x1600 New Game, 0x0f00/0x0a00 families and more).
claims.coverage: A 547-hit blind andi-0xff census over pro+exe found no other compare of the selector's low byte; the setter/commit/init are vector-reached, so per-overlay dispatchers cannot be enumerated by text caller search. Not established: the valid movie-index set on the else arm.
limitations: Each row is the worker's static read; the lead re-checked the quoted lines only, not the whole sweeps.
Save-selector movie-index set, pad type vocabulary beyond 4/7, and struct-field key writers remain bounded gaps, stated in the claim text.
derivation: taskset-capped grep for the selector's 0x26c4/0x26c8 consumers and a 547-hit andi-0xff census over pro+exe (worker-l)
checker reads of exe-decomp/c/F0x80018bcc.c, F0x800186e0.c, F0x80018928.c and fns.s axis block (worker-e)
read of data.rs D0x8004df6c/D0x8004dfa0 plus exe-decomp/stitshop_c/F0x8008321c.c register call (worker-n)

claims.statement: The shared screen selector is a staged transition register, not three independent verbs. F0x80016b88 writes a pending selector at save-context +0x26c8 and a companion argument at +0x26d0. On a construction pass, F0x80016b28 leaves state unchanged when pending is zero; otherwise it copies current +0x26c4 to previous +0x26cc, promotes pending to current, and clears pending. The library loader then reads current and uses current >> 8 as the loaded-engine/library number and as the index into its overlay table. Therefore the selector's high byte selects the engine/library; the low byte remains available to that loaded overlay's own dispatcher.
claims.coverage: Both register routines were read over their complete assembly extents, including delay slots. The loader was followed from the current-selector function pointer through the shift, cache comparison, table index, and load calls. This establishes the two-byte shape and commit order, not the accepted low-byte vocabulary of every overlay.
limitations: The low-byte dispatcher was independently reviewed only for stdwtitl in the canonical title decode; this packet does not claim an exhaustive selector vocabulary.
The companion argument at +0x26d0 is written here but its consumers and meaning were not traced.
Selectors with a set sign bit were not observed; the loader uses arithmetic rather than logical right shift.
derivation: Focused sed/nl reads of cited fns.s, f15.s, shocktst.s, and data.rs ranges

claims.statement: The save context slot +0x270C is not three verbs. It is F0x80016b88, whose entire body is two stores: argument 0 to context +0x26c8 and argument 1 to context +0x26d0. The surrounding slots make it a small transition register over four consecutive fields, and GYM-C003 already names two of them: +0x26c4 current selector, +0x26c8 pending selector. This claim adds the rest. Slot +0x2700 is F0x80016b28, the COMMIT: when the pending selector is non-zero it copies the current selector aside, makes the pending selector current, clears pending, and stores the old current at +0x26cc, which is therefore the PREVIOUS selector; when pending is zero it does nothing. Slot +0x2710 (F0x80016b9c) reports whether a transition is pending, slot +0x2714 (F0x80016b58) returns the previous selector at +0x26cc, and slot +0x2708 (F0x80016b78) returns the second word at +0x26d0. This closes what core-q001-16b58-16b78-global-getters-2026-08-10 left explicitly unestablished about the two globals those getters read: D0x8004b400 is the previous selector and D0x8004b404 is the setter's second word. It also disposes of the naming fight recorded in docs/research/ui/symbols/shared-objects.md section 11, where six overlays gave +0x270C the incompatible names launchOverlay, launch_stage, restore_field, setPartnerName and roster_flag_set: none is a verb the routine performs. It queues a pair, and the meaning of the pair belongs to whatever consumes the selector.
claims.coverage: F0x80016b88 and F0x80016b28 were each read in full from the original assembly, four and eleven instructions respectively including delay slots; the setter claim rests on there being exactly two store instructions between its entry and its jr, which is visible in the quoted pair. The five slot-to-function bindings were resolved by absolute arithmetic on the harvested base 0x80048D34 and then looked up in the shipped data segment via tools/decode_statics.py --list. The list of six disputed names is the complete set of proposed_name values for receiver 0x80048D34 offset 0x270c across all seventeen files of docs/research/ui/symbols/*.json. NOT established: what a selector value denotes. GYM-C003 records that New Game writes the literal 0x1600 into both current and pending, but nothing here reads a consumer that acts on a selector, so calling these stage ids or overlay ids would be an inference.
limitations: What a selector VALUE denotes is not established; no consumer of the selector was read.
The second word at +0x26d0 has a getter and a setter but no read consumer was traced, so its purpose is unknown.
Nothing was compared against the running game.

claims.statement: There is no scene or overlay-handoff service at 0x800519EC. The two slots that docs/research/ui/symbols/shared-objects.md groups under a 'Scene / overlay' object are audio calls. 0x800519EC+0x425C is the absolute cell 0x80055c48, which the shipped data segment initialises to F0x8002006c - the packed-sound entry point already established as verified by resident-play-sound-entry-and-exclusive-track - and 0x800519EC+0x4274 is the cell 0x80055c60, initialised to F0x8002043c, whose entire body returns whether the halfword at 0x80055c40 is non-zero. The values the six overlays pass to +0x425C are packed sound ids of exactly the shape F0x8002006c decodes: 0x609C0004 in cardgame, 0x60840002 in cnty_sel and stgtrain, 0x60800000 in stgmcard and stplnmet, 0x40005 in fieldstg. The recurring idiom across those screens, 'if the +0x4274 poll returns zero then call +0x425C', is therefore a sound played when the audio state at 0x80055c40 is clear, and not an overlay request gated on a scene being idle. Every name harvested for these two slots - request_overlay, overlay_request, sceneHandoff, overlay_loaded, overlay_idle, sceneBusy - is wrong, and so is the 'idle versus busy polarity' dispute recorded against them.
claims.coverage: Both cells were resolved by absolute arithmetic on the harvested base and offset (0x800519EC + 0x425C = 0x80055c48 and + 0x4274 = 0x80055c60) and then looked up in the shipped data segment through tools/decode_statics.py --list, which reads recovered/ddw3/function-inventory.json rather than reparsing data.rs. The scope word 'every name harvested for these two slots' was tested by enumerating all method_slots records with receiver 0x800519EC across all seventeen files of docs/research/ui/symbols/*.json: twelve records over six overlays, and the six distinct proposed names listed in the statement are the complete set. F0x8002043c was read to its return; it is four instructions with no branch. What the halfword at 0x80055c40 MEANS is not established here - no named writer of it exists anywhere in the 590,156-line original assembly corpus, so it is written base-relative and the poll's exact sense is open.
limitations: What the halfword at 0x80055c40 means is not established; it has no named writer in the assembly corpus.
The claim identifies the values passed as packed sound ids by their bit shape and by the verified claim's decoding of that shape; no individual sound was identified or heard.
Nothing was compared against the running game.
derivation: enumerate method_slots with receiver 0x800519EC across docs/research/ui/symbols/*.json

claims.statement: A screen launch code is two fields, not an opaque id. The resident screen manager only stores it: the launcher writes the code and its second argument into the game context, a commit step promotes the pending code to current and keeps the previous one, and three service slots read back current, previous and the second argument. The loaded overlay then dispatches on the code's own LOW BYTE. In the title overlay, low byte 0x00 runs the title screen, low byte 0x0d runs the END card, and any other low byte creates the movie player with index = low byte - 1. That resolves 0x0e01 as the first opening movie MOVIEOP2 and 0x0e02 as the second, MOVIEOPN, which are the two codes the title screen's idle timeout and the country-select screen's confirm hand off to.
claims.coverage: The dispatcher has exactly three arms and all three were read: the two equality tests on the low byte and the fall-through, which is the arm that computes the movie index. The index arithmetic was taken from the branch delay slot of the creation call rather than from the line above it, which is where an off-by-one would have come from. The mapping is asserted only for this overlay's low bytes; no claim is made that other overlays split their codes the same way.
claims.limitations: The high byte is treated here only as 'what selects the overlay', on the strength of the stage-select table giving one overlay per high byte. The code that turns a high byte into an overlay load was not read.
derivation: grep the shipped data for the 0x8004b430..0x8004b448 service slots
read stdwtitl.s file 0x218..0x374, the overlay's entry dispatcher

claims.statement: Nine draw sites in the DW3 UI overlays render a full-screen tiled backdrop at a position that advances on alternate frames rather than at a fixed position: ststatus 0x00016bd0 (clip 0x1d), stitshop 0x00008c44 (0x14), stfgtrep 0x0000210c (0x1e), stgdglab 0x0000c1b8 (0x37), stgmcard 0x00004da8 (0x1e), stcrdabm 0x00001910 (0x08), stcrddek 0x0000628c (0x08), stcrdshp 0x000054cc (0x08), and stgtrain 0x00002498 (clip id read from the object field +0x58 instead of an immediate). At each of these nine sites the backdrop counter is incremented by 1 only on frames where a companion toggle field is already set (the toggle being cleared on the advancing frame and set on the non-advancing one), is reset to 0 rather than ever holding 0x60, and is supplied as both the x argument and - through a 'move_ $a3, $a2' placed in the jalr branch delay slot, which therefore executes - the y argument of the clip draw. That is half a pixel per vsync toward the bottom-right with a 96-pixel period.
claims.notes: Wired 2026-08-14. Five of the nine were wrong in the walker and each was wrong differently: stgdglab and stgtrain were drawn frozen, stcrdabm/stcrddek/stcrdshp drew a flat colour and never drew the wall at all, and stgmcard scrolled at 60px/s instead of 25. All now route through drawPackBackdrop() in web/screenpack.js, whose pattern cache had to be re-keyed per clip first because stgtrain selects one of eight sttrng3 mosaics (0x2d..0x34). Full write-up in docs/research/ui/scrolling-backdrop-walls-2026-08-14.md. The card duel is a separate 64x64 / 0x40-wrap mechanism and is not covered here. STILL OPEN: which training ground selects which of the eight sttrng3 walls.
claims.coverage: Population enumerated mechanically, not sampled: every *.s file under ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003/pro was scanned for the y-argument signature 'move_ $a3, $a2' having, within the preceding 40 lines, both a memory-loaded $a2 (a live counter rather than an immediate) and an $a1 clip argument; each hit was then read by hand over the 30 preceding lines to confirm or reject the alternate-frame toggle. Sixteen sites matched the signature; the nine listed are those whose guard constant is 0x60. THE QUANTIFIER IS NOT PROVEN EXHAUSTIVE and the statement is scoped to the nine sites actually read: the matcher reaches only sites where the y argument is produced by that exact instruction, so a site computing y another way, or through a register-constructed call, would be missed. The seven matched sites with a different or absent wrap constant (fieldstg clip 0x3, stcrdshp 0x1 and 0x5, stdgname 0x24, ststatus 0x4 and 0x1, stplnmet 0x2 with wrap 0x2) were EXCLUDED because their guard differs, not because they were examined and shown not to be scrolling backdrops, which remains unchecked. The wstag* stage overlays were filtered out of the scan output as field stages and were not examined at all. Independent check that was run and did not falsify the cadence: a headless loop-time measurement (tools/verify_scrolling_walls.mjs) over the eight walker screens reachable from the UI lab, asserting the wall returns to its exact starting phase every 96/25 = 3.84s; measured 3.75-3.84s on all eight.

claims.contradiction_rationale: UI-SERVICE-DESCRIPTOR-16C-001 and UI-SERVICE-DESCRIPTOR-16C-002 inferred a shared opaque descriptor structure from the fact that three overlays carry the identical word pair {0x00000000, 0x00f00140}. shocktst builds the same argument on the stack from four s16 fields 0, 0, 0x140, 0xF0, showing the argument is a plain 320x240 rectangle and the recurring constant is just a full-screen rect, not a structure shared between overlays. Both earlier claims are retracted in favour of UI-SERVICE-RECT-16C-003.
claims.statement: RETRACTION of UI-SERVICE-DESCRIPTOR-16C-001 and UI-SERVICE-DESCRIPTOR-16C-002. The recurring 8-byte block passed to shared UI service slot +0x16c is not a shared descriptor structure; it is a rectangle {x, y, w, h} as four s16 fields, and every overlay in the set happens to request the same full-screen 320x240 rectangle. See UI-SERVICE-RECT-16C-003 for the corrected reading.

Refines UI-SERVICE-DESCRIPTOR-16C-001. A third overlay, cnty_sel, carries the same leading word pair {0x00000000, 0x00f00140} at file 0x1710 and passes it to shared UI service slot +0x16c, so the header is shared across stagslct, soundtst and cnty_sel. However the descriptor is NOT a fixed 8-byte block as that claim described it: stagslct and soundtst both call service+0x16c(ptr, 1, 0x1000) while cnty_sel calls service+0x16c(ptr, 3, 0x100), and cnty_sel's block continues with further structured data through file 0x173c. The second argument is therefore a count and the descriptor is variable length behind a shared eight-byte header. The meaning of the header words, of the third argument, and of slot +0x16c itself remain unestablished.
limitations: Consider naming the exact extent read: 'continues with further structured data through file 0x173c' - the words were read to 0x173c; what lies between 0x1740 and the cursor table at 0x1774 was not attributed by this review.

claims.statement: Shared UI service slot D0x8004de10 +0x16c takes (rect array, rect count, scale), and its first argument is an ordinary RECTANGLE of four s16 fields {x, y, width, height} -- not an opaque shared descriptor. shocktst settles this because it builds its rectangle on the STACK rather than in static data: F0x80082da0 sets four consecutive s16 stack slots to 0, 0, 0x140 and 0xF0 and passes their address as +0x16c(&rect, 1, 0x1000), so the rectangle is (0, 0, 320, 240), the same 320x240 the immediately preceding +0x174 call establishes. The static word pair {0x00000000, 0x00f00140} that stagslct, soundtst and cnty_sel each carry is byte-identical to those four s16 values, because 0x00f00140 is simply (240 << 16) | 320. This SUPERSEDES UI-SERVICE-DESCRIPTOR-16C-001 and UI-SERVICE-DESCRIPTOR-16C-002, which read the recurring constant as evidence of a shared STRUCTURE; the three overlays merely all request a full-screen rectangle. It also explains cnty_sel's rect count of 3, which matches its multiple window panes: its second and third rectangles read {0, 0, 1024, 512} and {0, -15, 320, 260}. The meaning of the third argument, 0x1000 in three overlays and 0x100 in cnty_sel, is NOT established, though 0x1000 is the 4.12 fixed-point unity used for scale elsewhere.

shocktst reads and writes files on the DEVELOPER'S OWN PC through the devkit host-filesystem link, and the absolute paths are still in the retail overlay. F0x80084714 allocates two 0x4000-byte buffers, calls fopen on the pointer at 0x80084af0 which is the string at file 0x74, sim:C:\DEVELOP\DLSKDATA.TXT, freads up to 0x4000 bytes into the first buffer and closes it; when the open returns -1 it immediately advances to the teardown state, which is what happens on any retail console. F0x800843f0 then COMPILES that text: it takes an atoi record count from the first line via F0x8002530c, splits records on the literals at file 0x90, 0x94 and 0x98 ('\t', '\t\n', '\n') using the delimiter scan F0x800251dc while skipping runs of tabs, terminates on '/', and lays the values into a binary image with a four-word header {count, 0x10, 0x10 + count*4, that + count*2} followed by the arrays. It then opens the SECOND devkit path at file 0x9c, sim:C:\DEVELOP\DLSKDATA.BIN, in write mode 0x200 and fwrites the compiled image back to the developer's machine. shocktst is therefore an ASSET COMPILER for the rumble pattern data that shipped on the retail disc, and it is the only overlay in the set that touches a filesystem at all. The 'sim:' prefix is the SN Systems / PSY-Q devkit host device. The FIELD SEMANTICS of DLSKDATA.TXT are NOT established -- which column is amplitude, which is duration, and what the two per-motor bytes mean physically are unknown, and the source file cannot be recovered because it never existed on the disc.

shocktst is the developers' DUALSHOCK VIBRATION TEST, the fourth tool of the set with stagslct, soundtst and cnty_sel. Its title string at file 0xb8 is the Shift-JIS しんどうテスト, 'vibration test'; its two on-screen legends at file 0xc8 and 0xdc read ×：じっこうていし ('X: stop execution') and ＳＴＡＲＴ：もどる ('START: back'); and its three mode labels at file 0x30, 0x3c and 0x48 read ていそく (low speed), こうそく (high speed) and パターンじっこう (pattern execute). It drives the controller through pad service slot D0x8004b7d0 +0x3EC, called as (padIndex, motorIndex, a, b) across motor indices 0 and 1; this slot was previously unnamed and is identified here as the VIBRATION SETTER from its exclusive use in a screen titled 'vibration test', its two-motor loop, and its being called with zeros on every exit path including the Cross handler, which matches the on-screen X legend (pad bit 14). The resident implementation of +0x3EC was not read, so the naming rests on call-site behaviour rather than on the function body.

shocktst is byte-accounted across its 0x1e44 bytes in eight regions: file 0x0000-0x0030 a 12-entry jump table into F0x80082ec4; 0x0030-0x0060 the three mode label strings; 0x0060-0x0074 a 5-entry jump table into F0x80083ea4; 0x0074-0x00b8 the DLSKDATA.TXT path, the tab and newline delimiter literals and the DLSKDATA.BIN path; 0x00b8-0x00f0 the title and the two button legends; 0x00f0-0x1d18 code in 17 functions; 0x1d18-0x1e38 small constant tables; and 0x1e38-0x1e44 three pointers to こうそく, ていそく and the .TXT path. Both front tables index into code, so following them as string pointers yields empty strings. The pattern player is created by F0x8008436c(count) as a task with handler F0x80083ea4 and two count*2-byte step buffers, one per motor, filled by F0x800842e0 de-interleaving the compiled image. F0x800833c0 is the per-frame driver: for each of the two motors it walks 2-byte step records, calls +0x3EC with both bytes when the second is non-zero, latches a countdown and advances when it expires, and pushes the live value of each motor onto a text widget through class-A slot +0x118. When both motors finish, or Cross (pad bit 14) is pressed, both motors are zeroed and the pattern ends. WHICH of the two step bytes is amplitude and which is duration is not established.

A second, distinct method table is installed over the SAME offsets as the F0x800143dc base object, so a struct_function_slot offset alone does NOT identify a method corpus-wide. The constructor ending at exe/fns 0x8001ecac (fns.s L16278-L16297, immediately preceding the draw-context block) installs +0x34 F0x8001e9e0, +0x38 F0x8001e938, +0x3c F0x8001e98c, +0x40 F0x8001e9a0, +0x44 F0x8001e9b4, +0x48 F0x8001e9c8, +0x4c F0x8001e9d4 and +0x50 F0x8001ebcc, then sets +0x1c = 8. Its +0x38/+0x3c/+0x40/+0x44 entries are therefore NOT the base-object state advancers F0x800142ac/F0x800142c8/F0x800142e0/F0x800142f4 recorded in UI-TASKOBJ-STATEMACHINE-001, and its +0x48 is a fixed function rather than a caller-supplied handler. This constructor is also the sole identified installer of slot +0x50 (284 unresolved sites across 282 of 319 modules). Consequently the site counts attributed to +0x38 and +0x40 in UI-TASKOBJ-STATEMACHINE-001 are UPPER BOUNDS on the base-object interpretation: each call site must be attributed to a receiver type before its slot meaning is assigned.
claims.notes: Does not contradict UI-TASKOBJ-STATEMACHINE-001 (the base table is correctly read); it bounds that claim's site attribution. Next step: determine which object type this second constructor builds and how many of the +0x38/+0x40 sites belong to each.
claims.frontier_rationale: Prevents mass-misattribution of the two highest-traffic dispatch slots; establishes that receiver-type attribution, not slot offset, is the unit of resolution for the remaining dispatch work.

claims.statement: A launch code written to 0x8004B3FC with 0 in 0x8004B404 is a screen-change request the resident consumer clears on acceptance. Codes taken from the developers' own stage-list rows launch from a live field (0x2d7 -> scene 0x1e9 Kusanagi street; 0x26b -> 0x653; 0x219 -> 0x344 A.o.A HQ); the Stage Select menu code 0x1500 does not, and leaves the field torn down with the request unconsumed until a state is reloaded.
claims.coverage: Four launch codes tested live from a healthy field scene, one run each: all three screen-row codes loaded and the one menu-row code hung. Not tested from battle, menu or boot contexts; no code repeated.
claims.frontier_rationale: First runtime confirmation of the stage-request mechanism; the menu-code failure and the boot launch path remain open.

claims.statement: F0x80084b70 (file 0x1ec0) reads ten bytes directly from PS1 BOOT ROM address 0x1fc0012c and displays them at screen position (220, 20). Each byte is transliterated to fullwidth Shift-JIS: bytes 0x30-0x39 and 0x41-0x5a are mapped by subtracting 0x7de1, producing the fullwidth digits 0x824f-0x8258 and fullwidth capitals from 0x8260; byte 0x2d becomes the fullwidth dash 0x815c; every other byte becomes the ideographic space 0x8140. Each resulting halfword is byte-swapped into big-endian Shift-JIS order and stored into the overlay's own 20-byte buffer at 0x80087194, with a NUL halfword at 0x800871a8. The routine builds the string once, guarded by object field +0x60, and thereafter only repositions the widget. Because the accepted character set is exactly digits, capitals and '-' over exactly ten characters, the displayed value is a boot ROM identification string; the specific field at 0x1fc0012c is not separately confirmed against a BIOS dump here.

STAGSLCT's screen layout is fully traceable from its own build routine F0x80084d9c because every widget is created with the shared class-A text-widget constructor F0x8001ae38(0x1000, 1, x, y), whose third and fourth arguments are the screen position. Traced values: title at (16,32); two further header widgets at (144,32) and (192,32); a two-column list whose left column is x=24 and right column x=152, first row y=45, row pitch 12 pixels, at most 14 rows visible; a row cursor at x=14 repositioned through class-A slot +0x134 to y = selection*12 + 45; and a footer row at y=220 with widgets at x=16, 48, 80, 208 and 256, the first of which is filled with an integer through class-A slot +0x118 from the word at 0x80042b1c. Cursor and scroll position persist across entries in the globals 0x80048d60 and 0x80048d5c.

The stagslct overlay is fully byte-accounted across its 0x44fc bytes, with no unexplained region: file 0x0000-0x1cf4 row label strings; 0x1cf4-0x1d1c the screen's own title, self-label and cursor strings; 0x1d1c-0x3220 code in nine functions; 0x3220-0x323c the seven-entry language name pointer table; 0x323c-0x44cc the 297 menu records; 0x44cc-0x44dc the type == -1 terminator record; 0x44dc-0x44e4 a scratch word pair passed as argument 1 of shared UI service slot +0x16c at file 0x2190; and 0x44e4-0x44fc the BIOS date string buffer. The nine functions are F0x800849cc (outer screen task handler), F0x80084a30 (registers it at priority 4), F0x80084a5c (move selection skipping unselectable records), F0x80084b2c (page scroll), F0x80084b70 (BIOS date readout), F0x80084c94 (a 0..0x1000 ramp fed to class-A slot +0x154), F0x80084d9c (the 1089-instruction screen over base states 0 build, 1 chrome-then-run, 2 idle, 3 launch), and F0x80085ea4 (registers the menu task). Only eight of these have m2c output at all: the overlay is m2c-blind because the auto-splitter carved 256 spurious functions out of the record table, so this decode is read from the original assembly. The overlay begins with 0x1cf4 bytes of pure string data ahead of any code, which is why the disassembler emitted 'Start of code' and 'End of code' back to back and rendered the whole file as .word directives.

STAGSLCT is a DEVELOPER stage and overlay launcher, not a player-facing travel menu. Its title widget is filled from a literal Shift-JIS string at RAM 0x800849a4 reading the katakana for 'Stage Select', and its row cursor is the single fullwidth '>' character at RAM 0x800849c8. The screen's own row in its record table is labelled with the overlay filename in fullwidth letters at RAM 0x800849b8. The overlay loads no screen art at all: the only five 'lui a0' constants in the whole file are 0x8008 and 0x8006 code and data pointers, not pack handles, and no lang_file/dw2003/eng TOML exists for this overlay, so its labels remain untranslated Japanese in the PAL build SLES03936. Together with the previously recorded absence of any trigger site, this identifies it as a debug tool rather than a menu whose chrome must be reproduced.

The 28 bytes at 0x80085ed0 (file 0x3220), previously unaccounted, are a seven-entry char* table naming the game's seven language builds: JPN, USA, ENG, FRA, ITA, GER and SPN, written as fullwidth Shift-JIS in the overlay's first 0x38 bytes. stagslct indexes it with a counter that wraps 0..6 and installs the selected name on the widget at (144, 32) through class-A slot +0x110 (file 0x297c). The counter is the global D0x8005cca8, advanced when bit 3 of D0x8004bbc4(0) is set, after which the overlay calls D0x80048a7c(). Resident code identifies D0x8005cca8 as the LANGUAGE INDEX rather than a menu-local counter: exe-decomp/c/F0x800110e0.c adds it to a string-bank base and passes the result to the resource-string resolver feeding class-A slot +0x114, and stdwtitl's F0x80086834 branches its title flow on whether 0x8005cca8 is zero and calls D0x80048a7c() after changing language, identifying D0x80048a7c as the apply/reload routine. The reading of bit 3 as the Start button follows the standard PS1 pad mask and is NOT independently proven here.

The stagslct record table has a FIXED 0x10-byte stride, {char *label_left, char *label_right, s32 type, s32 value}, terminated by the record whose type is -1 (file 0x44cc), and holds exactly 297 records. The `type` field is a LAUNCH CODE passed as the first argument to the resident screen launcher D0x8004b440, and `value` is that call's second argument; `type` is neither a screen id nor a value written to the master story ordinal. The launch state (state0 == 3, file 0x312c-0x31c4) loads value into a1, tests bit 15, and on the plain path calls D0x8004b440(type, value). Only when bit 15 is set does it pass 0 instead and force [0x8004b370] = (u8)value; NO shipped record sets bit 15, so that path is dead in the retail table. The Circle handler's comparison of type against 0x300 (file 0x28fc), which would write value to the master story ordinal without leaving the screen, is likewise dead: no shipped record has type 0x300. Confirmation that D0x8004b440 is the screen launcher and that these codes are its arguments comes from a second overlay: soundtst's F0x80084370 calls 0x8004B440(0x1500, 0), and 0x1500 is exactly the launch code of stagslct's own STSLCT/Stage Select record. Further corroboration that `value` is a real parameter: the eight gym records all share code 0xa00 and differ only in value 0-7, and each record's Japanese label literally begins with that number, so value is the gym id; the thirty-one shop records share code 0xf00 with value 0-29 plus 30 for the special shop. This CONTRADICTS docs/research/ui/stagslct-decoded-2026-07-11.md, which read `type` as a screen id written to 0x8004b370 via a tail-call to a 'resident transition trampoline 0x800855d4'; 0x800855d4 is not a resident routine but the next block inside F0x80084d9c itself.

stagslct's selection state occupies four words of the menu task object, and the two cursor fields are the REVERSE of the labels in docs/research/ui/stagslct-decoded-2026-07-11.md. +0x50 is the row within the visible window, clamped to 0..rowsVisible-1 (file 0x1e00); +0x54 is the scroll offset, clamped to 0..rowCount-rowsVisible (file 0x1e28); +0x58 is rowsVisible, set to min(rowCount, 14) at file 0x21f4; +0x5c is the total record count, obtained by walking records until type == -1 (file 0x21dc). The selected record index is +0x54 + +0x50. F0x80084a5c moves the selection and then re-moves in the same direction while it lands on a record whose type is 0, so horizontal rules and section headings can never be selected, restoring the entry position if it reaches either end while still on one; F0x80084b2c scrolls by whole pages without that skip. Scroll and row persist between visits in D0x80048d5c and D0x80048d60, written on launch (file 0x31b8, 0x31c4) and restored during the build state (file 0x2220). Screen geometry is entirely code-traced: every widget is a class-A text widget built by F0x8001ae38(0x1000, 1, x, y), the fourteen row pairs sit at x = 24 and x = 152 with y = 45 + 12*i, and the cursor at x = 14.

The record table at RAM 0x80085eec is a 16-byte-stride array of {char *label_left, char *label_right, s32 type, s32 value} terminated by a record whose type is -1, and it holds 297 rows. The left label is the target overlay's filename in fullwidth letters and the right label is its Japanese name; rows whose type is 0 are horizontal-rule separators or section headings rather than launchable entries. Walking it yields 270 entries, 20 separators and 7 headings, which reconciles exactly with the previously extracted 239 field-screen destinations plus 31 non-screen rows. This CONTRADICTS the earlier reading that the 31 non-screen rows were categories grouping the destinations: they are named launcher entries for other overlays, including the card game, status screen, save and load, the title screen, name entry, the Digimon lab, all eight gyms with the developers' own location names, and the country select.

A trigger site for stagslct DOES exist in the retail build, contradicting the supporting note in UI-STAGSLCT-IDENTITY-001 that 'no trigger site anywhere loads it'. soundtst's per-frame handler F0x80084370 calls the resident screen launcher 0x8004B440(0x1500, 0) when bit 3 of D0x8004BBC4(0) is set, and 0x1500 is the launch code stagslct's own table assigns to the STSLCT/Stage Select row. The two debug tools therefore reach each other through the ordinary screen launcher. This does not establish that a PLAYER can reach either screen: what remains unfound is an entry point into this pair from normal gameplay, and the identity finding (untranslated Japanese title, filename row label, no language file, no screen art) is unaffected.

DDW3's dispatch layer has a SECOND HALF that the installer-idiom scan structurally could not see. tools/scan_vtable_installers.py only finds tables an instruction stream builds at runtime (runs of la_/sw pairs), which is why UI-DISPATCH-CENSUS-COMPLETE-001 found only eight. The other kind is initialised DATA: consecutive words in the EXE's data segment that already hold function addresses at load time, which call sites reach by absolute address (la_ a base global, then lw at a fixed offset, then jalr). The new scanner tools/scan_static_fnptr_tables.py enumerates them from the transcribed data segment ~/ddw3/rust/dw2003_exe_data/src/data.rs by finding runs of at least three consecutive 4-byte statics whose initialiser is a function address, broken by any non-pointer word. It finds THIRTEEN such static tables holding about 130 function pointers: 0x8004bbb0 (17 slots, the pad/input service resolved in UI-PADSERVICE-STATIC-TABLE-001), 0x80055eb4 (15), 0x80048a78 (13), 0x80044f3c (12), 0x8004b464 (11), 0x80055c44 (11), 0x8004b5e8 (10, which contains the already-known allocator family D0x8004b5ec/b5f4/b5fc/b600), 0x8004dca0 (10), 0x8004b43c (9), 0x8004b7b0 (8), 0x80048ac4 (5), 0x80055df8 (5) and 0x80048740 (4). Measured against the recovered inventory, the eight instance tables plus these thirteen static tables account for 58.7 percent of the 11,388 unresolved struct-slot call sites by offset, but only 7.6 percent are owned by exactly one table - the rest sit in offset ranges two or more tables share, so receiver typing, not offset lookup, is what remains.
claims.notes: The table CONTENTS are authority 3 (transcribed data segment), so each table should be corroborated on the target side from exe/fns.s before its slots are treated as settled - that was done for the pad table only. COMPLETENESS LIMIT, stated plainly: the scan breaks a run on any non-pointer word, so a table interleaving data words with function pointers is split or missed, and a table living in an overlay's data rather than the EXE's is not covered at all since only the EXE data segment is transcribed. Thirteen is a lower bound. The measurement script is scratch, not committed; the two counts above (58.7 percent covered, 7.6 percent uniquely owned) come from joining recovered/ddw3/function-inventory.json indirect_calls against both scanners' output.
claims.frontier_rationale: Identifies the missing half of the dispatch layer and quantifies exactly what is left, which redirects the goal from enumerating tables to typing receivers.

claims.statement: The pause menu STATUS detail sheet opens on a prompt of exactly TWO rows, esstatus 0x2D "See Digivolve" and 0x2E "See Equipment", filled by F0x8008bd70 whose loop runs twice. F0x8008d684 state 5 assigns the selection 0 on pad bit 4 and 1 on pad bit 6 rather than incrementing it, and places the cursor at (0x98, selection * 0xE + 0x13). Confirming builds one of two sub-screens: root 0x8008B3C8 for row 0 and root 0x80088214, the full equipment screen, for row 1.
claims.coverage: The row count is the loop bound itself (`if (var_s0 < 2)`), not a sample. Every esstatus text-set call in the four detail-sheet label fillers was enumerated; none sets 0x2F "Demo Setup", which is why the earlier same-day statement that the prompt has three rows is withdrawn here. Both sub-screen factories were opened and resolved through their single F0x80014504 call.
limitations: No runtime observation; read from original assembly and from m2c decompilation cross-read against the .s file.

How the Digivolve Demo setup screen (root F0x800862A0, esstatus 0x2F "Demo Setup") is entered was NOT established. It is not one of the two prompt rows. Its factory sits one index past the last menu row in the 0x8009A988 table, but no caller that re-enters the overlay at that index was located.

The digivolve screen internals (Battle Digivolve On/Off, Skill LV, Technique Explanation) were not decoded beyond noting that only three esstatus ids appear in its state machine, so its row labels come from other text banks.
derivation: grep -n '0xB0), ' over exe-decomp/ststatus_c/F0x8008bd70.c F0x8008be34.c F0x8008c02c.c F0x8008c1c0.c

claims.statement: On the name-entry keyboard, the keys of the right-hand action column are dispatched by F0x80083994 from their ORIGIN cell rather than from the cell the cursor rests on. The branch is entered only when the cursor column is >= 10 (slti 0xa, stdgname.s L0x00000dcc) and the row is >= 3 (slti 0x3, L0x00000de0). It then walks LEFT along the row through the per-cell map at [0x80088e3c] + page*210 until it reaches a cell whose low byte is 1 (loop L0x00000e94-L0x00000eac), which is how a key wider than one column resolves to its leftmost column. It forms (origin_col + row*15) - 0x46 (L0x00000ed0), gates it with sltiu 0x22 (L0x00000ed4) and jumps through the 34-word table at the overlay's file offset 0 (L0x00000ee4-L0x00000ef4). Exactly four of those 34 words leave the default target 0x80083bac: table indices 0, 15, 31 and 33, which are origin cells 70, 85, 101 and 103, that is grid (row 4, col 10), (row 5, col 10), (row 6, col 11) and (row 6, col 13). Each of the five distinct targets sets a case number 0..4 (L0x00000efc, f04, f0c, f28, f44) that selects one draw record. Because the index is formed from the origin column, a cell on grid row 3 of columns 10..14 can only ever produce a negative index and therefore never dispatches an action.
claims.notes: Closes sub-gap (b) of stdgname_ui.json's first open_gaps entry, which said the 34 cases were 'only partially sampled'. Companion claim UI-STDGNAME-ACTIONKEY-SPRITES-2026-08-14 carries the draw records. claims.coverage: All 34 words of the gated table were read individually from stdgname.s file offsets 0x00..0x84; tools/extract_stdgname_ui.py reads every one of them on each run and raises SystemExit if any word is not one of the five known targets, so a 35th distinct handler could not pass unnoticed. Thirty of the 34 hold 0x80083bac and the four cited hold 0x80083bbc / 0x80083bd8 / 0x80083bb4 / 0x80083bf4. The word at file 0x88 (0x80084370) lies outside the sltiu 0x22 gate and belongs to a different table, which is the check that the 34 boundary is real rather than assumed. The 'never dispatches on row 3' clause is arithmetic over the whole row: the largest index row 3 can produce is 3*15+14-70 = -11.

claims.statement: Every case of the name-entry action-key dispatch converges on one draw (stdgname.s L0x00000f5c-L0x00000fa0) that reads record s0 of the five 12-byte records at 0x80087b70 (overlay file 0x4ec0) as the triple (clip, x, y) and draws it from the NAMEDTCS pack, handle 0x07700000 resolved through [0x80044f5c]. The five records are (0x2c, 203, 195), (0x2d, 222, 195), (0x3c, 203, 153), (0x44, 203, 174) and (0x4c, 246, 195). Records 2, 3 and 4 have their clip word rewritten at dispatch time with [0x8005cca8] + 0x3c, + 0x44 and + 0x4c (L0x00000f1c, L0x00000f38, L0x00000f54), so those three keys each draw one clip of a seven-clip block chosen by the language index that cnty_sel writes into that same global; the extracted NAMEDTCS sheet carries exactly seven clips at 0x3c..0x42, 0x44..0x4a and 0x4c..0x52, whose art reads delete, space and OK in the order jpn, usa, eng, fra, ita, ger, spn, reproducing the already-decoded language index table. Records 0 and 1 are not rewritten and are the same blank 16x17 frame, so those two keys carry no baked label. A plain character cell instead draws clip 0x27 at (col*14 + floor(col/5)*8 + 47, row*18 + 90) (L0x00000e18). These sprite positions do not follow the character grid: they step 21 pixels while the character rows step 18.
claims.notes: The language-order reading is an independent reproduction of ./dw3-research languages (global D0x8005cca8), not a new inference. NOT established: which of the two English indices (1 usa, 2 eng) a given build carries - their art is pixel-identical, so this screen cannot distinguish them; the walker ships index 2. Also not established: whether the original renders the unselected state of these keys from a second CLUT row, which is why the walker's selected state is a wash over the decoded rect rather than a swapped palette.
claims.coverage: All fifteen words of the record table were read individually from stdgname.s file offsets 0x4ec0..0x4ef8, so the five records are enumerated rather than sampled. The three language addends are the only three stores into that table anywhere in the dispatch tail (L0x00000f0c-L0x00000f5c read end to end). The positions were then checked against the rig framebuffer capture web/assets/ref/keyboard.png independently of the assembly: scanning every horizontal run of border-coloured pixels across x 195..305 for y 130..235 returns exactly three button rows, at y 153, 174 and 195, and a scan of y 211 returns exactly three lit pixels, at x 203, 222 and 246 - the three bottom-row record x values. claims.statement: The save screen's populate pass sets BOTH of its 'BIT' labels, not one. The loop at stgmcard.s L0x000006d0-L0x00000708 in F0x8008316c reads its widget pointer from s0+0xC at L0x000006e8, passes esmemcrd string 0x15 at L0x000006ec, and advances s0 by 4 in the delay slot at L0x000006fc, so consecutive iterations take widget 3 and then widget 4 of the record's descriptor table. The counter s2 is incremented once at L0x000006cc before the loop and again at L0x00000708, which is the DELAY SLOT of the branch-if-not-zero at L0x00000704 and therefore executes on the taken path as well as the fallthrough; with the set-less-than-immediate test against 2 at L0x00000700 the loop runs exactly twice. The m2c output shows a single iteration because it does not account for that delay-slot increment, which is what made this an open ambiguity.
claims.notes: Closes the stgmcard_ui.json gap 'widget 4 (BIT at 118,163) is set only by the empty-card pass; the populated pass touches widget 3 alone'. The walker already drew both labels from the descriptor table, so this confirms shipped behaviour rather than changing it; the extractor's per-widget disasm note is corrected. Evidence for the function body is checked decompilation at authority 3, but every line the trip count rests on is assembly at authority 2. Re-recorded 2026-08-14 to repair a statement whose backticked mnemonics were eaten by shell substitution on the first write.
claims.coverage: The loop was read as a whole in the assembly, from its entry at L0x000006cc through the branch and its delay slot at L0x00000708, rather than sampled: both increments of the counter and both uses of the widget pointer are accounted for, and the trip count follows from the initial value, the single test and the two increments with no other write to s2 in the body. This resolves the stated ambiguity in the direction OPPOSITE to the m2c reading it came from.

claims.statement: On the save screen the record's text and the record's frame are switched off at different moments, which settles whether the frame can outlive the text. F0x800836c4's exit band, reached when the screen's state at +0x10 is 2 and its sub-counter at +0x14 has not reached the running value, does three things in one step: it starts the window fold CLOSING through the data pointer [0x80088790] called as (screen+0x74, 0), it clears screen+0x60, and it calls F0x8008316c, whose first branch tests exactly that flag and calls the visibility slot +0x144 with 0 on all 19 record widgets. It clears screen+0x5C, the flag that gates the inner record frame (clips 0x24 and 0x25) and the party icons, only on a later pass, once the fold-done poll [0x80088794](screen+0x74) returns non-zero. The opening band passes 1 to the same fold start. So the record text disappears at the moment the window begins to close, and the frame and party icons keep drawing until the fold lands.
claims.notes: Closes the stgmcard_ui.json gap 'Whether the frame stays up behind a message is therefore not proven; the walker hides it with the record.' The answer is that it does stay up, for the length of the fold. Wired: web/save.js now plays the fold-out in reverse when the file card is left, hides the record text at once and keeps the frame until the tween lands, with three tests in tests/save-screen.test.js. NOT established: the flags' behaviour while a MESSAGE or CONFIRM window is up, which was the gap's original framing - the exit band this claim reads is the card leaving, and the message path was not traced. The fold start and done-poll are reached through data pointers whose targets were not re-read here; both functions are cited from checked decompilation at authority 3.
claims.coverage: Both branches of F0x800836c4 that write either flag were read, and they are the only writes to +0x5C or +0x60 on this object anywhere in the overlay's decompilation: a per-file scan of the twenty-three decompiled functions for assignments to those two fields returns F0x800836c4 and F0x80084dcc alone, and the latter sets both to 1 together on entry rather than clearing either. That is what makes the ordering a property of the code and not of one sampled path.

claims.statement: stgmcard is a member of the window-fold tween family (UI-C-FOLD-*), and its remaining chrome tables are resolved. The pair is F0x80087fdc start(obj, from, to, steps) writing +0x00 steps, +0x08 value, +0x0C value<<8, +0x10 target, +0x14 delta = ((to-from)<<8)/steps, +0x18 active, and F0x8008801c tick accumulating +0x0C by the delta, publishing +0x0C>>8 to +0x08, clamping direction-correctly at the target and returning 1 when done -- byte-for-byte the family shape. They are reached only indirectly, through the overlay data pointers at 0x80088798 and 0x8008879C. The one call site that fixes the animation is F0x80087534, which starts the message window's tween as (from 0x97, to 0, steps 0xA) on the object at screen+0x2824; F0x80087368 then draws the window clip 0x21 at (screen->unk58 + tweenX, screen->unk5C + screen+0x282C), i.e. the value at tween+0x08 is added to the window Y, so this member animates a 0x97-pixel vertical slide-in over 10 vsyncs. Data tables: 0x80088204 holds eight rows of seven s32 frame ids, -1 terminated, indexed by (save record starter byte - 3) -- rows [7,8,9,10,9,8], [14,15,16,15], [11,12,13,12], [3,4,5,6,5,4], [25,26,27,28,27,26], [0,1,2,1], [17,18,19,20,19,18], [21,22,23,24,23,22]. Those clip-id groups are identical to the ststat per-starter portrait groups already pinned in tools/extract_screen_packs.py STSTAT_PORTRAITS, which resolves the record's starter byte to a digimon id (3->1 Kotemon, 4->5 Veemon, 5->3 Monmon, 6->4 Agumon, 7->2 Kumamon, 8->6 Guilmon, 9->7 Renamon, 10->8 Patamon) without a second table. 0x800882E4 holds the eight per-starter nameplate clips [42,44,43,41,47,40,45,46] on the same (byte - 3) index, and 0x80088304 holds the slot chooser's three column x positions [109,177,245].
claims.notes: Lead-recorded 2026-08-05.
claims.frontier_rationale: Adds a named member and a concrete animated primitive to the fold family, but does not by itself answer UI-Q001, which asks the same question of fieldstg/stgtrain/stfgtrep/stitshop.

claims.statement: pro/stgmcard is the MEMORY CARD save/load screen, not the card battle game. The master-plan census row 'stgmcard / cardgame -> card battle game' is wrong; the card battle game is pro/cardgame.s and its front-ends are stcrdshp/stcrdabm/stcrddek. Proof 1: every text widget in stgmcard.s resolves its string bank with the standard 0x80044B38->unk414(*(s32*)0x8005CCA8 + BASE) idiom using BASE 0x78 = 120 = LBA_MSMEMCRD_BIN_IDX (~/ddw3/rust/dw2003_exe_data/src/lba.rs L123); the language variable holds 2 for English, giving 122 = LBA_ESMEMCRD_BIN_IDX, i.e. ~/ddw3/lang_file/dw2003/eng/esmemcrd.toml, a 41-string SAVE/LOAD/'Choose MEMORY CARD slot.' bank. Sixteen call sites use this base. The same idiom with BASE 0x39 = 57 = LBA_MSDGLABO resolves stgdglab to esdglabo, validating the model. Proof 2: the overlay resolves screen-pack handles 0x029D0000 and 0x029E0000 through 0x80044B38->unk424; the handle hi-word is the LBA index, and 0x29D/0x29E = 669/670 = LBA_STMCRDCS_BIN_IDX / LBA_STMCRDTM_BIN_IDX, the disc files AAA/DAT/MCARD/STMCRDCS.BIN and STMCRDTM.BIN. Proof 3: that pack, newly extracted (tools/extract_screen_packs.py DISC_PACKS entry 'stmcrd', 47 clip ids / 76 frames / 2 atlases), contains clip 0x22 = three PlayStation memory cards side by side, clip 0x23 = a console with its two card slots, clip 0x21 = the save-file card window, and clips 0x28..0x2F = eight per-starter save nameplates.
claims.notes: Recorded by the lead 2026-08-05 from a direct static decode; see docs/research/ui/stgmcard-decoded-2026-08-05.md.

claims.statement: On the memory-card save/load screen, which of the message window's two body boxes a given message lands in is decided by F0x80084dcc, and all sixteen of its resource-string call sites are now attributed. The constructor F0x80087534 stores its widgets in the caller's block: +0x00 the fold-following title at (205, 98), +0x14 a one-line box at (20, 113), +0x04 a FIVE-line box at (20, 129), +0x08 a TWO-line box at (20, 192), +0x0C the YES row at (207, 189) and +0x10 the NO row at (207, 203). Every one of F0x80084dcc's sixteen calls to the widget class's slot +0x114, the set-line-0-from-a-resource-string setter of UI-WIDGETCLASS-AE38-SETLINE-001, passes the bank [0x8005cca8] + 0x78, which is the language index plus the esmemcrd base LBA_MSMEMCRD 120. The five-line box takes esmemcrd 4 and 5, the two 'do not touch MEMORY CARD' waits, plus the card's own result message; the two-line box takes 7, 8, 9, 0x11, 0x12, 0x18 and 0x1D, which are the overwrite prompt, the saving and loading notices, the saved and loaded outcomes, 'No data here.' and 'Choose MEMORY CARD slot.'; the YES row takes 0x16 and the NO row 0x17. On the slot chooser both rows are instead set to string 3, '{1}', so the two option lines become the slot numbers rather than a yes/no pair. The five-line box's result message comes from a table of esmemcrd indices at 0x80088310, overlay file 0x5660, indexed by the value the screen holds at +0x68, which is the return code of the resident card services [0x80048A88] and [0x80048A94] called on the card handle at +0x64. Its first eleven entries are esmemcrd 1, 0x0A, 0x1B, 0x0A, 0x0B, 0x0C, 0x1C, 0x0D, 0x26, 0x24 and 0x25.
claims.notes: Closes most of the stgmcard_ui.json gap that called this an untraced 1116-line state machine. Wired: message_window.binding and message_window.result_messages in stgmcard_ui.json, and web/save.js now routes a message to the box its string is bound to instead of putting everything in the five-line box - 'Saved.', 'LOADED.' and 'No data here.' move 63 pixels down. STILL OPEN: the one-line box at +0x14 (20, 113) is bound by NONE of the sixteen sites, so what it holds is unestablished and the walker's SAVE/LOAD title there remains an assumption; esmemcrd 6 'Save here?' and 0x10 'Load which game?' are set somewhere other than a +0x114 site and were not traced; and the result table's LENGTH is inferred, not read - it has no terminator and the index is not bounds-checked, so the eleven-entry extent rests on entries 0..10 all being valid esmemcrd indices while entry 11 onward exceeds the bank's 41 strings and forms a consecutive ascending run. The evidence for both functions is checked decompilation at authority 3; the table itself is assembly at authority 2.
claims.coverage: The sixteen sites are the complete set, not a sample: the decompilation of F0x80084dcc was searched for every call through slot +0x114 and each of the sixteen hits was followed back to the assignment naming which of the caller-block widgets it targets, so no call is left unattributed. A census of the same file for the other widget-method slots found only +0x144 (visibility), +0x114, +0x118, +0x134 and +0x15C, which bounds the search. The eleven result-table entries were read word by word from stgmcard.s file offsets 0x5660 through 0x5688, and every one was checked to be a valid esmemcrd index whose text matches what the extractor records, asserted in tests/save-screen.test.js.

claims.statement: The stgmcard save-file card is built from a 19-entry widget descriptor table in the overlay's own data section at 0x80088088..0x80088204, stride 0x14, fields {+0x00 esmemcrd string index, +0x04 widget kind (1 = white text, 3 = the small/gold face), +0x08 x, +0x0C y, +0x10 numeric flag}. F0x800836c4 constructs them by calling the resident class-A text widget factory F0x8001ae38(handle, rec+0x4, rec+0x8, rec+0xC) once per record, count = screen->unk20, and patches record 0's string id by language first (0x20 = '-----' when 0x8005CCA8 is 0, else 0x21 = '--------'). F0x8008316c is the populate pass and has three branches: screen->unk60 == 0 hides all 19 widgets through slot +0x144(0); a card with no file sets each widget's text to its descriptor string and, for descriptors with the +0x10 flag set, also calls +0x118(1,0), +0x148(1) and +0x134(descriptor x, y); a card with a file binds the per-slot record at screen->unk50 + slot*0x44 + 0x74 as widget 0 = +0x114(record, -1) the record's own name string, widget 1 = esstarea (bank base 0xA9 = 169 = LBA_MSSTAREA) indexed by record+0x18, widget 2 = esshpnam (bank base 0x94 = 148 = LBA_MSSHPNAM, whose tail is every inn/save point) indexed by record+0x1C, widget 3 = 'BIT', widget 5 = +0x118(0, record+0x20) right-aligned, widgets 6..8 = 'LV', widgets 9..11 = record+0x3C+2i or '--' when the slot's starter byte is below 3, widgets 12..14 = record+0x28/+0x2A/+0x2C play hours/minutes/seconds right-aligned, widgets 15..16 = ':', and widgets 17..18 = a leading zero repositioned to (0x111,0xB2)/(0x124,0xB2) and shown only when the corresponding field is below 10. Right alignment is class-A slot +0x148, the justification toggle that measures line 0 and shifts it left by its own width (UI-WIDGETCLASS-AE38-TEXTLAYOUT-001/-CORRECTION-001), so the descriptor x of a numeric field is its RIGHT edge. Every constructed position lands inside clip 0x21's 312x151 window drawn at (5,0x59), an independent geometric check.
claims.notes: Lead-recorded 2026-08-05. Extractor tools/extract_stgmcard_ui.py reads the table from the .s at build time; consumer web/save.js.
claims.frontier_rationale: Screen-specific chrome decode; not one of the two open ui-chrome frontiers.

claims.statement: The save screen's rotating transition quad is a POLY_G4 -- the GPU's gouraud-shaded, untextured four-point polygon -- and its four vertex colours are really two. F0x80083c50 builds one primitive per frame, writing the tag's word count 8 at prim+0x3 and the GP0 command 0x38 at prim+0x7, then filling colour triples at prim+0x4, +0xC, +0x14 and +0x1C, which are exactly the four POLY_G4 vertex-colour offsets. Vertices 0 and 2 both take the byte triple at the object's +0x6C..+0x6E and vertices 1 and 3 both take +0x70..+0x72, so the quad shades across one axis rather than carrying four independent corners. Those two triples are not literals in the draw function: the object installs a five-slot method table at +0xC4..+0xD4 in its constructor F0x80084058, and slots +0xCC and +0xD0 point at the two three-store colour setters at stgmcard.s L0x00000f6c-L0x00000f74 and L0x00000f80-L0x00000f88, which write their three byte arguments to +0x6C..+0x6E and +0x70..+0x72 respectively. The one call site, F0x80084dcc L237 and L239, passes (0x7F, 0x32, 0xF2) and (0xD1, 0x2F, 0xDE) -- a violet and a magenta. The same construction site is F0x80084058(0xCD, 0xC1, 0x62, 0xA), whose four arguments land at +0x58, +0x5C, +0x60 and +0x64 and are read by the corner setup as origin x, origin y, width and height, giving a 98 by 10 bar at (205, 193). Its angle at +0x8C ramps by 0x1000 divided by +0x74 each frame and clamps at 0xF33, just short of the 0x1000 full turn.
claims.notes: Closes the last chrome gap on this screen. Wired: transition.quad in stgmcard_ui.json and drawTransitionQuad in web/save.js, reachable as __labOpen('savequad'); four tests in tests/save-screen.test.js; capture docs/research/ui/captures/save-transition-quad-2026-08-14.png. The walker renders the two-colour gouraud fill as a canvas linear gradient, which is an approximation of the hardware's interpolation, not a decode. NOT wired into normal play: the state that raises the quad is the card-access phase and this port has no memory card to check, so it is lab-only rather than faked - the same rule web/save.js already states for the card-insert, format, block-count and read-error paths. NOT established: the pivot offsets at +0x84 and +0x88, which the corner loop subtracts before the transform and adds back after, are written by no decompiled function, so the rotation centre is not settled and the walker turns the bar about its own middle. The three matrix helpers F0x8002b1dc, F0x8002b23c and F0x8002b65c were not read. All three functions are cited from checked decompilation at authority 3; the setters themselves are assembly at authority 2.
claims.coverage: Every write into the primitive was read from the builder in one contiguous block, so the four vertex colours are the complete set the function fills rather than a sample, and the identification rests on the two literals it also writes -- the word count and the command byte -- not on the offsets alone. The colour sources were then searched for exhaustively in two directions: a scan of all twenty-three decompiled functions of the overlay for assignments to those six fields returns only a DIFFERENT object, and a text search of the whole overlay assembly for any load or store at offsets 0x6c, 0x6d, 0x6e, 0x70, 0x71 or 0x72 returns exactly twelve lines: the six stores of the two setters and the six loads in the builder. That is what makes the two setters the only writers and the single call site the only source of the values.

claims.statement: The gym's mid-training viewport window IS drawn by stgtrain's own code, at chrome clip 0x28 positioned (114,75) by the rep-loop function F0x80086c0c. This CONTRADICTS the provenance note previously carried in web/assets/data/stgtrain_ui.json, which stated that the box was pixel-measured off a screenshot and that 'stgtrain.s has no dedicated spawn/draw code for this viewport in its own overlay (exhaustively checked)'. The exhaustive check searched for a spawn or an actor allocation and therefore missed a plain chrome-clip blit. The measured origin happened to be exactly right, so no rendered position changes; what changes is that the value is now evidence-backed rather than eyeballed, and the walker's last pixel-measured menu geometry is eliminated. The companion half of the old note still stands: stgtrain does not own the Digimon SPRITE drawn inside the window, and the punching-bag art and the idle-versus-punch clip selection remain unresolved.

The starter-pack membership table is static and readable. The binder indexes it as *(s32 *)0x80089B94 + selectedPack * 0xC, and the word at 0x80089B94 is a static .word holding 0x80089b6c, so the table is three records of three s32 roster ids: pack 0 = {0, 6, 7}, pack 1 = {2, 3, 6}, pack 2 = {1, 5, 7}. A fourth record would read unrelated pointer words, fixing the pack count at three. These ids reconcile exactly with the membership web/packs.js already shipped (Kotemon/Renamon/Patamon, Monmon/Agumon/Renamon, Kumamon/Guilmon/Patamon), independently confirming that browser data against original code and implying roster ids 0=Kotemon, 1=Kumamon, 2=Monmon, 3=Agumon, 5=Guilmon, 6=Renamon, 7=Patamon, with id 4 in no pack. INCIDENTAL: 0x80089b6c is listed in stplnmet_ui.json's open_gaps as one of seven functions that failed m2c decompilation; it is not a function at all but this data table, so that failure is a phantom and the other six should be re-checked for the same before effort is spent on them.

The starter-pack registration wizard's per-row text binding is resolved, closing the gap recorded in stplnmet_ui.json that said the string index for each pack row and each Digimon row was untraced. The binder F0x80087190 sets every label through class-A slot +0x114 (set line 0 from a resource string): the screen title takes string 6 of text bank 0x8D; the three pack rows take strings 7, 8 and 9 (index = row + 7); the two list headers take selectedPack + 0xA and selectedPack + 0x1A of the same bank; each Digimon row takes its NAME from a different bank, 0x4E, at index memberId + 1, and its DESCRIPTION from bank 0x8D at index memberId + 0xD. Separately, the three column headers built by F0x80087b14 sit at y=18 with x taken from the 4-byte-stride table at 0x80089A80, giving x = 228, 256 and 284, and bind strings 3, 4 and 5 of bank 0x8D.

No button in the pause-menu overlay opens the Sort Items submenu, because the overlay never reads Square at all. Every pad read in ststatus goes through the bit-remap accessor, and across the whole overlay -- including the six screen-object methods the disassembler's entry list never named -- the only bits ever asked for are Up, Right, Down, Left, L1, R1, Circle and Cross. The 'Sort Items' header and its By Strength / By Name rows exist in the string bank and nothing in this overlay can reach them, the same shape as the Digivolve Demo screen. This closes U-08, which had been left UNKNOWN because the pass that looked did not contain the site.
claims.notes: 151 pad reads against 152 remap calls, so the bit enumeration is exhaustive for this overlay rather than a sample. It does not rule out a reader in another overlay; it does rule out the bag, which is where the legend string sits. The By Strength comparator (U-07) is still undecoded and is now moot for the walker.
