claims.statement: The badge drawn beside a technique slot on the digivolve screen is the technique's CATEGORY, not its element. It is cmfont clip 0x37 plus the technique record's +4 byte, that byte takes only the five values 2..6 across all 443 records, and all five clips exist. Reading it as the element is what made the machine and dark badges undrawable: elements run 1..8, so those two asked for clips 0x3E and 0x3F, and the disc's cmfont directory has 94 clips whose id list skips exactly those. Nothing is missing from the extraction -- the original never asks for them, and never asks for 0x37 or 0x38 either, which an element badge would have needed for the 270 techniques whose element is 'normal'.
claims.notes: Fire is element 2 and most fire moves are category 2, so Kotemon's 'Hot Head' landed on the right clip under the wrong reading and hid the mistake for one capture. The byte is the one tools/build_battle_data.py already parsed as attack_cat; 443 of 443 records agree with the disc image.

claims.statement: The shared text widget built by F0x8001ae38 draws right-aligned when its method +0x148 is called with a non-zero argument. F0x8001a25c stores the measured string width into the widget at +0xBC, and the widget draw F0x800197a4 loads +0xBC, negates it and stores it to +0xB8 (assembly 0x80019808 lhu 0xbc, 0x80019810 negu, 0x80019814 sh 0xb8), after which the per-glyph pen x is +0xB8 plus +0xB0 plus the glyph offset. So the whole string is shifted left by its own width and the recorded x is the RIGHT edge of the text. With the argument zero, +0xBC is set to 0 and the text draws from its x rightwards. The widget's second constructor argument is a font kind clamped to 1..3 indexing D0x8004de00 + kind*0x18. The number setter is +0x118 (F0x800195b0): it formats through F0x80019508, a plain itoa that writes digits from the start of the buffer with no padding, then subtracts 0x2C from every byte to reach the glyph ids.
claims.notes: Found while closing the gym screen's coverage gap. Canonical documents read first: docs/research/ui/stgtrain-decoded-2026-07-11.md and docs/research/ui/symbols/stgtrain.md, both routed through docs/DOC_INDEX.md.
claims.coverage: Read end to end for the four routines named: F0x8001ae38, F0x8001a25c, F0x800195b0 and F0x80019508 in exe-decomp/c/, plus the one site in F0x800197a4 that reads +0xBC. The negate-and-store was then confirmed instruction by instruction in the assembly at exe-decomp/c/_asm/F0x800197a4.s lines 57-63, not only in the m2c output. The set of readers was enumerated by listing every file in exe-decomp/c that mentions unkBC -- four files -- so no other draw path was missed. NOT checked: the other two readers, F0x8001c4ec and F0x8001cab0; whether any caller passes +0x148 a value other than 0 or 1; the contents of the font table D0x8004de00; and nothing was observed in the running game.
claims.frontier_rationale: Explains why a decoded text place can be a right edge rather than a left one. Every screen that reads a number out of this widget family depends on it, and the gym HUD's two number columns were drawn in the wrong places without it.

claims.statement: F0x8001ffa8 is a THIRD global-singleton class, and it is a multi-line string layout context rather than the quad/texture-upload interface it has been called in passing. It constructs in place on caller-owned memory (usually a stack local): it clears 0x34 bytes through D0x8004b600, installs six method pointers at +0x1c..+0x30, calls its own +0x1c slot on itself, and defaults the field at +0x18 to 0xa800. Like the second draw context, none of its methods takes a receiver: +0x1c F0x8001fd1c(obj) stores its argument into gp+0x1d0 and every other slot re-reads that global, so constructing one makes it the active instance. +0x24 F0x8001fd28(a,b) sets the pair at +0x8/+0xc; +0x28 F0x8001fd3c(a,b) sets the pair at +0x10/+0x14; +0x30 F0x8001ff9c(v) sets +0x18, the scratch-buffer size. +0x2c F0x8001fe38(resourceId) is the layout pass: it allocates a scratch buffer of +0x18 bytes through D0x8004b5f4, then enumerates the resource's sub-records through the table entry D0x80044b38+0x428, and for each record whose first word is the magic 0x4e454c52 (the ASCII tag RLEN) it RLE-expands the payload from record+8 into the scratch buffer - control byte with the high bit set repeats one byte (value & 0x7f) times, high bit clear copies that many literal bytes - then passes either the expanded buffer or the raw record to +0x20, calls F0x80025868(0), and advances the cursor at +0x8 by 0x40 before the next record, freeing the scratch buffer through D0x8004b5ec when the enumeration ends. +0x20 F0x8001fd50(record) combines the two stored pairs with the record's own halfwords through F0x80025b14 and writes the resulting pen position into +0x0/+0x2. Separately, the helper F0x8001fcc0(dest) does NOT fetch a shared block from a global: it clears 0xc bytes at the caller's destination and BUILDS a three-entry interface there - +0x0 F0x8001f744, +0x4 F0x8001f770, +0x8 F0x8001fa20 - then registers that block's address in gp+0x1c8 through F0x8001f738. So the 'shared text service' other classes obtain from F0x8001fcc0 is a three-function interface, where slot +0x0 resolves a string by id and slot +0x4 measures a string.
claims.notes: Lead re-verified the two load-bearing points against raw MIPS: F0x8001fcc0 at fns.s L17408-L17428 clears 0xc bytes and stores exactly three function addresses at +0/+4/+8 before jal F0x8001f738, and F0x8001fd1c at L17432-L17435 is the single store 'sw a0, 0x1d0(gp)'. AFFECTS EXISTING RESEARCH: docs/research/field/character-drop-shadow-decoded-2026-07-27.md L192-194 labels F0x8001ffa8 the 'quad/texture-upload interface ctor'. That label is not supported for F0x8001ffa8 itself - the constructor and its six slots are string enumeration, RLE expansion and line layout. The label may still be right one level down, inside the undecoded F0x80025b14, so this is a refinement of that doc, not a refutation of the shadow decode that depends on it. NOT established: F0x80025b14 (the actual per-record geometry step, and the largest remaining gap here), F0x80025868, the contents of the D0x80044b38 table, slots +0x4 and +0x8 of the F0x8001fcc0 interface beyond their call-site shape, and whether gp+0x1c8 and gp+0x1d0 can ever hold the same object.
claims.frontier_rationale: Closes the eighth and last instance dispatch table of UI-DISPATCH-CENSUS-COMPLETE-001 and identifies a third singleton-by-gp-slot convention, which is the mechanism that makes those call sites attributable.

claims.statement: The title screen's idle timeout closes an attract loop, and on the Japanese build it alternates. When the language global is non-zero the timeout always launches 0xe02, the MOVIEOPN opening. When it is zero the timeout reads the PREVIOUS screen code and launches 0xe01 unless the previous screen was already 0xe01, in which case it launches 0xe02 - so the Japanese build plays its two opening movies in turn rather than repeating one. Both opening movie rows hand back to 0x0e00, the title screen, so the loop returns. The END card hands off to 0xe01 with no language test, so after the ending any build plays the MOVIEOP2 opening and then arrives at the title screen.
claims.coverage: Both arms of the language test were read, and inside the Japanese arm both arms of the previous-code test were read including their branch delay slots, which is what decides which of the two codes each path ends up passing. The END card's arm was checked for a language test and has none: its launch code is a single immediate with no branch around it.
limitations: The high-byte-to-overlay step is still unread. The stage-select table shows one overlay per high byte across its 297 rows, which is why the high byte is described as selecting the overlay, but the loader code that performs that selection was not opened.

Movie index 12 has no low byte available, because 0x0d is taken by the END card. The movie table's rows beyond index 11 are the language variants of index 11 rather than separate indices, so this is consistent, but no code was read that proves index 12 is unreachable.
Whether MOVIEOP2 and MOVIEOPN differ in content, and why the END card sends every build to MOVIEOP2, is not established - only that the code does it.
derivation: grep the shipped data for the 0x8004b430..0x8004b448 service slots

claims.statement: Independent consumer-side confirmation of four class-A (F0x8001ae38) widget slots, taken from the cursor object's per-frame handler F0x8001b0a4 which owns a class-A widget and pushes state into it every time its dirty flag is set. +0x110 is called with a char pointer taken from the string table D0x8004dce0 (set line 0 text - agrees with UI-WIDGETCLASS-AE38-SETLINE-001). +0x144 is called with a single BYTE read from the cursor's visible flag self+0x64, so on this class +0x144 is a VISIBILITY setter, not a close/teardown call. +0x134 is called with the cursor's two s16 position fields (self+0x58, self+0x5c) loaded with lh, so +0x134 is the widget's SET POSITION (x,y) slot. +0x15c is called with the s32 at the cursor's self+0x54. Ordering also matters: on the widget's creation tick the handler calls +0x110, then +0x144, then +0x15c, then a shared service at D0x8004de10+0x188, and stores that service's return into self+0x70 as a timestamp - so +0x110/+0x144/+0x15c form the widget's initial configuration sequence.
claims.notes: This settles the long-standing +0x144 ambiguity for class A specifically: docs/research/ui/shop-system-decompiled.md L63 reads +0x144 as 'close'. A byte-wide visible flag is not a close call, so the shop doc's +0x144 reading is CONTRADICTED for this receiver class while its +0x114 = 'set text' reading stands. Because F0x8001ae38 and F0x8001e5bc install different functions over the SAME offset range (UI-DISPATCH-TABLE-CENSUS-001), this does not settle +0x144 for class-B receivers. NOT established: the meaning of +0x15c's s32 argument or of the cursor field self+0x54 that supplies it.
claims.frontier_rationale: +0x144 carries 600 unresolved indirect-call sites, the highest of any slot offset in the corpus.

claims.statement: The F0x8001ae38 widget class stores SIX independent text lines in the receiver itself: line i is a 0xc-byte record at self+0x5c+0xc*i (+0 char buffer pointer, +4 s16 allocated capacity, +6 s16 length, +0xa s16 non-empty/dirty flag), so the array spans self+0x5c..self+0xa3. Every line setter funnels through F0x80019370(self, lineRecord, cString): it takes strlen (F0x8002525c, exe/fns.s L23173) of the incoming C string, stores the length at record+6, frees the old buffer through D0x8004b5ec when the existing capacity is too small, reallocates a 4-byte-granular rounded-up buffer through D0x8004b5f4, notifies D0x8004b600, then memcpy's the bytes with F0x8002514c (L23093). A null string argument recurses with the default literal D0x800101a4. It sets self+0xc1 to 1 when the resulting string is non-empty and 0 otherwise (the has-text flag the drawer F0x800197a4 also clears when the line-0 pointer is null), and calls F0x8001a1b8(self, 0) whenever self+0xaa is zero. This makes the class a MULTI-LINE TEXT WIDGET whose payload is ordinary NUL-terminated bytes in the game's own text encoding, not a cel or animation stream.
claims.notes: Stride confirmed arithmetically at L10342: (i<<1 + i)<<2 = 12*i, NOT the 0x18 stride previously assumed. The 0x18 figure in docs/research/battle/digivolution-tech-system-decoded-2026-07-11.md L522-527 is wrong. Line-record field names beyond +0/+4/+6/+0xa are not yet established.
claims.frontier_rationale: Slot bodies +0x110..+0x120 of the 25-slot F0x8001ae38 table (UI-DISPATCH-TABLE-CENSUS-001) all resolve to one shared setter, so naming the setter names five slots at once.

claims.statement: Three further slots of the F0x8001ae38 widget class are read, taking it to sixteen of twenty-five. +0x12c F0x8001a180(self, id) is a bounds-checked selector over a global record array: it computes (id - 1) as unsigned and, when that is not less than 3, forces id to 1, so the accepted domain is exactly 1..3 with 1 as the fallback; it then forms the byte offset id*24 (via id*3 shifted left 3), adds it to the pointer held in the global D0x8004de00, stores the resulting record pointer at receiver+0x50, and caches the record's first byte at receiver+0xbe. The array therefore holds 24-byte records and has at least three usable entries. +0x130 F0x8001a1b8(self, v) branches on the SIGN of v: when v is greater than zero it clears halfwords +0xa4, +0xa8 and +0xa6 and stores v at +0xaa; when v is zero or negative it copies the halfword at receiver+0x62 into +0xa4 and clears +0xa8 and +0xaa. +0x134 F0x8001a1e8(self, a, b) stores halfwords a and b at receiver+0xb0 and +0xb2. Receiver+0xbe is also the field written by slot +0x13c F0x8001a1fc (UI-WIDGETCLASS-AE38-SETTERS-001), so +0x12c sets it as a side effect of record selection while +0x13c sets it directly.
claims.notes: The contents and purpose of the 24-byte records at D0x8004de00 are NOT established, nor is the meaning of receiver fields +0x50, +0x62, +0xa4/+0xa6/+0xa8/+0xaa, +0xb0/+0xb2 or +0xbe. D0x8004de00 is adjacent to the already-characterised service block D0x8004de10 (docs/research/ui/shared-ui-service-families-2026-08-04.md L161) but no relationship between them is established. Nine slots remain unread: +0x110, +0x114, +0x118, +0x11c, +0x120, +0x124, +0x128, +0x148, +0x14c; all nine are large bodies rather than accessors.
claims.frontier_rationale: Continues the largest partially-read dispatch table and identifies a previously unrecorded global record array with a determinable element size and minimum length.

claims.statement: Eight slots of the text element class F0x8001ae38 and two of the cursor class F0x8001b364 gain a MEANING, by identifying the reader of the field each setter writes. Prior claims established WHAT each of these setters stores but not what the value does: UI-WIDGETCLASS-AE38-SETTERS-001 gives +0x138 stores byte +0xC0 and +0x140 stores halfwords +0xB4/+0xB6 with the +0xC2 flag; UI-WIDGETCLASS-AE38-TAIL-001 gives +0x15C stores word +0x58, +0x160 stores byte +0xBF, and +0x168 returns byte +0xC3; UI-WIDGETCLASS-AE38-MID-001 gives the sign branch of +0x130. The readers: +0x138 byte +0xC0 is ADDED INTO THE GLYPH CLUT WORD by the drawer F0x800197a4, which loads it at fns.s L10602, adds it to the per-glyph value, shifts left 6 and ORs the masked texture-page field before storing the halfword, so +0x138 is the TEXT COLOUR as a palette-row offset. +0x15C word +0x58 is passed as the SECOND ARGUMENT to the view the GPU ordering-table lookup returns: the drawer loads +0x54 into a0, calls D0x8004de10 slot +0x17C, then loads +0x58 into a1 and calls the returned object's own +0x138 slot (fns.s L10496-L10506), so +0x15C selects the ordering-table ROW the glyphs link into, not a maximum index and not an alignment. +0x160 byte +0xBF is the PAGE LINE COUNT: the page walk F0x80019fb0 compares its line counter against it and stops, and the line-break helper F0x8001a73c compares and temporarily decrements it. +0x168 byte +0xC3 is a PAUSE flag, set when the glyph walker meets control class 4, cleared at the start of every draw, and tested by the tick before it advances the typewriter, so the getter reports BUSY rather than finished. +0x148 measures line 0 and stores the width the drawer NEGATES into the pen offset, which is a RIGHT ALIGN switch and not a three-way justify; this agrees with UI-WIDGETCLASS-AE38-TEXTLAYOUT-CORRECTION-001 and adds only the name. +0x130 STARTS THE TYPEWRITER: a positive delay zeroes the visible end and the tick counter and stores the delay, and a non-positive delay copies the full length into the visible end, which shows the whole line at once. +0x128 SKIPS THE TYPEWRITER: it runs only while base state0 is 1 and writes the stop position into the visible end, revealing the rest of the page. +0x140 sets the GLYPH CELL SIZE: the drawer advances the pen by +0xB4 instead of the glyph's own width, the line-break helper advances by +0xB6 instead of the font default, and the measure call takes +0xB4 as a fixed advance, so it is a cell and not a digit-only width. On the cursor class, +0x88 stores a byte at +0x60 and raises the dirty flag at +0x68, and the next tick forwards that byte to the owned text element's +0x138, so it is the CURSOR TEXT COLOUR. +0x94 stores a word at +0x7C which the cursor tick tests as zero versus nonzero: nonzero snaps the glyph frame to 0 and skips the blink entirely, so it FREEZES the cursor animation and is neither a count nor a range.
claims.coverage: Ten slots gain a meaning here. Four readings were verified by the lead directly against the original assembly at authority 2 and are marked so: the +0x138 CLUT pack at fns.s L10598-L10614, the +0x15C ordering-table argument at fns.s L10494-L10512, the cursor +0x94 freeze setter at fns.s L12181-L12184 with its tick test at fns.s L12204-L12238, and the base-object family below. The remaining readings -- +0x140, +0x148, +0x160, +0x168, +0x130, +0x128 and cursor +0x88 -- rest on a delegated read of the decompilation and assembly that the lead did NOT re-verify line by line; they are recorded at partially_verified for that reason and each names its own reader for a reviewer to check. NOT NEW, and NOT re-derived here: the four base task object slots +0x28, +0x2C, +0x38 and +0x3C were already fully decoded in UI-TASKOBJ-STATEMACHINE-001 as the set and advance operations of a four-level nested state, and the lead re-read fns.s L4739-L4788 and the constructor to confirm that claim rather than to extend it; slot +0x110 line-0 string and slot +0x120 line-from-resource were already decoded in UI-WIDGETCLASS-AE38-SETLINE-001; slot +0x134 set position was already decoded in UI-WIDGETCLASS-AE38-CONSUMER-001. Slot +0x170 is NOT named here: UI-WIDGETCLASS-AE38-TAIL-001 establishes only that it returns true when base state1 equals 1, and whether that means waiting for a confirm press is a reading of one consumer arm, not of the slot. No player-visible effect is claimed for any slot beyond the drawer behaviour cited.
claims.frontier_rationale: Turns eight established field writes on the text element, plus two on the cursor, into named operations by finding the reader of each field. Settles 10 of the 18 slot-name disagreements recorded in docs/research/ui/symbols/shared-objects.md.

claims.statement: Nine further slots of the 25-entry widget class installed by exe/fns:F0x8001ae38 are single-purpose accessors over the receiver's field block, taking the class from four to thirteen slots read. Setters: +0x150 F0x8001a418 stores word a1 at +0xc8; +0x154 F0x8001a420 stores words a1 and a2 at +0xd0 and +0xd4, sets +0xd8 to the constant 0x1000 and +0xcc to 1; +0x158 F0x8001a43c stores words a1 and a2 at +0xe0 and +0xe4; +0x15c F0x8001a448 stores word a1 at +0x58; +0x160 F0x8001a450 stores byte a1 at +0xbf; +0x164 F0x8001a458 stores byte a1 at +0xc4. Getters: +0x168 F0x8001a460 returns byte +0xc3; +0x16c F0x8001a46c returns byte +0xc1, which is exactly the field written by +0x144 F0x8001a23c (UI-WIDGETCLASS-AE38-SETTERS-001), making +0x144 and +0x16c a setter/getter pair on one byte. Predicate: +0x170 F0x8001a478 computes ((state1 ^ 1) < 1) and therefore returns true if and only if the inherited base-object state1 field at +0x10 equals 1 — a third independent site confirming state1 at +0x10 per UI-TASKOBJ-STATEMACHINE-001. The 0x1000 constant written to +0xd8 matches the 4.12 fixed-point unity used for scale in the draw context (UI-DRAWCTX-VTABLE-001), which is suggestive but NOT established for this field.

claims.statement: The F0x8001ae38 widget class is a TEXT widget, and the long-standing operational label for its slot +0x114 is corroborated while the label for +0x144 is not. +0x110 F0x800194c4(self, arg) forwards to F0x80019370 passing self+0x5c as the second argument, so it writes into a buffer embedded in the receiver at +0x5c. +0x114 F0x800194e8 is a thin wrapper that tail-calls F0x800196e4 — the function installed at slot +0x120 of the same class — with a fourth argument of zero, so +0x114 and +0x120 are the short and long forms of one operation. The immediately adjacent resident routine F0x80019508 converts a signed integer to decimal ASCII in place: it emits the character 0x30 for a non-positive value, otherwise counts decimal digits by repeated division by ten and writes each remainder plus 0x30 into successive bytes of the destination. This places the whole F0x800194xx-F0x800195xx region in string formatting. Taken together with the receiver-embedded buffer at +0x5c, this supports the operational reading '+0x114 = set text' recorded in docs/research/ui/shop-system-decompiled.md L63 for this class. The same document's '+0x144 = close' remains CONTRADICTED by UI-WIDGETCLASS-AE38-SETTERS-001, which shows +0x144 performing only a conditionally-gated single-byte write paired with the getter at +0x16c.
claims.notes: The exact formatting contract of F0x80019370 and F0x800196e4 is NOT read, so 'set text' is supported by call shape and neighbourhood, not proven. Seven slots remain unread on this class: +0x118, +0x11c, +0x120, +0x124, +0x128, +0x148, +0x14c. Correction to the framing of UI-WIDGETCLASS-AE38-SETTERS-001: that claim's rejection of the shop labels applied only to +0x144 and should not be read as rejecting the +0x114 label, which this claim supports.
claims.frontier_rationale: Identifies the class of the highest-traffic ambiguous slot and resolves, in opposite directions, the two prior operational labels attached to it.

claims.statement: Three edits. (2) Replace 'all other classes advance by service[+4][class] bytes' with the per-class advances: 'classes 0, 3 and >=5 advance 1 or 2 by the line-0 flag halfword at +0x66; class 1 advances 2; class 4 ends the walk; the class-2 handler's non-0x08 path advances by service[+4][nextByte]'. claims.statement: Correction to UI-WIDGETCLASS-AE38-TEXTLAYOUT-001. That claim describes the class-A justification slot +0x148 (F0x8001a25c) as calling 'the text service block's slot +0x14'. The offset is wrong. F0x8001a25c calls F0x8001fcc0 with a0 = sp+0x10, so the three-entry interface F0x8001fcc0 builds (UI-TEXTCTX-FFA8-001) starts at sp+0x10; the subsequent load at fns.s L11183 is lw v0, 0x14(sp), which is interface slot +0x4, not +0x14. Interface slot +0x4 is F0x8001f770. So class-A slot +0x148 measures the line by calling F0x8001f770(line-0 record, self+0x50 font kind, self+0xb4) and stores the measured width at self+0xbc. Everything else in UI-WIDGETCLASS-AE38-TEXTLAYOUT-001 stands, including the drawer negating self+0xbc into the pen offset self+0xb8. The companion reading in UI-WIDGETCLASS-AE38-SETLINE-001 is NOT affected: class-A slot +0x120 (F0x800196e4) loads 0x10(sp) after the same call, which is interface slot +0x0 = F0x8001f744, the string-by-id lookup, exactly as that claim states.
claims.notes: The error came from reading the stack displacement as if it were the interface offset; the interface base is sp+0x10, so subtract 0x10 from every such displacement. Naming F0x8001f770 as a MEASURE function is an inference from its use here (its result becomes a pen shift) plus the parallel with F0x8001f744; its body was not read in this pass.
claims.frontier_rationale: Keeps the class-A table usable: a wrong service-slot offset would misdirect anyone following the justification path.

claims.statement: The remaining nine slots of the F0x8001e5bc widget class (class B) are two double-buffered mechanisms plus a destructor, all indexed by one shared global. The constructor allocates a 0x16c-byte object through D0x8004b5fc, stores its second argument at self+0x68, derives an element count self+0x64 from the global preset table D0x8004dfa0 indexed by that argument, allocates TWO parallel arrays of self+0x64 words at self+0x5c and self+0x60, and clears both with F0x80025d54. Mechanism one - the element array: +0x140 F0x8001dffc(self) returns the word at self + D0x8004de44*4 + 0x5c, i.e. it selects between the two parallel arrays using the shared global page index D0x8004de44; +0x138 F0x8001dfa8(self, index) returns the same base advanced by index*4; +0x13c F0x8001dfcc(self, value) reaches the same place after arithmetic-shifting its value right by (0x10 - self+0x68), a variable-precision scale driven by the same constructor argument that sized the array; and +0x144 F0x8001e01c(self) simply returns self+0x68, exposing that shift/size parameter. Slot +0x130 F0x8001de68 is the per-frame producer for this array: it snapshots the object's base block and its +0x6c/+0x6e origin, selects the array page through the shared UI service block field D0x8004de10+0x34, writes a packed value into the array whose low 24 bits are compared for equality by the helper F0x8001dddc (which merges runs of equal values from the end backwards), and pushes a 0x40-byte primitive through F0x800266b4 by advancing the display cursor at D0x8004de10+0x20; slot +0x134 F0x8001dda0(self) clears the whole array again with F0x80025d54(self + D0x8004de44*4 + 0x5c, self+0x64). Mechanism two - two independent save/restore pairs over 8-word global blocks, both using the SAME global D0x8004de44 but with a 0x20-byte stride: +0x15c F0x8001e404(self, flag, arg) always stores flag at self+0x84 and, when the flag is non-zero, stores arg at self+0x88 and copies the 8-word global D0x80081358 into self + (D0x8004de44<<5) + 0x8c..0xa8, while +0x158 F0x8001e470(self) copies that saved slot back out into D0x80081358 after calling F0x8002998c(self+0x88); +0x164 F0x8001e4f4(self, flag) always stores flag at self+0xcc and when non-zero copies the second 8-word global D0x800812f8 into self + (D0x8004de44<<5) + 0xd0..0xec, while +0x160 F0x8001e55c(self) copies that slot back out into D0x800812f8 unconditionally. +0x168 F0x8001e118(self) is the destructor: it calls F0x80025868(0), frees self+0x5c and self+0x60 through the allocator-family deallocator, and frees the callback-queue array at self+0x80 only when the capacity self+0x78 is non-zero.
claims.notes: NOT established, and deliberately left open: what the global D0x8004de44 counts (only its two stride uses are proven - times 4 into the +0x5c array pointer and shifted left 5 into the 0x20-byte save slots); whether the two-page selection is genuinely double buffering rather than some other paging; what the two 8-word global blocks D0x80081358 and D0x800812f8 hold; what F0x80025868 and F0x8002998c do; and what the packed array entries mean on screen. The strongest structural reading the evidence supports is a scrollable rectangular panel that emits one GPU primitive per run of equal array entries, but naming the on-screen widget requires tracing the constructor's callers and the screen that builds it, which was NOT done. Two independent readings of the page index disagree in source: slot +0x130 selects the page via D0x8004de10+0x34 while slots +0x134/+0x138/+0x140 use D0x8004de44 - whether those two always hold the same value is unresolved and matters, because a mismatch would mean the producer and the clear act on different pages.
claims.frontier_rationale: Completes all 23 slots of class B, the last unopened instance dispatch table in UI-DISPATCH-CENSUS-COMPLETE-001, which is the precondition for attributing +0x110..+0x168 call sites by receiver.

claims.statement: The first seven slots of the F0x8001e5bc widget class (class B, 23 slots at +0x110..+0x168) are one coherent screen-rectangle-with-scroll subsystem, and the composing method proves how they fit together. +0x110 F0x8001e0b0(self,x,y) writes the s16 pair at self+0x0/+0x2. +0x114 F0x8001e0bc(self,w,h) writes the s16 pair at self+0x4/+0x6. +0x118 F0x8001e058(self,ox,oy) writes the s16 anchor/origin pair at self+0x6c/+0x6e. +0x120 F0x8001e088(self,sx,sy) writes the s32 scroll pair at self+0x70/+0x74 absolutely, and +0x124 F0x8001e094(self,dx,dy) adds to the same pair, so scrolling can be driven either way. +0x11c F0x8001e064(self,out) reads that scroll pair back into a caller struct after an arithmetic-shift-right of 8, i.e. the scroll accumulator is fixed point with 256 sub-units per whole unit, which is what lets the widget scroll smoothly at less than one unit per frame. +0x128 F0x8001e0c8(self,outRect) composes all of them into a single output rectangle: out.x = (self+0x0 - self+0x6c) + (self+0x70 >> 8), out.y = (self+0x2 - self+0x6e) + (self+0x74 >> 8), out.w = self+0x4 and out.h = self+0x6 passed through unchanged. So position is anchor-relative and scroll-displaced while size is not, which is the standard scrolling-viewport arrangement. +0x12c F0x8001e028(self,r,g,b) writes three bytes at self+0x19/+0x1a/+0x1b and derives a boolean at self+0x18 that is 1 if and only if the bitwise OR of the three, masked to 8 bits, is non-zero - an all-channels-zero triple disables the effect.
claims.notes: Lead re-verified F0x8001e0c8 against raw MIPS at fns.s L15482-L15502 independently of the worker packet: the loads are lhu at +0/+0x6c/+0x2/+0x6e, the scroll loads are lw at +0x70/+0x74, the shift is sra 8 (SIGNED, so negative scroll works), and +0x4/+0x6 are copied with no arithmetic. NOT established: that the +0x19/+0x1a/+0x1b byte triple in +0x12c is literally R,G,B in that channel order - the ordering is inferred from the store order and from class-wide pattern, with no call site passing a known colour constant yet examined. Class B installs DIFFERENT functions than class A over the same +0x110..+0x168 offset range, so none of these readings transfer to a class-A receiver.
claims.frontier_rationale: Class B is the second-largest instance dispatch table in the corpus (UI-DISPATCH-CENSUS-COMPLETE-001) and shares the high-traffic +0x110..+0x168 offsets with class A, so its slots must be named before any slot in that range can be attributed from a call site alone.

claims.statement: Four slots of the F0x8001e5bc widget class (class B) implement a sorted, sentinel-headed callback queue, which is the class's actual behavioural engine. +0x148 F0x8001e1e8(self, capacity) allocates capacity*0x14 bytes through the allocator D0x8004b5f4, stores the block at self+0x80 and the capacity at self+0x78, then calls the shared reset helper F0x8001e19c(self), which writes a sentinel head record (key 0x7fffffff, payload 0, callback 0, next 0) and sets the live count self+0x7c to 1. Each record is 0x14 bytes: +0 s32 sort key, +4 payload word, +8 callback function pointer, +0xc callback first argument, +0x10 next pointer. +0x14c F0x8001e240(self, callback, callbackArg, key, payload) is the SORTED insert: if self+0x7c is below the capacity self+0x78 it fills the next free record, then walks the list from self+0x80 following the +0x10 next pointers, comparing each node's key against the new key, and splices the record in so the list stays in ascending key order, finally incrementing self+0x7c. +0x150 F0x8001e324(self, callback, callbackArg) appends an UNSORTED record into the same array with key, payload and next all zeroed. +0x154 F0x8001e38c(self) is the DISPATCH: when self+0x7c is non-zero it walks the list from self+0x80 and, for every node whose +0x8 callback pointer is non-null, calls it as callback(node+0xc, self, node+0x4) - so every queued callback receives its own argument, the widget itself, and its payload - and after the walk calls F0x8001e19c(self) to reset the queue back to sentinel-only. The queue is therefore drained and emptied in one pass, keyed order, once per dispatch.
claims.notes: Lead re-verified F0x8001e38c against raw MIPS at fns.s L15683-L15714: the guard is lw +0x7c / beqz, the head is lw +0x80, the null-callback test is lw +0x8 / beqz, the call is jalr with a0 from +0xc, a2 from +0x4 and a1 from the receiver in the delay slot, the loop reload is lw +0x10, and the tail call is jal F0x8001e19c. F0x8001e01c at +0x144 was also re-verified: it is a two-instruction pure getter returning the word at self+0x68, which means the corpus-wide hot slot +0x144 has DIFFERENT arity and meaning on class B (0-argument getter) than on class A (1-byte visibility setter, UI-WIDGETCLASS-AE38-CONSUMER-001) - direct confirmation that this offset cannot be attributed from the offset alone. NOT established: what the ordering key at record+0 represents (draw priority, time, or list position), and the purpose of the conditional word write at record-0x4 inside F0x8001e324 (fns.s L15671), which is read verbatim but unexplained.
claims.frontier_rationale: Names four of the 13 remaining class-B slots and settles the arity conflict on +0x144, the single highest-traffic unresolved slot offset in the corpus.

claims.statement: Packed-id bit 30 selects a single global 'exclusive track' register at D0x800519ec+0x4248 (aliased D0x80055c34), not a plain dedup test. F0x8002006c loads the register (0x80020100), and when it already holds this exact id returns without retriggering. When it holds a DIFFERENT non-zero id, the function loads a stop callback from the channel record at +0x427c (0x80020118) and calls it (0x80020120) on that old id before storing the new id into the register (0x80020128) and playing. A sound reaching the end of its sample does not clear it.

claims.statement: Past the bank lookup, F0x8002006c's exclusive-track gate at 0x800200f4 tests bit 30 of the packed id ($s2). If clear, it skips straight to path selection (0x8002012c) and always plays. If set, it compares the new packed id against a single global latch at D0x800519ec+0x4248 (not indexed by channel): if the latch already holds this exact id, the function returns 0 immediately without triggering any playback call (the sound is already the recorded exclusive track); otherwise, if the latch held a different non-zero id, it calls a stop-function pointer stored at D0x800519ec+0x427c with the old id as its argument, then overwrites the latch with the new id and falls through to actually play it. This implements a 'one exclusive track already playing, do not restart it' rule distinct from the always-retrigger behavior of a bit-30-clear (non-exclusive) sound.

claims.statement: The resident sound API exposes two different stops through its pointer table in shipped data: D0x80055c68 -> F0x800202d4 and D0x80055c6c -> F0x8002037c. Both take a packed id, resolve its channel through F0x80020030, and act on the row field at +0x4208. F0x800202d4 stops the sound at once by calling F0x800335b4 (the same routine the play path uses to seize the slot). F0x8002037c instead calls F0x800306e0 (0x80020404) with a step of 0x80 and a duration chosen by the video-mode flag D0x8005ccac, and F0x800306e0 hands F0x80033e1c the NEGATED step, writing a per-tick downward volume delta and a duration into the voice record - a fade-out rather than a cut. claims.statement: For the player-side FIGHTSTG_F0x8009fab4 path, the routine loads the skill +0x2 power, computes floor(50*attacker_effective(+0x6)/defender_effective(+0x6))+50, multiplies that by the skill power, divides by 100, then bounds the result to [floor(power/2), 2*power].
claims.notes: This is a source-derived correction candidate for the player-side base stage only. The checked decompilation is cross-anchored by original assembly instructions. The enemy-side scaling and the later field, affinity, critical, armor, and final-cap stages are outside this claim.
claims.frontier_rationale: Rosetta pilot evidence repair: this bounded formula correction is not a catalog frontier.

claims.statement: F0x8009fab4 uses the separate F0x800a0514 magical-critical roll. Its chance term is min(0x40, trunc(4 * skill[+0x08] * 9 / defender effective element)), followed by +0x40 instead of +4 when skill[+0x09] matches defender effective +0x25, then the three record-intensity contributions from the +0x1c status-bit field. On success the magical damage leaf adds running_damage * ((RAND_U16 & 0x3f) + 0x20) / 0x40. The engine implements the scalar and target-family terms and accepts the intensity sum as an optional input; the upstream mapping of those three intensity bytes into the browser combatant remains unimplemented.
claims.notes: Direct authority-2 assembly read. The optional intensity sum is exposed as magicalCritStatusBonus because Combatant does not yet carry the original record +0x1c/+0x1d/+0x1e/+0x1f fields as a decoded structure.
claims.frontier_rationale: The arithmetic is statically decoded; the remaining partial status reflects only the browser data-model boundary for the three record-intensity terms, not an unread branch in the magical damage leaf.

claims.frontier_rationale: Narrows the documented open player-side magical affinity stage to the source-visible element curve without asserting a player-facing name for the raw defender field.

claims.statement: Every card record's artwork is a standard PS1 TIM beginning at record+0x0C. exe/fns.s F0x8001e890 loads the card-record pointer from the card object and passes record+0xC to the context method installed at +0x20 by F0x8001ffa8, which is F0x8001fd50: it reads the word at +4 as TIM flags, tests bit 3 for a CLUT block and bits 0..2 for the bpp code, then for each block builds a RECT from {dx, dy, w, h} at block+4..+11 and calls LoadImage with block+0xC as the data pointer, advancing by the block's own u32 byte length. Every catalog record matches that shape exactly: +0x0C = 0x10 (the TIM magic, which is why that word is constant across all 316 records), +0x10 = 0x09 (bpp code 1 = 8bpp, bit 3 = CLUT present), CLUT block length 0x20C = 12 + 256 colours x 2 with dimensions 256x1, then an image block of length 0x40C = 12 + 1024 with w = 16 sixteen-bit units (= 32 pixels at 8bpp) and h = 32. The totals close with no slack: 8 + 524 + 1036 = 1568 = exactly the record space from +0x0C to the 1580-byte stride. So each of the 316 cards carries its own 32x32 8bpp icon with a private 256-entry BGR555 palette, colour index 0 transparent. All 316 decode without a single header exception; extracted by tools/extract_card_catalog.py to web/assets/cards/card_icons.png. This supersedes the earlier reading in this session's extractor that the trailing bytes were an undecoded encoded payload - that test failed only because it measured the CLUT as if it were pixel rows.

The 0x8D machine's helpers: F0x8008AD58 is a one-call wrapper whose result (F0x80089ED4 = 8*max(side-0 count, side-1 count)+0xE, the larger count clamped to at least 3) step 1 stores to duel+0x42C; F0x8008AD78 is a wrapper over F0x80089F18(duel, view, region, delta), the board-cursor mover — it plays packed sound 0x0004001B (SYSTEM06, the decoded cursor blip) on every call, maps region 0/1/2 to record base 0/6/0xC (your field / their field / played row), clears the old record's highlight bit (+0x150 bit0) and busy halfword (+0x12E), then adds delta to the cursor duel+0x43C; F0x80086A18 is a four-store view reset (view+0xE32 halfword and words +0xE34, +0xE4C, +0xE64, +0xE7C to zero). View method identities from the decoded view struct (docs/research/card/cardduel.h:239-282): +0xEB0 refreshGroup, +0xEC4 closeOverlay, +0xECC beginScreen, +0xEC8 resetScreen, +0xF14 placeSlot, +0xF1C revealSlot, +0xF24 scaleSlot, +0xF3C setSlotCard; slot record +0x12E busy, +0x14A progress, +0x150 bit0 highlighted.

claims.statement: The shared convergence at 0x80085ce8 in pro/cardgame stores a CONSTANT 2 into the duel object's step-complete flag at duel+0x2F4, not the return value of whatever routine the handler just called. The convergence itself is `j 0x80085dc8` with `sb $v0, 0x2f4($s1)` in its delay slot, so it stores whatever $v0 holds on arrival; and each handler that reaches it does so via `j 0x80085ce8` whose own branch delay slot is `li $v0, 0x2`, which executes even though the branch is taken and therefore overwrites the callee's returned $v0 before the store observes it. Across the whole overlay there are 31 jump sites targeting 0x80085ce8 and the delay slot of every one of them is `li $v0, 0x2`, so no handler routes a callee result through this convergence. Consequence: for the eligibility-scan opcode families, the scanner's boolean result does NOT gate step completion through duel+0x2F4 -- these steps mark themselves complete with the fixed value 2 once fired. Whether the scan result influences the duel by some other path was not established here.
claims.coverage: The universal 'every one of them' was tested by exhaustive enumeration of the denominator, not sampled: all 31 lines in /home/dorij/ddw3/asm/dw2003/pro/cardgame.s containing `j 0x80085ce8` were collected and the immediately following line (the branch delay slot) was read for each; tallying those 31 delay slots yields exactly one distinct instruction, `li $v0, 0x2`, with count 31 and no other value. A single differing delay slot would have appeared as a second entry in that tally, which is the check that would have exposed a counterexample. Scope limit: this covers jumps written as the literal text `j 0x80085ce8` in this one overlay's assembly; a register-computed jump to the same address, or a fall-through entry from the preceding instruction at 0x80085ce4, is not covered by that text match -- though 0x80085ce4 is itself `li $v0, 0x2` (EV-CQ2-TAIL-SETV0), so the fall-through path delivers the same constant.

claims.statement: For the opcode family 0x5E through 0x69 (docs/research/card/card-battle-complete-model-2026-08-06.md section G.3), the shared enter-phase callee F0x8008DEF8 does more than G.3 states, in two respects. (1) View split: after adding the packed amount to a flagged field slot's AP/HP target it calls the view struct's method at +0xF30 when its fourth argument (held in $s7) is 0, and the method at +0xF34 otherwise, passing the slot index; the branch is `bnez $s7` at 0x8008e374, so mode 0 takes +0xF30 and any non-zero mode takes +0xF34. (2) Destroy override: $s8 is loaded with the constant 2 at 0x8008e2c8, and both of the routine's slot families guard an extra store on `bne $s7, $s8`, i.e. on mode == 2. Under that guard the routine overwrites the AP target it has just updated with the NEGATED value of a neighbouring halfword in the same slot, rather than leaving the plain amount addition in place. The two families use different bases and offsets and are structurally identical: the first negates +0x734 over +0x730 relative to $s1, the second negates +0x7a6 over +0x7a2 relative to $a0 = $s2 + $s3. Neither the view-method split nor the destroy override appears in G.3, which lists only the packed amount and a 'mode' column. What the negated field means, and whether the result is a guaranteed knockout, is NOT established here: the field is named by offset and width only.

claims.statement: In pro/cardgame:F0x8008d854 the per-element counter byte at +0xC of the record the function indexes is incremented only while it is strictly below 99 (unsigned), so it saturates at 99 and never reaches 100. The load, the unsigned compare, the branch that skips the store, and the byte store all address the same +0xC byte; when the compare fails the byte is left unchanged rather than being written with a clamped value.
claims.coverage: The claim is scoped to the single function F0x8008d854 and to the single counter byte at +0xC; it is NOT a claim about every element counter in the overlay. The quantifier 'never reaches 100' was tested by reading the only path that writes the byte in this function: the store at 0x8008d8f8 is reached only by falling through the beqz at 0x8008d8f0, and the whole function was disassembled (0x8008d854..0x8008d918) to confirm there is no second store to +0xC. Scope of the shape elsewhere was enumerated, not assumed: `code-search 'sltiu $v0, $v1, 0x63' --corpus original` returns exactly 4 hits, all in pro/cardgame.s (0x8008d8ec, 0x8008f3fc, 0x80090660, 0x80090f7c). Only 0x8008d8ec was read. The other three, and the five signed-compare sites the decompilation shows in F0x8008e08c and F0x800a2f00, are NOT covered by this claim.
limitations: What the counter COUNTS is not established here. The plain-language description at docs/research/card/cardgame-plain-descriptions.md:104 calls it a per-element counter for a side at confidence 'med', and this claim corroborates only its cap, not that reading of its purpose.

claims.statement: The card-battle catalog is NOT an overlay table: it is the five disc files CARDPAK0..4.BIN, reached through the resident selector exe/fns.s F0x8001e7ec (the method installed at +0x2c by F0x8001ebf8, which every card front-end calls before reading a record). F0x8001e7ec computes block = (id-1) >> 6 and indexes the five-word table at D0x8004dfb8, whose values are 0x7f6..0x7fa = LBA_CARDPAK0..4_BIN_IDX (rust/dw2003_exe_data/src/lba.rs L2041-2045); the slot arithmetic on (id-1) & 0x3f multiplies by exactly 1580. File sizes confirm the stride with no slack: 4 x 101120 (64 x 1580) + 94800 (60 x 1580) = 316 records, matching the 316-string escardnm name bank one-for-one. Record header: +0x00 colour (6 values, 43/43/43/43/43/41 over the 256 Digimon cards), +0x01 AP, +0x02 HP, +0x03 kind (0x10 = Digimon, 1..8 = Program-card category), +0x04 Program cost, +0x05 summon tier, +0x06 evolution stage (2 Rookie / 3 Champion / 4 Ultimate / 5 Mega, counts 46/96/60/54), +0x07 always 0, +0x08 and +0x0a unresolved u16s, +0x0c..+0x1f constant image descriptor, +0x20..+0x62b card artwork (1548 bytes, geometry NOT decoded). AP/HP validate against the source material: Agumon 5/3 Rookie, Greymon 20/20 Champion, MetalGreymon 34/32 Ultimate, WarGreymon 52/52 Mega. Extracted by tools/extract_card_catalog.py to web/assets/data/card_catalog.json.

The catalog holds 316 records but stcrdshp's folder-grid draw validates a card id with (id-1) < 0x13a, admitting only 1..314 (claim cardgame-catalog-valid-id-range-1-314). The two records past that bound are exactly the two the collection cannot contain: 315 Calumon and 316 Impmon, and they are the only cards outside 1..314 with AP 0 and HP 0. Calumon being id 315 is corroborated by escardgm.toml's Start Phase prompt, which is literally 'Draw Calumon to go first.' - i.e. the Start Phase draws a card that is deliberately not part of any folder. This resolves the '315-card catalog vs 314-id bound' discrepancy that cardgame-catalog-valid-id-range-1-314 recorded without resolving: the catalog has 316 records, 314 of them collectable.

The CARDPAK card record's byte +0x06 is a 0..5 level index. cardgame.s .L0x00003fe0 selects a card record, loads +0x06, bounds it with `sltiu $v0, $v1, 0x6` and jumps through the six-entry table at 0x80083294 to choose the LV plate graphic written to ctx+0xe64. escardgm.toml carries exactly five level names - In-Training, Rookie, Champion, Ultimate, Mega - beside its 'LV' label, and the extracted catalog's +0x06 column takes the values 2..5 over the collectible Digimon, so the index reads 1 In-Training, 2 Rookie, 3 Champion, 4 Ultimate, 5 Mega.

claims.statement: The five constants 0x45/0x70/0x9B/0xC6/0xF1 matched in stcrdshp's CARD DETAIL/CONFIRM popup draw F0x80083ba8 - left unexplained in docs/research/ui/stcrdshp-decoded-2026-07-12.md and only guessed at by claim cardgame-shop-confirm-plate-five-cardid-match - are card IDs 69, 112, 155, 198, 241, and those are exactly the five catalog records carrying summon-tier byte +0x05 = 4, the only value above the 0..3 that tracks evolution stage. One falls in each colour block, which is why they are evenly spaced by 0x2b. So the popup gives a distinct confirm plate to the five top-tier cards. This upgrades the earlier reading from plausible-but-unproven to a match against decoded record data. Two of the five (69 RosemonII and 198 Gryphonmon) carry AP 0 and HP 0, which is not yet explained.

The three hold states are pure timers that drive the card effect clip runs. State 8 (F0x8009a540) runs 10 frames with effect selector +0x47 = 2 and hands over to state 11; states 9 and 10 (F0x8009a5b0 with arguments 0x24 and 0x1C) run 0x24 and 0x1C frames with +0x47 = 3 and 4 and return to idle. All of them clear +0x47 on completion. The command at 0x8009C7F8 writes selector 3 alongside state 9 and selector 4 alongside state 10, so state and selector are always consistent. The 0x24 and 0x1C durations are exactly the end points of effect clip runs 3 and 4 as decoded from F0x8009a998 ((t >> 1) % 9 ending at t == 0x24 and (t >> 1) % 7 ending at t == 0x1C), which is what pairs each state with its clip run. State 11 (settle) counts in +0x2C rather than +0x28, and the active border F0x8009b76c draws board clip 9 only for state 11 at CLUT row (+0x2C / 2) % 5.

F0x80098864(count, index) returns (count < 7 ? 0x2900 : 0xF600 / count) * index, and the row layout helper 0x8009CE94 places sprite i of a run at rowX + F0x80098864(count, i) with all of them sharing one row y, either constructing them through 0x8009C510 or moving them there through 0x8009C9A0. The card pitch is therefore 41.0 pixels (0x2900 in 8.8) for rows of up to six cards, and from seven cards up the pitch becomes 0xF600 / count, so the cards overlap rather than running off the 320 pixel screen. The row SPAN is (0xF600 / count) * (count - 1), which is strictly below 246.0 pixels and approaches it as the count grows - 0xF600 is the fixed dividend, not an exact row width. The row ORIGINS this offset is added to are NOT decoded: 0x8009CE94 takes them as arguments and no jal instruction and no pointer-table word anywhere in the original assembly reaches 0x8009CE94, the single textual match for that address being an unrelated instruction in pro/fightstg.s, which shares the 0x80082CB0 overlay load base.
claims.notes: Reviewed twice 2026-08-05. The second review returned decision=accept but recommended_status=partially_verified, so the promotion gate is NOT satisfied and the claim correctly rests at partially_verified. Its residual objections: the negative-search entry does not quote its exact query string, and a literal-text search cannot rule out a register-constructed indirect call - the statement is scoped to 'no jal and no pointer-table word' and concludes only that the row ORIGINS remain undecoded. Full verdict recorded at docs/research/evidence/reviews/cardanim-fanout-pitch-41px.review.json. The caller identification, the negative-search methodology, and the corrected row-span arithmetic were all verified.

claims.statement: The card flip (state 4, animator F0x8009a75c) runs 12 frames with scale_x = 0x1000 - F0x8002abcc((t << 12) / 24, (t << 12) / 6), sweeping the card's width 1.0 -> 0 -> 1.0 as a half sine, and at t >= 7 performs unk45 ^= 3 on the sprite's render kind exactly once. Because that XOR pairs render kind 1 with render kind 2, card-sheet clip 0x10 (kind 2) is the REVERSE of a Digimon card face rather than a separate card type; the same XOR would map kind 3 to 0, so kind 3 is nobody's reverse. This supersedes the provisional 'program' and 'back' labels assigned to kinds 2 and 3 by the 2026-08-05 screen decode, which were inferred from clip content alone with nothing tying the pair together. UNRESOLVED: that same screen decode also routes Program cards to clip 0x10, so either the Program-card mapping is wrong or clip 0x10 is not a plain card back; nothing decoded settles which.
claims.notes: The sine helper is called with TWO arguments in the decompilation, F0x8002abcc((t << 12) / 24, (t << 12) / 6); earlier prose abbreviated this to a single-argument rsin(). The UNRESOLVED clause about clip 0x10 versus the Program-card mapping is deliberately retained and is why this claim is not a candidate for promotion.

claims.statement: The card move (states 2 and 3) is a plain LINEAR tween. Both states' jump-table entries hold the word 0x8009b8e0, a thunk that jals the animator F0x80099ffc. Its timer +0x28 counts DOWN to zero (reduced on each invocation by the value returned through the resident pointer at 0x8004DF9C, with the interpolation branch taken only while the remainder is positive), and it computes cur = dest - (dest - start) * timer / duration, applied to position (+0x00/+0x04 against +0x08/+0x0C and +0x10/+0x14) and to scale (+0x18/+0x1A against +0x1C/+0x1E and +0x20/+0x22). There is no easing curve, lookup table, or squared term anywhere in the function. CORRECTION (2026-08-05 review): the guards are PAIRWISE, not per axis. The position guard skips only when x AND y both already equal their destinations (bne at .L0x00017388 falls into the update, beq at .L0x0001739c skips), and the scale guard is a single 32-bit compare of +0x18 against +0x1C spanning both halfword axes (.L0x00017400-.L0x0001740c), so a settled axis is still recomputed whenever its partner differs. On expiry it snaps position and scale to their destinations, writes state 1 to +0x42, zeroes timer and duration, and clears the +0x26 draw-layer field when +0x48 is zero - with a HALFWORD store (sh $zr, 0x26), not a byte store. States 2 and 3 differ in exactly one respect: the completion call through 0x80055C48 (argument 0x800460BD) is gated on +0x42 != 3, so state 3 skips it. No other branch in the function tests +0x42. NOT ESTABLISHED by this claim's evidence: the identity of the function at 0x80055C48, so the skipped call is named by address rather than described as a sound.
claims.notes: Reviewed twice (ddw3-claim-reviewer, then ddw3-claim-reviewer-deep). The deep review REJECTED the previous statement on two demonstrated errors, both re-derived and confirmed against the assembly: the interpolation guards are pairwise rather than per axis, and +0x26 is cleared with a halfword store. Both are corrected above. Remains partially_verified: review budget for this bundle is spent, and the identity of the call at 0x80055C48 is still unevidenced.

claims.statement: The two hit shakes each run 12 frames (both animators bound their counter with slti $v1, 0xc) and restore the sprite's rest position and scale on completion. State 7 (F0x8009a454) offsets x by table[t & 7] from 0x800A5AC8 and STRETCHES the card, adding the sine result shifted right by 4 to the unity scale 0x1000; on completion it restores the single position field +0x10 and writes 0x1000 back to the scale field +0x1a. State 6 (F0x8009a62c) offsets x by table[t & 7] from 0x800A5AD0, additionally offsets y by table[globalFrameCounter & 7] so its vertical jitter is not a function of the sprite's own timer, and SQUASHES the card, subtracting the sine result shifted right by 3 from 0x1000 - the opposite direction and exactly twice the magnitude; on completion it restores both position fields +0x10 and +0x14. Both bases are formed by lui 0x800a plus a positive addiu in the assembly. The tables are eight signed halfwords each and OVERLAP, since 0x800A5AC8 + 8 == 0x800A5AD0: the x table is -256, 768, -768, 256, -1024, 512, -512, 1024 and the xy table is -1024, 512, -512, 1024, 12, 0, 28, 0. The index is masked & 7, so the original does read all eight halfwords of each. The offsets are added to the position fields +0x00/+0x04, which F0x8009b76c draws at >>8, so the table values are 8.8 pixels.
claims.notes: Reviewed twice. Both reviews re-derived and CONFIRMED every substantive clause - table bases, all sixteen halfwords, the four-entry overlap, the 12-frame bounds, the stretch/squash shift asymmetry, and the asymmetric completion restores. The second review returned needs_evidence solely because the & 7 index masks, the offset-application stores, and state 6's y-index source had no citing locator; those entries are now added. Remains partially_verified because the two-review budget for this bundle is spent, not because any clause was contradicted.

claims.statement: The duel's two displayed card plates do not jump to a new value. On each invocation of the per-card update, the BYTES at +0x43 and +0x44 are compared against target HALFWORDS at duel+0x734 and duel+0x736 (indexed per card, not fixed cells); when a value already equals its target the update is skipped, and otherwise it is stepped by exactly plus or minus one toward it, so the plates roll to their new totals over successive updates rather than snapping. Render kind 1 draws the two values as two sequential number plates via F0x80096a94 at the card's own coordinates, +0x43 first and +0x44 second, SIDE BY SIDE: both calls use the same y, (+0x04 >> 8) + 0x21, and differ only in x, (+0x00 >> 8) + 4 versus (+0x00 >> 8) + 0x17. NOT ESTABLISHED by this claim's evidence: which plate is AP and which is HP (draw order alone does not label them), and the invocation cadence - the cited code proves the per-call step, not that the handler runs once per rendered frame.
claims.notes: Reviewed 2026-08-05: the mechanism (byte vs halfword, skip-on-equal, exact +/-1 step) was fully confirmed against the assembly. The unproven 'each frame' cadence and the AP/HP labelling were removed from the statement and recorded as explicit gaps. A second review then CONTRADICTED an upper/lower plate description added during that same correction: both draw calls share the y offset +0x21 and differ only in x, so the plates are side by side. That geometry is now corrected from the cited decompilation. The +/-1 step mechanism has been independently confirmed against the assembly by two separate reviews; the claim rests at partially_verified because the corrected statement has not itself been through a review and the two-review budget for this bundle is spent.

claims.statement: The summon (state 5, animator F0x8009a1a0) has three legs. While +0x30 is positive an intro grows both scales as 0x1C00 - t * 0xC0; on expiry it sets +0x48 |= 5, pins the current and start scales to 0x1C00 and arms the destination scale to 0x1200. The travel leg then runs the ordinary linear tween on both axes plus an arc added to y: arc = F0x8002abcc((t << 12) / (duration * 2), ...) * 0x1C00, negated when the destination y is greater than the start y, then y += arc >> 12 - and the sign flip makes the hop always bow away from the direction of travel. CONDITIONAL: the peak height is 28.0 pixels against the 8.8 position format IF the sine helper F0x8002ac08 returns a Q12 magnitude (peak 0x1000). That amplitude is NOT established here - F0x8002ac08 reads its peak from the table at D0x80056088, which lives in the EXE data segment the disassembly does not carry, so the 28 pixel figure rests on the Q12 convention and not on a read table value. The arc's shape, sign and 0x1C00 multiplier are established independently of it. On expiry the start and destination swap, the destination scale flattens to 0x1000, +0x48 &= 0xFA, the state becomes 2, and the duration becomes duration * 2 + duration / 2, so the return leg runs at 2.5x the length of the throw.
claims.notes: Reviewed 2026-08-05: every clause - intro grow, expiry handoff, travel tween, the arc negation direction, and the return-leg swap/flatten/state-2/2.5x duration - was independently re-derived from both the decompilation and the matching assembly at cardgame.s offset 0x174f0 and confirmed. The ONLY open item is the sine amplitude behind the 28 pixel figure, which is unobtainable statically because the sine table D0x80056088 is in the EXE data segment the disassembly does not carry; the statement now marks that figure conditional. A second review then found a real defect inherited from the original pass: evidence cardanim-summon-arc-amplitude cited the intro branch's li $s0, 0x1c00 (L23889) as the arc multiplier and asserted constant reuse between the legs. Re-derived and confirmed wrong - L23883's blez skips that instruction on the travel leg. The multiplier is synthesized at L23966-L23968 as (v0<<3 - v0)<<10 = v0*0x1C00; a corrected evidence entry was added and the old summary amended. The 0x1C00 VALUE was never in doubt.

claims.statement: Card motion in the duel is a twelve-state animation machine driven by code, not authored position data. F0x8009bac8 steps all 40 pooled 0x4C-byte card sprites (duel+0x108..duel+0xCE7, walked from offset 0xC9C down in steps of -0x4C) every frame through F0x8009b890, then draws the pool TWICE in two layer passes selected on the sprite's +0x26 byte: the first pass draws only sprites whose +0x26 is non-zero, the second only those whose +0x26 is zero. F0x8009b890 loads the sprite's +0x42 byte, bound-checks it against 12, and dispatches through the 12-entry jump table at 0x80083748 (formed as lui 0x8008 + addiu 0x3748 and indexed by sll 2), so the state space is exactly 0..11. The table's entries for states 2 and 3 are the same word (0x8009b8e0), a thunk that jals F0x80099ffc - direct evidence that those two states share one animator rather than merely resembling each other. Sprite positions +0x00/+0x04 are 8.8 fixed point, drawn at >>8, and the scale fields +0x18/+0x1A are expressed against a unity constant of 0x1000. The BEHAVIOUR of each individual state is carried by the sibling cardanim-* claims and is deliberately not asserted here.

Combo runs are announced on screen, one message per run, and the two sides get different messages: the first side's scan issues effect opcode 0x19 and the second side's issues 0x1A, each written to the pending-opcode latch duel+0x421 so the interpreter runs it, rather than being drawn directly. A third opcode, 0x1B, is issued repeatedly while the counter at duel+0x304 is set, once per unit of duel+0x305, which the state decrements each time it runs.
claims.coverage: The three banner ids were read at their own store sites inside this machine, and the latch they are written to is the same duel+0x421 the rest of the overlay uses for a pending message. The claim does not say what the messages read; the message ids are not resolved against the language file here, and the combo arithmetic that produces the runs is already decoded elsewhere and was not re-read.
limitations: What duel+0x304 and duel+0x305 count is not established here.
Static reading only; not observed in the running game.

The state plays packed sound 0x009C0002, creates a mid-grey overlay - all three colour arguments 0x80 - with a life of ten, and then runs the winner's set counter for fifty-one ticks of the resident frame delta, accumulated into duel+0x2FC, before it moves on.

claims.statement: A set is awarded by comparing the two sides' total HP on the field, and a tie does not go to the player. The Battle-Phase machine loads side 0's total from duel+0x59E and side 1's from duel+0x666 and tests whether side 1's is strictly less than side 0's. Only that case writes 0 to the set winner duel+0x301 and keeps effect opcode 0x18; every other case, equal totals included, writes 1 and issues opcode 0x17 instead.
claims.coverage: The comparison's direction and its branch were read as instructions, with the delay slot: the banner 0x18 load sits in the branch's delay slot and therefore executes on both paths, so the two outcomes are distinguished by which store follows, not by which constant is loaded. Reading the delay slot as belonging only to the taken path inverts this table, which is the trap this overlay has already produced once. The claim covers the two arms of this one comparison and does not describe the states that surround it.
limitations: This anchors what section D.5 of the model document already described from decompiled C; the reading agrees, and this pass raises it to original assembly.
Static reading only; not observed in the running game.
