claims.notes: WORDING CORRECTED 2026-08-21, same day, for the same reason as cardduel-playing-a-card-is-pick-confirm-commit-with-a-take-back-2026-08-21: the values written to duel+0x421 are effect-VM opcodes, not message ids. The HP comparison, its direction, the delay-slot reading and the tie outcome are unchanged; only the name given to 0x17 and 0x18 is corrected. Re-reviewed after the change.

claims.statement: duel+0x41B is a slot index measured from the opponent's current draw position, not a count of admitted deck entries. F0x8009D9E4 starts its scan at duel+0x668, the side-1 deck read cursor, advances while the slot's group byte is not greater than 2*duel[0x300]+2, stops at slot 0x28 at the latest, and stores the slot index it stopped on. At duel start the cursor is zero, which is where an index and a count coincide, and is why the count reading held.
claims.coverage: Read from the scan's own initial load - duel+0x668 is the side-1 block's +0x04 field per model document section E.3 - and from its terminal store, not from surrounding prose. This refines the wording of model document section E.5; searching the ledger for 0x41B returns no claim that states the count reading, so nothing recorded is contradicted.
limitations: Static reading only; not observed in the running game.
claims.notes: Rests at partially_verified. The scan's initial load and terminal store are anchored; the loop body that advances the index is not. Missing artifact for promotion: .L0x0001ad58 through .L0x0001ad78 quoted.

claims.statement: The claim cardduel-424-is-the-step-frame-tick-2026-08-28 cited L7462, L7466 and L7616 as the lines where F0x8008A068 zeroes duel+0x424 alongside +0x428 and +0x434. Those three lines contain no such store: L7462 is a register move, L7466 is a nop, and L7616 is an unrelated bound check on the step value. The real reset is at L7470-L7473. The conclusion that +0x424 is a frame tick survives and is re-recorded, correctly cited and narrowed, as cardduel-424-step-frame-tick-corrected-2026-08-28.
claims.contradiction_rationale: Three line citations in the statement prose were wrong. The packet's own evidence entries were all correct, because each was printed from the file before it was written down; these three numbers were typed into the statement by hand and nothing checked them. Found by an independent review, not by the author.
limitations: A review rejected cardduel-424-is-the-step-frame-tick-2026-08-28 for three bad line citations in its statement. The rejection was checked against the assembly by the lead and is correct. The claim is superseded here rather than defended.
The delegate that produced the 25 slot rows was NOT trusted for arithmetic; every address was recomputed from the file's own instruction encodings.

claims.statement: Replace 'at L7462/L7466 and L7616 the same routine zeroes it together with +0x428 and +0x434 when it changes step' with 'at L7470-L7473 it zeroes +0x424 together with +0x428 and +0x434; L7483-L7486 zeroes +0x424 and +0x428 and sets +0x434 to 2; L7561-L7563 zeroes +0x424 and +0x428 again - all as the step cases complete.'
claims.coverage: Scoped deliberately to F0x8008A068. The increment-and-compare shape was read at authority 2 at the cited lines; the claim does NOT assert this role for +0x424 in any other routine. || Isolated review 2026-10-05 (docs/research/evidence/reviews/card-battle-2026-10-05.json): The tick clause re-derives exactly, and the zeroing clause is substantively right but mis-cites its lines. F0x8008A068 = file 0x73B8 (prologue L7413; next prologue 0x80A8). Tick: L7680 .L0x000077e4 lw $v0,0x424($s3); L7682 addiu $v0,0x1; L7683 sw $v0,0x424($s3); L7684 slti $v0,0xb - loaded, incremented by one, stored back, compared against 11 - exactly as stated (the compare's 'less than 11' then  Anchors re-read: cardgame.s L7413-7505 and L7596-7700 (F0x8008A068: tick block and all stores to +0x424/+0x428/+0x434 in the function extent [0x73B8,0x80A8]); sha256 0e26d0d5...; Function extent check: prologues at 0x73B8, 0x80A8, 0x80C8, 0x80E8 bound F0x8008A068.
limitations: Whether +0x424 carries the same role in every routine that touches it is NOT established. The decompiled corpus shows 228 uses over 53 files and only F0x8008A068 was read at authority 2.

claims.statement: In F0x8008A068, duel+0x424 is a frame tick and not a step index: at cardgame.s L7680-L7684 it is loaded, incremented by one, stored back, and compared against 11, and at L7470-L7473 the routine zeroes it as it leaves a step. The reset is NOT uniform across the routine's exits and the earlier statement that it is zeroed together with +0x428 and +0x434 holds at only one of three sites: L7470-L7473 zeroes +0x428, +0x424 and +0x434; L7483-L7486 zeroes +0x428 and +0x424 but stores a NON-zero value into +0x434; L7561-L7563 zeroes +0x428 and +0x424 only. At two of those three sites the final store sits in a jump's branch delay slot, so an in-order reading undercounts them.
claims.coverage: The three reset sites were enumerated by scanning the routine's whole extent, L7413 to its end, for stores to 0x424, 0x428, 0x42C and 0x434, rather than by reading forward from the increment. That scan is what produced the two variants that falsify the uniform reading. The quantifier 'one of three' is over the reset sites inside F0x8008A068 only, and says nothing about the other 52 files that touch +0x424.
limitations: Scoped to F0x8008A068. The field has 228 uses over 53 files and the role was read in this routine only.
The units of the bound 11 are not established as frames; the routine compares a counter it increments once per call, and what calls it was not read.

claims.statement: In F0x80088F78 the four duel fields +0x428, +0x42C, +0x430 and +0x434 are pushed to the view's counter setter (slot +0xEA0) as four consecutive calls whose (side, arm) pairs are (0,8), (0,9), (1,8) and (1,9): cardgame.s L6583-L6604, where each arm number is passed in the jalr's branch delay slot. The four fields are therefore per-side pairs of the same two counters, one pair per player, and NOT four unrelated accumulators.
claims.coverage: Scoped to the four consecutive call sites read at authority 2 in F0x80088F78. The side and arm arguments were taken from the delay slots, which an in-order reading would have missed.
limitations: Which HUD element arms 8 and 9 drive rests on the animation atlas of 2026-08-26, which is authority 5 research prose with no anchor. This claim deliberately does not name them the AP and HP plaques.
Read only in F0x80088F78; other writers of these four fields were not read.

claims.statement: In F0x8008C8D8 duel+0x440 holds an INDEX, not a result code: the routine scans the eligible array at duel+0x446 from the start index at +0x668 up to the bound at +0x41B, stores the index of the first non-zero entry into duel+0x440 (cardgame.s L10014), and then writes 1 into the array at duel+0x46F at that same index (L10044, in the jr $ra delay slot). This supports the reading in CARD-DUEL-VERIFIED section 7.1 that +0x440 is the committed selection cursor, and does not support the gloss the card-battle model document gives it under opcode 0x9E, where it is called the draw-result code.
claims.coverage: Scoped to F0x8008C8D8. The contradiction between the two existing documents is reported, not resolved for every site: the claim states which of the two this one routine supports.
limitations: This does not establish that +0x440 carries the cursor role everywhere. F0x80089974 compares +0x440 against +0x434 and then writes 0 or 1 into it, which reads as a boolean at that site, so field reuse across routines remains open and is exactly the documented one-field-several-meanings trap.

claims.statement: Availability group 7 is the marker for an opponent deck slot that is out of play, not a set number. F0x8009DA68 writes the constant 7 into the group byte of each slot it retires, and F0x8009D9E4 derives duel+0x41C by scanning down from slot 0x27 across the trailing run of slots whose group byte is 7. A deck entry authored with byte +0x02 = 7 therefore begins inside that trailing run, below the window duel+0x41B walks, which is why the shipped decks' group-7 entries are never drawn: they begin retired.
claims.coverage: Both halves were read as instructions: the write is li $t3, 0x7 before the loop with sb $t3, 0x30b($v0) inside it, and the scan is the compare against 7 walking slot indices down from 0x27. The final clause is not an independent enumeration of the shipped decks: it follows from the window arithmetic recorded in model document section E.5, where the threshold 2*set+2 reaches at most 6 across a best-of-three, together with the two sites above, and is stated as a consequence of those rather than as a measurement of the 170 shipped decks.
limitations: The consequence for the shipped decks rests on the model document's threshold arithmetic, which this pass did not re-derive from the draw code.
Static reading only; not observed in the running game.
claims.notes: Rests at partially_verified. The two load-bearing sites are anchored, but the final clause - that shipped group-7 entries are therefore never drawn - is a consequence of the window arithmetic in section E.5 of the model document rather than something this bundle proves. Missing artifact for promotion: an anchor on the draw-side threshold, or a narrowed statement dropping the consequence.

claims.statement: The Battle Phase's ceremony is not a fixed list: its machine issues one beat per thing that happened. The machine dispatches through a 27-entry pointer table at 0x80083990 (cardgame.s:830-856). State 1 is the table's entry 1, 0x800A101C (cardgame.s:831): it scans YOUR board and, for each combo run it finds, latches 0x19 and comes back for the next (cardgame.s:30955 jumps into the shared store with 0x19 in its delay slot, which is why a scan for the immediate alone misses it). State 2 is entry 2, 0x800A1048 (cardgame.s:832): the same handler aimed at side 1, latching 0x1A (cardgame.s:30964). State 8 is entry 8, 0x800A1078 (cardgame.s:838): it latches 0x1B once per queued card reveal, counting the queue at +0x305 down and leaving only at zero (cardgame.s:30972). A scan that finds nothing issues nothing, so no rule can hang on any of the three. Whether 0x1B's update is an eight-step machine, and whether a pad poll sits at its step 6, is NOT established here and the earlier statement of it is withdrawn.
claims.notes: CORRECTION 2026-08-28 after an independent review recorded needs_evidence. The review asked for the dispatch-table words behind the state numbers 1, 2 and 8; those are now anchored. It also flagged an entirely unevidenced clause about an eight-step update machine with a pad poll at step 6, which is withdrawn here rather than defended. A separate open question the review raised is recorded and NOT resolved: +0x304 appears to gate whether 0x1B fires while +0x305 is the counter, and this statement mentions only +0x305. Status held at candidate.
claims.coverage: The three state numbers are now tied to the actual table words rather than asserted: the run of 27 consecutive address words beginning at cardgame.s:830 was enumerated and indices 1, 2 and 8 read directly from it, so a wrong index would have shown as a different address. The eight-step/step-6 clause is withdrawn rather than covered, because no enumeration was run that could have falsified it.

claims.statement: A card-duel beat's wait is counted in sixtieths of a second, not in displayed frames, and the counter it uses is not a constant 1 per update. The overlay's wait helper F0x8008DEAC loads the resident function pointer at RAM 0x8004DF9C (cardgame.s:11399), calls it, and adds the result into the object's timer at +0x424 before comparing it with the requested length (cardgame.s:11409). Three RAM dumps hold 0x8001D704 in that pointer, and F0x8001D704 is a three-instruction getter for the global word D0x8004DE28 (fns.s:14752-14753), which is +0x18 of the resident display table D0x8004DE10. F0x8001D504 publishes that word as the integer part of an 8.8 fixed-point accumulator at +0x1C - sra 8 into +0x18 (fns.s:14700-14701), remainder kept by andi 0xff back into +0x1C (fns.s:14704-14706) - and the per-interrupt feeder F0x8001D3F4 adds 0x100 to that accumulator on the 60Hz path (fns.s:14553) and 0x133 on the 50Hz path (fns.s:14564). 0x133/256 is 1.1992, so both paths accumulate about 60 units a second and a beat length is a wall-clock duration in sixtieths. The published integer is 1 in three field dumps and 3 and 4 in two battle dumps, so an update that arrives late publishes the whole backlog at once rather than stretching the animation.
claims.notes: Settles the open worry recorded on 2026-08-27 that every shipped tick count 'assumes the supplier returns 1'. It does not always return 1, but the unit is a sixtieth of a second either way, so the durations in PROGRAM_BEAT_TICKS carry over to the walker's 60Hz scheduler unchanged and no shipped number moves. NOT established: who writes the 50/60 flag D0x8005CCAC, and whether the interrupt the feeder is registered on is the vertical blank by name - it is registered as index 4 through an unidentified table.
claims.coverage: The pointer's value was read at 0x8004DF9C in three independent dumps (dri_s1.bin, dri_s4.bin, bd_ram1.bin) and agreed. The published word was read in five (dri_s1, dri_s4, dri_s6, bd_ram1, bd_ram7). The remainder field +0x1C was read in dri_s1.bin and holds 246, below the 256 the andi predicts, which is an independent check on the fixed-point reading. The 50/60 flag D0x8005CCAC was read as 0 in dri_s1.bin and bd_ram1.bin, matching the 0x133 path. Not exhaustive: no writes-scan was run to prove F0x8001D504 is the ONLY writer of +0x18; the claim rests on code-search finding no other reference to D0x8004DE28 and on that one computed store.

claims.statement: The duel board is three rows, not four: the opponent's hand at y=38, a single shared centre row at y=97, and the player's hand at y=156. Both hand rows start at x=24 and step by the already-decoded 41px cardFanOut pitch across six slots (24, 65, 106, 147, 188, 229). Recovered from every sprite observed idle with no pending destination across two separate duels. The decoded static board-slot table 0x800A5978 -- (73,97), (123,97), (173,97) -- lies on this same centre row, which corroborates it. There is no per-player field row.

A duel card is 40x46 and F0x8009b168 composes its face from the sprite's unk45 render kind. The size comes from the code, not the atlas: every card draw sets the rotate/scale pivot to (+0x14, +0x17) = (20, 23), exactly half of 40x46, and the sprite carries its position as 8.8 fixed point at +0x00 / +0x04, drawn at >> 8. Kind 1 is a Digimon card: the colour frame is CARD-sheet clip unk38, or unk38 + 0x3C when unk49 == 1, drawn at the card origin, followed by either the stats readout (BOARD clip 0x1F separator at +0x12,+0x21 with a number at +4,+0x21 for unk43 and one at +0x17,+0x21 for unk44) or, when unk3C == 0, the blank BOARD clip 0x1E at +4,+0x21. Kind 2 draws CARD clip 0x10 at the card origin, kind 3 draws CARD clip 0x0C, and kind 0 draws nothing. Numbers are laid out by F0x80096a94: the digits are BOARD clips 0x14..0x1D (8x12 each) on a 7px pitch, walked from the low end and placed at x + (width - 1 - k) * 7 so the field is right-aligned in a fixed box, with leading zeros suppressed when unkF == 0. Each colour frame's interior is transparent over a 30x28 window at (5, 4), measured from the extracted clips, which is where the record's own 32x32 TIM artwork shows through cropped by the frame border.

The card reveal does not swap the two sides' totals instantly. Beat 0x1B's update accumulates the resident frame delta into duel+0x424 and calls the tween helper F0x80093BC4 four times, each with the bound 0xF (cardgame.s:17465 slti 0xf) and that timer, feeding the result to the view's counter setter at +0xEA0. The four stores form a CROSSED exchange between the two sides, not between one side's own two numbers: +0x664 is written from +0x59C, +0x59C from +0x664, +0x666 from +0x59E, and +0x59E from +0x666 (cardgame.s:17517-17527; the loads are at 17517, 17518, 17519 and 17523 and the four stores at 17521, 17525, 17526 and 17527). The travel is BOUNDED at fifteen accumulator units. Whether fifteen units is fifteen displayed frames was NOT established, and WHICH on-screen plaques the two written properties are is likewise NOT established -- the earlier reading of them as the AP and HP plaques was an inference from the attack drain touching the same pair, and is withdrawn. The enter phase places view sprite 0x11 at (0x8300, 0x6100) with its face index taken from duel+0x304 minus one and scales it over 10 frames (cardgame.s:17383-17406).
claims.notes: CORRECTION 2026-08-28. An independent review recorded needs_evidence, and a separate enumeration pass then showed the review had CONFIRMED a citation it could not have read: the cited range cardgame.s:17468-17514 contains zero store instructions. The crossed swap is real but sits at 17517-17527. Two overstatements are also withdrawn here: 'over fifteen frames' is narrowed to the bound the code actually carries, and the identification of properties 8 and 9 as the AP and HP plaques is removed as an unanchored inference. Status held at candidate; nothing promoted.
claims.coverage: The four stores were located by enumerating EVERY reference to offsets 0x59c, 0x59e, 0x664 and 0x666 in cardgame.s lines 17400-17560 -- twenty references, of which exactly four are stores. That enumeration is what shows the previously cited range 17468-17514 contains no stores at all, so a counterexample to the old citation would have been found by the same scan. The bound of fifteen comes from the single slti at 17465 plus four li 0xf sites at 17471, 17483, 17495 and 17507; no other 0xf immediate or comparison exists in 17400-17560. No claim is made about displayed frames or about which plaque a property drives.

claims.statement: The centre row carries two behaviours the walker has no equivalent of. (1) A run of roughly 28 sprites fans across y=97 from x=24 to x=262 at about 7px pitch -- cardFanOut's count>=7 branch, 0xF600/count -- is held for around 377 frames and then dismissed together (run 1, frames 1761-2138). (2) A persistent centre card sits at (81,97) with render kind 1, taking over when a sprite that turns at the right-hand deck position (229,97) finishes. Candidate rather than partially_verified because what these represent in player terms is not established, only their geometry and timing.

A combo is a run of three or more copies of the same Digimon card on one side's field, gated on the CARDPAK record's +0x0a field being non-zero. F0x800a0cd4 copies the field into a scratch list of (slot, card id) pairs, bubble-sorts it by card id and walks the runs: a zero +0x0a ends a run, and a run reaching three flags its slots at +0x446, stores that +0x0a value into the duel's combo slot at +0x438 and returns the next scan index, or -1 when none remain. The +0x0a values are card ids following the digivolution lines - Patamon (100), Angemon (81) and Piddomon (84) all carry 71 = MagnaAngemon - so +0x0a names the card a combo produces; 200 of the 316 catalog records carry a non-zero value across 90 groups. The board evaluator F0x800a3934, installed at duel+0x820, is the only numeric statement of a combo's worth: it counts a qualifying run's AP and HP a second time on top of the plain field sum and adds a further 0x14 to each once the run reaches four. Whether the shipped rule doubles the run or replaces it with the +0x0a Digimon is NOT resolved by anything read here.

The card duel uses two distinct live objects, which the prior static documents conflated. The CardBattleContext (0xf48 bytes) holds the 40-entry animation sprite pool at +0x108..+0xCE7 and the 42-slot dispatch table at +0xEA0; the duel object holds the mode machine at +0x2f4..+0x676. They cannot be one struct because those ranges overlap. Measured live: context 0x800c7434, duel 0x800ac394, with context+0x50 == duel+0x50, matching F0x8009d310(arg0 + 0x50). The class word 0x8009bba8 is stored at context+0x48, not at +0x00.
claims.notes: Addresses are one allocation of one load and are not stable; locate the context by the sprite-pool signature. Offsets +0x424, +0x46f, +0x4e0, +0x5a0 and +0x600 were attributed to the context by card-duel-engine-2026-08-04.md and must be re-attributed.

claims.statement: A dealt card does not emerge from the deck pile. It starts at x=0x15F19 (351.7px), off the right edge of the 320px screen, already on its destination row's y, and runs the decoded linear move (state 2) for exactly 20 frames to (24 + 41*i, rowY). Over those same 20 frames BOTH scale axes ramp linearly from zero to 0x1000 -- run 2 slot 00 logs sx=sy= 205, 410, 615, 1024 against timer 19, 18, 17, 15 of dur 20, i.e. scale = 0x1000 * (dur - timer) / dur -- so the card grows from nothing as it crosses. Card i's move begins 6 frames after card i-1's.

The claim cardduel-view-slot-eb0-closes-one-banner-2026-08-28 called the routine at slot +0xEB0 'the teardown of one banner' and named its written fields a scale pair, a state byte and a duration pair. Every line it cited is correct and its count of five stores is correct, but none of that evidence reaches those names or the verb 'closes': no reader of +0xE23 was read, so nothing shows that the value 3 means closing rather than opening or idle. The mechanical content is re-recorded without the unproven vocabulary as cardduel-view-slot-eb0-writes-banner-record-2026-08-28.
claims.coverage: The half that says every cited line is correct was tested by re-reading all ten cited lines against the file; an independent review re-read the same ten and reached the same result. The half that says nothing shows what the value 3 means is a statement about the CITED EVIDENCE only: no search for a reader of view+0xE23 has been run, and this claim does not assert that no such reader exists in the overlay.
claims.contradiction_rationale: A semantic role was inherited from existing authority-5 prose and presented as if the assembly had established it. The shape of the values - 0x1000 reading as a fixed-point one, a small number reading as a countdown - is what made the names feel earned. Found by an independent review, not by the author.
limitations: A review rejected cardduel-424-is-the-step-frame-tick-2026-08-28 for three bad line citations in its statement. The rejection was checked against the assembly by the lead and is correct. The claim is superseded here rather than defended.
The delegate that produced the 25 slot rows was NOT trusted for arithmetic; every address was recomputed from the file's own instruction encodings.

claims.contradiction_rationale: The claim cardduel-program-effect-record-is-targeting-plus-message-list, and docs/research/card/cardduel-rules-2026-08-06.md section 7 which it records, state that the zero-terminated byte list at Program-effect record +0x04 is 'a zero-terminated list of on-screen message ids, not a bytecode'. That is falsified. The bytes are opcodes for the interpreter F0x80084320, which latches a running opcode at duel+0x420, dispatches a second switch on it, chains opcode 0x96 to 0x97, and skips an opcode by adding 2 to the program counter duel+0x4E0. A list of message ids has no running-opcode latch, no chaining and no program counter arithmetic. The rest of that claim - the 0x2C stride, the 60 records, row index = card id - 1, and the meanings of +0x00, +0x01 and +0x02 - is unaffected and stands.
claims.statement: FALSIFIED: 'the byte list at Program-effect record +0x04 is a zero-terminated list of on-screen message ids, not an effect bytecode'. It is an effect bytecode. See cardgame-effect-record-is-a-bytecode-program. The remainder of cardduel-program-effect-record-is-targeting-plus-message-list is unaffected.

A turn's Program-card effects resolve together after the turn's plays, not as each card is played. The play machine reaches its resolve state 0xC only when the turn is over - three plays made, or the side declining - and that state raises duel+0x2F4 = 2, clears duel+0x4DC, duel+0x4E8 and duel+0x4EC, and copies the turn's play count duel+0x575 into duel+0x4DE, the number of plays the effect interpreter is then given to work through.
claims.coverage: The routes into state 0xC were enumerated from the sites that load 0xC into duel+0x574: the play-count arm of state 1, and the pass branches of states 2 and 3 when a play has already been made. Both were read at instruction level. The statement does not assert in what order the interpreter resolves them; that is section D.4's reading and was not re-derived here.
limitations: Static reading only; not observed in the running game.
claims.notes: Rests at partially_verified. The routes into state 0xC and the store of the play count into duel+0x4DE are anchored; the rest of the state's body is not. Missing artifact for promotion: .L0x0001d7a4 through .L0x0001d7bc quoted, showing duel+0x2F4 = 2 and the three clears.

claims.statement: The duel builds three element-count panels, one per folder, from the folder-chooser machine F0x8009F110 at states 1, 3 and 5 (folder 0, 1, 2 in that order). The three call sites are cardgame.s:29023 (folder 0, x=23, y=80), :29048 (folder 1, x=23, y=125) and :29073 (folder 2, x=23, y=170); x is the low halfword and y the high halfword of the {s16 x, s16 y} table at 0x800A5D48 (cardgame.s:35886-35888 = 0x00500017, 0x007d0017, 0x00aa0017). The constructor F0x80096828 stores folder at +0x50, x at +0x58, y at +0x5A (cardgame.s:20256-20258) and the scale-out helper F0x80096808 sets +0x6A=6 total frames, +0x68=6 counter, +0x66=2 mode, +0x5C=0x1000 scale (cardgame.s:20189-20196). The same table feeds the folder-cursor marker, so the three panels sit on the three chooser rows; the panel plate is drawn at (x+5, y+3) and the six element counts at y+20 with x offsets 36,71,106,141,176,211 from the table at 0x800A5940.
claims.notes: Static authority 2/3. No rig capture; a global sprite-primitive screen origin was not traced (shared with the already-recorded chooser positions).
claims.coverage: Every call site, the constructor stores and the scale helper were read at their exact cardgame.s lines; the coordinate table was read as raw words rather than inferred from the gap doc. Bucket-index to colour/element naming is explicitly not established here.
claims.frontier_rationale: Closes cardduel-gap A6 x/y (MISSING/UNDECODED); the panels themselves remain unimplemented in the walker, which is a separate implementation gap.

claims.statement: Choosing a folder whose first card is zero does not start an empty duel. The chooser's final step reads the first card of the chosen folder out of save RAM and, when it is zero, fills the forty-card pile from a table inside the overlay instead of from the save. Either path sets both sides' deck counts to forty before the duel begins.
claims.coverage: The test is the routine's own branch on the first saved card, read as instructions with its delay slot, and the two arms were followed to the point where they rejoin. The claim is about what this one routine does with an empty folder; it does not assert that the game prevents an empty folder from being chosen, which was not investigated.
limitations: What the built-in table contains was not read.
Static reading only; not observed in the running game.
derivation: awk over F0x8009F110's extent for ori $a0 and the 0x2ea accesses

claims.statement: Each side's field holds six Digimon. F0x8008def8 and F0x8008e08c both iterate twelve field slots in one loop and split them with a `< 6` test between side 0's slot array at +0x72e (count +0x72c) and side 1's at +0x7a0 (count +0x79e), the two 0x72 bytes apart, which is the same per-side stride F0x800a3934 uses. A slot is 0xe bytes: +0x0 card-slot ref, +0x2 pending AP delta, +0x4 pending HP delta, +0x6 AP, +0x8 HP. The twelve-entry flag array at +0x46f is therefore one flag per field slot across both sides. The same roll bounds a slot's AP and HP to 0..0x63, i.e. 0..99, and its tail re-flags every slot whose HP has reached 0.

The field look-through is driven by opcode 0xA8's update F0x8008A068, which is a TWO-LEVEL step machine: its body holds two switches, the first with ten arms and the second with fifteen, over the same object (F0x8008a068.c:60 and :137). Its enter phase F0x80089EC8 is a three-line wrapper and its section cursor mover F0x80089F18 is twenty-five lines. The player-facing behaviour previously stated for this screen -- that it tries your board, then the opponent's, then the played stack and opens on the first that is not empty; that Up and Down then walk opponent row, played stack, your row; that empty lists are skipped; that the two ends refuse rather than wrap; and that an all-empty field shows text-bank entry 23 -- is NOT established. None of it was anchored: the claim carried a single citation, to the call site that reaches the function, and nothing from inside the function itself. The sprite slot layout of 0-5, 6-11 and 12-17 is likewise NOT established. Those descriptions are retained here only as the open question this claim now poses, not as findings.
claims.notes: CORRECTION 2026-08-28 after an independent review returned REJECT. The review's central objection was WRONG and is overridden: it stated that the cited decompilation file does not exist, having searched only ~/ddw3. The exe-decomp tree lives in the walker repository, and all three cited files are present (366, 3 and 25 lines). That error is recorded here so the same retraction is not attempted again. Its SEPARATE objection was right and is acted on: the claim carried one anchor -- a call site -- behind a dozen behavioural clauses, so every one of those clauses is demoted to an open question and only the structural facts that are now enumerated are asserted. Status held at candidate.
claims.coverage: The two switch statements and their arm counts come from enumerating every switch and case label in the function's 366 lines, so a third switch or a missing arm would have appeared. The line counts of the enter phase and the cursor mover are whole-file counts. NOTHING here is claimed about the screen's behaviour; every behavioural clause has been demoted to an open question precisely because no coverage test was ever run for it.

claims.statement: In the 0xE-byte field slot record based at duel+0x72E (side stride 0x72), the halfwords at slot+0x2 and slot+0x4 are the authoritative AP and HP, and slot+0x6 and slot+0x8 are the displayed values that F0x8008E08C steps toward them at one point per frame. F0x8008DEF8 reads slot+0x2 and slot+0x4 (as duel+0x730 and duel+0x732 off a base of duel + slot*0xE), adds the packed immediate's high and low halfwords, and stores them back; nothing in that path treats them as deltas to be consumed. F0x800A0844 corroborates the direction of travel by reading slot+0x2 and slot+0x4 as the base of its five dynamic-stat Mega formulas and writing the results to slot+0x6 and slot+0x8, i.e. snapping the display. The labelling of slot+0x2 and slot+0x4 as 'pending AP delta' and 'pending HP delta' in docs/research/card/cardduel-rules-2026-08-06.md section 2 is therefore wrong; they are absolute current stats. AP and HP remain capped at 99 and floored at 0, and a slot reaching 0 HP is re-flagged for removal.

The player's hand is not flipped card-by-card on arrival. Every card lands face down and the flip wave starts only once the LAST card has landed, then runs one card at a time in the same 6-frame stagger. Each flip is the decoded 12-frame half-sine (F0x8009a75c): sx sweeps 0x1000 -> 0 -> 0x1000 with sy held at 0x1000. Run 2: slot 00 reaches the sx=0 midpoint at frame 211 and slot 05 at frame 240, 29 frames later, after slot 05 landed at frame 200.

The folder chooser read statically from F0x8009F110 is the screen the original game actually shows. A capture taken from the running game on 2026-08-05 shows three folder plates on screen together, labelled Folder 1 to Folder 3, under a title bar reading 'Choose a folder', with the top plate highlighted and holding the cursor. That title is string index 0x41 of escardgm.toml, the id the chooser's first step hands the view, and the three plates are the three the routine opens in its three separate steps. The cursor resting on the top plate at the start is consistent with the statically read rule that a move up is refused there.
claims.coverage: This compares a static reading against an observation rather than quantifying over anything: the three plates and the title are counted and read off one captured frame of the original game, and the title is matched to the language file by index. It does NOT test the arrival cadence or the no-wrap rule - the capture keeps ten frames of a run that screenshotted every third frame, which cannot show either - and the claim says only that the observed cursor position is consistent with the rule, not that it demonstrates it.
limitations: The capture cannot show the plates arriving one at a time, the waits between them, or what happens when a move is refused at either end. Those parts of the static reading remain untested against the running game.
The capture is a still. Nothing here observes a sound.

claims.statement: The screen that opens a duel deals its three folder plates in one at a time, each arriving with the shared window-open sound, and takes them away the same way with the shared window-close sound. The choice runs over the three plates and does not wrap: up is refused on the top plate and down on the bottom. Each accepted move plays SYSTEM06, the same cursor sound the in-duel pickers use, and confirming plays SYSTEM07.
claims.coverage: The three arrivals and the three departures were each read as their own step with its own sound call, rather than counted from the decompiled switch; that is the test for 'one at a time'. Both bounds were read as instructions with their branch outcomes, which is the test for the no-wrap clause. The sound ids were read as the lui/ori pairs building each packed argument and resolved to names through docs/research/audio/soundtst-common-ids.json.
limitations: The waits between the steps are read from the decompiled C (eleven ticks between arrivals, four between departures) and are NOT anchored here; only the steps and their sounds are.
Static reading only; not observed in the running game.
derivation: awk over F0x8009F110's extent for ori $a0 and the 0x2ea accesses

claims.statement: The duel card frame drawn by F0x8009b168 is selected by the card's colour: CARD-sheet clips 0..5 are six 40x46 frames whose border colours, sampled from the extracted clips, are pale (168,176,144), blue (0,0,248), green (0,160,40), red (248,56,0), black (64,64,64) and brown (96,48,0). That is exactly the record's own colour-byte order (+0x00 = 1..6 mapping to white, blue, green, red, black, brown), so the frame index is colour - 1. CARD-sheet clips 60..65 are the same six frames at roughly half brightness, which is what the unk49 == 1 alternate that adds 0x3C selects. The colour-to-index correspondence is inferred from the sampled border pixels agreeing with the catalog's documented colour order; no line of code names a colour, so this is not a code-level decode of the mapping.

The in-duel inspect menu's marker sprite sits at x=10, and its row y is 101 + 14*row: the draw loads the row index and computes a2 = row*14 (sll 3; subu; sll 1) then addiu 0x65 = 101, with a1 = 0xa = 10 as x. The same row*14+101 pattern appears for the second menu. This reinstates the pitch of 14 that cardduel-inspect-menu-screen-position-2026-08-28 wrongly withdrew.
claims.notes: Static authority 2. Cross-checked against the local review of cardduel-inspect-menu-screen-position-2026-08-28 (docs/research/evidence/reviews/...review.json, decision reject) whose withdrawal of pitch 14 this claim corrects. Worker file not used; lead read the assembly.
claims.coverage: Both *14 sites were read end to end: 0x80098624-0x8009863c (sll 3 / subu / sll 1 / addiu 0x65, with a1=0xa) and 0x80098714-0x8009872c (same chain). The a1=0xa load and the addiu 0x65 are in the cited lines, so x=10 and y=101+14*row follow from the instructions, not from value shape.
claims.frontier_rationale: Corrects a material error in the resolved-inspect-menu candidate cardduel-inspect-menu-screen-position-2026-08-28 (the A2-style residual of the cardduel inspect menu); no open frontier owns it.

claims.statement: Pending opcodes 0x9B, 0xA8 and 0x9C are the Hand, Field and Trash arms of a five-row menu the card duel can open mid-duel, driven by the state machine F0x800A2608. The cursor moves on Up and Down, Circle confirms and Cross cancels, and the confirm indexes a table at 0x80083AF0: row 0 latches 0x9B and opens a read-only list of your own hand under escardgm entry 25 (Your Hand); row 1 latches 0xA8 and shows both boards side by side, answering escardgm entry 23 (No Cards in the Field.) when one is empty; row 2 latches 0x9C and opens the discard pile under escardgm entry 27 (Your Trash); row 3 cancels and restores what the duel was doing; row 4 surrenders behind escardgm entry 44 (Are you sure?). The identification is fixed by the counts the enter thunks read rather than by the handlers: 0x9B's thunk loads the hand count at duel+0x5A6 and 0x9C's loads the trash count at duel+0x5A2. All three are browse-only, closing on Cross with no confirm, and closing returns to the five-row menu.
claims.notes: This is the one row of the ceremony gap list with no walker surface at all: there is no in-duel menu, no look-through and no surrender in web/cardduel.js. GUESS, labelled: that the five rows draw escardgm entry 32, the string Hand/Field/Trash/Cancel/Surrender. The rows match that string in order but the prompt is opened with a zero id and no load of entry 32 was found. Also unresolved: what fills the trash browser's list object at duel+0x4D4, and every writer of the state byte the inspect machine runs on. Enter and update addresses came from a delegated pass; the two count loads quoted here were re-dumped from the overlay in this session.
claims.coverage: opcodes 0x9B, 0x9C, 0xA8, F0x800A2608, table 0x80083AF0, escardgm entries 23, 25, 27, 44

claims.statement: The inspect menu's marker pulses rather than blinking. It is an instance of the executable's colour-cycling display class (built by F0x8001B364, ticked by F0x8001B0A4), which holds a rest colour for its long period field and then steps a colour list at its short period field before dropping back. The marker's constructor sets the long period to 0x20 and the short one to 6 (exe/fns.s:12392, :12394), and the tick's list bound is 5 with a wrap to the rest entry, so the cycle is 32 ticks at rest, then four steps of 6 ticks, then rest again -- 56 ticks in all. Those ticks are frames: the class counts them from D0x8004DE10 + 0x188, the frame counter, but that identity is carried here at research authority only. The five list entries are the words at 0x8004DCE0..0x8004DCF0, which point at 0x8005CCDC, 0x8005CCD8, 0x8005CCD4, 0x8005CCD0 and 0x8005CCD4 holding 0x8581, 0x8681, 0x8781, 0x8881 and 0x8781; the third and fifth are the same entry, so the list index walks 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and back to 0 while the colour shown returns through a value it already used. Those values are palette ids, so what colour each one shows -- and therefore whether the pulse brightens or darkens -- is in video memory and is NOT established here.
claims.notes: Targeted evidence pass 2026-08-28 after two independent reviews. The second review re-derived all seven anchors against the live sources and found every one exact, and recommended partially_verified, which is where this claim rests. Two corrections were made in response to it. First, the earlier wording said the pulse 'brightens through three and returns through one'; that was a brightness direction inferred from the numeric ordering of palette ids, which the same statement elsewhere says is not established, so it is replaced by the plain index sequence. Second, the 'frames' unit rests on D0x8004DE10+0x188 being the per-frame counter; that is established in docs/research/engine/resident-core-services-2026-08-04.md L110-L126, which cites docs/research/infra/falsified-hypotheses.md L485, and is now anchored here at authority 5 (research) rather than left implicit. Still missing for promotion past partially_verified: a constructor call-site anchor tying this particular colour-cycling instance to the inspect menu's marker rather than to another element built from the same shared class. Review path substituted: tools/review_claim.py cannot run in this WSL environment (its nested claude CLI exits 1), so the ddw3-claim-reviewer subagent was dispatched against the same review bundle both times.
claims.coverage: exe F0x8001B364 constructor (both period stores and the immediates feeding them) and the whole tick body F0x8001B0A4 read end to end; the pointer block 0x8004DCE0..0x8004DCF0 read as five consecutive words and every distinct target address they name, so a sixth entry or an unread target would have shown as a gap in that consecutive address run. The 56-tick total is arithmetic over those two periods and the list bound of five; it was NOT counted against a running capture, so it is a derivation, not an observation. No claim is made about which colour any palette id renders as.

claims.statement: The in-duel inspect menu is opened with Triangle while a card picker is already up, not from a menu of its own. The card pickers' pad arm polls logical button 0xC (Triangle) and on it writes the pending step 0xB into duel+0x423; step 0xB sets the interpreter state byte duel+0x2F4 to 3, and the duel's own tick dispatches state 3 to the five-row machine F0x800A2608. The row cursor is the byte duel+0x569, bounded to five positions by an sltiu against 5 before the confirm table at 0x80083AF0 is indexed by cursor*4; row 0 latches pending opcode 0x9B, row 4 opens the prompt through the view's +0xEE4 with escardgm index 0x2C, 'Are you sure?'.
claims.notes: WALKER DIVERGENCE: in web/cardduel.js Triangle with nothing open LEAVES the card game, so building this menu also takes Triangle away from quit. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the Triangle arm is gated on the picker belonging to the player rather than the opponent.
claims.coverage: cardgame overlay: the picker pad arms, the state-3 dispatch and the five-row confirm table

claims.statement:
The in-duel inspect menu's five row words come from the duel's text bank, not from a caller: window B's open method stores only its second argument and carries no message id (cardgame.s:25927), and the window's own painter loads the bank pointer from the fixed global 0x8005CCA8 (cardgame.s:22125) and draws entry 0x20 from it through the same setter the duel's message windows use for their ids (cardgame.s:22135). escardgm entry 0x20 is 'Hand
Field
Trash
Cancel
Surrender'. That the five lines appear one per row, and that their order matches the order of the five actions dispatched on confirm, is NOT established -- no confirm or dispatch table mapping cursor rows to actions has been anchored. The load at :22125 is an unconditional fetch from a fixed address; the earlier description of it as 'keyed by the language variable' is withdrawn, since nothing here shows where or how that global is populated.
claims.notes: CORRECTION 2026-08-28 after an independent review recorded needs_evidence. The review doubted the note's claim that 'only three bank fetches exist in the whole overlay'. It was wrong: an enumeration of the literal displacement -0x3358 in cardgame.s returns 22 instructions, spread over four different base registers ($v0 15, $s0 3, $s1 2, $s2 2), not 3. (A first pass at this correction said 21; the exact count is 22.) The count is withdrawn entirely rather than replaced, because deciding which of those 22 resolve to the same global requires pairing each with its preceding lui and that pass has not been run. Two further overreaches flagged by the review are also withdrawn: the row-order-matches-dispatch clause, which had no anchor and no dispatch table behind it, and the description of a fixed global load as language-keyed. Status held at candidate.
claims.coverage: The escardgm entry index was resolved positionally against the language file. The claim about which instruction reads the bank is scoped to the two cited lines only. NO exhaustive claim is made about how many bank fetches exist -- see the notes; the previous count of three was wrong and is withdrawn rather than replaced, because the sites carry four different base registers and establishing which of them resolve to the same address needs each one's preceding lui, which was not done.

claims.statement: The in-duel inspect menu has no frame and no panel. Its painter places two things absolutely: one text object holding the five newline-separated row words at x=24, y=101 (cardgame.s:22136-22141), and a separate marker sprite whose x is 10 and whose first row sits at y=101 (cardgame.s:22113-22122). The spacing between rows was NOT established: a scan of cardgame.s:21400-22400 for the constant 14, and for any shift or multiply that would build a stride of 14, found no such site, so the previously stated pitch of 14 is withdrawn. The marker is an instance of the executable's colour-cycling class; it PULSES through a five-entry palette list rather than alternating between two entries -- see cardduel-inspect-menu-marker-pulses-2026-08-28, which supersedes the two-entry description previously given here. Nothing collides with the rows because the screen is taken apart first: on the Triangle press the picker closes its own message window (cardgame.s:3786-3790), then moves the side HUD away and waits before raising the menu; leaving the menu reverses it and reopens that window with the saved message, cursor and box, which is what the inspect machine's save/restore of the view's prompt fields is for. The naming of those calls as HUD panel slides is NOT established. The message window's own position is table-driven: box index N reads x and y from an eight-byte record at 0x800A59B0 (cardgame.s:21469). That table is shipped as data words at cardgame.s:35656-35663 and reads x=0 for every box with y = 138, 96, 50 and 96 for indices 0..3. Its text is drawn at x+27, y+18.
claims.notes: CORRECTION 2026-08-28 after an independent review recorded needs_evidence. Three changes. The table's contents are now anchored to the shipped data words rather than asserted; the review was right that only the table's base address had been evidenced, and the values it named all check out. The row pitch of 14 is withdrawn -- an enumeration found no site that could produce it. And the marker's description is corrected from a two-entry blink to the five-entry pulse established by the sibling marker claim; the two claims recorded on the same day contradicted each other and this one was the wrong half. Status held at candidate.
claims.coverage: The table's four records were read as eight consecutive data words at cardgame.s:35656-35663, so a fifth record or a non-zero x would have shown in that consecutive run. The withdrawal of the pitch rests on a scan of cardgame.s:21400-22400 for every instruction materialising 0xe and for every sll by 1 that could combine into a stride of 14; the two 0xe sites found (21739, 21753) are not stride computations. That scan is bounded to that window and would NOT find a pitch computed outside it.

claims.statement: Opening the in-duel inspect menu does NOT hide the hand row, on the evidence available. The card-picker arm's teardown issues six calls to the same view method: five in a row with selectors 4, 0, 1, 2 and 3, then a sixth with selector 5 (F0x80087edc.c:150-156). The yes/no arm stores 0 into +0x568 and 3 into +0x2F4 (F0x80087edc.c:449-450, and cardgame.s:6201 is that arm's handoff). Neither of those methods has been identified: naming them as banner closes, HUD panel slides, a menu state or an interpreter state is NOT established and those names are withdrawn from this statement. What IS established about the card sprites is one-sided: the other arm's whole function, F0x8008642C, contains no write to the per-slot bytes +0x150 or +0x151 anywhere in its 193 lines. F0x80087EDC does write them, at thirteen sites. Whether all thirteen belong to the cursor highlight and the greying pass, and therefore whether the pool is left alone by the teardown specifically, is NOT established. The claim that the row text is created at a higher draw priority than the cards is also NOT established -- it rested on a view constructor that was never cited or read.
claims.notes: CORRECTION 2026-08-28 after an independent review returned REJECT. Its central objection was a real citation error and is confirmed: the cited F0x80087edc.c:292-303 holds field-zeroing code, while the described six-call sequence is at :150-156, about 150 lines earlier. Every semantic name the review challenged -- banner close, HUD panel slide, menu state, interpreter state -- is withdrawn rather than defended, since none was anchored. One clause survives and is now anchored on an exhaustive per-file enumeration: the other arm never writes the card-sprite pool bytes. The draw-priority clause is withdrawn as it cited a function absent from the bundle. Status held at candidate.
claims.coverage: The +0x150/+0x151 statement is exhaustive over the two named functions: every occurrence of either field in both files was enumerated line by line, giving thirteen writes in F0x80087EDC and zero in F0x8008642C, so a missed write in either would have appeared. It is NOT exhaustive over the call graph -- a write performed by a callee of either function would not appear, which is why the pool conclusion is stated as unestablished rather than as a negative finding. The six-call teardown sequence was located by enumerating every call to that view method in the file, which is what showed the previously cited range 292-303 does not contain it.

claims.statement: The card-picker arm's teardown F0x80087EDC issues six calls to the same view method with selectors 4, 0, 1, 2 and 3 in that order, then a sixth with selector 5 only when duel+0x420 == 0x9A; the yes/no arm stores 0 into duel+0x568 and 3 into duel+0x2F4. The per-slot bytes +0x150/+0x151 are written at thirteen sites in F0x80087EDC and at none in F0x8008642C (193 lines). Whether opening the inspect menu hides the hand row is NOT established: the zero-write result is bounded to those two function bodies, not to their callees, and no drawing of the hand row was read.
claims.notes: Static authority 2/3. Supersedes the headline of the rejected cardduel-inspect-menu-teardown-leaves-the-hand-2026-08-28; the hand-visibility question stays open.
claims.coverage: The six selectors and the 0x9A guard are read directly at F0x80087EDC.c:150-158; +0x568/+0x2F4 at :449-450; the +0x150/+0x151 counts are exhaustive over the two named function bodies (13 references in F0x80087EDC.c, 0 in the 193-line F0x8008642C.c), not over their call graph.
