claims.statement: A duel is best of three: the first player whose set counter reaches 2 wins it. Mode 8 state 0x11 loads the per-player set counter at +0x5AE, tests it with `sltiu $v0, 0x2`, and on the >= 2 path writes the outcome byte +0x302 = 0; the mirrored test on the opponent's counter at +0x676 (= +0x5AE + 0xC8) writes +0x302 = 1. Only when NEITHER counter has reached two does the machine go to state 0x12 and another set. That same >= 2 path passes the literal 0x6004001E to the resident sound entry loaded from 0x80055C48; this claim states only that the duel-won path plays that id, NOT which audio sample it resolves to - the project's own audio research flags 0x6004001E as an unresolved mapping, so the earlier phrase 'the win jingle' has been withdrawn as an unproven semantic name. The counter itself is incremented in Battle-Phase state 0x0B: at 0x800A1484 the code forms the per-player block address as duel + side*0xC8 (confirming the 0xC8 stride), loads +0x5AE, adds one and stores it back, then sets the next state +0x2F9 = 0x0C. State 0x0B is established as the owning arm by the jump table at 0x80083990, whose entry [0x0B] is 0x800A12F8 and whose entry [0x0C] is 0x800A151C, a range that contains 0x800A1484.
claims.notes: Corrected 2026-08-07 after an independent review that re-derived the cited assembly and upheld the counter offsets, the sltiu direction, the 0xC8 mirroring and the outcome-byte writes, but raised two valid objections: 'win jingle' was a semantic name no cited evidence supported and which docs/research/audio/sound-system.md itself marks unresolved, and the closing sentence about state 0x0B had no citation at all. The sound name is now withdrawn to the neutral fact, and the state 0x0B increment is now cited directly at cardgame.s L31219 and L31228 plus the two jump-table entries that bound the arm - so the reviewer's second objection turned out to describe a TRUE statement that was merely uncited, and it is now evidenced rather than deleted.

claims.statement: Load and Compile are alternating turns that end on two empty turns in a row, not one action each. State 1 of the play machine dispatches on the turn's play count duel+0x575: counts 0 and 2 go to the side selected by duel+0x578, count 1 to the other side, and a count above 2 goes to the resolve state 0xC, which caps a turn at three plays. A side that declines with nothing played sets the delay counter duel+0x57C to twenty ticks, plays packed sound 0x00040019 and increments the consecutive-pass counter duel+0x577; a side that has already played a card this turn goes straight to state 0xC and does not touch duel+0x577, so only a turn with no play at all counts as a pass. State 0xE then flips duel+0x578, copies it into duel+0x579, raises the turn counter duel+0x576 and ends the phase only when duel+0x577 has reached 2.
claims.coverage: Each clause was read as instructions in the arm it describes, and the two branch outcomes that carry the rules - the play-count dispatch in state 1 and the pass test in states 2 and 3 - were read with their delay slots, which is where this table has been got wrong before. The pass rule was checked by diffing the two pass branches, the player's at lines 29999-30021 and the opponent's at lines 30054-30076: with labels normalised they differ in exactly two instructions, the branch displacement to their own resolve arm and the side argument passed to the view method (li $a1, 0x1 against move $a1, $zr). Every instruction that carries a rule - the play-count test, the twenty-tick load, the pass-counter increment and the sound - is identical between them. The sound id is the packed argument built by lui $a0, 0x4 plus the ori in the call's delay slot.
limitations: States 2, 3, 4/5, 6/7, 8, 9 and 0xA were not re-read in full in this pass; their behaviour is quoted from model document section D.4, which this pass corroborated where the two overlapped.
Static reading only; not observed in the running game.

claims.statement: The two list look-throughs opened from the in-duel menu are one driver with a different heading, chosen by the latched opcode: 0x9B (the hand) takes text-bank entry 25 and 0x9C (the trash) takes entry 27 (cardgame.s:5318, :5320), the same switch giving 28 to the opponent-hand arm 0x9D. Those entries read 'Your Hand', 'Your Trash' and 'Opponent Hand' in the English text file (escardgm.toml lines 27, 29 and 30), so the headings are confirmed from the shipped text and not inferred from the index numbers. The driver's dispatch table is at 0x800832E4 indexed by opcode minus 0x99 (cardgame.s:403-409); note that entries 1 and 2 -- opcodes 0x9A and 0x9B -- hold the SAME target 0x80087FB0, so 0x9A shares 0x9B's code path, which the earlier statement did not say. The driver is read-only for these two: Cross closes it and there is no confirm. The cursor moves one card at a time and refuses the move at each end rather than wrapping; that clamp is in the pad arm F0x80087B80, whose two guarded calls to the cursor mover sit behind comparisons at F0x80087b80.c:26 and :32. The earlier attribution of the clamp to the cursor mover F0x80086F24 was WRONG: that function is seventeen lines long and contains no comparison of any kind, so it cannot hold a bound. The per-card legality pass that greys unplayable cards is gated by a condition naming 0x9B and 0x9D at F0x80087edc.c:170; that it runs for ALL opcodes below 0x9B is NOT established, only that those two values appear in the gate.
claims.notes: CORRECTION 2026-08-28 after an independent review returned REJECT. Most of its objections were sound and are acted on here. Two of its points are now settled in the claim's favour with new anchors: the three headings are confirmed from the shipped English text rather than inferred from index numbers, and the 0x9A/0x9B shared target it spotted is now stated. One point is settled against the claim harder than the review put it: the no-wrap clamp was attributed to a function that provably cannot contain it, since that function has no comparison operators at all; the behaviour is real but lives one level up in the pad arm. The 'only for opcodes below 0x9B' universal is withdrawn -- the gate's condition is anchored, but nothing establishes the range. Status held at candidate.
claims.coverage: The dispatch table was read as a run of consecutive address words from its base, indices 0 through 6, so a shared or missing target would have shown in that run -- which is how the 0x9A/0x9B collision was found. The clamp's location was settled by enumerating EVERY if statement and comparison operator in both candidate functions: the cursor mover has zero of each across all seventeen of its lines, while the pad arm has four ifs and comparisons at lines 22, 26 and 32 guarding its two calls into the mover. The heading text was read directly from the English language file at the three line positions the index convention predicts, and the convention itself was checked against the file's first and last lines. No claim is made about the other six languages.

claims.statement: The CardDuel object is 0x824 (2084) bytes. Its factory F0x800A3240 saves its first argument in $s1, then calls the resident allocator F0x80014504 with handler 0x800A2F00, size 0x824 and flags 0x1C, and installs exactly five method pointers into the returned object: +0x810 = 0x8009F04C, +0x814 = 0x8009EEFC, +0x818 = 0x800A0754, +0x81C = 0x800A0708 and +0x820 = 0x800A3934. Each pointer is built as `lui $v0, 0x800a` followed by a signed `addiu`, so the two negative cases borrow from the upper half: -0xFB4 gives 0x8009F04C and -0x1104 gives 0x8009EEFC, not 0x800AF04C and 0x800AEEFC. The five pointers occupy +0x810..+0x823 inclusive and the last ends exactly at 0x824, so the allocation size closes the structure with no slack. The factory then stores its saved first argument as a byte at +0x2E8, and that byte is the opponent id: F0x8009D6E0 loads it back and uses it directly as the 1-based record index into CARD_NPC.BIN, computing 0xD0*(id-1). The installed handler F0x800A2F00 dispatches on duel+0x0C over four states, testing it against 1, 2 and 3 with the remaining path falling through, so it is the duel's own scene state machine and not a vtable.
claims.notes: Statement narrowed 2026-08-07 after review ad0bf327 returned needs_evidence: the CardDuelView identity, the enumeration of other duel offsets, and the names of the four handler states were dropped because this bundle carried no evidence for them; they remain in their own claims. Evidence added for every method-install addiu, the flags/handler arguments, the +0x2E8 store and its consumer, and the handler state tests.

claims.statement: The opponent's hand is dealt visibly, with the identical off-screen-right 20-frame move and scale ramp, to row y=38. It is then never flipped: after a brief hold each card's sx collapses to 0 over about five frames while sy stays 0x1000, leaving the card edge-on and zero-width for the rest of the duel rather than being removed. Run 2 slot 06 collapses over frames 328-331 and its slot is not released until frame 611.

The opponent's deck is retired a tier at a time instead of being shuffled. After returning its hand, F0x8009DA68 stamps each restored deck slot with availability group 2*duel[0x300] + 1, then repeats up to 40 times: while the group byte of the slot at the opponent's read cursor is not greater than the current window 2*duel[0x300] + 2, it lifts that slot's entry out, shifts the slots between the cursor and duel[0x41C]-1 up by one (entry and group byte together), writes the lifted entry into slot duel[0x41C]-1 and marks that slot's group byte 7. The loop stops at the first slot whose group is above the window. The cards the opponent could draw in the set just finished, played or not, are therefore pushed to the bottom and marked out of play, and the next set opens on the next availability tier.
claims.coverage: The bound of 40 is the loop's own slti against 0x28 and the stopping condition is the loop's gate, both read as instructions rather than inferred. The statement is scoped to F0x8009DA68 and does not assert that nothing else reorders the opponent's pile elsewhere in the duel.
limitations: What the opponent's draw code then does with duel+0x41B and duel+0x41C was not re-read in this pass; model document section E.5 covers the draw side.
Static reading only; not observed in the running game.
claims.notes: Rests at partially_verified after the 2026-08-21 review pass, deliberately. The behaviour was read end to end in F0x8009DA68, but the bundle anchors the stamp, the gate and the group-7 write without quoting the rotate loop's own shift instructions, the arithmetic that forms 2*duel[0x300]+1, or the slti 0x28 iteration bound. Missing artifact for promotion: those lines between .L0x0001ae9c and .L0x0001af14, quoted with their delay slots.

claims.statement: The card duel screen's art pack is CARDDATA.BIN, LBA_CARDDATA_BIN_IDX = 605, i.e. pack-handle hi-word 0x25d. Unlike every screen pack decoded so far it is NOT a <name>cs / <name>tm LBA pair: one archive holds both halves in four top-level slots and the pack handle's low u16 selects the physical slot directly, the rule sttrng already follows. Slots 0 and 1 are each archive{RLEN -> 16bpp TIM, 64 halfwords x 256}, a raw VRAM texture page behind a 20-byte TIM header (8 bytes magic/flags plus a 12-byte block {len, dx, dy, w=0x40, h=0x100}) whose payload is byte-identical to a tm block. Slot 2 is a FIELDCOM-format sprite directory of 82 frames / 65 clips (the CARD sheet: six class-coloured 40x46 card frames, the deck-pile and trash icons, the small pips). Slot 3 is one of 58 frames / 70 clips (the BOARD sheet: the 30-tile 64x64 field backdrop as clip 0, the AP/HP label plates, the ten 8x12 digits, the select and active card borders, the attack effect runs). pro/cardgame.s builds the handle 49 times; the following ori is 0x2 at 20 sites and 0x3 at 23 sites, and slots 0 and 1 are reached only by the texture upload in the scene entry F0x80095bfc. The name reads like a data table and the ddw3 splat leaves it as four opaque sub-archives, which is why no earlier pass looked inside; this is what closes the duel screen's total absence of decoded layout. Extracted by tools/extract_screen_packs.py BUNDLED_PACKS to web/assets/ui/carddata2_sheet.png and carddata3_sheet.png.

The card duel's per-player state is a 0xC8-byte block starting at +0x59C of the duel object, indexed as base + side * 0xC8 (the scale is emitted as a sll/addu chain computing 200 decimal, independently in F0x8008EC44 and F0x800A0ACC). Its zone arrays are contiguous, so each one's capacity is fixed by where the next field begins. Block layout, given as absolute offsets for side 0: total AP +0x59C (u16), total HP +0x59E (u16), deck cursor +0x5A0 (u16), trash count +0x5A2 (u16), deck count +0x5A4 (u16), hand count +0x5A6 (u16), S-Energy +0x5A8 through +0x5AC inclusive (FIVE u8 colour counters, one per colour, addressed only through the base because F0x80085FD0 indexes them as pool[colour - 1]), round-priority flag +0x5AD (u8), sets won +0x5AE (u8), one byte of alignment padding at +0x5AF, deck array +0x5B0 (u16, 40 entries, ending at +0x600), hand array +0x600 (10 entries, ending at +0x614) and trash array +0x614 (40 entries, ending at +0x664, which is the next player's +0x59C). The block therefore closes with no unaccounted bytes. A Folder holds 40 cards, a hand at most 10 and the trash 40. The two single-byte fields are confirmed by their side-1 counterparts one stride up: +0x5AD pairs with +0x675 and +0x5AE with +0x676. +0x5AD is a round-priority flag rather than padding - the round setup writes 0 to +0x5AD and 1 to +0x675 in consecutive instructions. +0x5AE is the sets-won counter: the set-resolution path reads it, adds one, stores it back, and then sets the Battle-Phase state duel+0x2F9 to 0xC. F0x8008EC44 reads all three counts and arrays by zone code (2 hand, 3 deck, 4 trash) and F0x800A0ACC writes the two totals.
claims.notes: Corrected 2026-08-07 after review a346528f returned needs_evidence. That review was right: the S-Energy/sets-won sub-clause carried no evidence and its arithmetic left an unexplained gap. S-Energy is five bytes 0x5A8..0x5AC inclusive (not four), and the byte at 0x5AD is a distinct round-priority field, not padding; evidence added for both plus their side-1 counterparts at 0x675/0x676. REVIEWED TWICE 2026-08-07; the promotion gate is NOT satisfied and the claim correctly rests at partially_verified. Review 1 (a346528f) found the S-Energy/sets-won sub-clause unevidenced with arithmetic that did not close; the sets-won and round-priority halves were then repaired with exact assembly. Review 2 (adeeefc1) accepted those but held that the S-Energy half is still unproven: the cited evidence quotes the CALLER's arg setup (cardgame.s L9838, addiu $a1, $s0, 0x670) rather than the pool[colour-1] indexing inside F0x80085FD0, and nothing bounds the colour count to exactly five - which is precisely the figure that makes the 0xC8 block close with no unaccounted bytes. NAMED MISSING ARTIFACTS: (1) an assembly citation inside F0x80085FD0 around .L0x00003388-.L0x0000339c showing pool_base + colour then lbu -0x1(...); (2) evidence bounding the colour argument to five values - a colour enum table, an sltiu range check guarding the call, or a caller loop over colours 1..5. Both reviews used the ddw3-claim-reviewer subagent path because tools/review_claim.py's nested claude CLI exits 1 in this WSL environment. Full verdict at docs/research/evidence/reviews/cardduel-per-player-block-is-0xc8-with-40-10-40-piles.review.json. EVIDENCE PASS 2026-08-07 (post-review): the first artifact review adeeefc1 named is now cited - cardgame.s L3307-L3310 inside F0x80085FD0, where the card record's colour byte at +0x00 is added to the pool base and the counter read as pool_base[colour - 1] (lbu -0x1), with the cost byte at record +0x05 compared against it. The SECOND artifact it named - anything bounding the colour count to exactly five - is still NOT supplied; docs/research/card/cardduel-rules-2026-08-06.md asserts five bytes at +0x5A8 with brown having no slot, but that is authority 5 research prose, not a range check or enum in code. The claim therefore still rests at partially_verified and its two-review budget is spent; a fresh review in a later session should be given the colour-bound artifact first.

claims.statement: F0x80098898(screen, player) draws one player's whole half of the duel board from a 0x4C-byte record at (player * 0x4C) + 0x800A59D0. There are exactly TWO records and they are one layout mirrored vertically: every widget shares its x and differs only in y, with the five field-slot plates at y 67 in record 0 and y 12 in record 1. Positions are offsets from the screen object's (unkC, unkE), except three that are added to (unk20, unk22) instead. The fields, with record 0 / record 1 values: +0x34 five field-slot plates (board clip 0x0D) at (11,67)/(11,12) stepping 0x2A in x; +0x08 their five 2-digit numbers at (38,71)/(38,16), same step; +0x18 label A at (30,52)/(30,35) and +0x1C its 3-digit total at (46,52)/(46,35); +0x20 label B at (78,52)/(78,35) and +0x24 its 3-digit total at (94,52)/(94,35); +0x0C and +0x10 two 2-digit counters at (249,71)/(249,16) and (291,71)/(291,16); +0x44 and +0x48 board clip 0x0C at (23,48)/(23,31) and (71,48)/(71,31); +0x38 and +0x3C board clip 0x0E at (222,64)/(222,9) and (264,64)/(264,9); +0x2C and +0x28 animated card clips at (270,69)/(270,14) and (228,69)/(228,14); +0x40 board clip 0x0F and +0x14 a 2-digit number, both on the alternate origin; and the byte at +0x02 (17 / 20) is a base clip added to screen->unk44. The two labelled totals are AP and HP: the label clip table at 0x800A5A70 is indexed by language * 2, English (0x8005CCA8 == 2) gives board clips 79 and 88, and those clips render as literal AP and HP plates. The halfword order of every pair above is anchored by the RECT at 0x800A5938 reading {0,0,320,240}. What the counters and totals mean in player terms beyond the AP/HP labels, and the runtime screen origin the offsets are relative to, are NOT established.

The card duel's seven phase banners, pending opcodes 0xA0 through 0xA6, are one routine and a two-byte table, and every one of them holds until the player presses Circle or Cross rather than for a fixed time. The seven enter thunks are consecutive and differ only in the immediate they pass, F0x800894E4(duel, view, op - 0xA0); that routine reads a two-byte record at 0x800A58C4 + i*2, hands byte 0 to the info-banner opener as a title id and byte 1 to openPrompt as a subtitle id, and sets the step byte duel+0x422 to 1. The fourteen table bytes are 01 02 03 04 05 06 07 08 09 0A 0B 0C 1F 3E, so the title/subtitle pairs are escardgm entries (1,2) Start Phase, (3,4) Draw Phase, (5,6) Load Phase, (7,8) Summon Phase, (9,10) Compile Phase, (11,12) Battle Phase and (31,62) Card Battle Challenge / LV for 0xA6. The shared update F0x80089580 is a four-step machine on duel+0x422 with no timer: it waits for the windows to open, then polls pad port 0 for logical buttons 0xD or 0xE and advances on either, then closes both windows and waits for them to go. Logical 0xD is Circle and 0xE is Cross.
claims.notes: 0xA6's wording was recorded as unresolved in the 2026-08-27 handoff; entry 0x1F is Card Battle Challenge and its subtitle entry 0x3E is LV, and web/cardduel.js:3853 already paints exactly that from a rig capture. The button identification is not assumed: exe-decomp/c/F0x800110e0.c:92-125 moves a cursor on logical 4 and 6, which are the hardware Up and Down bits, and takes 0xD as confirm and 0xE as cancel, so the logical index is the standard pad bit. LIVE DIVERGENCE, deliberately not fixed here: engine/systems/card-ceremony.ts holds each banner for a number measured off one capture (25, 49, 151, 71, 101, 63 frames), which is how long one player took to press, not a duration the game chooses. Not established: what the extra draw arm on 0xA6's subtitle adds beside the word LV.
claims.coverage: opcodes 0xA0-0xA6, F0x800894E4, F0x80089580, table 0x800A58C4, escardgm entries 1-12, 31, 62

claims.statement: Two of the picker's beats run to fixed durations rather than scaling with the row: the beat that hands control to the player ends at nineteen ticks, and the closing beat runs forty-six ticks before the driver reports what was picked. Three named sounds belong to the picker and are played from inside this driver: SYSTEM07 (0x0004001C) over the chosen cards as the picker closes, SYSTEM02 (0x8004513E) when the player moves between the two answers of the driver's own two-way prompt, and SYSTEM01 (0x800450BD) when the second answer is taken.
claims.coverage: The two durations are the driver's own compare constants, read as instructions. The three sound ids are read as the lui/ori pairs that build the packed argument, with the ori in each call's delay slot, and each id was resolved to a name through docs/research/audio/soundtst-common-ids.json rather than guessed. The claim says 'three named sounds belong to the picker', which is scoped to the ids played inside this one routine; sounds played by its callees, such as the cursor mover's SYSTEM06, are recorded separately.
limitations: What the two-way prompt asks is not established. The mechanism - a value toggled between two states and pushed to the view - is what is claimed, not its wording.
Static reading only; not observed in the running game.

claims.statement: None of the duel's three pickers wraps its cursor. In the hand picker F0x800875AC, the summon picker F0x800878B4 and the board picker F0x80087B80, a left step is taken only when the cursor duel+0x43C is above zero and a right step only when it is below the item count minus one; otherwise the input is consumed and nothing moves. In the hand picker, which is the one read line by line for this, direction is the union of the pad service's pressed word (slot +0x3F4) and its auto-repeat word (slot +0x3FC), so holding a direction repeats on the service's shared accelerating cadence, while confirm is read from the pressed word alone.
claims.coverage: The three pad handlers are the whole population for this claim: they are the three arms of the picker driver's own mode switch (F0x80087EDC switch 4, keyed on the pending opcode duel+0x420, with 0x99 taking the hand handler, 0x9A and 0x9D the summon handler, and 0x9B and 0x9C the board handler), and each of the three was read end to end in the overlay assembly. Both bounds were read in all three, and both branch outcomes were taken with their delay slots. The pressed-versus-repeat reading was checked on the direction path and on the confirm path separately in the hand handler, where they differ. The pressed-versus-repeat sentence is deliberately scoped to the hand picker: the other two handlers read the same two service slots, but this claim anchors that pairing only where it was read instruction by instruction.
limitations: Which physical button each logical index is depends on the pad service's button map; the shipped map is the identity, per the already-recorded resident-core claims. This claim names logical indices.
Static reading only; not observed in the running game.
The pickers opened outside the effect interpreter - the folder chooser and the coin toss - are different code and were not read here.

claims.statement: A cursor step in the two card pickers plays packed sound 0x0004001B and hands the view two commands: the card the cursor leaves is dropped back to its resting height and the card it arrives on is raised, through view method +0xF0C with the row's own spacing helper +0xED8. Both accepted steps in the hand and summon pickers reach this one mover, F0x800870A4, which is where the sound is played; the board picker steps through a different mover, F0x80086F24.
limitations: The mover's body is read from exe-decomp/cardgame_c/F0x800870a4.c (authority 3) apart from the sound, which is anchored in the overlay; the two view calls are not separately anchored.
Static reading only; not observed in the running game.
claims.coverage: The four call sites that move a card cursor were enumerated in the overlay - the left and right steps of the hand handler and of the summon handler - and all four are jal 0x800870a4. The sound is played once, unconditionally, at the top of that mover, so it cannot vary by direction; it is anchored there rather than at the call sites. The board handler's two steps call F0x80086F24 instead, which is why the statement names it separately rather than claiming one mover for all three pickers.

claims.statement: The duel's picker does not open in a fixed time: it holds its opening state until the elapsed counter duel+0x424 passes four ticks per item in the row plus fourteen, so a fuller hand takes visibly longer to become operable than a short one. The counter is advanced by the resident frame-delta getter at 0x8004DF9C rather than by one per call, which makes every threshold in this driver an engine-tick duration and not an iteration count.
claims.coverage: The threshold is read as instructions - the item-count load, the shift by two, the add of fourteen and the compare - rather than inferred from the decompiled expression, and the counter's source is read at the call that supplies the increment. The statement is scoped to this opening state; the driver's other beats use their own thresholds, two of which are recorded separately in this packet, and the claim does not assert that all of them scale.
limitations: Which quantity duel+0x4D4 counts in each of the driver's five modes was not established here; in the mode read it is the row the cursor walks.
Static reading only; not observed in the running game.

claims.statement: Playing a Program card is three prompts, not one press. State 2 issues effect opcode 0x98 through the pending-opcode latch duel+0x421 with duel+0x2F4 = 1, and opens the hand selector through the duel's method at +0x814, handing it the hand array at +0x600 and the side's hand count from +0x5A6; each state opens its prompt only on the pass where the sentinel duel+0x57A is -1. Choosing a card moves to the confirmation state, which issues a different opcode, 0x99. Accepting there moves to the commit state; declining there goes back to the pick. At the commit state, declining is a genuine take-back: the card is read out of the play history at duel+0x580, written back into the hand array at +0x600 at the slot the hand count points to, the hand count at +0x5A6 is raised by one, and the selector is reopened through the same method.
claims.coverage: Each clause is anchored in the state it describes, and the three transitions are read at the per-side next-state table's own column loads (+0x0, +0x2 and +0x4) rather than from the decompiled control flow, which is how the pick-confirm-commit order is established rather than assumed. The undo is claimed from the four instructions that perform it - the read from the history, the write into the hand, the count increment and the reopen - not from the state's name. The claim describes the player's side of the machine; the opponent's states 3 and 9 were not read in this pass.
limitations: What F0x8009F998 does at the commit step beyond returning a banner id was not read.
The banner ids are not resolved against escardgm.toml, so what the three prompts say is not established.
Static reading only; not observed in the running game.
derivation: sed -n over the three states' extents in ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003/pro/cardgame.s
claims.notes: WORDING CORRECTED 2026-08-21, same day: the first version of this statement called the values written to duel+0x421 'banners'. They are effect-VM opcodes. duel+0x421 is the pending-enter-opcode latch (claim cardgame-duel-0x421-is-the-pending-enter-opcode-latch), the shipped escardgm.toml holds only 71 strings (indices 0x00..0x46) so 0x98 and 0x99 cannot index it, and line 55 of card-battle-complete-model-2026-08-06.md already recorded 'there is no +0x421 message-id bank - the banners are opcodes'. The wording was inherited from that document's own legacy phrasing in section D.4. No evidence changed and no transition changed; what changed is what the values ARE. The earlier accepted review was invalidated by the statement change and the claim was re-reviewed.

claims.statement: The 0x2c-stride 60-record table at 0x800a4df4 read by F0x80083e34 is the per-Program-card record, row index = card id - 1, and it is a targeting descriptor plus a message list, not an effect bytecode. +0x00 is the targeting kind F0x800a36e4 switches on; +0x01 is an effect-visual selector and +0x02 an effect asset id, passed to F0x800954f8 and the screen's unkEE4 in F0x800a2180 case 6; +0x03 is a small enum stored into the play-history entry at +0x585 whose meaning is not established; +0x04 onward is a zero-terminated list of on-screen message ids that F0x800a2180 case 7 walks through the field getter's selector 4, writing each into the message id at +0x421. Targeting kinds 0x85..0x95 resolve to F0x8008eec8 field masks in which bit 8 is the acting player's own field, bit 9 the opponent's, and bits 2..7 the card colours white, blue, green, red, black and brown (the six u16 entries 0x0004..0x0080 at 0x800a58f4). Kinds 0x71/0x7f, 0x72/0x82, 0x80/0x81 and 0x96 resolve to F0x8008ec44 zones 2 hand, 3 deck and 4 trash with a kind mask whose bit 0 admits Digimon cards and bit 1 Program cards. Every decoded mask matches its card's escardst.toml text: kind 0x91 mask 0x3f8 is every colour but white on both fields and belongs to Sacred Spear, 'Put all non-white Digimon into trash can.'

Card-duel effect opcodes 0x1C and 0x1D are one enter routine (F0x80094B78) and one update routine (F0x80094B9C) aimed at one side each: the update's third argument is the side index, 0 for 0x1C (cardgame.s:2427) and 1 for 0x1D (cardgame.s:2435). Step 1 of the update walks that side's field block at duel+0x72C with stride 0x72 and calls F0x8008DA2C per occupied slot, which appends the slot's card into the trash list of the player who owns it - +0x614 for side 0 (cardgame.s:11136), +0x6DC for side 1 (cardgame.s:11146) - and then zeroes that side's field count (cardgame.s:18460). Step 2 seeds four scratch words from the two per-player blocks' hand and deck counts, +0x5A6/+0x5A4 for side 0 and +0x66E/+0x66C for side 1 (cardgame.s:18461-18464), and every third tick decrements a hand scratch and increments the matching deck scratch (cardgame.s:18495-18513), so the counters that move are hand into deck, not board into discard. Which of the two runs is chosen by the byte duel+0x301 (cardgame.s:31444-31449), and that byte names the side that WON the battle: the comparison at cardgame.s:31110-31118 tests side 0's field HP against side 1's and latches 0x17 or 0x18, the same sweep routine F0x80093ADC aimed at side 0 or side 1, so the LOSER's board is already gone by then and this empties the winner's.
claims.notes: Corrects two shipped documents that called this 'the round end: every card in the played row is sent to the discard, then both sides board counts drain into their discard counts'. Both halves were wrong. The walker's endSet already empties both fields and returns both hands, so there is no rules divergence: the disc reaches the same board in two stages (the loser's field at the battle comparison, the winner's at the round end) where the walker does it in one. What is missing on our side is that two-stage presentation. NOT established: the banner text either stage shows.
claims.coverage: Both dispatch arms were read, not one: the enter target 0x80084494 is shared and the two update targets 0x80085274 and 0x80085294 differ only in the third argument, which was read at both call sites. The update routine's seven steps were enumerated from its step table at 0x80083684; steps 1 and 2 are the two that touch cards or counters. The four counter offsets were checked against the per-player block map in engine/systems/card-battle.ts:24-26. The winner reading was checked against the 2026-08-26 state1 capture, which latched 0x17 once, 0x18 never and 0x1D once in a duel the player lost - the combination the reading predicts.

claims.statement: A row of cards is turned face-on in place, with no movement, by a bounded ten-frame scale ramp: the sprite stays in the idle state (45 = 1) while sx ramps 410 -> 0x1000 over dur 10 with sy held at 0x1000, and cards in the row start about 3-4 frames apart. Observed on the centre row y=97 at the 41px hand pitch (run 2 frames 614-625) and on the player hand row y=156 (run 2 frame 2055), so it is a reveal applied to a row wherever that row sits rather than a property of one row. This supersedes an earlier reading of the frame-2055 samples in isolation as a continuous idle animation of resting hand cards; the run is bounded and ends at full scale. That reading was never recorded as a ledger claim.

S-Energy is five bytes per player at +0x5a8..+0x5ac, one per colour, capped at 99. Drawing a card grants one point of the drawn card's colour: both draw paths (cardgame.s .L0x0000d9a8 and .L0x0000e2c4) select the drawn card's CARDPAK record, read its colour byte +0x00, bound it with `sltiu $v0, 0x6` and increment the energy byte at +0x5a8 + colour - 1 while it is below 0x63. Colour 6 is brown and falls out of that bound, so brown cards generate no S-Energy. F0x8008f560, the Anti-Power handler, clears exactly five bytes per player, confirming the block is five wide and not six; the byte at +0x5ad is separate and is seeded with the side index by the reset F0x800a1b2c.

At a set change the cards still in hand go back on top of the draw pile, for both sides. Mode 9 (F0x800A1A5C) calls F0x800A19F8 on the side-0 per-player block and F0x8009DA68 on the side-1 block, and each runs the same loop: while the hand count at block+0x0A is above zero it decrements both that count and the deck read cursor at block+0x04, copies the hand entry at block+0x64 + (count-1)*2 into the draw pile at block+0x14 + (cursor-1)*2, and raises the deck count at block+0x08. Neither routine references the trash array at block+0x78 or its count at block+0x06, so the discard pile is not recycled at a set boundary.
claims.coverage: The quantifiers cover the two per-player blocks, which are the whole population: the block has exactly two instances, duel+0x59C and duel+0x59C+0xC8 = duel+0x664 (model document section E.3), and mode 9's calls were enumerated by matching jal/jalr over its full extent, lines 31602-31639, giving five sites of which these two take a block. Each loop's exit test is itself on block+0x0A, so 'every card in hand' is the termination condition rather than an inference. The negative clause was tested by reading both routines end to end - F0x8009DA68 is lines 27509-27603 and contains no call at all - and no instruction in either names block+0x78 or block+0x06.

Static reading only; not observed in the running game.

claims.statement: Only the player's draw pile is shuffled at a set change. Mode 9's single indirect call is the duel's +0x810 shuffle method, and its base and count arguments are loaded from the side-0 block ($s1 = duel+0x59C, fields +0x04 and +0x08). No equivalent call is made for the side-1 block, and F0x8009DA68, the routine that handles side 1, contains no call instruction at all.
claims.coverage: Every call in both routines was enumerated rather than argued from prose: an awk match for jal/jalr over lines 31602-31639, the whole of F0x800A1A5C from its prologue to its jr $ra, returns exactly five sites (F0x800A19F8, F0x8009DA68, the +0x810 jalr, F0x8009EDCC, F0x8009D9E4); the same matcher over lines 27509-27603, the whole of F0x8009DA68, returns zero. A shuffle reached through F0x8009EDCC or F0x8009D9E4 would not be caught by that matcher; both were read and neither shuffles.
limitations: Static reading only; not observed in the running game.

claims.statement: A set is decided on total HP remaining, and a tie goes to side 1. Mode 8's state machine F0x800a0f94 decides it in states 9 and 10 by comparing side 1's total HP at +0x666 against side 0's at +0x59e: cardgame.s .L0x0001e438-.L0x0001e458 loads both halfwords, executes `slt $v0, $v1` so v0 is set only when +0x666 is strictly below +0x59e, and writes 0 into the set-winner byte +0x301 on that path and 1 on the fall-through. Side 0 is the player, so the player takes the set only on a strict win, which is escardgm.toml's 'It's a draw so you, the challenger, lose.' stated in code. The totals are plain sums of the live field slots recomputed by F0x800a0acc, so the attack has already been applied to the individual Digimon by the time the comparison runs.

The card duel view's counter setter (slot +0xEA0) dispatches on its arm argument through the ten-word table at 0x80083778 after checking the arm is below 10 (cardgame.s L26515, L26518). Arm 8 is 0x8009CC08 and arm 9 is 0x8009CC28 (table entries at L704 and L705). Both compute the same base, the view plus 0x54 times the side argument, and then arm 8 stores its value as a HALFWORD at +0x70 of that base (L26596) while arm 9 stores a halfword at +0x72 (L26603). Together with the separately recorded claim that F0x80088F78 pushes duel+0x428 and +0x42C to side 0's arms 8 and 9 and duel+0x430 and +0x434 to side 1's, this fixes those four duel fields to the two halfword panel fields +0x70 and +0x72, one pair per side.
claims.coverage: Only arms 8 and 9 were read; the claim makes no statement about the other eight arms. The bound of ten is quoted from the range check itself rather than inferred from the table, and the table's tenth word at L706 is 0x8009D7B4, which is outside the run of ten consecutive arm bodies and is not treated as an eleventh arm.
limitations: Which HUD element the panel fields +0x70 and +0x72 draw is NOT established by this claim. The animation atlas of 2026-08-26 identifies them as the AP and HP plaques by cross-reference to web/assets/data/cardduel_ui.json, which is browser data at authority 6.
An arm of 10 or more falls through to a bare return, so the setter silently does nothing; this was read from the branch target but no caller was checked for whether that can happen.

claims.statement: CARDDATA archive slot 2 renders against texture page 0 and slot 3 against texture page 1. The scene entry F0x80095bfc uploads the two pages naming their VRAM destinations outright, sp34(0x280, 0) before unk424(0x025D0000) and sp34(0x340, 0) before unk424(0x025D0001). Every duel draw then selects its page with sp84 before naming its pack, and the two never cross: sp84(0x280, 0) always accompanies handle 0x025D0002 and sp84(0x340, 0) always accompanies 0x025D0003, across all 20 and 23 call sites. This matters because both sprite directories' frame u values are below 256, so the usual u // 256 atlas rule cannot pick the page. Two independent checks agree: rendering either directory against the other page produces incoherent colour noise, and each directory's CLUT rows (slot 2 at cy 156..167 with cx 48; slot 3 at cy 241..251 with cx 0/16/32/48) carry palette data only on its own page.

The duel's full-screen wash is one colour transition per call, not one countdown over the whole white-black-white sequence. The wash routine is F0x800a3558 (installed at +0x6C by F0x800a367c); it stores the same immediate into the countdown +0x54 and the interpolation denominator +0x58, and its tick F0x800a3488 decrements the countdown by the shared frame-delta getter at 0x8004DF9C before interpolating. The duel open sets white then fades to black with countdown 100 (cardgame.s:33005 li v0,0x64; hold 0 at :33007), and the duel close fades black to white with the same countdown 100 (cardgame.s:33043; hold 0), so at one unit per 60 Hz frame each is about 1.667 s. The other two callers are not the start/end wash: F0x800a0f94 is a grey-to-black flash of 10 units with hold 1 (cardgame.s:31188), and F0x8009e560 is a card-effect colour flash of 10 units, or 15 when the mode byte is 2, with hold 1 (cardgame.s:28230 and :28243).
claims.notes: Static authority 2/3. Start/end role is read from code shape (state 0 opens the board, state 1 closes), not a rig capture.
claims.coverage: All four call sites and the two countdown stores were read at their exact cardgame.s lines, and the tick's decrement was read at its assembly. The unit (one countdown unit = one 60 Hz frame) is claimed from the prior candidate cardduel-beat-durations-are-sixtieths-not-frames-2026-08-27 and three RAM dumps, NOT re-established here; the static evidence names the frame-delta slot 0x8004DF9C, not its boot-installed target.
claims.frontier_rationale: Closes cardduel-gap A7 duration (UNDECODED); wiring the start/end wash into the walker is a separate implementation gap.

claims.statement: Four further duel geometry tables in pro/cardgame.s, all read as {u16 x, u16 y} pairs anchored by the RECT at 0x800A5938 = {0,0,320,240}. (1) 0x800A5978, indexed i * 4 by F0x80096c20: three board slot positions (73,97), (123,97), (173,97), drawn with pivot (+4, +0x17). The Summon Phase's end-of-turn button chain is: Square (0xF) raises the picker's commit prompt unconditionally (state 6 -> the 0x13-frame animation -> state 7, 'Put in Field? Yes/No', answer word +0x440 starting at Yes); Circle (0xD) is the only finish button - Yes returns the picker done, No drops back to the picker; Cross (0xE) answers No and drops back to the picker, so Cross does not end the turn; Up/Down (4/6) toggle the answer; Triangle is not read at the prompt. The picker does not commit its marks: the Summon Phase driver F0x800A0B80 calls duel method +0x818 (F0x800A0754) once per side after the picker returns.
claims.notes: Read 2026-09-14 from the three per-function assembly closures (authority 2; cardgame load base 0x80082CB0, so cardgame.s file 0x4c90-0x4ea4 is F0x800878B4 and file 0x5bd8-0x5d74 is F0x80087EDC state 7). Not re-read here: the state 0xB/0xC/0xD body beyond its return to state 3, and the mark toggle F0x80087458 internals (already covered by the 2026-09-13 claim).

claims.statement: Surrendering from the in-duel inspect menu ends the duel through the screen's own teardown rather than through the set-award machine. The Surrender row raises escardgm 44 'Are you sure?' and, on Yes, the inspect machine returns 2; the duel's tick treats a 2 as end-of-duel and the teardown stores 1 into duel+0x303 before starting the fade. It never writes duel+0x301, the byte the set-end machine uses to record who took the set.
claims.notes: NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a surrender is recorded as a loss anywhere else, and what the scores read afterwards. duel+0x301 is written only on the set-end path.
claims.coverage: cardgame overlay: the surrender arm of F0x800A2608 and the duel teardown F0x800A2F00

claims.statement: A duel that ends without a player win IS recorded as a loss, through exactly the same end-of-battle path a decided duel uses. The teardown writes 1 into the duel's end byte, and the duel's mode-2 loop reads that byte once (cardgame.s:33076) and then runs the recording: it tests the duel's lost flag at +0x302 (cardgame.s:33082) and, when that flag is set, clears the saved 'the player won' word at 0x80048AC0 and does NOT increment the saved win count at 0x80048D34 + [duel+0x2EC] + 0x7C; the loop then stamps the end byte to 2 so it happens once. The flag is raised when the duel is set up (cardgame.s:31658). It is written in FIVE places in the overlay, not three: cardgame.s:31658 (setup, raised), :31771 (raised on match decision 2), :31775 (cleared on match decision 3), and two more that a scan reading instructions in order does not see because they sit in jump delay slots -- :31421 clears it and :31441 raises it, on the two match-result banner arms. So the default is lost and only a decision of 3, or the banner arm at :31421, clears it. That a player-initiated SURRENDER specifically reaches this path is NOT established: no surrender handler has been located, and what is shown here is the general rule that any ending not routed through those two clearing sites leaves the flag set. Whether a separate loss counter exists elsewhere is also NOT established.
claims.notes: CORRECTION 2026-08-28 after an independent review recorded needs_evidence. The review was right on both counts and both are fixed here. First, the earlier coverage named three writers of +0x302 and asserted the flag was 'cleared in exactly one place'; an exhaustive enumeration finds five stores, and the two the old coverage missed are in branch delay slots -- the exact failure mode already on record in this repository for ceremony-issuer scans. Second, the headline word 'surrender' had no citation anywhere in the packet; no surrender handler was ever located, so the statement is narrowed to what the code shows and the surrender-specific claim is withdrawn pending that handler. The unevidenced negative about a separate loss counter is likewise downgraded to unestablished. Status held at candidate.
claims.coverage: The writer census is exhaustive over cardgame.s: every occurrence of the text '0x302(' in the file was enumerated, giving seven sites -- five stores (31421, 31441, 31658, 31771, 31775) and two loads (33082, 33111). That enumeration is what found the two delay-slot stores the earlier coverage missed, and it would equally have found a sixth. It is scoped to this one overlay and to the literal offset spelling, so a write through a computed pointer or from another overlay would NOT appear. No exhaustive search was run for a separate loss tally, which is why that clause is now stated as unestablished rather than as a negative finding.

claims.statement: The card duel's three selection handlers each read the pad service's auto-repeat word as well as its pressed word for the direction bits. The hand selector F0x800875AC and the summon selector F0x800878B4 load 0x8004B7D0->0x3FC (repeat) and 0x3F4 (pressed), mask each with (1<<bit) for bits 7 (left/decrease) and 5 (right/increase) and OR the results, so a held direction repeats; both clamp at the ends (cursor > 0 for left, cursor < count-1 for right) and move through F0x800870A4 (hand, count at candidate+0xA) or F0x80086F24 (board). The board selector F0x80087B80 does the same for bits 7/5, clamps and moves through F0x80086F24; its triangle arm plays 0x800450BD and sets +0x423 = 0xA. Both movers play packed sound 0x0004001B on every move. The hand's cross only starts a play when the highlighted entry's +0x446 is nonzero; the summon's cross gates on F0x80087458. The walker clamps, plays the same cursor sound, and (as of 2026-09-14) repeats held directions on the shared edge/16/6/4 curve.
claims.notes: The walker's implementation: left/right clamp with the cursor sound (DUEL_SOUND.cursor = SYSTEM06 0x4001B, matching the movers); stepHeld wires the held direction to the shared pad curve (web/cardduel.js, turn 81). The board handler has no cross arm in its own body; its confirm comes from the caller, as the hand's does via +0x423.
claims.coverage: Read all three handler bodies in the original cardgame overlay (F0x800875AC, F0x800878B4, F0x80087B80) plus the two movers (F0x800870A4, F0x80086F24) and the folder chooser F0x8009F110; drove the walker's held repeat live (tools/verify_cardduel_hold_repeat.mjs).

claims.statement: Who acts first inside Load and Compile is the coin-toss outcome, carried in duel+0x2F5. The play machine's reset arm, which jump-table entry 0 and the out-of-range default both reach, loads duel+0x2F5 and writes it into both turn-order registers duel+0x578 and duel+0x579 while clearing the play counter duel+0x575, the consecutive-pass counter duel+0x577 and the three play-history halfwords. The byte's only writers are in mode 3, which sets it to whether the selector result duel+0x440 is non-zero.
claims.coverage: 'Only' was tested by a literal text search of the whole overlay assembly for the string 0x2f5( , which returns exactly three sites: two stores at lines 29466-29467 inside mode 3 and one load at line 29799 inside the play machine's reset arm. That matcher would miss an access through a different base register or a computed offset, and the corpus searched is ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003/pro/cardgame.s alone, so a resident routine holding a pointer to the duel could reach the byte unmatched.
limitations: Which side duel+0x440 == 1 means is inherited from the already-decoded opcode 0xA7 ceremony, model document section G.5; neither half of it was re-read here.
Static reading only; not observed in the running game.
claims.notes: Rests at partially_verified. The bundle carries one of mode 3's two stores, the reset arm's load and one of its two stores. Missing artifact for promotion: the second store at .L0x0001cc50, the mirror store into duel+0x579 at .L0x0001d1ac, and the jump-table entry that shows the arm is the reset arm rather than an ordinary state.

claims.statement: The reading that who goes first is settled once per duel, recorded in docs/research/ui/cardgame-divergence-2026-08-21.md item 6 on the grounds that the Calumon draw lives in mode 2 and the machine never returns to mode 2, is WRONG. The draw is in mode 3, and the mode table returns to mode 3 after both the Battle Phase and the set change, so the toss is re-run every set. The premise was a misattribution of the ceremony to the wrong mode, and the conclusion inverted the actual behaviour.
claims.contradiction_rationale: The claim rested on the ceremony being in mode 2. The mode dispatcher sends mode 2 to the folder chooser F0x8009F110, whose decompiled body contains neither the 0xA7 latch nor any write to duel+0x2F5, while mode 3's routine F0x8009F8C0 contains both. The mode table then returns to 3 from both 8 and 9.
claims.coverage: Both candidate modes were checked rather than one: F0x8009F110 was searched for the 0xA7 latch and for duel+0x2F5 and has neither, and F0x8009F8C0 was read in full and has both.
limitations: Static reading only. The re-run has NOT been observed in the running game: the rig session of 2026-08-24 logged the seed as unchanged across one set boundary, but the input was a blind button pulse and a re-toss can return the same answer, so that observation neither confirms nor refutes this.
This corrects an implementation change made earlier the same day that had made the walker draw once per duel. That change has been reverted.

Which of the two faces the player must pick to lead is traced as a chain but its first link -- that face 0x57 is Calumon -- rests on the combo announcement's fallback pairing face 0x57 with card 0x13B, which is suggestive rather than a rendering proof.

claims.statement: Within a Load or Compile turn the plays resolve newest first, and a card that runs effect opcode 0x41 takes the play before it off the queue unrun. The effect driver F0x800A2180's fetch arm loads the turn's play count duel+0x575, subtracts one, scales by the eight-byte history stride and reads that entry's card slot at +0x580, so the program it runs is always the most recent play. When a program ends, the same driver stores play count minus one into duel+0x575, or play count minus TWO when duel+0x4dd is non-zero. In ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003/pro/cardgame.s the byte duel+0x4dd is written at exactly two sites: the driver clears it on the step before it starts a program, and the dispatch block at 0x800855a8 sets it, which cardgame-opcode-registry.json gives as the update target of effect opcode 0x41 - the cancel carried by Freeze Bug and Cancel Wheel.
claims.notes: Static reading only; not observed in the running game. Answers the order question that cardduel-effects-resolve-after-the-turn-2026-08-21 explicitly left open ('The statement does not assert in what order the interpreter resolves them'). Player-visible consequence: a cancel card played in answer to a Program card stops that card's effect, which is what its printed text says and what an oldest-first reading would have made impossible. Wired into the walker the same day: engine/systems/card-battle.ts pumpProgramTurns and engine/systems/card-effect-vm.ts opcode 0x41, with tests in tests/card-battle.test.js.
claims.coverage: The 'exactly two sites' clause was tested by matching the literal offset text 0x4dd( over the whole of pro/cardgame.s, which returns three lines and no more: the load in the completion arm at L32299 and the two stores named, at L32124 and L2635. That matcher would not catch a write through a computed offset or a different base displacement, so the clause is scoped to the overlay's direct 0x4dd(base) accesses. The newest-first clause rests on the fetch arm's own three instructions, read in order with the index arithmetic; it does not assert anything about the order in which the corresponding animations play.

claims.statement: Of the 42 CardDuelView method slots +0xEA0..+0xF44 that createCardBattleContext fills, 39 are dispatched from somewhere inside pro/cardgame.s and three are not: +0xEDC (0x8009BFCC), +0xEE0 (0x8009C010) and +0xF04 (0x8009CE94). This sharpens cardanim-fanout-pitch-41px, which reports that no jal and no pointer-table word reaches the row-layout helper 0x8009CE94 and concludes that its row origins are undecoded. The helper is in fact installed, at view slot +0xF04, by a register-constructed store no text search can see - so the earlier statement's literal wording held only because it asked about jal targets and .word entries. The stronger and more useful fact is that nothing in the overlay invokes slot +0xF04 at all, so the row origins cannot be recovered from cardgame alone. Recorded as candidate rather than partially_verified because the survey rests on this tool's object-field dispatch detection, which resolved 39 of 42 slots and may miss a dispatch whose base register it failed to track.

Correcting an over-reach recorded earlier the same day. duel+0x46F is a shared selection-flag array that several unrelated routines read, and it IS the array the per-slot stat applicator F0x8008DEF8 consumes -- so the half of row 5 that named 'F0x8008DEF8 over the +0x46F flags' was right, and only its 'walked by F0x800915D4' clause was wrong. Three distinct consumers are now established: F0x8008DEF8 reads it as twelve field slots to apply stat deltas; F0x800915D4 reads it as twelve field slots to remove cards (opcodes 0x4D/0x4E); and F0x800A0590 reads the SAME array indexed by HAND position, bounded by the per-player block's +0x0A hand count (lh 0xa($a1) at 0x800a0590, lb 0x46f at 0x800a05a8), to delete flagged cards from a hand. The array is therefore not specific to field slots at all, and the earlier statement that it is 'not a battle-damage target list' was wrong in the other direction: it is that list, among other uses. What remains genuinely unresolved is which code sets the flags in each context.

Those were computed from 0x72C, but 0x72C is the slot-count byte and the slot record begins at 0x72E, so the correct record-relative names are +0x0A and +0x00. claims.statement: The premise behind the open 'booster pack grant' question is wrong: 0x80048AC0 is not a card counter or any card-system variable, it is the SECOND WORD OF STORY FLAG BANK 0. The flag setter F0x800165AC takes a flag id, splits it into a bank selector (id >> 8) & 0xFFFE and a bit index id & 0x1FF, and for bank 0 calls the bit-set helper F0x800155D4 with the base D0x80048ABC; a 0x1FF bit index spans 512 bits, i.e. 64 bytes, so bank 0 runs 0x80048ABC..0x80048AFB and 0x80048AC0 is that base plus 4, holding flags 32..63. The only code that names 0x80048AC0 symbolically is the housekeeping routine at 0x80016A20, which reads the word, sets flag 0x10 to 1 when any bit in it is set and to 0 otherwise, and then zeroes the whole word, clearing flags 32..63. Nothing writes 0x80048AC0 under its own name because flags in that range are written through the bank base plus an offset, which is exactly the base-relative blindness a symbol search cannot see. Chasing writers of 0x80048AC0 therefore cannot succeed as a route to the booster pack; the grant, if it exists, is a flag in the 32..63 range or an item grant elsewhere, and belongs to the story-flag machinery rather than to this address.
claims.notes: Resolves the premise of worklist item 15 (the booster pack promised by escardgm.toml but absent from cardgame). LIMITATIONS: the bit-set helper F0x800155D4 was not opened, so the exact bit-to-address mapping inside the bank is inferred from the 0x1FF mask and the base argument rather than read; and no attempt was made here to identify which flag id, if any, corresponds to the booster pack. Also worth carrying forward: the main executable assembly lives at ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003/exe/fns.s and IS in the research index, contrary to an assumption made earlier in this session that only its decompilation was available. That means claims resting on exe-decomp/c/*.c can be re-anchored from authority 3 to authority 2.

claims.statement: docs/research/card/card-duel-engine-2026-08-04.md describes 0x800a4df4 in pro/cardgame.s as 'the card catalog, stride 0x2c' with +0x01 = AP and +0x02 = HP. That is wrong on both counts. The region cannot hold a 315-card catalog: its next referenced address is 0x800a5844, so it spans 0xa50 = 2640 bytes = exactly 60 records of 0x2c, and 60 is precisely the number of Program cards in the real catalog (card ids 1..60, the records whose +0x03 kind byte is not 0x10). claims.statement: The composite weight halfword duel+0x35E+4i, previously recorded as a stored value with no demonstrated consumer, HAS a reader, and reading it corrects which key is primary. The function at 0x8009D8xx is an in-place exchange (bubble) sort over the halfword array at duel+0x6C8, whose length is the halfword at duel+0x66E. Each array element is a card instance reference v, mapped to its per-instance record by (v - 0x28) * 4 added to the duel base, which is what puts the class byte at +0x35C and the composite weight at +0x35E. The comparator is two-level: it loads both elements' class bytes into $a2 and $a1 and swaps when `slt $a0, $a1, $a2` holds, i.e. when the second element's class is LESS than the first's; only when the two class bytes are EQUAL does it fall through to `slt $v0, $a3`, the two-operand form comparing the two +0x35E weights, and swap on that. So the RAW CLASS BYTE at +0x35C is the primary sort key and the composite weight at +0x35E is the TIE-BREAK - the reverse of the earlier description, which called +0x35E the primary sort weight. Because the composite is built as the class's table weight plus the deck slot index, the tie-break reduces to deck order within a class, which is why the earlier reading looked self-consistent despite inverting the two keys.

The opponent's Program-card policy is F0x8009D8FC followed by F0x800A4978, called only from state 3 of the play machine F0x8009FDD8. F0x8009D8FC bubble-sorts the opponent's hand (duel+0x6C8, count duel+0x66E) by the per-card AI record at duel+0x35C: class descending, then priority ascending. F0x800A4978 then walks that sorted hand and marks the FIRST entry that passes four gates - the wanted class (1 in the Load Phase, 3 in the Compile Phase, found via F0x800A4924), usability now (F0x80085F38), a legal target (F0x800A36E4 on card record +0x00), and a beneficial simulation (F0x800A44F0, or F0x800A45F8 on the response path) - by setting duel+0x46F for that hand index, and returns 1. It is greedy and first-match: there is no scoring across candidates and no lookahead. The only comparison of whole boards is the Compile-Phase gate, which returns 0 without playing when (duel+0x305 & 1) or when F0x800A3934(duel, 0, 0) < F0x800A3934(duel, 1, 0). The simulators also choose the target and write it into the play-history entry at +0x586, using F0x800A3D90 (pick the field slot whose exclusion gives the lowest board score), F0x800A41F8 (narrow to slots the amount would kill), F0x800A3F48 / F0x800A4078 (narrow to green / red), and F0x800A4328 (pick the hand card with the smallest card record +0x08). Two amount tables keyed by card id supply the numbers: F0x800A4440 damage {0x12:60, 0x15:30, 0x2E:30, 0x14:15, 0x38:10} and F0x800A4494 buff {0x0C:50, 0x03:30, 0x28:30, 0x0F:20, 0x02:15, 0x3A:10}. Within cardgame.s, and with tools/run-overlay-scan.sh as the matcher over that file alone, the AI cluster at 0x800A3934..0x800A4DFF contains no RNG call, no read of the player's hand array at duel+0x600, and no difficulty parameter; per-opponent variation comes only from the deck, the class bytes and the response list. Those three findings are absences within cardgame.s, not within the program. What class 1..7 means per card is not established, nor is the meaning of duel+0x305, nor of card record +0x08.

claims.contradiction_rationale: The claim cardgame-ai-is-greedy-first-match-with-no-rng states that within cardgame.s the AI cluster 'contains no RNG call, no read of the player's hand array at duel+0x600, and no difficulty parameter'. The RNG and difficulty legs stand and are strengthened by the closed callee enumeration. The hand leg is literally true of the cluster's own instructions but misleading about its behaviour: the cluster calls F0x800A36E4 on every candidate card, and that function calls F0x8008EC44 against side 0's hand, deck and trash for targeting kinds 0x7F, 0x72 and 0x80, reading card identities to answer whether a legal target exists. The original phrasing invited the reading 'the AI has no access to hidden information', which is false. This entry narrows that one leg; it does not retract the claim as a whole.
claims.statement: OVERSTATED: 'no read of the player's hand array at duel+0x600' in cardgame-ai-is-greedy-first-match-with-no-rng. True of the AI cluster's own instructions, false of its behaviour - the cluster's legality gate F0x800A36E4 probes side 0's hand, deck and trash through F0x8008EC44. See cardgame-ai-probes-hidden-zones-for-legality-only. The no-RNG and no-difficulty-parameter legs of that claim are unaffected and are strengthened by the closed callee set.

THE AI PLAY CLASSES ARE A CARD-TYPE AND PRIORITY SPLIT, which answers what the 1..7 domain means. Joining all 6800 shipped deck entries to the extracted catalog and grouping by class gives an almost perfectly clean separation by card kind: class 1 is 99.9% Program cards (1029 entries), class 2 is 99.6% DIGIMON (3394 entries, the bulk of every deck), class 3 is 99.7% Program (1942), class 4 is 100% Program (302), and class 5 is 94.7% Digimon (132). Because the AI's hand sort takes the class byte as its PRIMARY ascending key, the class number IS the play order: the opponent considers its class-1 Programs first, then summons from its class-2 Digimon, then its class-3 and class-4 Programs. Class 5 is the exception already recorded - those Digimon are skipped by the summon pass entirely, so they are dead weight the opponent holds. Class 4 is distinctive beyond its type: its mean strength rank is 15 of 315, meaning it is a small elite set of the game's rarest Program cards, held to the back of the order. A CONSEQUENCE FOR THE WEIGHT TABLE: the seven per-class weights at 0x800837A0 (400/300/500/200/600/100/700) are functionally DEAD. They only ever enter the composite tie-break at duel+0x35E, which the comparator reaches solely when two cards share a class - and cards of the same class share the same weight, so the comparison reduces to deck index every time. No ordering in the shipped game depends on the weight values.

Correction to cardgame-ai-probes-hidden-zones-for-legality-only, which describes the AI cluster's callee set as closed and consisting of thirteen internal functions 'plus exactly four externals: F0x8001EBF8, F0x80083E34, F0x80085F38 and F0x800A36E4'. That undercounts. The direct-call closure of F0x800A4978 and F0x8009D8FC is 20 overlay functions: F0x80083E34, F0x80085F38, F0x8008EC44, F0x8008EEC8, F0x8009D8FC, F0x800A36E4, F0x800A3934, F0x800A3D90, F0x800A3E9C, F0x800A3F48, F0x800A4078, F0x800A41A8, F0x800A41F8, F0x800A4328, F0x800A4440, F0x800A4494, F0x800A44F0, F0x800A45F8, F0x800A4924 and F0x800A4978, plus one resident import, F0x8001EBF8. F0x8008EC44 and F0x8008EEC8 are reached through F0x800A36E4 and belong in the set; the original claim's own prose already describes F0x8008EC44's behaviour while its enumeration excludes it. The correction does not change that claim's conclusion, since neither added function reaches a random source or the player's hand array.

The opponent AI's relationship to hidden information is narrower than 'it never reads the player's hand', and that stronger phrasing is withdrawn. A call-graph audit of the cluster 0x800A3934..0x800A4DFF finds no reference to duel+0x600 (the player's hand array), +0x5A6 (its count) or +0x59C/+0x59E in any of its own functions, and no pointer passed out of the cluster; its callee set is closed and consists of F0x800A4924, F0x800A3934, F0x800A3D90, F0x800A3E9C, F0x800A3F48, F0x800A4078, F0x800A41A8, F0x800A41F8, F0x800A4328, F0x800A4440, F0x800A4494, F0x800A44F0 and F0x800A45F8 internally, plus exactly four externals: F0x8001EBF8, F0x80083E34, F0x80085F38 and F0x800A36E4. However F0x800A36E4, the targeting-legality gate the AI calls for every candidate card, dispatches several kinds to F0x8008EC44(duel, side, zone, kindMask) with side 0 and zone 2, 3 or 4 - kind 0x7F is (0, hand), 0x72 is (0, deck), 0x80 is (0, trash) - and F0x8008EC44 walks that zone, resolves each entry through duel+0x50 to its card record, filters on the record's kind and colour bytes, sets duel+0x446 flags on matches and returns whether any matched. So the AI does obtain an existence answer about zones the human player cannot see, computed from actual card identities. What it does not do is score those contents: no path feeds the player's hand, deck or trash into the board evaluator F0x800A3934 or into the choice between candidate plays, which remains the greedy first-match over its own priority-sorted hand. The accurate statement is therefore: the AI probes hidden zones for target legality but does not evaluate their contents. Separately, the 'no RNG' finding is upgraded rather than weakened - the callee set above is complete and contains no random-number call, making that a call-graph absence rather than an offset-scan one.

The opponent's Digimon summon choice is F0x8008C5F0, the update handler of effect opcode 0x9D, which the Summon Phase issues at mode 6 sub-step 2 immediately after sorting the AI hand. It is a single greedy pass: for each entry of the opponent's hand in priority-sorted order it clears duel+0x46F[i], and then, if the running count duel+0x444 is below 6 and F0x80085FD0(duel, duel+0x670, instance) accepts the card on S-Energy grounds, and the per-card AI class at duel+0x35C[(instance - 0x28)] is not 5, it calls F0x8008735C to spend the energy, sets duel+0x46F[i] = 1 and increments duel+0x444. Mode 6 sub-step 3 then calls the duel method at +0x818, F0x800A0754, which commits exactly those flagged cards to the field. So the AI summons every affordable Digimon in its hand, in class-then-deck order, until the field holds six; there is no evaluation, no comparison against the player's board, and no randomness. Class 5 is excluded from summoning. The opcode's enter phase seeds duel+0x444 to 0, so that byte serves as both the selection quota and the running summon count. This closes the open item that mode 6 commits +0x46F flags nobody in the AI cluster sets: the setter is an effect-opcode handler, not part of the AI cluster at 0x800A3934..0x800A4DFF.

claims.statement: F0x8009E560 spawns an on-screen ANNOUNCEMENT from a request code in duel+0x306. The code, minus one, indexes a table of FOUR-BYTE records at 0x800A5D14; byte 3 of the record selects the kind and is passed to the constructor F0x800A367C, while bytes 0, 1 and 2 are handed straight to the new object's first method as its parameters. A second method call then receives a value that is 0x0F when the kind is 2 and 0x0A otherwise, so one kind of announcement is configured differently from the rest. The request field is cleared afterwards, making it a one-shot. Separately F0x800A1DB8 is a mode body with the usual shape: a one-shot guard at duel+0x4E8 does the entry work - raising duel+0x49D and +0x499 and calling the view's +0xEC8 - and every later call polls, returning 1 only once the view reports state 2 and no effect is pending at duel+0x498.

The deck field duel+0x30A CHANGES MEANING during a duel, which bears directly on the unexplained availability group 7. At load the CARD_NPC loader fills +0x30A+2i from deck entry byte +0x02, the per-set availability group, and F0x80085DE8 sorts the 40 entries by it so the earliest-available cards sit at the front. But F0x800907AC, the draw path, does two things after removing a card: it compacts the remaining entries forward and decrements both availability counts duel+0x41B and +0x41C, and then it runs a second loop over all 40 entries from 0x27 down to 0 - the full array from +0x30A to +0x358 - OVERWRITING each entry's +0x30A with its own position. From the first draw onward the field therefore holds a positional index, not a group. This makes the earlier reading of the field as 'the availability group' true only of the pre-draw state. It also offers a candidate explanation for the anomaly recorded against cardnpc-deck-entry-byte-02-is-the-per-set-availability-group, that 2756 of 6800 shipped deck entries carry group 7 which no best-of-three threshold can admit: if the group's only job is to ORDER the deck before play, then group 7 marks the cards that sort to the BACK, and they become reachable as the deck is drawn down and the field is re-stamped - not permanently unusable. RECORDED AS CANDIDATE: the re-stamping is directly evidenced, but the conclusion that group 7 cards become playable through it is an inference and was not traced to a draw that actually reaches them.

The six opcode-registry rows in the model's section G.0 that carry a bare function name with no described action - 0x1B, 0x1C/0x1D, 0x41, 0x4D/0x4E, 0x5A and 0x9E - are now read, and five of the six are ENTER-PHASE LATCHES with no board effect of their own. Each is between four and nine lines: it zeroes some prefix of the scratch block at duel+0x424..+0x438 and sets the step byte duel+0x422 to 1, which hands the actual work to the correspondingly numbered case of the interpreter's second switch. The prefix length is the only thing that varies and it is deliberate: 0x1C/0x1D clear through +0x438 inclusive, 0x5A clears the same block but STOPS at +0x434 leaving +0x438 intact, and 0x4D/0x4E clear only +0x428. So an opcode can preserve the reused +0x438 across its own execution by choosing the shorter clear. Two carry real content. Opcode 0x9E is a BOARD REFRESH request: it resets the cursor, calls view methods +0xECC and +0xEC8 and raises duel+0x49C, +0x49D and +0x499 - and +0x49C is exactly the pending-refresh flag the full board resync F0x8009E024 consumes and then clears, so 0x9E is how an effect says 'redraw everything'. Opcode 0x1B puts a card into view slot 0x11, the combo display slot, taking the card id from duel+0x304 minus one and popping it in with a scale animation. Opcode 0x41 is a latch that additionally notifies the view about the played-card stack entry two below the top rather than the top one. This narrows what 'call map, not a decode' means for these rows: the enter phase genuinely has almost nothing in it.

F0x80093710 is the Battle-phase attack presentation, and it bears on the open question of how battle damage is distributed across slots: in this function it is NOT distributed at all. The per-slot loop is an ANIMATION schedule - it starts one attacker's animation every 0x1C ticks while the tick counter is below slot-count times 0x1C, and each started slot is marked busy - but the damage itself is a SINGLE running total. The accumulator duel+0x430 is stepped down by duel+0x434 each tick and CLAMPED at a floor that is the opposing side's stored value at +0x59E shifted left by 8, and that running value is pushed to the view for the OPPOSING side under category 9; once the per-slot window ends, +0x430 is snapped exactly to that floor. The acting side's own figure animates separately under category 8 on a different ramp. So the post-battle totals are computed elsewhere and stored at +0x59E, and this function only counts the displayed number down to meet them. This claim describes the PRESENTATION path only; it does not establish where the totals at +0x59E are computed, and therefore does not by itself prove that no per-slot distribution happens in that computation.

Mode 8, the last mode of the repeating round, is itself a 27-state machine. F0x800a0f94 (cardgame.s L30912-L31271) reads the sub-step byte duel+0x2f9, bounds it to 0..0x1a and jumps through the 27-entry table at 0x80083990 (cardgame.s L830-L856, terminated by a 0x00000000 word at L857). Its entry hook F0x800a0f4c (L30894-L30911) resets +0x2f9 to 0 and calls context dispatch slot +0xec8, so the machine restarts at state 0 each round. The function returns 0 to stay in the mode, 1 from state 0x1a (target 0x800a19d0) and 2 from state 0x19 (target 0x800a19c8); mode 8's update stub turns return 1 into pending mode 9 and return 2 into an immediate finished report from the duel driver. States 0x14 and 0x17 gate on two resident pad/flag queries (ids 0xd and 0xe through the function-pointer table at 0x8004b7d0) before setting +0x2f9 = 0x19, and state 0x12 selects message id 0x1c or 0x1d from the byte +0x301 before setting +0x2f9 = 0x1a. The byte +0x2f9 is not a global phase index: modes 1, 3 and 4 also use it as their own small sub-step counter, and the 27-entry table belongs to mode 8 alone.

The open question 'what sets the duel+0x46F flags during Battle state 9, so that per-slot damage distribution can be recovered' rests on a false premise: nothing in the Battle Phase sets them. The Battle-Phase driver F0x800A0F94 does its work by writing the pending-opcode byte duel+0x421 and setting duel+0x2F4, i.e. by ISSUING effect opcodes through the interpreter's chaining latch rather than calling handlers directly; states 1, 2 and 8 issue opcodes 0x19, 0x1A and 0x1B. Those opcodes resolve to just four handlers, F0x800942DC, F0x8009403C, F0x80093C18 and F0x80093CAC, and the attack handler F0x800942DC applies its result by ADDING accumulated deltas from duel+0x42C and duel+0x430 to a per-player block's AP and HP TOTALS at block+0x00 and block+0x02, then pushing the new totals to view fields 8 and 9. Exactly ten functions in the whole overlay write duel+0x46F and none of the four is among them; those ten are selection, targeting and summon handlers. Battle damage is therefore applied to the side totals, which is why totals reconcile and per-Digimon figures never did - the game does not compute a per-slot breakdown during the Battle Phase for anything to recover.

The Battle-Phase machine F0x800A0F94's presentation states, anchored at authority 2: the combo-announcement states (1, 2, 8) latch pending effect opcodes 0x19/0x1A/0x1B into duel+0x421 rather than drawing directly; the set-award compare reads the two side totals at +0x59E and +0x666 and, because the slt result is false on an equal total, awards the set to side 1 (the opponent); the counter-roll state runs 51 ticks (slti 0x33) and on its first tick plays packed sound 0x009C0002 and creates a grey 0x80 flash; the result window is dismissed by logical 0xD or 0xE (Circle or Cross) read from the pressed word 0x3F4.

The combo arithmetic itself is not re-derived (already shipped); the view methods the states call were not read.
