claims.statement: Battle state 9 is the set-resolution test, not a damage step. It runs only when one side's field count has reached zero (duel+0x72C or duel+0x79E), and then sets the set-winner byte duel+0x301 from a single comparison of the two sides' stored HP totals: 0 when side 1's total at duel+0x666 is less than side 0's at duel+0x59E, and 1 otherwise - so an exact tie takes the else branch and goes to side 1. It then moves to state 0xB, or to state 0xA when the winner's field is empty while the loser's is not. When neither field is empty it instead goes to state 3 and calls view+0xEAC(5, 5, 0xD, 0, 0x6E). This independently corroborates cardduel-set-goes-to-higher-total-hp-tie-to-side-one from the Battle-Phase side.

BATTLE DAMAGE IS HELD PER SLOT; the side totals are DERIVED SUMS. F0x80094848, the update phase of opcode 0x5A, walks the acting side's field slots - +0x72C of them at stride 0xE - accumulating each slot record's two stat fields into duel+0x428 and +0x42C, then walks the opposing side's +0x79E slots accumulating its two fields into +0x430 and +0x434. It compares those four sums against the four STORED totals at duel+0x59C, +0x59E, +0x664 and +0x666, and when any differs it animates each displayed figure from the stored value to the new one through the interpolator F0x80093BC4 over duel+0x424, finally OVERWRITING the stored totals with the sums. So +0x59C..+0x666 are not independent state that damage is subtracted from - they are recomputed from the individual cards every time this opcode runs. This answers the standing question of whether battle damage is distributed per slot: it is applied to individual field slots' own stats, and what the player sees as a side total is the sum of the surviving cards. It also completes the earlier reading in cardgame-battle-damage-is-a-total-drain-not-per-slot, which correctly observed the DISPLAY converging on a precomputed figure at +0x59E but could not say where that figure came from: it comes from here, as a sum.

THE BOOSTER PACK EXISTS, AND +0x7C IS YOUR STOCK OF UNOPENED PACKS. Two questions recorded separately - 'the booster-pack grant, promised in text, absent from cardgame' and 'the +0x7C reward field, the only persistent gain from winning, identity unknown' - are one mechanic, and the reason the grant looked absent is that it is NOT in pro/cardgame at all. It is in the card shop overlay pro/stcrdshp, in F0x800844B8. Opening a pack runs a loop SIX times; each iteration calls the resident RNG, reduces the value modulo 16, uses it to index a per-set pool of card ids reached through the table at 0x8008C708, and grants that id through the save struct's method pointer at +0x2720 with a quantity of one. After the six grants it DECREMENTS the byte at save + setIndex + 0x7C. A separate pass skips any set whose +0x7C is zero or less. So +0x7C is a per-set count of unopened packs: winning a duel increments it - the already-recorded 'incremented on a win, capped at 99' - and opening a pack spends one and yields six random cards from that set's pool. THIS ALSO CLOSES THE GAP flagged in cardgame-starter-deck-grant-and-the-collection-api, which noted that the shop demonstrably sells cards yet no shop code called the collection's add routine, so an unseen path had to exist. That path is the save struct's +0x2720 method pointer - an indirect call, invisible to a direct-caller query, exactly the blindness class that limitation predicted. The nine-copy cap still applies, since the add routine clamps there regardless of caller.

The booster-pack card pools are decoded and extracted. The set table is at 0x8008C708 in pro/stcrdshp (formed as lui 0x8009 / addiu -0x38f8 at 0x80084d50), with a 0x1C-byte record stride (addiu $v1,0x1c at 0x80084d2c) and terminated by a record whose first word is zero (bnez at 0x80084d38). Each record is {u32 setId, u32 poolPtr[6]}. Opening a pack draws six cards (slti $s0,0x6 at 0x80084dcc); for draw i the code reads the pool pointer at record + 4 + i*4 (lw $v1,0x4($v0) at 0x80084d9c, with the running offset advanced four bytes per iteration by addiu $s3,0x4 at 0x80084d98), calls the resident RNG through [0x8004DC0C] (lw 0x8($s8) at 0x80084d64), reduces it modulo 16 (0x80084d8c/0x80084d90) and takes the pool word at that index (0x80084dac/0x80084db0), granting it through the save struct's +0x2720 method pointer. IMPORTANT STRUCTURAL POINT: the six pointers are NOT six interchangeable pools -- draw i always uses pool i, so a pack has a fixed slot structure and the pools are ordered, with the shipped data putting commoner cards in the early slots. Each pool is 16 u32 card ids; a card's repetition within its pool IS its rarity weighting, and there is no separate weight field. Extracted 2026-08-07 by tools/extract_card_boosters.py to web/assets/data/card_boosters.json: 35 sets (ids 91 and 361..394), 210 pools, 3360 card slots, 299 distinct ids, all inside the 316-card catalog. That 3360 accounts for the whole contiguous data region previously described in web/cardstate.js as a '3361-entry weighted card-id pool' whose group boundaries were 'not referenced by any absolute address in the overlay' -- they are, by this very table, so that note is superseded.

The card artwork geometry is pinned down to actual dimensions, independently of and consistently with F0x8009D0B0. F0x8009A82C builds the textured quad for one card face: it sets the texture page base to (0x140, 0x100) and the palette base to (0x300, 0x100) - the same two origins F0x8009D0B0 computes its per-card offsets from - and gives the source window a size of 0x20 by 0x20. Within that page the card at index i is taken from U = (i >> 3) * 0x20 and V = (i & 7) * 0x20, again eight cards to a column. So a card image is 32 by 32 texels, the sheet is eight rows tall, and each card has its own palette one line below the last. The quad is drawn at the element's own fixed-point position shifted right by 8 to pixels, and the same optional scale check used across the card element helpers applies.

CARD ARTWORK GEOMETRY is decoded. F0x8009D0B0 places one card's texture and palette in VRAM from a single card index. The texture page goes to x = 0x140 + (index >> 3) * 0x10 and y = 0x100 + (index & 7) * 0x20 - so card images are stacked EIGHT to a column, each 0x20 VRAM units tall, with each new column of eight advancing 0x10 in VRAM x. The palette is separate and one line per card: x = 0x300, y = 0x100 + index, so every card carries its OWN colour table rather than sharing one. The division is a signed floor - the code adds 7 before shifting when the index is negative - so the arithmetic is exact for the whole index range rather than only for non-negative values. After placing both it invokes the object's draw method with the caller's second argument. This addresses the open question 'card artwork geometry' at the VRAM-placement level.

F0x8009AF28, F0x8009B678 and F0x8009848C are three sibling card-element draw helpers sharing one object layout: a fixed-point x at +0x00 and y at +0x04, both shifted right by 8 to reach pixels, an optional scale pair at +0x18/+0x1A that is applied only when it is not the identity 0x10001000, and per-part enable bytes at +0x45, +0x46 and +0x49. Each draws a different piece: F0x8009AF28 takes bank 0x025D0002 at frame 0x33 plus the variant byte at +0x46, offset three pixels right and two down from the anchor; F0x8009B678 takes bank 0x025D0003 at fixed frame 0x0A, drawn at the anchor itself and gated on +0x49; F0x8009848C draws frame 1 of bank 0x025D0003 with a caller-supplied horizontal scale. So a card on screen is composed of several independently enabled layers from two sprite banks, not one image.

SELF-CORRECTION. Several claims recorded earlier in this session carry a limitation saying 'sprite bank 0x025D0002 and 0x025D0003 were not resolved to any extracted asset, so what is drawn is unknown'. THAT LIMITATION WAS WRONG - the mapping was already extracted, in web/assets/data/cardduel_ui.json, and its own disasm notes cite the very functions this session was reading. The banks are the two sheets of CARDDATA.BIN, pack handle hi-word 0x25D: 0x025D0002 is carddata2, the CARD sheet, and 0x025D0003 is carddata3, the BOARD sheet. With that, the card element draw helpers attributed this session gain their subjects. A card on screen is 40 by 46 pixels and is composed of three independently drawn parts, which is what the enable bytes at +0x45, +0x46 and +0x49 switch: F0x8009B678 draws the BODY, board-sheet clip 10; F0x8009AF28 draws the BADGE at the card's top-left corner, offset (3,2), from card-sheet frame 51 plus the card's own variant byte - so the badge art varies per card; and F0x8009B028 draws up to three PIPS in a row at offset (3,21) stepping 8 pixels, from card-sheet frames 55, 56 and 57. The lesson generalises: before recording a 'not resolved to an asset' limitation, check web/assets/data for an extracted UI pack covering that overlay.

Answers row 9 of the remaining-unknowns table, which asked whether card record byte +0x03 carries both a filter class and a card-kind marker. The zone-scan gate F0x8008EC44 reads that byte (lbu $v1,0x3($v0) at 0x8008edf0) and tests it against exactly one distinguished value, 0x10 (li $v0,0x10 at 0x8008edf4). It does not compare the byte against the small 0..8 field-filter classes at all. The caller's mask argument then decides which kind is admitted: bit 0 admits entries whose byte EQUALS 0x10 and bit 1 admits every other entry. Admitted entries are further filtered by colour against the six-entry halfword mask table at 0x800A58F4 (addiu $a1,$v0,0x58f4 at 0x8008ee44) compared with card record +0x00, and a match sets that entry's flag at duel+0x446 (sb $v0,0x446($s4) at 0x8008ee10). So the byte is one enum in which 0x10 is a reserved kind marker sitting outside the small class range, and the two readings coexist without conflict -- this consumer only ever asks the kind question.

The 0x2c-stride per-card catalog record at 0x800a4df4 (cardgame.s field-getter F0x80083e34) has byte field +0x0 = family/frame-class byte, +0x1 = AP, +0x2 = HP. This is independently corroborated by a SECOND, unrelated overlay: stcrdshp.s function F0x800857b0 (the card-folder grid AP/HP readout draw) reads the identical three byte offsets (+0x0 for the frame clip, +0x1 for AP digits, +0x2 for HP digits) from a per-card record pointer obtained via F0x8001ebf8 plus a card-select call, giving two-source agreement on the same struct layout rather than a single-overlay read.

F0x8009B028 draws a row of up to THREE small icons on a card element: it iterates three sub-entries, draws one for each whose byte at +0x3E is non-zero, taking consecutive sprite frames from 0x37 upward in bank 0x025D0002, stepping eight pixels right per icon drawn and sitting 0x15 pixels below the element's anchor. Because the horizontal step advances only when an icon is actually drawn while the frame number advances every iteration, the icons PACK LEFT: three possible badges, each with its own frame, drawn without gaps. It shares the card-element layout of F0x8009AF28 and F0x8009B678 including the identity-scale check. Separately F0x8009C898 is a second tween setter on a view card slot, operating on the channel at +0x120..+0x12A rather than the +0x108..+0x11C channel that F0x8009C960 sets, and when its last argument is not 1 it additionally arms the position channel and marks the slot busy at +0x14A and +0x12E. So a card slot carries at least TWO independent animation channels.

CARDPAK +0x08 IS A CARD STRENGTH RANK, and identifying it CORRECTS the recorded behaviour of the opponent AI. The field was previously listed in the model as 'the minimisation key aiPickCheapestHandCard uses' with its meaning marked unknown. Measured across all 316 extracted catalog records it takes 315 distinct values spanning 0..314 - effectively one unique rank per card, with a single duplicate at 0 - so it is an ORDERING, not a quantity. The ordering is by card power, ascending from strongest. Sorting the 248 Digimon with non-zero stats by the field and quartering them gives mean attack 43.9, 24.8, 12.5 and 4.5 across the four quarters, a strictly monotonic fall, with a Pearson correlation of -0.92 between the field and attack. The extremes confirm it: ranks 7 through 11 are Imperialdramon-P, Armageddemon, Omnimon II and Omnimon I - the top-statted Megas - while ranks 311 to 314 are the four basic 'Power' Program cards. THE CONSEQUENCE: two AI choosers minimise this field - F0x800A4328, named aiPickCheapestHandCard in the existing research, and its sibling F0x8008C988. Minimising a strength rank selects the STRONGEST card, not the cheapest. The opponent therefore plays its best available card rather than economising, and the recorded name aiPickCheapestHandCard is misleading and should be read as 'pick the highest-ranked card'. This also explains why the AI needs a separate affordability gate at all: its chooser does not consider cost.

stcrdshp.s's folder-grid draw (F0x800857b0) validates a card id read from a per-slot array with the unsigned check (cardId-1) < 0x13a, which admits cardId values 1..314 inclusive (314 values) as populated slots. This is one less than the '315-card catalog' figure already used elsewhere in card-battle documentation; a plausible but UNPROVEN reconciliation is that id 0 is reserved as an 'empty slot' sentinel within a 315-entry catalog. This claim records only the observed bound-check constant, not a resolution of the discrepancy.

The coin-toss ceremony F0x8008985C places two face-down cards at fixed positions, left at 0x7400 and right at 0xA400 and both at height 0x6100, and assigns the two faces 0x57 and 0x58 to them in an order chosen by a single random bit stored at duel+0x434. Its tick F0x80089974 animates the two cards in one after the other four frames apart over fifteen frames, then lets the player move between them with the left/right buttons and confirm; the chosen index is committed to duel+0x440. Both cards are then turned face up, the player's first and the other second, and the outcome is whether the pick matched duel+0x434, which rewrites duel+0x440 to 1 on a match and 0 otherwise.
claims.coverage: The enter routine was read in full and the tick's steps 1 and 2 plus the reveal and outcome arms were read. NOT established and deliberately excluded from the statement: which of faces 0x57 and 0x58 the player must pick to lead. Face 0x57 is paired with card 0x13B (315, Calumon) by the combo announcement's fallback, and the seed polarity would then have to be traced through mode 3 into duel+0x2F5 to close it; that chain was not read in this pass.
limitations: Static reading only; neither screen has been observed in the running game. The rig session of 2026-08-24 entered from a save state positioned past both of them.

The folder chooser claim covers its input state only. The plate arrival order, the waits between the three plates, the closing order, and what the final step copies out of save RAM including any empty-folder fallback were NOT read, and those are the rest of CARD-Q007.
The coin-toss claim deliberately stops short of which card must be picked to lead. Asserting it would require the seed polarity through mode 3, which was not traced here.

claims.statement: THE PER-CARD CEILING IS NINE, and it lives in the SHOP, not the deck editor. The card shop's purchase path in pro/stcrdshp F0x80086DC4 makes two checks in order before completing a sale: it refuses when the player's money at save+0x6C is less than the card's price, raising message 0x13; and it refuses when the owned-count byte for that card - the array at save+0x3A2 this session identified - already equals NINE, raising message 0x14. Only if both pass does it advance to the purchase state. This completes the deck-constraint picture and REFINES cardgame-folder-copy-limit-is-the-owned-count-not-four, which correctly found that the deck editor imposes no ceiling of its own and simply offers what you own: the ceiling is real but it is upstream, at acquisition. A player can therefore hold at most nine copies of any card and, since a folder may contain as many copies as are owned, a 40-card folder can legitimately run up to nine of one card. The browser implementation's four-copy rule is wrong in both respects - wrong number, and enforced in the wrong place.

A combo run ADDS its combined AP and HP to the side's stored battle totals and leaves the run's Digimon on the board; it does not replace them with the digivolved card. The combo announcement's enter phase F0x8009403C accumulates every slot flagged at duel+0x446 into duel+0x42C (AP) and duel+0x430 (HP), each saturating at 0x63, and adds a further 0x14 to each when the run holds four or more. Its update phase F0x800942DC then loads duel+0x42C, adds it to the side's stored total AP at duel+side*0xC8+0x59C and stores the sum back, and does the same for duel+0x430 into +0x59E. No slot record is rewritten and no card is removed anywhere in either phase; the digivolution target the scan left in duel+0x438 is used only to choose which face the announcement sprite shows, and when no matching instance is found the face falls back to 0x57 with duel+0x438 set to 0x13B.
claims.coverage: Both phases of the combo opcodes 0x19 and 0x1A were read end to end (they share both targets, F0x8009403C and F0x800942DC, per cardgame-opcode-registry.json). The negative half of the claim -- that nothing is replaced -- was tested by reading every write in both function bodies: the only stores are to duel+0x42C/+0x430, the two stored totals, view fields, and the per-sprite flag +0x150. The side-block multiplier 0xC8 was recomputed by hand from the shift-add chain at .L0x00011a90 rather than assumed.
limitations: Static reading only. The exchange has NOT been observed in the running game: the rig experiment was written and armed on 2026-08-24 and the emulator crashed before it produced a line.

Whether F0x80094848, which recomputes the totals from the field, also OVERWRITES the cached totals was not read. No recompute sits between Battle-Phase state 8 and the state 0xA comparison, so it cannot change the set decision, but a later phase is unverified.
The combo claim does not establish what the +0x14 four-copy bonus is called on screen, nor whether the announcement's face lookup can pick a wrong instance when duplicate card ids are present.

claims.statement: A COMBO DOES NOT REPLACE THE RUN WITH THE CATALOG +0x0A DIGIMON's STATS. The long-standing question - double the run, or become the +0x0A Digimon - is answerable statically after all, against the recorded expectation that it needed a controlled duel. The argument is a complete enumeration of who can change a field slot's stats. Since cardgame-battle-totals-are-sums-of-per-slot-stats establishes that a side's battle totals are recomputed as the SUM of its slots' own stat fields, any mechanism that changed the numbers by substituting a Digimon would have to write those per-slot fields. Exactly three functions in the overlay write them. F0x8008E08C is the stat-change ticker and only ever adds or subtracts ONE per frame, ramping toward a target queued by F0x8008DEF8. F0x8008E5BC only COPIES one slot's stats to another, the compaction performed when cards shift along the field. F0x8009535C only READS the health field to test it against zero. None of the three touches the combo-run flag +0x446, and the queuer F0x8008DEF8 is reached only from the explicit stat-change opcodes, each passing a packed literal amount - never from the combo opcodes. So no code path exists by which a combo rewrites a slot's stats. What the combo DOES do is already recorded: F0x8009403C sums the flagged run's stats a second time into the side totals and adds a further 20 to each at four or more copies, and F0x8009403C/F0x80093C18 put the +0x0A target card's ARTWORK on screen. The +0x0A field is therefore a DISPLAY identity plus the run's eligibility key, not a stat substitution: the game shows you the digivolution and scores the run twice.

A combo run is presented as a sequence, once per run, and its beats are timed. The tick machine F0x800942DC runs on the interpreter's step byte duel+0x422: it waits past 0x15 units of the resident frame delta and then tells each flagged slot of the run to rise; when the last of them settles it places the combined card and clears the run's marks; it opens a name plate over the fusing side's own row, positioned from the halfword pair table based at 0x800A5928 - side 0 at (130, 191) at 60Hz and (130, 203) at 50Hz - and passes duel+0x438 as the argument that names it, which is the combined card's id; it holds that plate for 0x5A units or until a button; and it then climbs the fusing side's two total plaques, readout indices 8 and 9, over 0x14 units before committing the fused pair into duel+0x59C and +0x59E. The build phase F0x8009403C places the combined card at 0x8300 / 0x6100, which is (131, 97) in the sprite layer's 8.8 fixed point, and writes card id 0x13B into duel+0x438 when no instance of the run's own target exists.
claims.notes: Static reading only; not observed in the running game. Built into the walker the same day as the duel screen's fusion beat (web/cardduel.js openComboBeat / stepComboBeat), with tools/verify_cardduel_combo.mjs driving the live page through it. The walker draws the rise as the decoded hold command 0x8009C770 because view method +0xF1C has no identified sprite command in the animation decode, and marks that at the site.
claims.coverage: The ten steps were read in order from the machine's own jump table at 0x8008365C through to its completion return, and each timing quoted here is the instruction in the step it belongs to rather than a figure carried over from a summary. The 'once per run' scope rests on the scan F0x800A0CD4, which clears the flag array duel+0x446 across the side's whole slot count on every call and sets it on one run only before returning the next scan index - so each issue of the announcement opcode sums, caps and scores exactly one run. The claim does not say what the plate's window looks like, and it does not assert a sound: no call in the machine reaches the sound service, its only resident calls being the pad service's two entries at the step that takes a button, but a sound raised elsewhere in the Battle-Phase machine would not be caught by reading this routine.

claims.statement: The combo run detector F0x800A0CD4 does TWO things and no more: it sets the per-slot flag +0x446 on each slot of a qualifying run, and it stores the run card's catalog +0x0A combo-target card id into duel+0x438. It does NOT write the target's stats into the field slot records, so nothing in the detector itself implements 'the run becomes the target Digimon'. The target id IS consumed for PRESENTATION: F0x8009403C scans the duel's card-instance table for an instance whose card id equals duel+0x438 minus one and hands the match to view sprite slot 0x11, i.e. the combo target's card art is put on screen. When no instance of the target is found it substitutes a fixed fallback and overwrites duel+0x438 with card id 0x13B, so a combo whose target is not present in the duel shows a substitute card rather than the digivolved one. The player-facing picker F0x8008AD98 gates selection on the same +0x446 flag, dimming every slot that is not part of a run. This NARROWS the long-standing open question rather than closing it: the target is resolved and displayed, but whether the run's AP and HP are REPLACED by the target's, as the published description says, or merely counted twice, as the board evaluator computes, is still not settled - no stat write from the target card has been found.

Two of the thirteen card-duel sound ids previously listed as unresolved literal argument words now have a decoded trigger, both played through the resident sound slot at 0x80055C48: 0x4001C is the SELECTION CONFIRMED sound, played by the target-confirm handlers F0x8008CFDC and F0x8008D594 on the accepted-confirm path, and 0x800450BD is the SELECTION CANCELLED sound, played by F0x8008D594's cancel path alongside the view calls that tear the highlight down. This identifies when each id is played; it does not identify which sample either id resolves to.

createCardBattleContext (F0x8009d310, cardgame.s L27039-L27178) fills exactly 42 function-pointer slots, not 41, covering every 4-byte offset from ctx+0xea0 to ctx+0xf44 inclusive with no gap and no duplicate; the stores are emitted out of ascending offset order, which is why a partial read undercounted them. The complete map is: +0xea0=0x8009cae0, +0xea4=0x8009be40, +0xea8=0x8009be78, +0xeac=0x8009beac, +0xeb0=0x8009bf5c, +0xeb4=0x8009cda4, +0xeb8=0x8009cc4c, +0xebc=0x8009c438, +0xec0=0x8009c3c0, +0xec4=0x8009c350, +0xec8=0x8009c2d0, +0xecc=0x8009c264, +0xed0=0x8009c4a4, +0xed4=0x8009c4d8, +0xed8=0x80098864, +0xedc=0x8009bfcc, +0xee0=0x8009c010, +0xee4=0x8009c054, +0xee8=0x8009c0dc, +0xeec=0x8009c124, +0xef0=0x8009c16c, +0xef4=0x8009c174, +0xef8=0x8009c1cc, +0xefc=0x8009c214, +0xf00=0x8009c25c, +0xf04=0x8009ce94, +0xf08=0x8009c9a0, +0xf0c=0x8009ca3c, +0xf10=0x8009ca80, +0xf14=0x8009c510, +0xf18=0x8009cdfc, +0xf1c=0x8009ce28, +0xf20=0x8009c904, +0xf24=0x8009c938, +0xf28=0x8009c5d8, +0xf2c=0x8009c654, +0xf30=0x8009c6e8, +0xf34=0x8009c770, +0xf38=0x8009c7f8, +0xf3c=0x8009cfbc, +0xf40=0x8009cf60, +0xf44=0x8009d15c. Forty-one of the targets lie in one contiguous 0x8009be40..0x8009d15c block and are function starts (0x8009be40 is immediately preceded by a jr $ra plus delay slot); the single outlier is +0xed8=0x80098864, a shared helper outside that block. The table is the duel's presentation/rules dispatch: the round engine's entry hook F0x800a0f4c calls slot +0xec8, and slot +0xf08 was already identified as a play-resolution step. Every address here was word-matched against cardgame.s itself, so the shared 0x80082cb0 load base with fieldstg.s is not in play.

A third card-duel sound id previously listed as an unresolved literal argument word now has a decoded trigger: 0x8004513E is the CURSOR MOVE sound, played through the resident sound slot at 0x80055C48 when the player moves between the two options of the prompt handled by F0x8008642C. Together with 0x4001C (selection confirmed) and 0x800450BD (selection cancelled), three of the thirteen ids now have a stated trigger. This identifies when the id is played, not which audio sample it resolves to.

THERE IS NO INSTANT AT WHICH DAMAGE IS SUBTRACTED - the card game has no subtraction step at all, only ramps, and this closes the question of when a card's stats drop. Two ramps run one behind the other. The TRUE per-slot stats at slot+0x734 and +0x736 are moved by exactly one point per frame by F0x8008E08C, toward a target queued through F0x8008DEF8; as established by cardgame-combo-does-not-replace-the-run-with-the-target-digimon, that ramp is the only writer of those fields in the overlay, so no code anywhere assigns a card's health outright. F0x8009535C then runs a SECOND ramp: for each field slot of both sides it compares the view slot's displayed figures at +0x43 and +0x44 against the duel's true values and steps the displayed one closer by one, so the number the player watches trails the real one. In the same step, on the frame the TRUE health reaches zero, it raises that slot's flag at +0x46F and sets duel+0x438 - which is how a defeated card is marked for removal. So a card dies the frame its real health ramps to zero, while the on-screen figure is still catching up, and the visible count-down is a genuine per-point animation rather than a number jumping to a precomputed result.

A card FOLDER is stored in the save area, not in the duel object: the deck editor overlay pro/stcrddek addresses folder entries as 0x80048D34 + folder*0x66 + index*2, reading a halfword per entry. Each folder therefore occupies 0x66 bytes and holds 40 halfword card entries (0x28 entries, 80 bytes), leaving 22 bytes per folder whose use is not established here. This ties the editor to the same 40-card folder size the duel uses. The editor also contains an in-place exchange sort over exactly those 40 entries which swaps the numerically smaller entry forward, i.e. a sort-folder command that orders a folder by card entry value. This claim states the STORAGE LAYOUT only. It does NOT establish any deck-construction rule: in particular the four-copies-per-card ceiling that the browser implementation currently enforces was not located here, and remains unsupported by any original-code evidence.

Security Hall and Illegal Access mill the opponent's deck with a counted loop, and their counts are opcode immediates. Both programs are 05 or 03 followed by 33 4B 40 0E 30 02 06: a repeat count of five or two, then look at the opponent's deck, choose the position the reveal reads from, reveal the card, and test the deck. Opcode 0x40's update phase F0x8008FA9C is what removes the card, appending the instance held in duel+0x438 to the per-player trash array at block +0x614, incrementing the trash count +0x5A2, advancing the deck read cursor +0x5A0, decrementing the deck count +0x5A4 and repainting the trash counter. Opcode 0x0E then jumps forward two while the opponent's deck still has cards, landing exactly on the loop's 0x06; when the deck has emptied the fall-through plays a flourish and uses 0x02 to skip that 0x06, breaking the loop early. The printed text of the two cards is 'Put 5 Cards' and 'Put 2 Cards' from the opponent's deck, matching the two repeat immediates.
claims.coverage: Both programs were taken in full from web/assets/data/card_effects.json and every opcode in them was resolved against the established table; they are the only two of the 60 carrying this sequence. The correspondence between the repeat immediates and the printed counts was checked against web/assets/data/card_catalog.json for both cards, not one.
limitations: F0x8008FA9C is quoted at authority 3 from the decompilation, not from cardgame.s.
Only the trash-append path of that 162-line update was read; its other states were not.
derivation: grep for the trash and deck fields in exe-decomp/cardgame_c/F0x8008fa9c.c

claims.statement: F0x8008F790 is the discard-to-trash handler and independently corroborates the per-player block layout. It takes the play-history entry two positions back, reads its owning side from that entry's +0x584, forms the per-player block as duel + side * 0xC8, and appends the entry's card id (+0x580) to the trash pile at block + 0x614 + trashCount * 2, then increments the trash count at block + 0x5A2. It pushes both sides' trash counts to view field 7, reading side 0's from duel+0x5A2 and side 1's from duel+0x66A, and 0x66A - 0x5A2 is exactly 0xC8. This is a third witness to the 0xC8 per-player stride and to the trash pile sitting at block+0x614 with its count at block+0x5A2, from a function unrelated to the two that the layout claim cites.

claims.coverage: The two-way split was read from the single branch at 0x80084368 that selects between the two dispatches, and both dispatch sites were then read to confirm which byte each keys on: the enter dispatch bounds duel+0x421 with sltiu 0xAE, the update dispatch bounds duel+0x420 with sltiu 0xAF. No third path out of the prologue exists, because the branch and its fall-through are the only successors. Not tested: which other functions write duel+0x421 besides opcode 0x96. || Isolated review 2026-10-05 (docs/research/evidence/reviews/card-battle-2026-10-05.json): All anchors re-read. Prologue: .L0x000016b0 lbu $v1,0x421($s1) @0x80084360; .L0x000016b8 beqz $v1,.L0x00002218 @0x80084368 - a zero pending byte branches to the update dispatch at 0x2218/0x2220, which keys on duel+0x420 (.L0x00002218 lbu $v1,0x420($s1); .L0x00002220 sltiu $v0,$v1,0xaf) and dispatches through the table at 0x80082FB0. Non-zero falls through to the enter dispatch: .L0x000016c0/.16c8/ Anchors re-read: cardgame.s file 0x16b0-0x16d0 (prologue load, branch, enter dispatch bound), 0x220C-0x2240 (enter tail and update dispatch, both bounds), 0x3064-0x3088 (opcode 0x96 arm and the 0x97 latch), 0x2B9C and 0x2D14 (other +0x421 latches); sha256 0e26d0d5...; Update/enter dispatch tables at file 0x300 and 0x48 for the opcode 0x96/0x97 mapping.
claims.statement: duel+0x421 is the pending-enter-opcode latch of the card-effect interpreter, and it selects which of the two phases F0x80084320 runs. The prologue loads it, and when it is zero the function branches to the update-phase dispatch, which keys on the separately latched opcode at duel+0x420 under a bound of sltiu 0xAF. When it is non-zero the function falls through to the enter-phase dispatch, which uses that same pending byte as its key under a bound of sltiu 0xAE. This explains the one member of the pile-sweep family that does not complete like the others: opcode 0x96 writes 0x97 into duel+0x421, which queues opcode 0x97's enter phase to run on the next call rather than ending the step.
limitations: Replace the 'Writers of duel+0x421 other than opcode 0x96 were not enumerated' limitation with what was found: 'Within F0x80084320 the writers of +0x421 are the enter tail's clear (0x2210), the 0x85..0x8C tail latching 0x8D (0x2D14), one arm latching 0x4D (0x2B9C) and opcode 0x96 latching 0x97 (0x3088). Other functions also write +0x421 (e.g. clears at file 0x5A30/0x5A38, 0x990C/0x9914); no complete census was made.'
derivation: ./tools/run-overlay-scan.sh dis cardgame 0x80084320 0x80084ef8 | filter writes to s2/s3/s4

claims.statement: duel+0x438 is a selection-validity flag, not undifferentiated scratch. In F0x8008CFDC, the handler that runs the human player's target confirm and cancel, the confirm button (pad bit 0x0D) is accepted only when duel+0x438 equals 1; on acceptance the handler plays sound 0x4001C through the resident slot at 0x80055C48, clears the pending card's highlight bit, writes duel+0x46F[playIndex + 0xB] = playIndex + 1 and records the choice in the play-history entry's +0x582. The combo investigation was previously recorded as stalled because duel+0x438 has 31 loads and 26 stores across unrelated handlers and was read as shared scratch; this gives a concrete meaning to test that question against. Recorded as candidate because only one of its readers has been decoded.

duel+0x438 has no single meaning across the whole duel: it is a per-opcode scratch word whose interpretation belongs to whichever handler currently owns it, which is why it shows 31 loads and 26 stores across unrelated handlers. Two distinct uses are decoded. In the selection and confirm handlers it holds the pending selection's TARGET-ZONE MASK: F0x8008CB5C switches on it against 0x0400, 0x1000, 0x1400, 0x2000, 0x4000 and 0x8000 and uses the matched bit to pick which zone count bounds the selection, while F0x8008CFDC and F0x8008D594 only test it for non-zero. In F0x80094B9C it is instead a FRAME ACCUMULATOR: the handler adds the resident frame delta to it each frame and subtracts a fixed 3 for every step it emits, exactly as other handlers use duel+0x424, +0x430 and +0x434. This qualifies cardgame-duel-0x438-is-the-target-zone-mask, whose statement that the word is 'not undifferentiated scratch' was too strong: the mask reading is correct for the selection handlers and wrong as a description of the word in general. Any future trace of it must therefore be scoped to one opcode at a time.

duel+0x438 is the pending selection's TARGET-ZONE BITMASK, not a boolean validity flag and not undifferentiated scratch. F0x8008CB5C, on an accepted confirm, switches on it against composite values and uses the matched bit to decide which zone's count bounds the selection: 0x1000 reads duel+0x5A4 (side 0's deck count), 0x2000 reads duel+0x66C (= 0x5A4 + 0xC8, side 1's deck count) and 0x8000 reads duel+0x66E (= 0x5A6 + 0xC8, side 1's hand count); 0x0400 and 0x4000 take other paths and 0x1400 is tested first as the combination 0x0400 | 0x1000. Handlers that merely need to know whether anything is selected test it as non-zero (F0x8008D594) or against 1 (F0x8008CFDC), which is why it first read as a validity flag. This supersedes cardgame-duel-0x438-is-a-selection-validity-gate and is the natural place to resolve the recorded discrepancy between interpreter opcodes 0x85..0x8C and the kind-to-mask table decoded from F0x800A36E4, since this is where a mask is actually consumed.

duel+0x438 names which pile a card effect's prompt runs over. F0x8008C6E0 subtracts 5 from it, bounds the result unsigned against 11, and jumps through the table at 0x8008349C. Selector 5 takes the acting side's hand count from per-player block +0x5A6, 7 its deck count from +0x5A4, 9 its trash count from +0x5A2, 11 the other side's hand count from +0x66E and 15 the other side's trash count from +0x66A. Selector 13 shares entry 6's arm and therefore also reads the other side's HAND count, not that side's deck count at +0x66C. Every even entry points at a default arm that leaves the count at zero.
claims.coverage: The eleven table entries were read as words out of the overlay's pointer region rather than taken from a decompiled switch, which is necessary here because the decompiler fails on this jump and is why these handlers have no decompiled body at all. Each entry was resolved to the arm it points at and each arm read to the field it loads, so the mapping is enumerated over the table's whole indexed range, 0 through 10, and the bound that defines that range is quoted. The clause about selector 13 is the reason to enumerate rather than assume: entries 6 and 8 hold the same address, so a table read as 'one zone per odd selector, in order' would name the other side's deck here and be wrong.
limitations: Which effect opcodes set duel+0x438 to which value was not traced in this pass; the opcodes that reach this routine are 0xA9, 0xAB and 0xAA per docs/research/card/cardgame-opcode-registry.json.
Whether selector 13 sharing the hand arm is deliberate or a defect in the original is not established, and is not claimed either way.
Static reading only; not observed in the running game.
derivation: python3 - measure card_effects.json against cardgame-opcode-registry.json and cardgame-plain-descriptions.md

claims.statement: Within opcode 0xA7, duel+0x440 carries two different meanings in sequence rather than being a single mis-attributed field: it holds the player's card PICK (a 0/1 index copied from the cursor duel+0x43C at 0x80089c20) during steps 2-5, and is then overwritten at step 6 with the BOOLEAN outcome of the toss (1 when the pick equalled duel+0x434, else 0). This is scoped to the 0xA7 path and does not by itself settle the 'status code vs hand index' question recorded as row 6 of the model's remaining-unknowns table for other readers of duel+0x440; it does show the field is legitimately reused.

duel+0x440 is the selection cursor, not solely a draw-result code. F0x8008CA4C, the handler behind the target-selector opcodes 0x70..0x82, opens a selector by calling view->unkECC, setting the selector mask through view->unkEB8(view, mask), storing that mask into duel+0x438, resetting duel+0x440 to 0, setting the sub-opcode byte duel+0x422 to 1, moving sprite slot 0xF to (0xE500, 0x6100) = (229, 97) in 8.8, clearing fifteen entries of duel+0x46F and setting duel+0x499 = 1. Effect opcode 0x97 then indexes the acting side's hand array with duel+0x440 * 2. The Draw Phase handler F0x8009F910 reads the same word as a 0, 1 or 2 status code, so the field is a shared scratch word with two uses rather than one field with a single meaning; the previously recorded ambiguity between the two readings is resolved in favour of both being real. Relatedly, duel+0x438 holds the selector mask here and a combo target elsewhere, which is why tracing it statically does not converge: it is scratch, with 31 loads and 26 stores across unrelated handlers. F0x80090A6C, the handler behind opcodes 0x45 and 0x47, clears FORTY entries of duel+0x46F (0x27 down to 0) before setting the quota duel+0x444, so the selection-flag array is at least 40 bytes and is reused for hand selections of 10, field selections of 12 and deck selections of 40; earlier descriptions of it as a 12-entry array describe only its field-targeting use.

The CardDuel method at +0x814, F0x8009EEFC, is a selection sort, not the card-selection UI. Its signature is (CardDuel *duel, u16 *array, s32 packedRange, s32 flags): it orders the array of card INSTANCE indices over the half-open range [packedRange & 0xFFFF, packedRange >> 16) ascending by card id, which it obtains by resolving each entry through the card-instance table at duel+0x50. Flag bit 0 additionally swaps the parallel byte pairs at duel+0x30A and +0x30B, and flag bit 1 additionally swaps the selection flags at duel+0x446. F0x8009FDD8 calls it as duel->unk814(duel, duel + 0x600, handCount << 16, 0), sorting the player's hand by card id before the selector opens. No instruction in the function reads controller state. This corrects the first revision of docs/research/card/card-battle-complete-model-2026-08-06.md, which guessed the method was the selection UI and named it as the place where the S-Energy spend check and the AI's Digimon summon choice would be found; both must instead be inside the effect interpreter's selection-opcode handlers, principally F0x8008CA4C, F0x80090A6C and F0x80090A90.

The duel's outcome is carried in the single byte duel+0x302, and an overlay-wide scan of cardgame.s for stores at that offset (tools/run-overlay-scan.sh stores cardgame 0x302) returns exactly five sites: 0x800a1788 and 0x800a17d8 inside mode 8 state 0x11, 0x800a1b3c in the reset F0x800a1b2c, and 0x800a1d00 and 0x800a1d10 in mode 4's handler. In normal play mode 4 decides it. F0x8009f910 reads the 32-bit result code at duel+0x440 and returns 1 for code 0, 2 for code 1, 3 for code 2; mode 4's handler then writes +0x302 = 1 on return 2, writes +0x302 = 0 on return 3, and in both cases reports the duel finished to the driver's caller, whereas return 1 merely sets pending mode 0xa so play continues into mode 5. The alternative exit is mode 8 state 0x11, which sets +0x302 = 1 when a per-player byte at +0x676 is at least 2 and +0x302 = 0 otherwise (that field is +0x10 inside the second of the two 0xc8-stride player records). The reset F0x800a1b2c presets +0x302 = 1 together with +0x2f8 = mode 1. Downstream, the same object's scene driver F0x800a2f00 - which calls that very reset in its state 0, proving it is one object - reads +0x302 in state 3 to play sound handle 0x6004001e when the byte is 0 and 0x609c0004 when it is non-zero, and in state 2 takes the +0x302 == 0 branch to write 1 to the resident word 0x80048ac0 and to increment, capped at 99, the byte at (0x80048d34 + scene->0x2ec) + 0x7c. Because the zero branch is the only one that grants the capped counter and the affirmative global flag, and because 0x609c0004 is the same handle the scene already starts unconditionally at the end of state 0, the reading that +0x302 == 0 is the player-won outcome and +0x302 != 0 the player-lost outcome is strongly indicated but not yet proven; the polarity is the one open point in this claim. In player terms: whether you won or lost a duel is a single yes/no byte, it is decided in the fourth step of the round from a result code the drawing logic sets, the same byte chooses the closing jingle, and the winning branch bumps a per-partner counter that saturates at 99.

The card duel does use the game's random number generator. Duel method +0x810 is F0x8009F04C, installed by the duel factory as 0x800A0000 - 0xFB4. Given (duel, base, count) it returns immediately when count < 2, and otherwise runs a fixed 40 iterations (`slti` against 0x28) in which it calls the resident RAND_U16 through the pointer at 0x8004DC0C twice - the base being formed as `lui 0x8005` plus `addiu -0x23FC` = 0x8004DC04, called at +8 - reduces each result modulo count by taking the remainder from `hi` after `div`, offsets both by base, and exchanges the two halfwords at duel+0x5B0 + 2*index, that address being formed as a base at duel+0x59C plus 0x14. It is therefore a randomised pile shuffle, not a deterministic one. Four sites dispatch it through the duel+0x810 method pointer, each a genuine load-then-jalr pair: the duel initialiser, the turn loop, the per-set setup and a pile rebuild. The first three form the pile header with a LITERAL +0x59C offset and so read base and count from duel+0x5A0 and duel+0x5A4. The fourth CALLER is parameterised: it computes the header as duel + index*0xC8 + 0x59C from a caller-supplied index and reads base and count at +0x04 and +0x08 of that. The shuffle routine itself is NOT parameterised -- F0x8009F04C forms its own array base as `addiu $s3, $a0, 0x59c` from its first argument (cardgame.s:28916) -- so that fourth site's forty swaps still land on the side-0 block even when the range it passes comes from side 1. CORRECTED 2026-10-05 by cardduel-opponent-pile-is-never-shuffled-2026-10-05, which is the authority for this sentence.
claims.notes: Evidence pass 2026-08-07 after review aae85604 returned needs_evidence. That review re-derived and confirmed the entire mechanism exactly at authority 2: the 0x8004DC04 base and its borrow, two RAND_U16 calls per iteration with the remainder taken from hi, the 40-iteration bound, the swap at duel+0x5B0 + 2*index, and the 0x8009F04C install. Its two objections are met here. First, all four dispatch sites are now cited (L29435 initialiser, L9780 turn loop, L31616 per-set setup, L14129 pile rebuild); previously only two were. Second, the two ABSENCE clauses have been REMOVED from the statement, because a closed review bundle cannot carry a null scan result as a literal quote: the claim no longer asserts 'never by a direct jal' or 'a literal search returns zero hits'. Those observations remain true and are recorded in cardgame-rand-u16-is-reached-by-exactly-one-cardgame-function and in the model document, where they are stated with the corpus and matcher that produced them. For the record: `./dw3-research code-search "0x8004dc0c"` reports ABSENT, 0 of 590074 lines scanned, and tools/overlay_callgraph.py's `reaches` command reports zero direct jal callers of F0x8009F04C. REVIEWED TWICE 2026-08-07; the promotion gate is NOT satisfied and the claim rests at partially_verified. Review aae85604 confirmed the mechanism exactly but found only two of the four dispatch sites cited and objected to two absence clauses; both were fixed. Review ac2a6da4 then confirmed the mechanism, the install and all four dispatch sites exactly, and found one remaining overgeneralisation: the statement said all four sites read duel+0x5A0 and duel+0x5A4, but the fourth computes duel + index*0xC8 + 0x59C from a caller-supplied index, so those absolute addresses hold only when the index is zero. The statement has been corrected to describe the fourth site parameterised, which is the resolution that review itself proposed, but the two-review budget is spent so the correction is unreviewed. A fresh review in a later session should be able to accept it; the one artifact that would settle it independently is an exact quote of the caller of the function at cardgame.s L14022 showing what it passes as the index argument. Both reviews used the ddw3-claim-reviewer subagent path because tools/review_claim.py's nested claude CLI exits 1 in this WSL environment. 2026-10-05: the fourth-site sentence above said the shuffle routine was parameterised by a caller-supplied index. It is not; the CALLER is. Corrected in place, and the consequence -- that no pile other than the player's is ever mixed -- is now its own claim.

claims.statement: The card duel's sound ids are RESOLVED TO NAMES by cross-referencing the already-decoded SOUND TEST screen, whose table is literally an array of {name, packed_id} pairs - so the ids the duel plays can simply be looked up rather than inferred. Six resolve: 0x609C0004 is CBTLMAIN in bank cbtl00, archive 39; 0x6004001E is W_JINGLE in the common bank; 0x800450BD is SYSTEM01; 0x8004513E is SYSTEM02; 0x0004001B is SYSTEM06; 0x0004001C is SYSTEM07. THIS SETTLES THE OPEN QUESTION of whether 0x609C0004 is BGM or a loss jingle: it is neither a jingle nor common at all. Its name is CBTLMAIN - card battle main - and it sits in a duel-specific bank, cbtl00, rather than the shared bank every one-shot effect comes from. It is the card battle's MUSIC. IT ALSO REINSTATES A WITHDRAWN READING. The claim cardduel-is-best-of-three-sets originally said the duel-won path plays 'the win jingle 0x6004001E'; a review objected that this was a semantic name no evidence supported, and it was withdrawn to the neutral 'the id played on the winning path'. The sound test names that id W_JINGLE, so the original reading was correct and is now evidenced. The reviewer's objection was procedurally right - the name was unsupported at the time - and the fix was to find the support, not to keep the name. The four SYSTEM ids are the shared UI bleeps, which is why the same ids appear in the duel's prompt, its field cursor, and its confirm and cancel actions rather than being card-specific.

The unattributed band around F0x80095E58 to F0x80097A24 is not duel logic at all; it is the duel's family of small SPRITE WIDGETS, and they follow one construction pattern. F0x80096180 is a constructor: it asks the resident allocator for a 0x74-byte object with F0x80095FB4 as its per-frame handler, installs three further method pointers at widget+0x68, +0x6C and +0x70, stores the caller's x and y at +0x54 and +0x56, and clears a mode byte at +0x63. F0x80095E58 is a draw routine for such a widget: it draws only when both size fields +0x58 and +0x5A are non-zero, sources its sprite from bank 0x025D0002 at frame base 0x47, and advances a phase counter at +0x50 by the resident frame delta on every call, so the thing animates on time rather than on events. The mode byte picks the animation shape: mode 0 divides the phase by 4 and wraps it modulo 16, a LOOPING sixteen-frame cycle; mode 1 divides by 2 and CLAMPS at 7, a one-shot eight-frame ramp that then holds. F0x80097A24 is a plain non-animating draw of frame 0x18 from the same bank, and F0x80097310 draws an element at a horizontal offset taken from the halfword table at 0x800A59A8 indexed by its argument - i.e. one of a laid-out ROW of elements - hiding it when its value is zero. This attributes the band as presentation code and explains why nothing in it writes duel state.

Three more members of the duel's sprite-widget band are attributed, extending cardgame-duel-sprite-widget-family. F0x800961F0 is a SECOND widget of the same shape as F0x80095E58 but a different sprite: it also gates on its size pair being non-zero, also draws from bank 0x025D0002, but at frame base 0x45 rather than 0x47, and keeps its x/y at +0x58 and +0x5A with its phase at +0x54 and its mode byte at +0x67 - the same layout shifted by four bytes. Its animation is the one-shot form: phase divided by two, CLAMPED at 7, advanced by the resident frame delta only while the mode byte is set, so it plays an eight-frame ramp once and then holds. F0x80097238 draws a stack of exactly two elements at a fixed horizontal offset of 0x67 from its anchor with a vertical pitch of 13 pixels, positioning, tinting and enabling each through the child object at its +0x04. F0x800973E4 is a CENTRED label: when its value is non-zero it measures the text and places it at x = 160 minus half the width - the middle of the 320-pixel screen - and when the value is zero it hides the element instead. It also singles out the value 0x1F for a different palette, so one specific entry is drawn highlighted; which entry that is was not identified.

A card duel is driven by F0x800a1b48 (cardgame.s L31661-L31797), a two-level mode machine over three bytes of the duel object: pending mode +0x2f7, current mode +0x2f8 and previous mode +0x2f6. Each tick, if +0x2f7 is non-zero it is range-checked to 1..9 and dispatched once through the enter table at 0x80083a00 (cardgame.s L858-L866), after which the driver rotates +0x2f6 := old +0x2f8, +0x2f8 := +0x2f7, +0x2f7 := 0; then the current mode is range-checked to 1..0xa and dispatched every tick through the update table at 0x80083a28 (L868-L877). Enter targets by mode: 1 and 2 -> 0x800a1ba0 (clear +0x2f9 and +0x2fc), 3, 4 and 6 -> 0x800a1bac (clear +0x2f9), 5 and 7 -> 0x800a1bb4 (call F0x800a0548), 8 -> 0x800a1bc8 (call F0x800a0f4c), 9 -> 0x800a1bdc (call F0x800a1a5c). Update targets by mode: 1 -> 0x800a1c30, 2 -> 0x800a1c7c (F0x8009f110), 3 -> 0x800a1c98 (F0x8009f8c0), 4 -> 0x800a1cb4 (F0x8009f910), 5 -> 0x800a1d14 (F0x8009fdd8), 6 -> 0x800a1d30 (F0x800a0b80), 7 -> 0x800a1d14 (F0x8009fdd8, the identical entry to mode 5), 8 -> 0x800a1d4c (F0x800a0f94), 9 -> 0x800a1d84, 0xa -> 0x800a1d90 (F0x800a1af8). Mode 0xa is the inter-phase step: F0x800a1af8 sets the message-pending flag +0x2f4 and indexes a 4-byte-stride table at 0x800a5d5c by the previous mode, writing byte 0 into the on-screen message id +0x421 and byte 2 into the pending mode +0x2f7. Its rows for previous mode 1..9 are (banner, next mode) = (0xa6,2), (0xa0,3), (0xa1,4), (0xa2,5), (0xa3,6), (0xa4,7), (0xa5,8), (0xa0,3), (0xa0,3). The resulting order of play is therefore 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> 6 -> 7 -> 8 -> 9 and then back to 3, i.e. two setup modes followed by a six-mode round (3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8) that repeats until the duel ends, with a banner shown before every mode change. In player terms: the duel runs a fixed six-step round, announcing each step by name, and loops that round until somebody wins.

The persistent reward for winning a card duel is a single capped byte in a per-opponent record. The duel-outcome path forms the base 0x80048D34 as `lui 0x8005` plus `addiu -0x72CC`, adds duel+0x2EC to it, and then reads the byte at +0x7C of the result: if that byte is below 0x63 it stores the byte plus one, so the field saturates at 99. The index duel+0x2EC is not an opponent id but a value the opponent record supplies indirectly: F0x8009D6E0 reads the CARD_NPC.BIN record's s32 at +0xCC and uses it to index the HALFWORD table at 0x800A5C2C, storing the halfword to duel+0x2EC. That table holds 0x005B at indices 0 and 1 and 0x0167 + n from index 2 to 35, and the shipped records use indices 1..15 and 31..35, so the reward byte lands at 0x80048D34 + 0x5B + 0x7C for one group of opponents and at 0x80048D34 + (0x0167 + n) + 0x7C for the rest. The identity of the record at 0x80048D34 and the meaning of its +0x7C byte are still unresolved; what is now established is that the table value is added as a BYTE OFFSET to the base, not used as an array index with a stride, which rules out reading it as a partner-slot number.
claims.notes: LIMITATIONS: the record at 0x80048D34 is not identified here and the meaning of its +0x7C byte remains open, so this states the mechanism and the addressing, not the reward. The 0x800A5C2C table contents are read from cardgame.s at file offset 0x22F7C. Do not conflate +0x7C with the charisma flag bank 0x72.

claims.statement: F0x800A0844(duel, slot, side, k) recomputes the AP and HP of the five dynamic-stat Megas. It returns immediately unless duel+0x50[slot->ref] equals the k-th halfword of the 5-entry table at 0x800A5C20 (card ids 68, 111, 154, 197, 240), then runs the same handler twice - once with base = slot+0x2 producing slot+0x6 (AP), once with base = slot+0x4 producing slot+0x8 (HP) - jumping through the 8-entry table at 0x80083960. The five formulas read from the assembly at file 0x0001DB94..0x0001DD48 are: k=0 (id 68) base + 20 * ownFieldCount; k=1 (id 111) base + 10 + 10 * ownHandCount; k=2 (id 154) base + 10 + 20 * ownTrashCount; k=3 (id 197) base + 10 * (duel+0x72C + duel+0x79E); k=4 (id 240) base + 10 + 10 * (duel+0x5A2 + duel+0x66A). Both results are then clamped with 'if (v >= 0x63) v = 0x63' and 'if (v <= 0) v = 0', i.e. capped at 99 and floored at 0. This closes and corrects open item 6 of docs/research/card/cardduel-rules-2026-08-06.md: the field-count variant multiplies by 20 with no +10 term, and there are two further variants (k=3 and k=4) that sum both sides, which the earlier partial read did not reach. F0x800A09FC runs all five over every field slot from step 3 of the Summon Phase, after F0x800A0754 has rebuilt the field: F0x800A0754 zeroes the side's field slot count and then places each hand card whose duel+0x46F flag is set, gated by the unsigned compare of the running field count against the selection quota byte duel+0x444.

The numeric magnitudes of Program-card effects are immediate operands of the stat-change opcodes 0x5E..0x69, not text-only values. Each of those opcodes calls F0x8008DEF8(duel, scene, packed, mode) with a constant. F0x8008DEF8 splits packed into a signed high and low halfword, stores them at duel+0x428 and +0x42C with their absolute values at +0x430 and +0x434, clears the roll timer +0x424, and then walks the twelve field slots adding the HIGH halfword to slot+0x2 and the LOW halfword to slot+0x4 for every slot whose duel+0x46F flag is set and which is within its side's field count. The twelve immediates are: 0x5E = 0x000A000A (AP +10, HP +10, mode 1), 0x5F = 0x0000001E (HP +30), 0x60 = 0x00320032 (+50/+50), 0x61 = 0x00140014 (+20/+20), 0x62 = 0x001E001E (+30/+30), 0x63 = 0x0000000A (HP +10), 0x64 = 0x000A0000 (AP +10), 0x65 = 0x0000FFC4 (HP -60, mode 0), 0x66 = 0x0000FFF1 (HP -15), 0x67 = 0x0000FFE2 (HP -30), 0x68 = 0x000AFFF6 (AP +10, HP -10), 0x69 = 0xFF9D0000 (AP -99, mode 2, the destruction path). Damage is therefore HP-only and symmetric buffs raise both stats, and the values line up with the printed card text: -60 with Volcanic Cannon's '60 damage points', -30 with Fire Cannon's and Break Launcher's '30 damage points', +30/+30 with Power Super Metal's '+30 to AP & HP', and +10/+10 with Gold Aura's '+10 to all own Digimon's AP & HP'. This closes open item 7 of docs/research/card/cardduel-rules-2026-08-06.md, which recorded that the numbers appear only in escardgm/escardst text and not in code. The card-id-keyed tables F0x800A4440 and F0x800A4494 are not this mechanism; they are the AI's estimate of a card's effect and are consumed only by its simulators.

In one card duel played end to end on the rig (save slot 5, s482 Tamer Mitch, through the opening ceremony, coin toss, Program-card play, summoning, the Battle Phase and into the second set), the duel's per-frame entry point F0x800A2DF8 ran a fixed chain each frame -- apply queued grey flags, dispatch one queued board-view request, run a queued colour wash -- and then handed the frame to EITHER the round/phase driver F0x800A1B48 OR the card-effect interpreter F0x80084320, never to both. Over the 5,776 traced frames in which the duel tick ran, the effect interpreter held the frame 4,768 times, the round driver 717 times, a board-view request took the slot 291 times, and the count of frames containing both was zero. The effect interpreter is therefore not a subroutine the phase machine calls and waits on; while a card's program runs it IS the duel's frame, and it holds it for roughly six frames in every seven of this duel.
claims.coverage: The 'never both' quantifier was tested over the full traced population, not a sample: every run-length-collapsed frame record in the trace was expanded by its repeat count and each frame's entry list was searched for both function indices, giving 4768 + 717 + 291 + 0 = 5776 frames accounted for with no residue. The obvious way this could be an artifact was checked and excluded: the recorder caps stored entries at 3000 per frame, and the busiest frame in the run held 561 -- 5.3x below the cap -- so no frame's list was truncated and no co-occurrence could have been dropped. The recorder itself was calibrated before the run: two breakpoints on adjacent instructions of one always-executing loop returned 1 hit and 6,849,405 hits over the same 60 frames, establishing that a callback returning nothing fires on every execution.
limitations: ONE duel, one opponent, one folder, one language. A different folder would run different card programs and could in principle reach a frame shape this duel never produced.

The measurement covers the cardgame overlay's 247 jal-reachable function entries taken from docs/generated/function-extents.json. A handler reached only through a register-computed call with no stack frame would not be in that list and would be invisible to this trace.
Entry ORDER within a frame is recorded; caller/callee EDGES are not. Two functions in one frame are not shown to be caller and callee.
The frame boundary is the GPU::Vsync event, so the attribution of an entry to a frame is only as precise as that event; an entry occurring within a frame is not timed inside it.
159 of the 247 functions ran. The other 88 are largely per-opcode effect machinery this duel never triggered; nothing here says they are unreachable.
derivation: per-frame event-count check over the trace

claims.statement: Card effect opcodes are not instantaneous. Nearly every handler reached by the interpreter F0x80084320 is a small state machine on the byte duel+0x422, run once per frame and returning non-zero only when the opcode has finished, so the interpreter advances the program counter only on completion and a single opcode may occupy arbitrarily many frames. The conventional states are 1 (entered: set up, or wait for a precondition), 2 (the working state: poll the pad, tick a counter, or step an iterator) and 3 and 4 where the view must settle twice. Handlers share scratch at duel+0x424 (a frame accumulator), duel+0x428 (a countdown) and the pair duel+0x42C / duel+0x430 (usually a side and an index). Recorded as candidate because the protocol is generalised from twelve handler bodies read in checked decompilation, not from all 92.

A card's effect record is a bytecode program, not a message list, and the mechanism is legible in original assembly. The duel object carries a program counter at +0x4E0 (u16), a current-opcode byte at +0x420 and a pending-next-opcode byte at +0x421. The fetch step in F0x800A2180 reads the program counter, adds one and stores it back, so the counter advances one byte per opcode - the defining property of a byte-oriented instruction stream. The interpreter F0x80084320 dispatches by reading the pending byte at +0x421, zeroing it, and latching it into the current-opcode byte at +0x420 in three consecutive instructions, so a handler schedules its successor simply by writing a byte; observed chain targets written this way include 0x4D, 0x8D and 0x97. Handlers also manipulate the program counter directly, which a message list has no need to do: one opcode advances it by two rather than one (skipping an inline operand), another loads it wholesale from the saved halfword at +0x4E4 (an absolute jump), and another subtracts four from it (a backward branch). A program counter that is incremented, skipped, loaded and rewound, together with an opcode-chaining latch, is an instruction interpreter. This supersedes cardduel-effect-record-message-list-is-not-a-bytecode.

claims.contradiction_rationale: The count 92 and the assertion that every dispatch block ends in at most one jal are both wrong. They came from a linear walk that stopped at the first unconditional jump and therefore never followed conditional branches. Six update blocks (0xA9..0xAE) begin with a conditional branch on the interpreter register $s2 and contain two exclusive call paths. A full control-flow walk reaches 96 distinct callees, and an independent check that every jal instruction in 0x800843A0..0x80085E40 is attributed to some opcode leaves nothing unreached; the linear walk left four targets unreached.
claims.statement: RETRACTED. The claim stated that the 174-opcode card-effect registry resolves to 92 distinct callee functions and that each dispatch block is a short argument setup ending in at most one jal. Both parts are wrong; see the superseding claim.

Card-effect opcodes 0x07 to 0x10, excluding 0x0F, are conditional relative branches on the effect VM's program counter duel+0x4E0, and their five callees share one shape: if the condition holds, add the call's delta argument to duel+0x4E0; otherwise do nothing. No dispatch block tests the callee's return value, so the branch is entirely inside the leaf. The conditions are: F0x80083F48, the last play's acting side equals the argument (0x07 delta +1, 0x08 delta +2); F0x80083F84, the argument is greater than or equal to the side's hand count (0x09 with 10, delta +9; 0x0B with 3, delta +9); F0x80083FC8, the argument is less than the side's hand count (0x0A with 10, delta -9; 0x0C with 3, delta -9; 0x0D with 2, delta +4); F0x8008400C, the side's deck count is above zero (0x0E, delta +2); F0x8008404C, the side's field slot count is below six (0x10, delta +5). The program counter already points at the following opcode when a branch runs. That convention is corroborated three times by landing sites in shipped programs rather than assumed. Opcode 0x06 completes the picture as a backward jump: it decrements duel+0x4E2 and, while any repeats remain, restores duel+0x4E0 from the position duel+0x4E4 that 0x03, 0x04 or 0x05 saved.
claims.coverage: Every opcode in the range 0x07 to 0x10 was taken, all nine that are branches plus 0x0F which is not, by reading each dispatch block in docs/research/card/cardgame-opcode-registry.json and then the callee it names. The five callees are the complete set the range dispatches to. The program-counter convention was tested against three shipped programs chosen because their jump distances have unambiguous landing sites: Summon Patamon (0x10, +5), Summon Angemon (0x10, +5) and Tidal Wave (0x09, +9 and 0x0A, -9). All four landings fall exactly on a step that makes the program coherent; a one-off convention would have missed every one of them.
limitations: The five callee bodies are quoted from exe-decomp/cardgame_c at authority 3. Promotion beyond partially_verified needs each `if` and its duel+0x4E0 store quoted from cardgame.s.
Which side each test asks about rests on section G.16's reading of the side registers, not on a fresh derivation.
The program-counter convention is corroborated, not proved: the fetch site that advances duel+0x4E0 was not read in this pass.

claims.statement: The card-effect bytecode VM has counted loops. duel+0x4E2 is a loop iteration counter and duel+0x4E4 saves the loop-start program counter. Update-phase opcode 0x03 stores the literal count 2 into +0x4E2, and opcodes 0x04 and 0x05 reach a shared store with the literal counts 3 and 5; all three copy the current program counter duel+0x4E0 into +0x4E4. Update-phase opcode 0x06 closes the loop: it decrements +0x4E2 and, when the decremented value is still greater than zero, reloads +0x4E0 from +0x4E4 so the enclosed opcode run repeats. Update-phase opcode 0x02 adds 2 to +0x4E0 as an unconditional forward skip. This is read from the update-phase halves only; the enter-phase halves of 0x02..0x06 are the convergence no-op.
claims.coverage: The 'referenced ONLY inside switch 2' quantifier was tested with dw3-research code-search over the whole original-assembly corpus, which reports its denominator: '0x4e2($s1)' returns 4 of 590074 lines scanned and '0x4e4($s1)' returns 2, and all six hits lie inside F0x80084320's switch 2. NOT tested: whether these offsets are reached under a different base register elsewhere, which that matcher cannot see.

claims.statement: The card-effect VM's complete two-phase opcode registry is two jump tables at the head of pro/cardgame's data, and both are readable mechanically from the overlay rather than opcode by opcode. The ENTER phase (switch 3 of F0x80084320) subtracts 1 from the opcode, bounds-checks the result against 0xae, and indexes the table at 0x80082cf8; so the legal opcode range is 1..0xae, exactly 174 opcodes, and that table is (opcode-1)-indexed. The UPDATE phase (switch 2) reads the opcode the interpreter latched into duel+0x420, bounds-checks it against 0xaf, and indexes the table at 0x80082fb0 by the RAW opcode scaled by 4, with no decrement. THE TRAP: the two tables use DIFFERENT index conventions. Enter is (opcode-1)*4 from 0x80082cf8; update is opcode*4 from 0x80082fb0. Anyone dumping both tables to build the registry mechanically will misalign the update half by one entry unless they apply each convention separately. The two tables sit inside a contiguous pointer region running from 0x80082cf8 to about 0x800838ac in which the overlay keeps its jump tables, individual tables being separated by zero words. This is where EVERY m2c 'Unable to determine jump table' failure in this overlay resolves - four have been resolved from it so far: 0x800834fc (F0x8008d274, opcodes 0x8e..0x95 enter), 0x8008334c (F0x80088f78, opcode 0x9e update), 0x8008363c (F0x80093cac, opcode 0x1b update) and 0x80083684 (F0x80094b9c, opcodes 0x1c/0x1d update). Limitations: the 174-entry extents of the two dispatch tables are inferred from the bound checks and the region layout, not by dumping and validating all 348 words - many entries are expected to share a common 'unimplemented opcode' target, which was not checked. The zero-word separation was observed across the region but is not guaranteed to delimit every table, so a scan splitting purely on zeros can merge adjacent tables; the four tables named above were each confirmed from their own function's bound check, not from the split.

A complete census of the card-effect VM's opcode space, taken by dumping both dispatch tables from the overlay and applying each table's own index convention. The enter table at 0x80082cf8 holds 174 entries for opcodes 0x01..0xae; the update table at 0x80082fb0 holds 175 entries for latched values 0x00..0xae. Of the 174 opcodes, 132 have a distinct enter-phase handler and 42 dispatch straight to 0x80084ebc, the post-switch convergence point, meaning they do NOTHING in the enter phase and all their work is in the update phase. Those 42 are exactly: 0x02..0x11, 0x2a, 0x32..0x3d, 0x4a..0x4b, 0x5b..0x5c, 0x85..0x8c and 0x96. THE READ IS CROSS-VALIDATED EXACTLY: the set of 132 opcodes with a non-convergence enter target is identical to the set of switch-3 cases in exe-decomp/cardgame_c/F0x80084320.c - 132 in each, with zero difference in either direction. That agreement between an independently dumped table and the decompiler's own case list is what establishes that the (opcode-1)*4 / opcode*4 conventions were applied correctly. The tables also expose handler sharing directly: 122 distinct enter targets and 105 distinct update targets across the space. Five enter-phase families share one target - 0x1e/0x1f/0x20/0x22/0x23, 0x24..0x28, 0x1c/0x1d, 0x4d/0x4e and 0x9f/0xa0 - and the update table independently confirms the two families decoded separately, with all eight of 0x8e..0x95 pointing at 0x80085cf0 and all seven of 0x4f..0x55 pointing at 0x80085760. Limitations: this counts and groups handlers, it does NOT decode them; a shared target proves two opcodes run the same code, not that they mean the same thing, since several decoded families select behaviour from an argument the dispatch passes. 0x80084ebc is identified as the enter-phase convergence from its position after the switch and from the decompiler rendering every enter case as 'goto block_133'; it was not read as a block. The update table's most-shared target (15 opcodes) was not checked for being a stub, so no equivalent 'does nothing in the update phase' count is claimed.

Update-phase opcodes 0x07..0x10 of the card-effect VM are conditional relative branches: each calls a small helper that tests one condition and, only when it holds, adds a displacement passed by the dispatch block to the program counter duel+0x4E0. Five helpers are used. F0x80083F48 (opcodes 0x07, 0x08) adds when the acting-side byte +0x584 of the previous play-history entry equals its a2 argument. F0x80083F84 (0x09, 0x0B) adds when the per-player counter at block +0x0A is less than or equal to a2. F0x80083FC8 (0x0A, 0x0C, 0x0D) adds when that same counter is strictly greater than a2. F0x8008400C (0x0E) adds when the per-player halfword at block +0x08 is greater than zero. F0x8008404C (0x10) adds when a field-slot byte at duel+0x72C, side stride 0x72, is unsigned-less-than 6. The per-opcode thresholds and displacements read from the dispatch blocks are 0x07 (side==1, +1), 0x08 (side==1, +2), 0x09 (<=10, +9), 0x0A (>10, -9), 0x0B (<=3, +9), 0x0C (>3, -9), 0x0D (>2, +4), 0x0E (>0, +2) and 0x10 (<6, +5). Opcode 0x0F is not covered by this claim: its update half calls the resident import F0x8001EBF8 and was not read.
claims.coverage: The set of opcodes covered was taken from the dumped update dispatch table rather than assumed: opcodes 0x07..0x10 are exactly the entries whose update target calls one of the five helpers, and each helper's branch polarity was read twice, once in the overlay disassembly and once in the authority-2 cardgame.s, including its .word encoding. 0x0F is excluded by name because its callee lies outside the overlay and was not read; the claim therefore covers nine opcodes, not ten.

claims.statement: RETRACTED 2026-08-09, hours after recording. The count 92 and the assertion that every dispatch block ends in at most one jal are both wrong: they came from a linear walk that stopped at the first unconditional jump and never followed conditional branches. Six update blocks (0xA9..0xAE) open with a conditional branch on interpreter register $s2 and hold two exclusive call paths. The corrected figure is 96 distinct callees (40 enter, 56 update). Superseded by cardgame-effect-vm-registry-collapses-to-96-distinct-callee-functions.

The 174-opcode card-effect registry does not contain 174 distinct handler bodies. A control-flow walk of all 348 dispatch blocks in 0x800843A0..0x80085E40, following both outcomes of every conditional branch, reaches exactly 96 distinct callee functions: 40 from the enter-phase table and 56 from the update-phase table, with no function reached from both tables. The walk is complete in the sense that every one of the 96 jal targets appearing anywhere in that address range is attributed to at least one opcode. 168 of the 174 opcodes reach at most one callee per phase; the exception is the last six, 0xA9..0xAE, whose update blocks open with a conditional branch on the interpreter register $s2 and hold two mutually exclusive call paths. Distinct table targets therefore overstate the remaining work, because many separate targets call the same function with different immediate arguments.
claims.coverage: Completeness was tested independently of the walk that produced the number: every jal instruction in 0x800843A0..0x80085E40 was extracted from the disassembly and checked against the walk's per-opcode attributions. The first, linear walk left 4 of 96 targets unattributed (F0x80084188, F0x8008C6E0, F0x8008C8D8, F0x8008C988), which is how its count of 92 was falsified; the control-flow walk leaves 0 unattributed. The disjointness of the enter and update callee sets was computed as a set intersection over the same walk, not asserted.

The 'never reassigned' quantifier was tested rather than assumed: the whole range from the function entry 0x80084320 to the update dispatch 0x80084EF8 was disassembled and every instruction writing s2, s3 or s4 was extracted mechanically. The only writes are the three prologue loads; the three other matches are register spills to the stack (sw) and one read (bnez $s2). Both dispatches lie inside that scanned range, so no path reaches either with different values. CORROBORATION: the already-recorded S-Energy family reads the same previous-entry +0x584 byte as the acting side and its XOR 1 as the opponent, derived independently from a different family. || Isolated review 2026-10-05 (docs/research/evidence/reviews/card-battle-2026-10-05.json): Prologue re-verified exactly: cardgame.s .L0x00001690 lb $v0,0x575($s1) (play-history index); .L0x00001698 addiu -0x1 / .L0x0000169c sll 3 / .L0x000016a0 addu -> entry at index minus one; .L0x000016ac lbu $s2,0x584($v1); .L0x000016a4/.a8 same for the index entry; .L0x000016b4 lbu $s3,0x584($v0); .L0x000016bc xori $s4,$s2,0x1. Function F0x80084320 starts .L0x00001670 (addiu $sp,-0x88) and ends .L0x Anchors re-read: /home/dorij/ddw3/asm/dw2003/pro/cardgame.s (sha256 0e26d0d5...): L1443-1493 (prologue and the two dispatch tables' heads); L2196-2265 (enter tail 0x220C, update dispatch 0x2220-0x2240, first update bodies); L2245-2320 (update arms 0x08/0x02/0x0f intro); L2257-2340 resolved arm extents; full-span mechanical write census of [0x1670,0x3134] (1714 instructions; 8 write sites found); decode of enter ta
claims.statement: Pin the quantifier: '... are fixed by the interpreter prologue of F0x80084320, each written once there, and no instruction writes any of them between the prologue and either dispatch.' Add one clause: 'A single update arm - opcode 0x0f, .L0x00002328-0x23C8 - reuses s3 ($s4*2, .L0x00002330) and s2 (200*s4, .L0x00002368) as scratch after its dispatch; it never passes either register to a callee, so the side attribution below is unaffected.' (Optionally note the update dispatch's jr is at 0x80084EF0 with its first case body at 0x80084EF8 - the coverage names the latter as 'the update dispatch'.)
