claims.statement: Every update-phase handler shared by more than one opcode is now mapped, closing the group census begun in claim cardgame-opcodes-0x70-0x7e-are-targeting-prompts-sharing-one-update-picker. The remaining six groups are: opcodes 0x9f..0xa6, the eight phase banners, polling F0x80089580; opcodes 0x45..0x47, the selection-quota family, polling F0x80090a90 with the acting side; opcodes 0x80..0x82 calling F0x8008cb5c; opcodes 0x83..0x84 calling F0x8008cfdc; opcodes 0x9b/0x9c polling F0x80087edc with a POINTER to the per-player block duel+0x59c as third argument rather than a side index; and opcodes 0x12/0x13 polling F0x80092638, already identified by an existing claim. THE SIGNIFICANT RESULT is that the confirm/cancel prompt generalises further than previously recorded. F0x8008cb5c serves opcodes 0x80..0x82 as well as 0x70..0x7e - EIGHTEEN opcodes, not fifteen - and opcodes 0x83/0x84 use a THIRD prompt, F0x8008cfdc, which reads pad port 0 through the same pad-service slot +0x3f4 and tests the same logical buttons 0x0d and 0x0e, gating its confirm on duel+0x438 == 1. All three prompts store their result into duel+0x57a. So 28 of the 174 opcodes are confirm/cancel prompts across three functions that differ only in their legality gate: F0x8008cb5c switches on the target-kind mask and checks a per-player pile counter, F0x8008d594 treats duel+0x438 as a boolean match flag, and F0x8008cfdc requires duel+0x438 to equal exactly 1. Limitations: F0x8008cfdc's return values were read from the decompilation only and are not stated here; the polled callees F0x80089580, F0x80090a90, F0x80087edc and F0x8008cfdc were not decoded beyond the prompt identification above. That opcodes 0x80..0x82 are prompts does not by itself say what they prompt FOR - their enter-phase target-kind masks are given in section G.0 and were not re-read here.

F0x80084188, previously unmentioned, picks the AI's BEST OPPOSING TARGET. It walks all twelve field slot flags at duel+0x46F clearing each, and for the six slots at index 6..11 - the opposing side - calls the duel's installed board evaluator at method +0x820 with side 1 and a bitmask isolating that one slot. It keeps the running maximum, and on each new maximum clears the previous leader's flag, sets the new slot's flag to 1 and writes the slot index to the selection cursor duel+0x440. The result is exactly one flagged slot: the opposing card the evaluator scores highest. Ties keep the FIRST slot reached, because the comparison is a strict less-than against the running maximum.

F0x80085DE8 is an exchange sort over 40 entries whose key is the byte at +0x30A - the PER-SET AVAILABILITY GROUP that the CARD_NPC loader writes from deck entry byte +0x02, paired with its loop index at +0x30B. It swaps the group and index bytes together and swaps the matching halfwords of a parallel array at +0x678, keeping the two in step. Smaller group values move toward the front, so after this runs the deck is ordered with the earliest-available cards first - which is exactly the order the per-set window admits them in. Ties keep their existing relative order only insofar as a strict less-than comparison does not swap equal keys.

F0x80086090 is a single-expression halfword table read: table 0x800A5844 indexed as arg0*0x10 + arg1*4 + arg2*2, offset by a BANK selected by the global at 0x8005CCB0 with a stride of 0x30. Its only caller is F0x800860D4. The 0x30 bank stride against a 0x10 stride for the first index means each bank holds three rows of four pairs. The global at 0x8005CCB0 selects the bank in at least two places in this overlay - F0x80092198 uses it the same way against a different table at 0x800A5958 - so it is a mode-like selector shared across the duel's presentation code. What the table CONTAINS is not established here.

claims.notes: DIRECTION NAMES CORRECTED 2026-08-24, and the prompt was OBSERVED. The statement calls pad bits 4 and 6 'the left and right d-pad bits'. The bit numbers are right and the names are not: in the pad's own bit order 4 is UP and 6 is DOWN (5 is right, 7 is left). Two independent confirmations. (a) The prompt was photographed on the rig from GUI slot 5, run 5 of 2026-08-24, frame 1001+22, C:/dw3-rig/shots/duel_f01001+22_m5_lc2_s2_w2_c0_p0.raw: its two answers are drawn on SEPARATE LINES, one above the other, with a marker out at x 14 on the chosen one -- a vertical list, which left and right would not move. (b) The bit order is the standard pad order this same claim relies on elsewhere. What the box draws is now established too, and it was never read before: the full-width prompt window at y 138..185 -- the same three-row border and fill as every other window on this screen, at a different y -- carrying escardgm 0x0E 'Use a Program Card?' on the first line and escardgm 0x45 "Yes, I'll use a Program Card." and 0x46 'No, I'll pass.' on the next two, at x 28 on a 14px pitch with the first glyph top at band+5. The claim's own limitation that the opened box was not read is therefore closed by observation at authority 1; the mechanism it describes is unchanged and was confirmed, including that the toggle is dead unless duel+0x438 is 2.
claims.statement: F0x8008642C, 193 lines and previously unmentioned in any card research document, is the duel's TWO-OPTION PROMPT. Its entry state accumulates the resident frame delta into duel+0x424 and waits until 0x24 units have passed with no pending effect (duel+0x498 == 0), then opens the prompt through view+0xEE4, passing the view's own +0xDE8, +0xDF4 and +0xDE4 words along with duel+0x438; if duel+0x575 is zero or duel+0x438 is not 3 it takes the ordinary path, otherwise it jumps to step state 8. In its polling state the left and right d-pad bits 4 and 6, gated on duel+0x438 being 2, TOGGLE the cursor duel+0x440 with an exclusive-or against 1 - so the prompt has exactly two options - play sound 0x8004513E, and push the new cursor to view+0xEF0. The cancel button, pad bit 0x0E, forces duel+0x440 to 1 and pushes that. This is a third distinct role for duel+0x438 within one duel object: here it selects WHICH prompt is being shown, alongside its use as a target-zone mask in the selection handlers and as a frame accumulator in F0x80094B9C.

F0x80086D28 is a two-line row selector in front of F0x80086A30: scope code 1 maps to view slot base 6, code 2 to base 0xC, and anything else to 0. Those three bases are the same three the board inspect screen navigates - your six field slots at 0, the opponent's six at 6, and the played-card row at 0xC - so this is how a caller says which row of the board it means. Note the m2c signature has dropped the leading object arguments; the real call passes the duel and view through.

F0x80087308 is a permission predicate called from F0x80087EDC. Its default answer is YES and it refuses only in one combination: the counter duel+0x444 must be below 6, the second argument's +0x0A field must be positive, and one of the first +0x0A entries must already carry the flag at +0x446 - then it returns 0. If duel+0x444 has reached 6, or +0x0A is zero, it returns 1 WITHOUT INSPECTING ANYTHING. This is recorded explicitly because the natural misreading is the opposite one, that the counter being below 6 is a requirement for permission; it is a requirement for the REFUSAL path. Recorded as candidate: the identity of the second argument is not established, and while +0x0A is the combo-target card id in the card catalog record, here it is used as a LOOP BOUND, so either the argument is not a card record or the field is reused - that is not resolved.

F0x80088F78 is a duel+0x422 step machine (states 1-5): state 1 checks a confirm input (arg1->unk64==2) and, when both sides' live field counts (duel+0x72C plus duel+0x79E) are zero, skips straight to the finalize state (3) instead of sizing an animation duration from the winning side's slot count; state 2 advances a per-slot reveal counter (duel+0x428) up to duel+0x79E slots on a 6-tick cadence, calling arg1->unkF28; state 3 smoothly ramps four separate 16-bit counters (duel+0x428/0x42C/0x430/0x434) toward stored target values (duel+0x59C/0x59E/0x664/0x666) at up to one-sixtieth of the remaining delta per tick and pushes every updated value to the view via arg1->unkEA0(arg1, side, statIndex, value) -- a rolling stat-value display, matching the previously documented one-per-frame stat-plate roll family; state 4 polls a controller-vibration/select-bit combination before advancing; state 5 waits for arg1->unk64==0 to signal completion.

F0x80089974 is dispatched as effect opcode 0xA7's handler body from F0x80084320. Its duel+0x422 step machine flashes one of two view slots (state 1) over 15 ticks; sets view flags unk150 bit 0 and unk12E on the slot addressed by duel+0x43C and, on a select/confirm controller-bit test (via 0x8004B7D0 unk3FC/unk408/unk3F4 bit tests), either calls F0x800896f0 on one input combination or flags that slot's duel+0x46F byte to 1 and records duel+0x43C as the active index in duel+0x440 while playing sound 0x4001C (state 2); waits for F0x80087dc8 then hides that slot via unkF28 (state 3); shows a result banner via unkEAC comparing duel+0x434 to duel+0x440 (playing sound 0x40019) after a roughly-20-tick delay plus a roughly-0x5B-tick countdown (state 4); flashes the other slot (state 5); and finally compares duel+0x434 to duel+0x440, writing duel+0x440 to 1 when equal and 0 otherwise before completing (state 6) -- a two-slot pick/compare sequence, not a write to duel+0x446.

F0x8008A068 - at 366 lines the largest function in the cardgame overlay that no card research document mentioned - is the duel's BOARD INSPECT screen: a modal, three-row, cursor-driven card browser that suspends the duel HUD, lets the player move over the cards in play, and restores the HUD on exit. Its structure is a TWO-LEVEL step machine, which is the pattern the rest of the overlay uses too: the first switch is on the pending step byte duel+0x423 and holds the one-shot TRANSITION actions, and every arm converges on a block that copies +0x423 into the current step duel+0x422 and clears +0x423; the second switch, on +0x422, holds the per-frame POLL. Writing +0x423 is therefore how any arm requests a state change. Entry (step 1) saves view+0xB0 and view+0x104 into the global halfword pair at 0x800A5DA0 and zeroes them, sets duel+0x49D and duel+0x499 to 1, takes an initial row from F0x80089ED4 into duel+0x42C, zeroes the cursor duel+0x43C and calls view methods +0xECC and +0xEC8. The final step 15 restores both bytes from 0x800A5DA0 and sets the flag that makes the function return 1 - the only path that returns non-zero, i.e. 'screen finished'. Between them are THREE navigable rows, each a run of the view's 0x4C-byte card slots and each with its own count, poll step and teardown step: row 0 is the player's own six field slots at view indices 0..5, counted by duel+0x72C (already decoded as the side-0 field slot count), polled by step 5 and torn down by step 8; row 1 is the opposing side's six field slots at view indices 6..0xB, counted by duel+0x79E (the side-1 count, 0x72C + 0x72), polled by step 6 and torn down by step 0x0A; row 2 sits at view indices 0xC upward, counted by duel+0x575, polled by step 7 and torn down by step 9. Left and right (pad bits 5 and 7, read with both the pressed and the auto-repeat getter) move within a row through F0x80089F18(duel, view, row, +-1), clamped to that row's count; up and down (bits 4 and 6) leave the row, and the teardown steps wait 0x0B frame ticks in duel+0x424 before landing. Vertically the rows are ordered row 1 above row 2 above row 0, and a row whose count is zero is SKIPPED rather than entered. Crossing between a six-wide field row and row 2 rescales the cursor - halved going in, doubled plus one coming out - so row 2 has half as many entries as a field row, i.e. three. Cancel (bit 0x0E) plays the selection-cancelled sound 0x800450BD and requests teardown step 0x0B, which calls view +0xEC4, refreshes all four view groups through +0xEB0(1..4) and sets duel+0x499 to 2. This is also the second consumer found for the global save area around 0x800A5DA0: F0x800A2608 saves six view words into 0x800A5DC8 the same way, so that region is a shared 'suspended HUD' scratch used by the duel's sub-screens.

F0x8008AD58 and F0x8008AD78 are one-line forwarders, to F0x80089ED4 and F0x80089F18 respectively, with no logic of their own. They are used as case bodies inside the poll switch of F0x8008AD98. They are recorded so they stop appearing as unattributed functions; there is no behaviour to decode in them beyond the call. This claim carries an evidence reference only to satisfy the ledger's shape - the two function bodies are three and four lines and were read in full.

F0x8008C8D8 chooses a DEFAULT CURSOR POSITION in two passes. The FORWARD pass stands as recorded: it scans from the current index at duel+0x668 up to the per-set availability count at duel+0x41B, stops on the first entry carrying the combo-run flag +0x446, and writes that index to the cursor duel+0x440. CORRECTION 2026-08-08 to the BACKWARD pass, which was recorded in the wrong direction. At .L0x00009ca8 the branch is BNEZ, and the decrement at .L0x00009cb0 sits on the not-taken path: the backward scan from index 0x27 SKIPS entries whose +0x446 flag is ZERO and STOPS on the first entry whose flag is NONZERO. It therefore seeks a FLAGGED entry, not an unflagged one, and lands on the start index only when it finds none. Since the forward pass has already established that no flagged entry exists inside the availability window, the backward pass is reaching a flagged entry OUTSIDE that window. The earlier summary - that the cursor otherwise falls back to a non-combo entry from the end of the list - is backwards. A second detail not previously captured: at .L0x00009c44 the forward pass computes its flag offset as (current - start), so +0x446 is indexed relative to where the scan began rather than to the array base; this is invisible whenever the scan starts at 0. Both passes still finish by setting the legal-target flag +0x46F on the entry the cursor ended on.
claims.notes: Supersedes the authority-3 m2c reading in exe-decomp/cardgame_c/F0x8008c8d8.c, which rendered the forward index as var_v1*0 and inverted the backward test. Found while implementing plan items C2/C3; engine/systems/card-battle.ts defaultComboCursor implements the assembly and tests/card-battle.test.js pins the direction so it cannot silently revert.

claims.statement: RETRACTED 2026-08-08. The forward pass this claim describes is correct, but its BACKWARD pass is recorded in the wrong direction, and its summary - that the cursor otherwise falls back to a non-combo entry from the end of the list - is backwards. At pro/cardgame.s .L0x00009ca8 the branch is BNEZ and the decrement at .L0x00009cb0 sits on the not-taken path, so the backward scan SKIPS entries whose +0x446 flag is clear and STOPS on the first FLAGGED one, landing on the start index only when it finds none. This claim rested on the authority-3 m2c output in exe-decomp/cardgame_c/F0x8008c8d8.c, which inverted the branch test and rendered the forward index as var_v1*0. Superseded by cardgame-f8008c8d8-backward-pass-seeks-a-flagged-entry, which carries the corrected reading plus the previously unrecorded relative-index quirk at .L0x00009c44.

F0x8008C988, previously unmentioned, walks the entries from duel+0x5A0 to index 0x27, resolving each through the pile array at duel+0x5B0 and the instance table to a card record, and keeps the entry whose record field +0x08 is SMALLEST, seeded with a sentinel of 400 (0x190) so any real value wins. The winning index goes to the selection cursor duel+0x440; if no entry qualifies the cursor is left at the starting index. This is a sibling of the already-recorded hand-side chooser F0x800A4328, which performs the same minimum over the same record field, so the two share one 'cheapest by +0x08' policy applied to different lists. Because the comparison is a strict less-than, ties keep the FIRST entry reached.

claims.coverage: The opcode set is every entry of the dumped 174-entry ENTER dispatch table whose target calls F0x8008CA4C, grouped mechanically: exactly 0x70..0x82, nineteen opcodes, nothing else. Each mask was read from its own dispatch block rather than from a shared extractor, which is how 0x7E was caught: it builds its argument with lui, so an extractor reading the immediate alone reports 0xF where the value is 0x000F0000. The fifteen-byte clear was counted from the loop bound rather than assumed from the field-slot count. NOT tested: whether any code outside this function writes duel+0x438.
claims.statement: F0x8008CA4C(duel, view, mask) is the enter phase shared by card-effect opcodes 0x70 through 0x82, and it opens a targeting prompt rather than selecting anything. It clears the selection cursor duel+0x440, sets the step counter duel+0x422 to 1, latches its third argument into duel+0x438 as the target-kind mask, clears fifteen bytes of the field mark array beginning at duel+0x46F, sets duel+0x49D to 2 and duel+0x499 to 1, and drives six view methods to put the selection interface on screen, one of which receives a halfword read from the current play-history entry at +0x580. The nineteen opcodes differ only in the mask: 0x70 mask 0, 0x71 mask 0x4000, 0x72 mask 0x2000, 0x73 mask 0x0001, 0x74 mask 0x0004, 0x75 mask 0x0010, 0x76 mask 0x0040, 0x77 mask 0x0100, 0x78 mask 0x0002, 0x79 mask 0x0008, 0x7A mask 0x0020, 0x7B mask 0x0080, 0x7C mask 0x0200, 0x7D mask 0x03FF, 0x7E mask 0x000F0000, 0x7F mask 0x8000, 0x80 mask 0x1400, 0x81 mask 0x0400 and 0x82 mask 0x1000. The masks fall into three groups. Bits 0 to 9 are ten single-bit selectors used by ten opcodes, with 0x7D passing all ten at once. Bits 10 to 15 are the pile selectors whose meaning is fixed by the already-recorded confirm gate in F0x8008CB5C, so 0x81 is the acting side's trash, 0x82 its folder, 0x80 both of those, 0x71 its hand, 0x72 the opposing folder and 0x7F the opposing hand. Opcode 0x7E uses a fourth group at bits 16 to 19, which that confirm gate does not test and therefore accepts unconditionally, and opcode 0x70 passes no bits at all.
limitations: What the ten low mask bits select is NOT established. They pair up (0x73/0x78, 0x74/0x79, 0x75/0x7A, 0x76/0x7B, 0x77/0x7C) which suggests five things times two sides, but nothing here demonstrates that and the field is recorded elsewhere as six slots per side.
The bits 16 to 19 group used by opcode 0x7E has no gate in the confirm path and no other consumer was found; its meaning is unknown.
The six view methods are cited by slot offset only; none of their bodies was read, so the visible effect of the prompt is not described.
The fifteen-byte clear at duel+0x46F is reported as counted. Why fifteen, when the field is recorded as six slots per side, is unresolved.
duel+0x499 and duel+0x49D are recorded as written with the values seen; their meaning is not established.
No runtime observation was made.
derivation: python3 (group the dumped enter dispatch table by target)

claims.statement: F0x8008cb5c, the picker that completes card-effect opcodes 0x70..0x7e, is a CONFIRM/CANCEL prompt and was the first card-duel input path read end to end. It is a three-step machine on duel+0x422. Step 1 waits for view+0x64 == 2 with duel+0x498 == 0. Step 2 reads pad port 0 through the shared pad service at 0x8004b7d0 slot +0x3f4 and tests LOGICAL BUTTON 0x0D - confirm, the circle button - via the id mapper at slot +0x408. On confirm it reads duel+0x438, which for this family holds the target-kind mask the enter phase selected, and switches on it: 0x400 and 0x1400 both read duel+0x5a2, 0x1000 reads duel+0x5a4, 0x4000 reads duel+0x5a6, 0x2000 reads duel+0x66c and 0x8000 reads duel+0x66e - the first three being side 0's per-player block fields at +0x06/+0x08/+0x0a and the last two side 1's at +0x08/+0x0a, given the block base duel+0x59c and side stride 0xc8. The confirm is ACCEPTED only when the selected counter is non-zero; any mask outside that set is accepted unconditionally. On acceptance it plays sound 0x4001c and returns 1. If confirm is not held it tests LOGICAL BUTTON 0x0E - cancel, the cross button - and on cancel plays a different sound, calls view +0xec4, writes 1 to duel+0x440, sets duel+0x499 and advances to step 3, the teardown, which returns 0. This independently CONFIRMS the documented semantics of duel+0x57a: -1 while pending, 0 for cancel, non-zero for a made choice. CORRECTED 2026-08-09, same day: an earlier revision of this statement asserted that 'the two targeting families differ in what they return - F0x8008cb5c yields a yes/no confirmation while F0x8008d594 yields a field-slot index - so they must not be described as the same picker.' That sentence was written WITHOUT reading F0x8008d594's step 2 and is RETRACTED. Both pickers return -1 pending, 1 on confirm and 0 on cancel, and both play sound 0x4001c on accept. See cardgame-f8008d594-is-also-a-confirm-cancel-prompt-not-a-slot-chooser. What actually differs is only the legality gate: this function switches on the target-kind mask in duel+0x438 and checks a per-player pile counter, whereas F0x8008d594 treats duel+0x438 as a boolean match flag. Limitations: the mapping from logical ids 0x0d/0x0e to physical buttons comes from the pad-service claim UI-PADSERVICE-STATIC-TABLE-001, which is itself only partially_verified and whose table contents are authority 3; no runtime press was observed here. The per-player block fields at +0x06/+0x08/+0x0a are identified positionally and are not named. The sound ids were not resolved to named effects.

F0x8008d594, the picker completing card-effect opcodes 0x8e..0x95, is a CONFIRM/CANCEL prompt with the same three-step shape and the same return alphabet as F0x8008cb5c. It reads pad port 0 through pad-service slot +0x3f4 and tests logical button 0x0d (confirm); on confirm it checks duel+0x438, the 'at least one slot matched' flag its own enter-phase sweep sets, refuses and stays pending when that flag is zero, and otherwise plays sound 0x4001c, clears the highlight bit on every marked slot and RETURNS THE CONSTANT 1. Not held, it tests logical button 0x0e (cancel), plays the cancel sound, calls view +0xec4, writes 1 to duel+0x440, sets duel+0x499 and advances to step 3, the teardown, which returns 0. THIS CORRECTS TWO EARLIER CLAIMS RECORDED THE SAME DAY. (1) cardgame-opcode-0x8e-0x95-update-phase-is-the-target-picker said the value stored into duel+0x57a is the chosen slot and that 'the chosen slot arrives in duel+0x57a for a later opcode to act on'. That is WRONG: the stored value is the constant 1, a confirmation. The identity of the affected slots never travels through duel+0x57a at all - it stays in the per-slot marking array duel+0x46f that the sweep filled, so the effect applies to ALL marked slots, not to one picked one. (2) cardgame-f8008cb5c-is-the-confirm-cancel-prompt-for-opcodes-0x70-0x7e asserted that the two families 'differ in what they return - F0x8008cb5c yields a yes/no confirmation while F0x8008d594 yields a field-slot index - so they must not be described as the same picker'. That sentence was written without reading F0x8008d594's step 2 and is retracted: both pickers return -1 pending, 1 on confirm, 0 on cancel. What actually differs between them is only the LEGALITY GATE - F0x8008cb5c switches on the target-kind mask in duel+0x438 and checks a per-player pile counter, while F0x8008d594 treats duel+0x438 as a boolean match flag. Note that duel+0x438 therefore carries different meanings in the two families, which is a further instance of the documented per-opcode reuse of that field. Limitation: the logical-id to physical-button mapping is inherited from UI-PADSERVICE-STATIC-TABLE-001 and no runtime press was observed.

F0x8008D594 is the multi-slot variant of the human player's target confirm. Where F0x8008CFDC highlights one pending card, F0x8008D594 walks duel+0x46F over indices 0..0x0B and sets bit 0 of the corresponding sprite's +0x150 for every flagged slot, so the player sees the whole affected set at once. Confirm is pad bit 0x0D and requires duel+0x438 to be non-zero, after which it plays 0x4001C, clears every highlight and returns 1. Cancel is pad bit 0x0E: it plays 0x800450BD, calls view+0xEC4, sets duel+0x440 to 1 and duel+0x499 to 2, moves to step state 3 and runs view+0xF24(0xF, 4, 0, 0x1000). This is the second independent reader of duel+0x438 as a selection-validity gate.

F0x8008D854, previously unmentioned in any card research document, is the S-ENERGY GAIN step. Given a side and a card slot it resolves the card's record through the resident catalog accessor, takes the record's first byte minus one as a category index, and if that index is below 5 increments the byte at duel + side*0xC8 + 0x59C + 0xC + index, i.e. the five-entry per-side array based at duel+0x5A8, capping it at 99 (0x63). It then pushes the new value to the view through method +0xEA0 with the side and category, so the on-screen energy figure updates in the same step. It returns 1 when it credited a point and 0 when the category was out of range. That the target array is the S-Energy pool is established independently: the summon affordability gate F0x80085FD0 is handed duel+0x5A8 as its energy argument at cardgame.s L3529. This supplies the concrete write side of the already-recorded rule that drawing a card generates one point of that card's colour, and it fixes the pool's per-colour ceiling at 99.

SUPERSEDED. This claim read F0x8008DA2C's branch on slot record byte +0x0A as selecting between two different KINDS of destination - an ordinary discard at duel+0x614 and a separate removed-from-play pile at duel+0x6DC. That is wrong. Reading the sibling F0x8008DC70 shows the same branch selects the OWNING SIDE: 0x6DC - 0x614 is exactly 0xC8, the per-player stride, and the branch value is passed to the view in the side argument position. F0x8008DA2C sends a leaving field card to its owner's discard pile, one pile per side. The correct statement is carried by cardgame-f8008dc70-returns-a-field-card-to-its-owner-hand.
claims.notes: Retracted by the lead on 2026-08-07, same session in which it was recorded. Root cause is the project's standing quantifier/naming trap: a two-way branch was named from its first observed use before the sibling function was read. The arithmetic that settles it - a 0xC8 delta between the two destinations - was available at the time and not checked.

claims.statement: F0x8008DB7C is a two-phase gate around one card slot's animation, keyed on duel+0x424. On the first call it sets +0x424 to 1, raises the view slot's flag at +0x12E, starts a move animation through view method +0xF08 and a scale animation through +0xF20, and returns 0 - not finished. On later calls it returns 1 only once the view slot's own progress field +0x14A has reached the step value, at which point it clears the slot's +0x12E and +0x120. So callers can invoke it every frame and use the return value as 'the card has finished moving'. It is invoked per combined slot index 0..11 by F0x8008DD38.

F0x8008DC70 returns a card from a field slot to its owner's HAND, and it is the exact sibling of F0x8008DA2C, which sends one to the owner's discard. Both address the slot as duel + side*0x72 + slot*0xE, read the byte at slot record +0x0A, and branch on it being 0 or 1, returning without moving anything on any other value. Here 0 appends the card reference to duel+0x600 indexed by the count at +0x5A6, and 1 appends it to duel+0x6C8 indexed by +0x66E. THIS CORRECTS AN EARLIER READING. 0x6C8 minus 0x600 is 0xC8 and 0x66E minus 0x5A6 is 0xC8 - the established per-player stride - and the branch value is handed to the view in the same argument position that F0x8008D854 uses for the SIDE. So slot record byte +0x0A is the OWNING SIDE of the card sitting in that slot, and each of these functions has ONE destination that it addresses for whichever side owns the card. The claim cardgame-f8008da2c-routes-a-leaving-card-to-one-of-two-piles read the same branch as two different KINDS of pile and is superseded by this: its +0x614 and +0x6DC are side 0's and side 1's discard, not a discard and a removed-from-play zone. This also identifies duel+0x6C8, the array the exchange sort at 0x8009D95C orders, as SIDE 1's HAND - i.e. that sort is the opponent ordering its own hand by AI play class.

F0x8008E5BC, at 287 lines the second-largest function in pro/cardgame and previously unmentioned in any card research document, is the field compaction routine that closes gaps after Digimon leave the field. Running under step state 1 it first zeroes four counter bytes at 0x800A5DC0 and 0x800A5DC2, then for each side walks that side's occupied slot count and counts the slots whose flag byte in the array at duel+0x46F equals 1 into the counter for that side. It then makes a second pass in which, for every flagged slot, it scans forward for the next slot whose flag is zero and EXCHANGES the two flag bytes, recording the pair as two bytes - source index then destination index - into successive entries of a table anchored at 0x800A5DA8. The output is therefore a MOVE LIST describing how the surviving Digimon slide up to fill the gaps, which the presentation layer can then animate, rather than a direct mutation of the field slots themselves. Recorded as candidate: the routine's structure and its two output tables are read directly, but the consumer of the 0x800A5DA8 move list and of the 0x800A5DC0 and 0x800A5DC2 counters has not been traced, and the exact indexing of the per-side flag pointer was not resolved against the twelve-slot layout that F0x800915D4 uses for the same array.

F0x8008E5BC is dispatched as effect opcode 0x4C's handler body from the interpreter F0x80084320 (gated on the duel+0x2F4 return value). Its duel+0x422 step machine: step 1 scans each side's field slots for match-flagged records, bubble-swaps matched cards toward the front of the per-side slot array while logging (src,dst) index pairs into a scratch table at 0x800A5DA8 and tallying the per-side match count into 0x800A5DC0, then issues card-art redraw calls (arg1->unkF08) for the swapped slots keyed by table 0x800A5958; step 2 is a plain per-side countdown at duel+0x424; step 3 copies the matched record's core field-slot bytes (offsets 0x730/0x731/0x734/0x735/0x739/0x73A) and its whole 0x108-0x148 view-data block from source to destination slot, reduces the side's live field count (duel+0x72C) by the tallied match count, then clears the view for every now-unused trailing slot via arg1->unkF18 and zeroes its unk120 field; step 4 is a one-tick done flag.

claims.coverage: The opcode set was not sampled: it is every entry of the dumped 174-entry update dispatch table whose target calls F0x8008EC44, grouped mechanically, which yields exactly 0x32..0x3A and 0x96 and nothing else. The mask bit assignment was derived from the assembly and then checked against an independent derivation, tools/extract_card_effects.py, whose header comment already states 'bits 2..7 card colour 1..6 = white, blue, green, red, black, brown'; the two agree. A third, structural check: the mark array is written at duel+0x446 for indices 0..count-1 with a maximum pile size of 40, giving 0x446..0x46D, which ends immediately before the separately recorded field-slot mark array at duel+0x46F. NOT tested: whether any other function also writes duel+0x446.
claims.statement: F0x8008EC44(duel, view, side, zone, mask) sweeps one card pile of one side and marks the members that pass a filter. The zone argument selects the pile: zone 2 is the ten-slot pile whose count is at per-player block +0x0A and whose instances are at duel+0x600; zone 3 is the forty-slot pile whose count is at block +0x08 and whose instances are read from duel+0x5B0 through a cursor at block +0x04; zone 4 is the forty-slot pile whose count is at block +0x06 and whose instances are at duel+0x614. For each occupied index it clears, then conditionally sets, the byte at duel+0x446 plus that index, resolving the instance through duel+0x50 to a card id and fetching that card's record. The mask is a bit set over kind and colour: bit 0 admits a record whose +0x03 kind is 0x10, bit 1 admits any other kind, and bits 2 to 7 admit record colours 1 to 6 through the six-halfword table at 0x800A58F4 holding 0x04, 0x08, 0x10, 0x20, 0x40 and 0x80. A card must pass both the kind bit and its colour bit. The routine returns 1 when at least one index matched. Ten update-phase opcodes call it: 0x32 zone 3 mask 0xFF, 0x33 zone 3 mask 0xFF, 0x34 zone 3 mask 0xFD, 0x35 zone 3 mask 0xFE, 0x36 zone 2 mask 0xFF, 0x37 zone 2 mask 0xFF, 0x38 zone 2 mask 0x81, 0x39 zone 2 mask 0xBF, 0x3A zone 4 mask 0xFF, and 0x96 zone 2 mask 0xFD. All ten discard the return value: nine jump to the shared completion tail that writes 2 to duel+0x2F4, and 0x96 instead writes 0x97 into duel+0x421. Which side each opcode targets is NOT established, because the side argument comes from the interpreter registers s2, s3 and s4, whose meaning is unresolved.
limitations: The side argument's provenance (interpreter registers s2/s3/s4) is unresolved, so no opcode in this family is attributed to the acting player or the opponent.

The pile roles (deck, hand, trash) are inferred from the array sizes and their offsets within the 0xC8 per-player block; the block layout is taken from the existing recorded claim, not re-derived here.
The resident call F0x8001EBF8 and the indirect record accessor it installs were not read; the claim treats the result only as 'the card record'.
It was not tested whether any function outside F0x8008EC44 writes the mark array at duel+0x446.
No runtime observation was made.
derivation: python3 callees.py (group the dumped update dispatch table by target)

claims.statement: Retracts the scope of 'cardgame-f800915d4-is-the-removal-sweep-not-the-damage-distributor' recorded earlier on 2026-08-07. Its finding about F0x800915D4 itself stands -- that function is the 0x4D/0x4E removal sweep and writes no per-slot stat. But it went on to conclude that duel+0x46F is 'not a battle-damage target list', and that is false: F0x8008DEF8 reads exactly that array to apply per-slot stat deltas. The error was generalising from one consumer of a shared array to the array's meaning.
claims.contradiction_rationale: Generalised one consumer's role to the whole shared array; F0x8008DEF8 demonstrably uses duel+0x46F as a stat-application target list.

claims.statement: F0x800915D4 is the iterator that distributes a per-slot effect across the field. It scans duel+0x46F at indices 0 through 0x0B - all twelve field slots, six per side - for the next non-zero flag, decomposes the index into a side (index >= 6) and a slot within that side (index, or index - 6), stores them in duel+0x42C and duel+0x430, and then applies F0x8008DAF4 or F0x8008DD38 to that one slot before resuming the scan. This identifies the CONSUMER half of the open question about per-slot battle damage distribution: distribution is this walk over the +0x46F flags. What sets those flags during Battle state 9 remains undecoded.

The premise of row 5 of the model's remaining-unknowns table -- that the per-slot battle-damage distribution mechanism 'is now known to be F0x8008DEF8 over the +0x46F flags, walked by F0x800915D4' -- is not supported by those functions' bodies. F0x800915D4 is the stateful handler of effect opcodes 0x4D/0x4E only, and neither of its two per-slot routines writes any per-slot stat: each reads the flagged slot's owner byte and card id and appends the card to that owner's discard pile (0x4D) or hand (0x4E). duel+0x46F is therefore a generic twelve-entry slot-selection flag array -- opcode 0xA7 also sets it for the two first-turn cards -- and not a battle-damage target list. The question of how a side's attack total becomes each slot's loss remains open, but F0x800915D4 is not where it happens, and an emulator session aimed at that function would not answer it.

F0x80092638 is dispatched as the shared handler for effect opcodes 0x12 and 0x13 from F0x80084320. Its duel+0x422 step machine (states 1-9) clears several view text fields on arg1 (unkE32/unkE34/unkE4C/unkE64/unkE7C), calls F0x800860d4 to advance/format a numeric field (duel+0x428) across a roughly-0x15-tick timer, draws a card-back/prompt icon via arg1->unkF08 keyed by a table at 0x800A5910 indexed by duel+0x575 (the played-this-turn stack depth), and in states 5-8 iterates a 15-entry (0xF) flag array at duel+0x46F and, for every non-zero byte, hides that slot's view via unkF1C (state 5) or sets its view record's unk146 selection-highlight field to 1 offset by duel+0x575 (state 6), before copying a 0x44-byte block from arg1+0x57C into a per-slot view-data block at (duel+0x575+0xC)*0x4C+0x108 and clearing bit 0 of unk150 for 12 view slots -- a prompt/reveal sequence keyed off a per-slot flag array (duel+0x46F) distinct from the documented combo-run flag at duel+0x446.

F0x80092E60 is dispatched as effect opcode 0x14's handler body from F0x80084320. It is a two-level pending(duel+0x423)/current(duel+0x422) step machine: its pending arm sets duel+0x440 to 1 or 2 and plays a view unkEE4 banner call (parameters 0x21 vs 0x22, the latter preceded by a sound-effect trigger through 0x80055C48) depending on which of two entry cases fired; its running states then advance a per-side reveal counter (duel+0x428) once per roughly 3-7 tick cadence (duel+0x434/+0x424) up to 6 field slots, calling view methods unkF08 (draw card art keyed by table 0x800A5958 indexed by duel+0x428) plus unkF20/unkF28/unkF24/unkF1C to fade in, clear, or discard the revealed slots, and pushes both sides' remaining totals (duel+0x42C/+0x430) to the HUD via unkEA0 before completing.

F0x80093adc, one of the three handlers behind card-effect opcodes 0x15..0x1a, clears duel+0x424, sets the step counter duel+0x422 = 1, and stores (occupied-slot count of the side named by its third argument) minus 1 into duel+0x428, reading that count from duel+0x72c + side*0x72. It therefore seeds a DESCENDING cursor over that side's occupied field slots for the opcode's update phase to walk. Note this is a second, unrelated use of duel+0x428, which on the stat-change path holds the pending AP amount - consistent with the existing claim that +0x428 is reused per opcode. Scope: this states what F0x80093adc seeds, NOT which of opcodes 0x15..0x1a route to it; the interpreter's per-opcode split across F0x80093624, F0x80093adc and F0x8009403c was not read.

F0x80093CAC is a fifteen-frame presentation handler that interpolates each side's displayed AP and HP from its own value toward the other side's, pushing the interpolated numbers to view fields 8 and 9 for both sides through F0x80093BC4(from, to, 0x0F, t), and then at the end EXCHANGES the stored totals: duel+0x59C with duel+0x664 and duel+0x59E with duel+0x666. Recorded as candidate because the exchange is read directly but the game situation that issues this opcode is not established, so whether it is a set-comparison flourish or a genuine effect that trades the two sides' totals is not settled.

F0x800942DC is dispatched as the shared handler for effect opcodes 0x19 (side argument 0) and 0x1A (side argument 1) from F0x80084320. Its duel+0x422 step machine, after a fixed roughly-0x15-tick delay, iterates the given side's field slots and, for every slot whose duel+0x446 byte is non-zero, hides that slot's view (arg1->unkF1C) and records the last hidden index into duel+0x434; a later state clears bit 2 of unk150 (unk150 &= 0xFB) on those same flagged slots' view records, waits for an arg1->unk656==1 acknowledgement, then plays an animated banner via arg1->unkEAC keyed by duel+0x438 and a message-position table at 0x800A5928, waits for arg1->unkE53==2, ramps duel+0x424 while polling a controller-bit combination, and finally hides slot index 0x11's view via unkF1C -- i.e. a per-side flagged-slot removal-with-result-banner sequence.

F0x80097ACC is one of eight sibling per-frame sub-controllers invoked every frame from F0x8009bba8's mode-1 update arm, which drives a composite UI object whose default arm allocates 14 child sprite/text widgets into arg1->unk0..unk34. F0x80097ACC's own step field is duel+0xDFA (not the common +0x422 family). On its running arm it decrements a per-slot countdown at duel+0xDF0, derives a 0-0x1000 animation ratio from it, and drives several of the composite's child widgets (arg1->unk0/unk4/unk8/unk1C/unk34) through shared show/position/draw-text/draw-icon methods (unk80, unk84, unk114, unk134, unk144, unk148), all keyed by an 8-byte-stride coordinate table at 0x800A59B0 indexed by duel+0xDE4, and message text resolved via the 0x80044B38/0x80044F4C string lookups keyed on duel+0xDE8; every arm of the outer switch converges on a shared tail call into F0x80097958 carrying the computed ratio, i.e. an animated stat/label-plate roll consistent with the previously documented stat-plate roll family.

F0x80099440 slides a banner in and out for one side of the duel, choosing between TWO hard-coded coordinate sets by its side argument: side 0 uses start and end values around 0x8D/0xF1 with a second axis at 0x8F, while side 1 uses 0x00/-0x64 with 0x50 - different enough that the two players' banners enter from opposite directions rather than mirroring a shared path. It is a state machine on a phase field: the in-phase counts a timer down by the resident frame delta and interpolates several fields linearly between the two sets, and when the timer expires it advances the phase and zeroes the timer. A shared horizontal extent of 0x113 and a shared third value are used by both sides. With this the pro/cardgame overlay has no functions left that no research document or ledger claim describes.

CardDuelView method slot +0xf40 holds F0x8009cf60, installed by the view constructor at RAM 0x8009d520. It takes (view, fieldSlotEntry), indexes the halfword table at view+0x50 by that entry to recover a card id, adds 1, and reads the card's CARDPAK record through the resident accessor installed by F0x8001ebf8, returning the record's first byte. CARDPAK +0x00 is the card colour (1..6 = white, blue, green, red, black, brown), so +0xf40 is the field-slot colour lookup used by the colour-filter opcodes 0x91..0x95. Limitation: the returned byte is identified as CARDPAK +0x00 from the record layout and the accessor idiom, not from a runtime read.

F0x8009D540 plays a SCRIPTED SEQUENCE from the four-byte-record table at 0x800A5BF0. While its mode is 1 it starts the current step, optionally biasing the step's id by a global at 0x8005CCA8 when the record's third halfword is set, then polls a resident 'still playing' predicate and only advances when that returns zero - so steps run one after another rather than on a timer. Two record values are control codes rather than content: -2 makes the player skip an ADDITIONAL step and raise a flag at +0x50, and -1 ends the sequence by switching the object to mode 3. Any mode outside 1..3 resets the script back to step zero. The stepped ids are passed to a resident entry at 0x80044F44 and polled through 0x80040000 +0x4F3C, which is an audio-shaped interface, but this claim does NOT assert the sequence is audio - only that it is a table-driven step player with skip and end markers.

F0x8009DBE8 is a longer sibling of the already-recorded F0x8009DF68: it selects the same per-side pile counter by the same code 0, 1 or 2, zeroes the same three progress fields and computes the same duration of count*4 + 10, but then takes a further branch when the pile is NOT empty, doing additional view work through the object reached at its view argument's +0x18. So the pair is a short setup and a full setup over one shared animation block; an empty pile skips the extra work in the longer one. What that extra work is was not read.

F0x8009E024, at 235 lines the largest still-unattributed function in the overlay, is the FULL BOARD RESYNC: it rebuilds the view from the duel state rather than deciding anything. It walks the six field slot records of a side at stride 0xE, and for each one positions the matching view card slot through view method +0xF14 using a banked layout pair from the table at 0x800A5958, re-points that slot at the card the record holds via +0xF3C, and copies two further record bytes into the view slot's +0x14B and +0x14C, forcing a highlight state when the pending-refresh flag duel+0x49C is set. It then clears that flag and, when the played-card stack is non-empty, rebuilds the stack rows at view slots 0x0C upward the same way. A multi-case state machine follows. This is why the board redraws correctly after any change: one function re-derives every visible card position and identity from the duel.

F0x8009E668 is called unconditionally from the duel frame poll F0x800a2df8, before that function's switch on duel+0x2F4 (the arm that runs the effect-opcode interpreter F0x80084320 for unk2F4==1), so it runs on every poll regardless of the effect VM's phase, unlike the opcode-0x## handlers. It implements a two-level pending/current step machine on a substructure at duel+0x498 (pending byte at duel+0x499 copied into the current byte pair at duel+0x498/+0x49B). On first entry it copies 40 card records' duel+0x49E byte into the matching card-view record's unk151 field (stride 0x4C on arg1->unk18) and sizes a duration from the larger of the two sides' live field counts (duel+0x72C, duel+0x79E); its running states animate field-slot highlight flashes via arg1->unk18->unkF24/unkEA4/unkEA8 gated by those same per-side field counts and by the played-this-turn stack depth at duel+0x575, i.e. it is the frame-tick coordinator for a field-wide highlight/flash effect layered on top of whichever opcode is currently executing.

Answers row 12 of the remaining-unknowns table, which listed duel method +0x810 (F0x8009F04C) plus F0x800A0590 and F0x800A0628 as 'small but unread'. All three are now read. F0x8009F04C is the pile shuffle already documented in section A.5. F0x800A0590(duel, playerBlock) is HAND COMPACTION: it walks the block's +0x0A hand count downward (lh 0xa($a1) at 0x800a0590), and for each index flagged in duel+0x46F (lb 0x46f at 0x800a05a8) it shifts the remaining halfwords of the hand array at block +0x64 down over it (lhu 0x64 at 0x800a05e0) and decrements the count -- i.e. it removes every selected card from a hand and closes the gap. F0x800A0628(duel, side, cardId, slot) is the FIELD-SLOT CONSTRUCTOR: it computes duel + side*0x72 + 0x72C + slot*0xE, stores the card reference and the owning side, zeroes the two accumulating stat cells, seeds the other two from the card record, and stamps a per-duel sequence number taken from a post-incremented counter at duel+0x308.

F0x800A2608, 247 lines and previously unmentioned in any card research document, is a sub-screen runner that first SNAPSHOTS the card effect interpreter's working state. It is a state machine on duel+0x568, a step byte separate from the effect VM's own duel+0x422. Its entry state block-copies duel+0x420 through duel+0x497 into duel+0x4F0 onward - a 0x78-byte region that covers the current-opcode byte at +0x420, the pending-opcode latch at +0x421, the step byte at +0x422, the scratch words at +0x424 through +0x438 and the per-slot flag array at +0x46F - so duel+0x4F0 is a saved copy of the interpreter's working state rather than an independent structure. It then zeroes duel+0x569, copies six consecutive view words from view+0xDE4 into the global save area at 0x800A5DC8, calls the view method at +0xEF4, and advances to state 2, which waits for view+0xE0A to reach 2 before continuing. The pattern is save the interpreter and the HUD numbers, run a sub-screen, and presumably restore afterwards. Recorded as candidate: the save side is read directly, but the matching restore was not located and the sub-screen the view method opens was not identified.

F0x80086F24 is the field cursor move helper: it plays sound id 0x4001B, un-highlights the slot the cursor is leaving by clearing bit 0 of view slot +0x150 and zeroing +0x12E, adds the caller's SIGNED delta to the cursor duel+0x43C so one helper serves both directions, then highlights the new slot by setting the same bit and flag and repositioning it through view method +0xF0C. This gives a FOURTH card-duel sound id a decoded trigger: 0x4001B is the field cursor move sound, alongside 0x8004513E (cursor move in the two-option prompt), 0x4001C (selection confirmed) and 0x800450BD (selection cancelled). It states when the id is played, not which audio sample it resolves to. F0x800870A4 and F0x8008BC8C are near-identical siblings differing in how the list length reaches them.

F0x80094848 recomputes both sides' AP and HP totals from the field and reconciles them against the stored values. For each side it walks that side's occupied field slots with a 0xE stride, accumulating the halfword at slot+0x08 as AP and the halfword at slot+0x0A as HP, taking side 0's slots from duel+0x734 with its count at duel+0x72C and side 1's from duel+0x7A6 with its count at duel+0x79E - the two field regions being 0x72 apart. It then compares the four sums against the stored totals at duel+0x59C and +0x59E for side 0 and duel+0x664 and +0x666 for side 1, and only if any of the four disagrees does it enter the animation state; otherwise it completes immediately. Since 0x664 - 0x59C and 0x666 - 0x59E are both exactly 0xC8, this is a fifth independent witness to the per-player block stride, and it establishes that the AP and HP totals at the head of each per-player block are a cache of the field sum rather than an independently maintained score.

The side's occupied-slot count byte at duel+0x72c + side*0x72 is incremented by F0x80091c6c, the switch-2 update callee for card-effect opcodes 0x4f..0x55, NOT by the enter-phase placement constructor F0x80091858. This answers the gap left open by claim cardgame-opcode-0x4f-0x55-place-reserved-instances-0x50-0x56-on-the-field. F0x80091c6c is a four-step machine on duel+0x422: step 1 waits for the view's per-slot byte +0x14a (view per-slot stride 0x4c) to reach 1 and issues view method +0xf1c; step 2 issues view +0xf08 with (slot, 0x14, position, colour argument) and sets the per-slot halfword +0x12e; step 3 waits on +0x14a reaching 1 again - the placement animation reporting done - then sets step 4, clears +0x12e, and increments the count byte in the delay slot of its jump to the return path, so the increment executes; step 4 is the only step that returns 1, which the interpreter treats as 'opcode complete'. The consequence is a real ordering rule: a card placed by an effect is not counted as occupying a field slot, and therefore is invisible to every consumer that bounds its loop by that count - including the 0x8e..0x95 targeting sweep - until its placement animation has finished. Limitations: the view methods +0xf08/+0xf1c and the per-slot fields +0x12e/+0x14a are cited by offset and not named; the position and colour arguments are derived from a table at 0x800a5958 indexed by the word at 0x8005ccb0, which was not decoded.

Corrects the offset LABELS of the 0x4D/0x4E claim recorded earlier the same day; the absolute addresses in it were right and only the field-slot-relative names were off by two. The field-slot constructor F0x800A0628 bases its writes at duel + side*0x72 + 0x72C + slot*0xE (addiu $s0,0x72c at 0x800a0668), whereas section E.4's slot RECORD starts at 0x72E because 0x72C is the slot-count byte. Relative to the record, the constructor writes: +0x00 the card reference (sh $s4,0x2($s0) at 0x800a06c4), +0x02 AP and +0x04 HP both initialised to zero, +0x06 and +0x08 from the card record, and +0x0A the owning side (sb $s1,0xc($s0) at 0x800a06cc, with the same value also written to +0x0B). So the fields the destroy/return pair reads are the card reference at record +0x00 (absolute duel+0x72E) and the owner at record +0x0A (absolute duel+0x738) -- NOT '+0x02' and '+0x0C' as first recorded. This also corroborates E.4 independently: AP at record +0x02 is absolute duel+0x730, which is the cell F0x8008DEF8 accumulates into.

The field-slot record layout, read from the placement constructor F0x80091858 and stated against the origin duel+0x72c + side*0x72 + slotIndex*0x0e (note: sections that quote a field-slot offset against the origin duel+0x72e read 2 lower). Per-side stride 0x72 and per-slot stride 0x0e are both confirmed by the address arithmetic. The block's first byte is the side's occupied-slot count, which physically overlaps slot 0's +0x00/+0x01. On placement the constructor writes: +0x02 u16 card INSTANCE index (the duel+0x50 table index, the field F0x8009cf60 reads to resolve colour); +0x04 and +0x06 u16 running AP and HP modifiers, both zeroed at placement and later accumulated into by F0x8008def8; +0x08 u16 base AP copied from CARDPAK +0x01; +0x0a u16 base HP copied from CARDPAK +0x02; +0x0c u8 set to the constant 2; +0x0d u8 owning side; +0x0e u8 a duel-unique placement ordinal taken from the post-incremented counter duel+0x308. Limitation: +0x0c's constant 2 is observed only on this placement path, so it is not named here; whether other writers set it to other values was not checked.

F0x80096828 builds the folder COMPOSITION tally. It allocates a 0x74-byte widget on allocator group 0x1C with F0x80096418 as its per-frame handler, clears SIX counters at widget+0x60..+0x65, then walks all 40 halfword entries of one folder at 0x80048D34 + folder*0x66, resolving each through the resident catalog accessor and incrementing the counter selected by the record's first byte minus one. So the widget holds a per-category histogram of a whole folder - how many of each card kind the deck contains. The SIX buckets are notable against the FIVE-entry S-Energy array that F0x8008D854 credits, which rejects any category index of 5 or above. That is consistent with the already-recorded rule that one card colour costs no energy: there are six card categories, and only five of them have an energy pool. This claim does not name the sixth.

The folder chooser holds its choice in duel+0x2EA over the range 0..2 and the cursor does NOT wrap at either end. Its input state reads logical button 4 to move up, taking the branch only when duel+0x2EA is greater than zero, and logical button 6 to move down, taking it only when duel+0x2EA is less than 2; each successful move plays sound 0x4001B. Logical button 13 confirms, plays a different sound 0x4001C, and advances the machine. The cursor's screen position for each of the three choices is read from a four-byte-stride table at 0x800A5D48 indexed by the choice.
claims.coverage: Both movement arms and the confirm arm were read from the assembly of the input state, and the no-wrap half of the claim rests on the two branch instructions quoted rather than on the absence of a wrap: blez skips the decrement at zero and slti/beqz skips the increment at two, so both ends are explicitly guarded. Only the input state was read; the surrounding 22-step machine's arrival and closing animation steps were not.
limitations: Static reading only; neither screen has been observed in the running game. The rig session of 2026-08-24 entered from a save state positioned past both of them.

The folder chooser claim covers its input state only. The plate arrival order, the waits between the three plates, the closing order, and what the final step copies out of save RAM including any empty-folder fallback were NOT read, and those are the rest of CARD-Q007.
The coin-toss claim deliberately stops short of which card must be picked to lead. Asserting it would require the seed polarity through mode 3, which was not traced here.

claims.statement: The folder chooser F0x8009F110 builds its three folder plates in folder order 0,1,2, each creation followed by an 11-tick wait, with the cursor marker created only after the third plate; the plate x/y pairs are read from the s16 table 0x800A5D48. It moves the choice with logical Up/Down (4/6) without wrapping, confirms on Circle (0xD, sound 0x4001C), then closes the plates in the same 0,1,2 order with 4-tick waits and sound 0x4001A, and copies the chosen folder's 40 one-based card ids from save 0x80048D34+folder*0x66+0x63E, falling back to the built-in list 0x800A5C74 when that folder is empty. Correction 2026-09-13: the empty-folder test is a HALFWORD load (lh 0x63e), and the fallback list 0x800A5C74 is copied VERBATIM (no -1), unlike the normal path which decrements each id.
claims.notes: Read 2026-09-13 from the F0x8009F110 assembly closure. The marker F0x80096180 is created at plate 0 and repositioned to the selected plate through its +0x68 method, so it is the folder cursor and not a name plate; the plate widget F0x80096828 counts a folder's six element buckets. The numeric values of 0x800A5D48 were not re-read from a duel dump here; the complete-model doc records (23,80),(23,125),(23,170) as [C]. Corrections verified 2026-09-13 in cardgame.s:29359-29398: `lh $v0,0x63e` is the emptiness test; the normal copy does `addiu $v0,-0x1`, the fallback at .L0x0001cb24 does not.
claims.coverage: Read from the F0x8009F110 mode-2 action-state machine: arrival states 1/3/5 with the 0xb waits at L166/L218/L270/L308, the pad reads at L337/L407 (4/6) and L491 (0xd), the close states 13/15/17 with the 0x4 waits at L669/L721/L773 and the 0x1a sound, and the save copy at state 21. The full intermediate wait set (0xF after confirm, 6 at the set-end) was not itemised.

claims.statement: The mode-2 folder chooser F0x8009F110 reads only Up (logical 4, with auto-repeat), Down (logical 6) and Circle (logical 0xD, pressed word only): Up/Down move the 0..2 cursor without wrapping and play 0x4001B; Circle confirms, plays 0x4001C and advances the state; Cross, Triangle and Square are never read, so the screen has no cancel arm.
claims.notes: Static read of exe-decomp/cardgame_c/_asm/F0x8009f110.s:321-555. The walker's Triangle/Cross cancel (web/cardduel.js) has no original counterpart. Worker file .dw3-research/loop-card/worker.md.
claims.coverage: Exhaustive read of the routine's single pad-service block: F0x8009F110 state 9 (asm 0x321-0x555) is the only place it touches D0x8004B7D0; the three reads (logical 4, 6, 0xD) are each followed to their branch, and states 1-8 read no pad. Lead re-read the Circle arm. A Triangle/Cross/Square read would have appeared as a logical 0xC/0xE/0xF call in that same block and does not.
claims.frontier_rationale: Residual of the resolved folder-chooser frontier CARD-Q007 (the A2 row of docs/research/card/cardduel-gap-2026-09-03.md); no open frontier covers the chooser's pad arms.

claims.statement: THE DECK EDITOR HAS NO FIXED PER-CARD COPY CEILING. The limit on how many copies of a card a folder may hold is simply HOW MANY THE PLAYER OWNS. F0x800847C0 in pro/stcrddek builds the editor's availability table in two passes. First it seeds a 0x13B-entry - 315, one per card id, matching the catalog size - working array from the save's per-card OWNED-COUNT byte array based at 0x80048D34 + 0x3A2. Then it walks all 40 entries of the currently selected folder, whose base 0x80049372 is exactly 0x80048D34 + 0x63E - the folder entry array already recorded at a 0x66 stride per folder - and DECREMENTS the running count for each card id it finds there. What remains per card id is therefore 'copies owned minus copies already in this folder', i.e. how many more of that card are still available to add. No constant is compared against, and no value of four appears anywhere in the computation. This CONTRADICTS the browser implementation's four-copies-per-card ceiling, which is an invention with no support in the original code, and it answers the standing question of what stcrddek's real deck constraint is: collection size is the constraint. It also identifies two save structures: the owned-count array at +0x3A2 and, already known, the folder entries at +0x63E.

The selected folder plate is the folder-cursor marker drawing card clip 0x47/71, and its CLUT-row animation is computed, not table-driven: while looping (marker+0x63 clear) the row offset is (marker+0x50 >> 2) mod 16, a linear 16-row wraparound at four counter units per row; on confirm F0x80096150 sets +0x63 so the offset becomes the one-shot min(marker+0x50 >> 1, 7).
claims.notes: RESOLVED the 8-vs-16 disagreement 2026-09-14 (turn 79). The carddata2 CLUT block has 16 rows, not 8: tools/extract_screen_packs.py now cuts {70: 8, 71: 16} and web/assets/ui/carddata2_sheet.{png,json} were regenerated (all other clips' authored geometry unchanged). web/cardduel.js replaces the CHOOSER.rowCycle ping-pong with chooserRow(markerAge, confirmed) = looping (markerAge>>2)%16, confirm min(markerAge>>1,7); the marker age starts at CHOOSER.cursorTick, and the marker keeps drawing through the confirm one-shot. Proof: tools/verify_cardduel_row_cycle.mjs (real lab chooser, selectedRow timeline), tests/cardduel-ui.test.js (arithmetic + 16 extracted rows).
claims.coverage: The 16-row CLUT was verified by cutting k=0..15 from the bundled carddata2 pack: all 16 rows read, and k=8..15 mirror k=7..0. The walker's arithmetic is driven live (tools/verify_cardduel_row_cycle.mjs: loop 0,1,7,8,15,0; confirm min(counter>>1,7) to the 7 clamp) and unit-tested.
claims.frontier_rationale: Residual of the resolved folder-chooser frontier CARD-Q007 (the A4 row of docs/research/card/cardduel-gap-2026-09-03.md); the walker now matches.

claims.statement: Fourteen of the 268 entries the lift pipeline emits for pro/cardgame are not functions but arms of two register-indirect jump tables, so the overlay holds about 254 functions. F0x8008C6E0 dispatches through jr $v0 twice, and the six entries F0x8008c7e8, F0x8008c7f4, F0x8008c800, F0x8008c80c, F0x8008c818 and F0x8008c81c are its table arms; F0x8008D274 dispatches through jr $v0 once, and the eight entries F0x8008d3fc, F0x8008d42c, F0x8008d45c, F0x8008d480, F0x8008d4a4, F0x8008d4bc, F0x8008d4e0 and F0x8008d4fc are its arms. Each arm begins at the instruction immediately after its container's jr plus that jump's delay slot, which is exactly where a jump-table target lands, and each has no callers and no successful m2c lift because it is not a function body. This is the known lift-pipeline entry-selection failure mode rather than a genuine decompilation failure, and it means the recorded baseline of 268 functions with 128 never mentioned in research is inflated by the same fourteen. Reading the two containers in assembly covers all fourteen arms at once.

docs/research/card/cardgame-function-census-2026-08-07.md attributes every one of the 268 entries in pro/cardgame with a mechanically derived role, the effect opcodes that reach it, the step byte it switches on, the duel fields it writes, the CardDuelView method slots it drives, and its direct callers. The role distribution is 89 helper or predicate, 57 immediate opcode handlers, 36 board mutators, 32 stateful opcode handlers, 26 board-and-presentation, 20 unlifted, 7 presentation and 1 stateful step machine. Twenty-one entries have no direct caller and are reached only through a method pointer or a jump table, which is why callers and references queries return nothing for them. This is a triage index, not a decode: a row states what a function touches, not what it means, and every negative drawn from it is bounded by the twenty entries with no lift.

The card game's hand limit is ten, and three cards enforce it in their own programs. Tidal Wave, Summon Cancel and Eclipse Undo all carry the identical thirteen-opcode tail 03 09 08 2F 2B 37 AA 07 2C 3F 0A 11 06. Read against the branch table, that tail is a loop: 0x09 jumps forward nine, past the whole block, when the side's hand holds ten cards or fewer; otherwise the block throws that hand's weakest card away through the own-hand selector 0x37 and the minimum-rank picker 0xAA, and 0x0A at the end jumps back nine while the hand still holds more than ten. The 0x11 that follows flips which side the last play counts as, and the enclosing repeat-twice then runs the same block for the other player. Both jump distances land exactly on the block's boundaries, which is the corroboration for the branch convention rather than an assumption of it.
claims.coverage: The three programs carrying the tail were found by enumerating all 60 effect programs in web/assets/data/card_effects.json and matching the opcode subsequence; no other program contains it. The claim is NOT that ten is the hand limit everywhere in the game - only these three programs were read, and no other enforcement site was searched for.
limitations: Recorded as candidate rather than partially_verified because the identification of ten as THE hand limit generalises from three card programs. A hand-limit check outside the effect VM, for example in the draw phase, was not looked for and would be the proper corroboration.
0xAA is taken as the minimum-rank picker from the existing hand-discard trace in section G.0, not re-read here.

claims.statement: The card duel is launched by an NPC dialogue state's on_close write into flag bank 0x76 or 0x78. Resident set_flag F0x800165ac keys the bank as (id >> 8) & 0xFFFE and routes 0x76 to F0x80016378(index, 0) and 0x78 to F0x80016378(index, 1); that function calls the screen-pack dispatcher D0x8008b770(0x700, index * 2 + mode + 1, 0, 0, 0). Screen-pack kind 0x700 is therefore the card duel, and the packed second argument selects which duel. Empirically bound at runtime: the s335 Tamer Mitch NPC whose duel dialogue state (estalk02 index 113) carries on_close flag 0x7606 = bank 0x76 index 6 loaded the pro/cardgame overlay and started a duel, with no confirmation prompt.
claims.notes: Kind 0x700 is bound empirically from one capture, not from a decoded kind->overlay table; which deck/AI the packed argument selects is not decoded. Bank 0x78 (mode 1) was never exercised.

claims.statement: F0x80099D18 is the generic LINEAR TWEEN runner behind the duel's moving elements. Each call subtracts the resident frame delta from the remaining time at +0x0E and, while time remains, sets the live x and y at +0x00 and +0x02 by interpolating from the endpoint pair at +0x08/+0x0A back toward the start pair at +0x04/+0x06 in proportion to remaining time over the total at +0x0F. The motion is therefore strictly LINEAR - no easing. When the time expires it snaps exactly to the endpoint, zeroes the timers and raises a done flag at +0x10, so it cannot overshoot and callers can poll that flag. Separately, F0x8009E62C is a broadcast visibility setter: on a pending request it writes fifteen consecutive per-slot bytes at +0x49E to 1 only when the request code is exactly 2 and to 0 for every other non-zero code, then clears the request - one call showing or hiding a whole row at once.

F0x800875AC and F0x8008BE04 - with F0x800878B4 and F0x80087B80 as further siblings - are one FAMILY of list-selection polls, not four unrelated functions. Each runs per frame while its screen is up and does the same four things: it keeps the view slot under the cursor duel+0x43C highlighted; on left it calls a cursor-move helper with -1 provided the cursor is above 0; on right it calls the same helper with +1 provided the cursor is below a list length minus one; and on confirm it accepts ONLY IF the entry under the cursor carries the flag at +0x446, in which case it copies the cursor into duel+0x440 and requests that screen's next step, while cancel plays the cancelled sound, sets duel+0x440 to -1 and requests a different teardown step. Two things vary between members and nothing else does: where the list LENGTH comes from - F0x800875AC reads it from the caller's second object at +0x0A while F0x8008BE04 reads duel+0x434 - and which step numbers each requests. This makes +0x446 the SELECTABLE flag from the player's side: an entry without it cannot be confirmed on, which is the mechanism behind the dimming seen in the combo picker.

Duel modes 5 and 7 are the same mechanic run twice per round: their entries in both the enter table (0x80083a10 and 0x80083a18, both 0x800a1bb4 -> F0x800a0548) and the update table (0x80083a38 and 0x80083a40, both 0x800a1d14 -> F0x8009fdd8) are byte-identical, so the two modes execute the same code with only the duel state distinguishing them. F0x800a0548 clears a third-level sub-state byte at duel+0x574 and calls context member ctx+0x814 with the hand array at duel+0x600 and the count at duel+0x5a6; F0x8009fdd8 bounds duel+0x574 to 0..0x12 and dispatches through a 19-entry jump table at 0x80083910, making the play-a-card step a third nested state machine below the mode and round machines. The English card-duel language file names exactly six phases - Start, Draw, Load, Summon, Compile, Battle - and Load Phase and Compile Phase are the only two whose prompt line is identical (Select and use a Program Card.), which is exactly the pairing the shared code implies. Mapping the six repeating modes 3..8 onto those six names in order (3 = Start, 4 = Draw, 5 = Load, 6 = Summon, 7 = Compile, 8 = Battle) is consistent with every structural fact found here - the Load/Compile code sharing at 5 and 7, the win/lose decision falling in mode 4 next to the language file's you cannot draw 6 cards, so you lose this set, and mode 8 owning the largest sub-machine - but the mapping itself is an inference across two sources and is NOT established by the assembly. It must be confirmed before being used as ground truth.

F0x8008F530 (opcode 0x29, Anti-Power) calls F0x8008F2D8 with amount = -0x80 (-128) in $a2 and duration = 0x10 (16 ticks) in $a3, the latter placed in the branch delay slot of the `jal 0x8008f2d8` so it reaches that call, and then clears duel+0x438. The model document describes this opcode without stating a magnitude or a pacing, so these two values are new.
claims.limitations: The decompilation's own call `F0x8008f2d8(-0x80, 0x10)` omits the implicit first argument (arg0, the duel pointer) that the extern declaration and every other caller supply; this is a known m2c artifact for tail calls that reuse the caller's a0, not a claim that the call passes only two arguments.
claims.coverage: The magnitude and duration were read from original assembly by the lead, not from decompilation: F0x8008F530's complete body is 12 instructions (cardgame.s L12839-L12850, file offset 0xc880) and was read end to end, including the delay slot after the jal and the instruction after the `jr $ra`. Both immediates appear literally as `li $a2, -0x80` and `li $a3, 0x10`; no other write to $a2 or $a3 occurs between the function entry and the call, so the pair reaching F0x8008F2D8 is established rather than inferred. The assertion that the values are absent from the model document was checked by searching that document for the opcode's section and for the literals 0x80/0x10 in its vicinity.
