claims.statement: F0x8009F8C0, listed as 'mode 3, round setup, never opened', is eighteen lines. On its first call, recognised by the Battle-Phase state duel+0x2F9 being 0, it issues effect opcode 0xA7 by writing the pending-opcode latch duel+0x421, sets duel+0x2F4 to 1 to tell the interpreter an opcode is pending, advances duel+0x2F9 to 1 and returns 0 so the mode repeats. On every later call it sets duel+0x2F5 to 0 when the selection cursor duel+0x440 is zero and to 1 otherwise, and returns 1 to finish. Recorded as candidate because what opcode 0xA7 does, and what duel+0x2F5 is subsequently read for, are not established here.

F0x800A1A5C, listed as 'mode 9, round end, never opened', is the SET TRANSITION and it ties the best-of-three structure together in eleven statements. Taking the side-0 per-player block at duel+0x59C it calls F0x800A19F8 on that block, then F0x8009DA68, then invokes the duel's +0x810 method - the RAND_U16 pile shuffle - with the block's +0x04 and +0x08 as base and count, i.e. it RESHUFFLES for the coming set. It then zeroes duel+0x304 and duel+0x305 and all four stored AP and HP totals at duel+0x59C, +0x59E, +0x664 and +0x666, calls F0x8009EDCC, INCREMENTS the set counter duel+0x300, and finally calls F0x8009D9E4, which is the function that recomputes duel+0x41B and duel+0x41C from the new 2*duel[0x300]+2 threshold. So one function performs the whole set change: reshuffle, clear the totals, advance the set number, and widen the opponent's usable deck. This also renames a dispatch site: the shuffle call previously described as 'per-set setup' is this round-END reset, since 0x800A1A5C contains the call site at file offset 0x1EDE4.

Card-effect opcode 0x0F is a conditional backward branch whose condition is inline rather than in a callee, and it is the loop test of Darkness Gale. Its update block at 0x80084FD8 builds the CARDPAK record accessor through F0x8001EBF8, takes the opponent side's hand count from per-player block +0x5A6, and walks that hand: for each position it maps the instance at +0x600 through duel+0x50 to a card id, calls the accessor with that id plus one, and reads byte +0x00 of the catalogue record, which section E.1.a establishes as the card's colour. The first card whose colour is not 5, black, subtracts 4 from the effect-VM program counter duel+0x4E0 and completes; the store sits in a j delay slot and always executes. If every card in the hand is black, or the hand is empty, the opcode completes without touching the counter. The comparison value 5 is a hard-coded immediate and is not read from the colour register duel+0x306 that opcode 0x6E sets. In Darkness Gale, program 6E 39 4A 3E 0F, the minus four lands exactly on the opponent-hand colour filter at step 2, making steps 2 to 5 a loop that trashes the opponent's non-black cards one at a time until none remain, which is what that card's printed text says it does. This closes the last opcode of the 100 that the 60 shipped card programs use.
claims.coverage: Every instruction of the block from the accessor construction to both exits was read, including the taken-branch target and the fall-through, so both outcomes of the only conditional are accounted for. 'The only one of the 60 that contains 0x0F' was tested by enumerating all 60 effect programs in web/assets/data/card_effects.json and counting occurrences: one, Darkness Gale. 'This closes the last opcode' is the output of tools/decode_card_programs.py, which fails any opcode with no gloss and now reports 100 used, 0 unknown, 60 of 60 cards readable end to end.
limitations: That byte +0x00 of the catalogue record is the colour is taken from section E.1.a, not re-derived in this pass.
That the walked hand is the opponent's rests on section G.16's reading of the side register $s4; the register the block uses was read directly, its identity was not.
derivation: grep for the trash and deck fields in exe-decomp/cardgame_c/F0x8008fa9c.c

claims.statement: Card-effect opcode 0x11 exclusive-ors 1 into the acting-side byte at history[(duel+0x575)-1] + 0x584 and stores it back, so it flips which side the last play counts as and thereby makes the block that follows run for the other player. This supersedes section G.0's row for 0x11, which said it 'reads back the previous play-history entry'; the block performs no read-back and the row is wrong. In Tidal Wave, Summon Cancel and Eclipse Undo, 0x11 sits immediately before the repeat-counter opcode 0x06, so the repeat-twice runs the preceding block once for each side.
limitations: The dispatch block is quoted from the opcode registry, which is authority 2 by cross-read, rather than from cardgame.s directly.
claims.coverage: The three programs said to place 0x11 immediately before 0x06 were found by enumerating all 60 effect programs in web/assets/data/card_effects.json and matching the pair: Tidal Wave, Summon Cancel and Eclipse Undo, and no others. The supersession of section G.0's row was checked by reading the whole dispatch block for 0x11, which contains no load other than the one feeding the xori, so there is no read-back for the old row to have described.

claims.statement: F0x80092438, opcodes 0x12/0x13, branches on whether the view is idle: an idle view is treated as a cancelled play and clears the selection cursor duel+0x440, plays the most recent play-history entry's sound, and (for side 0 only) clears the 15-entry duel+0x46F..+0x4E-relative flag array, before setting a banner code in duel+0x499; a non-idle view instead re-arms the played card's move animation or positions an effect sprite from the coordinate table at 0x800A5910, depending on arg2.

Opcode 0x13's enter handler F0x80092438 raises the card the player just played into the centre of the board. On the path taken when nothing is showing yet it places view sprite slot 15 at (229, 97) through the view method at +0xF14, binds that slot to the card id read out of the play history, and grows it from nothing to full scale over 8 ticks through the scale method at +0xF24, which pins the destination to the card's own position so it zooms in place. On the path taken when a card is already showing it instead moves slot 15 through the method at +0xF08 over 10 ticks toward a destination read from the table based at 0x800A5910.
claims.coverage: The handler was read in full, from its prologue to the start of the next function, so the two paths described are the only two it has: the entry test on the view halfword at +0x64 branches to exactly one of them and both were followed to their returns. The durations 8 and 10 are the immediates the handler itself passes, read at the two call sites named in the evidence, not values inferred from a capture. NOT tested: what the +0x64 test means, and whether any caller other than opcode 0x13's dispatch arm reaches this handler - the claim is scoped to what the handler does, not to who calls it.
limitations: The update handler F0x8008AD98 is not covered by these claims. It was read far enough to see that it consumes duel+0x438, but its states are not anchored here.
Opcode 0x13's two paths are separated by a test on a view halfword at +0x64 whose meaning was not established; the claim describes the two paths by what each does, not by naming the condition.
No runtime observation. Everything here is static, from the overlay assembly at authority 2.
The three seats at 0x800A5910 are a fact about the shipped data. What bounds the index into that table was not read.

claims.statement: F0x80092ba4, opcode 0x14, zeroes both sides' hand counts (duel+0x5A6 and duel+0x66E), pushes the zeroed counts to the view, and clears the selection cursor duel+0x440 -- a hand-wipe step not currently named in the model's per-round rule list.

F0x8009403c, opcodes 0x19/0x1A, sums the true AP (duel+0x734-relative) and HP (+0x736-relative) of every field slot flagged in the side field-flag array (duel+0x446, §E.2) into duel+0x42C/+0x430 (each capped at 99), and when 4 or more slots are flagged adds a further +20 to both totals (capped again at 99) -- confirming §F.1 item 12's 'plus 20 to each at four copies' at the exact opcode level. It also looks up a combo banner/sound index by matching duel+0x438-1 against a table bounded by duel+0x244, which is a further, opcode-scoped reading of duel+0x438 distinct from the selection-bound (F0x80090cd8) and plain-accumulator readings already on record; it does not resolve whether the run is additionally replaced by catalog +0x0A's Digimon.

The unidentified resident structure at 0x8004b7d0 read by card-effect opcode 0x1b's update step 6 and opcode 0x9e's update step 4 is the SHARED PAD SERVICE already decoded for the menu system (ledger claim UI-PADSERVICE-STATIC-TABLE-001), and slot +0x3f4 is its 'return a port's button words' entry. Both card opcodes call it through a static function-pointer slot with a0 = 0, i.e. pad port 0. In both encodings the lui/addiu pair resolves unambiguously because the assembled word itself ends in b7d0 (0x2452b7d0 and 0x2453b7d0), so no borrow ambiguity remains. The consequence for the card model is that these are not silent presentation steps: both opcodes reach a point where the sequence reads the controller, which is the shape of a 'press a button to continue' beat inside an effect animation. This resolves the open limitation recorded in claims cardgame-opcode-0x1b-update-phase-is-an-eight-step-machine-at-0x8008363c and cardgame-opcode-0x9e-update-phase-is-a-five-step-machine-at-0x8008334c, which named the field but not its owner. Limitation: which button each step tests is NOT established - that needs the returned word compared against the logical-id mapping at pad-service slot +0x408, which was not read here.

Effect opcode 0x1B's update phase F0x80093CAC exchanges the stored battle totals BETWEEN THE TWO SIDES: side 0's AP at duel+0x59C with side 1's AP at duel+0x664, and side 0's HP at duel+0x59E with side 1's HP at duel+0x666. It does not exchange a side's own AP with its own HP. This is the operation Fortune Gate reaches: the card's whole program is 6F 2A, and 0x2A's only phase F0x8008F948 raises the reveal counter duel+0x305 and sets the face index duel+0x304 without touching any stat, after which Battle-Phase state 8 issues 0x1B once per count. This also identifies the opcode that issues F0x80093CAC, which the model document recorded as an open question.
claims.coverage: The four stores that make up the exchange were read as raw assembly at .L0x000111a8 through .L0x000111c0, not from decompiler output, and the load/store pairing was checked register by register to confirm both directions are written rather than one being overwritten. The claim is deliberately confined to the exchange itself; the fifteen-frame display ramp that precedes it was not re-derived.
limitations: Static reading only. The exchange has NOT been observed in the running game: the rig experiment was written and armed on 2026-08-24 and the emulator crashed before it produced a line.

Whether F0x80094848, which recomputes the totals from the field, also OVERWRITES the cached totals was not read. No recompute sits between Battle-Phase state 8 and the state 0xA comparison, so it cannot change the set decision, but a later phase is unverified.
The combo claim does not establish what the +0x14 four-copy bonus is called on screen, nor whether the announcement's face lookup can pick a wrong instance when duplicate card ids are present.

claims.statement: The switch-2 update half of card-effect opcode 0x1b is F0x80093cac, an EIGHT-step machine dispatched through a second jump table at 0x8008363c indexed by (duel+0x422 - 1)*4 and bounds-checked against 8. This is the second such table in the card overlay: like F0x8008d274's, m2c cannot resolve it, so exe-decomp/cardgame_c/F0x80093cac.c does not show the dispatch. The eight targets are 0x80093d08, 0x80093d38, 0x80093d58, 0x80093f08, 0x80093f48, 0x80093f64, 0x80093ff8 and 0x80094014, all inside the function. The skeleton: steps 1, 2 and 4 each wait for the view byte +0x656 to reach 1 (step 1 also issuing view method +0xf1c for sprite 0x11, the sprite the enter phase placed, and step 2 clearing duel+0x424); step 3 is a bounded tween that accumulates a per-frame delta into duel+0x424 and branches once it reaches 15; step 5 waits for a different view byte +0xdfa to reach 2; step 6 reads a field at +0x3f4 of the resident structure at 0x8004b7d0; step 7 waits for +0xdfa to fall back to 0; step 8 returns 1, completing the opcode. So opcode 0x1b is a multi-stage presentation sequence, not the single plate draw its enter phase alone suggested. Limitations: the bodies of steps 3 and 6 were not fully decoded - in particular the resident callee at [0x8004df9c] whose return value step 3 accumulates, and the meaning of the 0x8004b7d0 field - and view bytes +0x656 and +0xdfa are cited as gates but not named.

Opcode 0x5a (F0x80094828) and opcodes 0x1c/0x1d (F0x80094b78) are accumulator resets, not board operations: each sets the opcode step counter duel+0x422 to 1 and zeroes duel+0x424, +0x428, +0x42c, +0x430 and +0x434 - the pair at +0x428/+0x42c being the pending AP/HP stat-change amounts that F0x8008def8 writes. The only difference between the two is that F0x80094b78 additionally zeroes duel+0x438, the 'at least one match' flag, in its jr delay slot. Scope: enter phase only.

Opcode 0x29 (Anti-Power) enters through F0x8008f530(duel), a 2-statement handler that calls F0x8008f2d8(-0x80, 0x10) -- which itself only writes the two arguments into duel+0x434/+0x430 and arms duel+0x423=1 -- and then separately sets duel+0x438=0. The actual per-colour S-Energy zeroing described in §E.1.c/§G.0 is not performed by either of these two immediate handlers; it lives in the unread 102-line stateful sibling F0x8008f560. The §G.0 table's claim that opcodes 0x1E-0x28 also route through F0x8008f2d8 with the same 4-argument (duel,view,k,0x1E) signature is NOT confirmed by this pass: the F0x8008f2d8 body read here takes only (duel, arg2, arg3) and the census attributes it to opcode 0x23 alone.

Card-effect opcode 0x2A selects the previously played card for display. Its update block calls F0x8008F948, twelve instructions that read the play-history entry at index (duel+0x575) - 1 with stride 8, take that entry's card instance from +0x580, store that value plus one into duel+0x304, increment duel+0x305, and return 1. duel+0x304 is the field the presentation opcode 0x1B consumes as a face index with a minus one, so the plus one here and the minus one there cancel: 0x2A names the last played card and 0x1B draws it. Exactly one shipped card program uses 0x2A, Fortune Gate, whose whole program is a colour selection followed by this opcode. No prior claim in the ledger covers this opcode.
limitations: What duel+0x305 counts is not established; the handler only increments it and nothing read here consumes it.
The pairing with opcode 0x1B rests on section G.12's already-recorded reading of 0x1B, not on a fresh read of 0x1B in this pass.
claims.coverage: 'twelve instructions' and 'the whole handler' were checked by reading cardgame.s L13101-L13112 through the jr $ra and its delay slot. 'Exactly one shipped card program uses 0x2A' was tested by enumerating all 60 programs in web/assets/data/card_effects.json and counting occurrences of 0x2A: one, Fortune Gate. 'No prior claim covers this opcode' was tested by searching every claim record in docs/research/evidence/ledger.json for '8008f948' and for 'opcode 0x2A', which returned zero claims.
derivation: grep of docs/research/evidence/ledger.json for each residue opcode and handler address

claims.statement: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-09 by reading the switch-2 update half. The enter phase's decrement of the play-history index duel+0x575 is a temporary REWIND, not a retirement: the update callees F0x80095208 / F0x800952f4 reload duel+0x575, add 1, and store it back, so the net change across the opcode is ZERO. Only the word 'retiring' is wrong; the guard on the previous entry's +0x584, the unconditional 0x2d/0x2e variants, the +0xec4 / +0xec8 split and the +0x499 / +0x49d flags all still hold and are restated in the superseding claim.

Read across BOTH phases, card-effect opcodes 0x2b/0x2d and 0x2c/0x2e do not retire a play. The enter phase (F0x8009518c / F0x80095274) decrements the play-history index duel+0x575 and makes a view call; the switch-2 update callee (F0x80095208 / F0x800952f4) waits on view+0x64 and duel+0x498, then reloads duel+0x575, adds 1, and stores it back - exactly undoing the decrement, with the store in a jump delay slot so it executes. The NET change to the play-history index across the whole opcode is ZERO. The decrement is a temporary rewind that makes the previous play the current one for the duration of the view call, not a pop. This supersedes claim cardgame-opcode-0x2b-0x2e-retire-the-last-play-history-entry, which read the enter phase alone and therefore described the rewind as retiring an entry. Everything else in that claim - the side-0 guard on the previous entry's +0x584, the third argument being the unconditional override that separates 0x2d/0x2e from 0x2b/0x2c, the +0xec4 versus +0xec8 split, and the +0x499/+0x49d flags - is unchanged and still holds. Limitation: what view methods +0xec4 and +0xec8 draw during the rewind is still not decoded, so the purpose of making the previous play current is described mechanically only.

Three more opcode bodies, all enter phase, read from original assembly. Opcodes 0x2f/0x30 (F0x80094fdc) clear the wait timer duel+0x424, call view method +0xee4 with the opcode-selected id (0x39 for 0x2f, 0x35 for 0x30) plus the constants 0, 0, 1, and set duel+0x422 = 1; they touch no other duel state, so they are presentation-only. Opcode 0x9e (F0x80088f0c) calls view +0xecc, clears duel+0x440 (the draw-result code), calls view +0xec8, and raises duel+0x49d, +0x49c and +0x499 together - +0x49c being set by this opcode alone among those decoded so far. Opcode 0x1b (F0x80093c18) places view sprite id 0x11 at the fixed screen position (0x8300, 0x6100), sets its face index from duel+0x304 minus 1 - the Battle-Phase state-8 counter, NOT an opcode immediate - clears view+0x62c, scales it via view +0xf24 with (0x0a, 0x1000, 0x1000), and sets duel+0x422 = 1.

F0x8008f978(duel, view, side, mode) is the enter-phase handler for opcodes 0x3E and 0x40 (the census lists both; the complete-model document's §G.0 names only 0x40 for this function). For mode 0 it reads the given side's hand slot at the current selection index (duel+0x440); for mode 1 it instead reads that side's draw-pile slot at the same index. Either way the fetched card id is written into duel+0x438 and shown as a banner icon; no card is moved by this handler.

Opcode 0x41 is the PAIRED RESPONSE resolution, and reading its update phase closes a previously open link. Its enter phase F0x8008F750 notifies the view about the played-card stack entry TWO below the top rather than the top one. Its update phase polls F0x8008F790 and, on success, sets duel+0x4DD before completing - and duel+0x4DD is exactly the flag that makes F0x800A2180 case 12 pop TWO entries off the played-card stack instead of one, sending both to the discard together. The limitation recorded against cardgame-played-card-stack-pops-one-or-two-to-the-discard, that nothing was traced which SETS that flag, is therefore resolved: opcode 0x41 sets it. The two facts corroborate each other - an opcode that addresses the entry two below the top is exactly the one that would want the top two entries retired as a pair, which is the shape of a card and the card played in response to it resolving together.

Opcodes 0x42/0x43 enter through F0x8008ff08(duel, view, side, mode), which appends a card instance to the given side's hand array (duel+0x600, at the current hand-count position) and increments that side's hand count (duel+0x5A6) by one. The source of the appended card is the trash array (+0x614) at the current selection index (duel+0x440) when mode==4, and the draw pile (+0x5B0) at that same index otherwise. This is the concrete card-movement step behind the 'draw paths' label in §G.0.

The opcode 0x42/0x43 ('the draw paths') update-phase handler F0x80090058 performs the actual draw: it decrements the acting side's per-player-block deck count (block+0x5A4), advances the deck-read cursor (block+0x5A0), increments the hand count (block+0x5A6) and copies the drawn instance into the hand array (block+0x600), then pushes the post-draw deck/hand/trash counts of both sides to the view, transitioning to a 'more to draw' or 'draw finished, arm timer' state depending on whether the resulting hand count is below 6.

The opcode 0x44 enter-phase handler F0x8009076c resets the draw-animation scratch words duel+0x424/+0x434 to 0 and seeds duel+0x428 from the acting side's per-player-block trash count and duel+0x42C from its deck count, before handing control to the stateful counter F0x800907AC already decoded in the model's §G.4.

F0x80090a6c, reached by opcodes 0x45 and 0x47, clears a 40-byte run at duel+0x46F..+0x496 (confirmed in original assembly: a byte-store loop over addresses (duel+i)+0x46f for i=0x27..0) and then writes the selection quota duel+0x444 = the opcode's own immediate operand (2 for 0x45, 6 for 0x47) and clears the clamp flag duel+0x445. The 40-byte clear width extends past the previously-documented 12-byte selection-flag array at +0x46F into currently-undocumented bytes +0x47B..+0x496.

F0x80090a90, also reached by opcode 0x47, fills the duel+0x46F selection-flag array according to the quota just written by F0x80090a6c: for arg2==0 it flags up to `quota` consecutive own-side slots starting at the deck-read cursor duel+0x5A0 (clamping and writing back the actual count/clamp-flag into duel+0x444/+0x445 if it runs out of room at slot 0x28); for arg2!=0 it instead flags opponent-side deck slots, clamped to the opponent's deck count (duel+0x66C), splitting the flag writes between low indices (opponent deck-cursor slots matching the acting side's chosen colour class, duel+0x300) and high indices counting down from 0x27 for the rest.

F0x80090ba0, the enter-phase handler for opcode 0x48, delivers the cards F0x80090a90 flagged: it scans duel+0x46F for the acting side across deck-cursor positions 0..0x27 and, for each flagged position, copies that card from the side's draw pile (block+0x5B0) into the next open hand slot (block+0x600) and increments the per-player-block hand count (block+0x5A6). It records the pre-move hand count in duel+0x438, sets a move-occurred flag in duel+0x42C, and selects one of four banner codes into duel+0x499 depending on side and whether anything moved.

Opcode 0x48's update phase, F0x80090CD8, is a ten-step windowed prompt rather than a board mutation. It is keyed on the effect interpreter's step byte duel+0x422, biased by one and bounded unsigned against 10, and dispatches through the table at 0x80083554. Among its steps are a wait for the view's window state at +0xDFA to reach 2, a read of the pad service's pressed-this-frame word at service slot +0x3F4, a wait for that window state to return to zero, and a push of the side's deck count from per-player block +0x5A4 to the view; the last step sets the return value to 1, which is how an update-phase handler reports the opcode complete. It reads the same pile selector duel+0x438 the pile prompts use.
claims.coverage: The step count is the machine's own unsigned bound, read as an instruction rather than counted from a decompiled switch - which is necessary here because the decompiler fails on this jump and emits no body. The steps named are the ones read; the claim says 'among its steps' and does not describe all ten. The input clause distinguishes the pressed word from the repeat word by the service slot the step reads, which is the same distinction already established for this overlay's pickers.
limitations: Four of the ten steps were not read in this pass; what the prompt shows and what it does with the answer are not established.
Which value duel+0x438 holds when this opcode runs was not traced.
Static reading only; not observed in the running game.

claims.statement: F0x80090cd8, the assembly-only update-phase counterpart of opcode 0x48 (m2c cannot lift its jr $v0 jump table), reads duel+0x438 and bounds-checks it against the acting side's hand count at block+0x5A6 in its state-2 body, independently corroborating (from a different opcode family than F0x8008CB5C in §G.4) that duel+0x438 carries a per-opcode selection-count-bound meaning rather than being pure shared scratch.

Opcode 0x49's enter-phase handler F0x8008f0b4(duel, side) arms the interpreter and stages a (current, target) counter pair for a side's hand size (into duel+0x428, from that side's block+0x5A6) and trash size (into duel+0x42C, from block+0x5A2), with duel+0x430 reset to 0. This pass did not read the stateful sibling F0x8008f0f4 that consumes these fields, so what UI element they drive is not established beyond 'a hand/trash counter widget'.

Card-effect opcode 0x4A makes the first marked card in a hand the current selection. Its update phase is inline at 0x80085694 with no callee: it takes the acting side's hand count from per-player block +0x5A6, and when that count is above zero it walks the shared selection array duel+0x446 from index zero, branching out on the first non-zero entry to store that index into the selection cursor duel+0x440. That store occupies the delay slot of the jump to the completion tail and therefore always executes. A hand with nothing marked, and an empty hand, both complete the opcode without changing the cursor. One shipped card uses 0x4A, Darkness Gale, where it follows the opponent-hand colour filter 0x39. With this opcode read, every one of the 100 opcodes the 60 shipped card programs use has an established meaning.
claims.coverage: 'One shipped card uses 0x4A' was tested by enumerating all 60 effect programs in web/assets/data/card_effects.json and counting occurrences: one, Darkness Gale. 'Every one of the 100 opcodes now has an established meaning' is the output of tools/decode_card_programs.py, which fails any opcode with no gloss; it reports 100 used, 0 unknown, 60 of 60 cards readable end to end.
limitations: What marks duel+0x446 for a HAND, as opposed to the twelve field slots, is not established here. Section G.7 already records that duel+0x46F is a shared array reindexed by each reader; duel+0x446 appears to be used the same way, and this claim does not settle it.

claims.statement: Card-effect opcode 0x4B chooses which position the following card reveal reads from. It has no enter phase; its update block calls F0x800840D0 with the acting-side register as third argument, and that handler is four instructions: when the argument is zero it loads the halfword deck read cursor at per-player-block +0x5A0 into duel+0x440, and otherwise it loads the byte deck-window index at duel+0x41C into the same field. Both stores occupy a jr $ra delay slot and so always execute. duel+0x440 is the index opcode 0x40 then uses to fetch the card it displays. In the shipped card programs 0x4B occurs exactly twice, in Security Hall and Illegal Access, and in both it is immediately followed by 0x40. No prior claim in the ledger covers this opcode.
limitations: Which of the two sources the argument actually selects in play is not established: the third argument is the side register $s4, so the reading 'side 0 uses the deck read cursor and side 1 uses the on-screen deck window index' follows from the register's identity in section G.16 rather than from a traced call. The distinction matters only if the two indices can differ.
The claim does not establish what duel+0x41C is set from.
claims.coverage: 'both stores occupy a delay slot' was checked by reading all four instructions of F0x800840D0 at cardgame.s L1295-L1302; the handler contains no other store. 'exactly twice, and in both immediately followed by 0x40' was tested by enumerating all 60 effect programs in web/assets/data/card_effects.json and listing every occurrence of 0x4B: two, in Security Hall and Illegal Access, each followed by 0x40. 'No prior claim covers this opcode' was tested by searching every claim record in docs/research/evidence/ledger.json for '800840d0' and for 'opcode 0x4B', which returned zero claims.
derivation: grep of docs/research/evidence/ledger.json for each residue opcode and handler address

claims.statement: Opcode 0x4C's enter-phase handler F0x8008e5b0 performs no board read or write beyond arming the interpreter (duel+0x422=1); all of the opcode's actual effect must be in the stateful sibling F0x8008e5bc, whose body is separately described (with a full step breakdown) in another packet already recorded against this same epoch (claim id cardgame-f8008e5bc-runs-as-opcode-0x4c-with-a-full-step-breakdown).

The limitation recorded on cardgame-f8008e5bc-compacts-the-field-and-builds-a-move-list - that the consumer of the move list at 0x800A5DA8 and of the counters at 0x800A5DC0 and 0x800A5DC2 had not been traced - is closed, and the consumer is a later step of the same function. F0x8008E5BC step 1 exits directly to step 4 when both 0x800A5DC2 counters are zero, so an opcode 0x4C that finds nothing marked completes with no delay and no drawing; otherwise it sets step 2 with duel+0x424 = 0x14, which step 2 counts down by the resident frame delta getter at 0x8004DF9C. Step 3 then walks 0x800A5DC0[side] recorded index pairs, swaps the two field-slot records and the two view blocks for each, subtracts 0x800A5DC2[side] from that side's live slot count at duel+0x72C, and clears the view of every trailing slot up to six. Opcode 0x4C's enter handler F0x8008E5B0 is two instructions that only arm step 1. Across the 60 shipped card programs 0x4C appears in 22 of them and its preceding opcode is always 0x4D or 0x4E, the destroy and return-to-hand pair, except for one further occurrence following 0x57. In player terms: when Digimon leave the board the survivors slide forward to close the gaps over about twenty ticks, and when nothing left the board there is no pause.
claims.coverage: The 'always 0x4D or 0x4E' clause was tested by enumerating every one of the 60 effect programs in web/assets/data/card_effects.json and inspecting the opcode preceding each of the 23 occurrences of 0x4C; 22 follow 0x4D or 0x4E and the twenty-third, in Control Parts, follows 0x57. No occurrence was excluded.
limitations: The step 2 and step 3 bodies are quoted from exe-decomp/cardgame_c/F0x8008e5bc.c at authority 3, not from the overlay assembly. Only the enter handler and the program enumeration are at authority 2 or better. Promotion beyond partially_verified needs the step 3 record swap and the duel+0x72C subtraction quoted from cardgame.s.
The 0x14 figure is a tick count in the units the resident frame-delta getter returns; it has not been converted to a time and has not been observed in the running game.
derivation: grep of docs/research/evidence/ledger.json for each residue opcode and handler address

claims.statement: Card-effect opcodes 0x4D and 0x4E are a destroy/return pair that share one stateful handler, F0x800915D4, distinguished only by its third argument: the interpreter F0x80084320 calls it with a2=0 for 0x4D (move $a2,$zr at 0x8008572c) and a2=1 for 0x4E (li $a2,0x1 at 0x8008574c). F0x800915D4 sweeps the twelve field-slot flag bytes at duel+0x46F starting from duel+0x428, and for each flagged slot i sets duel+0x42C = (i < 6 ? 0 : 1) as the side and duel+0x430 = i or i-6 as the slot within that side, then applies one per-slot routine (F0x8008DAF4 for 0x4D, F0x8008DD38 for 0x4E) until it returns non-zero, advancing duel+0x428 past the slot. Both per-slot routines compute the slot base as duel + side*0x72 + slot*0xE, read the owner byte at field-slot +0x0C (lbu 0x738 at 0x8008da5c) and the card-id halfword at field-slot +0x02 (lhu 0x72e at 0x8008da88), and append that id to one of the owning side's piles in the per-player block at duel + 0x59C + side*0xC8, incrementing its count. They differ only in destination: 0x4D writes block+0x78 (duel+0x614 / duel+0x6DC, count block+0x06) and reports zone code 7, while 0x4E writes block+0x64 (duel+0x600 / duel+0x6C8, count block+0x0A) and reports zone code 6. Since block+0x64 is the ten-entry hand, 0x4D destroys the flagged field cards to their owner's discard pile and 0x4E returns them to their owner's hand.

F0x80091858, opcodes 0x4F..0x55, appends a new occupied-field-slot record for card instance arg3 to side arg2's field array at duel+0x72C+side*0x72: it writes the card-instance field, zeroes the AP/HP target fields, fills the displayed AP/HP fields from a catalog lookup via F0x8001ebf8, and stamps a side echo and a monotonically increasing sequence counter (duel+0x308) into slot bytes not previously documented in §E.4's field-slot layout, before driving the new slot's sprite through view calls and the shared helper F0x8009170c.

Card-effect opcodes 0x4f..0x55 share the handler F0x80091858 and each places one card into the acting side's next free field slot. The seven interpreter call sites at RAM 0x80084744..0x800847ec pass the consecutive immediates 0x50..0x56 in their jal delay slots. Those immediates are INDICES into the card instance table at duel+0x50, NOT card ids: the handler loads the halfword at duel+0x50+arg*2, adds 1, and fetches that CARDPAK record. Since the opponent's and player's 40-card folders occupy instances 0x00..0x4f, indices 0x50..0x56 are seven instance slots reserved ABOVE both folders - i.e. cards an effect can put on the board that were never in either deck. Which card ids those seven instance slots hold, and who writes them, is NOT established here; reading them as card ids 0x50..0x56 would be an error. Scope: this is the enter phase only, and the handler notably does NOT increment the side's occupied-slot count byte at duel+0x72c/+0x79e, so the count is advanced elsewhere - in the callee F0x8009170c or in the switch-2 update case, neither of which was read.

F0x800919fc, opcode 0x56, removes one occupied field-slot record for side arg2, chosen by matching the most recent play-history entry's target class byte against each slot's class/colour byte, then shifts later slot records down by one and decrements the side's slot-count byte at duel+arg2*0x72+0x72C, before pushing the new count to the view and handing control to the shared helper F0x8009170c.

F0x80091eb0, opcode 0x57, locates the last of the 12 field slots flagged in duel+0x46F, copies that slot's full sprite animation state onto the acting side's own target slot sprite and its class byte into the target's priority field, and propagates a highlighted-sprite flag from the source slot to matching play-history-indexed sprites on the target slot. The exact role of this copy (a combo consolidation step, a card-replacement step, or something else) relative to the model's open combo-semantics question was not resolved here.

Opcodes 0x58/0x59 enter through F0x8008ddc0(duel, view, arg2), which walks all twelve field slots, and for every slot that is both occupied (within its side's field count) and currently flagged in the shared selection array duel+0x46F, triggers a per-slot view flash (view->unkF38) and, if any such slot exists, plays SFX 0x9C0001 or 0x9C0000 depending on arg2; it always resets the roll timer duel+0x424. The paired update-phase poll F0x8008deac accumulates the resident per-frame delta (0x8004DF9C) into duel+0x424 and reports 'not yet elapsed' while the total stays below its argument, i.e. it is a plain wait gate, consistent with §G.0's fixed 0x24/0x1C-tick durations for these two opcodes.

Card-effect opcode 0x5a is the board-total opcode, and its two phases fit together: the enter phase F0x80094828 zeroes duel+0x424, +0x428, +0x42c, +0x430 and +0x434, and the switch-2 update callee F0x80094848 then walks every occupied field slot on both sides - bounded by the count bytes at duel+0x72c and duel+0x79e - adding each slot's halfword at +0x08 into duel+0x428 and each slot's halfword at +0x0a into duel+0x42c. Per the placement constructor those two fields are the slot's BASE AP and BASE HP copied from CARDPAK +0x01/+0x02, so 0x5a leaves the total base AP of the board in duel+0x428 and the total base HP in duel+0x42c. NOTE the quantifier: it sums the BASE stats at +0x08 and +0x0a, NOT the running modifiers at +0x04 and +0x06, so buffs and damage accumulated during the set are not included in what this opcode totals. Limitations: F0x80094848 is a four-step machine and only step 1, the accumulation, was read instruction by instruction; steps 3 and 4 were not. Whether this total is the one the set-winner rule consumes is NOT established here - that link is plausible given the documented 'set goes to the higher total HP' rule but was not traced.

F0x8009535c, the update-phase function chained from opcode 0x5D, walks every occupied field slot on both sides once per frame, steps each slot's SPRITE-displayed AP/HP fields by +/-1 toward the duel's stored true AP/HP for that slot, and -- whenever a slot's true HP has reached exactly 0 during the walk -- flags that field-slot index in duel+0x46F and sets duel+0x438=1. This is a second, concrete source (besides the consumer F0x800915D4 already decoded in §G.4) for what sets the +0x46F removal flags during play, partially answering the model's open item about per-slot damage distribution: the zero-HP flag is set here, in the per-frame stat-roll handler, not in the earlier stat-change opcode itself (F0x8008DEF8/§G.3).

The target-kind selector opcodes 0x70-0x82 share one enter-phase handler, F0x8008ca4c(duel, view, mask), which resets and re-opens the view's target-selection UI for the given mask, zeroes duel+0x440, arms the interpreter (duel+0x422=1), stores the raw mask into duel+0x438, shows a banner with the just-played card's id, and clears the shared selection-flag range duel+0x46F..+0x47D (15 bytes) before setting duel+0x499=1. duel+0x438 here holds the target mask, a different meaning from the same offset's use elsewhere in this registry (see the 0x83/0x84 and 0x8D/0xAE claims) and from its documented 'combo result card id' role -- it is a shared scratch field with several unrelated per-opcode meanings, not a single semantic field.

Opcodes 0x83/0x84 ('the card just played') enter through F0x8008ce0c(duel, view, arg2), which performs the same UI reset/arm/flag-clear sequence as the 0x70-0x82 family (F0x8008ca4c) but additionally clears a second 15-byte flag run at duel+0x49E..+0x4AC, and, only on a follow-up play (duel+0x575 != 0) with arg2==1, looks up the just-played card's CARDPAK kind byte through the resident getter F0x8001EBF8 and, if it equals 6, flags a specific view slot ((playCount+0xB)th) and sets duel+0x438=1 as a boolean special-target marker -- a third distinct meaning for duel+0x438 within this registry.

Opcodes 0x8D/0xAE (the combo/summon sprite step, per §G.0) enter through F0x8008ad48(duel, arg2), a 2-statement handler that only writes the immediate arg2 into duel+0x438 (yet another distinct meaning of that offset within this registry) and arms the interpreter (duel+0x423=1). The real sprite-stepping work is in the unread 400-line stateful sibling F0x8008ad98.

Card-effect opcodes 0x8e..0x95 share one handler body, F0x8008d274, whose enter phase is a single sweep over all twelve field slots (loop bound 0xc, per-slot stride 0x0e, per-side stride 0x72) that MARKS the slots an effect will act on by storing 1 into the per-slot selection array at duel+0x46f, clearing duel+0x49e for that slot, and setting the 'at least one match' flag duel+0x438 to 1. A slot is only considered when its index is below its own side's live slot count (duel+0x72c for indices 0..5, duel+0x79e for 6..11). The opcode selects the test through a jump table of eight words at 0x800834fc indexed by (arg3-1)*4 - the table m2c could not resolve, which is why exe-decomp/cardgame_c/F0x8008d274.c is a decompilation failure. The eight tests are: 0x8e marks the acting side's own six slots and 0x8f the opposing six (both decided by comparing the slot index against 6 and the side argument saved at 0x50($sp)); 0x90 marks every live slot unconditionally; and 0x91/0x92/0x93/0x94/0x95 test the slot's card colour, obtained through view method +0xf40. The colour tests are NOT uniform in polarity: 0x91, 0x92 and 0x94 use a beq-skip and therefore mark every colour EXCEPT white(1), blue(2) and red(4) respectively, while 0x93 and 0x95 reach a shared bne test and mark ONLY green(3) and ONLY brown(6). Colour 5 (black) is not tested by any of the eight. This reading is corroborated with zero mismatches across all eight kinds by the independently extracted pre-flight targeting gate in web/assets/data/card_effects.json, which is derived from a different function (F0x800a36e4) and assigns the same side and colour sets. Scope: this states the ENTER phase only; the correspondingly numbered case of switch 2 that completes each opcode was not read.

SUPERSEDED 2026-08-09 by reading F0x8008d594's step 2. The mark-then-highlight protocol and the poll-until-non-minus-one shape stated here are correct, but the RETURN VALUE was wrong: F0x8008d594 returns the constant 1 on confirm, not a chosen field-slot index, so duel+0x57a receives a confirmation and the identity of the affected slots never passes through it. The affected slots stay in the per-slot marking array duel+0x46f, and the effect applies to ALL marked slots rather than to one picked one.

Opcode 0x97 enters through F0x8008bc6c, a zero-argument passthrough to F0x8008baa4(0). F0x8008baa4(duel, view, side, kind) is the real enter-phase handler shared by opcodes 0x97 (via the passthrough), 0xA9, 0xAB, 0xAC and 0xAD: for kind==1 it sorts that side's draw pile by card id through the duel's own +0x814 method (sortCardArrayByCardId, already documented in §C), records the pile's card count into duel+0x434 as a selection limit and a message code into duel+0x438; for kind 0 or 3 it instead uses that side's hand count or trash count with different message codes and no sort. It then initialises the selection/highlight flags (+0x46F, +0x49E) for up to duel+0x434 of the relevant 40-entry array based on each entry's own +0x446 flag, arms the interpreter (+0x423=1), and resets the pending selection result (duel+0x440=-1).

Effect opcode 0x98's update phase calls the two-option prompt F0x8008642C and writes the answer into duel+0x57A. Of the three branches out of that call, a return of 1 jumps to 0x80085DC4 with `sb $v1, 0x57a($s1)` in the jump's delay slot (storing 1, the value the immediately preceding `beq` established), a return of 2 jumps to the SAME address 0x80085DC4 with `sb $zr, 0x57a($s1)` in its delay slot (storing 0), and a return below 2 -- i.e. 0 -- takes the still-waiting path to .L0x00003118 without writing 0x57A. The two answering outcomes are therefore indistinguishable by jump target and are separated only by their delay slots, which on MIPS execute even when the branch is taken. Read together with cardgame-f8008642c-is-the-two-option-prompt, which establishes that the prompt returns 1 with the cursor on answer 0 and that cancel forces the cursor to 1, duel+0x57A holds 1 when the player accepted and 0 when they declined or cancelled.
claims.coverage: The quantifier 'of the three branches' was tested by enumerating every control-transfer instruction between the `jal 0x8008642c` at file offset 0x2DA8 and the block's return, reading cardgame.s L2928-L2943 contiguously rather than sampling: the `beq` at 0x2DB4, the `bnez` at 0x2DBC and the `beq` at 0x2DC4 are the only three, and each target was opened together with the instruction in its delay slot. A fourth path would have appeared in that contiguous range. NOT covered: what any later opcode reads back out of 0x57A, and the enter phase's duel+0x438 message code, which remains open.
limitations: Establishes where the answer is stored, not what any subsequent opcode does with it.

Opcode 0x98's enter phase F0x80086330 sets duel+0x438 to 3 or 2 depending on hand usability (claim cardgame-opcode-0x98-hand-usability-gate, status candidate); which code pairs with which outcome is NOT established here and was not read.
duel+0x57A is written by opcode 0x99's update as well (cardgame.s L2955, `sb $v1, 0x57a($s1)`), so it is a shared last-answer register rather than a yes/no flag specific to 0x98.
The pairing of prompt return value to on-screen answer rests on the existing claim cardgame-f8008642c-is-the-two-option-prompt, which is partially_verified, not on this read.

claims.statement: Effect opcode 0x98's enter-phase handler F0x80086330 scans every card in the player's hand (duel+0x600, count duel+0x5A6) against the summon-usability gate F0x80085FD0 using the fixed side-0 S-Energy array duel+0x5A8, and sets duel+0x440 to 1 if any hand card is usable (0 otherwise) and duel+0x438 to a corresponding message code (3 or 2). This handler's energy-array argument is literally the constant duel+0x5A8 in the code read this pass, not a side-selected offset; whether this opcode is only ever issued for side 0 in the shipped programs, or the same code is reused with a different effective base elsewhere, is not established here.

claims.notes: CONDITION CORRECTED 2026-08-24 by re-reading exe-decomp/cardgame_c/F0x80086d78.c end to end. The statement previously said the routine 'opens a banner (message 5 if the hand is empty, else 0xB)'. The branch is not on the hand count: it is 'if (arg2->unk11 == 0)', and block+0x11 is the SIDE INDEX -- the same field the summoning claim reads as 'the side index at block +0x11'. Side 0 writes 5 to duel+0x499 and calls view->unkEC0(view, side); side 1 writes 0xB and makes no such call. The hand count arg2->unkA gates only the outer highlight loop, and its else-arm merely clears duel+0x49E. Neither 5 nor 0xB is an escardgm index -- escardgm 5 is 'Load Phase' and 0xB is 'Battle Phase' -- so duel+0x499 is a view-mode byte, not a message id; F0x8008642C writes 1 and 2 to the same field. The per-card legality half of the claim is unchanged and was confirmed by the same read.
claims.statement: Opcodes 0x99/0x9A enter through F0x80086d78(duel, view, block), where block is a per-player-block pointer (§E.3). For each of up to 40 hand entries within the block's hand count it re-checks summon usability through the same gate F0x80085FD0(duel, block+0xC, instance) used by opcode 0x98 (block+0xC being that side's S-Energy array), sets duel+0x446=1 and clears the highlight-disable flag duel+0x49E for usable cards (or the reverse for unusable ones), clears duel+0x46F for every entry, then sets the view-mode byte duel+0x499 from the ACTING SIDE -- block+0x11, the side index -- writing 5 and calling view->unkEC0(view, side) for side 0 and 0xB with no such call for side 1, arms the interpreter (+0x423=1), clears the cursor duel+0x43C and resets duel+0x440=-1. This is the presentation-side counterpart to opcode 0x98's yes/no scan: it computes per-card legality rather than a single overall flag.

Opcodes 0x9B/0x9C enter through F0x80086eb0(duel, count, bannerCode). When count>0 it clears the highlight-disable flag duel+0x49E across a 40-entry run (duel+0x49E..+0x4C5); otherwise it clears only the single entry duel+0x49E. It then calls helper F0x80086A18(duel) (not read this pass), arms the interpreter (+0x423=1), writes bannerCode into duel+0x499, and resets duel+0x43C=0 and duel+0x440=-1. Matching §G.0's call description (handCount/trashCount, banner 5/9), count is presumably the hand or trash size of the relevant side and bannerCode selects which of two banners to show, but the caller-side argument values were not traced this pass.

The switch-2 update half of card-effect opcode 0x9e is F0x80088f78, a FIVE-step machine dispatched through a jump table at 0x8008334c indexed by (duel+0x422 - 1)*4 and bounds-checked against 5. This is the THIRD such table found in pro/cardgame (after F0x8008d274's at 0x800834fc and F0x80093cac's at 0x8008363c) that m2c does not resolve. The five targets are 0x80088fd8, 0x80089080, 0x80089150, 0x800893e0 and 0x8008949c. Step 1 waits for view+0x64 == 2 with duel+0x498 == 0. Step 2 is a paced reveal of side 1's field slots: while duel+0x434 holds at least 6 it compares the cursor duel+0x428 against side 1's occupied count at duel+0x79e, calls view method +0xf28 with the cursor offset by 6 (the global 0..11 slot index), advances the cursor by 1 and spends 6 from +0x434 - one slot every six ticks - then compares duel+0x42c against duel+0x424 and, on passing, moves to step 3 and zeroes +0x424, +0x428, +0x42c and +0x430. Step 3 performs a signed division of the halfword at duel+0x59c (the first field of the per-player block) by 15, using the standard magic constant 0x88888889. Step 4 calls through +0x3f4 of the resident structure at 0x8004b7d0. Step 5 waits for view+0x64 to return to 0 with duel+0x498 == 0. IMPORTANT ANTI-TRAP, and the reason this claim is worth recording separately: inside opcode 0x9e, duel+0x428 is a SLOT CURSOR and duel+0x434 is a TICK BUDGET. They are NOT the board AP total and accumulator that opcode 0x5a leaves in +0x428/+0x42c. Any reading that carries a meaning for these fields across opcodes is wrong; the existing claim that +0x428 is reused per opcode is confirmed again here. Limitations: what step 3's divide-by-15 result is used for was not traced, the resident field at 0x8004b7d0+0x3f4 is unidentified, and view methods +0xf28 and byte +0x64 are cited by offset only.

Card-effect opcode 0xA7 is the Start Phase first-turn draw (the 'Draw Calumon to go first.' ceremony), and it is a random source independent of the pile shuffle. Its immediate handler F0x8008985C loads the RNG through the pointer at 0x8004DC0C, keeps the low bit (andi $s0,$v0,0x1 at 0x80089890) and stores it to duel+0x434 (0x80089894). Its stateful handler F0x80089974 then runs a six-step machine counted by duel+0x422: step 2 latches the cursor duel+0x43C into duel+0x440 as the player's pick (0x80089c20) and sets that slot's flag byte at duel+0x46F (0x80089c28); step 4 compares duel+0x434 with duel+0x440 and selects escardgm message 0x43 'You go first.' when they DIFFER and 0x44 'Opponent goes first.' when they MATCH -- the bne at 0x80089cc4 carries li $a3,0x43 in its delay slot, so only the fallthrough reaches li $a3,0x44; step 6 rewrites duel+0x440 to 1 on a match (0x80089e88) and 0 otherwise (0x80089e8c). duel+0x440 = 1 therefore means the OPPONENT takes the first turn. This closes the '[?] what opcode 0xA7 does' left open at docs/research/card/card-battle-complete-model-2026-08-06.md L255.

Effect opcode 0xA7's enter-phase handler F0x8008985c (below 0x80090000) calls the resident RNG at 0x8004DC0C, masks it with 1, and stores the 0/1 result into duel+0x434; it uses that outcome only to choose which of two on-screen text boxes (view index 0 or 1) shows string id 0x57, with the other box always showing 0x58, then clears several scratch fields and arms the interpreter. This resolves the open question in the complete-model document's §D.6 ('[?] what opcode 0xA7 does') and establishes that the card duel uses RNG at round start (mode 3) in addition to the pile-shuffle RNG documented in §A.5. What duel+0x434 subsequently gates, and what strings 0x57/0x58 read as, is not traced by this pass.

Opcode 0xA8's enter-phase handler F0x80089ec8 performs no board read or write beyond arming the interpreter (duel+0x423=1); the opcode's actual behaviour is in the unread 366-line stateful sibling F0x8008a068.

The eleven S-Energy opcodes 0x1e..0x28 split their meaning across the two phases, and the UPDATE half is where the colour and the target side are decided. All eleven share the update handler at 0x800852b4, which polls F0x8008423c and completes when it returns non-zero. F0x8008423c reads the LATCHED opcode at duel+0x420, subtracts 0x1e, bounds-checks against 0xb and dispatches through a jump table at 0x80082cc8 - a fifth m2c-unresolvable table in this overlay and the lowest-addressed one found so far - whose eleven entries select a colour index 0..4. It then picks the target side: for opcodes 0x1e..0x23 the acting side taken from the previous play-history entry's +0x584, and for 0x24..0x28 that same byte XORed with 1, i.e. the OPPONENT. Both paths tail-call F0x8008f2ec with the side in a2 and the colour index in a3. The resulting per-opcode map, colour index then side: 0x1e (0, self), 0x1f (1, self), 0x20 (2, self), 0x21 (2, self), 0x22 (3, self), 0x23 (4, self), 0x24 (0, opponent), 0x25 (1, opponent), 0x26 (2, opponent), 0x27 (3, opponent), 0x28 (4, opponent). Note 0x20 and 0x21 share colour index 2 and differ only in the amount their enter phase sets, which section G.3.a already gives as +1 and +2 respectively; combined with that section's amounts the family reads as five single-colour gains to your own pool, one double gain, and five losses inflicted on the opponent's pool. Limitations: colour index 0..4 is stated as an INDEX. Mapping it onto the named colours white, blue, green, red, black would follow the catalogue's 1..6 colour order shifted by one, but that correspondence was NOT confirmed - F0x8008f2ec, which consumes the index, was not read. Nor is it established here that F0x8008f2ec is where the pool is actually changed rather than merely animated; the enter-phase call F0x8008f2d8 already carries the amount, and which of the two commits the change was not traced.

Opcodes 0x2F, 0x30 and 0x31 put a sentence on screen and wait. Their three enter dispatch arms are consecutive and identical apart from one immediate, all calling F0x80094FDC, and that immediate is a MESSAGE ID rather than an effect index: the routine forwards it to the view method at +0xEE4, which stores it at view+0xDE8 - the field the window's text is drawn from - and starts a 12-tick open wipe. Against the duel's own string bank the three ids are 0x39 "Pick a Card to Trash." for 0x2F, 0x35 "No Cards in Deck." for 0x30, and 0x3B "There are too many Digimon cards in field. Select which to throw away." for 0x31. Only 0x31's arm is skipped when the play-history side byte is set.
claims.coverage: The three arms were read together as one contiguous block, so 'identical apart from one immediate' is a complete comparison rather than a sample, and it is also what shows only 0x31 carries the skip. The id was followed from the dispatch arm through F0x80094FDC into the +0xEE4 method to the field it lands in, which is what rules out the index reading: nothing on that path multiplies it by a stride or adds it to a table base. NOT tested: whether the string bank the window draws from is escardgm rather than another - the ids were matched against escardgm.toml because two other literals this overlay passes the same way land on sensible lines of it, which is corroboration, not proof of the bank's identity.
limitations: The bank identity is inferred from fit, not from reading the bank-selection code.

claims.statement: Opcodes 0x4D and 0x4E take a marked card OFF the field. Their shared update routine F0x800915D4 scans the twelve field slot flags at duel+0x46F for a set one, derives the owning SIDE from whether that slot index is below six - the two sides' six slots being contiguous - stores the side in duel+0x42C and the slot in +0x430, and then routes the card through F0x8008DAF4 or F0x8008DD38 depending on its side argument. Those are the two movers already attributed as 'to the owner's discard' and 'back to the owner's hand', so 0x4D and 0x4E are the discard and bounce effects. The same owner-not-actor principle shows up in opcode 0x41's update F0x8008F790, which discards the played-card stack entry two below the top into the pile indexed by THAT ENTRY's owner field rather than the acting side's - so a card always returns to its own controller.

The update-phase family map for three large opcode groups, taken from the dispatch table dumped in claim cardgame-effect-vm-opcode-census-174-opcodes-132-with-enter-phase-work and confirmed in the assembly. (1) All FIFTEEN target-kind selector opcodes 0x70..0x7e share the single update handler at 0x80085888, which calls F0x8008cb5c and, while that returns -1, leaves the opcode pending; on any other return it stores the value into duel+0x57a, the selection result. That is the SAME completion shape as the 0x8e..0x95 family, which uses the different picker F0x8008d594. So the targeting-prompt model - enter phase marks the legal targets, update phase waits for a pick and returns it in duel+0x57a - now covers 23 opcodes across two groups, not just the eight originally decoded. (2) The twelve stat-change opcodes 0x5e..0x69 share the update handler at 0x80085850, which polls F0x8008e08c and stays pending while it returns zero. Since section G.3 already identifies F0x8008e08c as the routine that walks each slot's DISPLAYED AP/HP toward the targets the enter phase set, this pins the phase split for that family: the enter phase writes the amount, the update phase holds the opcode open until the number has finished rolling on screen. NOTE the amounts for 0x5e..0x69 were ALREADY decoded in section G.3 and are not re-claimed here; only the phase split is new. (3) The six colour-selection opcodes 0x6a..0x6f share the update handler at 0x8008586c, which polls F0x80084090 - the same shared timer poll opcode 0x01 uses - and completes by writing 2 to duel+0x2f4, the uniform switch-2 'done' write. Limitations: F0x8008cb5c itself was NOT decoded, so how the pick is read for 0x70..0x7e, and how cancel is encoded, is unestablished - the same gap that remains for F0x8008d594. Nothing here claims that the two pickers behave identically, only that the two families complete the same way.

Keep everything through '...mask 0x3BC, for which no opcode exists.' Replace the final two sentences with: 'The eight opcode masks and the kind-to-mask table read from F0x800A36E4 are two DIFFERENT partial maps over the same mask space (bit 8 own field, bit 9 opponent field, bits 2..7 the six colours). They agree on seven masks (0x1FC, 0x180, 0x2FC, 0x2BC, 0x280, 0x3FC, 0x380); 0x1BC occurs only on the opcode side; the kind table adds 0x3F8, 0x3F4, 0x310 and 0x3DC and reuses masks across kinds (0x85/0x8E, 0x88/0x8F, 0x8B/0x90, 0x8C/0x95); and 0x3BC occurs on neither side. Nothing is inconsistent: neither map is the other completed; each skips combinations no card needs.'
limitations: Add the missing coverage and limitations: coverage = 'the eight update arms plus the shared tail read in full at file 0x2c68-0x2d14; the kind table read in full from both the assembly (file 0x20b08-0x20c58, jump table 0x80083B04 entry-by-entry) and exe-decomp/cardgame_c/F0x800a36e4.c:13-113; 0x3BC searched over the whole overlay (absent)'.
