claims.notes: Driver result codes 2 and >=4 are only characterised as 'not settled'; the exact slot-probe identities F0x8003be78/F0x8003c1fc were not read here.
claims.coverage: exe/fns F0x80014aa8 with callee F0x8003d254 (cardEventPoll) and manager D0x80048750; consumers F0x80014b44/F0x80014c24

claims.statement: Six resident routines render the dialogue windows. F0x8001b814 draws the plain system window's companion band: for i=0,1 it resolves pack 0x02860000 (CMFONTCS) and draws clip i+8 at (0,166), folding the strips through the draw-context slots +0x9C/+0xA4 (scale from obj+0x68, pivot (320-i*320,196)) or adding the CLUT row obj+0x58 through +0x98. F0x8001b930 draws the companion's blinking advance cursor: palette row obj+0x64 advances every 4 ticks of D0x8004de10+0x188 and clip 0x0A is drawn at (292,205) through D0x80044f5c = F0x800140d8. The anchored speaker balloon's companion (F0x8001c4b4, tick F0x8001c448) draws F0x8001beec (CMFONTCS clip 7 at a per-mode offset from D0x8004dd10, using balloon+0x64-0x0E for modes 2/3, palette row +0x54 every 6 ticks, gated by flag +0x5C) and F0x8001c050 (the mode tail variant clip 3/5/4/6 plus clips 0 and 2 at offsets from D0x8004dcf8[mode], then a semi-transparent grey shadow quad allocated through D0x8004de10+0x158 and inserted through +0x15C using the +0x17C/+0x138 OT anchor). F0x8001c85c builds the balloon zoom object (0xC0 bytes, tick F0x8001c7d8, pack id +0x64, source rect from D0x8004dcf4[mode]+8/+0xA) and F0x8001c4ec draws its open/close scaling outline: ramps scale +0x60 by +0x5C to 0x1000 or 0, transforms +0x50..+0x5A through F0x8002b65c/F0x8002b23c/F0x8002b1dc and emits four PS1 flat-line packets (type byte 3, command 0x40, colour bytes 0,0,255) outlining the rectangle in vertex order D0x80010288 = {1,3,0,2} into the draw service found by F0x8001da84 at cell D0x8004df8c.
claims.notes: The clip-7 (F0x8001beec) art is 8x20 in the extracted cmfont sheet but its on-screen role is not established; whether the four blue line packets of F0x8001c4ec are visible in ordinary play is not established; the shadow-quad reading is a GUESS from its grey ramp and alpha 0x3E.
claims.coverage: exe/fns F0x8001b814, F0x8001b930, F0x8001beec, F0x8001c050, F0x8001c4ec, F0x8001c85c; consumers F0x8001ba2c/F0x8001c448/F0x8001c7d8; pack 0x02860000 = CMFONTCS; tables D0x8004dcf4/dcf8/dd00/dd10

claims.statement: F0x80032f8c applies the sound driver tick mode held at D0x8005c0a0 by programming PS1 Timer2 through the statically initialised timer base D0x8005c0c4 = 0x1F801100: F0x800333d4 clears the selected timer counter and F0x8003329c writes its mode and target (default key 0xF2000002 with target 0x44E8; mode 3 target 0x89D0; modes 1,4,>=6 target 0x204CC0/rate when rate<0x46 else 0x409980/rate; mode 5 target 1). It writes the volume byte D0x8005c0b2 (6, then 0x7F or 0 per case) and, under EnterCriticalSection, installs or releases the per-tick callback through the interrupt object D0x8005bfd8 (method +0x08 via F0x8002ea4c; method +0x14 via F0x8002eaac): volume 0 installs the chain callback F0x800331fc, otherwise the callback is F0x80033248 when flag +1 is set and the default D0x8005c0a8 = F0x8002f59c otherwise, with F0x80033248's one-shot latch at D0x8005c0b4. It is called from sound init F0x80020a10 through wrapper F0x800331dc(arg 0); the twin F0x800331bc(arg 1) has no caller in the asm tree.
claims.notes: The PsyQ/lib-snd identity of this tick install is a GUESS; the musical meaning of the 0x204CC0/0x409980 divisors is a GUESS (44,100-based tick lengths); which tick modes ordinary play selects is not established.
claims.coverage: exe/fns F0x80032f8c with wrappers F0x800331bc/F0x800331dc, timer cells D0x8005c0a4/c0c4 and interrupt object D0x8005bfd8

claims.statement: F0x8002bf1c zeroes the first 32-bit word of each 32-byte slot in the CD-stream slot table D0x80081488 for the slot range first..first+count-1. It is the range primitive of the stream reset F0x8002bc0c (clear all D0x8008148c slots, then zero the stream state block D0x80081448/4c/54/64/6c/70/74) and is called twice inside the CD-stream pump F0x8002c03c (fns.s L31041/L31092) with count=end-current; the pump reads slot+0 as a status word and supplies sectors through CD register cell D0x8005aac8 and DMA starter F0x8002c984. The base and count cells are installed together by F0x8002b94c(base,count), whose only caller seen in the asm tree is the stdwtitl movie setup at pro/stdwtitl.s:578.
claims.notes: Only slot word +0 is read here; the meaning of slot fields +2..+0x1F and the full writer set of D0x80081488 outside exe are not established.
claims.coverage: exe/fns F0x8002bf1c with callers F0x8002bc0c/F0x8002c03c and table D0x80081488

claims.statement: Five game-facing request helpers of the controller driver all enter through the provider slot D0x80055d84 with the caller's pad id as the still-live first argument (the lifted C drops that parameter). 0x80020d8c stores a caller data pointer at block+0x28 and its byte count at +0x34 (callers F0x800186e0 L30 and F0x80019224 L25 pass a per-port D0x8004bb98 slot and length 2). 0x80020dcc and 0x80020f3c first call the idle predicate slot D0x80055d8c on the block; only when it returns 0 do they set +0x46=1 and install a +0x14 callback plus a +0x18 callback: 0x80020dcc stores the caller's 6-byte table pointer at +0x20 and installs 0x80020e48/0x80020e70, while 0x80020f3c stores two caller bytes at +0x51/+0x52, installs 0x80020fd8/0x80021030 and records at +0x53 whether the first byte equals the block's current +0xE4 (xor plus sltiu). Both return 1 on acceptance and 0 when the predicate reported busy. The start callbacks queue controller commands through F0x80023d80 (padSetCommand): 0x80020e48 sends 0x4D with the 6 bytes pointed to by +0x20; 0x80020fd8 sends 0x44 with the 2 bytes at +0x51 when +0x46 is 2 and 0x4D with the 6 bytes at +0x5D when +0x46 is 3, doing nothing in any other state. Static reads only; the protocol meanings of 0x44/0x4D are not established.
claims.notes: Draft names: padSetActDirect, padQueueActAlign, padStartActAlign, padQueueActPair, padStartActPair. Limits: protocol bytes, the +4/+0xE9 capability table fields, and the identity of the reset hook D0x80055d74.
claims.coverage: Bodies read in full: 0x80020d8c L18514-L18529, 0x80020dcc L18534-L18562, 0x80020e48 L18567-L18576, 0x80020f3c L18636-L18672, 0x80020fd8 L18677-L18698. Caller argument use checked at F0x800186e0 L30, F0x80019224 L25, F0x80019148 L25, F0x8001902c L29 in the lifted C. The four pointer cells are statically zero in data.rs L7726-L7732.

claims.statement: Two continuation callbacks installed by the controller driver's request helpers. 0x80020e70 walks the block's +0xE9 five-byte entries at +4: for each entry ordinal it counts how many of the six bytes at +0x20 equal that ordinal, reads entry byte +2 as a minimum-1 threshold, and writes the block's +0x5D..+0x62 map so that each matching payload position receives the ordinal when the occurrence count reaches the threshold and 0xFF otherwise; it then sets +0x46=0xFE and returns 0. Because the count is only decremented on the 0xFF branch, an entry below its threshold produces 0xFF at every matching position; payload positions that do not equal a valid ordinal are never written. 0x80021030 reads the +0x53 flag: when set it returns 1 while +0x46 is 2 and otherwise forces +0x46=0xFE and returns 0; when clear it calls the reset hook D0x80055d74 with the block and returns 0. Static reads only.
claims.notes: Draft names: padFinishActAlign, padFinishActPair. Limits: what the +4 capability entries mean and what the reset hook D0x80055d74 does.

claims.statement: Three accessors of the controller driver. 0x8002109c resolves the caller's pad id through D0x80055d84 and returns the block's +0x49 state: when the block is busy - +0x37 or +0x38 nonzero, or +0x39 nonzero on a non-root block (+0x10 is the block's own root pointer), or the byte at the status pointer +0x30 nonzero - it maps raw 2 and 3 to 1 and raw 6 to 4; when none of those hold it returns +0x49 unchanged. 0x8002126c is the capability-table accessor: a negative index returns the entry count +0xE9; an index inside the count selects the 5-byte entry at +4 and returns field number 1..5 (byte field-1) through the jump table D0x800102b8, whose five words are at fns.s L268-L272; an out-of-range index or a field outside 1..5 returns 0. 0x8002131c is the fifth jump-table body: it returns byte +4 of the selected entry and rejoins 0x8002126c's epilogue, which is why no caller and no lifted C exist for it. Static reads only.
claims.notes: Draft names: padGetState, padGetCapability, padGetCapabilityField5. Limits: the meaning of the raw +0x49 state codes and of the five capability fields.
claims.coverage: 0x8002109c L18734-L18784, 0x8002126c L18858-L18889, 0x8002131c L18922-L18924 and the jump table L268-L272 read in full; callers checked at F0x80018ad8 L9 and F0x80019148 L13/L17.

claims.statement: The two block reset routines installed at D0x80055d74. Both test +0x49 first and do nothing when it is zero. 0x8002177c (non-multitap) clears +0x49, +0x46, the +0xE6 halfword twice, +0x14, +0x18, +0xE3, +0xE4, +0xE9, +0xEA, +0x00, +0x04 and +0x08, then fills the six bytes +0x5D..+0x62 with 0xFF. 0x800221e4 (multitap) performs the same sequence and additionally clears +0x37, +0x38 and +0x39 before the fill. Static reads only.
claims.notes: Draft names: padResetBlock, padResetBlockMtap. The +0xE6 halfword is cleared twice in both bodies, kept as written.

claims.statement: The two reply-buffer rotate routines installed at D0x80055d94. 0x800218d8 (non-multitap) copies the block's +0x37 into +0x38 and clears +0x37. 0x80022370 (multitap) does the same for the root and then, for each of the four child blocks at root+0xC (stride 0xF0), shifts the child's bytes down: child+2 = child+1, child+1 = child+0, child+0 = 0. Static reads only.
claims.notes: Draft names: padShiftReplyByte, padShiftReplyBytes. F0x800218d8 is called directly by F0x800217e4 L24.

claims.statement: The pad-block resolver pair and its free predicate. 0x80021c20 (non-multitap provider) returns D0x8007ed38, or D0x8007ed38+0xF0 when the id's high nibble is set. 0x80022740 (multitap provider) returns D0x8007efa8 or +0xF0 the same way, and when the multitap flag D0x80055dbc is set it further selects a child: with +0xE8 equal to 8 and the id's low nibble zero it returns base->C+0 (the first child); otherwise it returns the port base when (id & 3) is zero, or base->C + (id & 3)*0xF0 when it is not. 0x8002209c (non-multitap free predicate) returns 0 only when the block's +0xE6 halfword is nonzero and +0x46 equals 0xFF, otherwise 1. Static reads only; why the +0xE8==8 and slot-0 case resolves to a child rather than the port base is not established.
claims.notes: Draft names: padGetBlock, padGetBlockMtap, padBlockFree. Limits: the +0xE8==8 slot-0 child selection has no consumer read; D0x80055dbc is set by driver init not on this list.

claims.statement: The controller driver's outgoing-byte generators are F0x800218e8 (plain, installed at slot D0x80055d78 by F0x8002168c at fns.s L19184) and F0x800223b4 (multitap, installed by F0x800220cc at L19876). Both compute idx = block+0x45 - 3 and return one byte per call: with command +0x37 == 0 they emit block+0x28[idx] only when (idx >= 6 or block+0x57[idx] != 0) and idx < block+0x34, else 0 (L19315-L19336); with command 0x4D they emit block+0x2C[idx] while idx < block+0x36, else 0xFF (L19343-L19350); with any other command they emit block+0x2C[idx] while idx < block+0x36, else 0 (L19351-L19359). F0x800223b4 adds, for arg1 != 0, a slot mapping that selects one of the four 0xF0-stride blocks at block+0x0C by ((idx < 0 ? block+0x45+4 : idx) >> 3) and remaps the byte index to (idx mod 8) - 2 (L20036-L20048); a remapped index of -2 returns block+0x37 or 0x42 when block+0x37 == 0 (the 0x42 store at L20097 is a beqz delay slot), and any other negative index returns 0 (L20093-L20098).
claims.notes: Corrects worker-serial-card draft on the negative-index guard and records the 0x42 store at L20097 as a beqz delay-slot fallback. Protocol meaning of command bytes not established.
claims.coverage: exe/fns F0x800218e8 and F0x800223b4 with installers F0x8002168c/F0x800220cc and consumers padXferStage3 F0x80024964 / padXferStage4 F0x80024a80

claims.statement: The plain driver's request-lifecycle handlers are F0x80021c40, F0x80021d50 and the multitap resolver F0x800227b0. F0x80021c40 is installed at slot D0x80055d88 by F0x8002168c (fns.s L19196) and every path returns 0: it reads reply[0] from block+0x3C and queues F0x80024630(block,0) when reply[0]==0xF3 and (block+0xE8==0 or block+0x46==0xFF) (L19552, L19556), queues F0x80024630(block,1) when block+0x46==1 (L19584), returns for +0x46 in {0,0xFF}, and otherwise calls the block+0x14 callback or F0x80023d90 (L19601). F0x80021d50 is installed at slot D0x80055d90 (L19205) and consumes a reply: reply[0] high nibble 0 clears status[0]=0xFF, status[1]=0, block+0xE8=0 and block+0x35=0 and calls D0x80055d74 (L19616-L19625); otherwise block+0xE8=reply[0]>>4 with the old value restored when the nibble is 0xF, status[0]=0, status[1]=reply[0], status[2..+0x44-1]=reply[2..] with +0x35=+0x44 when +0x44>2 (L19641, L19653), D0x80055d74 is called when reply[1]!=0 or (+0x46==1 with +0x14==0) or +0x50!=0 or +0xE8 changed, and the +0x46 machine then runs when +0x46!=0xFF and (+0x46==0 or +0x37!=0): +0x46 2..0xFD with reply[0]!=0xF3 calls D0x80055d74 and returns without the switch (L19718), else 0 -> +0x49=1 and +0x46++ (L19741), 1 -> +0x47=0 and +0x46++, 0xFE -> +0x46=0xFF, other -> block+0x18 callback or F0x80023e14 (L19757) with +0x46 += its return. F0x800227b0 is installed at D0x80055d88 by F0x800220cc (L19888): block+0xC==NULL marks a slot block (only port roots get +0xC, set at L19865), a pending block+0x38 is accepted only when the per-port word D0x80055d58[port]!=0 (L20317) and is moved to block+0x37 unless it is 0x43 (L20323); with no pending byte it scans the root's four 0xF0-stride siblings (L20329) and returns 0 when a sibling holds 0x43 in +0x37/+0x38 with payload[0]==1 (L20340); its tail calls D0x80055d74 when reply[0]==0xF3 and block+0xE8 is neither 0 nor 8 and block+0x49==2, dispatches +0x46 (1 -> F0x80024630(block,1); 0xFE with +0x49==2 -> block+0x37=0, else F0x80024630(block,0); 0/0xFF -> 0; other -> +0x14 callback or F0x80023d90), and in the +0xFF case with +0xE8==8 recurses F0x800227b0 into the first child whose +0x46==1 (L20444), returning 1 when no child matches.
claims.notes: Corrects worker-serial-card on the F0x80021c40 reply==F3 && +0x46==0xFF path (queues F0x80024630(block,0), does not return 0) and on F0x800227b0's head (+0xC==NULL marks a slot block, not a root). F0x80024630 and F0x80023d90 bodies not read here.
claims.coverage: exe/fns F0x80021c40, F0x80021d50, F0x800227b0 with installers F0x8002168c/F0x800220cc; D0x80055d58 writer F0x80022258 L19959

claims.statement: F0x800219a4 and F0x800224c4 are two installations of one pad-request byte planner. They are installed at slot D0x80055d7c by the plain init F0x8002168c (fns.s L19187) and the multitap init F0x800220cc (L19879) and are called by padXferStage3 F0x80024964 and padXferStage4 F0x80024a80 at the start of a block pass. The two bodies are identical: fns.s L19366-L19524 and L20105-L20263 are both 160 lines and compare equal for all 160 after masking .L and F0x addresses as of 2026-09-11, and the two lifted C files are identical modulo the function name. Neither reads the reply buffer block+0x3C. Each clears the six flag bytes block+0x57..+0x5C (L19369-L19372) and then, when block+0xE6 != 0 and block+0x28 != 0 (L19373), walks the block+0xE9 five-byte descriptor entries at block+0x4 and scans the first min(6, block+0x34) bytes of the block+0x28 descriptor for a position i where the precomputed block+0x5D[i] equals the entry ordinal t0 and descriptor[i] & (entry+2 ? 0xFF : 1) is nonzero; a hit adds entry+3 to D0x80055db8 while the sum stays below 0x3D (L19429) and sets the block+0x57 flag bytes at the matching positions. Otherwise, for block+0xE8 in {4,5,7} with +0xE6 == 0 and +0x34 >= 2 and descriptor bytes 0x40/1 and D0x80055db8+0xA < 0x3D it sets block+0x57 and block+0x58 and adds 0xA (L19496); for +0xE8 == 3 it sets only block+0x57; with +0xE6 == 0 it sets all six flags (L19517).
claims.notes: Corrects the worker-serial-card draft label comment: this routine never reads +0x3C, so it plans outgoing bytes rather than processing replies. The multitap copy has zero instruction differences; the only second-half difference is the installer/mode context.
claims.coverage: exe/fns F0x800219a4 and F0x800224c4 with installers F0x8002168c/F0x800220cc and consumers F0x80024964/F0x80024a80; D0x80055db8 writer checked against F0x80023274

claims.statement: F0x80021fbc is the plain controller driver's per-block timeout and cancel handler, called by the poll loop F0x800217e4 at fns.s L19267. It increments block+0x4C on every call (L19775) and allows 11 increments of block+0x4A: for block+0x46==0 it goes straight to the reply check; for block+0x46==1 it increments block+0x4A and returns while below 0x0B (L19785), and at 0x0B sets block+0x49=2 and block+0x46=0xFF (L19789, L19790); for any other +0x46 it increments +0x4A and returns while below 0x0B, and at 0x0B calls D0x80055d74 when block+0x49!=0 (L19807), then clears status[0]=0xFF (L19817), status[1]=0, block+0xE8=0 and block+0x35=0 when reply[0]!=0xF3 (L19812).
claims.notes: What the 11 ticks count is not established (GUESS: transaction attempts/bytes). Whether the multitap path reaches this routine through F0x80022e08 is not verified here.
claims.coverage: exe/fns F0x80021fbc and its caller F0x800217e4

claims.statement: F0x80034fdc clears the u16 D0x80082600 to 0 and F0x80034fec sets it to 2. F0x800311fc chooses between them: it calls F0x80034fdc when its level argument (arg2 & 0xFF) is below 0x40 and F0x80034fec otherwise, then uploads the voice sample through F0x800301dc. F0x800354cc's driver init also writes 0, and F0x80034e0c reads the cell when staging a voice's tone words (low 5 bits plus the cell, clamped 0x1F).
claims.notes: What the 0/2 states mean is not established (GUESS: a coarse side-of-centre offset, because F0x800311fc switches at 0x40).
claims.coverage: Both one-store bodies were read in full in lifted C and their quoted lines re-checked in ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003/exe/fns.s; all four callers from dw3-research callers (F0x800311fc, F0x8003165c, F0x8003340c for the clear; F0x800311fc for the set) were checked, and the choosing condition was read in F0x800311fc.

claims.statement: F0x80034ffc() is the per-frame voice driver update. It advances the 16-deep ring (index D0x8008251c, words D0x80082520), runs every voice through F0x8003b1cc, and when D0x80082698 == 0 ANDs the whole ring and releases through F0x800394bc every voice whose D0x80081e55 state is 2; fires the per-voice callbacks D0x80082518 and D0x80082390 when the +0x38 flags D0x80081e56/1e62 are set; flushes each voice with D0x80082378 dirty bits set through F0x8003a9cc with the packed argument 3, 0x10, 0x80 or 0x60000 for bits 1, 4, 8 or 0x10; calls F0x8003a61c(0, D0x80082560/62) and F0x8003a61c(1, D0x80081e28/2a); then folds the voice masks through F0x8003a40c(8, ...) and F0x800394bc(8, ...) and zeroes D0x80082560/62 and D0x80081e28/2a/30/32. Callers: F0x8002f59c and F0x800354cc.
claims.notes: The hardware split of the F0x8003a61c / F0x8003a40c / F0x8003a9cc writes is not decoded here; D0x80082698's meaning is not established (the code treats it as a freeze-release switch).
claims.coverage: The body was read in full in lifted C and the quoted calls re-checked in ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003/exe/fns.s; both callers are the complete list from dw3-research callers.

claims.statement: The resident voice level and note-start family. F0x8003776c(voiceKey, program, tone, level, pan) recomputes live levels for every voice whose +0x38-stride keys D0x80081e48/1e4c/1e50 match voiceKey/tone/program (skipping bits set in D0x8005c070), applies the master volume [D0x80082654]+0x18, the [D0x8008264c] per-tone pan table and three 0x40-midpoint attenuation fields, squares, divides by 16383, writes D0x80082398/+2 with dirty bits 3 and returns the count. F0x8003619c(voice) starts one voice from the D0x8008267c note record: levels to D0x80082398/9a + voice*0x10 with dirty bits 3, state 0xA at D0x80081e3c+voice*0x38, 2 at D0x80081e55+voice*0x38, OR the voice bit into D0x80081e28/2a (and 1e2c/2e when D0x8008267a bit2), clear D0x80082560/62. F0x8003680c(track, pitch) is the sequencer variant keyed on D0x80082680, storing the pitch at D0x8008239c+voice*0x10 and as the state byte D0x80081e3c+voice*0x38 with dirty bits 7. F0x80034e0c() arms the voice at D0x80082680: 0x7FFF at D0x80081e3e+idx*0x38, clears the voice bit in the 16-word D0x80082520 ring, copies a pan word from [D0x8008264c] + ((D0x8008267e - 1)/2)*0x10 (field +0xC when bit0 of 0x8008267e is set, else +0xE) to D0x8008239e+idx*0x10, stages the tone record's +0x10/+0x12 halfwords (low 5 bits plus D0x80082600, clamped 0x1F) at D0x800823a0 and sets dirty bits. F0x80035fbc() returns F0x80036070(byte 0x8008266a, 0, byte 0x80082678, min(byte 0x80082679, 0x7F)) & 0xFFFF, the pitch F0x8003581c hands to F0x8003680c. F0x80036cdc(voice, owner, tone, program, slide) ramps a matched voice's D0x80081e46 byte by (slide - 0x40) scaled by the tone header's +0xD (up) or +0xC (down) slope modulo 63, writes F0x80036008's result to D0x8008239c+voice*0x10, sets dirty bit 4, records D0x80082674 and returns 1 on a match else 0.
claims.notes: The pan/square chain is read as arithmetic, not verified as a hardware pan law (GUESS). Field names inside the 0x38-stride voice records and the 0x38-adjacent note records are only partly named. No runtime verification was done.

claims.statement: Sequence track helpers. claims.statement: F0x800387ec(src, byteCount) is the manual (non-DMA) SPU RAM upload. It stores D0x8005c298 into the SPU transfer address +0x1A6, calls F0x80039044, then per chunk of min(0x40, remaining) bytes writes halfwords to SPU +0x1A8 and sets SPUCNT +0x1AA = (cnt & 0xFFCF) | 0x10, waits for status +0x1AE bit 0x400 (after 0xF00 spins it calls F0x800283fc with D0x80010b98/D0x80010bb8), delays twice per chunk, and at the end clears the 0x30 bits and waits for status bits 0x7FF to equal the saved value (second diagnostic D0x80010bcc). Callers: F0x8003856c and F0x80038d90.
claims.notes: The status bits 0x400/0x7FF are read as a transfer busy/ready handshake (GUESS); byteCount is a byte count (each chunk is min(0x40, remaining) bytes, written as 0x20 halfwords).

claims.statement: Resident SPU transfer engine. F0x80038b10 is the four-command SPU transfer dispatcher and F0x8003901c is one of its two D0x8005c294 (0x1F801014) access-delay writers. cmd0 sets D0x8005c2d0 = 1 and, after waiting for the SPU transfer-address register +0x1A6 to equal the shadow D0x8005c298 (up to 0xF00 spins, else return -2), ORs 0x30 into SPUCNT +0x1AA; cmd1 sets D0x8005c2d0 = 0 with the same wait and then SPUCNT = (cnt & 0xFFCF) | 0x20; cmd2 stores arg1 >> D0x8005c2a8 (=3) into both the shadow and +0x1A6; cmd3 waits for SPUCNT bits 0x30 to match the mode, calls F0x8003901c when D0x8005c2d0 == 1 else F0x80038ff4, then writes SPU DMA channel 4 MADR = arg1, BCR = (((arg2 + 63) >> 6) << 16) | 0x10 and CHCR = 0x01000200 in mode 1 or 0x01000201. F0x8003901c read-modify-writes D0x8005c294 (= 0x1F801014, data.rs L14260) to (*ptr & 0xF0FFFFFF) | 0x22000000; the paired F0x80038ff4 is the same store with 0x20000000. The three DMA pointer cells are D0x8005c284/288/28c = 0x1F8010C0/C4/C8 and D0x8005c280 = 0x1F801C00 (data.rs L14255-14258). Callers of F0x80038b10: F0x80038d90, F0x80038e14, F0x8003a46c.
claims.notes: BCR and CHCR bit meanings remain GUESS-level (chopping/trigger/direction) and whether cmd3 uploads or reads back SPU RAM is not settled. F0x80038ff4 is outside this worklist and is named only as the pairing writer.

claims.statement: F0x800399cc(sampleWord) is the SPU-RAM block-membership test. It walks the 8-byte block list at D0x8005c2e8: an entry whose word0 bit31 is set is skipped to the next, bit30 set returns 0, the low 28 bits are the base and the second word the size. It returns 1 when the target (sampleWord << D0x8005c2a8 (=3)) is at or before a flag-free entry's base, or when base < target < base+size (exclusive at both ends); a null list returns 0. Both consumers treat a 1 as a stop: F0x80039a5c returns -1 for the record whose table word D0x8005c810[idx] yields 1, and F0x8003985c's enable-1 path clears D0x8005c214 and SPUCNT bit 0x80 when the test yields 1 while the D0x8005c218 latch is not 1. The list is initialized by F0x800390dc(0x20, D0x80082730) from F0x800354cc; F0x8003913c marks a released entry arg0 | 0x80000000 and F0x800391bc merges, sorts and compacts the list.
claims.notes: Whether the list records allocated or free SPU blocks is not established (GUESS: an allocation map, because releasing a bank marks its entry through F0x8003913c and the compactor merges marked entries). No runtime read was taken.
claims.coverage: The body was read in full in lifted C, including the branch delay slot at 0x80039a24 that makes the target <= base case return 1; F0x80039a5c (L45340 jal), F0x8003985c (L45197 jal), F0x800390dc, F0x8003913c and F0x800391bc were all read; the comment that a return of 1 is a stop is checked against both consumers' branch directions.

claims.statement: Resident reverb-preset records. Ten 0x44-byte records live at D0x8005c840 and their SPU addresses are the word table D0x8005c810 (0xfffe,0xfb28,0xfc18,0xf6f8,0xf204,0xea44,0xe128,0xcff8,0xcff8,0xf880). F0x80039a5c applies or updates one: index = cmd+4 with bit 0x100 meaning release; when the mask word is 0 or bit0 it validates with F0x800399cc(D0x8005c810[idx]) (reject -1 on 1), copies the record into a stack block {u32 register mask; 32 u16 values}, writes SPU +0x184/+0x186 from record +8/+0xA, pushes the 32 values to SPU +0x1C0..+0x1FE through F0x80039f3c, then sets the work address with F0x80038e78(0xD1, D0x8005c21c, 0). On the copy path it saves SPUCNT bit 0x80, clears it for the update and restores it afterwards; when the index carried bit 0x100 it calls F0x8003a46c(idx). Mask bits 1/2 write the level pair; bits 3/4 patch records 7/8 from cmd+0xC (to D0x8005c22c) and cmd+0x10 (to D0x8005c230) and are ignored for any other index. The four builders feed it: F0x8003481c {mask 6, +8/+0xA = arg*0x7FFF/127 via magic 0x81020409}, F0x800348ac {mask 1, index | 0x100 for a negative id, F0x8003985c(0) first for id 0, returns |id| or -1}, F0x800347dc {mask 8, +0xC}, F0x8003494c {mask 0x10, +0x10}.
claims.notes: These records are described as reverb presets because F0x80039f3c writes the SPU +0x1C0 block, F0x80038e78(0xD1,...) writes the reverb work address and core-q001-8003856c-spu-driver-init names +0x184/+0x186 reverb volumes; no ear check was made and the D0x8005c810 constants' individual effects are not established. The release bit's fade amount is not decoded.

claims.statement: Controller byte-exchange primitives F0x80023a4c and F0x80023828. Both are invoked per byte from the pad transaction stages and each: waits for JOY_STAT bit1 (receive FIFO not empty), picks JOY_BAUD 0x88 or 0x22 (0x22 when the first buffered reply byte high nibble is 8 and at least 9 bytes are already buffered), writes its byte argument to JOY_DATA through D0x80055de8=0x1F801040, appends the byte that was waiting in JOY_DATA to the block reply buffer at +0x3C[+0x44], increments +0x44 and +0x45, and returns the received byte. F0x80023a4c arms the wait with timerWindowStart(0x190); F0x80023828 stores the 0x1AE deadline into D0x8007f9a0, latches Timer-2 mode into D0x8007f9a4, and for a negative argument sends its complement as a command byte without touching the reply buffer.

claims.statement: Resident card file operations on top of the card manager. cardReadChunkStart F0x8003cba4(chan,name,buf,offset,size) and cardWriteChunkStart F0x8003cdc4 are identical apart from their state 3/4 and step F0x8003ccbc/F0x8003cedc: each refuses when the manager is busy, when the handle at D0x800828d0+0x14 is already open, or when offset or size is not a multiple of 0x80, otherwise it formats the bu00: name (F0x8003d5e0), appends the name argument (F0x8003d90c), stores the channel at +0x10, offset at +0x18, size at +0x1C and buffer at +0x20, and pushes its step through F0x8003dabc. cardReadStep F0x8003c790 and cardWriteStep F0x8003c9f8 run that file: after pushing a nested cardInfoStep F0x8003bee0 they fseek the handle to +0x18 then fread/fwrite size bytes at +0x20, and finish by storing cardResultToCode(F0x8003d4e0) of the event code into D0x800828d0+4. cardListFiles F0x8003cfe4(chan,pattern,buf,countOut,first,max) waits for idle, calls cardFirstFile F0x8003d65c for the first entry and nextfile (B0:0x43) for the rest, copies 0x28-byte records into the caller buffer, returns the number copied through countOut, and on a failed first entry re-runs the state-2 directory machine blocking through cardEventPoll(0,0,&code) up to 4 times. cardFirstFile F0x8003d65c copies the caller name up to the byte 0x3B into D0x80082938, scans the kernel file list (entry pointer at absolute 0x150, byte count at 0x154 divided by the 0x50-byte entry size), matches entry names through F0x8003d9bc, saves the matched entry word at +0x34 into D0x80082930 and overwrites +0x34 with F0x8003d7f8, then calls firstfile (B0:0x42). cardFlagSwap F0x8003d240 returns the old D0x80082914 and stores its argument there; callers use it as clear/restore around blocking card polls. cardFormat F0x8003d46c waits for idle, runs the formatter F0x8003e27c (writes the MC header at sector 0, the 0xA0 directory frames at sectors 1..15 and 20 further sectors) and maps its result through cardResultToCode, with raw result 4 mapped to 2. cardWipeSectors F0x8003ed1c waits for idle, fills a 0x80-byte stack buffer with 0xFF and writes sectors 0..14 through write_card_sector (B0:0x4E), calling allow_new_card (B0:0x50) before each attempt, and returns 1 after 15 sectors or 0 on an event.
claims.notes: INCOMPLETE: the request type numbering that selects format (type 2) versus wipe (type 3) was read from the caller dispatch at 0x800153f0/0x80015408/0x80015418 but the UI side was not traced. Writing sectors 0..14 with 0xFF also overwrites the sector-0 MC header, so this is a full wipe, not a file clear; why the manager would leave the card headerless is not established.

A successful queue start stores state 4 at 0x80015174 and returns 0; the state clear at 0x80015178 returns 1 for a non-zero driver result.

claims.statement: The exe CD subsystem init is F0x8002ba0c: it calls the reset F0x8002dc7c and, only when that returns 0, the SPU/CD-audio init F0x8002db40; it returns success only when both succeed. F0x8002dc7c clears D0x8005ab3c/3d, the callback slots D0x8005ab24/20 and the last interrupt bytes D0x8005ab2c/30, resets the interrupt dispatcher (F0x8002ea1c) and installs handler F0x8002dfd0 at slot 2 (F0x8002ea4c), drains pending CD IRQ flags through index 1/0x1F801803/0x1F801802=7, resets status D0x8005adfc (+2,+1,+0 = 0,0,2), sets CD index/mask 0 and the delay register 0x1325, then sends Nop (1) twice if the last interrupt byte has bit 0x10, Init (0xA), Demagic (0xC) via CD_cw F0x8002d5d8 and finishes with CD_sync F0x8002d090 (0 only when the sync status is 2). claims.statement: The exe disc-stream subsystem is a slot ring at D0x80081488 (count D0x8008148c, stride 0x20, slot word0 status, word4 subheader, word6 count, word8 stream word, +0x1C timecode) driven by the pump F0x8002c03c and its helpers. The pump reports progress through D0x8005ab10: it skips a busy ring (D0x80081464==1), polls F0x8002e23c(1,&b), refuses a busy current slot, programs the CD cells D0x8005aac8/aad4/aad8/aadc, starts the sector transfer with the CD-DMA starter F0x8002c984 (or the debug memory source D0x80081478 through F0x8002c958), then validates the header (word0==0x160, word2 bits10-14==D0x80081460) and recycles the ring through F0x8002bf1c on mismatch. A data sector (word4==0) sets D0x80081448 = word8&0xFFFF, applies the D0x8008147c limit and the D0x800814a4 callback, computes the destination D0x80081484 = slot + count*0x20 + index*0x7E0 and starts the 0x1F8-word payload transfer, marks slot word0=3 and bumps D0x8008146c. F0x8002bc0c resets the ring and counters, F0x8002bcec completes a consumed slot (word0=2, copies +0x1C to D0x80081490, slot+8 to D0x80081494, advances the consumer and calls D0x800814a0), F0x8002c01c stores the mode/expected-id/limit words D0x80081480/5c/7c, and F0x8002badc converts the 3-byte BCD MSF timecode to a sector number ((BCD(m)*60+BCD(s))*75+BCD(f)-150).

claims.statement: The resident GPU driver table D0x80055eb0 holds two methods lifted from data.rs: +0x0C = F0x80026e00 (data.rs:7814) and +0x20 = F0x80027030 (data.rs:7819). F0x80026e00 takes a rect (xy at +0, wh at +4), clamps wh to D0x80055efc-1 / D0x80055efe-1, and when x or w has any low-6 bits set builds an 8-word packet (tag, E3/E4/E5 draw area and offset refreshed through F0x80027590(3/4/5), E6 mask, E1 texpage from GPUSTAT, then a GP0 0x60 variable rectangle coloured from arg1's low 24 bits) and otherwise a 5-word packet (tag, E6, E1, GP0 0x02 fill, xy, wh); both are handed to the sender F0x80027548. F0x80027030 is LoadImage: it clamps wh, computes (w*h+1), returns -1 when the halfword count is zero, waits for GPU/DMA readiness (F0x80027da0), sets GP1 DMA direction off, writes GP0 0x01000000 then 0xA0000000 (0xB0000000 when arg2 nonzero) then xy and wh to the GP0 port, writes the remainder words from arg1 by CPU, and DMA2s the rest with MADR=arg1+remainder, BCR=(blocks<<16)|0x10, CHCR=0x01000201.

claims.statement: F0x80022a20 is the multitap-mode transaction finaliser installed at D0x80055d90. It clears the 2-byte status, +0xE8 and +0x35 when the first reply byte's high nibble is 0 and runs D0x80055d74(arg0); reports a non-root block whose second reply byte is neither 0 nor 0x5A (or whose nibble is 8) to F0x80022e08(arg0,0xFF); for a 0x5A reply copies the reply into +0x30 (length E8=8 -> +0x35=2, else +0x35=+0x44, non-root always six bytes) and calls D0x80055d74(arg0,status,nibble,oldE8); then runs the +0x46 state machine (0 -> +0x49=1/+0x46++ or +0x49=2/+0x46=0xFF when E8==8 and the child reply is 0xFF; 1 -> +0x47=0/+0x46++; 0xFE -> +0x46=0xFF; default -> callback +0x18 or F0x80023e14, +0x46 += result). F0x80022e08 is the per-port state transition: it latches E8=8 with status 0xFF/0x80 and +0x35=2 on a root 8-nibble reply, recurses into the four 0xF0-stride children at +0xC with -1, decides waiting vs advance from +0x38/+0x37 child flags, rotates +0x37 into +0x38/+0x39 bumping +0x4C, caps retries at +0x4A 0x0B/0x15 before failing to +0x49=2/+0x46=0xFF or 0xFE (callback D0x80055d74), and clears or re-arms E8/status[1] from the new nibble.

claims.statement: F0x8001d264 decodes one 2-byte text token to a font glyph index. A zero first byte returns 0x400; with arg1&0xFF nonzero, first bytes < 4 return the raw big-endian halfword, byte 0x0A returns 0x201, and a token whose 16-bit value v satisfies (v+0x7DB1)&0xFFFF < 0x146 (SJIS 0x824F..0x8394) is searched in the sparse 4-byte {u16 key; u8 value} table at arg2+0xC, otherwise in arg2+0x10 where the found value is ORed with 0x100; a 0xFFFF key terminates the table and a miss returns 0x300. With arg1&0xFF zero, first byte 1 returns ((u16)arg2+0x16 + 1 & 0xFF)|0x100 when the second byte exceeds the signed limit at arg2+0x16, first bytes >= 4 return the byte when below the signed limit at arg2+0x14 else 0x300, and bytes 2/3 return the raw halfword. Installed in the global pointer cell D0x8004de0c (data.rs:4087) and called by F0x8001aa10 with (string base + index, mode byte at object+0x66, pointer at object+0x50), which stores the result as a halfword at object+0x14.
claims.notes: The interpretation of the 0x824F..0x8394 key range as SJIS kana/digit/letter codes and of the tables as glyph maps is a GUESS supported by the range arithmetic; the two table formats (4-byte entries, 0xFFFF terminator) are read from the assembly; which screen F0x8001aa10 serves was not traced.

It fires immediately after the three fields the dive launcher seeded on the type-7 object -- a0 = [obj+0x74] player x, a1 = [obj+0x78] player y, a2 = [obj+0x70] hole/water mode (file 0x874c-0x8758) -- are passed to the effect spawner F0x80085e0c, whose result is stored to [s5]; the body then calls [obj+0x40]. Both dives were captured on the rig and dispatched 0x00040004 at frame 10 from the IDENTICAL return address 0x8008b42c, with no other packed sound through frame 360 (water) / 480 (hole). The hole/water mode is therefore not a sound selector but a VISUAL one, consumed at file 0x8754 (into F0x80085e0c) and file 0x88ac (a0 = [obj+0x70] into F0x80085ac4, result stored to [s5+0x8]); the captures show the divergence directly -- a shared blackout with bright-blue particles through f96, then form-specific content from f108 (Submarimon: underwater vignette, bubbles; Digmon: oval spotlight, disturbed dirt ring, digging with debris particles), rejoining for the shared cyan rectangular-tile wipe and sliding location title. claims.statement: The resident display service's frame-delta accumulator is advanced by F0x8001D3F4, which is installed as entry 4 of the eight-entry vertical-blank callback table D0x8005BFF8 and therefore runs exactly once per vertical blank. F0x8001D4E0 hands the feeder to F0x8002EAAC, which calls service-table slot +0x14 with (4, callback); that slot holds F0x8002F270, which writes the callback into D0x8005BFF8[n]. F0x8002F204 walks all eight entries in order and is itself installed on IRQ 0 by F0x8002F1AC through F0x8002EE58, which sets bit irq of the hardware interrupt mask at 0x1F801074; IRQ 0 is VBLANK. Because the feeder adds 0x100 per blank at 60Hz and 0x133 per blank at 50Hz and the published counter is the accumulator >> 8, the published unit is 59.96 per second in both regions, i.e. a sixtieth of a second.

The demo object callback F0x80085590 loads SDIGDEMO.BIN (0x88d) when its +0x50 mode is nonzero (hole) and SSUBDEMO.BIN (0x88c) when zero (water) in phase 0 sub1 0, polls the load in sub1 1, then uploads sub-entry 1 and plays packed sound 0x00040003 DIG_DEMO (hole) or 0x00040018 SUB_DEMO (water) before incrementing to phase 1. Phase 1 is water-only and steps the 4-byte {s16 cell, s16 duration} table at 0x80096cc8 (158 frames, -1 = END -> setPhase 2); the shared tail is hole-only and steps two looping layers at 0x80096d14 and 0x80096d40 (-1 = LOOP to that record's duration field) until the elapsed accumulator +0x18 reaches 161 frames. Both forms render every cell full-screen at (0,0) over a 640x240 region from archive sub-entry 0, plus one unconditional static cell (hole cell 0, water cell 0xa). The particle object F0x80085bd4 runs four independent 8-byte channels {u32 active, u16 cursor, u16 timer} whose streams come from the pointer table 0x80096e84 indexed [mode][channel]; it draws FIELDCOM (archive 0x160) sub-entry 1 cells at the seeded screen position, uses 0xff as channel END and 0x12c as a hide-this-step sentinel, lives 168 frames, and is not in any teardown list so it keeps drawing over the demo. claims.statement: The per-frame channel program for a fight effect sprite is a bitmask-driven delta stream read by FIGHTSTG_F0x800893dc, the update function of the 0x90 sprite object that F0x8008966c allocates. On its first state the update walks a header off the stream pointer at +0x50: one halfword to +0x70, one to +0x74, one to +0x78, then nine consecutive halfwords into +0x7C upward. Thereafter each tick it indexes the stream at +0x50 by (frame counter +0x6C) times (+0x74) times two, and then tests +0x70 bit by bit, consuming one halfword from that row for each set bit and writing it to the matching one of the nine channels. So +0x70 is a nine-bit channel mask, +0x74 is the row stride in halfwords, the nine header halfwords are the channel defaults, and each row carries values only for the masked channels. This is the mechanism behind the extracted manifest's mask/stride/defaults/frames shape, and it settles where a sprite's SCALE comes from: channel 5 is the vertical scale, and an effect whose default scale is zero is expanded by later rows rather than being inert. Effect type 1007 is the worked example - mask 35 sets bits 0, 1 and 5, its stride is 3, and its rows raise channel 5 from 0 through 512, 1024, 1536 and upward.
claims.notes: The practical finding is that nothing was missing. The walker's EffectPlayer.step already applies mask-driven rows, so Blast's own effects animate correctly in real playback; they looked absent only because the verification harness seeks the presentation clock while effect instances advance on the wall clock, so a seek photographs them at whatever scale they had reached. tools/verify_blast.mjs now takes REALTIME=1 for that reason.
claims.coverage: The header parse and the per-tick masked update were read from the complete body of exe-decomp/fightstg_c/F0x800893dc.c; the object allocation and the fields it is handed were read from the F0x8008966c body in ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003/pro/fightstg.s, which is 40 instructions between its entry and its jr. The identification of channel 5 as vertical scale is CORROBORATION rather than direct proof: it rests on the extracted manifest agreeing with the assembly's shape and on type 1007's rows monotonically raising exactly the channel whose absence stopped the shipped renderer from drawing. claims.statement: In the player-side branch of the FIGHTSTG effective-stat builder F0x8009ec94 (fightstg.s, function head 0x8009ec94 at L29186; the non-zero-side branch at 0x8009f4a4 instead builds enemy stats from a 0x20-stride descriptor at 0x800a44d0), the battle effective-stat struct is filled from a 0x26-byte stat scratch block at sp+0x10 whose internal offsets match Unknown4Stats exactly (level at +0x00, cur_str at +0x0c, cur_fire at +0x18). Exactly 13 fields are consumed: the level halfword at block+0x00 into effective +0x00; a 5-iteration loop copying block+0x0c..+0x14 (cur_str, cur_def, cur_spt, cur_wis, cur_spd) into effective +0x02..+0x0a; and a 7-iteration loop whose source pointer restarts at block+0x18, copying cur_fire..cur_dark into effective +0x0c..+0x18. Each copied stat is floored at 1: a source halfword <= 0 stores the constant 1 instead. The two loops step over block+0x16 (cur_chr) without reading it, and the four HP/MP fields are likewise not copied (battle HP lives in the combatant record at +0x06/+0x08). PARTIAL: the identity of the shared helper (dispatch table 0x80048d34 + 0x2734) that fills the sp+0x10 scratch block was inferred from the exact offset correspondence with Unknown4Stats and was not itself disassembled; confirming it would raise this to a full read of the roster block.

The seven persistent elemental stats trace end to end. They are stored per roster Digimon as seven consecutive u16 fields from +0x34 of the Unknown4Stats block, written by the gym-training helper for effect ids 8 to 14 and clamped at 999, copied at battle init into the effective-stat struct at +0xc through +0x18 (the player branch clamps a non-positive value up to 1; the enemy branch instead copies twelve halfwords straight from the encounter descriptor at +0x18, covering the seven elements plus five status resistances with no clamp), and finally consumed in the damage stage F0x8009f6dc as a DIVISOR: when the attacker has an Elemental Power item equipped, the bonus is the running damage times the item magnitude, divided by the defender's own value for that element. Training a Digimon's elemental stats therefore makes it more resistant specifically to enemy Elemental Power accessory damage of that element.
claims.notes: IMPORTANT BOUNDARY: this trainable seven-element block is NOT the general type/weakness system. Ordinary attack matching runs through a separate, non-trainable species-family byte - skill+0x9 compared against defender effective +0x25 for a flat 1.5x, plus a +0x26 affinity scaling term - which does not read Unknown4Stats at all. UNKNOWNS: the roster-storage and training-writer legs are authority 4/5 and were not re-disassembled in this pass, and the species/roster lookup that fills the init source buffer was not proven byte-exact to read +0x34..+0x40. Separately open and NOT part of this chain: nothing was found that STORES a nonzero value to combatant record +0x1b, the effectiveness flag that doubles crit and some elemental damage - a corpus-wide scan of that offset pattern found only reads and zero-clears.

claims.statement: The shape of the encounter step-counter reload distribution is derived from the reload site, not from samples. F0x8009252c computes r = rand() mod 2304 (exact magic division by 0x38e38e39 with an mfhi>>9) and applies the deterministic fold c = r for r <= 255, c = (r + 256) >> 1 otherwise. The fold is exactly 2-to-1 on its upper leg: the 2048 residues 256..2303 map onto the 1024 outputs 256..1279 with exactly two preimages each, while the 256 residues 0..255 map one-to-one. So the reload is a two-step piecewise-uniform distribution on 0..1279 in which every value from 256 up is exactly twice as likely as every value below 256. Taking rand() uniform on the modulus, P(counter <= 255) = 1/9 exactly, mean = 696 + 7/18, median = 703, sd = 344.6; taking the conventional 15-bit generator instead, the modulo bias gives P(counter <= 255) = 11.72 percent, mean = 689 exactly and median 694 -- the same shape, a shift of about 7. Combined with the already-verified 8-tick beat and the rate tiers 3/4/6/9/18, the mean walking distance between rolls that expire is about 1861, 1397, 933, 623 and 314 movement ticks. Within every address form a text matcher can decide, this is the only reload: the reload function has exactly one caller (the driver's expiry path), its function-pointer cell is never loaded indirectly, and the counter has exactly three stores corpus-wide. Static only, and one input is unproven -- see the limitation on rand().
claims.notes: This addresses the frontier's 'SHAPE of the counter reset distribution (two samples only)' residue and replaces the sampling framing entirely: the two runtime samples 17 and 826 are consistent with the fold but were never capable of distinguishing the two candidate PMFs, whereas the fold determines the shape outright. The one residual input is the output distribution of the resident rand() at [0x8004dc0c], which is not a shape question about the encounter code. In player terms: about one reload in nine lands in the fast lower fifth of the range, so back-to-back encounters are an ordinary, roughly 11 percent event rather than a bug; and expiry is 'not greater than zero', so a large rate can overshoot without wasting the overshoot, because the reload is unconditional. Reinforces encounter-step-counter and encounter-rate-runtime-confirmed; supersedes and contradicts nothing, so no companion 'contradicted' entry is required.

claims.statement: A controlled runtime walk confirms the step-counter model end to end: the counter at 0x80048d64 does not change while the player is given no input, drops once per 8 frames of continuous movement, drops by exactly one of the two rates the stage's two walkable zone levels select -- 6 for level 3 and 3 for level 1, with no other value in 380 of 380 observations -- and on reaching a non-positive value launches a battle and reloads to a value inside the decoded 0..1279 reset domain.

Only rate levels 1 and 3 were exercised. That is not treated as a gap for levels 2, 4 and 5: the driver performs a single indexed load from one six-word array whose contents were read from live RAM in the same session (EV-encounter-live-ram-s330-2026-07-26) and whose indexing is established in assembly, and two different indices of it were observed firing correctly here. Two reset samples are far too few to test the shape of the reset distribution -- they show only that both branches of the fold are reachable and land in range. Three inter-drop gaps of 4 frames occurred at direction changes and are unexplained; the 6-frame gaps in the first run track the script's own burst input pattern, not the game. The period is measured in GPU vsync frames, which matched the decoded 8 movement ticks one-for-one under a continuously held direction but was not separately instrumented.

claims.statement: The field random-encounter driver F0x80092664 runs once per 8 field ticks of player movement (F0x8008fd74 calls it when moving and actor->+0x18 & 7 == 0, and only when its a2 argument is nonzero; +0x18 increments on every call, idle included). claims.statement: A live field frame confirms the decoded encounter data model: the rate table at 0x8009b6ac holds 2000/3/4/6/9/18 in RAM, the zonemgr word at 0x8009b6c4+0x10 that the driver gates on is populated (0x01b50003), +0x40 and +0x44 hold 0x800928cc and the zone lookup F0x80092914, the scene word at 0x80099da0 (scene+0x20) addresses a positional zone-pointer array, and each zone block is a nine-word header {u32 rate_level; record *slot[8]} over 0xc-byte records; on that frame the array's first four entries are blocks with rate levels [3,1,0,0] whose third block's eight record pointers all resolve to records with screen id 0, so an all-empty block still occupies a zone number in the array.
claims.notes: Single frame, single stage: it fixes values and layout but observes no motion, so the 8-tick driver period, the per-run decrement and the counter reset distribution are untested. The stage is identified as s330 by matching the live pools against the extracted stage table (authority 4), not from the capture alone; nothing in the claim depends on that name. 0x800928cc is given as an address only -- its role is not shown by this packet. That the pointer-array order is the engine's zone order is shown only here, where four blocks and four pointers coincide; overlays carrying several groups of four blocks (s335 has twelve) may expose only one group through the scene array, so the flat overlay order is not established as the zone order for them. Consequence for tooling, not part of the claim: tools/extract_stage_encounters.py previously dropped all-empty blocks, which renumbered every later block relative to the engine's zone-1 index; it now keeps them. The savestate was read offline; no emulator ran.

claims.statement: The record whose two adjacent u16 fields become the family-B encounter zone-group key pair at 0x80048d78/0x80048d7a is, at BOTH writer sites, the same type-7 step record the field trigger dispatcher selects from the tile the player walked onto: record = [ctrl+0x54] + (trigger_byte & 0x1f) * 0x18, stashed at ctrl+0x64 (fieldstg .L0x00005638-.L0x00005644). Site A (script-VM opcode 1) reads record+0x14 and record+0x16 directly. Site B's previously untraced pointer [$s4+0x7c] is that same record plus 0xa -- the address of the record's parameter array -- so its reads at rec+0xa and rec+0xc are record+0x14 and record+0x16, the identical two fields. The pointer arrives there through one chain, established instruction by instruction: script-VM opcodes 9 and 10 converge at RAM 0x80088860 and call the field character's secondary vtable slot +0x124 (installed as 0x8008f3e4 at fieldstg .L0x0000e544-.L0x0000e54c) with a1 = record+0xa and a mode argument that is the ONLY difference between the two opcodes -- 0 for opcode 10, 1 for opcode 9; F0x8008f3e4 sets the character to state 1, raises [0x80099dd8], and calls F0x8008c078, which fetches the resident type-7 transition entity and stores mode at obj+0x70, the character's live x/y at obj+0x74/+0x78 and record+0xa at obj+0x7c, then drives that entity into state 3; F0x8008aa10 is that entity's handler and reads obj+0x7c as $s4+0x7c. Therefore site B is not an independent writer and the two sites cannot disagree. Static only: no runtime capture was taken, so this is at most partially_verified.
claims.notes: This claim adds to, and contradicts nothing in, the existing ledger, so no companion 'contradicted' entry is required. It re-derives independently at authority 2, with exact line numbers, the chain already recorded as a correction note on the route-pair claims, and adds two facts not previously recorded: (a) the opcode 9 versus opcode 10 discriminator is a single argument, 0 for opcode 10 and 1 for opcode 9, latched at transition-object +0x70, which is the natural place to look for the difference between a surface entry warp and a maze self-warp; (b) obj+0x74/+0x78 capture the character's coordinates at the instant of the transition. It also removes the last hedge in the encounter doc's 'Still not established' box -- 'Site B's [$s4+0x7c] provenance is still untraced' -- which is prose rather than a ledger claim and should be struck at integration. It reinforces encounter-zone-group-key-written-on-map-transition, route-pair-clears-on-unkeyed-warp and encounter-companion-scalar-is-second-route-coordinate.

claims.statement: The route pair's value domain is fixed by its only predicate consumer, F0x800160a8 (exe/fns.s L6679-6705). Both cells are read as unsigned 16-bit. For bank-0x7E index < 0x1e the predicate is [0x80048d78] == index + 1, so the key is addressable only for values 1..30; for index >= 0x1e it is [0x80048d7a] == index - 0x1d, so the companion is addressable for values 1..0x1e2 given the dispatcher's 0x1ff index mask. The value 0 is addressed by no index on either cell, which is what makes the unconditional store of a (0,0) record a genuine clear: every bank-0x7E equality predicate becomes false. The argument a1 is pure polarity, selecting the equality or the inequality test, not a value. Every group key and entry-warp key so far extracted from the shipped family-B stages lies inside 1..30, so nothing in the shipped data needs a key this reader cannot express. Static only.
claims.notes: The code-side bound (key 1..30, companion up to 0x1e2) is authority 2 and is what a port must implement. The tighter data-side bound already in the ledger (shipped ids 0x7E00-0x7E25 = 30 key slots plus 8 companion slots) is authority 4 and is a statement about the shipped content, not about the engine; the two should be kept distinct rather than merged. Reinforces route-pair-gates-family-b-npc-spawns; supersedes and contradicts nothing, so no companion 'contradicted' entry is required.

claims.statement: The family-B encounter zone-group key at 0x80048d78, and its companion u16 at 0x80048d7a, ARE written by the original code, at exactly two sites, both in pro/fieldstg.s and both on a map-transition path. This supersedes and CONTRADICTS encounter-zone-group-runtime-key-writer-unresolved, whose 'nothing in the original corpus writes it' rested on matchers that could not see the store: both sites materialize the address as base 0x80048d34 (lui 0x8005 / addiu -0x72cc) plus offset 0x44 and 0x46, so the literal strings '80048d78', '0x7288' and '0x8d78' do not occur at the store at all. The two scalars are always written together as a pair, from two adjacent u16 fields of a transition record. Site A is the opcode-1 case of the field script command VM F0x800885d4 (opcode at cmd+0x8, 14-entry jump table at RAM 0x80082e98), storing cmd+0x14 and cmd+0x16 at the case's unconditional convergence point RAM 0x800886b8-0x800886dc. Site B is the field screen handler F0x8008aa10 (prologue at fieldstg file 0x7d60), storing rec+0xa and rec+0xc where rec = [$s4+0x7c] is a record whose first three halfwords are a coordinate triple passed to the following call with $a1 = -1. Corpus completeness for halfword stores at these two offsets: code-search 'sh \$[a-z0-9]+, 0x44\(' --regex returns 5 hits of 590,078 lines scanned (3 are $sp stack stores) and 'sh \$[a-z0-9]+, 0x46\(' --regex returns 2 hits of 590,078 lines scanned, the same two sites. Authority 2, original assembly. SEMANTICS ESTABLISHED 2026-07-27 (evidence EV-encounter-zone-group-key-is-entry-warp-2026-07-27, authority 4): the value written is the ENTRY WARP'S OWN PARAMETER. The step record holds op at +0x8 and params[i] at 0xa+2i, so params[5] is exactly the +0x14 field site A stores into 0x80048d78 and params[6] the +0x16 field it stores into 0x80048d7a. Across the shipped step data all 26 op=10 warps target a stage with more than one selector group and none targets a stage without one; for all 5 family-B stages reachable this way the entry keys are a subset of the destination's own group keys (s825 [2,7,17] of [1,2,7,8,11,12,17,18]; s830 [2,12] of [2,12]; s835 [4,5,15] of [...]; s840 [3,4] of [...]; s850 [1,4,11,14] of [1,4,11,14]), and within each destination every entrance carries a DIFFERENT key. So the map's monster pool is selected by which entrance was used: entering the Seabed s825 from s320 sets key 2 and from s525 sets key 7, same destination and same spawn point.
claims.notes: CORRECTION TO THIS CLAIM'S OWN REASONING 2026-07-27 (evidence EV-route-pair-writers-exhaustive-ea-scan-2026-07-27). This claim previously argued that 'the two writers agreeing on the same logical fields is an internal consistency check neither provides alone.' That is WRONG and is withdrawn. Site B is not an independent writer: ops 9/10 pass cmd+0xa to the field-character vtable slot +0x124, which reaches F0x8008f3e4 -> the transition-screen constructor F0x8008c078, which stores that same pointer at obj+0x7c. So [$s4+0x7c] == cmd+0xa by construction and the two sites are two arms of ONE mechanism reading one record. Their agreement is definitional, not corroboration, and no independent confirmation should be inferred from it. The open 'identity of the record at [$s4+0x7c]' question is however now CLOSED by that same chain. WRITER SET NOW MATCHER-INDEPENDENT: a constant-propagating effective-address scan over all 345 .s files (595,489 lines) resolving every sb/sh/sw/swl/swr against any base and offset finds exactly these two site pairs and nothing else, so the earlier text-matcher negatives are corroborated by a method that does not depend on how the address is spelled. FULL MECHANISM: route_pair := ([scene_struct+0x14])[grid_byte & 0x1f].params[5..6], written when the selected record's op is 1, 9 or 10; the dispatcher indexes the scene+0x14 table by the low 5 bits of the type-7 grid byte at the player tile, stride 0x18. CENSUS CORRECTED: op 1 ALSO carries a nonzero key in four records (s630/s631/s645/s646, the Mobius Desert entries into s635/s636), so the earlier 'only op 9/10' framing was wrong; params[0] is a screen id, not a stage id; and s825/s830/s835/s840/s850 carry zero bank-0x7E NPCs, so on those the pair drives encounters only. WALKER FIXED accordingly: tools/gen_scenes.py now emits entryKey for op 1, 9 and 10 rather than 9 and 10 only, which recovers the four dropped Mobius Desert keys. CORPUS CORRECTION 2026-07-27 (evidence EV-entry-key-corpus-corrected-2026-07-27). After extract_story_steps.py gained scene+0x14 coverage (98 -> 287 stages) the keyed-warp corpus grew from 42 to 157 and TWO recorded properties changed. The core property SURVIVES and is unchanged: every keyed warp into a stage with more than one selector group carries a key belonging to that stage's own group keys, 152 of 152. FALSIFIED: 'within one destination every entrance carries a DIFFERENT key', which this claim previously called the substantive property. It is false on the fuller corpus -- s850 is entered with key 1 from both s330 and s450, s865 with key 7 from both s396 and s695. The key identifies the maze SECTION, not the door uniquely; several surface doors can deliver the player to the same section. The property that actually holds, and that makes group selection observable, is that a destination is reached under more than one key. WEAKENED: 'all keyed warps target a multi-group stage, none otherwise' becomes 152 of 157, the five exceptions targeting s961/s962/s965 which carry at most one group. The earlier 26 and 42 counts were artifacts of step-program coverage, not facts about the game. None of this disturbs the decode or the walker: the key still selects the group by matching a record's key word, and the wiring is unchanged. PROMOTED to partially_verified 2026-07-27 on two independent lines: the store sites and record layout from original assembly (authority 2) and the key correspondence from the shipped extracted tables (authority 4), which agree on the same offset without being derived from each other. STILL NOT ESTABLISHED: the meaning of the companion scalar at 0x80048d7a (params[6]); it is written by the same two sites and read by F0x800160a8 for predicate index >= 0x1e, but nothing here explains what it selects. No runtime observation has been taken -- the correspondence is static, so it shows the fields line up and the keys match, not that the game was watched doing it. Site B's [$s4+0x7c] provenance is RESOLVED 2026-07-27 (evidence EV-encounter-entry-key-op9-op10-path-2026-07-27): it is the op=9/op=10 params pointer (cmd+0xa) handed to the field-character vtable slot +0x124, so site B's rec+0xa/rec+0xc are params[5]/params[6] -- the same two fields the opcode-1 case writes as cmd+0x14/cmd+0x16, reached from a different base. The two writers agreeing on the same logical fields is an internal consistency check neither provides alone. The key-carrying ops are op=9 (16 records) and op=10 (26 records), 42 of 42 with a nonzero params[5]; the earlier '26 of 26' counted op=10 only. Exact evidence to reach verified: read [0x80048d78] at runtime entering one Seabed map through two different doors and confirm it takes the two predicted key values. WALKER: engine/dw3/encounters.ts still ignores the key and pins every family-B stage to record 0; story_steps.json ALREADY carries params[5], so wiring this needs no re-extraction, only engine plumbing of an entry-key through the warp. WALKER: WIRED 2026-07-27. engine/dw3/encounters.ts encounterGroupIndex/stageZoneBlocks/pickEncounter take an optional entryKey and match it against the runtime_key groups' key word, falling back to group 0 when absent or unmatched; tools/gen_scenes.py emits entryKey on op=9/op=10 exits; web/game.js latches state.entryKey on the map change; web/battle.js passes it into pickEncounter and zoneRateLevel. Verified end to end headless (tools/verify_entry_key.mjs, npm run verify:entry-key): in the real page, s825 with entryKey 2 yields screen 62 at rate 4, entryKey 7 yields screen 61 at rate 4, entryKey 11 yields screen 103 at rate 2, and entryKey 0 falls back to the group-0 mix of 61/62 at rate 2. That is browser evidence for the WALKER's plumbing only; it is not evidence about the original game and does not raise this claim's status. WITHDRAWN 2026-07-27 (evidence EV-route-pair-deep-maps-static-tables-complete-2026-07-27): the note added earlier today that the deep maze maps are 'runtime-only' and need 'one legitimate in-game transition with those two halfwords dumped' is retracted. It rested on the 2026-07-09 rig harvest of s845's live table, which the 2026-07-10 ordinal-45 re-harvest in docs/todo/2026-07-09-self-warp-maze-wiring.md had already superseded and whose patching hypothesis it explicitly falsifies; a base-register-checked static read of scene+0x14 across all 294 overlays reproduces those live tables record-for-record, including the s885 screen the 2026-07-09 pass failed to capture. The tables are static and complete. The open question is narrower and is NOT runtime-only: what sets a nonzero route pair on screens 746-750. AMENDED 2026-10-03: the pair's only consumers are the destination stage's encounter-selector init (key half) and the bank-0x7E NPC spawn gates (both halves); it is NOT an item marker and F0x800161d8 never touches either half (claim item-store-gap6-new-item-marker-refuted-2026-10-03). Both writer sites store BOTH halves - the earlier single-store-per-site reading left +0x46 looking unwritten.

claims.statement: The family-B (runtime_key) encounter zone-group selector reads a u16 at 0x80048d78, and NOTHING in the original corpus writes it. dw3-research code-search "80048d78" over the original assembly reports 3 hits of 590,078 lines scanned, all three in ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003/exe/fns.s and all three inside F0x800160a8 (fns.s L6679-6700): one lui %hi and two lhu %lo reads, no store. 0x80048d78 is the bank-0x7E scalar: the bank dispatcher F0x800163b0 routes bank 0x7E to F0x800160a8 (fns.s .L0x8001654c bne $v1,$v0 with $v0 = 0x7e, fall-through .L0x80016558 jal F0x800160a8, $v1 = (id >> 8) & 0xfe), and F0x800160a8 compares 0x80048d78 for predicate index < 0x1e (slti $v0,$a2,0x1e) and 0x80048d7a at or above it. Thirty wstag overlays read it directly in their stage-init (dw3-research code-search "lhu \\$a1, \\-0x7288\\(" --regex: 30 hits of 590,078 lines scanned, in wstag825/830/835/840/845/850/855/860/865/870/875/880/885/890/895 and wstag960-974); 27 of those stages carry more than one selector record and therefore actually branch on it. The producer of the value is therefore UNIDENTIFIED and family-B group selection is unresolved; the extractor records the family, the key address and each group key, and consumers fall back to the first record. TOOLING TRAP, recorded so the null is not mistaken for evidence: dw3-research references D0x80048d78 and dw3-research references 0x80048d78 both answer "function not found", and tools/overlay_scan.py refs pairs only lui+addiu and never lui+lhu, so neither tool can see these reads at all. Authority 2, original assembly.
claims.notes: CONTRADICTED 2026-07-27 by encounter-zone-group-key-written-on-map-transition (evidence EV-encounter-zone-group-key-writer-found-2026-07-27, authority 2). The central assertion of this claim -- that nothing in the original corpus writes 0x80048d78 -- is FALSE. Two sites write it, both in pro/fieldstg.s, and every matcher used here was structurally blind to them because the store materializes the address as base 0x80048d34 plus offset 0x44 rather than as a %hi/%lo symbol pair or a -0x7288 offset. This is the third consecutive negative on this address to be produced by an address-materialization assumption rather than by the code. The reader-side content of this claim (the 30 wstag readers, the bank-0x7E routing, the second scalar at 0x80048d7a, the references/overlay_scan tooling trap) remains accurate and is carried forward by the superseding claim. SEARCH-PATH NARROWING 2026-07-27 (evidence EV-encounter-bank-7e-is-read-only-2026-07-27, authority 2): one of the two proposed next steps is now FALSIFIED. The flag system has a read dispatcher (F0x800163b0) and a separate write dispatcher (chain at 0x80016734-0x80016848); bank 0x7E is routed on the read chain only and is absent from the write chain, alongside bank 0x72. There is therefore NO write-side counterpart of the flag dispatcher for this bank, and looking for one is wasted effort -- 0x80048d78 is not written through the flag API at all. Two search paths remain, both still open: (a) a store computed through a register-held base rather than a %hi/%lo symbol pair or the -0x7288 offset form, which every text matcher used so far is structurally blind to (the three forms together give 50 hits and 0 stores of 590078 lines scanned), the most likely shape being a bulk save-restore copy over the 0x80048xxx global block; and (b) the runtime read below. RECOMMENDED next step is now (b), the runtime observation, since it does not depend on guessing the store's addressing mode. PLAYER IMPACT (corrected 2026-07-27): this is not a latent gap. 12 of the 27 family-B stages are wired and reachable in ordinary play, and all 12 have groups whose pools and/or rate_level genuinely differ, so until the key's writer is identified those 12 stages show record-0 encounters that the original would not necessarily show. What the correct pools ARE cannot be stated until the key is decoded. Exact evidence needed to close: the write site of the u16 at 0x80048d78, or a runtime read of it across a Seabed/Circuit self-warp transition showing what it tracks. A value held in a binary data section not rendered as text in the .s files, or a store computed through a register base rather than a %hi/%lo symbol pair, would still be invisible to the text matcher used here.

claims.statement: The field screen zeroes the encounter zone-map handle on every entry, so a stage that does not register its own type-4 map rolls no random encounters. F0x8008aa10 (fieldstg file 0x7d60) is the field screen handler; it dispatches on self->+0xc (phase) and, in phase 0, on self->+0x10 (sub-state) through the 5-entry jump table at 0x80082ef0. Sub-state 0 clears the frame and then calls set_resource(4, 0) at RAM 0x8008ac38 (file 0x7f8c) via the zonemgr method cell 0x8009b704, storing 0 into zonemgr+0x10; the [0x8004b40c] guard above it skips only the preceding free_resource(4), never the clear. Sub-state 0 is the sub-state that runs on entry: the screen object is constructed fresh per entry (fieldstg file 0x489c -> F0x8008b6a4 -> exe F0x800143dc), and the allocator it uses, F0x80017f54 via the statically initialized cell D0x8004b5fc, bzeroes the whole 0x80-byte object, so +0xc and +0x10 are both 0. Sub-state 1 is what requests the incoming map's archive, so the clear strictly precedes the new wstag overlay's own set_resource calls. Because the driver F0x80092664's module gate returns when zonemgr[4] is 0, the 52 stages that carry encounter blocks but register no type-4 map roll nothing at all: they neither inherit the previous stage's zone map nor depend on entry order.
claims.notes: Supersedes the contradicted encounter-engine-overlay-residency, whose reserved 'clear through a pointer loaded from data' scope hole is exactly this site (it materializes the method cell 0x8009b704, never the struct base 0x8009b6c4). Corroborated three ways: (1) the s330 live capture shows a POPULATED zonemgr[4], which requires the clear to run before the wstag init rather than after, i.e. the decoded sub-state order is the order that actually executes; (2) all 52 gridless stages have every populated pool at rate level 0, the never-walkable sentinel, at zone 4; (3) no extracted grid returns a zone above 3, so those zone-4 pools are unreachable except through the scripted path F0x800927a0. Not established here: that sub-states 2-4 are where the wstag init's own set_resource calls land -- only that sub-state 1 issues the archive request and so follows the clear. Scope on the census: it rests on extract_zone_grids.py's instruction matcher not producing false negatives, and the two committed matchers already disagree (extract_zone_resource_ids.py finds 135 registrations, extract_zone_grids.py 151), so a missed registration is a demonstrated failure mode, not a hypothetical. What contains it is that a stage misfiled into the 52 would need a walkable block -- a non-empty pool at a non-zero rate level -- to have random encounters at all, and none of the 52 has one.

claims.statement: stdwtitl's top-level screen dispatcher F0x80082ec8 selects the END card from the launch mode byte: it reads `[0x8004B438] & 0xFF` and, when that byte is 13, creates the END screen object through F0x80082e9c (a 0x50-byte object whose handler is F0x80082d70), which loads the end__all pack and calls F0x8008483c to allocate the END sequence object 0x80084628 (0x54 bytes). The developer stage-select table's launch code 0x0e0d (STENDS) is overlay STDWTITL entered with mode 13.
claims.notes: Authority 2 for the dispatcher and the two allocators (raw stdwtitl.s; the allocators are F0x80082e9c = F0x80014504(0x80082D70,0x50,4) and F0x8008483c = F0x80014504(0x80084628,0x54,0)). NEGATIVE, and the reason the walker's END card stays lab-only: a scan of all 294 pro overlays and the exe (matcher: literal '0e0d', '0E0D', '3597', '0x0e0d', '0x0e00' in every ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003/{pro,exe}/*.s line; plus the resident launcher [0x8004B440] call sites, which pass a0 from constants or record fields) found NO caller passing 0x0e0d; the only one is the developer stagslct table row (docs/research/ui/stagslct-full-decode-2026-08-05.md), which the plan treats as not_applicable. The converted story content's HANDOFF ids top out at 0x0E09 (3587-3593), so no converted event launches it either. What WOULD settle a retail producer: a caller of [0x8004B440] with a0 == 0x0e0d, or a reads of [0x8004B438] written to 13 by a non-developer path; neither was found.

claims.statement: The accessory table is right and the 'flat weapon-power/armour pool' reading is wrong: the dispute is settled, not open. The initialiser F0x8009ec94 adds the weapon record's +0x0E byte into effective +0x3A (fightstg.s:29428-29432) and the armour record's +0x10 byte into effective +0x3B (fightstg.s:29447-29450), and the accessory ladder then accumulates Glasses/Goggles (331/332) magnitude into +0x3A, DanceFeather/Wing (333/334) into +0x3B, and OVERWRITES +0x3C with RunnerSandal/Shoes (335/336) (fightstg.s:29637-29642, :29653-29658, :29670-29672). Those bytes are read by the accuracy/evade pools, not by power or armour: the physical hit roll F0x800a06ac adds +0x3A to the attacker's term and subtracts +0x3B from the defender's (fightstg.s:30947-30949, :30992-30994), and the escape roll adds +0x3C (fightstg.s:31988-31990, addu into the escape score). claims.statement: The three tables FIGHTSTG_F0x80089be4 is handed for the transformation effects are 8-byte spawn POSITION records, not channel programs. Read as four s16 fields the three records in fightstg.s L60-L64 are: 0x80082DC8 = 0x00000000 0x00007fff = (0, 0, 32767); 0x80082DD0 = 0x007800a0 0x00007fff = (160, 120, 32767); 0x80082DD8 = 0xff88ff60 0x0000ffff = (-160, -120, -1). So each transformation effect has a decoded spawn point: 0x3E8, 0x3E9 and 0x3EF use the origin record, 0x3EA the centre record, and 0x3EB and 0x3F0 the negative-centre record.

claims.statement: When ordinary directional movement ends from action mode 3, SLES-03936 changes the player and moving party followers to action mode 4. claims.statement: Each of the three field-party Digimon independently copies the player’s exact historical fixed-point x, y, and facing from a 64-record ring buffer. The write cursor advances modulo 64 while follower read cursors initialize to 55, 46, and 37 against write cursor 0, producing exact lags of 9, 18, and 27 native field ticks. The followers do not steer toward, interpolate to, or use catch-up speed against those samples.

claims.statement: In SLES-03936 fieldstg, ordinary directional input with actor+0xbc clear selects player action mode 3; that mode latches animation clip 5 and advances the actor by the full PAL 24.8 fixed-point magnitude 0x4cc once per 50 Hz PAL field/vsync tick, yielding 4.796875 map pixels per tick (239.84375 px/s). Clip 5 is the sprite-directory run cycle; clip 4 is the reduced-speed walk mode. Native clip durations advance in those PAL ticks and the loader resets its timer on clip changes. There is no separate player-input run-speed modifier.
