claims.statement: A party follower can never be denied a drop shadow. The value plumbed into the field-entity constructor's kind argument for a follower comes from F0x80016fd8, which returns the fixed roster-slot ordinal 0-7 rather than the follower's live species or form id, so the kind is always 3..10. The six-value shadow denylist (130, 131, 213, 287, 316, 319) is therefore reachable only through the npc_id path, and every party member always has a shadow no matter what it digivolves into.
claims.notes: Supersedes the refuted candidate shadow-denylist-includes-aquatic-partner-forms. The roster slot is fixed at starter-pack selection and never changes on digivolution, which is what makes the denial unreachable for followers. Cross-checked: an unrelated DRI/gym caller treats the same ctx+0x2728 return as a small index into a 7-8 entry table, consistent with a roster ordinal and not with a ~250-entry species space.

claims.statement: The field drop shadow does not scale with the actor and is not attached to the actor's feet in the air: its width and height are the constants 32 and 16, and its screen position is x = actorScreenX - 16, y = actorGroundScreenY + ((entity+0x90) >> 8) - 8, where actorGroundScreenY is recovered by re-adding the actor height (entity+0x64 >> 8) that was subtracted for the billboard. The 32x16 rect is therefore centred horizontally on the actor's world X and vertically on the actor's ground row plus the 8.8 fixed-point offset entity+0x90, so a jumping or floating actor keeps its shadow on the ground. entity+0x90 is written by the entity move methods +0x114 (0x8008f128, sets 0), +0x118 (0x8008f1d4) and +0x11c (0x8008f280) as the move's target Z shifted left by 8.
claims.notes: Geometry read directly from the stores; no multiply by any per-actor scale exists on this path. Runtime cross-check: the measured ellipse (semi-axes ~12.5x5 px) is identical in size across all five captures. Not verified: whether anything outside those three move methods writes entity+0x90 (e.g. per-frame terrain height) - see SHDW-Q003 in the canonical doc section 7.

claims.statement: entity+0x90 (the signed 8.8 shadow ground offset) is written outside the three originally-documented move methods (+0x114/+0x118/+0x11c): inside the move dispatcher F0x8008fed0's clip-0x17 branch (fieldstg.s file 0xdbc8-0xdbe4), entity+0x90 -= 0x300 (8.8 fixed point) is stored in the delay slot of a bne and therefore executes UNCONDITIONALLY every time this code path runs. entity+0xa0==0x17 does NOT gate the decrement itself -- it gates the block immediately after it (file 0xdbe8-0xdc04), a threshold test of entity+0x94 against the new offset that transitions the entity to clip 0x18 once crossed. The same decrement block is also reached directly (skipping the clip-0x17 entry calls) from a different entity+0x14 sub-phase value, consistent with the write recurring across multiple consecutive frames of a single clip-0x17 episode by a fixed per-frame decrement, not a one-time correction. SHDW-Q003 is therefore REOPENED, not reinforced: this is evidence toward the continuous/per-frame side of the original either/or question, though it is a scripted fixed-rate ramp, not terrain-geometry sampling, so 'follows per-frame terrain height' specifically remains unconfirmed.
claims.notes: Corrects a 2026-07-27 misreading that had the decrement itself gated on entity+0xa0==0x17 and concluded it 'reinforced' the discrete-state-change reading; re-derivation of file 0xdbc8-0xdc08 (delay-slot analysis) shows the opposite. Whether the per-frame field collision/terrain-height update code separately writes +0x90, and whether entity+0x14 auto-increments frame-to-frame during this state, remain unresolved -- neither was traced this session (scope: F0x8009116c and F0x8008fed0 only, both in fieldstg.s).

claims.statement: The entity move/animation dispatcher F0x8008fed0 (dispatched via entity+0x10 jump table, base 0x80083590) re-toggles entity+0x74 as part of several of its per-mode branches: transitions into clip 1 (idle), 4 (walk) or 5 (run) set it to 1 (shadow ON); transitions into clip 0x1d, 0x1e or 0x16 set it to 0 (shadow OFF); two further unconditional stores restore it to 1 at the end of the clip-0x1e completion branch and inside the clip-0x17 entry block. The shadow gate is therefore not a static per-entity-class property but an actively re-driven per-frame-dispatch state. F0x8008fed0 has exactly one direct caller in fieldstg.s (file 0xe3d0, RAM 0x80091080), inside a generic per-entity per-frame update routine that calls it for any entity unless a per-entity script override at entity+0x108 intervenes -- this is broader than 'player only' but was not independently confirmed to run for every NPC.
claims.notes: All 11 confirmed toggle sites in F0x8008fed0 are now cited with exact attribution (9 delay-slot-exact + 2 unconditional-but-traced). The earlier 'entity+0x40 method resolves to this dispatcher' hedge was wrong -- entity+0x40 is a callee F0x8008fed0 itself invokes, not a pointer to F0x8008fed0 -- and has been replaced with the actual routing evidence (the single jal call site and its entity+0x108 override check). Whether every NPC's update path reaches that call site (vs. always taking the entity+0x108 override) was not traced this session.

claims.statement: REFUTED 2026-07-27. The field character drop shadow texture IS inside FIELDCOM.BIN: it is the 32x16 4-bpp rect at atlas-local texels u=112..143, v=166..181 of FIELDCOM sub-entry 2, with its own 16-entry CLUT at atlas halfword (48,254). The earlier elimination scanned the decoded sprite sheet web/assets/ui/fieldcom0.png, which contains only the texels reachable through the FIELDCOM sprite directory; no dir0 clip frame overlaps the shadow rect and no dir0 frame ever selects CLUT column 48 on atlas row 254, so neither the shadow pixels nor its colour can appear in that sheet. The shadow is addressed only through the FIELDSTG texture-slot descriptor at 0x80097d0c, whose tpage origin (512,256) names the resident VRAM corner of sub-entry 2. Superseded by claim field-shadow-texture-source-fieldcom-sub2. The character-sprite-pack half of the original statement was NOT refuted and is carried forward as its own live claim field-shadow-not-in-character-sprite-packs.

Root cause of the bad elimination: fieldcom0.png is a directory-driven sheet, not the whole atlas, so absence from it is not absence from FIELDCOM.BIN. Treat other elimination claims built on decoded sheets rather than raw atlases with the same suspicion.

claims.statement: The drop-shadow texture is not part of any character field-sprite pack. In the 146-frame player pack ~/ddw3/tim/dw2003/field/sprite/p001play the only frame sizes present are 24x32 (133), 32x24 (6), 24x24 (4) and 32x32 (3) - none is the shadow's 32x16 - and the shadow colour RGB(0x30,0x30,0x38) occurs in none of the 146 frames nor anywhere in the built clip sheet web/assets/sprites/clips/p001play.png. This is consistent with the decoded draw path, in which the shadow SPRT takes its u/v/CLUT from texture-slot record 0 of the array at scene_struct+0x28 rather than from the actor's own frame slot at entity+0x6c, and with the positive identification of the texture in FIELDCOM sub-entry 2 (claim field-shadow-texture-source-fieldcom-sub2).
claims.notes: Carried forward from the character-sprite-pack half of the now-contradicted claim field-shadow-not-a-fieldcom-or-sprite-pack-asset, and re-measured from the extracted pack this session rather than inherited on trust. claims.statement: The field character drop shadow is a fixed 32x16 4-bpp textured SPRT (psyq len=4, GP0 code 0x64: variable-size textured rectangle, texture-blending, ABE=0 so fully opaque with no ABR mode applied) drawn with the neutral colour 0x80,0x80,0x80. It is emitted per actor by the FIELDSTG field-actor renderer F0x8008f52c (file 0xc87c) at RAM 0x8008f874-0x8008f92c, immediately after that actor's POLY_FT4 billboard (code 0x2c), linked into the ordering table at bucket entity+0x78 plus 1 so it draws behind the actor, and gated on entity+0x74 being non-zero. Its u0/v0/CLUT come from texture-slot record 0 of the array at 0x80097d0c (scene_struct+0x28), and its tpage from GetTPage(tp=0, abr=0, s16[slot+0], s16[slot+2]) via F0x800290ac fed to SetDrawTPage F0x8002915c, so the texture is 4 bits per pixel.
claims.notes: Static evidence: original assembly of fieldstg.s read via tools/overlay_scan.py under the mandated 1-core/4GiB cap; EXE helpers checked against fns.s:27476 (GetTPage byte-for-byte psyq formula) and exe-decomp/c/F0x8002915c.c (SetDrawTPage, GP0 0xE1). Cross-checked against 5 authority-1 rig captures whose shadow pixels are a single constant colour over patterned floor art, independently confirming ABE=0. Not verified: no runtime capture of the primitive words; the resource filling texture slot 0 is unidentified (SHDW-Q001) and the producers of entity+0x74 are unidentified (SHDW-Q002). Doc: docs/research/field/character-drop-shadow-decoded-2026-07-27.md
claims.frontier_rationale: Decodes the shadow's SPRT draw primitive, OT bucket ordering, and texture-slot/tpage mechanics - closed SHDW-Q001 territory; it only flags SHDW-Q002 as a separate open unknown, it does not answer it.

claims.statement: A distinct controller-style object at fieldstg.s RAM 0x8008c598/0x8008c5c8 holds a pointer to another entity at controller+0x50 and, in two of its own state-transition branches, unconditionally clears that entity's shadow (entity+0x74=0) and restores it to a caller-supplied value in a different branch -- a second, independent shadow on/off mechanism beyond the constructor default and the move dispatcher.
claims.notes: What this controller represents (cutscene actor controller, camera-follow controller, or something else) and what triggers each branch was not traced this session.

claims.statement: The shadow texture is the same everywhere and never animates. The VRAM texture-slot descriptor array reached through scene_struct+0x28 is baked static overlay data, not zero-initialised BSS, and every stage overlay ships its own copy: scanning all 294 wstag*.s overlays for the constant-tracked store to scene_struct+0x28 resolves 293 array addresses, and all 293 hold a byte-identical slot-0 record (01000200 01a6021c 00a60070 01fe0230); the one unresolved overlay, wstag260, is the known pure-bytecode overlay with no init code and so inherits the FIELDSTG default at 0x80097d0c, which holds the same bytes. Slot-0 u/v therefore do not vary per stage and there is no per-variant or animated shadow, and the ellipse measured in the s415 captures is the shared global texture, not an s415-local variant.
claims.notes: Supporting negative: in wstag330 the array address 0x800a6210 is materialized exactly once in the entire overlay (feeding only the scene+0x28 store) and 0x80097d0c is materialized exactly once in fieldstg, so neither overlay can write into the table. Not verified: a resident-EXE writer reached through the pointer propagated into entity+0x70 was not exhaustively excluded; the five runtime captures are consistent with the baked bits but were all taken in one stage.
claims.frontier_rationale: Proves the shadow texture-slot descriptor is byte-identical baked data across all 293 resolvable stage overlays (global, non-animated) - the closed SHDW-Q001 texture-identity finding, with no bearing on SHDW-Q002 or SHDW-Q003.

claims.statement: The typed-resource object at 0x8009b6c4 is 16 zeroed u32 resource slots followed by a baked method table, and its +0x40 entry is the baked pointer to F0x800928cc, a two-instruction set_resource(slot, handle) that stores [0x8009b6c4 + slot*4] = handle. In a handle such as 0x01ad0002 the HIGH halfword is established to be the EXE LBA master-file-table index: the live s330 read of slot 0 is 0x01b50001 and 0x1b5 = LBA_S330TMPK_BIN_IDX, the stage's own TMPK pack. The LOW halfword is the archive sub-entry index BY ANALOGY with the committed zone-map decode in tools/extract_zone_grids.py (archive begins with a u32 offset TOC; resolver F0x800140d8); no consumer of 0x8009b6c4 slot data was traced that splits the word and uses the low half as a TOC index, so the low half is inferred, not established. Slot 0 is re-issued by every stage: wstag330's stage init is a structural clone of the FIELDSTG default F0x80091e60 and issues slot 0 <- 0x01b50001, matching the live s330 RAM read of 0x8009b6c4+0x00. This resource-slot table is NOT the source of the shadow texture: the shadow reads the separate VRAM texture-slot descriptor array reached through scene_struct+0x28.
claims.notes: Corrects the 2026-07-27 first-pass conflation of resource slot 0 at 0x8009b6c4 with texture-descriptor slot 0 at 0x80097d0c. Not verified: which resource type slot 0 denotes and which routine consumes it were not traced, because they are not on the shadow path; that untraced consumer is exactly why the handle's low halfword is inference by analogy rather than established fact.
claims.frontier_rationale: Decodes an unrelated resource-slot setter/handle mechanism at 0x8009b6c4 and concludes it is NOT the source of the shadow texture, correcting a prior conflation with SHDW-Q001's texture descriptor; it does not touch SHDW-Q002 or SHDW-Q003.

claims.statement: The field character drop-shadow texture is a fixed, global 32x16 4-bpp image inside FIELDCOM.BIN sub-entry 2, at atlas-local texels u=112..143, v=166..181, with the 16-entry CLUT at atlas halfword (48,254). It uses only two indices: index 0 = CLUT 0x0000 (transparent) and index 1 = CLUT 0x9cc6, i.e. 15-bit 0x1cc6 with the STP bit set = RGB 0x30,0x30,0x38. The opaque texels form an ellipse 25 px wide by 11 px tall centred in the 32x16 rect. The renderer reaches it through the baked VRAM texture-slot descriptor record 0 of the array at scene_struct+0x28, which holds tpage (512,256), VRAM corner (540,422), u=0x70, v=0xa6 and CLUT corner (560,510); tpage origin (512,256) is the resident VRAM corner of FIELDCOM sub-entry 2, and u/v are exactly the texel offset of the VRAM corner inside that page.
claims.notes: Cross-check passed: the extracted texture's per-row spans reproduce the shadow-coloured pixel spans of all five authority-1 s415 captures exactly, at two different screen positions. Extraction is asserted in tools/extract_fieldcom.py (index set must be exactly {0,1}; CLUT[1] & 0x7fff must be 0x1cc6), so a wrong descriptor or atlas fails loudly. Not verified: no runtime capture of VRAM or of the primitive words was taken this pass; the identification rests on original assembly plus checked extraction plus the pixel comparison.
claims.frontier_rationale: Positively identifies the shadow texture inside FIELDCOM.BIN sub-entry 2 with exact atlas coordinates and CLUT - the resolution of the now-closed SHDW-Q001 frontier, unrelated to actor eligibility (SHDW-Q002) or the per-frame entity+0x90 writer question (SHDW-Q003).

The remaining 9 stores at file offsets 0x3a5c, 0x3eec, 0x4580, 0x4e04, 0x8664, 0x940c, 0xab7c, 0xabb0, 0xabb8 are NOT confirmed to be on that struct -- at least two (0x3a5c, 0x3eec) show the shape of an unrelated array-building loop, and one (0x940c) is inside a distinct second allocator with the same +0x70/+0x74/+0x78/+0x7c offset shape but not traced to the render path.
claims.notes: Recorded so a future pass does not have to re-run the stores scan from scratch, and so '31 stores' is never mistaken for '31 shadow producers'. This is an open question, not a resolved negative -- some of these sites could still turn out to be shadow-relevant.

claims.statement: A field-used permanent-boost chip does not grant its listed value; it rolls `rand() % value + 1` (1..value) and adds that to the target stat, then clamps the stat at the applier's own cap. The caps (ststatus table file 0x17c2c) are 9999 for max HP and max MP and 999 for STR, DEF, SPT, WIS, SPD, CHR and the seven elemental tolerances.
claims.notes: Authority 2 (original assembly). The walker applied the item's full value (a +30 HP Chip always gave 30) and had no cap; engine/dw3/items.ts useItem now rolls 1..value with an injectable rng and applies the caps (9999 HP/MP, 999 others), and web/menu.js shows the amount actually applied. Browser proof tools/verify_item_chip_roll.mjs (HPChip rolled 23: maxHp 1000->1023, message "Max HP increased by 23."). For non-HP/MP stats the walker carries only the chip contribution (bonuses), so the 999 cap is applied to that contribution rather than the summed stat; the original caps the summed stat. The applier's message shows the rolled delta even when the cap clips the stat; the walker shows the applied (post-clip) amount.

Not read: the schedule table contents (runtime data), so the exact per-tile order and total frame count are not established here; a rig dump of 0x80097770 on this build returned 16 twelve-byte records of {pointer, direction, limit} but their semantics are not yet joined to the draw.

claims.statement: The field's transition wipes are two routines, not three. The iris/tile wipe F0x8008A5E4 starts a 320x240 closing rectangle that closes 10 px per frame horizontally and 7 px per frame vertically toward the player (fallback centre 160,120), reopens at 8 px per frame, ramps its fade from 0 to 0x8000 in steps of 0x400, and draws a grey tile grid through F0x80086CE4 in a 2x2 arrangement of 64x64 tiles. The battle-transition checkerboard F0x80089F7C is a 5-column by 6-row grid of 64x40 tiles over 320x240, drawn row-outer/column-inner, grey 0x80 with a per-row ramp step 0x28, ending on a 0x200 sentinel. The ordinary stage-change dispatch F0x8008AA10 chooses the checkerboard when scene descriptor +0x5C is non-zero and the iris otherwise, so the earlier document split of an 'iris' A27 from a separate 'cyan tile' A29 is one routine reached two ways.
claims.notes: Read 2026-09-13 from the fieldstg assembly closures. The cyan tint of the stage-change wipe is NOT established: the tile drawer F0x80086060 writes a grey value (arg3>>8) into R=G=B, so any cyan must come from a stage mask texture or CLUT at descriptor+0x28 that was not read. The routing has an extra test: when +0x5C is zero the iris path also requires actor +0x68 <= 0.
claims.coverage: The constants were each read from the F0x8008A5E4 / F0x80089F7C / F0x8008AA10 closures; the tile-grid drawer F0x80086CE4 has one caller. The colour source is the one unresolved value and is called out as unverified.
claims.frontier_rationale: Field transition presentation constants, not a catalogued frontier; recorded for the field-gap A27/A28/A29 rows before the browser replaces its black fade.

claims.statement: FIGHTSTG_F0x80087f38 places a fight actor from that Digimon's own smdldata record and from the side nibble of the slot id it is given. It zeroes the actor's X, sets Y to the record's +0x18 negated, and sets Z to -(0x1400 + record+0x10) when the slot id is below 0x10 or to +(0x1400 + record+0x10) when it is not. The near-side branch also writes 0x800 to the actor's Y rotation halfword at +0x24, while the far-side branch zeroes the rotation halfwords at +0x22, +0x24 and +0x26. The routine then copies the position triple at +0x1c into the home triple at +0x28 and the rotation triple at +0x22 into +0x2e. The two fighters are therefore placed symmetrically about arena Z = 0, at a distance that differs per Digimon, and the near-side fighter is the one turned 180 degrees.
claims.notes: Reproduces the only runtime capture we have on both fighters: Renamon's stand-off 128 gives 5120+128 = 5248 for the player slot and the opposing model's 768 gives 5120+768 = 5888, the two values recorded in docs/research/fight-3d/battle-camera.md from fight_rena.bin. That document's caveat that the arena slots were assumed shared across matchups is answered: they are not shared, they are per Digimon. The rotation split also matches the same capture, which recorded diag(-1,1,-1) for the player and identity for the enemy.
claims.frontier_rationale: Arena geometry for the 3D fight presentation. The battle system carries no open frontier in the catalog; this is recorded against the system directly, as the existing fx-mesh and fx-sprite claims are.

It resolves the model record via F0x80087e28 then *(0x800a4570) (L5422-5431, v1) and splits on the slot id: `slti $v0, $s1, 0x10` (L5433). Near branch (id < 0x10): `sh $zr, 0x1c` (X=0), `lhu $v0, 0x18($v1); negu; sh $v0, 0x1e` (Y = -record[+0x18]), `lhu $v1, 0x10($v1); li $v0, -0x1400; ...; subu $v0, $v1` => Z = - Anchors re-read: /home/dorij/ddw3/asm/dw2003/pro/fightstg.s:5418-5476 (F0x80087f38 full body: record resolve L5422-31; slti 0x10 L5433; near branch L5436-48; far branch L5449-58; copies L5460-71).; docs/research/fight-3d/battle-camera.md:58-60, L180-185 (captured 5248/5888 values; symmetric about z=0; cites this claim).

claims.statement: The fight camera manager's +0x104 method is FIGHTSTG_F0x800923b4, installed statically by the manager's constructor, and it is the canned-shot selector. It takes a slot id and a shot index, resolves the acting Digimon's smdldata record through FIGHTSTG_F0x8009e994, and writes the battle camera struct at 0x800a46d8. The eye triple is read from record+0x1a + 6*shot with the second and third components negated, on either side. The look-at triple is read from record+0x62 + 6*shot when the slot id's high nibble is clear and from record+0x2c + 6*shot when it is set, again with the second and third components negated. The view size written to camera+0x30 is read from record+0xaa + 2*shot on the near side and record+0x3e + 2*shot on the far side. Those offsets make the 0xC4 section-2 record a twelve-shot table and the 0x48 section-3 record a three-shot table.
claims.notes: This retires the 2026-07-05 conclusion in docs/research/fight-3d/tech-effects-decode.md that the +0x104 method address is a runtime pointer that is not statically resolvable and needs an emulator read: the manager's constructor installs +0xf8, +0xfc, +0x100 and +0x104 with static addresses in fightstg. The shot indices match the already-decoded op5 preset mapping exactly, presets 1 to 4 selecting near shots 8 to 11 and presets 5 to 7 selecting far shots 0 to 2, and only three far shots exist. Airdramon's three view-size halfwords all read 280, the same view size recorded from the running game in docs/research/fight-3d/battle-camera.md.
claims.coverage: The twelve-shot and three-shot figures are derived from the offsets the routine itself uses, then checked against the record sizes already established: 0x62 minus 0x1a is 0x48, twelve six-byte entries, and 0xaa plus twelve two-byte entries ends at 0xc2 inside a 0xC4 record; 0x2c minus 0x1a is 0x12, three entries, and 0x3e plus three two-byte entries ends at 0x44 inside a 0x48 record. claims.statement: Which of an animated texture patch's three variants is shown depends on the pool slot the entry came from. For pool slots 0 and 1, FIGHTSTG_F0x8008b200 runs a countdown at object +0x1a0: while timer >> 1 is 7 or more the variant is 0, and below that the jump table D0x80082e1c indexed by timer >> 1 selects variants 1, 1, 2, 2, 1, 1 as the timer falls through indices 6 down to 1, with index 0 reloading the timer to (rand() & 0x7f) + 0x3c, that is 60 to 187 ticks (0x8008b2a4, 0x8008b2e0). The sequence open, half, shut, half, open followed by a random pause is a blink, so variant 1 is half-closed and variant 2 closed. FIGHTSTG_F0x8008b118 overrides the timer from the fighter's own state code at +0x78: the value 2 forces variant 1, values 4 through 11 force variant 2, and every other value lets the blink run (0x8008b120); F0x80083f90 sets that field to 1 straight after creating the object. For pool slots 2 through 15 there is no timer: object +0x1a4 accumulates the frame delta at D0x800a4464 and the variant is (t mod 18) / 6, so 0, 1 and 2 each hold for six ticks and repeat forever (0x8008b308). An entry is only re-blitted when its selected variant differs from the one cached at element +0x04.
claims.notes: That variant 1 is a half-closed eye and variant 2 a closed one is read off the SHAPE of the sequence, not off the artwork; the code proves only the order and the timings. The fighter state codes 2 and 4..11 are not named here - only the branch boundaries in F0x8008b118 are established.
claims.coverage: The variant sequence is read from the jump table itself, not inferred: D0x80082e1c holds seven cells and all seven were resolved - 0x8008b2cc (reload, variant 0), 0x8008b2f4 (variant 1) at indices 1, 2, 5 and 6, and 0x8008b2fc (variant 2) at indices 3 and 4 - with the out-of-range path at 0x8008b2ec giving variant 0. The two loops in F0x8008b200 were both read to their bounds, the first covering elements 0 and 1 (slti 0x2) and the second elements 2 to 15 (slti 0x10), which is what establishes that the slot index alone decides between the two selectors.

claims.statement: The three halfwords at op5 camera-record +0x24/+0x26/+0x28 are the ORIENTATION of the frame whose origin is the record's +0x18 anchor, and the record's eye/target pair is stated inside that frame. F0x80091df4 builds a GsCOORDINATE2 on its stack, fills its coord matrix rotation by calling F0x8002b65c on the live angle triple at object+0x78 and its translation slot from the live anchor at object+0x6c..+0x74, and passes the struct pointer as field +0x1c of the argument block handed to the view builder. F0x8002a1ac loads that pointer and, when it is non-null, derives the frame's world matrix, inverts it and composes the inverse onto the look-at it built from eye/target. The finished view is V_local . W^-1, which is the same camera as a world-space look-at from R.eye + anchor to R.target + anchor with its up vector turned by R. F0x8002b65c is RotMatrixYXZ: R = Ry(vy) . Rx(vx) . Rz(vz), read off its four store sites - m[2][2] = cos(vx)cos(vy), m[1][1] = cos(vx)cos(vz), m[1][2] = -sin(vx), m[0][2] = sin(vy)cos(vx), m[1][0] = cos(vx)sin(vz), m[0][0] = cos(vy)cos(vz) + sin(vy)sin(vx)sin(vz), m[0][1] = cos(vz)sin(vy)sin(vx) - cos(vy)sin(vz). Its sin/cos table D0x80056a28 is indexed with (abs(angle) * 4) & 0x3ffc, so one full turn is 4096 units, and the conditionally-negated low halfword of an entry is sin while the high halfword is cos.

claims.statement: The op5 camera-record word at +0x2c is a camera roll in DEGREES, and it pre-multiplies the finished look-at as a screen rotation. F0x80091df4 shifts it left 12 into argument field +0x18; F0x8002a1ac negates it into F0x8002a7cc; F0x8002a7cc divides by 360 with the signed magic multiply 0xb60b60b7, so the net conversion is roll * 4096/360 truncated to a whole 4096-unit angle, which is what makes the field degrees rather than raw units. F0x8002a7cc then builds a pure Z rotation (m[0][0] = m[1][1] = cos, m[0][1] = -sin, m[1][0] = +sin, m[2][2] = 4096, zero translation) from the 4096-unit cos/sin routines F0x8002ac9c (even, hence cosine) and F0x8002abcc (odd, hence sine), returning immediately when the angle is zero. Because MulMatrix F0x8002afbc computes m0 = m0 x m1, and the view builder starts from the identity, the roll matrix PRE-multiplies the pitch and yaw rotations: V.R = Rz(roll) . Rx(pitch) . Ry(yaw) with Rz(roll) = [[cos,sin,0],[-sin,cos,0],[0,0,1]]. Roll is not held constant across a camera move: a fifth interpolation call in F0x80091df4 tweens roll and H together as one pseudo-vector with a zero third component. The remaining routines on this path are: F0x8002a74c, a full AFFINE compose writing m1 := m0 . m1 (rotation via F0x8002b0cc, translation via F0x8002ae5c plus m0's own), which is what makes the finished view exactly V_local . W^-1; F0x8002b41c, a matrix TRANSPOSE, used with a negated rotated translation to form the rigid inverse of the shot's frame; F0x8002ae5c, a rotation-only matrix-times-vector that splits each 32-bit component into high and low halves for the GTE; F0x8002a57c, an overflow NORMALIZER that uniformly shifts the six eye/target words right when the largest absolute value among them (F0x8002a668) exceeds 15 bits (F0x8002a730), preserving direction and feeding only the pitch/yaw derivation while the translation uses the unscaled eye; F0x8002adcc, an integer square root built on the GTE leading-zero-count registers; and F0x8002a88c, which for a struct whose super pointer at +0x48 and flag word at +0x00 are both zero - as the op5 camera's is - simply copies the coord matrix to the work matrix, so the shot's world matrix is the coord matrix itself.
claims.notes: NOT verified against a running console. The SIGN of the roll as applied by the browser port rests on a screen-space argument - PS1 screen v runs down where the renderer's runs up, so the port turns the look-at up vector by MINUS the roll - which is sound only given that the un-rolled framing already agrees between the 3D layer and the 2D screen-space effect layer. That agreement is measured (19 px worst effect-to-body distance) but it is not a capture of a rolled shot, and no rolled shot has been compared against the original. The port reproduces the truncation to a whole 4096-unit angle but not the sin/cos table's own 1/4096 rounding, worth about 0.014 degrees. A negative roll would pass through the tween's unsigned-halfword reads and wrap through 16 bits; no shipped pack sets one, so that path is untested. Shipped in web/fight/battle-camera.js applyScreenRoll/rollRadians and web/battle3d.js.

claims.statement: Resolving each animated-texture patch out of the model's own 4bpp page through the palette covering its destination shows what the three variants depict. For a patch in pool slot 0 or 1 - the two the blink timer drives - the three pictures are the eye open, half closed and shut, in that order, matching the order F0x8008b200 plays them; Giromon (m041giro) is the case that shows why there are two such slots, carrying its left and right eye as separate patches, while models such as Agumon carry a single eye rectangle that both eyes sample. A few models put a light rather than an eyelid in a blink slot: Imperialdramon Paladin Mode (m444ipd2) has a red glow that is lit in variant 0 and dark in variants 1 and 2. For a patch in pool slot 2 or above - the ones on the free 3-phase cycle - the three pictures are the frames of a looping animation on the body: Flarerizamon (m069flar) and Meramon (m009mera) carry flames, Giromon (m041giro) scrolling light bands. Variant 0 is the resting picture: over the 249 patch entries whose pack can be read, the destination rectangle in the shipped page is byte-identical to variant 0 in 242 of them.
claims.notes: The pixel-to-VRAM mapping is texel_x = vram_x * 4, texel_y = vram_y: the record's units are 16-bit VRAM words against a 64x256 strip and the baked page is 256x256 texels at 4bpp. All four rectangles must be resolved through the DESTINATION's palette, because a VRAM copy moves raw indices; the spare source regions are covered by no face and have no palette of their own. Seven entries whose destination is not byte-identical to variant 0 are authored that way - m384koet and m124tirs differ most, by a small shift of the eye.
claims.coverage: The picture identification is checked extraction (authority 4), not a reading of code, and both population statements were measured over every patch by tools/render_texture_patches.py --audit rather than over the models that were looked at. Destination equals variant 0 in 209 of 216 blink entries and 33 of 33 cycle entries; 3 models have no readable pack. The blink ordering was tested by a statistic that could have failed and that separates the two selectors: for blink slots variant 1 is nearer variant 0 than variant 2 is in 198 of 216 entries, with 13 exact ties and 5 inversions, which is what a monotone open-half-shut sequence looks like, whereas for the free-cycle slots the same measure gives 17 of 33 with 10 inversions - no ordering at all, as three frames of a loop should show. The five blink inversions are the light-rather-than-eyelid cases.

claims.statement: World-space fight effect and projectile positions are not mirrored for the far-side fighter. The op3 spawn handler FIGHTSTG_F0x8008bc80 copies its x, y and z operands into a stack record with no side test; the effect owner constructor FIGHTSTG_F0x80089be4 copies those eight bytes onto itself at +0x5c; the owner's per-tick driver hands the address of that same +0x5c field to the sprite spawner FIGHTSTG_F0x8008966c, which copies it unchanged to the sprite at +0x54; and the sprite draw FIGHTSTG_F0x8008921c projects it through the pointer at D0x800a454c, which is FIGHTSTG_F0x8009e53c, composing the global battle-camera matrix at 0x80081358 with the fixed identity matrix D0x8004dc20 and nothing else. Inside the action VM's opcode-handler range the side flag at VM+0x50 is loaded three times, by the slot-operand resolver FIGHTSTG_F0x8008b630 and by the two sub-script constructors, and none of those loads reaches a coordinate. Instead the two sides carry separately authored data: over the shipped attack clips 5 to 8, the 52 player-side model packs place 677 world-space op3 spawns at positive Z against 1 at negative Z, while the 193 enemy-side packs place 153 at negative Z against 65 at positive Z, and the op6 projectile root yaw operand is 2048 in 223 of the 224 player-side records and 0 in the 121 enemy-side records.
claims.notes: This resolves the open question left by the 2026-07-05 decode, which recorded op3 coordinates as absolute arena coordinates authored from the player's perspective and inferred a far-side mirror of x to -x and z to 640-z from the two slot positions in one runtime capture. There is no such mirror in the code, and the 640 constant was an artefact of treating two per-Digimon stand-off values as fixed arena slots (see fight-arena-slot-is-per-model-standoff-and-hover-2026-08-18). The walker applies that mirror in web/battle3d.js for effects, projectile flights and camera presets; it is not authentic. What remains unestablished is whether a far-side fighter's own positive-Z effects stay inside the framing of the impact camera; that needs a capture.
claims.coverage: The negative half was tested two ways. First, the loads of the VM side flag were enumerated by regex over the assembly text of the whole opcode-handler range 0x8008b630 to 0x8008c500, giving four hits of which one is a stack restore; a side test on a coordinate would have had to appear as a branch on that flag and none does. Second, the operand-to-sprite path was read line by line from the op3 handler through the owner constructor, the spawner call site and the sprite draw to the projector, so an inserted transform would have been visible at any step. The data half is a full enumeration rather than a sample: every anim.json under web/assets/battle/models (245 packs) was parsed and every op 3 record with sub-opcode 0 and every op 6 record was counted, partitioned by the model's smdldata section. The one player-side yaw of 0 and the 65 enemy-side positive-Z spawns are counted, not excluded; they are consistent with effects placed at the caster's own end rather than the target's.

claims.statement: Field +0x78 of the fight model actor is the playing timeline table index plus one, and it is what the eye override reads. FIGHTSTG_F0x80083a54(actor, animId, force) is the animation setter: unless force is 1 it returns early when +0x78 already equals animId (0x80083a78), otherwise it writes animId to +0x78 (0x80083a94), sets +0x80 to 1 and clears +0x7c and +0x9c, resolves the directory at actor+0x74 - the record's +0x04 packed reference - and takes member animId minus one from it (0x80083ab4) before walking that member's pose stream to its 0x7fff sentinel. tools/decode_timeline.py is a port of this routine and builds the walker's timeline tables from the same directory, so walker timeline table i is animId i+1. FIGHTSTG_F0x80083f90's caller writes 1 to +0x78 immediately after creating the animated-texture object (0x80083fa8), which is table 0, the idle - an independent check of the plus-one. FIGHTSTG_F0x8008b118 reads this field through the patch object's +0x50 back-pointer, so the eye is held half closed while timeline table 1 plays and shut while tables 3 through 10 play, and blinks freely otherwise.
claims.notes: The eye override therefore reads an ANIMATION, not a health or damage state: an earlier reading of +0x78 as a fighter status code would have been wrong. The walker exposes it as ActorAnimator.animationId (timeline table + 1) and web/battle3d.js feeds that to the patch animator.
claims.coverage: The plus-one is established twice over and each check could have failed: the setter's own arithmetic subtracts one before indexing the directory, and the creation site writes the literal 1 at a moment when the actor is necessarily on its idle, which is directory member 0. The claim is deliberately narrow - it names the field's role and the two branch bands F0x8008b118 tests, not what any particular table depicts. Which motion each table holds is NOT established here and the walker's own table-to-motion mapping was not re-derived for this claim.

claims.statement: The player leader entity's animation-directory handle at +0x9c is NEVER repointed in pro/fieldstg.s. An exhaustive whole-overlay store census finds exactly three writes to +0x9c, none reachable from the cast controller, the ladder mounts, SETANIM or the shared leader dispatcher. The cast path raises the scene lock, sets leader mode 0x48 and spawns the bobber through the generic object allocator, none of which touches +0x9c. The fishing clips must therefore already be resolvable through the handle the player carries from entity creation, rather than through a swap-and-restore around the cast.
claims.notes: Falsifies FISH-Q009's premise. UNRESOLVED: why the P002PLYF fishing clips are reachable without a swap. The per-tick clip resolver's fallback reuses the existing +0x9c unchanged, so the answer likely lies in the species-pack table reached via scene_struct+0x74, whose contents were NOT enumerated and are not statically reachable from this file alone. Contradicted 2026-09-13: the census's three +0x9c stores are real, but the store at fieldstg.s:13172 (RAM 0x8008fa64) is the player's repoint, not an unrelated actor. It sits inside the per-frame resolver F0x8008F9C0, called from the character tick right after the leader-mode dispatcher; it is gated on entity+0x4 == 2 (the player) and remaps clips 9..0x15 to P002PLYF (and 0x1a..0x24 to P002PLYL). See claim fishing-q009-resolver-repoints-player-anim-handle-2026-09-13.

claims.statement: FISH-Q009's premise is false: the player entity's animation-directory handle (+0x9C) IS repointed for a cast. The per-frame resolver F0x8008F9C0 reads +0x9C and, when entity+0x4 == 2 (the player), rewrites +0x9C from a clip-range remap before resolving. The verified arms are: clip<8 -> 0x01870070 (P002PLAY), clip==8 -> 0x03CB001E, clips 9..0x15 (9..21) -> 0x03CA0064 (P002PLYF), clips 0x16..0x19 (22..25) -> 0x03C9000B, clips 0x1a..0x24 (26..36) -> 0x03CC0017 (P002PLYL), clips >=37 -> 0x03CA0064. Non-player actors reuse +0x9C unchanged. So the exclusive-clip problem is answered: the resolver supplies P002PLYF when the cast latches clip 0x11..0x15, one frame after SETANIM, with no separate swap site. The earlier census claim 'fishing-player-anim-handle-never-repointed' is CONTRADICTED -- its store #2 (fieldstg.s:13172) is this repoint. scene_struct+0x74 is falsified as the mechanism: it is the npc_id -> sprite-LBA table (F0x800920DC), never yields P002PLYF.

claims.statement: A fishing strike parks the marker at the press position plus the strike tick's 0x100 plus the brake glide. The brake decays speed +0x60 by 0x10 (three rolls in four) or 4 (one in four) each tick while the meter +0x5c moves by the decaying speed, so the glide is exactly 0x780 (fast, 7.5 of the 48 bands) or 0x1F80 (slow, 31.5 bands); the band is then read at that parked position. This is what decides the cast, and why the same press can land differently between casts.
claims.notes: Authority 2 (original assembly). Walker side pinned the same day: tests/fishing.test.js asserts both glide distances from a controlled cast, and tools/verify_fishing_strike_stop.mjs drives the real screen (cast, sweep, strike at a safe meter): the press at meter 0 glided exactly 2176 = 0x880 = the strike tick's 0x100 + the 0x780 fast glide, parked at 2176 with a band read. The full controlled replay tools/verify_fishing.mjs covers pole gate, settle, angler clips, control lock, band -> battle, budget and no item. Still missing for FISH-Q006: the original's own strike capture (the existing 2026-07-29 capture supplied cast and withdraw only).

claims.statement: The folder chooser's three element-count panels animate their WIDTH only (+0x5C; 0x1000 = 1.0 in 12-bit fixed point, +0x5E stays 0x1000). ENTRY is the panel handler F0x80096418 state 1: +0x5C = 0x1000 - (counter<<12)/0xC, a 12-tick grow from 0 to full, run by the panel's own default/state-1 path with no call from the chooser. CLOSE is F0x80096808, the panel's +0x70 method, called by the chooser at its take-down states: it sets +0x6A=6, +0x68=6, +0x66=2 and +0x5C=0x1000, and state 2 computes (counter<<12)/6, a 6-tick shrink. The chooser F0x8009F110 builds the panels 11 ticks apart (entry starts 0/11/22) and closes them 4 ticks apart (close starts 0/4/8). The earlier reading that F0x80096808 is the entry is refuted.
claims.notes: Read 2026-09-14 by the lead from the per-function assembly closures (authority 2). The walker anchors the scale at the row's left edge as a stated guess because the primitive's origin was not read. claims.coverage: Every +0x5C write and read in F0x80096418.s was enumerated (default 0, state-1 expression and completion 0x1000, state-2 expression); the chooser's build jal sites, close lw/jalr sites and both slti waits were enumerated in F0x8009f110.s, and F0x80096808's four constants were read from cardgame.s. claims.statement: The battle form-change 'director script sequences' are message STRING ids, not animation clips. The chain resolves entirely statically: getObj is D0x80044f4c = F0x80013e5c = resourceGetBase, which returns a file's RAM base from the 64-entry 0x10-byte cache at D0x80044b3c; file id 0x7f is MSMFIGHT_BIN and file id 0x4e is MSDIGNAM_BIN in the bootstrap LBA table, the M/U/E/F/I/D/S prefixes being the seven language variants of the battle message bank and the Digimon name bank. F0x8001f744 is therefore a string-table lookup of exactly the same self-relative shape as the already-decoded packGetEntry (base + base[index]), and F0x8002525c, which F0x80019370 calls on the returned pointer to size its buffer, is strlen over an s8*. Reading the English bank esmfight.toml at those indices gives the presentation text directly: 0x16 = '{1}', 0x37 = 'Digivolved! {1}!', 0x38 = 'Back!', 0x61 = 'Blasted!', 0x62 = 'Back to normal!'. This explains why manual DV alone carries the extra call [objB+0x120](objB, getObj(0x4e), profile[+0x55], 1): its string 0x37 is the only one of the five containing a {1} placeholder, and that call installs the target Digimon's name from the name bank, indexed by the profile byte +0x55 already documented as the name-string index, into channel 1 as the substitution.
claims.notes: Falsifies the standing reading in docs/research/battle/digivolution-tech-system-decoded-2026-07-11.md section 9d that 'seq 0x61/0x62/0x38/0x16/0x37 are animation clips' and that the per-frame sound/camera/model-hide timing lives inside them needing a runtime capture. They are strings; whatever drives the visuals is elsewhere and is still unlocated. Also corrects the framing of claim actor-sequence-directory-is-self-relative-2026-08-13, whose structural finding stands but which called the subsystem an animation VM. BLAST-C006's selector/payload mapping is unaffected and remains correct.
claims.coverage: Each link was resolved from a named source rather than inferred: D0x80044f4c's value is a linker-initialised pointer read from ~/ddw3/rust/dw2003_exe_data/src/data.rs L2229 (all twelve assembly references to that address are lw, no store, so the shipped data is the only source); the cache layout and resourceGetBase/packGetEntry identities were already established in docs/research/engine/resident-core-services-2026-08-04.md and were re-read rather than re-derived; the file ids were resolved by indexing ~/ddw3/iso/dw2003-bootstrap/lbas.toml, a flat 2382-entry array, at 127 and 78; F0x8002525c was read in full from exe-decomp/c/F0x8002525c.c and is a NUL-scan returning a count; the five strings were read by indexing ~/ddw3/lang_file/dw2003/eng/esmfight.toml, a 145-entry array. LIMITS: only the ENGLISH bank was read, so the ids are asserted for esmfight and the other six language files were not checked; and this claim covers the five ids named and makes no statement about any other sequence id used elsewhere in the game.

claims.statement: The op6 mesh display list's 0xEn state register is a ONE-BASED semi-transparency selector, not the hardware blend mode. FIGHTSTG_F0x80085110 splits each opcode byte into nibbles at 0x80085358 and dispatches a high nibble of 8..0xE through the seven-entry jump table at D0x80082cb0; that table's 0xE entry is 0x800853c0, which parks the low nibble in the stack slot sp+0x48. The slot is read at one site, 0x80085484, while the tex-op assembles the texpage halfword: a stored zero branches past the computation and leaves the texpage ABR bits at 0, and a non-zero value contributes ((n - 1) & 3) << 5, which is the texpage's semi-transparency field. The hardware blend mode is therefore (n - 1) & 3. Across the 129 extracted packs the nibble takes only the values 0, 2 and 4, resolving to ABR 0 (0.5B + 0.5F), ABR 1 (B + F, additive) and ABR 3 (B + 0.25F); no shipped primitive selects the subtractive ABR 2. The walker had been feeding the raw nibble to its blend switch, so 17,394 primitives across 115 of the 129 packs were drawn subtractive instead of additive - which renders a blue-white texture as a dark red-brown stain on the arena floor - and the 92 primitives with nibble 4 were drawn at full additive instead of quarter. Armormon's basic attack, pack 39, carries both errors: its flat ground arc is nibble 2 and its three upright rings are nibble 4.
claims.notes: NOT established: the primitive command word's own semi-transparent bit. This reads only what reaches the texpage's ABR field, which the hardware consults only for a primitive already marked semi-transparent. Every shipped non-zero nibble therefore has a proven blend mode, but whether a nibble-0 primitive is drawn opaque or as ABR 0 is untested - the walker keeps its existing 0.5B+0.5F behaviour for that case either way. Also not established: whether the per-primitive CLUT bytes should select different palettes within one pack. 117 of 129 packs name more than one CLUT, all on the standard {0,16,32,48} x {252..255} grid, but tools/extract_fight_effects.py bakes a single best-ramp palette per pack and points every layer at it. For pack 39 the palettes at x=0 and x=32 were decoded and compared and both give the same blue-white ramp, so that shortcut is not what made the floor brown.
claims.coverage: The nibble population was enumerated exhaustively, not sampled: every textured primitive of every layer of all 129 pack JSONs under web/assets/battle/effects/proj, 21,051 primitives, giving 0 -> 3,565 prims / 37 packs, 2 -> 17,394 / 115, 4 -> 92 / 2. tests/proj-layer-transform.test.js asserts those exact counts and the value set {0,2,4}, so a fourth nibble value or a changed count fails the suite. The 'one site' claim for the sp+0x48 read was tested by matching the literal '0x48($sp)' over the whole of F0x80085110 (fightstg.s lines 2382-2914): exactly two hits, the store at 0x800853c0 and the read at 0x80085484. The jump-table entry for nibble 0xE was read out of fightstg's own data section rather than inferred from the address order of the seven handler blocks.
claims.frontier_rationale: Extends the op6 mesh-effect chain already covered by fx-mesh-layer-rotation-is-rz-ry-rx, fx-mesh-layer-hide-test-is-a-signed-or and fx-mesh-layer-array-has-implicit-root-and-parent-index, which carry no frontier id either; this is the same per-frame draw path, one step further down into the GPU state.

claims.statement: An op6 mesh effect's lifetime is its META bin's compiled clip, not how far its layer tracks are authored. FIGHTSTG_F0x80083a54 compiles that bin - 8-byte records of {previous last frame, count, first frame, last frame}, ending at a record whose first halfword is 0x7fff - into a per-tick stream of frame numbers held at animator+0xa4, records the stream length at animator+0xa0, and sets the playback cursor at +0x80 to 1. A record whose last-frame field is nonzero emits count entries counting up from its first-frame field, so a later segment can replay an earlier frame range. Each tick FIGHTSTG_F0x80083c30 reads the entry under the cursor as the frame at which the layer tracks are sampled, advances the cursor by the global D0x800a4464, and on reaching a 0xffff entry sets its finished flag and writes 1 into the control block's +0x10, which is flight+0x84; the flight's own update FIGHTSTG_F0x8008970c then calls its +0x28 teardown with argument 3 and the effect ends.
claims.notes: UNRESOLVED: the cursor step D0x800a4464 is zero in the shipped data and nothing in fightstg writes it, so its runtime value is not established here; the port assumes one stream entry per logic tick. Ported as decode_clip in tools/extract_fight_effects.py and clipFrameAt/clipTicks in web/fight/proj-layers.js. Before this the walker fed the raw tick to the layer tracks and ended a flight at the last authored keyframe, so packs 108 and 109 played their sustained beam once instead of four times.
claims.coverage: The record grammar was tested by decoding the meta bin of all 129 projectile packs, not by reading one: every pack yields a single clip section, every clip ends with the 0xffff terminal record, and none uses the compiler's other record form (the interpolating hold taken when the last-frame field is zero) or the 0x8000 loop terminator - so those two forms are named here as decoded branches of the code but are NOT asserted of any shipped data. The replay finding is an enumeration over the same 129: exactly 2 packs, 108 and 109, contain a segment whose first frame is not greater than the previous segment's, and both repeat frames 36..80 four times. The claim that the clip and not the keyframe span is the lifetime was cross-checked against the authored tracks: the two numbers disagree for 17 of the 129 packs, in both directions. || Isolated review 2026-10-05 (docs/research/evidence/reviews/battle-2026-10-05.json): Both halves re-read. Compiler F0x80083a54: `li $v0, 0x7fff; beq $v1, $v0, .L0x80083c0c` (L911-912, re-checked at L986-988) stops at the 0x7fff first halfword; the ramp emit `sh $v0, 0xa4($v1)` (L979) sits in a loop emitting count entries counting up from the record's first-frame field (`lhu $v0, ($a3)` = +0x4 field, `addu $v0, $a0; sh $v0, 0xa4`; the loop bound is the count field; records step by  Anchors re-read: fightstg.s:887-1005 (compiler: terminator L911-912/L986-988, ramp emit L974-983, length L991, cursor L897/L992).; fightstg.s:1051-1092 (tick: frame read L1054-59/L1078, advance+clamp L1064-73, 0x8000 redirect L1086-88, 0xffff end flag + control+0x10 L1089-92).; fightstg.s:6706-6713 (flight tests +0x84, calls +0x28 with a1=3).

claims.statement: The op6 projectile-mesh animator built by FIGHTSTG_F0x80084560 allocates count+1 layer blocks of 0x84 bytes, where count is the program table's second word: index 0 is an implicit root layer whose mesh and ctrl bin pointers are stored as zero and whose parent-matrix pointer is the fixed identity D0x8004dc20, and the count program rows fill indices 1..count. Each program row is three words copied to layer+0x00, +0x04 and +0x08, so the row's first word - previously treated as a zero pad - is the layer's PARENT INDEX; the per-frame builder FIGHTSTG_F0x80083e0c reads layer+0x00, multiplies it by the 0x84 layer stride and adds 0x4c to point layer+0x48 at the parent's concatenated matrix, which it then multiplies into the child's matrix with three GTE MVMVA passes, one per column.
claims.notes: Ported in web/fight/proj-layers.js (projLayerWorlds) and shipped by tools/extract_fight_effects.py as the per-layer 'parent' field. Before this the walker hung every layer directly off the root.
claims.coverage: The 'each program row is three words' quantifier is over the constructor's single copy loop, which was read entry to exit at fightstg.s L1700-L1720: it advances the source pointer by 4 three times per iteration and writes exactly +0x00/+0x04/+0x08, with no other store to a layer block inside the loop. The parent-index reading was then tested against the shipped data by parsing all 129 projectile descriptor bins (572 rows): 184 rows carry a nonzero first word, every one of them is strictly less than its own row index, and none exceeds the row count - which is what a parent index must satisfy and what an unused pad has no reason to. A pad hypothesis predicts 572 zeros; 184 nonzero values falsify it. || Isolated review 2026-10-05 (docs/research/evidence/reviews/battle-2026-10-05.json): Constructor F0x80084560 and builder F0x80083e0c both re-read. Ctor: `lw $a2, 0x4($s3)` takes the count from the program table's second word, `addiu $s4, $a2, 0x1` (L1630) sizes count+1, allocation `sll/addu/sll` L1634-36 = 33*4 = 0x84 per layer via F0x800143dc, animator+0x50 = count+1 (L1657). Layer 0: +0x00/+0x04/+0x08 zeroed (L1658-64), +0x48 set to 0x8004dc20 (L1665-68, lui 0x8005 addiu -0x23e0 Anchors re-read: fightstg.s:1628-1636 (count from desc+0x4; count+1; 0x84 stride alloc), L1656-1668 (root zeros + identity D0x8004dc20), L1671-1695 (root defaults incl. scale 0x1000), L1694-1720 (row copy +0x00/+0x04/+0x08, 1..count).; fightstg.s:1170-1188 (parent resolve: skip layer 0; index*0x84 + 0x4c -> +0x48; stride).

claims.statement: An op6 mesh layer is hidden when the bitwise OR of its three sampled scale components is below 0x31. The three components are loaded with 'lh', which sign-extends, before being ORed, so a negative component sets the sign bit of the result and the comparison at 0x80084190 therefore hides the layer: the test is a signed OR, not an absolute-value test. When it fails the builder writes zero to the layer's visible flag at +0x0c and jumps past the entire matrix build, which leaves the layer's concatenated matrix at +0x4c holding the value it had on the last frame the layer was visible. The three scale components themselves come from the third of the sampler's sub-tracks: FIGHTSTG_F0x800835f4 loops its selector 0, 3, 6 and writes translation to +0x10, rotation to +0x18 and scale to +0x20.
claims.notes: The walker took the absolute value first. Only one shipped layer authors a negative scale key, but three packs (301, 329, 367) hide a parent while a child is still visible, where the stale-matrix behaviour is what keeps the child on screen.
claims.coverage: Statement is scoped to the single hide test at fightstg.s L1340-L1353, which was read instruction by instruction including the sign-extending 'lh' loads at 0x8008416c/0x80084178/0x80084184 and the branch target of the failing case. The stale-matrix consequence is a claim about that branch skipping the stores, not about any wider set of layers, and the skipped range was checked by reading to the loop tail at 0x80084328. The sampler's three sub-tracks were counted from its own loop bound (step 3, stop below 9), not assumed. || Isolated review 2026-10-05 (docs/research/evidence/reviews/battle-2026-10-05.json): All clauses re-read. The test (fightstg.s L1340-1353): `lh $v0, -0x40($s1)`, `lh $a0, -0x3e($s1)`, `lh $v1, -0x3c($s1)` load the layer's three +0x20-scale halfwords with sign extension; `or $v0, $a0; or $v0, $v1; slti $v0, 0x31; beqz` - SLTI is signed, so any negative component makes the OR negative and the layer is hidden (branch falls through to `j .L0x80084328; sw $zr, -0x54($s1)` = visible fla Anchors re-read: fightstg.s:1340-1359 (three sign-extending lh loads; or/or; slti 0x31; hide path `sw $zr` + jump; matrix-build entry).; fightstg.s:620-634 (sub-track destinations +0x10/+0x18/+0x20), L731-733 (selector += 3, < 9 loop bound).

claims.statement: The rotation matrix for an op6 mesh layer is built by EXE routine F0x8002b45c, which fightstg calls from one site only, 0x800841b4 inside the per-frame layer builder FIGHTSTG_F0x80083e0c, passing the layer's sampled rotation at +0x18 and receiving the matrix at +0x28. The routine composes M = Rz . Ry . Rx: it writes m[2][0] = -sin_y, negating sin_y with 'neg $a3' immediately before the store, and writes m[1][1] = sin_x.sin_y.sin_z + cos_x.cos_z. This is a different routine from the 2D sprite path's F0x8002b65c, which composes Ry . Rx . Rz. The scale that follows it, F0x8002b23c, multiplies each element by the scale component selected by its column, forming M.diag(s), so the layer's local transform is T.(R.S).
claims.notes: The walker had Rx.Ry.Rz, the exact reverse, with a comment claiming libgte RotMatrix order. The two agree whenever at most one angle is nonzero, which is why single-axis spins looked right; 109 of the 572 shipped layers author two or more nonzero rotation axes. Fixed in web/fight/proj-layers.js mat4RotPSX.
claims.coverage: The 'one site only' quantifier was tested by scanning the whole of ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003/pro/fightstg.s for 'jal F0x8002b45c': 1 hit, at L1358 (0x800841b4). The same scan for the sprite-path routine 'jal F0x8002b65c' returns 3 hits, none of them in the mesh builder, which is how the two paths were separated. The axis order was not assumed from a library convention: the two named matrix elements were read from the routine's own stores, and Rz.Ry.Rx is the only one of the six axis orders that produces both m[2][0] = -sin_y and m[1][1] = sx.sy.sz + cx.cz. || Isolated review 2026-10-05 (docs/research/evidence/reviews/battle-2026-10-05.json): All anchors re-read. `grep 8002b45c fightstg.s` returns exactly one hit - L1358/0x800841b4 `jal F0x8002b45c` - so the one-call-site clause is exact; the call passes `addiu $a0, $s2, 0x18` (layer's sampled rotation) and takes the result to +0x28 (`addiu $s0, $s2, 0x28` L1355, stored via -0x54($s1) L1359). In fns.s F0x8002b45c: `neg $a3, $a3` (L30021) followed by `or $a3, $at; sw $a3, 0xc($v0)` (L30 Anchors re-read: fightstg.s:1354-1362 (single call site L1358; a0 = +0x18; result +0x28; scale call follows).; fns.s:29995-30056 (F0x8002b45c: neg at L30021, +0xc store L30035, +0x8 store L30056; other element stores).; fns.s:29764-29785 (F0x8002b23c scale: column-selected products, multu L29775).; Algebra cross-check of m[1][1] and m[2][0] against Rz.Ry.Rx vs the five other axis orders.
