claims.statement: A mesh primitive whose 0xEn state nibble is zero is drawn OPAQUE - the walker's previous reading of it as blend mode 0 was wrong in kind, not just in degree. All four of fightstg's primitive-emit paths write their base GPU command byte first (0x3C textured quad in F0x80084bc0, 0x34 textured triangle in F0x80084d74, 0x2C in F0x80084e0c and its second shape), then load $a3+0x18 - which is sp+0x48 in the interpreter's frame, the slot the 0xE state register writes - and OR bit 1, the GPU's semi-transparent flag, into the command byte ONLY when that slot is non-zero. No branch in any of the four sets the flag for a zero nibble, and the texpage ABR field is left at 0 because the hardware never consults it for an opaque primitive. This resolves the limitation carried by fx-mesh-abr-nibble-is-one-based. In the shipped data 3,565 primitives across 37 packs carry the zero nibble; the walker had been drawing them at half strength against the background.
claims.notes: The GPU also applies a per-TEXEL semi-transparency bit within a primitive that carries the command flag. That is now measured and closed by fx-mesh-per-texel-stp-is-never-exercised: no texel in any blended primitive of any of the 129 packs has the bit clear, so a uniform per-group blend is exact for this artwork.
claims.coverage: All four emit paths were read, not sampled: matching the literal '0x18($a3)' over fightstg.s returns four hits, one per path, and each is followed within six instructions by the same beqz/ori 0x2 pair on the command byte. The primitive population was enumerated over all 129 pack JSONs, every layer and every primitive: nibble 0 appears on 3,565 of 21,051 primitives in 37 packs, asserted in tests/proj-layer-transform.test.js.
claims.frontier_rationale: Closes the one limitation recorded against fx-mesh-abr-nibble-is-one-based, in the same op6 mesh draw path.

claims.statement: The transparent-texel claim fx-mesh-transparent-texel-is-palette-entry-zero carries a stale palette tally in its statement: it says entry 0 is 0x0000 in 318 of the 456 live palettes. Both numbers predate the clut_is_live liveness fix recorded in the sibling claim fx-mesh-palette-is-per-primitive, which raised the live-palette count to 476. Recounted 2026-08-17 over the corrected set by importing the shipped extractor own clut_is_live and _clut_entries: 476 live palettes, of which entry 0 is 0x0000 in 322, leaving 154 with a NON-ZERO entry 0. The corrected figure is therefore 322 of 476. The transparency RULE itself is unaffected: it rests on the per-texel test cl[idx] == 0, which is independent of how many palettes happen to have a zero entry 0. Separately, the decode_atlas docstring in tools/extract_fight_effects.py asserts that entry 0 is 0x0000 in every real palette here, and that universal is FALSE by the same count - 154 of 476 palettes contradict it.
claims.notes: Found by an isolated Fable review of the pair on 2026-08-17 and then quantified by the lead. Claims cannot be edited in place, so this records the corrected number rather than amending the original; fx-mesh-transparent-texel-is-palette-entry-zero is consequently HELD at partially_verified and NOT promoted, pending its statement being restated with 322 of 476. Recommended follow-up in implementation: correct the false universal in the decode_atlas docstring. NOT established here: whether any of the 154 non-zero entry-0 palettes is actually sampled at index 0 by a drawn primitive, which is what would decide whether the wrong docstring ever changes a rendered pixel.
claims.coverage: Exhaustive over the shipped population, not sampled, and reproduced with the committed extractor rather than a reimplementation: tools/extract_fight_effects.py was imported and its own clut_is_live and _clut_entries were called, so the liveness test is byte-identical to the one the shipped build uses. Every (pack, texture bin, CLUT slot) triple named by any layer or any primitive across all 129 shipped pack JSONs under web/assets/battle/effects/proj was enumerated - 476 distinct slots - and each was classified. The run independently reproduces two figures it did not take as input: 476 live palettes, matching the assertion atlases.size == 476 in tests/proj-layer-transform.test.js:392, and ZERO palettes holding the 0xffff fill, matching the sibling claim assertion that nothing names an all-fill slot. Because every slot was classified individually and the tally printed, a miscount would appear as a changed total rather than being averaged away. The 154 non-zero entry-0 palettes are the direct counterexample set to the docstring universal.
claims.frontier_rationale: No frontier applies. This is a correction to an existing decoded claim in a system with no open frontier for it, raised by the promotion review gate rather than by new research. Opening a frontier would put a settled arithmetic fix into the actionable research queue.

claims.statement: The mesh tex-op's CLUT bytes are the palette selector and they apply PER PRIMITIVE, not per pack. In F0x80085110 the fifth and sixth tex-op bytes are added to mesh+0x70 and mesh+0x74 and then packed as (y << 6) | (x >> 4), the GPU's CLUT field, so they are a VRAM position measured from the mesh object's own palette base. That base is F0x8008610c's second and third arguments; the per-frame layer builder F0x80083e0c supplies them from the animator's +0x68 and +0x6c, which the animator constructor took from the flight object's +0x6c and +0x70, and the op6 flight sets those to 0x280 and 0x100 - so the base is (640, 256) for every projectile mesh. The same mesh+0x70 also forms the texture PAGE origin at 0x8008547c, so page and palettes share one base and the tex-op bytes are page-local coordinates: the base cancels. MEFT0039's page bears this out - it holds real palettes at exactly three slots, row 255 halfword 0, 16 and 32, and its layers name exactly those three: the upright rings 0, the outward shards 16, the flat ground arc 32. The extractor had been scoring the candidate slots and baking ONE guessed palette per pack, which for pack 39 was a tie between two of the three. Per-primitive resolution yields 476 distinct palettes over the 129 packs where the guess yielded 129, and 183 layers draw with more than one palette. Every one of the 21,051 primitives uses the palette its own data names: no shipped primitive names a slot that is the 0xffff fill, so no fallback is needed.
claims.notes: Not established: whether the tex-op's third byte, which would select a texture page 64 VRAM columns further along from the same base, is ever non-zero in content this extraction does not cover - it is 0 for all 21,051 primitives here.
claims.coverage: The CLUT population was enumerated over every textured primitive of every layer of all 129 pack JSONs - 21,051 primitives - and every one lands on the grid x in {0,16,32,48}, y in {252,253,254,255}, the embedded-palette layout of the pack's own page, with no exception outside it. Liveness was then tested slot by slot against each pack's decoded page: not one names a slot that is all 0xffff, so the claim that every primitive uses its own named palette is exhaustive rather than typical, and the extractor prints the fallback count on every run (currently 0) so a regression is visible. An earlier pass reported 1,181 exceptions; that was a four-distinct-entry threshold misclassifying small real palettes, re-tested by tabulating the distinct-entry count of every named slot (1,149 twos, 16 threes, 16 ones, zero all-fill). The tex-op's page-select byte was read for all 21,051 primitives by re-walking the display lists: it is 0 everywhere, so there is exactly one texture page and no primitive samples another.
claims.frontier_rationale: Same op6 mesh draw path as fx-mesh-abr-nibble-is-one-based and fx-mesh-nibble-zero-primitive-is-opaque; it is the colour half of the same tex-op.

claims.statement: The op6 mesh artwork never uses the PS1's per-texel semi-transparency bit, so blending a whole primitive uniformly reproduces it exactly. Inside a semi-transparent primitive the hardware blends only those texels whose palette entry has bit 15 set; a texel with the bit clear is drawn solid, which a uniform per-primitive blend cannot express. Over the 18,120,302 texels lying inside the 16,382 blended primitives of all 129 packs, 12,686,288 (70.01%) have the bit set and 5,434,014 (29.99%) are the transparent 0x0000 entry - and none has the bit clear. No primitive in any pack mixes the two classes. The walker's per-group blend is therefore exact for this data rather than an approximation, and the two-pass rendering that the mixed case would require is not needed.
claims.notes: This bounds the shipped op6 projectile packs. The counterpart measurement for the 2D sprite path is claim fx-sprite-per-texel-stp-is-used, which found the OPPOSITE - 62 of 1,757 sprite clips do mix the two classes - so the two paths genuinely differ and the mesh result is not a general property of the game's art. The mesh population is complete: F0x8008610c, which installs the mesh draw entry points, has exactly one caller, so the op6 projectile meshes are all the content that uses this display-list grammar. The finding is that the mesh data never exercises the feature, NOT that the hardware or the game lacks it.
claims.coverage: Exhaustive, not sampled: every texel inside the UV rectangle of every blended primitive of every layer of all 129 packs was classified against its own primitive's palette - 18,120,302 texels over 16,382 primitives. Opaque primitives were excluded because the hardware never consults the bit for them. The count of primitives mixing the two classes is 0, so a single counterexample anywhere in the shipped data would have shown up as a non-zero tally rather than being averaged away.
claims.frontier_rationale: Closes the per-texel STP limitation carried by fx-mesh-nibble-zero-primitive-is-opaque and fx-mesh-transparent-texel-is-palette-entry-zero.

claims.statement: The op6 flight object's update FIGHTSTG_F0x8008970c, in state 0, copies the launch command's two vectors into the object at +0x90..+0x94 and +0x96..+0x9a, then builds the mesh animator through FIGHTSTG_F0x800847c4 while passing a pointer to flight+0x74 as the animator's control block. Because flight+0x74+0x1c is flight+0x90 and flight+0x74+0x22 is flight+0x96, the per-frame builder FIGHTSTG_F0x80083e0c reaches those same two vectors when it overwrites the root layer's translation at layer0+0x10 from control+0x1c and the root layer's rotation at layer0+0x18 from control+0x22. That overwrite happens AFTER the track sampler has run, so the root layer's placement each frame is the launch command's data and any keyframes sampled into the root are discarded.
claims.notes: Confirms the walker's existing root placement, which the 2026-07-06 addendum had described in prose but never anchored.
claims.coverage: The ordering claim - sampler first, overwrite second - was read from the builder's straight-line control flow rather than inferred: the call to the sampler driver FIGHTSTG_F0x80083c30 is at 0x800840cc and the six overwrite stores run at 0x800840f0 through 0x80084154, with no branch between them that could reverse the order. The offset arithmetic tying control+0x1c to flight+0x90 was resolved to absolute offsets rather than compared as written. || Isolated review 2026-10-05 (docs/research/evidence/reviews/battle-2026-10-05.json): All anchors re-read exact. F0x8008970c state 0 writes the launch command's two vectors to flight+0x90..+0x94 and +0x96..+0x9a (`sh $v1, 0x90` .. `sh $t0, 0x9a` at L6686-6691), then `addiu $v0, $s0, 0x74; sw $v0, 0x10($sp)` (L6683/6692) passes flight+0x74 as the fifth argument to the animator build `jal FIGHTSTG_F0x800847c4` (L6697). The builder F0x80083e0c calls the track sampler F0x80083854 (L130 Anchors re-read: fightstg.s:6683-6699 (state 0: +0x74 fifth arg, two vectors to +0x90..+0x9a, jal F0x800847c4).; fightstg.s:1300-1330 (sampler call at L1303; root overwrite stores L1309, L1314, L1319, L1324, L1329).
claims.frontier_rationale: No catalogued frontier covers the op6 mesh path; tracked in docs/todo/2026-07-05-meft-projectile-mesh-decode.md.

claims.statement: A mesh texel is transparent when its palette ENTRY is 0x0000, which in these pages is index 0 - not when its index is 15, which is what the extractor had assumed. Both halves of the mistake were visible. Index 0 is the background: it is 29.4 percent of the texels inside the rectangles the meshes actually sample, and palette entry 0 is 0x0000 in 318 of the 456 live palettes; it was being baked as opaque BLACK, which is invisible under an additive blend and so went unnoticed until the zero-nibble primitives were correctly drawn opaque. Index 15 is the brightest step of the colour ramp, 7.7 percent of sampled texels, and it was being punched out - deleting the highlight core of every effect. The 89 percent index-15 share measured over a whole page is the unused remainder of the 256x256 page, filled with 0xffff halfwords, which no mesh samples.
claims.notes: This is an extraction-level finding at authority 4, derived from the shipped pages and the PS1's documented texel rule, not from a fightstg instruction that tests the value - the test is in GPU hardware, not in the game's code, so there is no instruction to anchor. It is corroborated by the rendered result: pack 85's two projectiles change from holed near-black silhouettes to solid green bodies with yellow tips. The per-texel STP bit, previously listed here as unmodelled, is measured and closed by fx-mesh-per-texel-stp-is-never-exercised.
claims.coverage: Two texel censuses over all 129 pack pages, one whole-page (8,454,144 texels) and one restricted to the union of the primitives' UV rectangles (1,057,649 texels); the two disagree in exactly the way the unused-fill explanation predicts. Palette entry 0 and entry 15 were tabulated over all 456 live palettes rather than a sample. The page geometry the census depends on was checked for every pack: all 129 texture bins carry the identical 20-byte header declaring 64 halfwords by 256 rows.
claims.frontier_rationale: Same op6 mesh draw path; it is what makes the opaque reading in fx-mesh-nibble-zero-primitive-is-opaque render correctly instead of as black boxes.

claims.statement: The 2D sprite effect path DOES use the PS1's per-texel semi-transparency bit, unlike the op6 mesh path. A sprite clip's semi field is a zero-based ABR mode with -1 meaning not semi-transparent - the shipped values are -1, 0, 1, 2 and 3 - so the bit is consulted exactly when semi is 0 or more, and a texel whose palette entry has bit 15 clear is drawn solid inside an otherwise blended sprite. Of the 1,757 shipped clips, 62 mix the two classes, and within those 62 the drawn pixels are 60.6 percent solid: 96,413 blended against 148,510 solid. Archive 1's ring clips 80 to 83 are 99 percent solid and E144ROSE's 128 by 128 petal is 86 percent, whose palette puts the bright greens at indices 1 to 8 and 11 with the bit clear and the darker greens at 9, 10 and 12 to 14 with it set - a solid body with a blended trailing edge. The walker had been drawing all 62 wholly blended, which reduced archive 1's ring to two stray dots against the arena.
claims.notes: The two paths differ and the difference is now measured, not assumed: the mesh art never sets a texel solid inside a blended primitive and the sprite art does. Not covered: field-overlay MEFT content, which is a different overlay. The mesh display-list grammar itself is fightstg-only - F0x8008610c, which installs the mesh draw entry points, has exactly one caller, so the op6 projectile meshes are the whole mesh population.
claims.coverage: Exhaustive over the sprite path, not sampled: every texel of every frame of every clip of all 50 effect archives was classified against that frame's own palette at that clip's CLUT row, using the extractor's VRAM model, directory parser and frame cutter so the population is exactly what ships. The blended predicate was taken from the semi field's observed domain (-1 39 clips, 0 43, 1 797, 2 90, 3 129) rather than from truthiness, which would have wrongly included the 39 opaque clips and excluded the 43 at mode 0. The 62 figure is re-derived by the extractor on every run and asserted against the shipped manifest in tests/effect-player.test.js, so a change in either direction fails the suite.
claims.frontier_rationale: Bounds the counterpart claim fx-mesh-per-texel-stp-is-never-exercised, which measured only the op6 projectile meshes and explicitly left the sprite path unmeasured.

claims.statement: Two routines in the main program build the graphics processor's drawing-area commands, which fence off the rectangle of the frame buffer the hardware is allowed to draw into. One builds the top-left command and the other the bottom-right; the two bodies are identical apart from the command byte, 0xE3 against 0xE4. Each takes a signed x and y, clamps x to at most one less than the halfword at 0x80055efc and y to at most one less than the halfword at 0x80055efe, replaces a negative coordinate with zero, masks each to 10 bits, and packs them as x in bits 0-9 and y in bits 10-19 under the command byte. The two globals therefore act as the current drawing width and height limits.
claims.coverage: Every clause is anchored to its own line of the original assembly of F0x80026b3c, read instruction by instruction from entry to the delayed return, including the branch that handles a negative coordinate and the jump that skips the second mask. 'Identical apart from the command byte' was tested, not assumed: both bodies were read and the only difference in the operation sequence is the lui immediate 0xe300 against 0xe400 and the global pair each clamps against. The reading that 0xE3 and 0xE4 are the drawing-area commands is NOT taken from documentation: it is consistent with the packing this code performs, x in the low ten bits and y in the next ten, which is the only fact the claim rests on. NOTHING is claimed about where 0x80055efc and 0x80055efe get their values; a scan of the decompiled C for a store to either returned no hits, and that zero is not evidence, because the scan cannot see assembly-only stores.
limitations: Where 0x80055efc and 0x80055efe are written is not established, so 'current drawing width and height limits' describes how they are USED here, not where they come from.
The three callers of these builders were not read, so what sets the drawing area and when is unknown.
Static only; no runtime capture.

claims.statement: s810 native events 9000 and 9001 implement an inverse persistent layout switch: depending on D0x80048d34+0x26e4, they register type-7 resource 0x06ed0003 or 0x06ed0004, replace scene context +0x14 with step program 0x800a7aac or 0x800a7dac, and write latch 0 or 0x20. Because type 7 is consumed by story/warp region selection and the replacement pointers are 24-byte step programs, the strongest player-facing interpretation is a two-state Gunslinger 1F multi-destination warp/topology switch. The pointer/resource transaction is assembly-direct; the visible destination mapping requires runtime observation.
claims.coverage: || Re-read 2026-10-06 (docs/research/evidence/reviews/quest-events-2026-10-06.json): wstag810.s 0xc4c/0xcb0 re-read: +0x26e4 gate, register(7,0x06ed0003/4), [0x80099d94]=0x800a7aac/0x800a7dac, latch 0/0x20.

claims.statement: The 3D fight's HP bar is drawn by FIGHTSTG_F0x800934f0. Its length is HP multiplied by 128 and divided by max HP, expressed in 128ths of the full bar, and when HP is above zero but that length would be under 4 the length is forced to 3. Its colour comes from the same quarter-HP comparison the resting pose uses: the routine sign-extends max HP, shifts it right by two, and compares that quarter against the HP the bar is currently showing; when the quarter is less than the shown HP it loads the gradient at 0x800a3490+0x00 and +0x04, packed words 0x00287100 and 0x003ec800, which are RGB 0,113,40 and RGB 0,200,62, green; otherwise it loads +0x08 and +0x0c, 0x001637b3 and 0x000d37ff, which are RGB 179,55,22 and RGB 255,55,13, red. The shown HP is a value eased from the old HP to the new one over 0x1e frames by FIGHTSTG_F0x80093108 and FIGHTSTG_F0x8009328c, so the colour flips during the drain animation rather than at the instant damage lands.
claims.notes: The bar quad's two gradient colours were not tied to particular vertices; the walker draws them top to bottom. The 30-frame drain tween is decoded but not implemented in web/battle.js, which draws live HP. FIGHTSTG_F0x800934f0 was read for the bar and the party status icons only; the rest of the HUD draw, and the DV/Blast gauge that follows it from 0x800a34a0, were not read.
claims.coverage: Read as a single straight-line block: the length computation at .L0x800936b4-.L0x800936d4 and the colour branch at .L0x80093714-.L0x800937dc have no other predecessors inside the loop body, which runs twice (slti 0x2 at .L0x80093814), once per drawn fighter, with the same code. The claim is about that one routine's code, not about every bar the game draws anywhere; the field and menu HP bars were not read.
claims.frontier_rationale: Closes the colour-threshold gap left open by low-hp-resting-stance-threshold-2026-08-19; no cataloged battle frontier covers the fight HUD.

claims.statement: Field actor action mode 0x4c is the Ice Dungeon forced-slide state.
claims.notes: Contradicted 2026-07-28. Controlled s735 capture uses modes 0x4f/0x50, while the separately decoded Submarimon handler selects 0x4b/0x4c for thrust/coast. The old static mode-0x4c mechanics remain valid but their Ice Dungeon semantic attribution does not.
claims.contradiction_rationale: Contradicted 2026-07-28. Controlled s735 capture uses modes 0x4f/0x50, while the separately decoded Submarimon handler selects 0x4b/0x4c for thrust/coast. The old static mode-0x4c mechanics remain valid but their Ice Dungeon semantic attribution does not.

claims.statement: In the controlled s735 Ice Dungeon slide, field step-program record/op 11 calls the leader actor's +0x150 method to enter forced-movement mode 0x4f with a supplied facing and normal +0x68 magnitude; record/op 12 calls +0x154 to enter timed recovery mode 0x50, which restores idle mode 1 and the normal tick handler. Party followers do not enter 0x4f/0x50 and continue through their delayed follower-ring path. The slide region and its direction come from the type-7 trigger grid: a cell's low 5 bits select the step record and its high 3 bits are op 11's glide facing, so the slide direction is a property of the floor cell rather than of player input. Ops 11 and 12 occur only in stages 735 and 736, 35 op-11 and 33 op-12 cells each, with only diagonal facings.
claims.notes: Runtime sampled one s735 edge; original assembly establishes the op-11/op-12 paths, the mode-0x4f/0x50 bodies and the type-7 cell-to-record/argument split, and the extracted grids account for every slide cell in both stages statically. Remains partially_verified until s736 is runtime-sampled and the actor+0x14 cadence behind the 25-tick mode-0x50 hold is identified.

claims.statement: In Ice Dungeon, field step-program op 13 invokes the leader actor method at +0x158 to run a type-0x17 launch-pad transition: it locks the scene, walks the leader to pad center (pad.x+20,pad.y+13), requests and waits for pad state 2, then moves the leader to the signed x/y destination in the op-13 record with quarter-sine easing before snapping exact coordinates and restoring the normal handler. In the controlled second-record s735 replay, the pad center was (464,665), the record destination was (960,80), and controller cleanup completed at trace frame 268. Followers are hidden or parked during the sequence and begin recovery when the controller detaches. The pads themselves are per-stage overlay actors built from a 12-byte record table ({clipBase, guard, x, y}; s735's is at RAM 0x800a67dc, ten slots, slot 3 = (444,652) = the traced pad); the controller selects one by |dx| + 2*|dy|, plays packed 0x0004001d = TELEPORT when it flips the pad into state 2, and the leader's facing during flight is ([0x8004de20] >> 1) & 7. A pad is never inert: alongside the strobe it runs a looping idle script ({0,6}{1,6}{2,68}{1,4}{0,4}, 88 ticks, wstag735 RAM 0x800a6854) whose value is a CLUT row offset on the pad's floor disc, so an untouched pad pulses through three palettes of its own hue - and the hue is its record's clipBase, giving red (base 20/44), blue (28/52/68) and green (36/60) pads.
claims.notes: Runtime sampled only the second s735 record. The reverse s735 pad, both s736 records, record facing 7 semantics, and full follower recovery duration remain open. 2026-07-28: pad actor, art source, strobe script and sound decoded (docs/research/field/launch-pad-actor-decoded.md, EV-field-launch-pad-actor-static). The sampled 'irregular 3,3,4 strobe hold' is superseded by the script's uniform 4 ticks; the sequence's wall-clock rate remains unproven. 2026-07-28 (second pass, from a player report): the idle CLUT-cycling script decoded (EV-field-launch-pad-idle-clut-static) and wired; the strobe column's own CLUT field is left unwritten and assumed zero.
claims.coverage: || Isolated review 2026-10-06 (reviews/world-exploration-2026-10-06.json): Static decode re-read and correct. wstag735 pad table at RAM 0x800a67dc (file 0x9fc): 10 x 12-byte records, slot 3 = {clipBase 0x1c, x 444, y 652} - exactly the traced pad. The init walk (file 0x40-0x88) iterates 10 slots of stride 0xc, skips nonzero guards, passes +4/+8/+0 as a0/a1/a2 to the ctor F0x800a649c. Idle script at 0x800a6854 = {0,6}{1,6}{2,68}{1,4

claims.statement: Three homolog clusters in exe/fns (6 routines, representatives F0x8003198c, F0x80031d5c and F0x8003210c) are read-modify-write operations on one record of an indexed table: each opens with the already-named readIndexedTableRecord4, builds a small record on the stack from its trailing arguments, applies it through the helpers F0x80031a3c and F0x80031a98, and closes with the already-named writeIndexedTableRecord4 on the same three index arguments.
claims.coverage: All 6 members of the 3 clusters were tested for the presence of both accessor calls with the reader occurring before the writer; 6 of 6 matched with no cluster split. F0x8003198c was confirmed against the original assembly. The population searched was the 39 clusters still unnamed at the time, so this does not claim to enumerate every read-modify-write pair in the executable.
limitations: Which table is indexed, and what the modified field means, are not established. The two helpers F0x80031a3c and F0x80031a98 remain unnamed and were not read.
derivation: scratchpad next.py (fingerprint the 39 unnamed clusters by called slots and size band)
scratchpad bracket.py (reader-before-writer test over all unnamed clusters)

claims.statement: The inn's window fold drives the X (horizontal) scale axis. The live draw context's scale triple is (X, Y, Z): the setter F0x8001F5D0 stores its first argument to gp+0x1C0 +0x38, the second to +0x3C and the third to +0x40 (fns.s:16918-16924), and the consumer F0x8002B23C reads component 0 at ($a1) and scales the matrix's row 0 — the first basis — by it, with components 1 and 2 applied to the other basis vectors (fns.s:29767-29785). The inn's fold calls pass the fold value as the first argument, so the fold is a horizontal scale, consistent with the pivot at x=320 (the panel's right edge).
claims.notes: Read 2026-09-13. This is the consumer read the frontier asked for (the three defaults are identical, so only the consumer distinguishes the axes). The inn's exact stack-slot linkage from its scale setter to F0x8001F5D0 was not traced; the axis claim rests on the setter's argument order and the consumer's component mapping, both read directly.
claims.coverage: Both the setter (fns.s:16918-16924) and the consumer (fns.s:29767-29785) were read in the original assembly; the component-to-axis mapping follows from which matrix row each component multiplies.

claims.statement: The inn screen's two 'resolvers' are the same pointer, not two: 0x80044B38 + 0x424 = 0x80044F5C, and the assembly loads both the prompt fold and the refusal (third) fold through that one address — the prompt folds via 'lw $v0, 0x424($s0)' with $s0 = 0x80044B38 and the refusal fold via 'lw $v0, %lo(D0x80044F5C)', then jalr the same value. The decompiler's field access 'D0x80044b38.unk424' and the absolute 'D0x80044f5c' are two spellings of one slot, so the frontier's question of what separates them has no answer.
claims.notes: Read 2026-09-13. The same shape (a struct-base + offset that equals an absolute address the decompiler spells separately) can masquerade as two routines elsewhere; the arithmetic 0x80044b38+0x424=0x80044f5c settles it here.
claims.coverage: The two load sites in F0x80011a? (fns.s .L0x80011cac and .L0x80011d64) were read directly; both jalr the value loaded from the same address.

claims.statement: The player's item bag has a hard, silent 99-per-item stack cap and never goes negative: giving the player one more of an item they already hold 99 of (GiveItem on an id whose bank is 0x80-0x8e) still adds 1 internally and then re-clamps the stored count back down to 99, with no rejection message, no 'inventory full' popup, and no distinct check-before-add; taking away an item they have 0 of similarly floors at 0 instead of going negative. Mechanically: setGameState (F0x800165ac) routes any id whose bank falls in {0x80,0x82,...,0x8e} to F0x800161d8(index, incrementFlag), which stores the per-item count as a single byte at save base D0x80048d34 + 0x7c + index (the same +0x7c array already confirmed to hold single-bit collection items like FishingPole/TreeBoots), incrementing/decrementing by 1 and clamping to [0,99]. All eight nominal banks in that span alias the SAME flat count array because only the index, not the bank value, selects the byte -- there is no evidence of eight separate item categories here, only one shared cap mechanism. This directly answers the frontier's 'quantity limits' question for the stackable-item side of the inventory; it does not cover the field-use effect appliers for the individual consumable effect codes (permanent stat boosts, TP grants, field HP/MP heals), which remain untraced this session.
claims.notes: 2026-09-13 (turn 45) WIRED AND DRIVEN: the walker enforced the cap in the shop's buy path but not in the story/flag grant path. engine/dw3/items.ts addItem and engine/core/state/inventory.ts Inventory.add now clamp each stack to 99 (silent, no rejection), matching F0x800161d8. Pinned by tests/engine/systems/items.test.ts, tests/engine/unit/inventory-party.test.ts and tests/item-economy.test.js (a real s420 GiveItem at 99 stays 99 while the event's other grant lands). Browser proof tools/verify_item_stack_cap.mjs: seeded bag [[9,99]], drove s420's own POST grant; bag after [[9,99],[40,2]] and persisted localStorage keeps 9 at 99.
claims.coverage: || Isolated review 2026-10-06 (reviews/items-2026-10-06.json): Re-read F0x800161d8 (fns.s:6714-6747) and the setGameState dispatch (F0x800165ac, fns.s:6972-7112) against fns.s sha256 803f8ebc589e856d801b173663f7ff1408cdfab36cf5419125d2b8286c647339. Increment path (a1 != 0): `lbu 0x7c(v1); addiu 0x1; sb 0x7c(v1)` stores +1 FIRST, then `sll 0x

claims.statement: In a 3D fight a Digimon's resting pose is the hurt stance while its HP is at or below max HP divided by four, truncating toward zero. WFIGHTMN_F0x800aa9f0 loads the combatant record's max HP (+0x06) and current HP (+0x08), subtracts the pending HP delta, shifts max HP right by two after a round-toward-zero fixup, and calls the fight-stage actor manager's +0x198 entry with 1 when the quarter is not less than the resulting HP and with 0 otherwise. That entry is the address fightstg installs at FIGHTSTG_F0x80088054, FIGHTSTG_F0x80088024, which looks the actor up by slot and stores the flag into its +0x18 base-table field, the same field the animation latch writes and the field an action script's trailing return-to-base record reads.
claims.notes: Read from wfightmn.s (load base 0x800a5de0, function offset 0x4c10) and fightstg.s. Not established: whether the in-fight HP bar changes colour at the same quarter; the bar's drawing code was not located in wfightmn or wfightts. Also unread: the branch at .L0x00004c60 that, for slot 0x10 when the global at 0x800a4460+0xd6 is 6, takes the flag from 0x800a4460+0xdb instead of from HP.
claims.frontier_rationale: No open battle frontier covers the fight-3D resting pose; this closes the 'Not established' note left in docs/research/fight-3d/original-fight-engine.md on 2026-08-19.

claims.statement: The word each map-tile layer hands the draw context is the same ordering-table bucket index that a point-sprite record's layer byte supplies. The point-sprite passes call the graphics-service slot +0x7C with (0x1002, bucket); that body resolves object id 0x1002 and tail-calls F0x8001ecf8, which dispatches through the resolved object's slot 0x138 with the bucket unchanged. The map-tile draw resolves the same id 0x1002 itself and calls the same slot 0x138 directly, passing the per-layer word from the table at 0x8009702c. The routine behind slot 0x138 returns the address of ordering-table entry [argument] in the frame currently being built, and the map draw then links its tile primitives into that entry with the standard 24-bit head/next swap. So the map layers' 7, 3 and 11 and the point sprites' layer byte are indices into one ordering table.
claims.coverage: Both call chains were followed instruction by instruction from the call site to the ordering-table pointer arithmetic; the argument register was checked for intervening writes at each hop. The slot number is identical (0x138) and the object is resolved through the same resident dispatcher at D0x8004df8c with the same id 0x1002 on both paths, so the identity does not rest on a name match.
limitations: No positional test was run: the bucket-8/10 finding is stage-level co-occurrence with layer-2 art, not proof that any prop overlaps it. An anchor-point test was run and did not discriminate -- 0/562 bucket-10 and 35/3582 bucket-6 anchors land on opaque ground art -- which says point sprites of both kinds generally sit in ground cut-outs, and says nothing about their footprints.
The no-toggle finding is scoped to pro/fieldstg.s. Resident code and other overlays were not searched for a write to the map object's presence words.

claims.statement: The game fades the screen with one routine that every menu overlay carries its own copy of. The object it drives has a phase at +0xc, an enable at +0x10, a direction flag at +0x58, a level at +0x5c and a per-frame delta at +0x60. In phase 1 the level moves by the delta each frame; with the direction flag clear it rises and is clamped at 0xff00, with the flag set it falls and is clamped at 0. Reaching either end moves the object to phase 2. Phases 1 and 2 both call the same drawing step, which shifts the level right by 8 and writes the resulting 0..255 value into all three colour bytes of a 320-wide full-screen primitive - so the level is 8.8 fixed point and the fade is a neutral grey, never a tint. Phase 0 and any unrecognised phase call the object's own method at +0x38 instead; phase 3 does nothing. The routine is in the EXE at F0x80011fb8 and is copied into 10 further overlays: stcrdabm, stcrddek, stcrdshp, stdgname, stfgtrep, stgdglab, stgmcard, stgtrain, stitshop and ststatus.
claims.coverage: The list of 10 overlays is an enumeration over all 318 ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003/pro/*.s files: each was reduced to its instruction-word stream and searched for the full 45-word pattern with value-construction immediates masked and every load/store displacement intact, so the object layout stayed the discriminator. All 10 hits are exactly the 10 pro/ members the semantic family index lists; the eleventh member is the EXE copy, which that scan cannot reach because it only covers pro/. The mechanism is read from the EXE copy's assembly instruction by instruction, including both clamp branches and the fall-through into the shared drawing step; the 10 overlay copies inherit it from matching that pattern. 26 of the 318 files carry no instruction-word column and are outside the scan. 'Every menu overlay' in the first sentence means the 10 named ones, not a tested claim about the full overlay set.
claims.frontier_rationale: Found while naming unnamed function families, not while working a listed UI frontier. It is a shared chrome primitive spanning ten menu overlays plus the EXE, so it belongs to ui-chrome rather than to any single screen's frontier.

claims.statement: The claim that F0x800143dc generally stores ceil(extraSize/4) at object+0x20 is falsified. For non-negative a2 the code stores a2 >> 2 directly; its add-three adjustment occurs only for negative a2 to implement signed division truncating toward zero.

The complete F0x80014504 body contains only its stack prologue, jal F0x800143dc with delay-slot a3=0, and epilogue, so it preserves incoming a0-a2. F0x800143dc uses a0 as callback, allocates a1 bytes for the primary object, and when a2 is nonzero allocates a2 bytes separately into object+0x24 and stores signed a2/4 truncated toward zero at object+0x20. When a3 is nonzero it stores a3 at object+0x00 and registers the object. Thus the shipped positive, four-byte-aligned tutorial and Fire Dungeon values 0x28, 0x14, and 0x0c are separate extra-state byte sizes, not object types.

claims.statement: F0x80014504 preserves callback, primary object size, and the third argument when it calls F0x800143dc, forcing only a3 to zero. In F0x800143dc the third argument is an optional separately allocated extra-state byte size: its allocation result is stored at object+0x24 and signed size/4 truncated toward zero at object+0x20 (the add-3 path applies to negative inputs only; the shipped 0x28/0x14/0x0c are 4-aligned so both readings agree there). The fourth argument is the optional registry key stored at object+0x00 before registration. Therefore the tutorial and Fire Dungeon allocator values 0x28, 0x14, and 0x0c are extra-state sizes, not object types.

They split into two classes by the extractor's is_overlay_ptr/is_resident_ptr test: 53 events point into their own WSTAG overlay, covering 23 distinct (stage, overlay offset) entry points — s210 {0xa00, 0xfe8, 0x15d0}, s220 {0x650, 0xc38, 0x1220}, s270 {0x61c, 0xc04}, s280 {0x5ec}, s740 {0x28c x16}, s741 {0x28c x16}, s745 {0x244, 0x2c4, 0x344}, s746 {0x244, 0x2c4, 0x344}, s810 {0xc4c, 0xcb0}, s924 {0xc88, 0x1620}, s935 {0xc24, 0x15bc} — and 16 events point at the single RESIDENT fieldstg routine at RAM 0x8008bf38, exactly once each in s350, s351, s375, s376, s380, s400, s401, s530, s531, s535, s538, s550, s551, s740, s949 and s953. Two of the 24 distinct entry points (the resident 0x8008bf38 and wstag740 file 0x28c) were verified instruction-by-instruction against original assembly at recording; of the remaining 22 in-overlay entry points, 21 were decoded by 2026-08-04 (the tutorial controllers, the s745/s746 switch commands and the s810 type-7 switch) and s741 file 0x28c remains enumerated only.

claims.statement: The card duel hides the opponent's hand after the deal collapse and does not re-show it until the opponent's Summon Phase: the run-2 dump has the hand slots go to state 0 at frame 611, with no sample until frame 2055, where each card is revealed by the same in-place scale ramp the player's rows use (anim 2, duration 10, scaleX rising from 820 to 4096 over frames 2055-2062). The dealt-board capture's frame-1176 full-width reading is not in the frame-by-frame dump, so the walker's immediate post-deal reopen was a guess; it now stays edge-on and reveals on the Summon Phase.

claims.statement: The Change-digivolve-type grid confirm reaches set_equipped through the pointer cell at 0x8004b470: the screen loads the word at 0x8004b470 and jumps through it with jalr (stgdglab.s:3752-3756), and the cell holds F0x800177d0, the roster-context +0x273c method (checked extraction, data.rs:3197). F0x800177d0 calls the id matcher F0x8001764c (a 44-entry matcher, slti 0x2c, returning an index or -1, with no stores) and, on a match, writes the chosen triple to record+0x50, i.e. ctx+slot*0x3dc+0x7b0 (fns.s:8195). On a no-match it writes 0xffff into that same first word (fns.s:8198), which is the blank-triple mark -- the earlier 'no entry writes 0xffff' negative was wrong and is withdrawn. It does not write the deployed order: the caller reads record+0x4 but never writes it, and the set_equipped body writes only the three triple words.
claims.notes: Static authority 2/4. Supersedes the rejected negative of PARTY-C-CONFIRM-WRITEBACK-TRIPLE.

claims.statement: stgdglab F0x8008ec50 (the Lab screen method at +0x74, lab_count_and_pack_party) counts the three fixed party words at 0x80048d34+0x70 into the object's +0x60, incrementing for each word that is not negative, then packs the non-negative words toward the front of the same three slots and writes -1 into each slot it moved a word out of. The party array stays three words wide; a negative word is an empty slot, contributes nothing to the count, and matches no candidate ordinal in the Switch builder that PARTY-C004 reads. In this overlay the routine occupies the +0x74 method-table slot (pointer at stgdglab.s file 0xc364) and is entered by one jal at L12361, in a caller that first writes 3 to object+0x5c.

It does NOT establish whether the Switch first list offers an empty slot or how the confirm writes; that remains PARTY-Q001's open part. The walker stores the party densely (the packed form) and uses party.length as the count.

claims.statement: Writers are identified for 19 of the 19 persistent stat fields, across four distinct paths. (1) The resident generic mutator F0x800170c8 can add a signed clamped delta to any of the 19 fields by index (all 19 of 19), but the checked-in EXE assembly shows no symbolic call site for it, so it is a shared utility rather than a mapped gameplay entrypoint. (2) The stgtrain gym overlay writes the roster halfwords directly with its own helpers: 0x800861bc adds and 0x800862d0 subtracts across +0x28..+0x30 (cur_str..cur_spd, clamp 999 / floor 0), 0x800863d4 adds across +0x34..+0x40 (cur_fire..cur_dark, clamp 999), and 0x800865a0 adds max_hp at +0x22 and max_mp at +0x26 (clamp 9999) - 14 of 19 fields, excluding level, tp, cur_hp, cur_mp and cur_chr. (3) F0x8001104c restores the three deployed party members by copying max_hp into cur_hp and max_mp into cur_mp (2 of 19). (4) Per-level growth is driven by the species DigimonProfile per-level growth rate bytes growth_hp/mp/str/def/spt/wis/spd/chr and growth_fire..growth_dark (18 growth bytes), which is the only identified writer of cur_chr. CANDIDATE: paths (1)-(3) rest on prior research documents that cite assembly (authority 5) and were not re-verified against assembly in this session; path (4) is a structural field list from the decoded profile table and the actual level-up application routine was not located or disassembled here, so the arithmetic that turns a growth byte into a stat delta remains unproven.

The card duel's count*4+10 widget (duel+0x4D8) is the centre-row pile FAN/REVEAL, not a HUD deck or trash pile lift. F0x8009DBE8 places every card of the pile edge-on at its final fan position (fan x, y 0x6100, sprite scale x = 0) and binds it to its pile card; F0x8009E668 then reveals them in index order: the +0x4D0 cadence accumulator is zeroed at setup and a card may start only once it has reached 4 (then the accumulator is reduced by 4 and the card index incremented), and each start runs the shared scale command F0x8009C898 as a 10-frame linear tween of scale x from 0 to 0x1000 with scale y held at 0x1000 (the collapse family uses a 5-frame tween to 0). So card i starts at tick 4*(i+1), nothing moves in y, there is no alpha fade, and the last card's ramp ends exactly at count*4+10. It also corrects two earlier texts: the duration claim's 'shuffling a full pile' rationale is unsupported, and the pile-picker claim's 'duel+0x4D4 written at none' is falsified because +0x4D4 is the count, written by F0x8009DF68/F0x8009DBE8.

F0x800140d8 (exe/fns, RAM 0x800140d8-0x8001410c) resolves one member of an archive in 14 instructions and contains no compare and no conditional branch. It keeps the low 16 bits of its argument as an entry index, passes the argument shifted right 16 to F0x80013e5c, scales the index by 4, adds it to F0x80013e5c's return value, loads the word stored there, and returns that word added to the same return value -- i.e. base + base[index], with the entry table sitting at the base and holding offsets relative to it. The base is a loaded resource: F0x80013e5c looks its argument up through F0x800139fc and returns the word at +0x0c of the resulting record only when that record's state halfword at +0x00 equals 3, spinning on a poll otherwise, so the low and high halves of F0x800140d8's argument are an entry index and a resource id respectively. Because the body holds no conditional branch, it range-checks nothing and null-checks nothing: an out-of-range index reads whatever follows the entry table and returns a pointer derived from it, and a null base is not detected. It is reached only through a pointer: no direct call to it exists anywhere in the original assembly corpus, and the shipped data segment initialises the cell 0x80044f5c to its address (data.rs L2233).

claims.statement: F0x8002006c (exe/fns, RAM 0x8002006c-0x80020200) is the routine that receives packed sound ids. Two controlled runtime captures with a breakpoint on this address each recorded the value 0x00040004 arriving in its argument register at a scripted field entrance, from the same return address, and nothing else arriving through the following several hundred frames (EV-holeentry, EV-seabed9entry, authority 1); those captures record the instrumented value and a visual timeline, not the audio itself. It is reached only through a pointer: no direct call to it exists anywhere in the original assembly corpus, and the shipped data segment initialises the cell 0x80055c48 to its address (data.rs L7643). Its head splits one 32-bit argument into eight overlapping bit fields (bits 24-18, bit 31, bit 30, bits 17-11, bits 10-7, bits 6-0, bits 15-8, bits 7-0) using paired shift and mask instructions at 0x80020078-0x800200c0. Two early returns follow, both returning 0 through the epilogue at 0x800201d4: first, the bits 24-18 field -- unmodified between its extraction and the call -- is passed to F0x80020030, and a -1 result returns immediately, so a request whose 24-18 field that routine rejects does nothing and reports no error; second, and ONLY when the bit 30 field is set (the gate at 0x800200f4), the word at D0x800519ec+0x4248 is compared with the incoming argument and an equal value returns immediately, so repeating a request whose argument already equals that stored word does not run the rest of the routine. What each bit field SELECTS is not established here, nor is anything the routine does after the exclusive-track gate.

claims.statement: On stage s276 the map-tile ground layer is cut out completely underneath the layer-2 art: none of the 116,307 opaque layer-2 texels, spread over 16 of the stage's 28 map cells, sits over an opaque layer-0 texel. In nine of those cells layer 0 carries no object at all; in the other seven the two layers' rectangles intersect but their art does not. The two layers therefore partition the stage surface rather than stacking, so layer 2's ordering-table depth of 11 (behind layer 0's 7) cannot hide it, and ddw3's stitcher compositing layer 2 on top of layer 0 produces the same visible result on this stage as the console's back-to-front order would.
claims.coverage: The quantifier is an exhaustive per-texel enumeration, not a sample. tools/audit_map_layer_overlap.py walked all 28 entries of s276pack.toml, took the 16 that carry any layer-2 object, and rasterised EVERY object of layers 0 and 2 in those cells into the cell's coordinate space, discarding only texels whose alpha is 0 in the extracted tile image. The intersection was counted, not inferred: a single overlapping texel anywhere would have shown as a non-zero count in the per-cell row. The same tool run over all 60 stages that carry layer-2 art reports 85,750 overlapping texels on 14 other stages, up to 47.3 percent on s411, which demonstrates the counter is capable of returning non-zero and that a zero on s276 is a measurement rather than a defect.
limitations: Measured on ddw3's extracted map-tile configs and tile PNGs, not re-derived from the disc image. If the extractor mis-places an object the same error moves both layers together, so the disjointness would survive an offset error but an alpha error would not.

Geometry only. This says nothing about whether layer 2 is always visible, or what would toggle it; the 2026-07-04 note's 'visibility-toggled roof/interior layer' reading is neither supported nor refuted here.
Nothing was checked against the running game. No rig capture of s276 was taken.

claims.statement: In stage s415 the effect-object animation player at wstag415 0x800a645c walks a table of 4-byte records laid out as halfword 0 = frame id and halfword 2 = hold time in ticks, not the reverse: halfword 2 is added to the countdown at obj+0x16, while halfword 0 is both the value returned to the caller as the frame to show and the value compared against 0xff to end the sequence. On reaching the 0xff record the player steps back one record and re-adds that record's hold time, so the sequence stops on its last real frame and stays there; there is no loop back to the start. Elapsed ticks come from a function pointer read at 0x8004df9c and are clamped to at most 4 per call. The three shipped sequences are 0x800a73f0 (9 steps, frames 50,52,53,54,55,56,57,58,59 held 5,5,5,40,8,8,10,12,180), 0x800a7418 (3 steps, frames 60,61,62 held 4,4,999) and 0x800a7428 (47 steps, frames 1 to 47 each held 4 ticks).
claims.notes: Corrects docs/research/field/s415-deeper-crevice-ride-decode.md, which records the layout as {u16 duration, u16 frame_id} (inverted) and describes 0x800a7428 as a '14+ frame loop' (it is 47 frames, and this player has no loop-back). The terminator record's own halfword 2 is never read by this player. The identity of the 0x8004df9c provider was not established.
claims.coverage: Layout read from the four instructions that consume a record -- cursor advance, hold-time load, terminator compare, return value -- which is every read of a record in the function; the disassembly of 0x800a645c is 40 instructions and was read in full. The three sequence tables were walked programmatically from their first record to the 0xff terminator, so the step counts are enumerated, not sampled: 0x800a7428 is 47 records with frame fields exactly 1..47 contiguous and every hold field equal to 4. Scoped to wstag415 alone -- about 294 wstag overlays share load base 0x800a5de0 and no other overlay was read, so nothing here is claimed for any other stage.

If the flag is clear the player gets the first-visit version: the scrolling layer object is spawned with its parameter set to 1, the boulder actor is spawned as well, and event 0x97 (151) is started. If the flag is already set the return-visit version runs instead: the scrolling layer is spawned with parameter 0, no boulder actor is spawned, and event 0x96 (150) is started. claims.statement: Stage s415 has two animation players in wstag415, not one, and they differ only in what happens at the end of a sequence. Both read the same 4-byte records. The player at 0x800a645c steps back one record on the 0xff terminator, so its sequence ends on its last real frame and stays there. The player at 0x800a5df4 instead resets the cursor to the table base and the step index to zero, so its sequence repeats from the beginning forever. The one-shot player is used by the main actor at 0x800a6558 for its three canned sequences 0x800a73f0, 0x800a7418 and 0x800a7428; the looping player is used by the falling-object update at 0x800a5fa8, whose sequence pointer is the first word of a 16-byte-per-entry table at 0x800a7350 indexed by the object's spawn parameter.

claims.statement: The scene descriptor at 0x80099d80 has a fifteenth field that no published field map lists: +0x44, written by 293 of the 294 stage overlays. Its value is not a constant. The setup routine loads the seven-language selection index from 0x8005cca8 and adds a per-stage constant to it. Across all 293 stages only ten distinct constants appear, and they form an exact arithmetic run with a step of 7: 197, 204, 211, 218, 225, 232, 239, 246, 253, 260. Seven is the number of languages the game ships, so the field resolves to base + language over ten blocks of seven consecutive ids - a per-area, per-language resource id, with the 293 stages falling into ten area groups of 56, 46, 40, 31, 29, 26, 24, 23, 13 and 5 stages. Which resource the id names, and which code reads +0x44, are NOT established: a reader scan of fieldstg finds no read of +0x44 through a tracked base, and that scan cannot see reads through an untracked base or from another overlay.
claims.coverage: '293 of 294' and 'only ten distinct constants' are both enumerations over every wstagNNN.s file in ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003/pro/ (294 files), using the committed overlay scanner's own constant tracker but WITHOUT the filter that requires the stored value to be known: a store counts whenever the base register demonstrably holds 0x80099d80. That run reports +0x44 in 293 files and 0 under the original filter, which is what makes the field invisible to the published census. The ten constants were collected in the same pass and counted; the arithmetic step of 7 was checked by sorting them, and the ten group sizes sum to 293. The identification of 0x8005cca8 as the language index is prior established project knowledge (the seven-language table reached by `dw3-research languages`), not a new inference. The reading 'base + language' is an INTERPRETATION of the step-7 structure, not an observation - no consumer was found, so it is offered as the meaning of the arithmetic and is explicitly marked unresolved in the statement.
limitations: Nothing here identifies the consumer of descriptor +0x44. tools/descriptor_readers.py reports no read in fieldstg or stdwtitl through a tracked base, and that tool only accepts pro/*.s overlays, so the EXE was not searched at all. A zero from it is not evidence of absence and is not used as any.

The 'base + language' reading of +0x44 is an interpretation of a step-7 arithmetic run, supported by the language index being the addend's other operand. It is not confirmed by any consumer, by a resource table, or by a runtime observation.

The scene-setup shape scan covers ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003/pro/*.s only, and only the 292 files that carry an instruction-word column. 66 routines match one of four exact shapes; the remaining stage setups were not classified.
Which stage belongs to which of the ten +0x44 area groups was collected but is not recorded here, and the groups were not checked against any independent notion of a game area.

claims.statement: MEFT1001-1055 are BATTLE effect packs bound by SFSTDATA, not field map effects, which is why no field stage references any of them. SFSTDATA (fight resource 0x1cb) is a flat array of 57 records at stride 0x58; its file is exactly 1254 words with contiguous 4-byte labels, i.e. 57 x 22 words and nothing else. Resolving each record's +0x00 high half through the game's LBA name table (~/ddw3/iso/dw2003-bootstrap/lbas.toml) maps records 1 through 55 onto MEFT1001 through MEFT1055 one-to-one with no exception, plus exactly two aliases: record 0 duplicates MEFT1001 and record 56 duplicates MEFT1034. +0x00 and +0x04 are therefore (fileId<<16)|binIdx resource pointers into the MEFT pack, verified on record 55 which gives program bin 0x20 and CLUT bin 6, byte-matching the independent MEFT1055 pack decode. The readers are in fightstg (F0x80086304 motion rebuild, F0x8008b06c accessor) per special-attack-backdrop-decode.md section 9b, and the record ids reaching them come from the technique table's effect/sigEffect/motion fields. This corrects two recorded statements: falsified-hypotheses.md called the 57-records-to-57-MEFT-files match 'pure numeric coincidence' (it is a real 1:1 mapping), and map-effects-meft.md labelled ids 1001-1055 'FIELD map effects' from the id-range split alone (they are battle assets). What remains correctly falsified is that SFSTDATA is a PER-STAGE binding table: it is indexed by battle effect/motion id, not by stage.

SFSTDATA is the attack-to-effect-pack binding for the 3D battle effect packs MEFT1001-1055, and the mapping is now enumerated exhaustively rather than asserted. The file holds exactly 1254 data words = 57 records x 22 words at stride 0x58. Resolving EVERY record +0x00 high half through the game own LBA name table maps records 1 through 55 onto MEFT1001 through MEFT1055 one-to-one with ZERO mismatches, plus exactly two aliases: record 0 duplicates MEFT1001 and record 56 duplicates MEFT1034. Record +0x00 is therefore a (fileId<<16)|binIdx pack pointer, NOT the baseA<<16|lenA that docs/research/field/map-effects-meft.md recorded for it. There are exactly 55 MEFT10xx packs on disc, not 57: the 57 is this table record count, and that number leaking into a supposed 57 field MEFT files is the origin of the long-lived and false MEFT1001-1055 are field map effects label. This does not supersede sfstdata-binds-meft10xx-battle-packs; it supplies the coverage record that claim never carried.

Every .word line of ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003/pro/sfstdata.s was parsed in order (1254 words, matching the 57 x 22 shape the existing anchor states), reshaped into all 57 records at stride 0x58, and each record +0x00 high half was resolved through ~/ddw3/rust/dw2003_exe_data/src/lba.rs (2368 LBA name constants). claims.statement: Three of the six shadow-denied constructor kinds are reachable by a party follower, not just by an NPC. Follower kind is speciesId + 3, so denied kinds 130, 131 and 213 correspond to species 127 MarineDevimon, 128 Dragomon and 210 Scorpiomon2; the remaining denied kinds 287, 316 and 319 would require species 284, 313 and 316, which exceed the maximum valid species id of 250 and so can only ever be npc_ids. All three follower-reachable species are aquatic Digimon, which is the first candidate explanation for the denylist: a swimming partner form is drawn without a ground drop shadow. A player would see that specific partner walking with no shadow while other party members have one.
claims.notes: Derived 2026-08-04 from the verified constructor decode (field-shadow-ctor-default-and-denylist) plus the canonical DigimonId enum. TWO EXPLICIT UNKNOWNS, neither of which this claim asserts past: (1) it is NOT verified that the value the constructor receives as speciesId uses this DigimonId numbering rather than a roster-relative index - the producing method at party-controller ctx+0x2728 was not traced, and the separately documented ctx+0x2718 is a DIFFERENT offset; (2) the aquatic reading is a HYPOTHESIS from the three species' identities, not a decoded rule - no code tests an aquatic attribute, and the three unreachable kinds 287/316/319 are unexplained by it. Do not present the aquatic explanation as ground truth. Settling (1) is the bounded next step and would also decide whether this is a real in-game visual behaviour or an unreachable code path.
claims.contradiction_rationale: REFUTED 2026-08-04 by tracing the producer at ctx+0x2728 to F0x80016fd8, which returns the roster-slot ordinal (0-7), not a DigimonId. The follower kind is roster_slot + 3, i.e. 3..10, and is numerically incapable of reaching the denylist regardless of which form the partner has digivolved into. The unverified assumption this claim explicitly flagged - that the constructor's speciesId used the canonical DigimonId numbering - was wrong, and the aquatic reading built on it does not survive. The denylist is reachable only through the npc_id path.

claims.statement: The shadow's ground offset at entity+0x90 is discrete and scripted, not continuous terrain following. An exhaustive store census over the whole field overlay finds eleven writers: the three known scripted move methods, seven sites inside the move dispatcher F0x8008fed0 (including its private reset helper F0x8008fd60, which only that dispatcher calls and which always stores literal zero), and one write that belongs to a different, larger object entirely. Every genuine writer changes the offset by a fixed step of 0, plus or minus 0x100, or plus or minus 0x300, gated on clip or sub-phase state and clamped against fixed thresholds. None reads terrain geometry, a collision result, or any per-frame continuous input. In play the shadow never slides smoothly with the ground under a character; it steps at a fixed rate while a movement clip runs and then snaps back at the clip boundary.

Stack-relative stores are excluded by the scanner and cannot alias a heap-allocated entity.

claims.statement: FIGHTSTG_F0x8009e994, reached through the fightstg data pointer D0x800a4570, is the smdldata consumer. It requests resource 0x1cc, takes the file's header words 1 to 3 as the index-table, section-2 and section-3 base offsets, and linear-scans the 4-byte index entries comparing their u16 key field against its argument until a zero key terminates the walk. On a match it reads the entry's self-index byte and slot byte; a slot byte below 0x3a (58) selects section 2 and resolves the record as section2_base + selfIndex * 0xC4, otherwise section 3 and section3_base + selfIndex * 0x48. The resolved key, the section flag, the self-index, the slot and the resolved record pointer are cached at 0x800a4558 so a repeat request for the same key skips the scan.
claims.notes: Resolves MDL-Q002, which asked which code loads and walks smdldata given that a name search returns nothing. The consumer was found structurally, through the fightstg data pointer D0x800a4570, not by name. The 0xC4 stride is formed at 0x8009ea88-0x8009ea98 as ((v1*2+v1)<<4 + v1)<<2 = 196*selfIndex and the 0x48 stride at 0x8009e9e4-0x8009e9f0 as ((v1*8)+v1)<<3 = 72*selfIndex.

claims.statement: pro/smdldata.s is a self-describing container, not code. Its first four words are a header: word0 = 0x80082cb0, the base every interior self-pointer resolves against, then three section offsets 0x10, 0x2458 and 0x4e74. Record strides were measured from the period of the self-pointers, not assumed, and both close exactly: section 2 is 55 records of 0xC4 bytes, since 0x2458 + 55*0xC4 = 0x4E74, the header's own next section offset; section 3 is 193 records of 0x48 bytes, since 0x4E74 + 193*0x48 = 0x84BC, exactly end of file (last word at 0x84B8). Each record in both sections carries a pointer at +0x0C into a shared data pool that begins at file 0x3F0; the first such pointer, 0x800830a4, resolves to file 0x3F4. Section 1 is not payload but two index tables plus that pool. The file therefore has the shape of a two-population asset container: 55 of one kind, 193 of another, sharing one blob pool.

Section 1 holds two 4-byte-per-entry index tables ahead of the shared pool. Table A is 55 entries at file 0x10..0xEC; table B is 193 entries at file 0xEC..0x3F0; the pool follows at 0x3F0. Their entry counts equal the record counts of sections 2 and 3 exactly. Each entry is little-endian [u16 key][u8 self-index][u8 slot]. The self-index field is the decisive structural evidence: it runs 0..54 across table A and restarts at 0 and runs 0..192 across table B, with no gap, which fixes both the 4-byte stride and the field split and locates the boundary between the tables at file 0xEC. The slot field is a permutation - table A's 55 slot values are exactly the set 1..55 with no repeat, and table B's 193 slot values are exactly the set 58..250 with no repeat - so together the two tables partition a single 1..250 slot space with 56 and 57 unused. The key field holds 55 distinct values in 0x0003..0x01D6 for table A and 193 distinct values in 0x0004..0x01D3 for table B. So each table is a lookup from an external id (key) to a slot in that shared 250-entry space, carrying its own position as the third field.

The shared pool that each smdldata record's +0x0c points at holds that Digimon's animated-texture list. FIGHTSTG_F0x8009eb94 relocates the stored pointer by subtracting header word 0, and FIGHTSTG_F0x8008b508 - its only caller, reached from 0x80083f90 with the fighter's model key taken from fighter+0x64 then +0x14 - walks the slot as up to 16 ten-byte entries, ending on 0xff in byte 0 (0x8008b5a4) and skipping an entry whose byte 2 is zero. Each live entry becomes one element of a 0x14-stride array at +0x60 of a 0x1a8-byte display object and is re-issued every frame as a GP0(0x80) VRAM-to-VRAM copy rectangle: FIGHTSTG_F0x8008b160 reads destination x/y from bytes 0 and 1 (0x8008b1c0), width and height from bytes 2 and 3, and a source x/y pair chosen by the current variant from bytes 4..9 (0x8008b180), then F0x8002918c writes the 0x80000000 command word plus source, destination and size into the primitive (fns.s 0x800291c0). Every coordinate is relative to the fighter's own VRAM strip, whose origin F0x8008b508 copies off the parent at +0x68/+0x6c (0x8008b550) and which F0x80084560 filled from the four-entry table D0x800a2530 = (832,0), (896,0), (960,0), (960,256).
claims.notes: The pool slot pointer of one record (key 148) is emitted by the disassembler as a symbol rather than a hex literal, so a hex-only .word pattern reads it as zero; tools/extract_smdldata.py was fixed for this. What the picture in each rectangle actually depicts is not established from the code - only that three variants exist and which one is selected when.
claims.coverage: That the coordinates are strip-relative is tested, not assumed, and the test could have failed: all 248 pool slots were walked by the game's own rule and every live entry's destination rectangle and all three source rectangles were checked against a 64x256 box. Maxima are 63 in x and 232 in y, with 0 violations out of 204 records that have at least one live entry; a wrong origin or a wrong field order would put rectangles outside the strip. The per-record counts are a full enumeration of the same walk: 44 records have no live entry, 173 have one, 19 have two, 7 have three, 2 have four, 1 has five and 2 have six; pool slot 0 is live in 202 records and slot 1 in 17, and 18 records use a slot of 2 or higher.

claims.statement: LEAD, NOT A DECODE. smdldata's two populations are 55 and 193. The project's extracted web/assets/data/digimon.json holds exactly 55 playable Digimon with ids 1..55, and table A's slot field is exactly a permutation of 1..55 - two independent 1..55 spaces of the same size. web/assets/data/enemies.json holds 194 enemy records against section 3's 193. The natural reading is that section 2 (0xC4 records) describes the 55 player-side Digimon and section 3 (0x48 records, half the size) the enemy roster, which would make the file battle model/animation data as its name suggests. THIS IS A COUNT CORRELATION ONLY. No field inside any record has been interpreted, no key has been shown to be a species id, and the enemy count is off by one with no explanation offered. The overlay census explicitly warns that smdldata's filename is not a description of its contents, and that warning is NOT yet discharged: nothing here proves the records hold geometry or animation rather than, say, per-combatant presentation parameters. To settle it, interpret the 0xC4 record for one table-A key and check whether its pool blob has the shape of a known PS1 model or animation container.

Two fields of an smdldata record are interpreted by the fight arena placement routine FIGHTSTG_F0x80087f38, which reaches the record through FIGHTSTG_F0x8009e994. Field +0x10 is the Digimon's arena stand-off: it is added to the constant 0x1400 to form the magnitude of that fighter's slot Z. Field +0x18 is its hover height: it is negated to form the fighter's slot Y, so a value of zero stands the Digimon on the arena floor and a positive value lifts it. Resolved across the 248 index entries, +0x10 spans 128 to 12160 and +0x18 is zero in 197 records and between 384 and 2560 in the other 51. Renamon (key 373) carries stand-off 128, which reproduces the player slot Z of -5248 measured in the fight_rena.bin capture.
claims.notes: The 248 keys are 55 section-2 entries plus 193 section-3 entries, matching the record counts already established in docs/research/battle/smdldata-container-2026-08-05.md. Every one of the 245 shipped model packs under web/assets/battle/models is matched by its folder number to one of these keys; the 3 unmatched keys are 468, 469 and 470.
claims.coverage: The 248 figure and the two value distributions are a full enumeration, not a sample: smdldata.s was parsed word by word into a flat image, the index table at header word 1 was walked to its zero-key terminator (248 entries), each entry's record was resolved by the same slot-byte rule the game uses, and both halfwords were read from every resolved record. A record outside that walk cannot be reached by the game's own lookup, which is the same walk.

claims.statement: No instruction in the original code reads smdldata record fields +0x12, +0x14 or +0x16. The arena placement routine FIGHTSTG_F0x80087f38 reads the halfword on either side of them - +0x18 at 0x80087f84 and +0x10 at 0x80087f94 - and skips the three between. A forward taint of the record pointer over all of pro/fightstg.s, seeded at every entry a record pointer has into a register, reports the complete set of offsets read as +0x00, +0x02, +0x04, +0x08, +0x0c, +0x10, +0x18 and +0x44 plus the index-scaled camera offsets +0x1a/+0x1c/+0x1e, +0x2c/+0x2e/+0x30, +0x3e, +0x62/+0x64/+0x66 and +0xaa; +0x12, +0x14 and +0x16 are absent. Because they have no reader they cannot be named from behaviour, and the earlier reading of +0x14/+0x16 as a body-size pair remains an untested guess. Their shipped values are regular: +0x12 is zero in 209 of 248 records and otherwise spans -640 to 742, +0x14 is positive in every record and spans 384 to 7680, and +0x16 is zero in 75 records and otherwise spans -1024 to 10240.
claims.notes: A negative about the shipped code, not about the data: the three fields hold structured values and were presumably meaningful to whatever tool authored the table. They are extracted into web/assets/battle/model_placement.json as models[key].unread so the values are preserved without being interpreted.
claims.coverage: The absence is mechanical, not a reading. tools/trace_smdldata_record_reads.py performs a conservative intra-procedural forward taint over pro/fightstg.s, seeded at (a) the return register after each of the eight calls through the accessor cell D0x800a4570, (b) the return register after the one jal to FIGHTSTG_F0x8009e994, and (c) both loads of the cached record pointer at 0x800a4558+0x10 and +0x14 - ten seeds, which is every path by which a record pointer enters a register. It propagates through move, addiu and addu and drops a register on any other write, so it can only under-report, never over-report; it independently recovers all eleven camera-array offsets that were decoded by hand, which is the check that it is not simply failing to follow the pointer. Restricting the scan to fightstg is justified by the resolved frontier MDL-Q002: fightstg is the only overlay that walks the container, and code-search over 590137 lines of original assembly finds the accessor object 0x800a4558 referenced in only one other overlay, wfightts, which reads the cached key at +0x00, the cached slot at +0x0c and the by-index method cell at +0x1c and never a record field. No routine passes a record pointer as an argument, which is what makes an intra-procedural walk sufficient.

claims.statement: Field +0x44 of a section-3 (0x48-byte) smdldata record is a 1-based canned camera shot number. FIGHTSTG_F0x8009257c resolves the fighter standing in arena slot 0x10 (the far side), calls the record lookup through the accessor cell, takes the cached record pointer at 0x800a4558+0x14 (0x800925e4), reads lh 0x44 of it (0x800925ec) and passes the value minus one to the canned-shot selector F0x800923b4 as its shot index, with the near-side layout selector 0. Over all 193 section-3 records the field takes only the values 1 through 6, so the index handed to the selector is 0..5, inside the twelve-shot near-side array. The offset exists only in the 0x48 stride: in a 0xC4 record +0x44 is still inside the camera eye array (eye[7].x).
claims.notes: That the far slot always holds a section-3 record is NOT established here; the routine reads slot 0x10 and whatever record that fighter resolves to. The walker extracts the field as models[key].shot but does not yet drive its intro camera from it.
claims.coverage: The 1..6 range is a full enumeration of the shipped table, not a sample: all 248 index entries were walked to the zero-key terminator and +0x44 read from every record, split by the same slot-byte rule the game uses; the 193 section-3 records give 1 (15), 2 (70), 3 (45), 4 (32), 5 (30), 6 (1), and the 55 section-2 records give 50 distinct large signed values consistent with camera data rather than a count, which is the independent check that would have exposed a wrong stride.

claims.statement: The first three words of an smdldata record are three packed resource references of the form (resource << 16) | member, the split F0x800140d8 performs at fns.s 0x800140e0 and 0x800140ec before resolving the resource with F0x80013e5c and returning base + base[member]. The +0x00 reference is the model's part directory, read at FIGHTSTG 0x80087d94 and passed with the +0x04 reference (0x80087d98) into F0x80084790 -> F0x80084560, which takes directory word 1 as a part count (0x800845bc) and builds one 0x84-byte actor part block per following (index, member, member) triple, OR-ing the record's resource id back into the two member halves (0x80084704). The +0x08 reference is read at 0x8008c650 and stored on the fight actor at +0x80. The high half the three words share is read separately as a halfword at +0x02 (0x80086b08, 0x80089e2c, 0x8008bae4) and handed to the loader ready-test F0x80013a6c and request F0x80013c30; it is a CD resource index in the same 2382-entry LBA id space in which smdldata itself is 0x1cc, and it names that Digimon's own model pack.

claims.statement: F0x8001f648 fills a caller-owned stack handle with twelve fixed routine addresses, the same twelve on every call, chosen by no argument and no object class: handle+0x70 F0x8001ecb0, +0x74 F0x8001ecbc, +0x78 F0x8001ecd8, +0x7c F0x8001ed34, +0x80 F0x8001ecf8, +0x84 F0x8001ed6c, +0x88 F0x8001ecec, +0x8c F0x8001f5d0, +0x90 F0x8001f5ec, +0x94 F0x8001f608, +0x98 F0x8001f61c, +0x9c F0x8001f628. It also presets +0x24, +0x28..+0x2a and +0x38..+0x40 and publishes the handle by tail-calling F0x8001ecb0, which stores it at gp+0x1c0. The offsets recorded in recovered/ddw3/function-inventory.json for these call sites are FRAME offsets, and the handle sits at sp+0x10 in the functions carrying 1741 of the 2104 stack-based sites, so a frame offset must have its function's handle base subtracted before it is read as a slot. With that subtraction, 1750 of the 9204 unresolved struct_function_slot sites resolve to a named routine with no dataflow on the receiver, distributed handle+0x74 245, +0x78 23, +0x7c 204, +0x80 4, +0x84 556, +0x88 139, +0x8c 303, +0x94 258, +0x98 17, +0x9c 1.
claims.notes: What the twelve routines do is NOT established, only that the table is constant. The 275 sites with no recovered base and the 79 outside the band were not read. The handle base was taken from the m2c body (authority 3), not from the assembly, for every function; only the twelve-address table itself is assembly-checked. No claim is made about receivers held in a register or passed in as an argument.
claims.coverage: The twelve stores are the routine's whole straight-line body between prologue and epilogue, read consecutively at fns.s L16977-L17011 (RAM 0x8001f668-0x8001f724); no branch separates them, which is what establishes 'the same twelve on every call'. claims.statement: Ten stage overlays carry the same 23-instruction constructor for a class-0x17 field actor. It calls the shared actor factory F0x800143dc with four arguments - a per-stage code address, size 0x6c, 0, and class 0x17 - and then stores its own three arguments into the returned object at +0x54, +0x58 and +0x50. The factory allocates 0x6c bytes, installs the default method table, keeps the first argument at object +0x48, writes class 0x17 to object +0 and registers the object through the global at 0x8004b7b4. Between the ten copies exactly one word differs: the low half of that per-stage code address. The copies are in wstag311, wstag735, wstag736, wstag745, wstag746, wstag750, wstag800, wstag810, wstag815 and wstag820.
claims.coverage: Same enumeration method and same 318-file denominator, with the 23-word pattern taken from wstag311 file 0x15a8; 10 copies found, exactly the 10 the semantic family index lists. 'Exactly one word differs' was tested by printing the complete word-by-word diff of each copy against the wstag311 copy rather than the first divergence: each reports two differing words, one being the addiu that carries the low half of the per-stage address and the other being the jal to F0x800143dc, which my comparison normalises relative to each copy's own start address and which resolves to the same absolute target 0x800143dc in every copy. The lui that carries the high half is identical in all ten because every copy's address is in 0x800a. The 26 files without an instruction-word column are outside the scan.
limitations: The scan denominator is ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003/pro/*.s only. The EXE and every non-pro overlay were not searched, so copies of these routines may exist outside the stage overlays.

26 of the 318 pro/*.s files carry no instruction-word column (they are hand-annotated or data-only, e.g. fightstg, smdldata, stagslct). The scan is blind to them and their zero is not evidence of absence.

What each copy's script actually animates is per-stage and is NOT claimed here; only the stepper's mechanism and its population are. The launch-pad research decodes one stage's scripts in detail; the other stages' scripts are unread.

The class-0x17 constructor's per-stage first argument is identified as a code address from the factory's use of it, and it is a known function start in wstag735 (F0x800a620c). It was not confirmed to be a function start in all ten overlays.
The routines' behaviour is read statically from the assembly. No runtime capture of a cursor advancing was taken in this pass.
