claims.statement: A seventh form of the stage animation stepper drives an actor from a TABLE of sequences rather than from one script, so an actor can play several animations back to back and then repeat the whole set. Its cursor is three fields - a sequence index at +0, an entry index at +2 and a hold timer at +4 which is a full word here rather than a halfword. Its second argument is an array of pointers, one per sequence, each pointing at 4-byte entries. Each call subtracts the frame delta clamped to 4 from the timer, and when the timer runs out it looks at byte 3 of the current entry: zero means advance to the next entry of the same sequence, non-zero means this was the last entry, so the sequence index advances and the entry index resets to 0. If the next pointer in the table is null the sequence index wraps to 0, so the table loops as a whole and there is no way to stop it. The new entry's byte 1 is added to the timer and the routine recurses, so several short entries can retire in one tick. On the outermost call only, byte 0 of the current entry is written to the actor at +4 and byte 2 at +9, so one entry drives two separate actor fields at once. Two copies exist, in wstag480 and wstag481.

claims.statement: Each stage overlay carries a scene-setup routine with one job: fill the scene descriptor at 0x80099d80 with this stage's constants, then ask the zone manager at 0x8009b6c4 to load the stage's resources. The routine puts 0x80099d80 in one register and writes every slot through it, mixing per-stage immediates (map pack id, music id, spawn coordinates) with per-stage overlay addresses (point-sprite table, story-step program, texture-slot array, cast list). It then calls the zone manager's +0x40 method once per resource, each call passing a small kind selector and a 32-bit resource id, and finishes with the +0x50 method to start the queued loads. The number of load requests is per stage: wstag245 makes two, wstag371 and wstag406 make three. The semantic family index splits these routines into four clusters that differ only in which optional descriptor slots the stage writes (+0x20 and +0x24 are the ones that come and go) and in the number of load requests; 66 routines match one of the four shapes word for word once the per-stage constants are masked.
claims.coverage: The 66 is an enumeration over the same 318-file denominator: four scans of ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003/pro/*.s, one per family shape, matching the representative's full instruction-word sequence with the value-construction immediates (lui, ori, addi, addiu) masked and every load/store displacement left intact, so the descriptor layout stays the discriminator while the per-stage values are free. The four scans return 26, 15, 14 and 11. That is two fewer than the family index's 68: wstag305 and wstag525 cluster structurally but are genuinely different shapes (60 and 69 instructions against the representatives' 62 and 71), so the exact scan correctly excludes them. The claim deliberately does NOT say all 294 stage overlays use one of these four shapes - only 66 do. What IS true of all of them, from the independent descriptor-store census, is that 293 of the 294 write the descriptor. The meaning of each descriptor slot is not claimed here; it is prior work in scene-descriptor-complete-field-map and its successors. The 26 files with no instruction-word column are outside the scan.
limitations: Nothing here identifies the consumer of descriptor +0x44. tools/descriptor_readers.py reports no read in fieldstg or stdwtitl through a tracked base, and that tool only accepts pro/*.s overlays, so the EXE was not searched at all. A zero from it is not evidence of absence and is not used as any.

The 'base + language' reading of +0x44 is an interpretation of a step-7 arithmetic run, supported by the language index being the addend's other operand. It is not confirmed by any consumer, by a resource table, or by a runtime observation.

The scene-setup shape scan covers ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003/pro/*.s only, and only the 292 files that carry an instruction-word column. 66 routines match one of four exact shapes; the remaining stage setups were not classified.
Which stage belongs to which of the ten +0x44 area groups was collected but is not recorded here, and the groups were not checked against any independent notion of a game area.
All of this is static. No runtime capture was taken this pass.

claims.statement: Submarimon's vertical motion is fieldstg F0x8008e45c, the per-tick method the character constructor F0x8009116c installs at char+0x108 for sprite id 327 (0x147, p122sbmm) ALONE, in place of the default 0x8008e8ac, seeding char+0x64 = 0x3000 and char+0x84 = 1 (file 0xe6b4-0xe6f8). char+0x64 is a signed 8.8 HEIGHT (up positive) and char+0xc4 its signed 8.8 per-tick velocity. Each 50 Hz field tick, and regardless of horizontal movement: while CROSS (pad bit 0x4000, action id char+0x10 == 0x4b) is held the velocity steps -4 clamped at -0xC0, otherwise +4 clamped at +0x80; then height += velocity; then ONE terrain-code limit table is consulted, chosen by the post-step velocity (`slti 0x5`: >= 5 reads ceilings, else floors). The ceiling table (jump table 0x80083538, index code-0x12) caps the height at 0x6000/0x5000/0x4000/0x3000/0x2000 for codes 0x12/0x13/0x14/0x15/0x16 and carries no snap value, so a violation only zeroes the velocity. The floor table (0x80083550, index code-0x02) floors it at 0x2000/0x3000/0x4000/0x5000/0x6000 for codes 0x02/0x03/0x04/0x05/0x06 and snaps the height to limit+0xC. Independently the height is hard-clamped to [0x1800, 0x7000], and leaving that band also zeroes the velocity; landing exactly on either bound is not a violation. The handler returns changing nothing when any of scene_struct+0x50/+0x58/+0x5c is set, so height does not drift on a frozen frame. The field-actor renderer consumes the height as actorScreenY = groundScreenY - (height >> 8) at 0x8008f5d0 and the drop shadow re-adds the identical term at 0x8008f834, so buoyancy moves the billboard only -- collision, exit triggers and the maze resolver all keep reading the ground char+0x50/+0x54. Junior (id 2) and Digmon (id 326) keep the default handler and have no height state at all.

claims.statement: Submarimon is tank-steered with a single throttle, not D-pad steered. Its handler F0x8008e45c writes no position; the field-character tick driver calls the per-form handler and then runs the shared state dispatcher F0x8008fed0 unconditionally, so the handler's job is to select a STATE. It selects 0x4b while CROSS is held and 0x4c otherwise, and those two states are Submarimon's alone (one field-character setter call in the whole corpus, fieldstg.s L11832). State 0x4b zeroes char+0x68 on entry, then adds 8 per tick up to a cap, calls the direction helper with (facing, speed) and adds the result to char+0x50/+0x54, then calls the encounter driver F0x8008fd74; state 0x4c skips its body entirely when char+0x68 is 0, else subtracts 8 clamped at 0, moves the same way, and does NOT call the encounter driver -- so coasting cannot start a battle. The cap is 0x266 on PAL and 0x200 on NTSC, selected by [0x8005ccac], which is never written anywhere in the disassembly and is a video-mode compensation (F0x8001d3f4 branches on the same global for 0x133 vs 0x100, the same 6:5 ratio); each cap is exactly half its mode's run magnitude, so the sub tops out at half Junior's running pace. Turning is in the handler itself: LEFT (pad 0x80) and RIGHT (pad 0x20) rotate char+0x60 by -1 and +1 mod 8, gated to one step every 8 field ticks. Holding CROSS therefore drives the sub forward along its facing AND downward at the same time, and releasing it coasts the hull to a stop while buoyancy floats it back up.

claims.statement: Six one-line routines in the main program each start a one-byte tagged record inside the same object. Every one of them stores a single letter code at object offset +0x37, points the write cursor at +0x2c to the object's own 36-byte buffer at +0x24, writes the caller's byte as that buffer's only byte, and sets the record length at +0x36 to 1. The letter codes are 0x43, 0x46, 0x47, 0x4b and 0x4c; a sixth routine writes code 0x45 and instead clears both the cursor and the length, so it starts an EMPTY record. A dispatcher chooses between them from a state byte at +0x46, passing the payload byte held at +0x47: state 2 selects code 0x4c, state 3 selects 0x46, and state 4 selects 0x47 or, when the flag at +0x48 is set, the payload-free 0x4b builder.
claims.coverage: The six are an enumeration, not a sample: every *.c file below exe-decomp/ was scanned for a store of a literal to the +0x37 field and exactly six matched, all adjacent in the main program between 0x80024630 and 0x800246c4. The field layout is read from the original assembly of one of them, all eight instructions including the return delay slot, rather than from the decompiler; the other five differ from it only in the letter code, which is what the decompiled bodies show. The dispatcher mapping is read from decompiled C only and covers states 2, 3 and 4; states 0, 1, 0xFE and 0xFF appear in sibling dispatchers that were NOT read here, so no mapping is claimed for them.
limitations: WHAT SUBSYSTEM THIS IS remains unidentified, and the claim deliberately does not say. The owning object is 0x1e0 bytes, exists in two instances, and is reached through a ten-entry function table that two initialisers fill with two different implementations; the second instance owns eight further 0xf0-byte objects in two groups of four. The object also holds a byte-stream pointer whose first byte is tested against 0xf3. None of that was decoded.
The meaning of the letter codes is NOT established. They are recorded as the byte values they are; reading them as initials of anything would be a guess.
Nothing was found that READS the +0x37 code. A scan of the decompiled C found no comparison against these values, and that zero is not evidence, because the scan cannot see assembly-only code.
The two hardware-timer routines in the same neighbourhood are what led here, but no call path from them to these builders was traced beyond the one dispatcher.
Static only; no runtime capture.

claims.statement: Fold-in vs fold-out is decided by the start routine's second argument at named call sites, and the sequencing is a strict one-window-at-a-time cascade in each screen's own state machine. Entry: F0x8008e744's init pass folds IN the party-card rows, header and footer (start with argument 1); the six sheet detail windows are armed only and are started by the sheet sub-machine F0x8008d684 in three waiting pairs — default state starts sheet card (+0xD8, only when unk18==0) + name tab (+0xE8); case 1, after the name tab completes, starts EXP plate (+0x128, only when its value word unk130 is 0) + Digivolve panel (+0x108); case 2, after the Digivolve panel completes, starts stat window (+0xF8, only when unk100 is 0) + Equip panel (+0x118); case 3 waits for the Equip panel, then reaches the input state (case 5). Fold-OUT triggers: on the sheet's two-row prompt (case 5), Circle (pad bit 0xD) sets unk14=0xA with unk18=0 and Cross (bit 0xE) sets unk14=0xA with unk74=0 and unk18=1; case 10 then starts fold-outs (start with argument 0) — name tab, Digivolve panel and Equip panel always, sheet card only when unk18!=0, EXP plate + stat window only when unk74==0 — and case 11 ticks them per frame until the Equip panel completes, after which case 12 hands over to the child screen (phase 0x14) on Circle or back to the chooser (phase 0) on Cross. The member chooser (F0x8008ddb0 case 0xB) triggers the row fold-OUT cascade (phase 0x32, the reverse of the open cascade) on Circle (with unk14=1) or Cross, and phase 0x39 then enters the sheet (phase 0xF) only when unk14!=0, else the screen exits (unkC=3).

claims.statement: The +0x2C phase-setter is exe routine F0x80014288 (installed by the factory at F0x800143dc.c:27): it stores its argument into the main phase +0x10 and unconditionally zeroes both sub-phase words +0x14 and +0x18 (F0x80014288.c:2-4; fns.s:4750-4753). This confirms and refines the wave-3 guess: every phase change into or within the STATUS screen clears the sub-phases, and any flag that must survive a phase change is stored AFTER the setter call, never before — the chooser's Circle confirm calls the setter with 0x32 and then writes unk14=1 (F0x8008ddb0.c:138-139), and the child-return case calls it with 0xF and then writes unk18=1 (:164-165). Consequence decoded: both entry paths into sheet phase 0xF (cascade end at case 0x39 and child return at case 0x15) arrive with unk14 == 0, so the confirm marker never survives into the sheet machine — it only steers the case-0x39 branch (sheet when set, screen exit unkC=3 when clear); the sheet machine's default case reads only unk18 to decide whether to restart the sheet card (F0x8008d684.c:34-38), which is the static basis of the already-decoded 'coming back from See Equipment keeps the card open' behavior. The setter family is a strict hierarchy: +0x28 sets the lifecycle flag and clears all three sub-phases (F0x80014274), +0x2C sets the phase and clears the two sub-phases (F0x80014288), +0x30 sets the sub-phase and clears unk18 (fns.s:4757-4760, RAM 0x80014298), +0x34 sets unk18 only (fns.s:4764-4766, RAM 0x800142a4).
claims.coverage: Universals used and their exhausted enumerations: (a) 'both entry paths into sheet phase 0xF' — F0x8008ddb0.c was read in full (238 lines); the only stores of 0xF into unk10 are the setter calls at :164 and :232, so the enumeration of entry paths is exhaustive. (b) 'every phase change ... clears the sub-phases' holds for the setter body itself (verified authority 2 and 3); it is a property of the routine, not an enumeration of call sites. (c) 'any flag that must survive ... is stored AFTER the setter call' is established for the two survivor flags found (unk14=1 at :139, unk18=1 at :165); no other store into unk14/unk18 exists in F0x8008ddb0.c (read in full) — within this routine the enumeration is exhaustive, and no claim is made about other overlays.

The per-frame invoker of the screen function (factory slot +0x48, filled from the factory argument — STATUS screenFn formed at ststatus.s:12061 as lui 0x8009 + addiu -0x18bc, object size 0x14c) is the generic tick F0x80018140, which skips the call on a pause path and, when it observed the flag at 3 on entry, runs the +0x4C teardown and returns NULL; the list context is F0x80018230, which walks a pointer array and stores that NULL back. The prior wave's identification of F0x8001270c as 'the runner' is falsified: it is the resident home screen root, a sibling callback.

claims.statement: On the shared 0x174-byte text element built by F0x8001AE38, method slot +0x144 holds F0x8001A23C, a six-instruction routine that writes byte +0xC1: it stores its second argument there when the halfword at +0x62 is non-zero, and stores 0 instead when +0x62 is zero. Both stores are in jr $ra delay slots. Byte +0xC1 has exactly two readers in the resident executable: the one-instruction getter F0x8001A46C, and the mode-1 arm of the element's frame callback F0x8001AC14, which returns immediately to its epilogue when the byte is zero and otherwise advances the counter at +0xA8. The mode-3 arm that runs the six-entry submit loop is reached by a branch taken before the +0xC1 test and is therefore not gated by it. Consequently the name 'close' recorded for +0x144 in docs/research/ui/symbols/shared-objects.md does not fit the routine, which takes a value rather than closing anything; 'set_visible' is equally unestablished, because the byte gates only the mode-1 arm and not the submit arm. What consumes +0x62, and what modes 0, 2 and 3 mean, were not read.
claims.coverage: The reader/writer census of byte +0xC1 is exhaustive over the original assembly corpus: `code-search "0xc1\($" --regex --corpus original` scanned 590306 lines across ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003 and returned 7 hits in 1 file, all shown and all accounted for here (two writers inside F0x8001A23C, two writers at 0x800193B0/0x800193B4, one at 0x800197EC, and the two readers named in the statement). The matcher reaches assembly instruction text, so a base-relative store spelled with a different immediate would be missed; that limitation is recorded. The claim that mode 1 is the only arm reaching the +0xC1 test was checked by reading all four dispatch branches at 0x8001AC38-0x8001AC50.

claims.statement: The scene-test tool's asset list occupies slots 0..54 of the pointer run at file 0x3634 and names a single contiguous 1..55 id space in which slot = id - 1: slots 0..28 are labelled MFSTG001..MFSTG029 and slots 29..54 are labelled MEFT0030..MEFT0055, with the prefix changing between 029 and 030 and no gap or restart in the numbering. Slot 55 is an animation clip name, not an asset, which bounds the run at exactly 55. On disc there are exactly 55 MEFT10xx_BIN files and no MFSTG file at all, so MFSTG is not a filename: it is the developers' own content classification of the low part of the MEFT1001-1055 range. Combined with the established SFSTDATA record i -> MEFT10<i> mapping, this says MEFT1001-MEFT1029 hold battle STAGE packs and MEFT1030-MEFT1055 hold battle EFFECT packs. This REFINES, and does not contradict, the 2026-08-05 conclusion in docs/research/field/map-effects-meft.md that MEFT1001-1055 are battle rather than field assets - that conclusion stands, and this adds the internal split. It also explains why the range read as heterogeneous: two different kinds of battle asset share one filename prefix.

Beyond the 55 asset slots, the same pointer run carries two further lists in the developers' own vocabulary. Slots 55..116 are 62 numbered battle animation clip names, grouped as WAIT-0/1, GUARD, S-DAMAGE, L-DAMAGE-0..5, DEAD, GET-UP, VICTORY-POSE, ANGER, FIGHT-0..5, three six-frame combo families WA:BU:1/2/3-0..5, WA:MA:U-0..5, WA:MA:KA-0..5, HISSATSU(special attack)-0..5 and JOGRESS(DNA digivolution)-0..5. Slots 117..136 are 20 unnumbered family names headed by a -NONE- sentinel, covering the same families plus ITEM:DA, FIELD:KO, STATUS:DA, STATUS:DAA and PRO:doku. A separate 15-entry run at file 0x35f0 holds a third, hiragana-spelled vocabulary that repeats three of its own entries. IMPORTANT LIMIT: this establishes an ORDERED NAME LIST, not an id mapping. Nothing here shows that a clip's slot index equals the clip id passed to the battle engine, and the frontier's join against the fightstg.s animation selectors has NOT been done. Do not publish slot indices as clip ids.

pro/wfightts.s is a developer battle-scene test tool: an operator-driven menu that selects a battle stage pack, an effect pack and an animation clip and plays them in isolation. Its label image is entirely untranslated Japanese developer shorthand while the shipped player-facing text for this game lives in ~/ddw3/lang_file/dw2003/eng/*.toml, and the tool's handlers read the controller directly (mask chain 0x2000/0x800/0x200/0x100 in handler 0) and drive a six-state machine off a shared sub-state word at +0x14. LIMIT: this is an identification from the label vocabulary, the untranslated-text asymmetry and the input-driven state machine. The call path by which the tool actually launches a scene is NOT yet traced, and no runtime observation of the tool running exists; it is not established whether the tool is reachable in the retail build.

pro/wfightts.s loads at base 0x800a5de0. The base is fixed arithmetically, not assumed: the overlay's lowest self-pointer, 0x800a5df8 at file 0x361c, points at the first Shift-JIS label, which begins at file 0x18, and 0x800a5df8 - 0x18 = 0x800a5de0; every other self-pointer in the file then lands on a label start. Under that base, file 0x00..0x14 is a six-entry handler table holding 0x800a6e3c, 0x800a6f34, 0x800a70a8, 0x800a7410, 0x800a7514 and 0x800a761c, which resolve to file offsets 0x105c, 0x1154, 0x12c8, 0x1630, 0x1734 and 0x183c. All six targets are code and all six open with the same `lw $vX, 0x14($s1)` sub-state load, so the six words are one handler table, not six unrelated addresses. The table is exactly six wide because a seventh slot would fall at file 0x18, which is the first string. File 0x18..0x9d6 is a Shift-JIS label image and code starts at file 0x9d8.

In fieldstg, the two block-actor factory sites (file 0xe210 and file 0xe290) each install a per-tick method pointer at the newly-spawned entity's own +0x108 slot right after creation: site A (0xe210) installs F0x8008ed2c, site B (0xe290) installs F0x8008eae8. The general field-character constructor's s4-mode branch at file 0xe7c8 stores the SAME F0x8008eae8 into char+0x108 that factory site B installs -- it is not a third, block-specific controller, it is the identical shared handler. F0x8008ed2c is a rotating 0x40-slot history/queue buffer on the entity's own sub-records (clears fields, advances a mod-0x40 cursor, copies the prior slot's field into +0x50, and forwards mode 3 to a queued entity's own interact callback at +0x2c when one is pending). F0x8008eae8 walks the entity's own queued-entity linked list at +0x104, classifies the head entity by its kind field into numeric ranges, and either forwards a literal mode (1, 3, or 4) to that entity's own +0x2c interact callback, or (for kind==3) mirrors that entity's position/facing back into itself. In neither function does the code that fires when npc 328/351/352 are engaged move a sprite, spawn an item, or write a flag directly -- it dispatches to whichever OTHER entity is queued against the block via that entity's own interact callback, using a small integer mode code (1/3/4) whose exact in-game meaning (which direction/outcome each mode selects) is not resolved by this packet.
limitations: The mode integers 1/3/4 forwarded by F0x8008eae8, and mode 3 forwarded by F0x8008ed2c, are not yet traced into the callee's own +0x2c handler, so the concrete player-visible outcome (which push direction, or whether it is a push at all) is unresolved.

Which of npc 328/351/352 uses factory A vs factory B, and which corresponds to the established 'target clip 0x4e' vs 'engager clip 0x4d' roles, was not resolved: the id-selection tables read by the two factory loops (RAM 0x80097cb4 and 0x80097cc0, 3 words each) sit past fieldstg.s's own disassembled instruction range and could not be retrieved through the compact bundle -- tools/run-overlay-scan.sh words/dis both refuse that byte range ('fieldstg.s has no `# .word` encoding comments' there), and the same absolute addresses fall inside fightstg.s's own *code* region (a different overlay sharing the 0x80082cb0 base), so a direct read at those RAM addresses is ambiguous-overlay and was not used. /home/dorij/ddw3/rust/dw2003_pro_fieldstg/src/data.rs documents a word table at that same address (comment offsets are relative to 0x80080000, not to the fieldstg load base) but that source is a checked-extraction dump of undetermined record semantics here, not itself proof of which ids sit in which slot.

claims.statement: F0x80090e70 and F0x80090ef0 iterate three mode selectors {2,4,8} and replace actor+0x108 with F0x8008ed2c and F0x8008eae8 respectively. The resident object iterator compares those selectors to actor+0x8. Field setup passes modes 2, 4 and 8 to the three optional party actors, while authored stage actors pass mode 1. Constructor F0x8009116c installs F0x8008eae8 for the party-mode branch at file 0xe7c8; that routine copies delayed leader position/state history to a follower, while F0x8008ed2c drains zero records through that history and removes itself when the delayed x reaches zero. This controller family is separate from the special confirm branch for sprite ids 0x148, 0x15f and 0x160. That branch assigns target action-state 0x4e and engager action-state 0x4d. State 0x4d starts engager clip 0x45 and holds the scene busy until the clip completes. State 0x4e waits 20 native ticks, starts target clip 0x54, dispatches packed cue 0x800446c9, sets bank-0 completion bit 8, 9 or 10 according to target id, and moves the target to lifecycle 3 after its animation completes. Lifecycle 3 takes the cleanup path rather than the lifecycle-1 update/render path, so the target leaves the rendered field. The action depicted by clips 0x45 and 0x54 is not named from the p188blok asset.

claims.statement: WORLD-Q007's two residuals are closed. (1) entity+0xE0 enters the billboard Y math as an unscaled additive registration offset: the renderer F0x8008F52C computes screenY = owner world Y - projection, subtracts (entity+0x64 >> 8), then adds +0xE0 to the top edge (+0xA/+0x12) and adds +0xE0 + height(+0xE6) to the bottom edge (+0x1A/+0x22). It never enters X. (2) Mirrored facing: facing >= 5 negates (entity+0xDC + entity+0xE4) to place the mirrored X, and the sprite is also flipped by reversing its U coordinates, so +0xE4 participates in both. This is the origin of the walker's baked horizontal offset; the walker still feet-anchors vertically and does not apply +0xE0.
claims.notes: Read 2026-09-13 in fieldstg.s:12892-12940. +0xE0 is a per-frame additive Y offset applied after world-Y projection and after the height subtraction, with no shift. The only readers of the field actor's +0xDC/+0xE0/+0xE4/+0xE6 are in F0x8008f52c; the writers are the resolver F0x8008f9c0.
claims.coverage: Both mechanisms were read instruction-by-instruction at the cited lines, including the facing test, the negu, the U reversal branch, and the four top/bottom edge stores.

claims.statement: The fieldstg routine at RAM 0x800928e4 -- the target of the zone-manager method cell 0x8009b714, which the extracted overlay data resolves statically -- writes its argument into [0x8004b414] ONLY when [0x8004b40c] is non-zero. When that word is zero the routine returns having written nothing at all. Both addresses are formed from the base 0x80048d34, which the routine materialises with `lui 0x8005` plus the negative displacement -0x72cc, so the displacement borrows into the high half: 0x80050000 - 0x72cc = 0x80048d34, then +0x26d8 = 0x8004b40c and +0x26e0 = 0x8004b414. This confirms as a guard the '(guarded)' annotation that docs/research/field/typed-terrain-layer-decoded-2026-07-28.md records for this cell without stating what the guard tests.
claims.coverage: 'ONLY when' and 'nothing at all' are over the COMPLETE body: the routine is 9 instructions from entry to the delay slot after `jr $ra`, quoted in full, and it contains exactly one branch and exactly one store, with the store on the not-taken side. The two absolute addresses were computed from the lui/addiu pair rather than read off a comment, and the borrow was applied deliberately -- taking 0x80050000 + 0x72cc instead would put both addresses in the wrong object.
limitations: What [0x8004b40c] means is not established here. Ledger evidence for the field screen handler describes it as a map-changed flag, which is consistent with a guard but is not re-derived by this claim.
What [0x8004b414] is subsequently read by is not established.
The other five zone-manager method cells were not read.

claims.statement: F0x8009E668 dispatchDuelViewQueue is the duel's board-view request queue, keyed by two 18-entry jump tables read from the shipped overlay. The duel queues a request in duel+0x499; the routine skips both switches when it is zero, otherwise runs that request's setup arm from D0x80083800 indexed by (request-1) under `sltiu 0x12`, promotes the request (duel+0x498 = the request, duel+0x499 = 0, duel+0x49B = the request+1), then runs the promoted request's tick from D0x80083848 the same way. Requests 1 and 2 are the two hand rows' scale reveal (windows 8*max(duel+0x72C,duel+0x79E) and 5*max(...), and request 1 copies the 40 bytes at duel+0x49E into the view records at +0x151+0x4C*i through F0x8009E024); requests 3 and 4 wipe the centre plates open (F0x8009E7B8+0xEA4) and closed (+0xEA8) over 10*(s8)duel+0x575 and 5*(s8)duel+0x575+0x16 tick windows; requests 5,7,9,11,13,15,17 are F0x8009DBE8(duel, scene, row, kind) with the six s16 records of D0x800A5D2C at index 6,5,4,3,2,1; requests 6,8,10,12,14,16 are F0x8009DF68 with the same records and no portraits; requests 17 and 18 finish in their own frame and chain 6 and 12 into duel+0x49B. Every tick spends one slot per four ticks of duel+0x4D0 while it is >= 4, adds the frame delta ([0x8004DF9C]() = the resident getFrameDelta, read from [0x8004DE28]) twice - once into duel+0x4C8 and once into duel+0x4D0 - and reports back when the window duel+0x4D8 is passed. The three callees and the view's +0xF24/+0xEA4/+0xEA8 slots are the routine's only host edges; none of them executes in the idle-plus-pad probe run, so the routine's only Phase 4 dependencies are its own tables.
claims.notes: Read 2026-09-16 by the lead from the original listing (authority 2) because the m2c rendering of this routine writes both switches as an irregular C switch and does not recover which case is which request. The two tables were then read from the shipped overlay image and are carried verbatim in engine/dw3/ui/duel-view-queue.ts; tests/duel-view-queue-oracle.test.js pins them against the overlay words and compares the port to the interpreter on pro_cardgame.bin + resident.bin over every request number 1..18 plus out-of-range values (4 tests, 27/27 mutations caught). It also settles that claim's open note 'the exact frame-delta source behind +0x4D0'.

claims.statement: F0x800197A4 is the resident text drawer: one routine whose five coverage rows (0x80019994/0x8001999C/0x800199A4/0x80019ED0/0x80019F68) are its dispatch arms, not functions. It walks the element's reveal window one token at a time through the decoder F0x8001D264 and the stepper F0x8001A48C, and for each placed glyph writes [DR_TPAGE previous page][SPRT 0x14][DR_TPAGE current page] into the packet arena at [D0x8004DE10+0x158], each linked into the layer's ordering bucket (the layer found by [D0x8004DE10+0x17C], its +0x138 method) with the AddPrim head insertion, then advances the pen by the glyph's own width plus bearing or by the stored cell width in fixed-pitch mode. Arm 1 (count+emit) and arm 4 (page break, count only) increment the reveal count; arm 2 (the next-glyph opcode F0x8001AA10 drawing from a sibling line) does not; arm 3 is a control token that consumes no glyph; arm 0 and anything above 4 flush the packet cursor without the closing page change. The transform path (element +0xCC set with a non-identity scale) writes one 0x28-byte four-corner quad whose corners go through the resident GTE helper F0x8002B1DC. The entry's `sh $zero, 0x28($sp)` is the stepper's page/wait counter at the token scratch +0x18, not a dead store. Translated as engine/dw3/ui/text-drawer.ts#drawTextElement and proven equivalent to the original by tests/text-drawer-oracle.test.js.

The three libgte helpers of the transformed path are host boundaries in the browser and are stubbed identically on both sides in the oracle; their own bodies are not part of this claim.

claims.statement: The DIGIMON logo and DIGIMON WORLD wordmark on the title screen slide in because the title sequence's state-0 arm (F0x80086A20, table word at file 0x4c) calls each picture-object's +0x70 start-slide slot (F0x8008503C for the logo, F0x80084BB0 for the wordmark) exactly once; each handler is `if (+0xC == 1) +0x2C(1)` and +0x2C writes the sub-phase +0x10 = 1, which is the value the object's own tick draws at. The guard passes because the resident tick F0x80018140 recurses into the owner's LIVE +0x20/+0x24 child array in the same pass that the owner's create arm filled it, so both children have already advanced +0xC to 1 when the arm runs on the next frame.
claims.coverage: The arm and the guard were read from the overlay assembly; the guard condition was reproduced in the browser port, where the pre-fix runtime (tick order computed from a pre-pass snapshot) left both objects at +0x10 = 0 and no logo/wordmark draw, and the live-child tick made both clips draw every frame.
limitations: The arm's timer thresholds are not stated here.
The claim does not cover the Japanese branch's separate creators (F0x80085074 / F0x80084BE8).

claims.statement: The memory-card screen's SAVE entry point is a save-point event. Each of the 25 inn/tower/city save points carries a 'PREPARE TO SAVE.' event whose final opcode is `HANDOFF 0xC00|slot`; the field event interpreter hands that id to the type-7 transition manager, whose state-2 arm passes it to the resident screen launcher D0x8004b440 as (code, -1); `f15` loads the overlay by code >> 8 (0x0C = STMCRD = pro/stgmcard) and the overlay constructor reads code & 0xFF as the save-point slot and the value's bit 31 as the mode (set -> save). The player sees the slot as the saved record's place: esshpnam[42 + slot]. The same launch family's value-0 form is the title's Continue (code 0xC00, load).
claims.coverage: The launcher chain, the library split and the slot/mode reads were read from the overlay and resident assembly. The 25 events, their HANDOFF operands and the place mapping were re-read mechanically from the extracted event table and the screen's place bank by tests/save-points.test.js. The walker route is proven by tools/verify_native_save_point_event.mjs (the Guardromon bank-0x90 write starts the event; the screen opens with 0 traps and the saved record carries place index 43) and tools/verify_native_save_point.mjs (per-map indices 43 and 55).
limitations: The `0x8008833C` per-save-point table the constructor reads with the slot was not decoded.
The launcher's per-screen spawn/return words (ctx+0x26CC and friends) are not covered.
The D0x8008833C lookup and the launcher's exact overlay-name resolution were not executed on the rig; the mapping rests on the assembly reads plus the extracted tables.

claims.statement: The country/language select screen (pro/cnty_sel) is the game's BOOT screen, not a lab-only developer tool. The boot main f12 calls F0x80016a94, which sets the current screen code to 0x1600; f15 resolves the code's high byte (0x16) through the overlay-library LBA table at D0x80055ccc, whose entry 0x16 is 0x165 (357) = CNTY_SEL.PRO. The developer stage-select table's row for 0x1600 is labelled くにせんたく (country selection). The screen's confirm writes the language byte 0x8005CCA8 and hands 0xE01/0xE02 - the two opening movies - to the resident launcher, which then returns to the title (0xE00). So the retail boot order is country select -> opening movie -> title.
claims.coverage: The boot call, the screen code it sets and the promotion step were read from exe/f12.s and F0x80016a94; the library resolution was read from f15 plus the LBA table words in data.rs, cross-checked against eleven other launch codes whose overlays are independently known. The walker route is proven by tools/verify_native_boot_language.mjs: an ordinary page load (no query switch) opens pro/cnty_sel with 0 traps, Down moves the screen's own row, confirm commits language byte 5 for row 2 and the title follows; tools/verify_native_cntysel.mjs still proves the lab entry, and ?skipLanguage=1 / ?legacyCntysel=1 are the documented switches. Confirmed against the running original 2026-09-22 (authority 1, read-only): the console shows the SELECT LANGUAGE screen with current and previous screen codes both 0x1600, which is the boot init's pair of stores (EV-CNTYSEL-BOOT-LIVE).
limitations: Whether the PAL retail disc shows this screen on every boot or only when no language is configured was not tested on hardware; the boot code has no conditional before setting 0x1600.
The walker ships one language, so the committed byte is recorded rather than used to swap assets.

claims.statement: On the text-line and cursor boxes of the original pause menu, fifteen shared action slots do this: +0x144 sets a text line's shown byte (+0xC1), or 0 when the line is empty; +0x84 moves a cursor (x +0x58, y +0x5C); +0x80 shows or hides a cursor and resets its blink when hidden; +0x134 sets a text line's position (+0xB0/+0xB2); +0x138 sets its colour byte (+0xC0); +0x130 starts the letter-by-letter text (0 or less shows the line at once); +0x148 sets the right-align offset (+0xBC); +0x114 sets line 1's text through the +0x120 routine with line index 0; +0x120 sets line N's text; +0x118 sets a number; +0x110 sets a raw string; +0x15C sets +0x58 (the layer); on screen objects +0x28 sets the main state (+0x0C) and clears the step words, +0x2C sets the step (+0x10), and +0x38 advances the main state by one.
claims.notes: Routine bodies: resident decompilation (authority 3); F0x800194e8 checked in its assembly (jal F0x800196e4 with a3=0 in the delay slot). Runtime: run 2 of docs/research/ui/captures/pause-menu-traced-2026-09-30.md (.dw3-research/game-use/pause-trace2-dw3-8533dbc2cf8a) hooked each routine a box or page held at those slots on 76 pause presses and logged each call with its box, arguments, and the box's words before and after; the recorded effects agree (e.g. +0x144 with 0: shown byte 1 to 0 on 44 lines; +0x84 (0xB0,0x3F): y 0x31 to 0x3F). Scope: only the box kinds met in the pause menu. +0x118 and +0x110 bodies are longer and were read only for their target (a line record), not every branch.
claims.coverage: The fifteen slots are every slot whose routine was called in run 2 (76 pause presses, all hooked routines logged); each routine body was read in the resident decompilation. The claim covers only the routines those boxes held; other object kinds were not enumerated.
claims.frontier_rationale: No frontier covers the shared box actions; the trace settles the competing names in shared-objects.md.

claims.statement: The field balloon actor (constructor F0x80088144, tick F0x80087F84, draw F0x80087E7C) draws cel 0x37 for exactly one frame at the end of its life, AFTER it has already switched to state 3. On the close the tick adds the frame delta to the counter at +0x60 and tests it against the third checkpoint +0x5c; while the counter is still below that checkpoint it only draws, and on the tick where it reaches it the tick calls setState(3) while the delay slot stores the checkpoint back into +0x60. The call then falls through to the draw, which blits +0x60 >> 2 = 0xdc >> 2 = 0x37. State 3's own arm returns before the draw, so nothing is drawn from the following tick on. The complete close cel sequence is therefore 0x35 (hold), 0x36, 0x37 - three cels, not two.
claims.notes: Read 2026-10-02 from ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003/pro/fieldstg.s, re-derived independently of the 2026-09-13 anchor claim, and re-read a second time on 2026-10-02 (overlay base 0x80082cb0, so label 0x5460 is RAM 0x80088110). Extends claim fishing-q008-balloon-draw-cel-and-owner-anchor-2026-09-13, which covered the anchor and the cel formula but not the one-frame tail. RESTING AT partially_verified, NOT verified: the substance is statically legible at authority 2 (the counter bump, the comparison against +0x5c, the counter snap in setState(3)'s delay slot, the branch order, and the state-3 early return), but the review gate for `verified` was not satisfied - ./dw3-research review-bundle and tools/record_local_review.py both refuse in this worktree because its index belongs to another root and rebuilding it was out of scope for this job. The missing artifact is therefore that one hash-bound review packet, not a rig run; a rig capture could only confirm that the single frame is visible.
claims.coverage: Labels 0x5450-0x547c (the counter bump at +0x60, the checkpoint load and comparison at +0x5c, the setState(3) call with its counter snap in the delay slot, and the draw call they fall into) plus the state-3 early return at 0x5304 and the freeze arm that makes sub-state 2 draw without bumping the counter at 0x53d8.

claims.statement: The partner chooser on pro/stdgname reads the pad in exactly one sub-state: slot 4 of the seven-word table at 0x80082F58, target F0x8008601C, the only branch of F0x80085DE4 that calls the input handler F0x80085B70. The other six slots (0x80085ED8, 0x80085F10, 0x80085F78, 0x80086090 twice, 0x800860C0) only enable the six row widgets, wait for them to report ready one step at a time and, in slot 6, call obj+0x28(3); none of them examines a button. A Back (Cross, logical bit 14) pressed while the chooser is in slots 0-3 is therefore dropped by the original itself. Once the chooser is in slot 4 a single Back plays 0x800450BD, stores -1 into the root screen's +0x60 and calls the root's +0x68, which starts the close fade, and F0x80086184 case 1 (F0x800861F4) reads that -1 and jumps to its own sub-state 5, the exit path. So after a name has been committed the chooser leaves the screen on the FIRST Back press, and the number of frames between the chooser appearing and slot 4 is the only window in which Back does nothing.
claims.notes: Authority 2: read from the original assembly at ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003/pro/stdgname.s (sha256 a4c259c8...), all seven table words and all seven arms enumerated from the file, not sampled. The slti/slt operand text in that dump prints rs and rt in the wrong order for SLT, so the two wrap comparisons were decoded from the shipped overlay image web/assets/native/screens/pro_stdgname.bin instead: 0x80085CBC is the word 0x0043102a = slt $v0,$v0,$v1 (down wraps to 0 when count-1 < index) and 0x80085FC8 is 0x0062102a = slt $v0,$v1,$v0 (the row walk advances while index < count-1). The shipped translation already matched both. NOT established, and not claimed: the exact frame count of the setup window, which depends on how fast the six row widgets report ready and is therefore a property of the host renderer, not of this code; and what the player sees in the original during those frames, since no rig capture of this screen at the chooser was taken in this session. The walker's behaviour is pinned by tests/name-root-session.test.js ('Back is dropped until the chooser reads the pad, then one Back leaves the screen') and driven end to end by tools/verify_native_nameentry.mjs, which waits for slot 4, presses Back once, and fails if a second press would have been needed.
claims.coverage: All seven words of the chooser's jump table were read individually from stdgname.s file offsets 0x2A8-0x2C0 and all seven arms read to their return, so 'only slot 4 reads the pad' is a complete enumeration of the dispatch, not a sample. All six words of the sequence's table were read from 0x2C4-0x2D8, and case 1 (0x2F74 + 4) and its exit jump to sub-state 5 were followed to the epilogue at label 0x369C. The input handler's four arms (up code 4, down code 6, confirm code 0xD, cancel code 0xE) were read end to end over labels 0x2EC0-0x3130.

claims.statement: The in-battle message panel (pro/fightstg FIGHTSTG_F0x80099588, object FIGHTSTG_F0x8009a298) is a blocking modal: the battle's own sequencers stop while a line is up and resume only after the player presses Circle. The screen object FIGHTSTG_F0x8009a898 draws (F0x8009a3b4 at .L0x8009ab24), runs the reveal machine FIGHTSTG_F0x8009a514 (.L0x8009ab30), reads the message object's state at .L0x8009ab38 and clears the pointer it holds for the caller (.L0x8009ab50, self+0x58) only when that state is 3; state 3 is written in exactly one place (.L0x8009a664/.L0x8009a668), reachable only through .L0x8009a618 andi $v0,$s2,0x2000 (pad bit 0x2000 = Circle) with no timeout (.L0x8009a61c returns with the line up). Every caller returns while the pointer is set: lw $v0,($s2) / bnez -> return at .L0x80091094 in the attack-resolution sequencer F0x80090e84 (kind 2 at .L0x80090fe4, kind 3 at .L0x80091040) and the same check at .L0x80088680, .L0x8008876c, .L0x80088ac0 and .L0x80088afc in the action object FIGHTSTG_F0x80088564, whose ten F0x8009a298 call sites (fightstg.s:5878-6204) feed kinds 1, 2, 13 and 19. Two further facts read in the same pass: (a) self+0xac, which F0x8009a3b4 tests as the prompt's gate (.L0x8009a3e4), holds the VM method pointer from the constructor (lui 0x800a / addiu -0x6a78 = 0x80099588, sw at fightstg.s:24206), so the blinking glyph is up for the whole life of a message and .L0x8009a698 stops it on the press that ends the line; (b) after the close the panel and both lines stay on screen, because the screen stays in its state 2 and F0x8009a3b4 has no hide path (.L0x8009a4b8 draws the panel unconditionally).
claims.notes: Authority 2: read from the original assembly ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003/pro/fightstg.s; every line cited was re-read in this pass, and grep of 'sw .*, 0xac(' over the whole overlay returns eight hits, of which only fightstg.s:24206, :24432 and :24462 touch this object. The shipped walker translation now holds the turn on PLAYER_ACT/ENEMY_ACT/RESULT_MSG while a line is up (web/battle.js msgHoldsTurn) and never on the command menu or the results pages, which own the pad themselves; that choice of states is the walker's, the blocking itself is the original's. claims.statement: The freeze roll is taken by the command-menu instruction itself, before it arms the command list, so a turn blocked by the roll never opens the list. Step 1 of wfightmn F0x800a7418 masks the acting record's ailment byte at 0x1c with 0x2 and skips the roll when the bit is clear (wfightmn.s L1503-L1506); when the bit is set it calls the roll pointer read at 0x4660 with argument 0 in the call's delay slot, and a zero answer branches past the arming code (wfightmn.s L1508-L1512). A blocked turn stores message id 0x56 with a zero second word and shows it through the line object's method +0xac called with 2 and the address of the first word (wfightmn.s L1517-L1525), then re-queues the turn by calling the pointer read at 0x437c into the ordinary player-turn enqueuer 0x8009c4bc, and finally calls instr+0x2c(2) before returning (wfightmn.s L1526-L1538). Reaching the menu needs a zero roll and a clear confusion bit: the confusion bit 0x4 instead calls instr+0x2c(0x11), and only the clear path arms the list with jal 0x80092d80 and stores step 2 (wfightmn.s L1541-L1556). So the roll is taken once per turn, before the list, and a blocked turn costs the ordinary turn, not the command.
claims.coverage: Both arms of the freeze test and the whole of the blocked branch were read instruction by instruction from pro/wfightmn.s at the routine's own labels .L0x0000173c to .L0x00001834, which is the entire step-1 body; the step test at .L0x0000173c and the arming at .L0x00001824 are the only ways out of it, and each was read. The roll routine itself is not re-read here: it is F0x800a19d8 as recorded in battle-formula-leaves.md and in claim UI-DISPLAY-TICK-CHAIN-2026-08-21's sibling STATUS-C002 contradiction note, and only its call site and argument are claimed. Not established by this read: whether the enemy's command-menu instruction takes the same roll with argument 0x10, which was not looked for.
claims.notes: Recorded 2026-10-03 from the merged helper run b073fa71 after the lead re-read .L0x0000173c-.L0x00001834. What was missing from the ledger before this was the PLACE the roll is taken, not the roll: STATUS-C002's contradiction note already records that F0x800a19d8 is a frozen can-act roll, and battle-formula-leaves.md cites this very branch as the second site for the roll's polarity. The new fact is that the roll sits inside the command-menu instruction and gates the list, which is why a frozen partner's turn ends at the name plate. This claim also closes the 'instr+0x2C(2)' detail: 2 is the ordinary turn cost the blocked branch pays, the same value the confusion branch replaces with 0x11.

claims.statement: A digivolution the battle report grants is auto-equipped into the first equipped slot whose halfword is below 3, and an equipped form is never pushed out to make room. After acquiring the form the routine reads the equipped triple into a stack buffer and walks it from index 0 (stfgtrep.s L3561-L3572); a slot below 3 branches to the write, with the index advance in the branch delay slot (stfgtrep.s L3574-L3576), and the loop stops once the index reaches 3, leaving through j 0x80086590 with the new form id in the return register and nothing stored (stfgtrep.s L3577-L3581). The write arm stores the new id into that one slot and calls set_equipped with the whole triple (stfgtrep.s L3542-L3546). The reader is what makes an empty slot findable at all: it emits only ids of 3 or above and fills the unused positions of the three with -1 (fns.s L8112-L8118, fns.s L8139-L8142), so a padded position reads back as 0xffff and is not below 3. A fourth form therefore lands in padding while one is free and, with all three slots holding real forms, leaves the triple exactly as the player set it.
claims.coverage: The whole three-slot scan and its write arm were read instruction by instruction in pro/stfgtrep.s across the labels .L0x00003874 to .L0x000038c4 and .L0x00003824 to .L0x00003840, so the loop's three exits - the write branch, the index-3 fall-through and the set_equipped return - were each read rather than sampled. The resident reader F0x800176ac was read in full in exe/fns.s from .L0x800176ac to its return. Independent cross-check: the m2c body exe-decomp/stfgtrep_c/F0x8008634c.c reaches the same three conclusions (tree, gates, and a walk that returns without writing when all three slots are >= 3), recorded as EV-STFGTREP-EVOTREE-C-2026-10-03. Not established here: what the report then TELLS the player when the triple is full, which is a text question and not part of this routine.
claims.notes: Recorded 2026-10-03 from merged helper run 227a5f87 after the lead re-read stfgtrep 0x3884-0x38C4 and get_equipped F0x800176ac. digivolution-tech-system-decoded-2026-07-11.md section 5 already described the auto-equip as 'if any slot holds an id < 3 (empty), place the new form there and set_equipped', which is right but leaves the full-triple case implicit; the claim makes it explicit because a walker that shifts its array forward to make room is wrong there and the ledger did not say so. The delay-slot reading matters: `slti $v0, 0x3` is the short form of `slt $v0, $v0, 0x3` with $v0 already holding the slot value from `lh $v0, ($v1)`, and `bnez` on it is the write branch.

claims.statement: The eight digivolution trees are per ROSTER SLOT, not per form, and each line's unlock scan is one ordered pass over that line's 44 records of 0x10 bytes. The routine picks its tree with `lui $v1, 0x8009` / `addiu $v1, -0x6fc4`, indexing the eight-word block by `sll $v0, $s4, 0x2` and loading the pointer with `lw $s7, ($v0)` (stfgtrep.s L3452-L3463); the record cursor then advances `addiu $s3, 0x10` against an end pointer built as `addiu $v0, $s7, 0x2c0`, which is 44 records, and falling past it returns 0 (stfgtrep.s L3582-L3586). Each record's own gates are read in table order: a form already in the ledger is skipped on `bgez` after the ledger lookup, then up to TWO requirement pairs at +0x4/+0x6 and +0x8/+0xa each require the partner to be in the ledger with a level not below the record's own level word, and the requirement kind at +0xc then selects a combat stat at 0x26 + 2*kind for kinds 1 to 6, the roster level at +0x1c for kind 7, or an elemental stat at 0x24 + 2*kind for kinds 8 and up, each compared with the record's threshold at +0xe (stfgtrep.s L3486-L3559). A line has no shared index keyed by the partner's current form: two partners on different lines reach different trees through the same slot-indexed table.
claims.coverage: The routine was read instruction by instruction in pro/stfgtrep.s from .L0x0000369c to .L0x0000390c, which is its whole body: the tree pick, the record loop, the ledger skip, both requirement pairs, all three kind ranges and the grant-and-return path. The record-count claim was tested by dividing the bound the code builds (0x2c0) by the stride the code advances (0x10) rather than by reading the data arrays. An independent second read of the same routine, the m2c body exe-decomp/stfgtrep_c/F0x8008634c.c, agrees on every clause, so the two sources are not one misreading. The trees' CONTENTS (44 records x 8 lines of shipped ids) are not re-extracted here; digivolution-tech-system-decoded-2026-07-11.md section 5 names the eight arrays and the pointer block and remains the source for the data. Not established: the four per-line name spellings the 2026-10-03 lead check found between the disc rows and the walker's old hand-written rows, because that is a data comparison and not a read of this routine.

claims.statement: The battle DNA pane's partner strip leads with the partner's STARTER species and lists its equipped forms after it, because the pane keys off the roster slot and not the profile row of the live form. The pane's constructor resolves the party position through the service cell 0x8004b44c and stores the answer at +0x60 (fightstg.s L22492-L22498). The strip build takes that slot back out, calls the equipped-forms reader with it, and reads row 0 straight out of the profile table at 0x8003ef5c with stride 0x58 built from the slot (fightstg.s L22003-L22023) - so row 0 is that slot's base species and rows 1 to 3 are the compacted triple. The pairing test is unaffected and still compares the acting record's own live form against the cursor row. The resolver answers -1 for a party position of 3 or more (fns.s L7507-L7516), so the pane is keyed by the party position it was built for and not by any combatant index.

The ledger already held the constructor half as EV-FIGHTSTG-80098884-ASM-2026-09-12 / claim fightstg-80098884-role-2026-09-12; what is new is what the pane DOES with +0x60. claims.statement: A partner knocked out during the fight earns no battle reward and does not shrink what the survivors are paid, because its reward-participant flag is CLEARED at the battle outcome before the report divides anything. The outcome sweep reads each position's live current HP and, for a position at 0 or below, writes 1 HP into its roster record and clears the four flag bytes at +0x6 through +0x9 of its participant row (wfightmn.s L2072-L2087). The report then counts only rows whose +0x6 byte is still set and divides the reward by that count (stfgtrep.s L2786-L2790), and a row whose flag was cleared is handed a share of zero to the EXP applier rather than its share (stfgtrep.s L2884-L2886). The marking itself is still unconditional - a knockout does not stop the row being marked at setup or on a Tag-in - so the flag is what a knockout changes, not the marking.
claims.coverage: The outcome sweep was read instruction by instruction in pro/wfightmn.s across .L0x00002044 to .L0x00002080, and both stfgtrep.s consumers across .L0x00002c58 to .L0x00002c68 and .L0x00002de0 to .L0x00002de8. The byte the report reads as the flag is the same +0x6 offset the sweep clears, which is the join between the two overlays and is not an assumption: it is the same offset literal in both files. The DVEXP ladder and the level-up pass read the same divisor and were not re-read separately. Not established here: whether the flag column also gates any report ROW DISPLAY, which the helper report suggested and which was not checked.

claims.statement: The Tag partner list keeps ONE cursor-row word for the whole battle: the list is handed the word behind the caller's cell at +0x54 when it is built, with no clamp against the row count, and a successful confirm writes the cursor row back into that same cell (fightstg.s L21254-L21259, fightstg.s L21311-L21326). Its rows are built by skipping EMPTY slots and the acting slot and nothing else - no instruction in the build loop reads the live HP, so a knocked-out partner keeps its row and the player can see it (fightstg.s L21205-L21243). Choosing a fallen row is refused instead: the confirm reads the chosen partner's live HP and returns having done nothing when it is zero, before the write-back (fightstg.s L21311-L21326). So the second forced Tag of a battle opens on the row the player took last time even when that row is now a fallen partner, and Circle on it does nothing - the original does not guard the seed against that.
claims.coverage: The row build was read instruction by instruction in pro/fightstg.s across .L0x800974ec to .L0x80097588, so the 'no HP test' negative is a read-based one over the whole loop rather than a search for one field: the loop body was walked and the only loads are the +0x1a byte, the leading halfword, the acting-slot compare and the row store. The seed and the confirm arm were read at .L0x800975bc to .L0x800975d0 and .L0x800976a0 to .L0x800976dc. Not established here: what the list DRAWS on a fallen row (the helper report describes grey plates) and whether any other consumer reads the same +0x54 cell, neither of which was read in this pass.

claims.statement: The Digimon Lab's evolution chart decides which rows to draw from the partner's LEARNED list and from nothing else, so a form the unlock rule would grant after the next battle but that the partner has not learned never appears. The screen fills its list buffer at +0x60 from ctx+0x2740, the resident routine that enumerates the acquired ledger, and keeps the returned count at +0xb8 (stgdglab.s L1470-L1487); the membership test then walks that buffer as halfwords up to that count and answers 1 on the first match (stgdglab.s L546-L562). Nothing in that test consults the level, the stats or the per-line tree, so the chart cannot show a form the partner has not learned. Combined with the row-packing rule already recorded as DRI-CHART-ROWPACK-001, a row whose first form is not learned is skipped entirely and the rows above it close up.

The identification of ctx+0x2740 as the acquired-ledger enumerator is not taken on trust: it is the routine DIGI-C010-form-ledger-api already records as F0x80017898, and the +0x60 buffer and +0xb8 count are read here as the screen's own fields. The 'nothing else' negative is a read of the whole loop body, which is eight instructions. The helper's own test passed against the old code and so proved nothing; the lead replaced it with tests/dri-chart-learned.test.js, which fails on the old code. claims.statement: When a stage event ends, its completion routine is a straight-line leaf with no effect beyond two doors: the story-flag writer reached through the pointer cell 0x80048ac8, and the master story ordinal at 0x8004b370 written as `lui $v1, 0x8005` / `sw $v0, -0x4c90($v1)`. Counting by EFFECT rather than by masked instruction body, 244 of the disc's 246 such routines fall in five shapes - two flags, one flag, the ordinal alone, the ordinal and one flag - nine write the ordinal first (exemplar wstag460) and four write the flag first: s210/685, s212/352, s520/261, s605/511, three flags - and 2 sit outside them, both still the same ordered list of writes: wstag420's routine sets two flags and only then the ordinal (wstag420.s L86-L107), and wstag400's clears five flags in a row (wstag400.s L136-L169). One shape-C routine stores the ordinal ZERO rather than a beat number (wstag780.s L1554-L1556), so an extractor that reads a zero literal as 'no value' reports it empty. `move_ $a1, $zr` in a jalr delay slot is set_flag(id, 0), a real write and not an absence.
claims.coverage: One routine per shape plus both outliers plus the zero-ordinal routine were read instruction by instruction in the original assembly - wstag200 .L0x000000f8 (shape A) and .L0x00000144 (shape C), wstag205 .L0x0000045c (B), wstag460 .L0x00001298 (D), wstag211 .L0x000000a8 (E), wstag420 .L0x0000013c and wstag400 .L0x00000204 (the outliers), wstag780 .L0x0000182c (the zero ordinal) - and the lead independently re-read the A and D exemplars on 2026-10-03. That is 8 of the 246: the per-shape COUNTS and the 'no other store and no other call in any of the 246' figure are the shipped extractor's, not a second read of all 246 bodies, and they are the residual this claim rests at partially_verified for. An independent check of the whole set does exist and was run by the lead on the merged change: every one of the 250 events' own routine was executed from its own overlay image over 795 starting story states and its ordered flag writes and final ordinal were diffed against the port, with 0 differences over 1,044 flag writes - that bounds what the routines DO, not how many of each shape there are. MISSING ARTIFACT: a second pass, by a different matcher than the extractor's, over all 246 bodies confirming the five-shape tally and that no sixth shape hides in the residue. || Re-read 2026-10-06 (docs/research/evidence/reviews/quest-events-2026-10-06.json): Exemplars re-read (wstag200 0xf8 FF, wstag205 0x45c F, wstag460 0x1298 OF ordinal-first, wstag211 0xa8 FFF, wstag780 0x182c zero-ordinal). Four routines are FLAG-first (s210/685, s212/352, s520/261, s605/511), so shape D's wording is corrected to cover both orders.
claims.notes: Recorded 2026-10-03 from merged helper run 755e512c after the lead re-read wstag200 .L0x000000f8 and wstag460 .L0x00001298 and checked the oracle. CORRECTION to the prior sceneengine-report.md section 2.3, which counted A=98, B=92, C=30, D=9, E=6 and called the remaining 11 'longer': nine of those 11 are one of the five shapes written with a different register choice or with a clear instead of a set (s285/272 and s305/660 are shape B with a clear; s210/685, s212/352, s520/261 and s605/511 are shape D; s400/1304 is A; s395/1305 is E; s780/0 is C storing 0), because clustering on masked instruction bodies splits a `move_ $a1, $zr` off from `li $a1, 1`. Counting by effect gives 244 plus 2. That report is a git-ignored scratch file, so nothing under docs/ carried the wrong tally and needed changing; the correction lives here. The lead also marked one helper sentence wrong: 'the old reader recorded the 21 clears as sets' is false - the old converted content already wrote 0 for them - so what is claimed here is only that 21 of the routines' flag writes are clears, which wstag400's five-clear routine demonstrates directly. claims.statement: The part of EXP-C001 that survives its 2026-10-03 contradiction. The share formula is a function of how many roster slots are still flagged as reward participants: a lone participant takes the whole amount, two take six tenths each, and three or more split it evenly. The four special-cased story-fight battle ids 0xb, 0x1e, 0x143 and 0x144 do NOT bypass the reward path - each writes an extra chapter/outcome word and then jumps to the same continuation the ordinary path falls through to, and all four have nonzero reward-table records - so story bosses grant real EXP, Bits and DVEXP like any other fight. claims.statement: The console draws the battle in its own frame - X right, Y DOWN, Z away from the viewer - and its view matrix takes screen-right as cross(+Y, forward), the LEFT-HANDED-camera convention, in which right x up is the away-from-viewer axis (X x Y = +Z). WebGL's look-at takes the other convention, cross(up, backward), whose right x up points AT the viewer. A Y-up renderer therefore has two ways to draw this world and they must agree with each other: negate Y only and use the console's convention, or keep the right-handed look-at and map the world by a proper rotation, which is diag(1,-1,-1), the 180-degree rotation about X. Negating Y alone while keeping a right-handed look-at is a reflection mismatched against a reflection, and that mismatch was the whole of the walker's left-right flip: models, cameras, effects, the face box, the DNA presentation and the loss camera all ran through one map, diag(1,-1,1). For an orthogonal map M, cross(Ma,Mb) = det(M)*M*cross(a,b), so under that reflection the screen-right row comes out negated and every battle point lands on the wrong side of the screen. The console's screen X is row 0 of the GTE view matrix over depth (FIGHTSTG_F0x80083854 runs RTPS and stores GTE[25]/GTE[26]/GTE[27] as SX1/SY1/SZ1), with no per-side term in the loop, and the basis F0x8002a1ac builds takes +Y as the screen-DOWN axis, which is what makes its right row read as screen right. One PS1 yaw therefore arrives in render space negated (M.Ry(t).M = Ry(-t)); the +0x2c screen roll is unaffected because its derivation is in screen terms.

claims.statement: A field stage overlay builds the extra objects it needs for itself through ONE shared resident call, F0x800143DC (or its three-argument wrapper F0x80014504), and the argument that carries the object's identity is the FIRST argument: the tick, stored at object+0x48 and called by the object runner as tick(object, object+0x24). Reading the tick therefore reads what the object is. Across the 294 wstag overlays there are 432 such create calls in 293 stages, and normalising each tick (masking the immediates and jump targets that name the stage's own overlay, masking both halves of every lui+addiu pair, and masking local labels, while keeping every jump out of the overlay) groups them into 222 families. The largest is one 18-instruction dispatcher in 167 stages that reads the state word at object+0x0C and, only once it has reached 4, calls the object's own +0x38 frame-counter method -- stage-owned housekeeping that draws nothing; those 167 members are only 7 distinct instruction texts with nothing masked, and the only difference between them is local-label offsets, so the family is one real routine rather than a normalisation artefact. s415's falling rock is one of the families: ten builders at 0x800A6230..0x800A643C, all attaching the tick 0x800A5FA8, each 116 bytes, each writing a distinct 0..8 into the new object's +0x04, so one tick and ten instances. 88 of the 222 families' ticks call straight into the battle overlay and 13 build battle participants, so a large part of what a stage builds for itself is its own battle-setup hook rather than something standing in the room. 75 of the 432 ticks are a label inside a bigger routine, which the object runner cannot enter at, so a tick must be read as its whole enclosing routine.
claims.coverage: Read the two create routines and the object runner in exe/fns.s; read s415's ten builders and its tick body line by line; read the common dispatcher in s201 and compared it word for word across all 167 stages that carry it; read wstag232's tick to establish the mid-routine case; read wstag260 and wstag825 to establish the all-.word overlays. The grouping itself is tools/inventory_stage_objects.py over all 294 overlays, whose call count (432) and overlay count (293) match grep -c / grep -l over ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003/pro/wstag*.s exactly, and whose every-create-call-read and every-overlay-accounted-for properties are asserted by tests/stage-object-families.test.js. The 167-stage family's members were additionally hashed with NOTHING masked and collapse to 7 distinct instruction texts, differing only in local-label offsets, which is recorded per family as distinct_raw_tick_bodies.

(1) Only the largest five unported families and the s415 rockfall were read for behaviour; the other 204 families are named by hash only, and the biggest of them are per-stage COPIES of one shared system (s210/s924/s935/s961 each carry their own 587-603 instruction copy of the help-menu launcher; s305/s310/s400/s405/s526/s780 each carry their own battle hook), so they should be read as one system with per-stage data rather than as separate objects. (2) Why 167 stages need a tick that does nothing is not established, and neither is the function pointer the 167-stage builder calls out of its own overlay table. (4) Nothing in this claim has been checked against a running game, and no shipped file was changed: the 13 'ported' marks are citation searches over engine/ and web/ with the citing file and line recorded, and one further citation (web/game.js:4884, a comment naming wstag780 0x800a74cc) was found and deliberately NOT counted because the line does not bind the address as that stage's tick. claims.statement: A stage overlay can build its own falling/bouncing rock actor over a 16-byte record table, and s415 is the only stage that carries one. Its state word (obj+0xc, from the resident allocator F0x800143dc) runs 0 = load the record, 1 = fall, 3 = despawned; falling adds the record's accel to an 8.8 velocity before adding that velocity to an 8.8 y accumulator, and the bounce — guarded by a non-zero divisor, a clear obj+0x6e and y having reached the record's line — snaps y onto the line, sets the velocity to -(velocity / divisor) with a signed truncating divide, triples the x step, latches obj+0x6e and plays packed sound 0x00040012. At y >= 581 the actor switches to its dead state, and because its draw callback tests state == 1 it draws nothing on that frame. Its frame comes from a {clip, hold} animation sequence whose end marker is clip 255, not -1, and whose first drawn frame is entry 1 rather than entry 0 because the cursor's timer starts at zero. The rock's whole frame family is 70..77, split across two sequences: 0x800a7328 carries 70..73 and 0x800a733c carries 74..77.
claims.notes: Authority 2 (original assembly) for every constant, cross-checked at authority 1 by running the interpreter's copy of the same actor and the translated port side by side: tools/verify_s415_rockfall_oracle.mjs compares 80 frames of drawSprite calls and finds the clip, x and y of every rock identical. Two corrections this pass made to earlier readings, both settled against the assembly: the record halves are {x, y} {bounceY, xStep} {accel, divisor} in that halfword order (not xStep before bounceY), and the sequence end marker is +255. Ledger s415-event-150-151-selected-by-flag-4018-2026-08-12 still leaves the 150/151 labelling unreconciled; nothing here depends on it. The second half, registry id 0x321, is the screen-content driver that submits the news tiles as 40 textured quads. Both ids, and every stage that reaches them, are s780 alone. The walker ran none of it in ordinary play because the stage overlay only boots behind the explicit ?nativeStages=1 research route; the vehicle family is now ported to engine/systems/street-vehicles.ts and runs in ordinary play, reproducing a live read of the original's two cars frame for frame. The news screens are now ported as well (engine/systems/street-screens.ts): the driver walks two 0x14-byte cursor blocks through the overlay's own tile/hold sequences, the announcement's SETANIM 801 802 opcode moves both cursors onto the news tiles on the following tick, and the port and the original machine code agree on all eight cursor words and all forty quads' geometry on every one of 240 consecutive PAL blanks.

claims.statement: A field script's SETANIM with a first operand of 0x320 or more creates and configures a STAGE OBJECT through one static table of 56 twelve-byte records {id, construct_fn, draw_fn} at RAM 0x8009B3E8 in FIELDSTG.PRO, walked linearly by F0x8009243c and terminated by a zero id. The constructor is called with the id as its only argument and returns the instance; the draw function is then called with (instance, second operand, third operand). Six of the 56 records name fieldstg's own resident code and mean the same thing on every stage (the four speech bubbles 803-806 and the scene object 813, plus 826 which no recovered script fires); the other fifty name an address inside the stage overlay window, all overlays loading at 0x800A5DE0, so one record means different code on different stages and the table's ids are allocated one stage each. The scripts honour that: over the 139 recovered script tables every one of the 48 stage-owned ids is fired by exactly one stage, and 261 (stage, id) members exist over 128 stages. The original does not test whether the resident overlay has code at a record's constructor address -- it jalrs whatever is there -- which is why the two records no script fires (833, 834) are the clearest evidence of the rule, and why thirteen records carry a zero constructor: those objects are made by their own stage through the shared allocator with the id as its fourth argument, so the live-object lookup finds them and the construct step is never taken. Twenty records carry a zero draw and are construct-only, ten of them the ten s415 boulder builders.

Each is a resident state-machine object whose TICK is the stage overlay's own code, and each reads the stage's point table through the resident global 0x80099D90, takes the three records whose tag byte is 1, 2 or 3, moves them onto the pad the SETANIM's second operand names (X = padX, Y = padY + a signed-byte per-slot offset, y-sort = padY + its y-sort offset) and drives each through its own script of {s16 spriteId, u16 duration} entries. Sprite 300 blinks a record off for its entry's duration and 0xFF ends a script; when all three have ended the records go inactive and the actor rearms. The entry stepper is the SAME 4-byte-cell routine the s415 rockfall uses -- min(delta,4) subtracted at depth 0, 0xFF the end marker -- so one port serves both. s925's copy has no configure routine on its record: its pad is two literals its constructor stores, 336 and 274. claims.statement: A technique's result line is decided by its own 18-byte record and by nothing else, so no technique can lose it. The apply arm of the record machine FIGHTSTG_F0x8008f714 reads the technique id off self+0x54, forms 0x80042bca + 18*id, reads the category byte at +0x04 and dispatches through the five-word table at 0x80083004 (categories 2..6; anything else builds no page). Record +0x10, the action clip the animation plays, is not read anywhere on that path, and the action VM's strike opcode FIGHTSTG_F0x8008c454 only spawns an effect, so the animation is presentation and cannot gate the page. The walker had the coupling inverted: it built the page inside the strike, so SEVENTEEN of the disc's 443 techniques put up no line at all - the seven field techniques 213-219 (clip 15, whose script is op4/op4/wait/op4/wait/op255) and the ten big-attack techniques 374-380 and 432-434 (clip 12, the cinematic whose only op10 is the non-contact type 66). Both counts are read out of all 246 shipped model anim.json files. Four further clips are strike-less per model only (9 in 5 models, 10 in 16, 11 in 1, 16 in 2) and four models ship clip 5 empty. The shared fix is one rule, not seventeen exceptions: all three commitImpact sites (basic attack, player technique, enemy technique) arm their result and the ST.RESULT_MSG tick commits it as soon as no action is playing, while a strike still commits it early. The category-4 heal amount is also settled: [0x800a4614] is ONE function pointer (.L0x800a4614: .word 0x800a0108), not a table, and FIGHTSTG_F0x800a0108 computes (power << 6) + (wisdom * power) / 8, truncated toward zero, capped at 9999 from the record's own +0x02 power and the effective stat block's +0x08, which is WISDOM; that amount is ported, and the arm's heal application with it.

claims.statement: Which event WRITES a story step and which site STARTS it are two different questions, and the writer's own routine never answers the second. Writing is uniform: a beat's completion routine ends in the leaf setter lui $v1,0x8005 / li $v0,N / jr $ra / sw $v0,-0x4c90($v1), where the store is in the jr's delay slot (so it always runs) and -0x4c90 off 0x80050000 is the master ordinal 0x8004b370; N is the step. Consumers are the bank-0x60 predicate (get_flag(0x60NN,e) = (step==0xNN)==e) read out of decoded DATA, never as an immediate: counting every decoded read site gives 16 for 0x6007 (1 stage-entry arrival chain, 2 step-program op-8 records, 10 NPC spawn-flag entries (9 distinct NPC records), 1 NPC dialogue-state gate, 2 talk-launch spawn flags), 74 for 0x600e (73 at recording; one spawn flag added by the 2026-10-05 scene extraction) and 20 for 0x6019. claims.statement: The field's dungeon and Spy Satellite rooms draw through ONE resident 2D draw-context service: the display table's thirty-slot registry object with id 0x1002, reached through the getter at 0x8004DF8C (F0x8001DA84, a lookup, not an allocator) and built once by the EXE through F0x8001DBE0 into a 0x16C-byte object with twenty-three method slots (F0x8001E5BC). Slot +0x128 writes the layer's effective screen rect (position - origin + 16.16 scroll, top byte only) and the overlays pair it with their own four-compare rectangle test; slot +0x14C emits nothing and instead queues a 20-byte record in a descending-by-y list, dropping the insert when full, and slot +0x154 flushes that list in order and resets it to a 0x7FFFFFFF sentinel. The layer's own flush writes six PS1 GP0 state commands (E3 texture window, E4 area top-left, E5 area bottom-right, E1 draw mode, E2 draw mode 2, E6 drawing offset reset) and then a GP0(60h) scissor rectangle; a queued shape is a four-word record -- [command][X][Y][U][V][CLUT][W][H] -- whose command is GP0(64h) and becomes GP0(66h) when the shape's record does not carry -1 in its third halfword, which every clip in this family does not, so every marker rectangle is TEXTURED. Forty-four sites reach it, in fieldstg and sixteen stage overlays, and twenty-two of those are one two-pass family -- a disc pass queued at the drawable's y and a column pass at y + 0x12 -- of which two members are ported: s805 0x349 (841), twenty-seven pooled children on a rand-driven delay walk, and s820 0x34d (845), four children of which one takes the default position. The shape routine's contract is the same on both members and is settled per overlay: each pass owns a pair of child halfwords whose first is the shape id and whose second is a CLUT-ROW offset, at child+0x64+tag*4 on s820 and child+0x60+tag*12 on s805 (so s805's column pair is +0x70/+0x72, two literals of 40, and +0x68/+0x6A are not its pass at all), and s805 reaches that routine by calling it directly rather than through the queue. The shape set the emitter reads is the stage's own TMPK sprite directory member 0, decoded for all fifteen family overlays, and the texels of the ids the two ported members ask for are in the per-stage sprite sheet the field already draws from, so both members' markers now draw the disc's own pixels.
