claims.statement: One attack action rolls ONE damage value, ONE critical and ONE accuracy per attempt. In FIGHTSTG_F0x8009e0cc the physical arm (record +0x04 == 2) calls the +0x9c accuracy method once (fightstg.s:28477), stores it at action-context +0x30 (:28484), then calls the +0x84 damage leaf once (:28487) and stores the result at +0x28 from a branch DELAY SLOT (:28490), so the leaf runs -- and its critical is decided -- even when the accuracy roll missed; the magical arm (record +0x04 == 3) has the identical shape with +0xa0 and +0x88 (:28559 / :28569 / :28571). The critical itself is INSIDE the shared tail F0x8009f6dc: one proc call (:29973) and one magnitude draw (:29979-29989), so a three-hit technique cannot crit three times. The multi-hit applier F0x8009d4b8 (:27621-27660) then rolls the +0x9c accuracy method `hits - 1` more times and writes only the per-attempt flag byte and the two counters; it never calls a damage routine or the critical proc. Its one early-exit arm is gated on the battle-mode word 0x800a4536 being exactly 6 (:27611-27620), which the shipped corpus never stores, so a three-hit technique spends three accuracy draws whatever happens, in the order FIRST, leaf, remaining. The applier is reached from exactly two routes that converge on :28580: the record's effect opcode +0x0a == 9 (both sides, both categories), and -- on the PLAYER side only -- the three-term plain-attack gate of record +0x0a < 2 AND record clip byte +0x10 outside {0x0b,0x0c} AND acting-side effective +0x37 nonzero (:28491-28504); the enemy's plain attack has neither the clip-byte nor the Multi-Crest term (:28546-28552). The applied total is ONE product of the landed-hit count and the single value (wfightmn.s:4682-4693). The drain heal is likewise computed once from that single value (fightstg.s:27724-27732) and sits behind the resolver's OWN accuracy result rather than behind 'any hit landed', because the whole secondary chain re-reads ctx+0x30 and returns when it is zero (:28506-28508). On the attacker-side affinity term: it is NOT the stage-2 weapon-family x1.5 of commit d4208584. It is the NEXT stage, stage 3, at its own lines: the tail adds trunc(running * acting-side effective +0x26 / 64) (:29904-29913), the effective-stat builder fills that block byte from the live combatant record's byte +0x0E (:29409-29411), and the only writes of a NONZERO value to that byte on a combatant record in pro/fightstg.s are FIGHTSTG_F0x80084bc0 (:2081-2084) and FIGHTSTG_F0x80084e0c (:2212-2215), which reach the record through a POINTER at arg0+0x54 and copy arg0+0x42 -- a halfword F0x80085110 PACKS from two 16-bit source fields and two table bytes (:2584-2598). An exhaustive displacement sweep finds nine stores to 0x0e in the overlay; the other seven zero or touch 0x20-stride slot arrays (the party/roster record family) or a different record at :14016, and are itemised in EV-Q004-AFFINITY-WRITER's summary. The reader was already ported (engine/dw3/battle-formulas.ts stage 3, acting side); the producer's operand is a packed field this claim names but does not measure, and the walker supplies 0 for it. The browser now follows the table through ONE shared resolver, engine/dw3/battle-combat.ts::resolveAttackSequence -- accuracy, then the leaf, then hits-1 more accuracy rolls -- for the player's plain attack, the player's techniques, the enemy's plain attack and the enemy's techniques, with no per-technique branch; resolveAttack is that function with hits = 1 and resolveMultiHit is it with the record's own hit count.
claims.coverage: Read the physical arm :28463-28512 and the magical arm :28553-28579 in full, the applier :27581-27670 in full, and the crit block :29966-29989 of the shared tail. The two-route claim is the enumeration of every branch that reaches :28580 in FIGHTSTG_F0x8009e0cc. The 'no damage in the loop' negative was checked by listing every instruction in :27628-:27660, not by sampling. The affinity producer was found by sweeping EVERY store in pro/fightstg.s whose displacement is 0x0e, any width and any base register -- nine hits, each classified by its base register's addressing (pointer through arg0+0x54, or an indexed 0x20-stride array) and by reading both builder routines and their only caller's frame stores. The first, narrower grep of `(sh|sb|sw) $v[01], 0xe($v[01])` returned three sites and would have supported a false 'only three stores' statement; the displacement sweep is the one that holds. The applied product was read in wfightmn.s. The mode-6 arm's deadness was measured by grepping every writer of 0x800a4536 across pro/ (four, values 0-4). The implementation side is pinned by tests/engine/systems/battle-combat.test.ts, five of whose six new tests were run against the pre-change engine and failed (the sixth pins the shared single-hit path and passes on both).
limitations: Static only. No capture against a running game was made for this claim; the rig has been a player session since 2026-09-13.

The claim says the AFFINITY WRITER is F0x80084bc0/F0x80084e0c and that their operand is a packed field. It does NOT say the affinity stage is ever nonzero in the disc's data: the packed operand of F0x80085110 was not measured. Frontier row (d) carries that.

F0x80085110 is a cop2 vector routine reached through an eight-way byte dispatch (fightstg.s:2530-2560) whose parameter list was not decoded; the packing arithmetic at :2584-2598 was read, the meaning of its source fields was not.
The accuracy leaf's own arithmetic was not re-read here; it rests on verified claim battle-accuracy-* and is unchanged by this work.
The special-mode finalize 0x800aabf0 (battle-mode word 0x800a4536 nonzero) still replaces the product with its own return; this claim does not model that arm and it is unchanged by this work.

The classification of the seven non-builder sites rests on their base register (a 0x20-stride indexed array or an init block), not on a decoded identification of each of those records. A record read through a pointer could in principle alias one of them; no aliasing check was made.

claims.statement: Two bounds the NPC spawn record decoder must honour, both read off the spawn loop and its flag-list predicate. (1) record+0x10 is read as a SIGNED halfword (pro/fieldstg.s:8487 lh) and stored to char+0x60 (pro/fieldstg.s:8489 sw), so it holds the 0-7 facing enum. The decoder therefore stops its run-scan at a word >= 256 there; that is a plausibility bound in the decoder, not a terminator the spawner tests (the spawner loop ends on a zero pointer word, pro/fieldstg.s:8490-8498). (2) F0x80016924 (exe/fns.s:7184-7211) walks {u16 id,u16 expected} pairs until the id word reads 0xFFFF with no entry count and fails at the first get_flag mismatch, so a flag list may be any length and a run with no terminator inside its overlay is not a list.
claims.coverage: Both quantifiers were measured over all 294 wstag overlays with the two scans that admit a spawn record (the longest contiguous run and find_puppet_records' strictly validated scan, tools/wstag_extract.py): 3,307 records carry n in {0,1,2,3,5,6,7} except exactly one word >= 256 (wstag805 file 0x14d0, n=0x4002a), and of 4,607 gate/on_close flag lists across 5,009 ptrB triples none is unterminated inside its overlay and the longest is 15 pairs. Commands: .venv/bin/python3 .bunny-scratch/measure_records.py and .venv/bin/python3 .bunny-scratch/measure_triples.py (both read-only over the overlays).
limitations: The census counts the records those two scans admit; a real record neither scan reaches would not be counted, so '3,307 records' is a lower bound on the discs records and 'no list is unterminated' holds for the lists those records name.
n >= 256 is a decode-side stop rule justified by the signed halfword the engine reads plus char+0x60 being the 0-7 DIR8 facing field; the disc does not itself write a terminator there.

claims.statement: s545 0x34f (847), s620 0x351 (849) and s680 0x32e (814) are three more shapes of THE point-record actor -- one claim walk, one stepper per overlay, one method block -- and are ported into the same module (engine/systems/point-record-actor.ts) and the same mined table (web/assets/data/point_record_actors.json), which is now twenty members over sixteen stages with 519 anchors. s545 0x34f is the recipe machine with two fields it alone needed: `advance`, because its claim arm ends in the object's own +0x38 (the tail every copy of this actor has), and `cue`/`latchClip`, because the cue 0x004C0002 sits inside its animate arm behind its own +0x10 clip test and the setClip(1) that makes the gate fire once; its 0x00ff blank is the flash frame again because the j's delay slot writes ctr 9 and the jump lands past the ordinary ctr store. s620 0x351 is a four-row grid whose per-slot write target is the overlay's own flag byte at slot+3, whose script is an ENTRY in its own 8-byte table at 0x800a7648 whose +4 halfword is the stepper's $a2 and whose +6 is the next index, and where a zero +6 puts the row out. s680 0x32e is eleven lane rows plus three scriptless traffic rows off ONE non-breaking claim walk, so its slots are the k-th MATCHING ROW in table order and claimRecord's first-match rule cannot express it; its configure routine is a 63-entry jump table of which eight arms do anything, and lighting a lane writes the lane's CURSOR INDEX, so a lit lane starts at entry 1. s680's overlay carries a FIFTH stepper copy whose end arm reads the end entry's third byte as a one-shot RISE in map pixels, parks it in the cursor's own +4 word and puts the index back to 0 rather than following it -- which is what walks a lane down the screen. Still interpreter only, with the whole read recorded: s545 0x350 (848), whose state 0 claims its own row AND builds five child objects whose tick is 0x800a5f20 and not its own -- a pad-flash child per {x,y,tag} row of the overlay's table at 0x800a6df4, driven by a six-arm clip machine and an eight-entry configure table that plays 0x8004474A on every SETANIM -- and s785 0x327 (807), which is not this actor at all but a raw sprite-packet player at a live sound object's position, needing a pack and a position source the walker does not have. NOT established: what fieldstg's live object NAMED 5 is for -- s680's subId 891 adds a pixel a blank to its +0x54 and that write is read and recorded, not ported, which is the same open gap s926 and s261 already left.

F0x80017174 folds a worn piece's stat add into the halfword its 0x2c-byte copy already filled with the member's own stored value, and re-tests that RUNNING total after every add: the sum is stored back, read as a signed halfword and replaced by 999 when it reaches 1000. claims.statement: A bit-31-clear sound id is a SEQ phrase (mpcommon/1.seq + 2.seq), and the original plays it ONE SPU VOICE PER NOTE-ON. F0x8003581c (exe fns.s L40884-L41301) asks the shared 24-voice allocator F0x80034b9c once per entry of its note list (L41033), handing it byte 0 of THAT note's own 32-byte tone record (L41016-L41018, via the single global D0x80082677); a refusal stores -1 and falls into the next entry (L41039-L41040), so one note is silent and the phrase carries on. One note-on can be several voices: F0x8003769c (L42886-L42961) returns one entry per VAB tone whose note range covers the note, so a layered note costs two voices on the same tick. The score's note-off is a 9n event with velocity 0 (F0x8002fe2c L34896/L34989 -> F0x800327ec L37660), and F0x80035d38 (L41213-L41301) then frees EVERY voice whose four key halfwords match -- the note, the per-entry byte, channel<<8|bank and the channel's program byte (L41245/L41251/L41257/L41263). Nothing in that key is the note's onset, so one note-off releases every repeat of that note and both tones of a layered note; (channel, note) is a complete key for all 32 phrases the disc ships, because no shipped score changes a channel's program between a note-on and the note-off that releases it. Both branches of the key-off clear the voice record at once (F0x8003670c L41864-L41881, F0x8003674c L41884-L41931), so the pool slot is free from the note-off onwards while the SPU's envelope still rings the release.
claims.coverage: Note-on and note-off paths quoted from the exe assembly at authority 2, including the allocator call, the priority byte, the refusal branch, the four key halfwords and both record-clearing branches. The census of the phrases themselves is the disc's data: build_sfx.py parse_seq_phrases()/parse_phrase_events() over mpcommon/1.seq + 2.seq, with the note->tone expansion from the mpcommon VAB; docs/research/audio/phrase-notes.json holds all 32 slots, 2113 note voices, each note's covering tones and each tone's byte-0 priority, and the walker's 27 of them are the ones a decoded call site reaches. tests/sfx-phrase-voices.test.js recomputes the (channel, note) pairing from that census and compares all 971 shipped note voices against the build's own digest.
claims.limitations: The per-note PAIRING is decided from the disc's score data plus the four key words; it was not observed on hardware. The tie-break's 'sample left' field is still modelled as milliseconds of audio remaining rather than the SPU's 16-bit ADPCM block counter (carried over from the voice-pool pass). The walker's key-off of a whole cue is per-sound, while the driver's stop path also takes the per-slot parameter byte into the key; and a note's release is baked into its rendered audio, so one voice cannot free its slot and ring on as two separate pieces.

claims.statement: Every state of the folder chooser F0x8009F110 - the screen that opens a duel - is anchored at its own address, and all twenty-two of them are reachable. The routine is mode 2 of the card-battle screen's mode machine F0x800A1B48: mode 2's update entry is the table word 0x80083A28[1] = 0x800A1C7C, which is cardgame.s:31739 and the only call site, and mode 2's enter entry 0x80083A00[1] = 0x800A1BA0 (cardgame.s:31683) zeroes duel+0x2F9 and duel+0x2FC, so the machine always starts at state 0. The index is duel+0x2F9, range-checked by sltiu 0x16, dispatched through the 22 words at 0x80083890; a value of 22 or more is not refused but behaves like state 0. Read in index order: state 0 is the opening gate, which waits with no timeout for the context at arg1+0 to exist with +0xC == 1 and +0x50 != 0, and always hands on to state 1 - the 1 it tests +0xC against is in the delay slot of its own first branch; state 1 raises the title band (escardgm 0x41 at y 38) and creates plate 0; 2/4/6/8 are the eleven-tick waits between the plates and the picker, with state 8's delay slot resetting the choice to folder 0 as it leaves, so the chooser always opens on Folder 1; 3 and 5 create plates 1 and 2; state 7 creates the cursor marker on plate 0's coordinates, which is what finally places the marker sprite of section 24.1; state 9 is the picker, reading logical 4 and 6 ORed with the auto-repeat word and never wrapping, and 0x0D to confirm, and it puts the marker back on the chosen plate every tick; 0x0A is the fifteen-tick hold; 0x0B shrinks the cursor marker away; 0x0C is a six-tick wait; 0x0D/0x0F/0x11 take the three plates down IN FOLDER ORDER, five ticks apart, four ticks between them against a six-tick shrink; 0x0E/0x10/0x12 are the four-tick waits; 0x13 takes the title band down over six units and is the one state whose 0x4001A is played inside the routine it calls rather than by the chooser; 0x14 is a six-tick wait served by the SAME table word as 0x0C; 0x15 builds the duel and returns 1. Because each wait moves on the tick its counter REACHES the bound - the bound itself is computed in the delay slot of the jump that tests it - the three plates are twelve ticks apart and the whole take-down is forty-five ticks from the confirm to the duel. NOT established here: what board-view slot +0xF44 fills, what F0x8009D9E4 and F0x8009EDCC do, the readers of the two index permutation arrays, whether two identical sound calls in one frame merge, and what arg1+0x00 is beyond its two conditions.

The screen that opens a duel is the original's own machine, and what a player sees on it is not what the browser showed. Coming up: the words "Choose a folder" and the first folder plate on tick 0, the second twelve ticks later, the third twelve after that, the cursor arrow on the first plate at tick 36, and buttons accepted from tick 48 - twelve ticks apart, not the eleven a reader who took the waits for gaps would say. Confirming: the chosen plate and the cursor both flash, then NOTHING at all moves for fifteen ticks, then the cursor shrinks away over five ticks, then the three plates go IN FOLDER ORDER five ticks apart with a dismiss sound on each, then the title band wipes shut over six units, and the duel builds itself on tick forty-five. So a player who picks Folder 3 watches Folder 1 leave first. The chooser reads only Up, Down and Circle: the directions do not wrap, an end press does nothing and is silent because the sound is inside the arm that moved, and there is no cancel. Confirming an EMPTY folder is not an error: the arm tests the folder's FIRST saved card and, on zero, copies a built-in forty-card list out of the overlay's own data verbatim - the save path subtracts one from every id and this one does not - so a player with nothing saved in a folder duels on the disc's own deck of 312, 42, 43, 310, 310, 310, 33, 33, 80, 41 and thirty cheap cards, instead of on nothing at all. Four divergences this removes: the plate spacing was eleven, the take-down began on the confirm frame with the plates four ticks apart and the duel opened twelve ticks after the confirm, the cursor stayed up until the confirm and then never came back, and the whole screen was silent in both directions. NOT established here: what the 0xF44 hand-off fills at duel+0x248, and the byte it returns at duel+0x244.

The four routines that build a duel are read end to end at authority 2. F0x8009D15C, board-view slot +0xF44, fills duel+0x50 with 189 halfwords in four passes -- 40 from duel+0x298 (the chosen folder, ids already one below the save's), 40 from duel+0x248 (the opponent's forty), 9 from the static table at 0x800A5BDC and 100 from the table at 0x800A5B14 read through F0x8009D140 -- at destination offsets 0x00, 0x50, 0xA0 and 0xB2, and returns 40+40+9+100 = 189, which the caller stores as one byte at duel+0x244. THE BUFFER IT FILLS IS duel+0x50, NOT duel+0x248: at the call site the third argument, duel+0x248, is built in the delay slot of the jalr, so it always runs, and it is an input. duel+0x248 has exactly one reader in the overlay, used as a bound (89 = 40+40+9) rather than an index. F0x8009D9E4 computes two bytes from the opponent's pile: duel+0x41B is the first slot whose availability byte exceeds 2*duel+0x300+2, walking up from duel+0x668 under a bound of 40, and duel+0x41C is the highest slot still carrying the retired marker 7 (40 if none is), written in the delay slot of jr $ra so it always runs. F0x8009EDCC makes no deck change at all: for each of the two sides it calls board-view slot +0xEA0 ten times, pushing the five S-Energy bytes (slots 0..4), the deck count (5), the hand count (6), the trash count (7) and the two totals (8 and 9). The two forty-entry arrays at duel+0x5B0 and duel+0x678 are INDEX PERMUTATIONS into duel+0x50, filled 0..39 and 40..79, not card ids. Finally, the disc's duel numbers cards from ZERO and its graphics service is one-based: F0x8009D15C loads each id signed and hands the texture helper id+1, and the 0x800A5B14 table's largest value is 315 against an album of 316 cards numbered from one.

Its four dispatch sites are the duel initialiser (cardgame.s:29435, base and count read from duel+0x5A0 and duel+0x5A4, i.e. 0 and 40), the turn loop (:9780), the round-end set reset (:31616) and a pile rebuild (:14129); each reaches it as (duel, rangeStart, count) through the duel pointer. claims.statement: FISH-Q009's premise is false and the mechanism is now closed statically. The player entity's animation-directory handle +0x9C is not swapped around a cast or a ladder mount; it is REWRITTEN BY THE CLIP RESOLVER ITSELF, from the clip id, in one store (fieldstg.s:13172, RAM 0x8008FA66) reached by six arms that each build a whole (pack LBA << 16) | clip-directory-bin constant across a branch and its delay slot: clip<8 -> 0x01870070 (P002PLAY), clip==8 -> 0x03CB001E (P002PLYK), 9..0x15 -> 0x03CA0064 (P002PLYF), 0x16..0x19 -> 0x03C9000B (P002PLYD), 0x1a..0x24 -> 0x03CC0017 (P002PLYL), and >=0x25 falls through to 0x03CA0064. Each low half equals that pack's own highest .bin, i.e. its clip directory, so the ranges and the packs' directories agree on every clip either defines. F0x800140D8 (fns.s:4605) splits a handle into pack (high16) and bin (low16), which is why a clip id can name a pack at all. So the angler's clip 0x11 reaches P002PLYF (LBA 970, dir bin 100) and the ladder's clip 26 reaches P002PLYL (LBA 972, dir bin 23), both one frame after SETANIM latched them, with no swap site anywhere. The resolver runs only when the clip CHANGES (:13143 skips an unchanged clip) and only for the entity whose character id is 2 (:13149-:13152), which is why an ordinary walk keeps its own sprite. The 'species-pack table reached through scene_struct+0x74' lead is falsified: that resolver (F0x800920DC, fieldstg.s:15635) is a bare TABLE[npc_id] over one flat global word array and supplies the CONSTRUCTOR value only. claims.statement: A per-map area-bank sound is a SEQ PHRASE of that archive's own score, played by the same sequencer as a common-bank 2D cue and taking one SPU voice per note-on out of the same 24-voice pool. F0x8002006c's 2D branch passes the id's low byte as the SLOT to F0x800335b4 -> F0x8003340c, together with the bank the current channel's +0x4208 row array holds for the id's row; the archive bits (18-24) are consumed earlier and only by F0x80020030, which picks the hardware channel holding that archive and does not reach the play call. F0x8003340c addresses *(D0x800815a0 + archive*4) + 0xB0*slot, i.e. a 176-byte record per phrase slot inside that archive, keys off the voices owned by (slot<<8|archive), and sets bit 2 of record+0x98. F0x8002f59c walks every resident archive's every slot each tick and on bit 2 calls F0x8003340c again, advancing the record's cursor through the score. The walker had resolved an area cue as a VAB tone ordinal selected by the slot (build_sfx.py bank_flat_slot), a rule no line of the original performs: the tone ordinal belongs to the positional (bit-31) path, where the id carries a program row, a tone and a note.
claims.coverage: The play path, the record address and its stride, the flag that says a score is playing, and the per-tick player that advances it are each quoted from the exe assembly at authority 2, with the delay-slot instructions marked as such. The disc side is the disc's own files: all 71 archives ship a score, and every block of every score parses to its declared terminator, which build_sfx.py records per slot in docs/research/audio/phrase-notes.json (archives). Of the 1152 slots, the 32 the disc's Sound Test names outside the common bank all land on a real block of their own archive's score, and tests/sfx-area-phrases.test.js recomputes that archive list from the Sound Test's own category table rather than from the census, requires the runtime note table's rows to equal it both ways, and renders every one of those 1532 note voices to the build's exact bytes.
claims.limitations: Which of the six resident bank slots holds which archive, and the eviction order that fills them (F0x800205f0's loader state machine), was not traced; the walker resolves by archive name, which is the same answer whenever the archive is resident. The 1120 slots no call site names are census rows only, not built voices. D0x800815a0 has 128 entries but only 6 are initialised, and what a seventh request addresses is not established. Static only: no emulator or rig run, and no listening test of the new area cues.

claims.statement: One .seq file is SIXTEEN phrase slots and an archive maps its score onto them in file-name order: F0x8003086c takes a free bank slot from the 32-bit residency mask at D0x80081598, installs the meta-handler table at D0x80081500, and calls F0x8003293c once per phrase while the index is below the count, which its caller passes as the literal 16 in the call's delay slot. Sound init sizes the whole record area once as six banks of sixteen slots based at D0x800519ec, and 6*16*0xB0 = 0x4200 is exactly the span up to D0x80055bec, the sound API pointer block. On the disc that is 71 archives, 70 of them with one score file and common with two, so 1152 phrase slots; the common bank's 32 are the ones the Sound Test's own id table names.

claims.statement: In a SEP score FF is a META PREFIX: the score player sets its running status to 0xff, reads exactly one more byte as the meta type, compares it with 0x2f for end of track, and otherwise calls the handler in the cell D0x8008150c, which F0x8003086c fills with F0x8003261c (it reads three bytes as one 24-bit tempo). Every meta event on this disc is type 51, set tempo with a three-byte payload, so a score may retime itself from its own tick onwards and the block header's tempo is the change at tick 0. Reading FF as a status byte with two data bytes, as build_sfx.py did, swallows the type byte and part of the tempo as event data and desynchronises the rest of the score: under that reading EVOLUTIO (evo_00 slot 0) renders 15,015,719 samples (340 s) instead of 768,557 (17.4 s), and three env cues render to silence. 88 of the disc's 1152 blocks carry such an event, 13 of them cues the walker plays.
claims.coverage: The 0xf0 arm, the running-status store, the single type byte, the 0x2f compare and the handler cell are quoted from the exe assembly at authority 2, together with the call that installs that cell. The disc side is measured: the meta-type census over all 1152 blocks finds only 0x51, and the tempo-change count per block is recorded in the census (tempoChanges), with the two builds' lengths compared per phrase.
claims.limitations: F0x800322ac's own body was not read (it forwards to F0x8003494c), so that the 0x51 payload is three bytes rests on the block walk landing exactly on every FF 2F 00 terminator, which tests/sfx-area-phrases.test.js checks for all 1152 blocks, plus the fact that no other meta type occurs. Whether any runtime path re-times a phrase other than through a score meta event is not established. Static only: no emulator run and no listening test of the corrected cues.
derivation: disc side: build_sfx.py parse_phrase_events() meta-type census over all 1152 blocks (only 0x51), and phrase_mix_row() rendering each superseded reading to compare lengths

claims.statement: s460 registry member 0x33e (830) and s526 registry member 0x33d (829) are ONE shape, ported as the `triple` machine of engine/systems/point-record-actor.ts beside its `parent` machine. Each parent is the same object -- the same display chain at [0x80099d90], the same shared stepper, the same method block at EXE F0x800143dc -- with a companion child array whose entry count is the allocator's third argument (36 and 48), and each builds its pool in state 0 and pokes every child in state 2. s460 makes NINE children from three makers (ticks 0x800a6118 / 0x800a64a4 / 0x800a6c2c, the last seven times); s526 makes TWELVE from four (0x800a6178 / 0x800a64fc / 0x800a693c / 0x800a6fb4, the last nine times). Every one of those children is a FOUR-STATE ROW ACTOR over the same block: state 0 claims a row of the stage's own chain by the tag its maker stamped, state 1 runs a first script with $a2 = 0 so the stepper restarts, state 2 runs a second with $a2 = 1 so it stops, and state 3 is the epilogue. s526's nine-times maker IS one of s460's makers in shape -- the same allocate-and-stamp routine -- and its child is the same WALKER as s460's third maker's, with the same field offsets, the same radius 30, the same andi 0xfff angle mask, the same (rand & 0xf) - 7 jitter and the same rsin/rcos pair; its copy differs only in its own state 0 (an indirect table instead of a literal) and in claiming a second row, the one whose tag is nine higher. So the family is SEVEN distinct child machines over ONE shape, and the module grew one machine, not seven. Three numbers a delay-slot reading gets wrong and the port carries: the single row's picture is the LITERAL 60 in state 1 and 61 in state 2, not the stepper's return, because those stores sit in the stepper call's own delay slot; the twin's picture comes from four bytes at 0x800a73d8 (62, 63, 64, 65) indexed by the row loop, at offset 0 in state 1 and 2 in state 2; and s526's fixed-picture child holds 33 for its whole run. A walking child's countdown is the WORD at +0x58 and its expiry JUMPS BACK TO STATE 0 with selector 3 in the delay slot, so the walkers re-claim every 60 blanks and the copies' selector==3 speed-bleed arm is dead code in the shipped build. s460's fourth stamped child claims nothing, because the stage's own table carries no row tagged 4; the port records that claim as null and the child writes nothing, which is the only answer that cannot be wrong about memory the disc never wrote. ONE ORDER FACT is OPEN: for an id >= 0x320 the SETANIM handler first asks [0x8004b7bc] for an existing instance (fieldstg file 0x2180-0x21a0) and only configures it if one is found; only otherwise does it construct (0x21bc, with move_ $s1,$v0 in the delay slot of the j at 0x21cc) and then configure. The configure's only arm is setState(2), so state 0 (the pool build) runs only if the object exists before the event sends 844/843. Which path the disc takes is not read; the port builds the pool at construction, as the `parent` machine in the same module does. The walkers' HEADING is not the original's: the original aims through a 33-entry table scan (wstag460 file 0xb60-0xccc) that reads the game's single random stream [0x8004DC0C], the walker's RAND_U16 is Math.random(), and the port takes the heading from the walker's own source while keeping the integrator's counter, period gate, Manhattan test, sin/cos step and row write. The census is 258 ported / 3 interpreter only.
claims.notes: Authority 2 (original assembly), re-read this pass end to end in both overlays and cross-checked by tools/extract_child_pool_parents.py --check over all 294 wstag images, so nothing in the table is typed in. Pinned by tests/triple-parents.test.js (18 tests) and by the census in tests/stage-registry-members.test.js, tests/child-pool-parents.test.js and tests/point-record-actors.test.js, whose pins move to 258/3; the OLD table fails them, since HEAD carries s460's 0x33e as "machine": null, "ported": false with no triple key and the HEAD module has no triple at all. Player-visible evidence: tools/verify_triple_parents.mjs, which boots s460 and s526 in ordinary play with no ?nativeStages, replays the census's own one command per room and reports the rows that changed and the pictures they hold (s460: 9 rows claimed, 14 changed, 14 lit, 7 walkers moved; s526: 22 claimed, 24 changed, 24 lit, 9 walkers moved), plus verify_child_pool_parents, verify_point_record_actors and verify_object5_slide, all VERDICT OK. Stays partially_verified for those reasons.

claims.statement: The game's timed battle effects are ONE pool of 99 entries of 28 bytes at 0x800a3868, advanced by the ACTION rather than by a frame: F0x8009ba4c takes the earliest entry, subtracts its time from every other entry and returns the code that came due, and each action-resolution epilogue re-prices the turn as F0x8009bda4(side, 0) halved (pro/wfightmn.s:1210-:1219). A stat change is code 0x0d/0x0e/0x0f staged by F0x8009cc20 with opcode 12's cost 2000 + rand % base + 10 * own SPT, refreshed in place when the same code, side and slot are already queued, and expired by writing zero into the record's own modifier halfword (pro/wfightmn.s:2816). The two locks are codes 0x10/0x11 from F0x8009cd1c, priced (rand % 101 + 100) * technique[+0x0C], and expired by clearing bit 4 or 5 of the record's +0x1c (pro/wfightmn.s:2743-:2773). The pick prefers the earliest entry but a code 2 or 3 incumbent yields to any newcomer, codes 4, 6 and 9 keep their slot when they fire, and only codes 1..24 have a consumer row at 0x800a5e6c. Both doubts the job raised are settled on review. (1) The opcode table needs no shift: read in place, opcode 12 is [2001, 0, 0], so its divisor is 2001 and it has no bounds (0x8009c174-0x8009c194). (2) The getter's flag only picks its scratch block; the default arm's numerator is the OTHER side's SPD, because the move_ $s0, $v0 in the second getter jalr's delay slot keeps the handed-side result in $s0 and $a3 takes the other side's (0x8009c21c-0x8009c228, lh $v0, 0xa($a3) at 0x8009c284). The delay is base * sqrt(opp/own).

The opponent's forty-card array at duel+0x678 starts in the order the disc's own data lists them. The identity fill writes duel+0x5B0[i] = i and duel+0x678[i] = 40 + i for i = 0..39 (cardgame.s:29413-29414), so the two piles are the two halves of the 189-entry card table at duel+0x50: entries 0..39 are the player's folder and 40..79 the opponent's, in slot order. Every later change to that array preserves order: each draw removes one entry and shifts the tail down one (cardgame.s:14629-14648), so the array only shortens from the front, and the one routine that writes NEW entries into it, F0x8009DA68, appends them at the tail below the live length. This is the answer to the question section 33.7 left open: the opponent draws its folder from the front, in the order the disc lists it.
claims.coverage: The fill is read at cardgame.s:29409-29418 with every delay slot accounted for; the removal loop is read at :14629-14648 and its two sibling shapes at :14661-14680 and :14689-14708; the only other writer of duel+0x678 in the whole overlay is F0x8009DA68, whose single call site is :31613. grep -n '0x678(' over cardgame.s returns exactly seventeen lines and all seventeen are listed in CARD-DUEL-VERIFIED.md section 34.2. The browser side is a census: the opponent's pile is byte-for-byte unchanged through the Start phase and a set reset, asserted in tests/card-battle.test.js against the SHUFFLED_PILES member list.
limitations: Static reading only; not observed in the running game.

The claim is about the array's order. Which INDEX a given draw removes is settled separately by cardduel-each-side-draws-against-its-own-block-counter-2026-10-05, and the selector at cardgame.s:1295-1302 was not traced past the two fields it reads.
Rests on the reference enumeration described in cardduel-opponent-pile-order-is-never-reversed-2026-10-05, including its displacement-grep caveat.

claims.statement: Nothing reachable in the card game overlay reverses or permutes the opponent's forty-card array at duel+0x678. Of its seventeen DIRECT references, eight are in state 2 of the six-state machine at 0x80090058, eight in state 3 of the ten-state machine at 0x800A0CD8, and one is the identity fill; within the sixteen, each is one half of a shift-down, a rotate-from-the-tail, or a swap with the halfword at duel+0x6C6, and all eight shapes move an entry DOWN the array or to its tail. F0x80090190 and F0x80090ED4 are not routines: they are jump-table arms chosen from the state byte at duel+0x422 through the tables at 0x8008353C and 0x80083554. The two WRITES through a pointer rather than an offset are F0x8009DA68 (0x14($a3) off a block hard-wired to duel+0x664) and F0x8009F04C (0x14($s0) off duel+0x59C, so the side-0 pile). This CONFIRMS cardduel-opponent-pile-is-never-shuffled-2026-10-05 with the loophole closed: that claim rested on the shuffle routine being unable to address the array, and this pass shows the array's other sixteen direct references are shifts and rotations, none of which is a permutation.

The seventeen references were enumerated mechanically by grep over the whole overlay, not by hand.

The seventeen references are the DIRECT ones, enumerated mechanically by grep over the whole overlay. A writer that reaches the array through a pointer with a register-computed displacement would not appear in that count. The pointer-based writers were narrowed separately: grep for '0x664' over cardgame.s returns every site that builds side 1's block pointer, and only two of those routines also write at 0x14 -- F0x8009DA68 (:27510) and the set-change caller -- so the list above is believed complete for this overlay, but the check is a displacement grep and a computed displacement would escape it.

That the same check misses readers is not a gap for this claim (a reader cannot permute) but it IS a gap for the hand-array claim: cardgame.s:9841 reads duel+0x6C8 through a pointer, and a direct-offset scan does not see it.

Only state 2 and state 3 of the two machines were read in full. States 1 and 4-6 of the six-state machine and states 1, 2 and 4-10 of the ten-state machine were not read end to end; they cannot write duel+0x678 without one of the seventeen references, and none is in them, but what they DO is not established.
The claim covers the card game overlay only. The parent exe was not searched for a writer of the array.

The block offset is built inside state 3 of the ten-state machine at cardgame.s:14492-14496 as 25 * side shifted left three, i.e. 0xC8 * side, and the read at :14499 adds 0x600 to it; 0x600 + 0 is duel+0x600 and 0x600 + 0xC8 is duel+0x6C8, the +0x64 field of each block. This is consistent with the block layout already in engine/systems/card-battle.ts's header, which calls +0x600 the hand array and +0x614 the trash array, and it closes the third of section 33.7's five open names.

claims.statement: Each side's pile removal is bounded by its OWN block's +0x04 field, and the two are different addresses. Side 0's arm loads duel+0x5A0 at cardgame.s:13690 and again at :13703; side 1's arm loads duel+0x668 at :14623, :14644, :14675 and :14686. duel+0x5A0 is side 0's +0x04 and duel+0x668 is side 1's +0x04, the blocks being duel+0x59C and duel+0x664, 0xC8 apart. The opponent's draws therefore never read duel+0x5A0. The INDEX removed comes from a separate selector at cardgame.s:1295-1302, which writes duel+0x440 from duel+0x5A0 when its argument is zero and from duel+0x41C when it is not; both stores are delay slots and always run. This closes the last of section 33.7's five open names.

claims.statement: The opponent's hand array is physically sorted, in place, at two points in the opponent's own turn, and the sort is ascending, on a key no two entries share (class, then +0x35E = weight(class) + entry), so its exchange-sort order is fully determined. The routine is F0x8009D8FC (cardgame.s:27418-27475): it takes no side argument, keeps the duel pointer at :27418, and can only reach +0x6C8, which is side 1's hand array. Its key is the byte at duel+0x35C + 4 * (index - 0x28) and, on a tie, the halfword at +0x35E of the same 4-byte record -- so the key is indexed by the opponent's own folder entry and 0x28 is 40, the first index of the opponent's half of the card table. A swap happens only on a STRICTLY smaller key (slt at :27446, bne at :27449, beqz $t2 at :27454), which makes it stable, and the swap is between two halfwords of the array itself (:27456-:27459), so there is no index list and every later reader sees class order. Its only two call sites are cardgame.s:29949, in the Program Phase immediately before the AI's legality scan F0x800A4978, and :30688 at the Summon Phase kickoff. Before this the browser left the opponent's hand in the order it was dealt and derived the order only inside the AI policy (aiHandOrder returned a sorted index list), so the row of cards the player sees across the top of the board came out in dealt order. engine/systems/card-battle.ts now carries the decoded member list SORTED_HAND_ARRAYS = ['opponent'] and one function sortDuelHands that reads it, called from the two phase opens; aiHandOrder sorts through the same routine and returns the straight order.
claims.coverage: The sort was read from its first instruction to its jr $ra at cardgame.s:27474 with every delay slot resolved, and the two call sites were enumerated mechanically by grep for the jal target over the whole overlay -- there are two, not more. The key table at duel+0x35C was already decoded in tools/extract_card_opponents.py and read through one function (slotClass, which handClass also uses), so there is one ordering rule and not two. The browser side is a census: tests/card-battle.test.js reads SORTED_HAND_ARRAYS back, requires it to equal ['opponent'], asserts the player's hand array is untouched, and checks the stability tie case. The old engine bundle fails that test file outright (no export named SORTED_HAND_ARRAYS), and a check written only against exports the old bundle had shows the opponent's hand going from 61,62,63,64 as dealt to 62,64,63,61 (slots 1,3,2,0 -- classes 1,1,2,3) across the phase open, with the player's hand unchanged. One pointer-based reader of the same array was found and is named here because a direct-offset scan cannot see it: cardgame.s:9841 `lh $a3, 0x6c8($s2)` reads an opponent hand entry through a pointer, tests the class byte at duel+0x35C + 4*(entry - 0x28) at :9846 and skips class 5 at :9847, which is the summon scan rather than the sort. It confirms the same key table and the same 0x28 base from a second site.
limitations: Static reading only; not observed in the running game.
WHY only the opponent's hand is sorted is established from the routine's hard-wired offset and its two call sites, both inside the opponent's turn. No mode outside those two sites was read.

The +0x35C class byte's own table was decoded in an earlier pass (cardnpc-deck-entry-byte-03-is-the-ai-play-class-with-5-never-summoned); this pass confirms the sort reads it and does not re-derive the table.

claims.statement: F0x8009DA68 is the opponent's set-change handler and moves its own hand back into its own pile, last entry first. It hard-wires side 1's block (addiu $a3, $t1, 0x664 at cardgame.s:27510) and never reads the side argument its caller passes in $a1 at cardgame.s:31614 -- the $a0 it uses is the duel pointer written in the delay slot of that same jal at :31612, overwriting the duel+0x59C that :31611 had set for the side-0 handler F0x800A19F8 one line earlier, which has already returned. Each pass steps the opponent's deck cursor and hand count down, reads the hand array at duel+0x6C8 + 2*(handCount-1) and writes it into duel+0x678 + 2*(cursor-1) (cardgame.s:27519-:27528), and raises the deck count by one. So the hand is walked from its last card to its first and the pile is written below the live length, not in front of it. The thirty-nine bytes cleared to 39 at duel+0x332 (:27597-:27602) and the exact shape of the group value 2*duel+0x300 + 1 were not traced.
claims.coverage: Read end to end from cardgame.s:27509 to its jr $ra at :27603, with the call site at :31613 and the delay slot at :31612 resolved by hand. claims.statement: A ladder in this game only answers the button while you are LOOKING at its tile, and the way it mounts you is read out of one word. One shared system arms every ladder: the type-7 step-load F0x80088288 (pro/fieldstg.s:5501) splits the grid byte under the player into a facing group (:5519) and a step index (:5520), keeps the group in the step object's +0x60 (:5521), and returns live only when the player entity's own +0x60 - its facing - indexes a non-zero byte of that tile's row in the 8x8 cone table at RAM 0x80097624 (:5544-:5552). Opcodes 2 and 3 are the ladder foot and head (:5799, :5815), so a rail end answers Confirm only inside its own three-facing cone; this is why standing on a ladder tile and pressing Confirm does nothing unless you turn to face it, and it is the whole reason a browser check that pressed Confirm from a fixed facing could never mount. The mount then stores the word it was handed into the player entity's +0x60 - the very field the step-load reads back (:12601 foot, :12644 head, reached through entity slots +0x114 and +0x118) - and picks the climb sprite's side from that same word (`beq $s3,$v0(=5)`, :12605 / :12648). Opcode 2 hands its own group through untouched (:5808); opcode 3 hands 5 when the group is exactly 1 and 3 otherwise, because the `li $a1,0x3` at :5819 is the `bne`'s DELAY SLOT and only the fall-through at :5820 changes it. Over all 216 rails in the shipped stages (432 ends) only four (opcode, group) shapes exist and every one hands over facing 3 or 5, so a ladder always mounts you looking up-left or up-right, and both ends of a rail hand over the SAME side because the data pairs every group-3 foot with a group-7 head and every group-5 foot with a group-1 head. 429 of the 432 ends are armed; the three that are not carry opcode 8 (a cutscene cell) or 6 (a party-slot cell) and mount nothing. Finally, letting go at the foot writes zero into +0x60 (:13983), so the player faces down on the floor, while letting go at the head never stores +0x60, so the head's cone stays unarmed until the player turns - true of every rail in the game, not of one stage.

claims.statement: The four timed battle ailments and the per-side status tick are entries in the SAME 99-slot pool at 0x800a3868, not per-ailment counters. Code 0x09 is poison (record +0x1c bit 0x01, time the constant 1000), 0x0a the FROZEN recovery (bit 0x02, delay opcode 9), 0x0b the CONFUSED recovery (bit 0x04, delay opcode 8 or 10 chosen by the CALLER's technique id) and 0x0c the ASLEEP recovery (bit 0x08, delay opcode 11); code 0x05 is the per-side status tick (delay opcode 2). All four refresh an existing entry in place - poison rewrites only the payload, the three cures only the time, and each of those writes is its own j's delay slot. The fired code is dispatched through the 24-row table at 0x800a5e6c into one action type and then through the table at 0x800aade4 into one per-actor machine. Code 0x09's slot survives its own fire (0x800a3800's word is -1) and its consumer re-arms +0x02 with 1000; codes 0x0a/0x0b/0x0c are freed on the fire, and FIGHTSTG_F0x8009c330 clears the matching bit and frees the entry, so the entry's expiry IS the cure. Opcode 8's own magic divides by 2710 while its rebuild multiplies by 8001, so the confusion recovery answers 2000 for every draw from 2710 up. Every store into the queue in the whole 319-file assembly corpus is one of 17 sites in pro/fightstg.s, and 15 of them take the slot from that record byte; exactly one of the disc's 443 techniques has byte 35, id 393 "Cross Slash", so Cross Slash is the only technique that can set +0x5B.
claims.coverage: Denominator: a header-base-propagating sweep of all 318 pro/*.s plus exe/fns.s returning exactly 27 stores into the queue, all of them in fightstg.s -- 17 through a header+index or header+counter base (13 slot-indexed at +0x38+index, 2 at +0x30+counter, 2 inside the consumer) and 10 at fixed byte offsets (+0x3A, +0x3B, +0x3C, +0x3E, +0x41 three times, +0x42, +0x43). Corpus-wide literal sweeps find zero `sb ...,0x5b(` and zero covering `sh 0x5a` / `sw 0x58` into the header in any file. claims.statement: The mirrored facings of the field-actor billboard (F0x8008f52c, entity+0x60 >= 5) differ from the left-side ones in three ways and NOT in a fourth. They place the quad's left edge at screenX - (entity+0xE4 + entity+0xDC), they take the far X column one short, and they store the REVERSED U row (u0 = base+E4-1, u1 = base, u2 = base+E4-1, u3 = base). They do not touch Y: all four lhu 0xe0($s1) reads of the Y side are unconditional and sit before the second facing test, so entity+0xE0 is added identically whichever way the sprite faces and a right-facing actor stands on the same screen row as a left-facing one. The two branches separate at fieldstg.s L12959 `j 0x8008f770`, whose delay-slot `addu $v0, $v1` always runs and supplies the left side's u3; reading that block as a fall-through would overwrite the mirrored U row with the forward one.

claims.statement: There is no second, offset-less frame-list format on the disc. The resolver's walk is one loop with one 4-word stride, so every frame it can draw carries record words 3 and 4 as its billboard X and Y registration. What the walker's extractor previously called 'Format B' is the packs' clip DIRECTORY -- a 0xc-byte record structure reached through the directory path (fieldstg.s L13203-L13233, .L0x0000ce40-.L0x0000ce68) and never as a frame list -- which the u16 guess mis-read and handed to the build as offset-less frames. A zero duration word is not an end-of-list marker: the resolver stores 0 back into entity+0xCC and re-reads word 0 (fieldstg.s L13205), making such a row a HELD frame.
claims.notes:
Census 2026-10-05 over the whole corpus, run through the extractor's own walk by tests/field-billboard-anchor.test.js: 179 packs decode, 771 walk rows / 2,989 walk frames and 2,125 clip directions / 13,474 clip frames, 16,463 frames each on exactly one decided row, none of them a guess, and exactly one held row (p188blok up = frame 6, forever). The same census against the previous extractor reports 8 walk rows with no registration at all and 17 + 5 frames and 5 clip directions the u16 fallback had thrown away. Consequence for the walker: build_assets.py's _anchor_correction bounding-box fallback and every getbbox() call in it are deleted, and the build now raises on a row the disc registers nothing for. partially_verified: the corpus census is a mechanical count, but the ONE remaining question is whether any .bin outside the 179 decodable packs is ever loaded as a frame list -- the undecodable packs were not swept for their own frame lists. Whole-corpus file sweep, same pass: the 179 packs hold 1,457 .bin files and every one is classified -- 1,278 frame lists (7,226 records, each carrying both registration words) and 179 clip directories (one per pack, exactly the set the directory path reads), with NONE unclassified. So no pack and no file sits outside the census: the member list the code handles and the member list the disc holds are the same set, and there is no unread frame list hiding in a pack whose walk row the walker does not read. Still partially_verified for one reason only: no original runtime comparison was run (static pass, no rig time used), so the numbers are authority-2 legible but uncaptured. GAP FOUND BY THIS CENSUS, in the anim grouping rather than in the billboard: 46 of the 179 packs have their direction-sheet `up` row filled from `down_p` instead of from their own up-facing frames, because decode_sprite_anims picks the pack's CLIP DIRECTORY as its last row (a 3- or 5-bin pack's last .bin is its directory, so _decode_bin_records yields nothing and clean_pairs substitutes down_p). Those rows carry the down row's own disc words, so every one is registered -- but 46 up-facing sheet rows show the down-facing frames. Measured cause, over all 179 packs: the positional group equals the directory's clip 1 (idle) for 57 packs, its clip 4 (walk) for 35, and neither for 87 (5 of which have neither clip), so the positional rule is not the pack's own directory and re-deriving it would change most of the corpus's walk animation. Left as a named gap in docs/research/field/field-actor-sprite-anchor-decoded-2026-08-17.md section 3, not patched: no hand row and no override was added. What settles it is reading each pack's sheet rows from the directory (clip 4 for walk, clip 1 for idle) instead of a bin position, with its own claim, census and before/after captures.

 CONSEQUENCE OF THAT GAP, measured 2026-10-05 (opaque pixels per cell, every cell of all 171 sheets sampled): those 8 rows are the only rows the corrected stride-4 walk ENLARGED (up 1 -> 3-4 frames), and web/assets/sprites is a symlink to the shared tree this branch may not write, so the shared sheets still hold 1 frame of art there -- p045amst, p048gdam, p076hanm, p077hasm, p082etem, p083mete, p084kete, p086aird draw frames 1-3 of their up row from empty cells and so flicker out while walking away from the camera, until the lead's rebuild bakes the down art into all of them (build_assets.py fills a missing direction's row from down). Registration is correct on those rows throughout; this is stale art plus the anim-grouping gap, not a hole in the port. Of the 20 rows with at least one empty cell across the corpus, the other 12 (p015lumo left/right, p126itmb up, p149sncm up-right, p198adme's eight rows) have identical frame counts before and after this pass and are pre-existing.

claims.statement: A place's scene is started by a GATE OBJECT: an object the stage overlay hands the shared allocator (F0x80014504) whose own routine calls start_event (jal 0x800853f8). Counted over all 294 wstag overlays there are 86 such routines and they fall into exactly three groups and nothing else: 76 stage-entry objects on the RESET band (phase 0, negative or >=4), a SECOND object on the PHASE-1 band installed only by s795 (tick 0x800a637c, pro/wstag795.s:0x5b4-0x5d0) and s800 (tick 0x800a6688, pro/wstag800.s:0x8c0-0x8dc), and 8 interactive help-menu / yes-no controllers that can hand start_event a CHOICE of two or more event ids and so belong to the controller system, not this one (tools/measure_gate_objects.py, which returns a non-zero exit if any routine is left unclassified). The phase-1 object reaches its band on its SECOND turn, because a fresh allocation's phase word is 0 and its phase-0 arm returns through the object's own vt+0x38 (exe/fns.s:8955-8963, phase = phase + 1), so it latches exactly once per field load like the reset band. It also calls its overlay's own ambient updater first and then tests the scene descriptor idle (pro/wstag795.s:0x600-0x654 reads +0x50/+0x54/+0x58/+0x5c/+0x60). Engine side: engine/systems/scene-arrival.ts carries both bands and every gate object a place installs, tools/extract_arrival_candidates.py recognises both shapes, and the converted rows carry the band so a later raise in the same visit skips only the reset band (web/game.js playTalkEvent / web/engine-bridge.js rechain).

A scene's own HANDOFF warps on all three of the routes that start one. The disc has three starts (the stage's gate object, the position step's op-8 record, and the bank-0x90 talk launcher) and all three call the same start_event, so all three run the same bytecode and all three perform the scene's HANDOFF. The walker honoured it on the gate-object route only (web/engine-bridge.js:92 doHandoff) and dropped it on the other two: playTalkEvent routed only the save-point and yes/no families, and the position step's playEvent used the handoff solely to decide whether to chain a battle. Measured consequences: s410's event 90 (started by the stage's own step, 'who's in charge') ran to its end and left the player standing in the station instead of sending them out through HANDOFF 554 -> s400, and the East/South Station gondola's four scenes said their line and did not move. Both routes now hand the handoff to the same doStoryHandoff the bridge uses. A second shared fault fell out of the same experiment and is fixed here: the field's confirm probe ran while a scene was between its ops, so a press meant for the scene restarted whatever conversation stood in front of the player (measured: the gondola ride scene restarted 22 times in a row and never reached its HANDOFF); web/game.js's `circle` branch now returns while a cutscene is active, which is what the disc's confirm probe does behind the scene runner's state.

The per-place hand rows in the scene build are gone, and the census that proves it is mechanical. tools/engine-convert/decode-table.json lost 64 rows, every one of them measured to name an event a decoded start already reaches: 15 cutscene rows marked `trigger: "None"` by hand (13 the ported gate objects or op-8 steps, and s795/1505 + s800/1506 the places' second phase-1 gate object), 26 native-handler rows (the 16 fire traps, the 6 trap-pad switches, the 2 Gunslinger layout switches, the 2 ambush-tile handlers) whose own note already said the step program owns them, 13 interactive-controller rows (the eight-topic help menus and the yes/no tutorials) started by the bank-0x90 launcher, and 10 `OnExit` rows naming a trigger no decoded routine supplies (the disc has no exit trigger: 3 were gate-object candidates, 3 were op-8 step records, and 4 were the two stations' console conversations). Only the two vestigial ambush rows (s949/9000, s953/9000) stay, because no step program reaches them and their stage's slot 5 is empty. In the generated scene files exactly ONE hand field existed in 294 stages - s410's `gondola: true` exit with `consoleX`/`consoleY`, written by tools/wire_gondola.py (deleted) so an invented exit trigger could fire the gondola; the console is a decoded invisible talk point (npc 63) whose conversation starts the scene, so the zone and the four rows are replaced by data plus the two warp ports above. tests/scene-rebuild-reproduces.test.js pins both: the whole field vocabulary of all 294 scene files (68 keys; `gondola`, `consoleX`, `consoleY` are gone) and the rule that no row may stand in for a start a decoded system already owns. Both fail on the old data.

The game has exactly ONE random source in its own code and the battle and the field read the same one: rand_u16 at the function pointer 0x8004dc0c (exe/fns.s:10116-10134) counts the index word at 0x8004dc04 up by one, wraps it at 0xfff, and hands back the disc's own 4096-halfword table at 0x8004bc04 under it -- an unsigned halfword, so 0..0x0fff, with no multiply and no addend. A cold boot's first draw reads table index 1, because the routine counts up before it reads. rand_u16_set_seed (exe/fns.s:10107-10112) stores `seed & 0xfff` and has NO caller anywhere in the corpus, and nothing else writes the index word, so the index word's data-image value of 0 is what every cold boot runs from and the stream is one 4096-value cycle. A census of every reference to 0x8004dc0c across all 318 disassembled overlays and the EXE finds 87 references in 12 overlays, every one an indirect jalr, and nothing anywhere else: the card duel, the field, the fight, the card shop, the title, the fight report, the gym, the pause screen and the three stage overlays with moving objects all pull the one count, and the EXE never calls it.
claims.notes: Authority 2 throughout: original assembly plus the exe's data image. The two negatives (no seeder caller, no second stream) rest on a per-register lui/addiu/ori constant scan that clears a register whenever any instruction writes it, because a naive scan reported thirteen phantom hits in stgtrain from a saved-register reuse; both materialisation spellings of 0x8004dc0c are handled (`addiu $r,-0x23f4` after `lui $r,0x8005`, and the two-operand `addiu $r,$r,-0x23fc` that keeps 0x8004dc04 in a register for `lw 0x8($r)`). NOT verified against the running game: no emulator was started and no RAM image was read. Shipped as engine/dw3/random-stream.ts, with the table extracted verbatim by tools/build_native_overlays.py into web/assets/native/exe_tables.json and re-checked against the engine's copy by tests/random-stream.test.js. Canonical document: docs/research/battle/game-random-stream-2026-10-05.md.
claims.coverage: The census is the whole population, over every disassembled file in ~/ddw3/asm/dw2003, not a sample; per-site rows with the exact instruction forms are in the canonical document's section 2 and the code's member list is pinned against them by tests/random-stream.test.js. What is deliberately NOT claimed: that a retail disc always boots at index 0 (that rests on the data image plus the empty caller census, not on a run), and the semantics of any individual caller's mask -- the callers' own formulas are separate claims.
claims.frontier_rationale: Answers the four decoder questions of BATTLE3D-Q001 that named this stream: the idle camera's RNG is `rand_u16() % 3` (already decoded by bunny/camdirector) and where that number comes from was the open half.

claims.statement: A moving stage object's heading is drawn from the game's one random stream: `(rand & 0xff) << 4`, written to the child's own word 0x76 on the integrator's re-aim arm (wstag460 file 0xd54-0xd70, wstag526 0x10dc-0x10f8 -- the same machine twice), and again when the pool builds the child (0xf5c-0xf80 / 0x1324-0x1344). The re-aim then draws a SECOND value for the counter, `(rand & 0xf) - 7` (0xd8c-0xdac / 0x1110-0x1134), so a re-aim frame costs two draws per walking child and a pool build costs one, in that order. So the path a player sees as a row walks the map is the disc's, not the walker's.
claims.notes: Authority 2: the two stage overlays' own assembly. The walker previously called Math.random() at all three sites in engine/systems/point-record-actor.ts and its module header said so; both are gone and the header now carries the citations. NOT ported, and named in the module header: the disc's separate angle routine that turns a DIRECTION into a heading (a 33-entry halfword table scan and an interpolation, wstag460 file 0xb60-0xccc) -- this change routes the stream, not that routine. wstag780's four draws are a different consumer (a one-bit `andi $a3,$v0,0x1` coin flip that decides whether a street object spawns at all) and are not a heading.

claims.frontier_rationale: The stagegate job's own-gap note said the original aims by reading the game's single random stream while the walker used its own; this is that gap, closed.

claims.statement: All four of BATTLE3D-Q001's remaining values are settled from static evidence, and three of them confirm the walker rather than change it. (1) The idle camera's RNG/dwell were already decoded and shipped by bunny/camdirector (four shot lists at 0x800a24b8, `rand_u16() % 3` over three bytes per row at 0x800a2518, the dwell in raw per-frame deltas); what was open was where the NUMBER comes from, and it is the game's one stream (claim game-single-random-stream-is-a-disc-table-walk-2026-10-05). (2) The op6 clip cursor's step global D0x800a4464 has exactly ONE writer, FIGHTSTG_F0x8009e428, with a four-arm mode table: 0 = the frame delta, 1 = frozen at 0, 2 = a `while (acc >= 5) { step++; acc -= 4 }` accumulator, 3 = twice the delta -- so 'one clip entry per logic tick' is mode 0's own value rather than an assumption, and the mode word 0x800a453c has exactly one writer (F0x8009e510, reachable only through the method table at 0x800a4544/0x800a4548). The walker's slowMoStep already matches all four arms. (3) The HP bar's gradient is green above a quarter of maximum HP and red at or below it, with each branch's first word on vertices 0 and 2 and its second on 1 and 3, over two mirror-image quads -- which is what engine/dw3/ui/native/battle-hud.ts already ships. (4) The camera roll sign is UNOBSERVABLE on the disc's own records: the canned-shot loader zeroes the roll for every canned shot and every op5 preset, and no shipped record sets one, so the walker's MINUS-roll convention is a reasoned derivation that cannot diverge today.
claims.notes: Authority 2: original assembly for all four. Item (4) is deliberately reported as unobservable rather than as a proven sign -- the loader's `sw $zr, 0x2c($v0)` at fightstg.s:15948 zeroes the roll on every path that reaches it, and the shipped placement table's camera schema carries no roll field, so nothing on the disc can currently disagree with the walker. Resolving the SIGN would need a script op5 record with a non-zero roll word, which this corpus does not contain. Items (2) and (3) required no code change; item (1) required the stream change recorded in the other two claims.

claims.frontier_rationale: Closes BATTLE3D-Q001: all four values decided from code, with the honest answer recorded for the one that is decided by the disc's own silence rather than by a value.

claims.statement: The special interaction on the three block actors (npc 328/351/352) is settled in mechanism and timing, statically. Pressing confirm while facing one starts a two-part scene: the player - in Digmon form on every screen that spawns these actors - plays a 36-tick animation while the block waits 20 ticks, then plays a 21-tick clip and vanishes; the landing cue (COMEX113) fires as the block starts to move, about 0.4 s in; the field is held busy until the player's own animation ends, about 0.72 s, and the block is gone about 0.82 s after confirm. Each block carries its own completion bit, so each can be done once. The engager and target modes 0x4d/0x4e are action states, not clips - the clips are 0x45 (engager) and 0x54 (target). What the two clips depict is not in the data; the depiction still needs a capture.

Clip ownership was swept over all 358 field sprite packs: clip 0x45 is defined by exactly one pack, p123digm (bins [90,91,92,93,94]; durations [10,7,2,2,10,5] = 36 ticks); clip 0x54 by exactly one, p188blok (frame list 12; 5+4+4+4+4 = 21 ticks). claims.statement: The memory-card block is a verbatim RAM image of the resident interval beginning at 0x80048D34 (0x26C4 bytes) with exactly two bytes overridden: a checksum at image+0 and the format byte 4 at image+2. Loading verifies those two bytes and copies the image back over RAM whole; there is no per-field packing inside. The checksum test the original itself applies is lenient - it passes when the recomputed byte has no bit the stored byte lacks - so a two-card diff checker should compare for equality. A separate 0xD4-byte summary side block (checksum, slot, format, 'DMW3' magic, three nameplate records) is built alongside, not inside. What the retained bytes mean is still unnamed.
claims.coverage: Write side re-read: pro/stgmcard.s:3511-3554 (0x26C0-byte copy loop plus final word, checksum store at :3549, format store at :3552), with F0x80015564 an 8-bit XOR fold (exe/fns.s:5876-5886) reached through pointer slot 0x80048AA8 (rust/dw2003_exe_data/src/data.rs:2460). Load side re-read: pro/stgmcard.s:3214-3252 (read into the buffer with a3=slot+2; recompute F0x80015564(buffer+4, 0x26C0); bit-subset compare vs buffer+0; format==4 gate, error 8 otherwise) and :3253-3269 (copy-back). The stat/level frame was re-derived: the 19-halfword block starts at image + 0x784 + slot*0x3DC (roster_stats+0x1C; level seed exe/fns.s:7463), not at +0x1C + slot*0x3DC.
limitations: Settled for the image content, layout and the load path only. The semantics of the retained bytes are not established: image +0x0001 and +0x0003, the gap 0x04DE, 0x061B..0x0628, 0x075A..0x0760, roster +0x4A..+0x50, +0x56..+0x58, +0x3D5..+0x3D8 and the non-final records' +0x3D8..+0x3DC, and most of the resident control block 0x0004..0x0030 remain unnamed.

No organic memory-card capture: no original save was dumped. Everything here is a static re-read (authority 2). Raw card-file identity I/O and the BIOS-title/folder text conversion remain open companion/platform contracts.

Drafting note: Diff prediction for two cards differing by one added form entry: the first zero-id ledger cell at 0x7B8 + slot*0x3DC + i*0x14 gains its id (+0) and level 1 (+2); image byte +0 (the checksum) changes; nothing else moves unless the standing form or the equipped triple also changed. Compute equality for the checksum, not the original's subset test. Rig watch warning: a watch placed at 0x80048D34 + s*0x3DC + 0x1C is 0x768 bytes early - the stat block's first field is at image + 0x784 + s*0x3DC.

claims.statement: Each acquired-form card entry is 0x14 bytes: the form id as a halfword at entry+0, form level as a byte at entry+2 (acquisition writes level 1 there), a preserved byte at entry+3 that no writer in the corpus touches, the form's DVEXP bank as a word at entry+4, and six flagged technique words at entry+8..entry+0x13. The card carries this representation unchanged: whole entries copy in and out verbatim, and the card driver copies the resident interval with no separate save packing. What static reading cannot show is the organic case - no diff of two real cards exists yet.
claims.coverage: Byte-level stores re-read at exe/fns.s:8309-8310 (id halfword + level byte) and the whole-entry copies at :8341-8348 (read-out) and :8386-8392 (write-in), which include the DVEXP word. The preserved-byte search was a literal-displacement grep for 0x7bb over exe/ and every pro/ overlay: zero store hits - a matcher that cannot see computed addresses. The acquisition path F0x80017924 (exe/fns.s:8255-8316) writes the id and the level only.
limitations: The requested direct proof - an organic memory-card comparison of two cards differing by one acquired form - was not made; the representation is established statically. A failed lookup treats ids below 3 as empty (F0x8001764c skip rule, DIGI-C010-form-ledger-api).
Entry+3's purpose is unknown: zero literal writers found is not proof of absence, because computed addresses are invisible to the scan.

claims.statement: The battle overlay's sounds are settled trigger by trigger. The menu blips are a move sound and a confirm sound (both captured first-hand on the original command menu in our lab) plus a cancel sound. A landed blow plays the attack's hit sound - a technique's own contact sound, a basic attack's fixed one - and a missed blow swaps that to a distinct evade sound. A technique plays the sounds authored in its animation clip, plus its element's backdrop loop while the effect runs, plus the signature whirl while it is held; a Jogress plays its own bank sound. Using an item plays nothing beyond the menu blips it was chosen with. A KO has no dedicated cue: the defeated monster's death animation carries its own thud. A win plays the win jingle and a loss plays the gameover jingle; the fight-report screen plays its own two branch jingles.

claims.statement: Our fight is missing four sounds the original plays and one re-trigger. (2) The entrance cue of one battle effect actor (COMCD103) - nothing in our game code plays it. (3) The victory jingle after a battle win (W_JINGLE): our fight never plays it; the only place our build plays it is the card duel. (4) The final boss's mid-fight phase change onto its second track (boss04 / LASTB_02): the original switches the battle track mid-fight; ours never does. And the post-digivolution track replay: the original re-plays the battle track once the evolution jingle finishes; ours lets the jingle play over the running music and never restores. Everything else the overlay plays, ours plays too: the menu blips, contact sounds, the element loops, the signature whirl, the Jogress sound, EVOLUTIO, PLAYER11, GAMEOVER, ITEM_GET, the report jingles and the system blips, with batl00 as the battle default. claims.statement: A sound's life belongs to the game's sound driver, not to the screen that started it. A track or jingle goes through one exclusive slot: starting another track ends the previous one, and only an explicit stop ends a track on its own. Ordinary effect cues are held in the driver's slots and are never swept away when you leave a screen - a screen can end one only by naming it, and a movie stop-all is the one big exception. That is why a jingle keeps playing until the next track starts, and why the download's cues are not cut when the scene changes.
claims.coverage: Full start/stop table and the boundary call sites read from the disc: play F0x8002006c; stops 0x80020204 / 0x800202d4 / 0x8002037c / 0x5c50->F0x8002096c->F0x80034698; the exclusive register D0x80055c34 and its replacement callback fns.s:17704-17; per-screen leave stops (title stdwtitl.s:4159-4162, cnty_sel 106/113, stgtrain 2669/2678, stgmcard 4871/4983, stplnmet 5488/5496) and the movie/END stop-all (stdwtitl.s:1162, :1659).
limitations: Single static pass with no isolated review; the fade's callers and two register cells had no caller found (0x5c6c/0x5c4c) and music loop metas are left to the music document.
The rule was not yet confirmed by a live watch of the register cell 0x80055c34.
claims.derivation: Read the driver's play and stop entries, every caller of the stop cells across the overlays, and the exclusive register's writers.

claims.statement: Every sound in the game starts through one entry point, and there is no separate music entry: tracks are ordinary ids carrying a track flag, so the same call starts a jingle or a tune. What ends a sound is one of four stops - stop everything, stop one named cue, fade out, or stop the voice a positional cue handed back - plus the driver's own cuts when the same slot is reused or a whole channel's bank is reloaded.
claims.coverage: The stop set and their parameters, with the play entry and the request/load/stepper/busy cells (0x5c50/0x5c54/0x5c58/0x5c5c/0x5c60), read from fns.s and the overlays that call them.
limitations: Same single static pass; 'bit30 marks a track' is read from the start paths but the id space's other bits are the separate packed-word question, still open.
No live watch was run.
claims.derivation: Enumerated the start/stop API from the driver and the boundary callers from the overlays.

claims.statement: A sound id packs everything the driver needs: which archive to look in, whether the cue is placed in the world or played flat, whether it is a track that replaces the previous one, and which tone to play. Two things people might expect are not there at all - loudness and priority are not in the id, and nothing in the game reads the bits that look like a loop flag, even though several authored ids set them.
claims.coverage: Field-by-field table with the reading instruction for each: archive bits 18-24, bit31 positional vs flat, bit30 the exclusive gate, program 11-17, tone 7-10, note 0-6, row 8-15 (its halfword names the bank), slot 0-7; the port's unpackSound matches the assembly's split exactly.
limitations: Bits 25-29 are read by nothing in the corpus (5 unrelated shifts by 0x19-0x1d in fns.s; the whole entry read instruction by instruction), so the 'looping (bit 29)' gloss in the system document is unbacked and is corrected there.
The row table at +0x4208 has five loads and zero static stores; who fills it is untraced (the document points at F0x800205f0).
Single static pass, no isolated review.
claims.derivation: Read the play entry instruction by instruction and cross-checked the port and the live ids.

claims.statement: The driver's voice bookkeeping is a word of eleven flag bits, and each has a job: whether the voice is sounding, whether a release has been asked for, whether it is being re-seized, whether a fade is armed, and whether the note has ended - with five bits that something tests but nothing in the game ever sets.
claims.coverage: Each bit with its set/clear/test site cited (keyed-on also cleared by the note-end routine at fns.s:34739-34740, which the system document's table missed); the pool's record is a separate structure at 0x38 stride whose keyed-on flag is +0x1b.
limitations: Bits 3/4/6/7/8/10 have no setter in 338 files and their handlers are unreachable - named, not explained.
Bit 9's consumer was not found; the +0x14 byte has writers and no reader. Single static pass, no isolated review.
claims.derivation: Enumerated every set/clear/test of the flag word and the pool record across the sound region.

The rest are zero in every real save we hold, so naming them needs a save from further into the game or a live watch on those bytes.
claims.coverage: Field-by-field with writers and readers cited across 338 assembly files and four matchers, plus a diff of the two real cards (all 14 differing bytes classified, checksums re-verified) and a walker round trip through the native save screen (0/9924 bytes differ).
limitations: The unattributed spans (ledger +3, roster +0x56..+0x58 and +0x3D5..+0x3D8, image +1/+3/0x4DE/0x61B..+0x628/0x75A..+0x75F, control +5..+0x2F) are all zero in both real saves.
The RAM service-table installer for block+0x26C4..+0x2760 is not in the disassembly and its routines have no visible callers.
Static plus our own harness; no console-side third dump was taken.
claims.derivation: Read every writer and reader of the named spans, classified the real card diff byte by byte, and round-tripped a real card through our save screen.

claims.statement: The deeper crevice's ride now plays: the Bulbmon drops onto its rail with a bounce and a thud, then rolls in through the ride's three sequences, driven by the stage's own animation operands rather than a hand row. Of the stage scripts that were interpreter-only, one remains.
claims.coverage: Ported as a shared machine with an extractor (776 anchors verified), a re-run census (260 ported / 1 interpreter-only) and a headless check that the stage's own operands drive all five phases.
limitations: The scene entry's own spawn call site is story-gated and not yet wired: the browser builds the walker from the stage's SETANIM operand instead.
The scrolling layer (item 1c) is decoded end to end but its port is blocked on the tile-to-screen quad geometry and one capture of the first seconds after the stage loads.
claims.derivation: Read the script's integrator and stepper from the disc, implemented them as one machine, and verified against the stage's own data.

claims.statement: The post-game sequence's last missing piece now plays: the fight that follows the Spy Satellite terminal boss opens with its half-minute movie, at the native picture size and rate, and then the fight the field was already starting; at every other story number a field fight starts directly, and the movie can be skipped with Start. That closes the chain that was settled except for this clip.
claims.coverage: The launch condition, the format, the cadence and the hand-back are all read from the disc with citations, and a headless check drives the whole hand-off (35 legs): picture rate, self-end, the fight following, the skip, and the no-movie case one story number later.
limitations: The title screen's own movie player was not rebased on this shared module - merging the two is future work.
No console capture: the disc settles the mechanism and the check drives the walker.
claims.derivation: Read the launch funnel, the movie table row and the hand-back from the disc, ported the player once, and verified the hand-off headlessly.

claims.statement: When a partner is confused in a fight, the game swaps the battle music for its own confusion piece and puts the fight's music back when the state ends - captured on the live game, with the id and the register cell recorded. That closes the first of the two sounds that had no caller in the code: it had one, and it only appears in play.
claims.coverage: Live capture of the swap and the restore with the register cell's values and the call sites, matching the static reading that only one playing block forms this id.
limitations: The static side had found no address-forming site; the capture is what settles it.
One observation, no isolated review.
claims.derivation: Set the Confused state in a live battle, watched the track register and the play entry, and recorded the swap and restore.

claims.statement: A bounded sweep of one Giant Hill stage did not turn up the two event sounds: nothing played them, and the stage's own blocks, when interacted with, all dispatch one field cue and flip a completion bit instead. So those two sounds are either unused in the shipped game or they fire only somewhere the sweep did not reach - which is the honest state, not a closed one.
claims.coverage: The play log has zero occurrences of either id across the whole sweep, with the register cell read at every sample; the same session also produced the live facts for the block actors, which corroborate the decoded interaction (clip 0x54, the completion bit).
